//! The document type declaration and its internal subset.
//!
//! Nothing here validates. The subset is read for the three things that change what a document means to a parser that
//! doesn't validate: the entities it declares, the attributes it defaults, and the attributes it gives a type other
//! than CDATA, whose values are normalized differently. Everything else is only checked for being well-formed. The
//! external subset and external parameter entities are never read.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::rc::Rc;

use crate::chars;
use crate::chars::CLASS;
use crate::names::IdMap;
use crate::names::flag;
use crate::parser::In;
use crate::parser::MAX_ENTITY_DEPTH;
use crate::parser::Parser;
use crate::parser::R;
use crate::parser::at;
use crate::parser::lossy;
use crate::parser::scan_name;
use crate::parser::scan_nmtoken;
use crate::parser::skip_spaces;
use crate::tape::NONE;
use crate::tape::kind;

/// How deep the groups of a content model can nest.
const MAX_CONTENT_MODEL_DEPTH: u32 = 256;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum EntityKind {
    Internal,
    /// An external parsed entity. Its text is never read.
    External,
    /// An external entity with a notation: not XML, and not something a document can include.
    Unparsed,
}

pub(crate) struct Entity {
    pub kind: EntityKind,
    /// The replacement text of an internal entity.
    pub text: Rc<[u8]>,
    /// Set while the entity's text is being parsed, to catch an entity that includes itself.
    pub expanding: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct AttributeDefinition {
    pub name: u32,
    /// The string operands of the default value.
    pub default: (u32, u32),
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Dtd {
    pub general: HashMap<u32, Entity>,
    pub parameter: HashMap<u32, Entity>,
    /// The attribute definitions that have a default value, of each element type that has any, by the element's
    /// name.
    pub attlists: IdMap<Rc<Vec<AttributeDefinition>>>,
    /// Every (element, attribute) that has a definition, with whether its type is a tokenized one. This is what
    /// says which definition of an attribute came first, and it keeps an element with a great many attributes from
    /// costing a walk of a list for each of them.
    pub defined_attributes: HashMap<(u32, u32), bool>,
}

/// The public identifiers of the XHTML family of DTDs. A document with one of them can use the HTML character
/// entities, as if it had read the DTD.
fn is_xhtml_public_id(public_id: &[u8]) -> bool {
    matches!(
        public_id,
        b"-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Transitional//EN"
            | b"-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.1//EN"
            | b"-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Strict//EN"
            | b"-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Frameset//EN"
            | b"-//W3C//DTD XHTML Basic 1.0//EN"
            | b"-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.1 plus MathML 2.0//EN"
            | b"-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.1 plus MathML 2.0 plus SVG 1.1//EN"
            | b"-//W3C//DTD MathML 2.0//EN"
            | b"-//WAPFORUM//DTD XHTML Mobile 1.0//EN"
            | b"-//WAPFORUM//DTD XHTML Mobile 1.1//EN"
            | b"-//WAPFORUM//DTD XHTML Mobile 1.2//EN"
    )
}

/// The public and system identifiers of an ExternalID, as ranges of the input.
#[derive(Default)]
struct ExternalId {
    public: Option<(usize, usize)>,
    system: Option<(usize, usize)>,
}

impl Parser<'_, '_> {
    fn dtd_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Dtd {
        self.dtd.get_or_insert_with(Default::default)
    }

    /// Skips white space that has to be there.
    fn required_spaces(&mut self, inp: In, pos: usize, message: &str) -> R<usize> {
        let after = skip_spaces(inp.bytes, pos);
        if after == pos {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, message);
        }
        Ok(after)
    }

    /// doctypedecl ::= '<!DOCTYPE' S Name (S ExternalID)? S? ('[' intSubset ']' S?)? '>'
    pub(crate) fn doctype(&mut self, inp: In, start: usize) -> R<usize> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        let mut pos = self.required_spaces(inp, start + 9, "Space required after 'DOCTYPE'")?;
        let name_end = scan_name(bytes, pos);
        if name_end == pos {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, "xmlParseDocTypeDecl : no DOCTYPE name !");
        }
        let name = self.intern_name(inp, pos, name_end);
        pos = skip_spaces(bytes, name_end);

        let (external_id, next) = self.external_id(inp, pos, true)?;
        pos = next;
        self.has_external_subset = external_id.public.is_some() || external_id.system.is_some();
        if let Some((public_start, public_end)) = external_id.public {
            self.is_xhtml = is_xhtml_public_id(&bytes[public_start..public_end]);
        }

        self.tape.push(kind::DOCTYPE, name, NONE);
        for id in [external_id.public, external_id.system] {
            match id {
                Some((id_start, id_end)) => {
                    let id = &bytes[id_start..id_end];
                    // A line end is a LF wherever it is, and the source can't be edited to make it one.
                    let (offset, length) = if id.contains(&b'\r') {
                        let mut normalized = Vec::with_capacity(id.len());
                        let mut index = 0;
                        while index < id.len() {
                            if id[index] == b'\r' {
                                normalized.push(b'\n');
                                index += if id.get(index + 1) == Some(&b'\n') { 2 } else { 1 };
                            } else {
                                normalized.push(id[index]);
                                index += 1;
                            }
                        }
                        self.arena_push(&normalized)
                    } else {
                        self.string(inp, id_start, id_end)
                    };
                    self.tape.push(kind::VALUE, offset, length);
                }
                None => self.tape.push(kind::VALUE | kind::ABSENT, self.src.len() as u32, 0),
            }
        }

        pos = skip_spaces(bytes, pos);
        if at(bytes, pos) == b'[' {
            pos = self.subset(inp, pos + 1, true)?;
            pos = skip_spaces(bytes, pos);
        }
        if at(bytes, pos) != b'>' {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, "DOCTYPE improperly terminated");
        }
        Ok(pos + 1)
    }

    /// ExternalID ::= 'SYSTEM' S SystemLiteral | 'PUBLIC' S PubidLiteral S SystemLiteral
    ///
    /// A notation declaration can also have a public identifier alone, which `strict` rules out.
    fn external_id(&mut self, inp: In, pos: usize, strict: bool) -> R<(ExternalId, usize)> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        let mut id = ExternalId::default();
        if bytes[pos.min(bytes.len())..].starts_with(b"SYSTEM") {
            let literal = self.required_spaces(inp, pos + 6, "Space required after 'SYSTEM'")?;
            let (literal_start, literal_end) = self.system_literal(inp, literal)?;
            id.system = Some((literal_start, literal_end));
            return Ok((id, literal_end + 1));
        }
        if bytes[pos.min(bytes.len())..].starts_with(b"PUBLIC") {
            let literal = self.required_spaces(inp, pos + 6, "Space required after 'PUBLIC'")?;
            let (literal_start, literal_end) = self.pubid_literal(inp, literal)?;
            id.public = Some((literal_start, literal_end));
            let after = skip_spaces(bytes, literal_end + 1);
            let quote = at(bytes, after);
            if !strict && quote != b'"' && quote != b'\'' {
                return Ok((id, literal_end + 1));
            }
            if after == literal_end + 1 {
                return self.fail(inp, after, "Space required after the Public Identifier");
            }
            let (literal_start, literal_end) = self.system_literal(inp, after)?;
            id.system = Some((literal_start, literal_end));
            return Ok((id, literal_end + 1));
        }
        Ok((id, pos))
    }

    /// SystemLiteral ::= ('"' [^"]* '"') | ("'" [^']* "'")
    ///
    /// Returns where the literal's text starts and ends, the end being the closing quote.
    fn system_literal(&mut self, inp: In, pos: usize) -> R<(usize, usize)> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        let quote = at(bytes, pos);
        if quote != b'"' && quote != b'\'' {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, "SystemLiteral \" or ' expected");
        }
        let start = pos + 1;
        let mut end = start;
        loop {
            if end >= bytes.len() {
                return self.fail(inp, pos, "Unfinished System or Public ID \" or ' expected");
            }
            let byte = bytes[end];
            if byte == quote {
                break;
            }
            if byte >= 0x80 {
                end += self.check_non_ascii(inp, end)?;
            } else if CLASS[byte as usize] & chars::INVALID != 0 {
                return self.fail(inp, end, "Unfinished System or Public ID \" or ' expected");
            } else {
                end += 1;
            }
        }
        Ok((start, end))
    }

    /// PubidLiteral ::= '"' PubidChar* '"' | "'" (PubidChar - "'")* "'"
    fn pubid_literal(&mut self, inp: In, pos: usize) -> R<(usize, usize)> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        let quote = at(bytes, pos);
        if quote != b'"' && quote != b'\'' {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, "PubidLiteral \" or ' expected");
        }
        let start = pos + 1;
        let mut end = start;
        while end < bytes.len() && bytes[end] != quote && CLASS[bytes[end] as usize] & chars::PUBID != 0 {
            end += 1;
        }
        if at(bytes, end) != quote {
            return self.fail(inp, end, "Unfinished PubidLiteral");
        }
        Ok((start, end))
    }

    /// intSubset ::= (markupdecl | PEReference | S)*
    ///
    /// For the subset itself (`top`), parses up to the closing bracket and returns where it ends. For the
    /// replacement text of a parameter entity, parses all of it: a declaration can't start in an entity and end
    /// outside of it.
    fn subset(&mut self, inp: In, mut pos: usize, top: bool) -> R<usize> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        loop {
            pos = skip_spaces(bytes, pos);
            if pos >= bytes.len() {
                if top {
                    return self.fail(inp, pos, "internal subset is not finished");
                }
                return Ok(pos);
            }
            match bytes[pos] {
                b']' if top => return Ok(pos + 1),
                b'%' => pos = self.parameter_entity_reference(inp, pos)?,
                b'<' => {
                    let rest = &bytes[pos..];
                    pos = if rest.starts_with(b"<!ELEMENT") {
                        self.element_declaration(inp, pos)?
                    } else if rest.starts_with(b"<!ATTLIST") {
                        self.attlist_declaration(inp, pos)?
                    } else if rest.starts_with(b"<!ENTITY") {
                        self.entity_declaration(inp, pos)?
                    } else if rest.starts_with(b"<!NOTATION") {
                        self.notation_declaration(inp, pos)?
                    } else if rest.starts_with(b"<!--") {
                        self.comment(inp, pos, false)?
                    } else if rest.starts_with(b"<?") {
                        self.processing_instruction(inp, pos, false)?
                    } else {
                        return self.fail(inp, pos, "internal subset is not finished");
                    };
                }
                _ => return self.fail(inp, pos, "internal subset is not finished"),
            }
        }
    }

    /// PEReference ::= '%' Name ';'
    ///
    /// Between declarations, a reference to a parameter entity stands for more declarations.
    fn parameter_entity_reference(&mut self, inp: In, start: usize) -> R<usize> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        let name_start = start + 1;
        let name_end = scan_name(bytes, name_start);
        if name_end == name_start {
            return self.fail(inp, start, "PEReference: no name");
        }
        if at(bytes, name_end) != b';' {
            return self.fail(inp, name_end, "PEReference: expecting ';'");
        }
        let name = &bytes[name_start..name_end];
        let next = name_end + 1;
        self.has_parameter_entity_references = true;

        let found = self.names.find(name, self.storage()).and_then(|id| {
            let entity = self.dtd.as_ref()?.parameter.get(&id)?;
            Some((id, entity.kind, entity.text.clone(), entity.expanding))
        });
        let Some((id, entity_kind, text, expanding)) = found else {
            // The entity may be declared in something this parser doesn't read.
            if self.standalone {
                return self.fail(inp, start, format!("PEReference: %{}; not found", lossy(name)));
            }
            return Ok(next);
        };
        if entity_kind != EntityKind::Internal {
            return Ok(next);
        }
        if expanding {
            return self.fail(inp, start, "Detected an entity reference loop");
        }
        if self.entity_depth >= MAX_ENTITY_DEPTH {
            return self.fail(inp, start, "Maximum entity nesting depth exceeded");
        }
        self.account_for_expansion(inp, start, text.len())?;

        if let Some(entity) = self.dtd_mut().parameter.get_mut(&id) {
            entity.expanding = true;
        }
        self.entity_depth += 1;
        // An error in the entity's text is reported where the document refers to the entity.
        let saved_offset = self.entity_reference_offset;
        if inp.main {
            self.entity_reference_offset = start;
        }
        let result = self.subset(
            In {
                bytes: &text,
                main: false,
            },
            0,
            false,
        );
        self.entity_reference_offset = saved_offset;
        self.entity_depth -= 1;
        if let Some(entity) = self.dtd_mut().parameter.get_mut(&id) {
            entity.expanding = false;
        }
        result?;
        Ok(next)
    }

    /// Checks that a declaration ends where it should.
    fn end_of_declaration(&mut self, inp: In, pos: usize, message: &str) -> R<usize> {
        let pos = skip_spaces(inp.bytes, pos);
        if at(inp.bytes, pos) != b'>' {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, message);
        }
        Ok(pos + 1)
    }

    /// elementdecl ::= '<!ELEMENT' S Name S contentspec S? '>'
    /// contentspec ::= 'EMPTY' | 'ANY' | Mixed | children
    fn element_declaration(&mut self, inp: In, start: usize) -> R<usize> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        let mut pos = self.required_spaces(inp, start + 9, "Space required after 'ELEMENT'")?;
        let name_end = scan_name(bytes, pos);
        if name_end == pos {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, "xmlParseElementDecl: no name for Element");
        }
        pos = self.required_spaces(inp, name_end, "Space required after the element name")?;

        let rest = &bytes[pos..];
        if rest.starts_with(b"EMPTY") {
            pos += 5;
        } else if rest.starts_with(b"ANY") {
            pos += 3;
        } else if rest.starts_with(b"(") {
            let inside = skip_spaces(bytes, pos + 1);
            if bytes[inside..].starts_with(b"#PCDATA") {
                pos = self.mixed_content(inp, inside + 7)?;
            } else {
                pos = self.content_group(inp, inside, 1)?;
                if matches!(at(bytes, pos), b'?' | b'*' | b'+') {
                    pos += 1;
                }
            }
        } else {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, "xmlParseElementDecl: 'EMPTY', 'ANY' or '(' expected");
        }
        self.end_of_declaration(inp, pos, "xmlParseElementDecl: expected '>' at the end")
    }

    /// Mixed ::= '(' S? '#PCDATA' (S? '|' S? Name)* S? ')*' | '(' S? '#PCDATA' S? ')'
    ///
    /// `pos` is right after '#PCDATA'.
    fn mixed_content(&mut self, inp: In, mut pos: usize) -> R<usize> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        let mut names = 0;
        loop {
            pos = skip_spaces(bytes, pos);
            match at(bytes, pos) {
                b')' => {
                    pos += 1;
                    break;
                }
                b'|' => {
                    pos = skip_spaces(bytes, pos + 1);
                    let name_end = scan_name(bytes, pos);
                    if name_end == pos {
                        return self.fail(inp, pos, "xmlParseElementMixedContentDecl : Name expected");
                    }
                    names += 1;
                    pos = name_end;
                }
                _ => return self.fail(inp, pos, "MixedContentDecl : '|' or ')*' expected"),
            }
        }
        if at(bytes, pos) == b'*' {
            return Ok(pos + 1);
        }
        if names > 0 {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, "MixedContentDecl : '|' or ')*' expected");
        }
        Ok(pos)
    }

    /// choice ::= '(' S? cp ( S? '|' S? cp )+ S? ')'
    /// seq ::= '(' S? cp ( S? ',' S? cp )* S? ')'
    /// cp ::= (Name | choice | seq) ('?' | '*' | '+')?
    ///
    /// `pos` is after the opening parenthesis and the white space that follows it. Returns where the closing
    /// parenthesis ends.
    fn content_group(&mut self, inp: In, mut pos: usize, depth: u32) -> R<usize> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        if depth > MAX_CONTENT_MODEL_DEPTH {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, "xmlParseElementChildrenContentDecl : depth too deep");
        }
        let mut separator = 0u8;
        loop {
            // A content particle.
            if at(bytes, pos) == b'(' {
                let inside = skip_spaces(bytes, pos + 1);
                pos = self.content_group(inp, inside, depth + 1)?;
            } else {
                let name_end = scan_name(bytes, pos);
                if name_end == pos {
                    return self.fail(inp, pos, "ContentDecl : Name or '(' expected");
                }
                pos = name_end;
            }
            if matches!(at(bytes, pos), b'?' | b'*' | b'+') {
                pos += 1;
            }

            pos = skip_spaces(bytes, pos);
            let byte = at(bytes, pos);
            if byte == b')' {
                return Ok(pos + 1);
            }
            if byte != b',' && byte != b'|' {
                return self.fail(inp, pos, "ContentDecl : ',' '|' or ')' expected");
            }
            if separator == 0 {
                separator = byte;
            } else if separator != byte {
                let message = format!("xmlParseElementChildrenContentDecl : '{}' expected", separator as char);
                return self.fail(inp, pos, message);
            }
            pos = skip_spaces(bytes, pos + 1);
        }
    }

    /// AttlistDecl ::= '<!ATTLIST' S Name AttDef* S? '>'
    /// AttDef ::= S Name S AttType S DefaultDecl
    fn attlist_declaration(&mut self, inp: In, start: usize) -> R<usize> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        let mut pos = self.required_spaces(inp, start + 9, "Space required after '<!ATTLIST'")?;
        let element_end = scan_name(bytes, pos);
        if element_end == pos {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, "ATTLIST: no name for Element");
        }
        let element = self.intern_name(inp, pos, element_end);
        pos = element_end;

        loop {
            let after_spaces = skip_spaces(bytes, pos);
            if at(bytes, after_spaces) == b'>' {
                return Ok(after_spaces + 1);
            }
            if after_spaces == pos {
                return self.fail(inp, pos, "Space required after the attribute default value");
            }
            let name_end = scan_name(bytes, after_spaces);
            if name_end == after_spaces {
                return self.fail(inp, after_spaces, "ATTLIST: no name for Attribute");
            }
            let name = self.intern_name(inp, after_spaces, name_end);
            pos = self.required_spaces(inp, name_end, "Space required after the attribute name")?;

            let (tokenized, next) = self.attribute_type(inp, pos)?;
            pos = self.required_spaces(inp, next, "Space required after the attribute type")?;

            // DefaultDecl ::= '#REQUIRED' | '#IMPLIED' | (('#FIXED' S)? AttValue)
            let rest = &bytes[pos..];
            let mut default = None;
            if rest.starts_with(b"#REQUIRED") {
                pos += 9;
            } else if rest.starts_with(b"#IMPLIED") {
                pos += 8;
            } else {
                if rest.starts_with(b"#FIXED") {
                    pos = self.required_spaces(inp, pos + 6, "Space required after '#FIXED'")?;
                }
                let quote = at(bytes, pos);
                if quote != b'"' && quote != b'\'' {
                    return self.fail(inp, pos, "Attribute default value declaration error");
                }
                let (offset, length, next) = self.attribute_value(inp, pos, tokenized)?;
                default = Some((offset, length));
                pos = next;
            }

            // The first definition of an attribute is the one that counts.
            let mut element_flags = 0;
            if default.is_some() {
                element_flags |= flag::HAS_DEFAULTS;
            }
            if tokenized {
                element_flags |= flag::HAS_TOKENIZED;
            }
            self.names.get_mut(element).flags |= element_flags;
            let dtd = self.dtd_mut();
            if let std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Vacant(entry) = dtd.defined_attributes.entry((element, name)) {
                entry.insert(tokenized);
                // Only a definition with a default is ever looked at again, and an element can have a great many
                // without one.
                if let Some(default) = default {
                    Rc::make_mut(dtd.attlists.entry(element).or_default()).push(AttributeDefinition { name, default });
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// AttType ::= StringType | TokenizedType | EnumeratedType
    ///
    /// Returns whether the type is anything other than CDATA, and where it ends.
    fn attribute_type(&mut self, inp: In, pos: usize) -> R<(bool, usize)> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        let rest = &bytes[pos..];
        if rest.starts_with(b"CDATA") {
            return Ok((false, pos + 5));
        }
        // The longer of two keywords that start the same has to be tried first.
        for keyword in [
            &b"IDREFS"[..],
            b"IDREF",
            b"ID",
            b"ENTITY",
            b"ENTITIES",
            b"NMTOKENS",
            b"NMTOKEN",
        ] {
            if rest.starts_with(keyword) {
                return Ok((true, pos + keyword.len()));
            }
        }

        // EnumeratedType ::= NotationType | Enumeration
        // NotationType ::= 'NOTATION' S '(' S? Name (S? '|' S? Name)* S? ')'
        // Enumeration ::= '(' S? Nmtoken (S? '|' S? Nmtoken)* S? ')'
        let mut pos = pos;
        let is_notation = rest.starts_with(b"NOTATION");
        if is_notation {
            pos = self.required_spaces(inp, pos + 8, "Space required after 'NOTATION'")?;
        }
        if at(bytes, pos) != b'(' {
            let message = if is_notation {
                "'(' required to start 'NOTATION'"
            } else {
                "Invalid attribute type"
            };
            return self.fail(inp, pos, message);
        }
        pos += 1;
        loop {
            pos = skip_spaces(bytes, pos);
            let token_end = if is_notation {
                scan_name(bytes, pos)
            } else {
                scan_nmtoken(bytes, pos)
            };
            if token_end == pos {
                let message = if is_notation {
                    "Name expected in NOTATION declaration"
                } else {
                    "NmToken expected in ATTLIST enumeration"
                };
                return self.fail(inp, pos, message);
            }
            pos = skip_spaces(bytes, token_end);
            match at(bytes, pos) {
                b')' => return Ok((true, pos + 1)),
                b'|' => pos += 1,
                _ => {
                    let message = if is_notation {
                        "')' required to finish NOTATION declaration"
                    } else {
                        "')' required to finish ATTLIST enumeration"
                    };
                    return self.fail(inp, pos, message);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// EntityDecl ::= '<!ENTITY' S Name S EntityDef S? '>' | '<!ENTITY' S '%' S Name S PEDef S? '>'
    /// EntityDef ::= EntityValue | (ExternalID NDataDecl?)
    /// PEDef ::= EntityValue | ExternalID
    fn entity_declaration(&mut self, inp: In, start: usize) -> R<usize> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        let mut pos = self.required_spaces(inp, start + 8, "Space required after '<!ENTITY'")?;
        let is_parameter = at(bytes, pos) == b'%';
        if is_parameter {
            pos = self.required_spaces(inp, pos + 1, "Space required after '%'")?;
        }
        let name_end = scan_name(bytes, pos);
        if name_end == pos {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, "xmlParseEntityDecl: no name");
        }
        let name_bytes = &bytes[pos..name_end];
        if name_bytes.contains(&b':') {
            let message = format!("colons are forbidden from entities names '{}'", lossy(name_bytes));
            self.namespace_error(inp, pos, message);
        }
        let name = self.intern_name(inp, pos, name_end);
        pos = self.required_spaces(inp, name_end, "Space required after the entity name")?;

        let entity;
        let quote = at(bytes, pos);
        if quote == b'"' || quote == b'\'' {
            let (text, next) = self.entity_value(inp, pos)?;
            entity = Entity {
                kind: EntityKind::Internal,
                text,
                expanding: false,
            };
            pos = next;
        } else {
            let (external_id, next) = self.external_id(inp, pos, true)?;
            let Some((system_start, system_end)) = external_id.system else {
                return self.fail(inp, pos, "Entity value required");
            };
            if bytes[system_start..system_end].contains(&b'#') {
                return self.fail(inp, system_start, "Fragment not allowed");
            }
            pos = next;
            let mut entity_kind = EntityKind::External;
            if !is_parameter {
                let after_spaces = skip_spaces(bytes, pos);
                if bytes[after_spaces..].starts_with(b"NDATA") {
                    if after_spaces == pos {
                        return self.fail(inp, pos, "Space required before 'NDATA'");
                    }
                    pos = self.required_spaces(inp, after_spaces + 5, "Space required after 'NDATA'")?;
                    let notation_end = scan_name(bytes, pos);
                    if notation_end == pos {
                        return self.fail(inp, pos, "xmlParseEntityDecl: no notation name");
                    }
                    pos = notation_end;
                    entity_kind = EntityKind::Unparsed;
                }
            }
            entity = Entity {
                kind: entity_kind,
                text: Rc::from(&b""[..]),
                expanding: false,
            };
        }

        let message = format!("xmlParseEntityDecl: entity {} not terminated", lossy(name_bytes));
        pos = self.end_of_declaration(inp, pos, &message)?;

        // The first declaration of an entity is the one that counts. The five predefined entities are what they are.
        let is_predefined = matches!(name_bytes, b"lt" | b"gt" | b"amp" | b"apos" | b"quot");
        let dtd = self.dtd_mut();
        if is_parameter {
            dtd.parameter.entry(name).or_insert(entity);
        } else if !is_predefined {
            dtd.general.entry(name).or_insert(entity);
        }
        Ok(pos)
    }

    /// EntityValue ::= '"' ([^%&"] | PEReference | Reference)* '"' | "'" ([^%&'] | PEReference | Reference)* "'"
    ///
    /// Returns the entity's replacement text: the literal with its character references replaced. References to
    /// general entities stay as they are, to be followed when the entity is used.
    ///
    /// Line ends stay as they are too, and are normalized where the entity is used, as they are in libxml2. So a CR
    /// that is written as a character reference becomes a line end in content like one that is written out, and a
    /// CR LF pair is two spaces in an attribute value.
    fn entity_value(&mut self, inp: In, start: usize) -> R<(Rc<[u8]>, usize)> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        let quote = bytes[start];
        let mut pos = start + 1;
        let mut text = Vec::new();
        loop {
            if pos >= bytes.len() {
                return self.fail(inp, start, "EntityValue: \" expected");
            }
            let byte = bytes[pos];
            if byte == quote {
                break;
            }
            match byte {
                b'&' => {
                    if at(bytes, pos + 1) == b'#' {
                        let (c, next) = self.character_reference(inp, pos)?;
                        chars::encode_utf8(c, &mut text);
                        pos = next;
                    } else {
                        let name_end = scan_name(bytes, pos + 1);
                        if name_end == pos + 1 || at(bytes, name_end) != b';' {
                            return self.fail(inp, pos, "EntityValue: '&' forbidden except for entities references");
                        }
                        text.extend_from_slice(&bytes[pos..=name_end]);
                        pos = name_end + 1;
                    }
                }
                // In the internal subset a parameter entity can only be referenced between declarations.
                b'%' => return self.fail(inp, pos, "PEReferences forbidden in internal subset"),
                _ if byte >= 0x80 => {
                    let length = self.check_non_ascii(inp, pos)?;
                    text.extend_from_slice(&bytes[pos..pos + length]);
                    pos += length;
                }
                _ if CLASS[byte as usize] & chars::INVALID != 0 => {
                    return self.fail(inp, pos, "invalid character in entity value");
                }
                _ => {
                    text.push(byte);
                    pos += 1;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok((Rc::from(text), pos + 1))
    }

    /// NotationDecl ::= '<!NOTATION' S Name S (ExternalID | PublicID) S? '>'
    fn notation_declaration(&mut self, inp: In, start: usize) -> R<usize> {
        let bytes = inp.bytes;
        let mut pos = self.required_spaces(inp, start + 10, "Space required after '<!NOTATION'")?;
        let name_end = scan_name(bytes, pos);
        if name_end == pos {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, "NOTATION: Name expected here");
        }
        if bytes[pos..name_end].contains(&b':') {
            let message = format!(
                "colons are forbidden from notation names '{}'",
                lossy(&bytes[pos..name_end])
            );
            self.namespace_error(inp, pos, message);
        }
        pos = self.required_spaces(inp, name_end, "Space required after the NOTATION name'")?;
        let (external_id, next) = self.external_id(inp, pos, false)?;
        if external_id.public.is_none() && external_id.system.is_none() {
            return self.fail(inp, pos, "NOTATION: external identifier expected");
        }
        self.end_of_declaration(inp, next, "'>' required to close NOTATION declaration")
    }
}

//! A tape as text, one event to a line, for tests and for comparing against another parser.

use std::fmt::Write;

use crate::Document;
use crate::tape::NONE;
use crate::tape::kind;

fn escape(bytes: &[u8], out: &mut String) {
    for &byte in bytes {
        match byte {
            b'\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            b'\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            b'\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            b'\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            b'"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            0x20..=0x7E => out.push(byte as char),
            _ => {
                let _ = write!(out, "\\x{byte:02X}");
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Writes the events of `document`. Adjacent text is joined, since where a parser splits a run of text is up to it.
/// With `namespaces`, each element and attribute name is followed by its namespace name in braces.
pub fn dump(document: &Document, source: &[u8], namespaces: bool) -> String {
    let storage = document.storage(source);
    let tape = &document.tape;
    let mut out = String::new();
    let name = |id: u32, out: &mut String| escape(document.names.bytes(id, storage), out);
    let namespace = |id: u32, out: &mut String| {
        if namespaces && id != NONE {
            out.push('{');
            escape(document.names.bytes(id, storage), out);
            out.push('}');
        }
    };

    let mut errors = document.errors.iter().peekable();
    let mut in_text = false;
    let mut index = 0;
    loop {
        while let Some(error) = errors.peek() {
            if error.row as usize > index {
                break;
            }
            if in_text {
                out.push('\n');
                in_text = false;
            }
            let _ = writeln!(out, "{} {}", if error.fatal { "FATAL" } else { "ERROR" }, error.message);
            errors.next();
        }
        if index >= tape.len() {
            break;
        }
        let (row_kind, a, b) = tape.row(index);
        let is_text = row_kind & kind::MASK == kind::TEXT;
        if in_text && !is_text {
            out.push('\n');
            in_text = false;
        }
        match row_kind & kind::MASK {
            kind::START => {
                out.push_str("START ");
                name(a, &mut out);
                namespace(b, &mut out);
                index += 1;
                while index < tape.len() && tape.row(index).0 & kind::MASK == kind::ATTR {
                    let (_, attribute, attribute_namespace) = tape.row(index);
                    let (_, offset, length) = tape.row(index + 1);
                    out.push(' ');
                    name(attribute, &mut out);
                    namespace(attribute_namespace, &mut out);
                    out.push_str("=\"");
                    escape(storage.get(offset, length), &mut out);
                    out.push('"');
                    index += 2;
                }
                out.push('\n');
                continue;
            }
            kind::END => {
                out.push_str("END ");
                name(a, &mut out);
                out.push('\n');
            }
            kind::TEXT => {
                if !in_text {
                    out.push_str("TEXT ");
                    in_text = true;
                }
                escape(storage.get(a, b), &mut out);
            }
            kind::CDATA => {
                out.push_str("CDATA ");
                escape(storage.get(a, b), &mut out);
                out.push('\n');
            }
            kind::COMMENT => {
                out.push_str("COMMENT ");
                escape(storage.get(a, b), &mut out);
                out.push('\n');
            }
            kind::PI => {
                let (_, offset, length) = tape.row(index + 1);
                out.push_str("PI ");
                name(a, &mut out);
                out.push(' ');
                escape(storage.get(offset, length), &mut out);
                out.push('\n');
                index += 1;
            }
            kind::DOCTYPE => {
                out.push_str("DOCTYPE ");
                name(a, &mut out);
                for id in [index + 1, index + 2] {
                    let (value_kind, offset, length) = tape.row(id);
                    if value_kind & kind::ABSENT != 0 {
                        out.push_str(" -");
                    } else {
                        out.push_str(" \"");
                        escape(storage.get(offset, length), &mut out);
                        out.push('"');
                    }
                }
                out.push('\n');
                index += 2;
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        index += 1;
    }
    out
}

//! The C interface. `rust_xml_parse` returns an opaque document, `rust_xml_document_view` hands out pointers to its
//! columns, and `rust_xml_document_free` releases it. The view is plain data: reading a document from C++ is loops
//! over arrays, with no call back into Rust per row.

use std::ffi::c_void;

use crate::Document;
use crate::Options;
use crate::rust_panic::abort_on_panic;

/// What the low bits of a row's kind byte say. See `tape`.
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum XmlRowKind {
    Start = 1,
    Attribute = 2,
    Value = 3,
    End = 4,
    Text = 5,
    Cdata = 6,
    Comment = 7,
    ProcessingInstruction = 8,
    Doctype = 9,
}

/// The bits of a kind byte that hold the kind.

    Mask = 0x0F,
}

/// The flags in the kind byte of an attribute row.

#[repr(u8)]
pub enum XmlValueFlag {
    /// On an id of a doctype: there is no such id, as opposed to an empty one.
    Absent = 0x80,
}

/// Resolves the name of an HTML character entity. Writes what it stands for, as UTF-8, to `out`, which has room for
/// `capacity` bytes, and returns how many bytes that was, or a negative number if there is no such entity.
/// Null for no resolver.
pub type XmlHtmlEntityResolver = Option<
    unsafe extern "C" fn(
        context: *mut c_void,
        name: *const u8,
        name_length: usize,
        out: *mut u8,
        capacity: usize,
    ) -> isize,
>;

#[repr(C)]
pub struct XmlParseOptions {
    pub preserve_comments: bool,
    pub preserve_cdata: bool,
    /// Used for references to undeclared entities in a document whose doctype has one of the XHTML public ids.
    pub resolve_html_entity: XmlHtmlEntityResolver,
    pub resolver_context: *mut c_void,
}

/// Where a name is, in the address space string operands point into: the source, then the arena.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct XmlName {
    pub offset: u32,
    pub length: u32,
}

#[repr(C)]
pub struct XmlError {
    pub message: *const u8,
    pub message_length: usize,
    pub offset: u32,
    pub line: u32,
    pub column: u32,
    /// The row the error comes before.
    pub row: u32,
    pub fatal: bool,
}

/// Pointers into a document. They are good until the document is freed.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct XmlDocumentView {
    pub kinds: *const u8,
    pub a: *const u32,
    pub b: *const u32,
    pub row_count: usize,
    pub arena: *const u8,
    pub arena_length: usize,
    pub names: *const XmlName,
    pub name_count: usize,
    pub errors: *const XmlError,
    pub error_count: usize,
    pub version_1_0: bool,
    /// Whether the parser got past the XML declaration. If it didn't, the document never started.
    pub started: bool,
}

pub struct XmlDocument {
    document: Document,
    names: Vec<XmlName>,
    errors: Vec<XmlError>,
}

/// Parses the `length` bytes of UTF-8 at `source` as a whole document. Never returns null: a document that isn't
/// well-formed is a document with errors in it. The result has to be freed with `rust_xml_document_free`.
///
/// # Safety
/// `source` must point to `length` readable bytes, or `length` must be zero. `options` must be null or point to a
/// valid `XmlParseOptions`. The resolver, if there is one, must be safe to call with `resolver_context` for as long
/// as this call lasts.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_xml_parse(
    source: *const u8,
    length: usize,
    options: *const XmlParseOptions,
) -> *mut XmlDocument {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        // SAFETY: The caller promises `length` readable bytes at `source`.
        let source: &[u8] = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(source, length) };
        // SAFETY: The caller promises `options` is null or valid.
        let options = unsafe { options.as_ref() };

        let resolver = options.and_then(|options| {
            let resolve = options.resolve_html_entity?;
            let context = options.resolver_context;
            Some(move |name: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>| -> bool {
                let mut buffer = [0u8; 64];
                // SAFETY: The caller promises the resolver can be called with its context. It is given a buffer and
                // the buffer's true size.
                let written = unsafe { resolve(context, name.as_ptr(), name.len(), buffer.as_mut_ptr(), buffer.len()) };
                match usize::try_from(written) {
                    Ok(written) if written <= buffer.len() => {
                        out.extend_from_slice(&buffer[..written]);
                        true
                    }
                    _ => false,
                }
            })
        });
        let document = crate::parse(
            source,
            Options {
                preserve_comments: options.is_some_and(|options| options.preserve_comments),
                preserve_cdata: options.is_none_or(|options| options.preserve_cdata),
                resolve_html_entity: resolver.as_ref().map(|resolver| resolver as crate::HtmlEntityResolver),
            },
        );

        let names = document
            .names
            .entries()
            .iter()
            .map(|name| XmlName {
                offset: name.offset,
                length: name.length,
            })
            .collect();
        let errors = document
            .errors
            .iter()
            .map(|error| XmlError {
                // The message is owned by `document`, which lives exactly as long as this pointer to it.
                message: error.message.as_ptr(),
                message_length: error.message.len(),
                offset: error.offset,
                line: error.line,
                column: error.column,
                row: error.row,
                fatal: error.fatal,
            })
            .collect();
        Box::into_raw(Box::new(XmlDocument {
            document,
            names,
            errors,
        }))
    })
}

/// # Safety
/// `document` must be a document from `rust_xml_parse` that hasn't been freed.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_xml_document_view(document: *const XmlDocument) -> XmlDocumentView {
    // SAFETY: The caller promises a live document.
    let document = unsafe { &*document };
    let tape = &document.document.tape;
    XmlDocumentView {
        kinds: tape.kinds().as_ptr(),
        a: tape.a().as_ptr(),
        b: tape.b().as_ptr(),
        row_count: tape.len(),
        arena: document.document.arena.as_ptr(),
        arena_length: document.document.arena.len(),
        names: document.names.as_ptr(),
        name_count: document.names.len(),
        errors: document.errors.as_ptr(),
        error_count: document.errors.len(),
        version_1_0: document.document.version_1_0,
        started: document.document.started,
    }
}

/// # Safety
/// `document` must be null or a document from `rust_xml_parse` that hasn't been freed.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_xml_document_free(document: *mut XmlDocument) {
    if !document.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: The caller promises the pointer came from `rust_xml_parse`, where it was a Box, and that this is
        // the only time it is freed.
        drop(unsafe { Box::from_raw(document) });
    }
}

/// Compiles an XPath 1.0 expression. Returns null if it isn't one.
///

/// `source` must point to `length` readable bytes.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_xpath_compile(source: *const u8, length: usize) -> *mut XPathProgram {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        // SAFETY: The caller promises `length` readable bytes at `source`.
        let source: &[u8] = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(source, length) };
        match crate::xpath::compile(source) {
            Ok(program) => Box::into_raw(Box::new(XPathProgram { program })),
            Err(_) => std::ptr::null_mut(),
        }
    })
}

    let program = unsafe { &(*program).program };
    XPathProgramView {
        kinds: program.kinds.as_ptr(),
        a: program.a.as_ptr(),
        b: program.b.as_ptr(),
        c: program.c.as_ptr(),
        node_count: program.kinds.len(),
        steps: program.steps.as_ptr(),
        step_count: program.steps.len(),
        lists: program.lists.as_ptr(),
        list_count: program.lists.len(),
        numbers: program.numbers.as_ptr(),
        number_count: program.numbers.len(),
        root: program.root,
    }
}

//! The table of every distinct name in a document: element and attribute names, prefixes, namespace names.
//!
//! A name is interned the first time it is seen and is a 32-bit id from then on, so that comparing two names, finding
//! a prefix's namespace or checking a tag for a repeated attribute never looks at the name's bytes again. An entry
//! doesn't own its bytes: it points at the first place the name was written, in the source or in the arena.

use std::hash::BuildHasher;
use std::hash::RandomState;
use std::sync::OnceLock;

use crate::chars;
use crate::tape::NONE;

pub mod flag {
    /// The name is "xmlns".
    pub const IS_XMLNS: u8 = 1 << 0;
    /// The name is a QName with the prefix "xmlns".
    pub const PREFIX_XMLNS: u8 = 1 << 1;
    /// The name is a QName with the prefix "xml".
    pub const PREFIX_XML: u8 = 1 << 2;
    /// The name is a QName with a prefix.
    pub const HAS_PREFIX: u8 = 1 << 3;
    /// The name has a colon but isn't a QName: more than one colon, or nothing or no NCName on one side of it.
    pub const NOT_A_QNAME: u8 = 1 << 4;
    /// As an element name: the DTD declares an attribute with a default value for it.
    pub const HAS_DEFAULTS: u8 = 1 << 5;
    /// The flags above have been worked out.
    pub const ANALYZED: u8 = 1 << 6;
    /// As an element name: the DTD declares an attribute of a type other than CDATA for it.
    pub const HAS_TOKENIZED: u8 = 1 << 7;

    /// The flags that are about a name as an element name, and say nothing when it is an attribute's.
    pub const ELEMENT_ONLY: u8 = HAS_DEFAULTS | HAS_TOKENIZED;
    /// The flags that send a start tag through namespace processing.
    pub const NEEDS_NAMESPACE_PROCESSING: u8 = IS_XMLNS | PREFIX_XMLNS | HAS_PREFIX | NOT_A_QNAME | HAS_DEFAULTS;
}

/// The first sixteen bytes of a name as two little-endian words, with zeros past its end.
///
/// OPTIMIZATION: Nearly every name is at most sixteen bytes long, and then its key is all of it. Hashing a name and
/// comparing it to an entry are a few operations on two registers, with no loop over bytes, no call to memcmp, and
/// no trip to wherever in the document the entry's bytes are.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Key(u64, u64);

impl Key {
    /// The key of `bytes[start..start + length]`.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn at(bytes: &[u8], start: usize, length: usize) -> Key {
        if start + 16 <= bytes.len() {
            let w0 = u64::from_le_bytes(bytes[start..start + 8].try_into().unwrap_or([0; 8]));
            let w1 = u64::from_le_bytes(bytes[start + 8..start + 16].try_into().unwrap_or([0; 8]));
            if length >= 16 {
                Key(w0, w1)
            } else if length >= 8 {
                Key(w0, w1 & !(u64::MAX << ((length - 8) * 8)))
            } else {
                Key(w0 & !(u64::MAX << (length * 8)), 0)
            }
        } else {
            Key::near_end(&bytes[start..start + length])
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn of(bytes: &[u8]) -> Key {
        Key::at(bytes, 0, bytes.len())
    }

    /// For a name with fewer than sixteen bytes of input from its start on.
    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    fn near_end(name: &[u8]) -> Key {
        let mut buffer = [0u8; 16];
        let length = name.len().min(16);
        buffer[..length].copy_from_slice(&name[..length]);
        let w0 = u64::from_le_bytes(buffer[..8].try_into().unwrap_or([0; 8]));
        let w1 = u64::from_le_bytes(buffer[8..].try_into().unwrap_or([0; 8]));
        Key(w0, w1)
    }
}

/// Hashes a name id for a map keyed by one.
///
/// OPTIMIZATION: Ids are small integers the parser hands out itself, in order, so there is nothing for a keyed hash
/// to defend against, and one multiplication spreads them well enough.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct IdHasher(u64);

impl std::hash::Hasher for IdHasher {
    fn finish(&self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }

    fn write(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        for &byte in bytes {
            self.0 = (self.0 ^ byte as u64).wrapping_mul(K0);
        }
    }

    fn write_u32(&mut self, id: u32) {
        self.0 = (id as u64 + 1).wrapping_mul(K0).rotate_left(32);
    }
}

pub type IdMap<V> = std::collections::HashMap<u32, V, std::hash::BuildHasherDefault<IdHasher>>;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Name {
    key: Key,
    hash: u32,
    pub length: u32,
    pub offset: u32,
    /// The id of the prefix, or NONE.
    pub prefix: u32,
    /// The id of the local part. For a name without a prefix, the name itself.
    pub local: u32,
    /// As a prefix: the index of its innermost binding in scope, or NONE.
    pub binding: u32,
    /// The start tag the name was last seen as an attribute of.
    pub stamp: u32,
    pub flags: u8,
}

pub struct Names {
    entries: Vec<Name>,
    /// Open addressing with linear probing. A slot holds an id plus one, or zero when empty.
    table: Vec<u32>,
    seed: u64,
}

/// The two byte ranges a name's offset can point into.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Storage<'a> {
    pub source: &'a [u8],
    pub arena: &'a [u8],
}

impl<'a> Storage<'a> {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn new(source: &'a [u8], arena: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
        Storage { source, arena }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn get(self, offset: u32, length: u32) -> &'a [u8] {
        let offset = offset as usize;
        let length = length as usize;
        if offset < self.source.len() {
            &self.source[offset..offset + length]
        } else {
            let offset = offset - self.source.len();
            &self.arena[offset..offset + length]
        }
    }
}

fn process_seed() -> u64 {
    // The seed only has to be unpredictable to whoever wrote the document, so that a document can't be built to make
    // every name collide.
    static SEED: OnceLock<u64> = OnceLock::new();
    *SEED.get_or_init(|| RandomState::new().hash_one(0x584D4Cu32) | 1)
}

const K0: u64 = 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15;
const K1: u64 = 0xD6E8_FEB8_6659_FD93;

#[inline(always)]
fn hash_name(seed: u64, key: Key, name: &[u8]) -> u32 {
    let mut hash = (key.0 ^ seed).wrapping_mul(K0);
    hash = (hash.rotate_left(29) ^ key.1 ^ name.len() as u64).wrapping_mul(K1);
    if name.len() > 16 {
        hash = hash_tail(hash, &name[16..]);
    }
    (hash >> 32) as u32 ^ hash as u32
}

#[inline(never)]
fn hash_tail(mut hash: u64, tail: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    for chunk in tail.chunks(8) {
        let mut word = 0u64;
        for (index, &byte) in chunk.iter().enumerate() {
            word |= (byte as u64) << (index * 8);
        }
        hash = (hash.rotate_left(29) ^ word).wrapping_mul(K1);
    }
    hash
}

impl Default for Names {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl Names {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Names {
            entries: Vec::with_capacity(64),
            table: vec![0; 128],
            seed: process_seed(),
        }
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.entries.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.entries.is_empty()
    }

    pub fn entries(&self) -> &[Name] {
        &self.entries
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn get(&self, id: u32) -> &Name {
        &self.entries[id as usize]
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn get_mut(&mut self, id: u32) -> &mut Name {
        &mut self.entries[id as usize]
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn bytes<'a>(&self, id: u32, storage: Storage<'a>) -> &'a [u8] {
        let name = &self.entries[id as usize];
        storage.get(name.offset, name.length)
    }

    /// Whether the name `id` is what is written at `bytes[start..]`. The caller checks what comes after it.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn is_at(&self, id: u32, bytes: &[u8], start: usize, storage: Storage) -> bool {
        let name = &self.entries[id as usize];
        let length = name.length as usize;
        if start + length > bytes.len() || Key::at(bytes, start, length) != name.key {
            return false;
        }
        length <= 16 || storage.get(name.offset, name.length)[16..] == bytes[start + 16..start + length]
    }

    /// Looks `name` up. Returns its id, or the slot it belongs in.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn lookup(&self, key: Key, hash: u32, name: &[u8], storage: Storage) -> Result<u32, usize> {
        let mask = self.table.len() - 1;
        let mut slot = hash as usize & mask;
        loop {
            let entry = self.table[slot];
            if entry == 0 {
                return Err(slot);
            }
            let candidate = &self.entries[entry as usize - 1];
            if candidate.hash == hash
                && candidate.key == key
                && candidate.length as usize == name.len()
                && (name.len() <= 16 || storage.get(candidate.offset, candidate.length)[16..] == name[16..])
            {
                return Ok(entry - 1);
            }
            slot = (slot + 1) & mask;
        }
    }

    /// Returns the id of `name` if it is in the table.
    pub fn find(&self, name: &[u8], storage: Storage) -> Option<u32> {
        let key = Key::of(name);
        self.lookup(key, hash_name(self.seed, key, name), name, storage).ok()
    }

    /// Returns the id of `name`, adding it to the table if it is new. `offset` is where `name` is in `storage`: an
    /// entry doesn't copy its bytes.
    pub fn intern(&mut self, name: &[u8], offset: u32, storage: Storage) -> u32 {
        let key = Key::of(name);
        let hash = hash_name(self.seed, key, name);
        match self.lookup(key, hash, name, storage) {
            Ok(id) => id,
            Err(slot) => self.insert(slot, key, hash, name.len() as u32, offset),
        }
    }

    /// `intern` for the name at `source[start..end]`, where `source` is the document itself.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn intern_in_source(&mut self, source: &[u8], start: usize, end: usize, arena: &[u8]) -> u32 {
        let name = &source[start..end];
        let key = Key::at(source, start, end - start);
        let hash = hash_name(self.seed, key, name);
        match self.lookup(key, hash, name, Storage { source, arena }) {
            Ok(id) => id,
            Err(slot) => self.insert(slot, key, hash, name.len() as u32, start as u32),
        }
    }

    #[inline(never)]
    fn insert(&mut self, slot: usize, key: Key, hash: u32, length: u32, offset: u32) -> u32 {
        let id = self.entries.len() as u32;
        self.entries.push(Name {
            key,
            hash,
            length,
            offset,
            prefix: NONE,
            local: id,
            binding: NONE,
            stamp: 0,
            flags: 0,
        });
        self.table[slot] = id + 1;
        if self.entries.len() * 2 > self.table.len() {
            self.grow();
        }
        id
    }

    fn grow(&mut self) {
        let size = self.table.len() * 2;
        let mask = size - 1;
        let mut table = vec![0u32; size];
        for (index, name) in self.entries.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut slot = name.hash as usize & mask;
            while table[slot] != 0 {
                slot = (slot + 1) & mask;
            }
            table[slot] = index as u32 + 1;
        }
        self.table = table;
    }

    /// Works out how the name `id` splits into a prefix and a local part, interning both, if that hasn't been done.
    /// Returns the name's flags.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn analyze(&mut self, id: u32, storage: Storage) -> u8 {
        let flags = self.entries[id as usize].flags;
        if flags & flag::ANALYZED != 0 {
            return flags;
        }
        self.analyze_slow(id, storage)
    }

    #[inline(never)]
    fn analyze_slow(&mut self, id: u32, storage: Storage) -> u8 {
        let entry = self.entries[id as usize];
        let bytes = storage.get(entry.offset, entry.length);
        let mut flags = entry.flags | flag::ANALYZED;
        if let Some(colon) = bytes.iter().position(|&byte| byte == b':') {
            let (prefix, local) = (&bytes[..colon], &bytes[colon + 1..]);
            if chars::is_name(prefix, false) && chars::is_name(local, false) {
                let prefix_id = self.intern(prefix, entry.offset, storage);
                let local_id = self.intern(local, entry.offset + colon as u32 + 1, storage);
                flags |= flag::HAS_PREFIX;
                if prefix == b"xmlns" {
                    flags |= flag::PREFIX_XMLNS;
                } else if prefix == b"xml" {
                    flags |= flag::PREFIX_XML;
                }
                let entry = &mut self.entries[id as usize];
                entry.prefix = prefix_id;
                entry.local = local_id;
            } else {
                flags |= flag::NOT_A_QNAME;
            }
        } else if bytes == b"xmlns" {
            flags |= flag::IS_XMLNS;
        }
        self.entries[id as usize].flags = flags;
        flags
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn keys() {
        let text = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789";
        for start in 0..text.len() {
            for length in 0..=(text.len() - start).min(20) {
                let name = &text[start..start + length];
                // A key is the same wherever the name is read from, and however much input follows it.
                assert!(Key::at(text, start, length) == Key::of(name), "{start} {length}");
                assert!(Key::at(text, start, length) == Key::near_end(name), "{start} {length}");
            }
        }
        assert!(Key::of(b"abc") != Key::of(b"abd"));
        assert!(Key::of(b"abcdefghi") != Key::of(b"abcdefghj"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn interning() {
        let source = b"short a-name-longer-than-sixteen-bytes a-name-longer-than-sixteen-bytez short";
        let storage = Storage { source, arena: &[] };
        let mut names = Names::new();
        let short = names.intern(&source[0..5], 0, storage);
        let long = names.intern(&source[6..38], 6, storage);
        let other = names.intern(&source[39..71], 39, storage);
        assert_ne!(long, other);
        assert_eq!(names.intern_in_source(source, 72, 77, &[]), short);
        assert_eq!(names.find(b"a-name-longer-than-sixteen-bytes", storage), Some(long));
        assert_eq!(names.find(b"a-name-longer-than-sixteen-bytex", storage), None);
        assert!(names.is_at(long, source, 6, storage));
        assert!(!names.is_at(long, source, 39, storage));
        assert!(names.is_at(short, source, 72, storage));
        // Enough names to make the table grow several times.
        let mut arena = Vec::new();
        let mut ranges = Vec::new();
        for index in 0..1000u32 {
            let name = format!("name-number-{index}");
            ranges.push((arena.len(), name.len()));
            arena.extend_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
        }
        let storage = Storage { source, arena: &arena };
        let base = source.len();
        let ids: Vec<u32> = ranges
            .iter()
            .map(|&(start, length)| names.intern(&arena[start..start + length], (base + start) as u32, storage))
            .collect();
        for (&(start, length), &id) in ranges.iter().zip(&ids) {
            assert_eq!(names.find(&arena[start..start + length], storage), Some(id));
        }
        assert_eq!(names.find(b"short", storage), Some(short));
    }
}
