//! The loops that skip over runs of plain characters: the text between two tags, the inside of an attribute value, a
//! comment. Each returns the position of the first byte the caller has to look at, or the length of the input.
//!
//! OPTIMIZATION: Most of a document's bytes are in such runs, so these loops look at a block of bytes at a time. A
//! byte needs the caller's attention when it is one of up to three delimiters, a C0 control, or the start of a
//! non-ASCII sequence. The last two share one signed comparison: as an i8, a byte at or above 0x80 is negative, so
//! "less than 0x20" covers both.

/// Which C0 controls end a run, besides the ones that are never allowed.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Controls {
    /// Tab and LF are plain. CR ends the run: it has to be normalized.
    StopAtCr,
    /// Tab, LF and CR all end the run: in an attribute value each becomes a space.
    StopAtAll,
}

#[inline(always)]
fn needs_attention(byte: u8, d0: u8, d1: u8, d2: u8, controls: Controls) -> bool {
    if byte == d0 || byte == d1 || byte == d2 {
        return true;
    }
    if (byte as i8) < 0x20 {
        return controls == Controls::StopAtAll || (byte != b'\t' && byte != b'\n');
    }
    false
}

#[inline(always)]
fn scalar(bytes: &[u8], mut pos: usize, d0: u8, d1: u8, d2: u8, controls: Controls) -> usize {
    while pos < bytes.len() && !needs_attention(bytes[pos], d0, d1, d2, controls) {
        pos += 1;
    }
    pos
}

/// The first position at or after `pos` whose byte is `d0`, `d1`, `d2`, a control selected by `controls`, or at or
/// above 0x80. Pass the same delimiter more than once to look for fewer than three.
#[inline(always)]
pub fn find(bytes: &[u8], pos: usize, d0: u8, d1: u8, d2: u8, controls: Controls) -> usize {
    let pos = block::find(bytes, pos, d0, d1, d2, controls);
    scalar(bytes, pos, d0, d1, d2, controls)
}

/// The reference implementation, for testing the block versions against.
#[cfg(test)]
pub fn find_scalar(bytes: &[u8], pos: usize, d0: u8, d1: u8, d2: u8, controls: Controls) -> usize {
    scalar(bytes, pos, d0, d1, d2, controls)
}

#[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", target_feature = "avx2"))]
mod block {
    use super::Controls;
    use core::arch::x86_64::*;

    const BLOCK: usize = 32;

    /// Returns the position of the first byte that needs attention if a whole block containing it could be read, or
    /// else the position of the first byte no whole block covers.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn find(bytes: &[u8], mut pos: usize, d0: u8, d1: u8, d2: u8, controls: Controls) -> usize {
        while pos + BLOCK <= bytes.len() {
            // SAFETY: The block [pos, pos + BLOCK) is inside `bytes`, and AVX2 is statically enabled.
            let mask = unsafe {
                let x = _mm256_loadu_si256(bytes.as_ptr().add(pos) as *const __m256i);
                let delimiters = _mm256_or_si256(
                    _mm256_or_si256(
                        _mm256_cmpeq_epi8(x, _mm256_set1_epi8(d0 as i8)),
                        _mm256_cmpeq_epi8(x, _mm256_set1_epi8(d1 as i8)),
                    ),
                    _mm256_cmpeq_epi8(x, _mm256_set1_epi8(d2 as i8)),
                );
                let mut low = _mm256_cmpgt_epi8(_mm256_set1_epi8(0x20), x);
                if controls == Controls::StopAtCr {
                    let plain = _mm256_or_si256(
                        _mm256_cmpeq_epi8(x, _mm256_set1_epi8(b'\t' as i8)),
                        _mm256_cmpeq_epi8(x, _mm256_set1_epi8(b'\n' as i8)),
                    );
                    low = _mm256_andnot_si256(plain, low);
                }
                _mm256_movemask_epi8(_mm256_or_si256(delimiters, low)) as u32
            };
            if mask != 0 {
                return pos + mask.trailing_zeros() as usize;
            }
            pos += BLOCK;
        }
        pos
    }
}

#[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", not(target_feature = "avx2")))]
mod block {
    use super::Controls;
    use core::arch::x86_64::*;

    const BLOCK: usize = 16;

    /// Returns the position of the first byte that needs attention if a whole block containing it could be read, or
    /// else the position of the first byte no whole block covers.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn find(bytes: &[u8], mut pos: usize, d0: u8, d1: u8, d2: u8, controls: Controls) -> usize {
        while pos + BLOCK <= bytes.len() {
            // SAFETY: The block [pos, pos + BLOCK) is inside `bytes`, and SSE2 is part of the x86_64 baseline.
            let mask = unsafe {
                let x = _mm_loadu_si128(bytes.as_ptr().add(pos) as *const __m128i);
                let delimiters = _mm_or_si128(
                    _mm_or_si128(
                        _mm_cmpeq_epi8(x, _mm_set1_epi8(d0 as i8)),
                        _mm_cmpeq_epi8(x, _mm_set1_epi8(d1 as i8)),
                    ),
                    _mm_cmpeq_epi8(x, _mm_set1_epi8(d2 as i8)),
                );
                let mut low = _mm_cmplt_epi8(x, _mm_set1_epi8(0x20));
                if controls == Controls::StopAtCr {
                    let plain = _mm_or_si128(
                        _mm_cmpeq_epi8(x, _mm_set1_epi8(b'\t' as i8)),
                        _mm_cmpeq_epi8(x, _mm_set1_epi8(b'\n' as i8)),
                    );
                    low = _mm_andnot_si128(plain, low);
                }
                _mm_movemask_epi8(_mm_or_si128(delimiters, low)) as u32
            };
            if mask != 0 {
                return pos + mask.trailing_zeros() as usize;
            }
            pos += BLOCK;
        }
        pos
    }
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
mod block {
    use super::Controls;
    use core::arch::aarch64::*;

    const BLOCK: usize = 16;

    /// Returns the position of the first byte that needs attention if a whole block containing it could be read, or
    /// else the position of the first byte no whole block covers.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn find(bytes: &[u8], mut pos: usize, d0: u8, d1: u8, d2: u8, controls: Controls) -> usize {
        while pos + BLOCK <= bytes.len() {
            // SAFETY: The block [pos, pos + BLOCK) is inside `bytes`, and NEON is part of the aarch64 baseline.
            let mask = unsafe {
                let x = vld1q_u8(bytes.as_ptr().add(pos));
                let delimiters = vorrq_u8(
                    vorrq_u8(vceqq_u8(x, vdupq_n_u8(d0)), vceqq_u8(x, vdupq_n_u8(d1))),
                    vceqq_u8(x, vdupq_n_u8(d2)),
                );
                let mut low = vcltq_s8(vreinterpretq_s8_u8(x), vdupq_n_s8(0x20));
                if controls == Controls::StopAtCr {
                    let plain = vorrq_u8(vceqq_u8(x, vdupq_n_u8(b'\t')), vceqq_u8(x, vdupq_n_u8(b'\n')));
                    low = vbicq_u8(low, plain);
                }
                // Narrowing each 16-bit lane by four bits leaves four mask bits per byte, in order.
                let any = vreinterpretq_u16_u8(vorrq_u8(delimiters, low));
                vget_lane_u64::<0>(vreinterpret_u64_u8(vshrn_n_u16::<4>(any)))
            };
            if mask != 0 {
                return pos + (mask.trailing_zeros() / 4) as usize;
            }
            pos += BLOCK;
        }
        pos
    }
}

#[cfg(not(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]
mod block {
    use super::Controls;

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn find(_bytes: &[u8], pos: usize, _d0: u8, _d1: u8, _d2: u8, _controls: Controls) -> usize {
        pos
    }
}

/// Returns where the run of ASCII name characters that starts at `pos` ends. A caller parsing a name has to look at
/// the byte there: if it is at or above 0x80 the name may go on.
#[inline(always)]
pub fn ascii_name_end(bytes: &[u8], mut pos: usize) -> usize {
    pos = name_block::ascii_name_end(bytes, pos);
    while pos < bytes.len() && crate::chars::CLASS[bytes[pos] as usize] & crate::chars::NAME != 0 {
        pos += 1;
    }
    pos
}

// OPTIMIZATION: A name is a handful of bytes, and where it ends is anyone's guess, so a loop over its bytes ends in a
// mispredicted branch nearly every time. Classifying sixteen bytes at once and counting the leading name characters
// has no such branch. The classification is two table lookups on the halves of each byte: a byte is a name
// character if the entries for its high and low nibbles share a bit.
//
// | high nibble | name characters | bit |
// |-------------|-----------------|-----|
// | 2           | - .             | 0   |
// | 3           | 0-9 :           | 1   |
// | 4, 6        | A-O, a-o        | 2   |
// | 5           | P-Z _           | 3   |
// | 7           | p-z             | 4   |
#[cfg(any(all(target_arch = "x86_64", target_feature = "ssse3"), target_arch = "aarch64"))]
const NAME_LOW_NIBBLES: [u8; 16] = [26, 30, 30, 30, 30, 30, 30, 30, 30, 30, 30, 4, 4, 5, 5, 12];
#[cfg(any(all(target_arch = "x86_64", target_feature = "ssse3"), target_arch = "aarch64"))]
const NAME_HIGH_NIBBLES: [u8; 16] = [0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 4, 16, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0];

#[cfg(all(target_arch = "x86_64", target_feature = "ssse3"))]
mod name_block {
    use super::NAME_HIGH_NIBBLES;
    use super::NAME_LOW_NIBBLES;
    use core::arch::x86_64::*;

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn ascii_name_end(bytes: &[u8], mut pos: usize) -> usize {
        while pos + 16 <= bytes.len() {
            // SAFETY: The block [pos, pos + 16) is inside `bytes`, the tables are sixteen bytes, and SSSE3 is
            // statically enabled.
            let others = unsafe {
                let x = _mm_loadu_si128(bytes.as_ptr().add(pos) as *const __m128i);
                let low_table = _mm_loadu_si128(NAME_LOW_NIBBLES.as_ptr() as *const __m128i);
                let high_table = _mm_loadu_si128(NAME_HIGH_NIBBLES.as_ptr() as *const __m128i);
                // A byte at or above 0x80 selects zero from the first table, and so is never a name character.
                let low = _mm_shuffle_epi8(low_table, x);
                let high = _mm_shuffle_epi8(high_table, _mm_and_si128(_mm_srli_epi16::<4>(x), _mm_set1_epi8(0x0F)));
                _mm_movemask_epi8(_mm_cmpeq_epi8(_mm_and_si128(low, high), _mm_setzero_si128())) as u32
            };
            if others != 0 {
                return pos + others.trailing_zeros() as usize;
            }
            pos += 16;
        }
        pos
    }
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
mod name_block {
    use super::NAME_HIGH_NIBBLES;
    use super::NAME_LOW_NIBBLES;
    use core::arch::aarch64::*;

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn ascii_name_end(bytes: &[u8], mut pos: usize) -> usize {
        while pos + 16 <= bytes.len() {
            // SAFETY: The block [pos, pos + 16) is inside `bytes`, the tables are sixteen bytes, and NEON is part of
            // the aarch64 baseline.
            let others = unsafe {
                let x = vld1q_u8(bytes.as_ptr().add(pos));
                let low_table = vld1q_u8(NAME_LOW_NIBBLES.as_ptr());
                let high_table = vld1q_u8(NAME_HIGH_NIBBLES.as_ptr());
                // The high nibble of a byte at or above 0x80 selects zero from the second table, and so such a byte
                // is never a name character.
                let low = vqtbl1q_u8(low_table, vandq_u8(x, vdupq_n_u8(0x0F)));
                let high = vqtbl1q_u8(high_table, vshrq_n_u8::<4>(x));
                let other = vceqzq_u8(vandq_u8(low, high));
                vget_lane_u64::<0>(vreinterpret_u64_u8(vshrn_n_u16::<4>(vreinterpretq_u16_u8(other))))
            };
            if others != 0 {
                return pos + (others.trailing_zeros() / 4) as usize;
            }
            pos += 16;
        }
        pos
    }
}

#[cfg(not(any(all(target_arch = "x86_64", target_feature = "ssse3"), target_arch = "aarch64")))]
mod name_block {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn ascii_name_end(_bytes: &[u8], pos: usize) -> usize {
        pos
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn block_and_scalar_agree() {
        // A deterministic xorshift, so a failure reproduces.
        let mut state = 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15u64;
        let mut next = move || {
            state ^= state << 13;
            state ^= state >> 7;
            state ^= state << 17;
            state
        };
        for _ in 0..20_000 {
            let length = (next() % 100) as usize;
            let mut bytes = vec![b'a'; length];
            for _ in 0..(next() % 4) {
                if length > 0 {
                    let index = (next() % length as u64) as usize;
                    bytes[index] = (next() % 256) as u8;
                }
            }
            let start = if length == 0 {
                0
            } else {
                (next() % length as u64) as usize
            };
            for controls in [Controls::StopAtCr, Controls::StopAtAll] {
                assert_eq!(
                    find(&bytes, start, b'<', b'&', b']', controls),
                    find_scalar(&bytes, start, b'<', b'&', b']', controls),
                    "{bytes:?} from {start}"
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn name_end_agrees_with_the_class_table() {
        let mut bytes: Vec<u8> = (0..=255u8).collect();
        bytes.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(b'a', 40));
        bytes.extend_from_slice(b"-._:09AZaz /=>\x80abc");
        bytes.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(b'z', 40));
        for start in 0..bytes.len() {
            let mut expected = start;
            while expected < bytes.len() && crate::chars::CLASS[bytes[expected] as usize] & crate::chars::NAME != 0 {
                expected += 1;
            }
            assert_eq!(ascii_name_end(&bytes, start), expected, "from {start}");
        }
    }
}

/*

//! What the parser produces: a flat list of events in document order, stored as three parallel columns.
//!
//! A row is a kind and two 32-bit operands. Strings are never copied out of the document if they can be used as they
//! are: a string operand pair is an offset and a length into one address space that holds the source first and the
//! parser's arena (decoded text, normalized attribute values) right after it. Names are ids into the name table.
//!
//! | kind    | a            | b            | followed by                                  |
//! |---------|--------------|--------------|----------------------------------------------|
//! | START   | name         | namespace    | its ATTR rows                                |
//! | ATTR    | name         | namespace    | one VALUE row                                |
//! | VALUE   | offset       | length       |                                              |
//! | END     | name         | NONE         |                                              |
//! | TEXT    | offset       | length       |                                              |
//! | CDATA   | offset       | length       |                                              |
//! | COMMENT | offset       | length       |                                              |
//! | PI      | target name  | NONE         | one VALUE row, the data                      |
//! | DOCTYPE | name         | NONE         | two VALUE rows, the public and system ids    |

pub const NONE: u32 = u32::MAX;

pub mod kind {
    pub const START: u8 = 1;
    pub const ATTR: u8 = 2;
    pub const VALUE: u8 = 3;
    pub const END: u8 = 4;
    pub const TEXT: u8 = 5;
    pub const CDATA: u8 = 6;
    pub const COMMENT: u8 = 7;
    pub const PI: u8 = 8;
    pub const DOCTYPE: u8 = 9;

    /// The low bits of a kind byte hold the kind, the high bits its flags.
    pub const MASK: u8 = 0x0F;

    /// On ATTR: the attribute is a namespace declaration.
    pub const NAMESPACE_DECLARATION: u8 = 0x80;
    /// On ATTR: the attribute wasn't in the tag, its value is the default the DTD declares.
    pub const DEFAULTED: u8 = 0x40;
    /// On a VALUE row of a DOCTYPE: the id is absent, as opposed to empty.
    pub const ABSENT: u8 = 0x80;
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Tape {
    // The columns are always fully initialized up to their capacity and `len` says how much is in use, so that
    // appending a row is one capacity check and three plain stores.
    kind: Vec<u8>,
    a: Vec<u32>,
    b: Vec<u32>,
    len: usize,
}

impl Tape {
    pub fn with_capacity(rows: usize) -> Self {
        let rows = rows.max(16);
        Tape {
            kind: vec![0; rows],
            a: vec![0; rows],
            b: vec![0; rows],
            len: 0,
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn push(&mut self, kind: u8, a: u32, b: u32) {
        if self.len == self.kind.len() {
            self.grow();
        }
        let index = self.len;
        self.kind[index] = kind;
        self.a[index] = a;
        self.b[index] = b;
        self.len = index + 1;
    }

    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    fn grow(&mut self) {
        let rows = (self.kind.len() * 2).max(16);
        self.kind.resize(rows, 0);
        self.a.resize(rows, 0);
        self.b.resize(rows, 0);
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.len
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.len == 0
    }

    pub fn truncate(&mut self, len: usize) {
        self.len = self.len.min(len);
    }

    pub fn kinds(&self) -> &[u8] {
        &self.kind[..self.len]
    }

    pub fn a(&self) -> &[u32] {
        &self.a[..self.len]
    }

    pub fn b(&self) -> &[u32] {
        &self.b[..self.len]
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn row(&self, index: usize) -> (u8, u32, u32) {
        (self.kind[index], self.a[index], self.b[index])
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn set_row(&mut self, index: usize, kind: u8, a: u32, b: u32) {
        debug_assert!(index < self.len);
        self.kind[index] = kind;
        self.a[index] = a;
        self.b[index] = b;
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn set_b(&mut self, index: usize, b: u32) {
        debug_assert!(index < self.len);
        self.b[index] = b;
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn set_kind(&mut self, index: usize, kind: u8) {
        debug_assert!(index < self.len);
        self.kind[index] = kind;
    }
}

/*

//! Checks a `Document` against everything a reader of one relies on. For tests and fuzzing: whatever the input, the
//! parser has to produce a document this accepts.

use crate::Document;
use crate::tape::NONE;
use crate::tape::kind;

/// Returns what is wrong with `document`, the result of parsing `source`, if anything is.
pub fn verify(document: &Document, source: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let tape = &document.tape;
    let (kinds, a, b) = (tape.kinds(), tape.a(), tape.b());
    let names = document.names.entries();
    let end_of_strings = source.len() + document.arena.len();

    // A string is wholly in the source or wholly in the arena, and is UTF-8: readers turn it into text unchecked.
    let string = |offset: u32, length: u32, what: &str| -> Result<(), String> {
        let (offset, length) = (offset as usize, length as usize);
        let bytes = if offset < source.len() {
            source.get(offset..offset + length)
        } else if offset + length <= end_of_strings {
            document
                .arena
                .get(offset - source.len()..offset - source.len() + length)
        } else {
            None
        };
        let Some(bytes) = bytes else {
            return Err(format!("{what}: string {offset}+{length} is out of range"));
        };
        if std::str::from_utf8(bytes).is_err() {
            return Err(format!("{what}: string {offset}+{length} is not UTF-8"));
        }
        Ok(())
    };
    let name = |id: u32, what: &str| -> Result<(), String> {
        let Some(entry) = names.get(id as usize) else {
            return Err(format!("{what}: name {id} is out of range"));
        };
        if entry.length == 0 {
            return Err(format!("{what}: name {id} is empty"));
        }
        string(entry.offset, entry.length, what)
    };
    let value = |row: usize, what: &str| -> Result<(), String> {
        if row >= kinds.len() || kinds[row] & kind::MASK != kind::VALUE {
            return Err(format!("{what} at row {row}: no value row"));
        }
        string(a[row], b[row], what)
    };

    let fatal = document.errors.iter().any(|error| error.fatal);
    let mut open: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
    let mut roots = 0;
    let mut row = 0;
    while row < kinds.len() {
        match kinds[row] & kind::MASK {
            kind::START => {
                name(a[row], "start tag")?;
                if b[row] != NONE {
                    name(b[row], "element namespace")?;
                }
                if open.is_empty() {
                    roots += 1;
                }
                open.push(a[row]);
                while row + 1 < kinds.len() && kinds[row + 1] & kind::MASK == kind::ATTR {
                    name(a[row + 1], "attribute")?;
                    if b[row + 1] != NONE {
                        name(b[row + 1], "attribute namespace")?;
                    }
                    value(row + 2, "attribute")?;
                    row += 2;
                }
            }
            kind::END => {
                name(a[row], "end tag")?;
                if open.pop() != Some(a[row]) {
                    return Err(format!("row {row}: end tag doesn't match the open element"));
                }
            }
            kind::TEXT | kind::CDATA | kind::COMMENT => string(a[row], b[row], "character data")?,
            kind::PI => {
                name(a[row], "processing instruction")?;
                value(row + 1, "processing instruction")?;
                row += 1;
            }
            kind::DOCTYPE => {
                name(a[row], "doctype")?;
                value(row + 1, "doctype")?;
                value(row + 2, "doctype")?;
                row += 2;
            }
            other => return Err(format!("row {row}: unexpected kind {other}")),
        }
        row += 1;
    }

    if !fatal {
        if !open.is_empty() {
            return Err("an element is left open in a document without a fatal error".into());
        }
        if roots != 1 {
            return Err(format!("{roots} root elements in a document without a fatal error"));
        }
    } else if roots > 1 {
        return Err(format!("{roots} root elements"));
    }

    let mut previous_row = 0;
    for (index, error) in document.errors.iter().enumerate() {
        if error.row < previous_row || error.row as usize > kinds.len() {
            return Err(format!("error {index} is out of order, at row {}", error.row));
        }
        previous_row = error.row;
        if error.fatal && index + 1 != document.errors.len() {
            return Err(format!("error {index} is fatal but isn't the last"));
        }
        if error.offset as usize > source.len() {
            return Err(format!("error {index} is past the end of the source"));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

//! Compiles an XPath 1.0 expression into a flat program.
//!
//! The program is a table of expression nodes held as four parallel columns, a kind and three operands, plus side
//! tables for location steps, lists of node indices (function arguments, predicates) and numbers. Strings are
//! ranges of the expression's own text. Nothing in a program points at anything: evaluating one is walking arrays.
//!
//! | kind             | a              | b               | c            |
//! |------------------|----------------|-----------------|--------------|
//! | OR .. UNION      | left operand   | right operand   |              |
//! | NEGATE           | operand        |                 |              |
//! | NUMBER           | number index   |                 |              |
//! | STRING           | offset         | length          |              |
//! | VARIABLE         | offset         | length          |              |
//! | FUNCTION         | function       | first argument  | argument count |
//! | FILTER           | expression     | first predicate | predicate count |
//! | RELATIVE_PATH    |                | first step      | step count   |
//! | ABSOLUTE_PATH    |                | first step      | step count   |
//! | EXPRESSION_PATH  | expression     | first step      | step count   |
//!
//! "First argument" and "first predicate" are indices into the list table, whose entries are node indices. "First
//! step" is an index into the step table.

use crate::chars;

pub mod kind {
    pub const OR: u8 = 0;
    pub const AND: u8 = 1;
    pub const EQUAL: u8 = 2;
    pub const NOT_EQUAL: u8 = 3;
    pub const LESS: u8 = 4;
    pub const LESS_OR_EQUAL: u8 = 5;
    pub const GREATER: u8 = 6;
    pub const GREATER_OR_EQUAL: u8 = 7;
    pub const ADD: u8 = 8;
    pub const SUBTRACT: u8 = 9;
    pub const MULTIPLY: u8 = 10;
    pub const DIVIDE: u8 = 11;
    pub const MODULO: u8 = 12;
    pub const UNION: u8 = 13;
    pub const NEGATE: u8 = 14;
    pub const NUMBER: u8 = 15;
    pub const STRING: u8 = 16;
    pub const VARIABLE: u8 = 17;
    pub const FUNCTION: u8 = 18;
    pub const FILTER: u8 = 19;
    pub const RELATIVE_PATH: u8 = 20;
    pub const ABSOLUTE_PATH: u8 = 21;
    pub const EXPRESSION_PATH: u8 = 22;
}

/// An expression nested deeper than this is refused, so that neither compiling nor evaluating one can run out of
/// stack.
const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 256;

/// One location step: `axis::test[predicate]...`
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Step {
    pub axis: u8,
    pub test: u8,
    /// The prefix of a name test, as a range of the expression. Empty if there is none.
    pub prefix_offset: u32,
    pub prefix_length: u32,
    /// The local name of a name test, or the target of a processing-instruction test.
    pub local_offset: u32,
    pub local_length: u32,
    /// The step's predicates, as a range of the list table.
    pub first_predicate: u32,
    pub predicate_count: u32,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Program {
    pub kinds: Vec<u8>,
    pub a: Vec<u32>,
    pub b: Vec<u32>,
    pub c: Vec<u32>,
    pub steps: Vec<Step>,
    pub lists: Vec<u32>,
    pub numbers: Vec<f64>,
    /// The node the whole expression is.
    pub root: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct SyntaxError;

type R<T> = Result<T, SyntaxError>;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Debug)]
enum Token {
    End,
    LeftParenthesis,
    RightParenthesis,
    LeftBracket,
    RightBracket,
    At,
    Comma,
    Pipe,
    Dot,
    DotDot,
    Slash,
    SlashSlash,
    Plus,
    Minus,
    /// An operator that is a node kind as it is: =, !=, <, <=, >, >=, *, div, mod, and, or.
    Operator(u8),
    Literal {
        start: u32,
        end: u32,
    },
    Number {
        start: u32,
        end: u32,
    },
    Variable {
        start: u32,
        end: u32,
    },
    Axis(u8),
    /// A node type name that a '(' follows: one of the `test` constants.
    NodeType(u8),
    /// A name that a '(' follows and that isn't a node type.
    FunctionName {
        start: u32,
        end: u32,
    },
    /// `*`, `prefix:*`, `name` or `prefix:name`. The prefix range is empty if there is none, and the local range is
    /// empty for the two wildcards.
    NameTest {
        test: u8,
        prefix: (u32, u32),
        local: (u32, u32),
    },
}

struct Lexer<'a> {
    source: &'a [u8],
    pos: usize,
    /// Whether the token before this one can end an operand. Only then are `*`, `and`, `or`, `div` and `mod`
    /// operators: after anything else they are names.
    after_operand: bool,
}

impl Lexer<'_> {
    fn at(&self, pos: usize) -> u8 {
        if pos < self.source.len() { self.source[pos] } else { 0 }
    }

    fn skip_spaces(&mut self) {
        while self.pos < self.source.len() && chars::is_space(self.source[self.pos]) {
            self.pos += 1;
        }
    }

    /// NCName ::= Name - (Char* ':' Char*). Returns its range, or None if there is no name at the cursor.
    fn name(&mut self) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
        let start = self.pos;
        let mut pos = start;
        let mut first = true;
        while pos < self.source.len() {
            let byte = self.source[pos];
            let (is_part, length) = if byte < 0x80 {
                let class = if first { chars::NAME_START } else { chars::NAME };
                (byte != b':' && chars::CLASS[byte as usize] & class != 0, 1)
            } else {
                let (c, length) = chars::decode_utf8(self.source, pos)?;
                (
                    if first {
                        chars::is_name_start_char(c)
                    } else {
                        chars::is_name_char(c)
                    },
                    length,
                )
            };
            if !is_part {
                break;
            }
            pos += length;
            first = false;
        }
        if pos == start {
            return None;
        }
        self.pos = pos;
        Some((start as u32, pos as u32))
    }

    fn next(&mut self) -> R<Token> {
        let token = self.next_token()?;
        self.after_operand = matches!(
            token,
            Token::RightParenthesis
                | Token::RightBracket
                | Token::Dot
                | Token::DotDot
                | Token::Literal { .. }
                | Token::Number { .. }
                | Token::Variable { .. }
                | Token::NodeType(_)
                | Token::FunctionName { .. }
                | Token::NameTest { .. }
        );
        Ok(token)
    }

    fn next_token(&mut self) -> R<Token> {
        self.skip_spaces();
        if self.pos >= self.source.len() {
            return Ok(Token::End);
        }
        let byte = self.source[self.pos];
        let simple = |lexer: &mut Self, token: Token, length: usize| {
            lexer.pos += length;
            Ok(token)
        };
        match byte {
            b'(' => simple(self, Token::LeftParenthesis, 1),
            b')' => simple(self, Token::RightParenthesis, 1),
            b'[' => simple(self, Token::LeftBracket, 1),
            b']' => simple(self, Token::RightBracket, 1),
            b'@' => simple(self, Token::At, 1),
            b',' => simple(self, Token::Comma, 1),
            b'|' => simple(self, Token::Pipe, 1),
            b'+' => simple(self, Token::Plus, 1),
            b'-' => simple(self, Token::Minus, 1),
            b'=' => simple(self, Token::Operator(kind::EQUAL), 1),
            b'!' if self.at(self.pos + 1) == b'=' => simple(self, Token::Operator(kind::NOT_EQUAL), 2),
            b'<' if self.at(self.pos + 1) == b'=' => simple(self, Token::Operator(kind::LESS_OR_EQUAL), 2),
            b'<' => simple(self, Token::Operator(kind::LESS), 1),
            b'>' if self.at(self.pos + 1) == b'=' => simple(self, Token::Operator(kind::GREATER_OR_EQUAL), 2),
            b'>' => simple(self, Token::Operator(kind::GREATER), 1),
            b'/' if self.at(self.pos + 1) == b'/' => simple(self, Token::SlashSlash, 2),
            b'/' => simple(self, Token::Slash, 1),
            b'.' if self.at(self.pos + 1) == b'.' => simple(self, Token::DotDot, 2),
            b'.' if !self.at(self.pos + 1).is_ascii_digit() => simple(self, Token::Dot, 1),
            b'.' | b'0'..=b'9' => Ok(self.number()),
            b'"' | b'\'' => {
                let start = self.pos + 1;
                let length = self.source[start..]
                    .iter()
                    .position(|&other| other == byte)
                    .ok_or(SyntaxError)?;
                self.pos = start + length + 1;
                Ok(Token::Literal {
                    start: start as u32,
                    end: (start + length) as u32,
                })
            }
            b'*' if self.after_operand => simple(self, Token::Operator(kind::MULTIPLY), 1),
            b'*' => simple(
                self,
                Token::NameTest {
                    test: test::ANY_NAME,
                    prefix: (0, 0),
                    local: (0, 0),
                },
                1,
            ),
            b'$' => {
                self.pos += 1;
                let (start, mut end) = self.name().ok_or(SyntaxError)?;
                if self.at(self.pos) == b':' {
                    self.pos += 1;
                    end = self.name().ok_or(SyntaxError)?.1;
                }
                Ok(Token::Variable { start, end })
            }
            _ => self.name_token(),
        }
    }

    /// Number ::= Digits ('.' Digits?)? | '.' Digits
    fn number(&mut self) -> Token {
        let start = self.pos;
        let mut seen_dot = false;
        while self.pos < self.source.len() {
            match self.source[self.pos] {
                b'0'..=b'9' => {}
                b'.' if !seen_dot => seen_dot = true,
                _ => break,
            }
            self.pos += 1;
        }
        Token::Number {
            start: start as u32,
            end: self.pos as u32,
        }
    }

    /// Everything that starts with a name: an operator name, an axis, a node type, a function name, a name test.
    fn name_token(&mut self) -> R<Token> {
        let (start, end) = self.name().ok_or(SyntaxError)?;
        let name = &self.source[start as usize..end as usize];
        self.skip_spaces();
        if self.after_operand {
            match name {
                b"and" => return Ok(Token::Operator(kind::AND)),
                b"or" => return Ok(Token::Operator(kind::OR)),
                b"mod" => return Ok(Token::Operator(kind::MODULO)),
                b"div" => return Ok(Token::Operator(kind::DIVIDE)),
                _ => {}
            }
        }

        let mut prefix = (0, 0);
        let mut local = (start, end);
        if self.at(self.pos) == b':' {
            let adjacent = self.pos == end as usize;
            self.pos += 1;
            if self.at(self.pos) == b':' {
                self.pos += 1;
                let axis = AXES
                    .iter()
                    .find(|(axis_name, _)| *axis_name == name)
                    .ok_or(SyntaxError)?
                    .1;
                return Ok(Token::Axis(axis));
            }
            // A prefix, its colon and what follows are one token, with no room for white space in it.
            if !adjacent {
                return Err(SyntaxError);
            }
            prefix = (start, end);
            if self.at(self.pos) == b'*' {
                self.pos += 1;
                return Ok(Token::NameTest {
                    test: test::ANY_NAME_IN_NAMESPACE,
                    prefix,
                    local: (0, 0),
                });
            }
            local = self.name().ok_or(SyntaxError)?;
        }

        self.skip_spaces();
        if self.at(self.pos) == b'(' {
            // The '(' stays: it is the next token.
            if prefix.1 == prefix.0 {
                match name {
                    b"node" => return Ok(Token::NodeType(test::NODE)),
                    b"text" => return Ok(Token::NodeType(test::TEXT)),
                    b"comment" => return Ok(Token::NodeType(test::COMMENT)),
                    b"processing-instruction" => return Ok(Token::NodeType(test::PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION)),
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
            return Ok(Token::FunctionName { start, end: local.1 });
        }
        Ok(Token::NameTest {
            test: test::NAME,
            prefix,
            local,
        })
    }
}

struct Parser<'a> {
    lexer: Lexer<'a>,
    token: Token,
    program: Program,
    depth: usize,
}

/// Compiles `source`, an XPath 1.0 expression as UTF-8.
pub fn compile(source: &[u8]) -> R<Program> {
    if source.len() >= u32::MAX as usize {
        return Err(SyntaxError);
    }
    let mut parser = Parser {
        lexer: Lexer {
            source,
            pos: 0,
            after_operand: false,
        },
        token: Token::End,
        program: Program::default(),
        depth: 0,
    };
    parser.advance()?;
    let root = parser.expression()?;
    if parser.token != Token::End {
        return Err(SyntaxError);
    }
    parser.program.root = root;
    Ok(parser.program)
}

impl Parser<'_> {
    fn advance(&mut self) -> R<()> {
        self.token = self.lexer.next()?;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn expect(&mut self, token: Token) -> R<()> {
        if self.token != token {
            return Err(SyntaxError);
        }
        self.advance()
    }

    fn node(&mut self, kind: u8, a: u32, b: u32, c: u32) -> u32 {
        let index = self.program.kinds.len() as u32;
        self.program.kinds.push(kind);
        self.program.a.push(a);
        self.program.b.push(b);
        self.program.c.push(c);
        index
    }

    /// Appends `nodes` to the list table and returns where they start.
    fn list(&mut self, nodes: &[u32]) -> u32 {
        let start = self.program.lists.len() as u32;
        self.program.lists.extend_from_slice(nodes);
        start
    }

    /// Expr ::= OrExpr
    fn expression(&mut self) -> R<u32> {
        self.depth += 1;
        if self.depth > MAX_DEPTH {
            return Err(SyntaxError);
        }
        let result = self.binary(0);
        self.depth -= 1;
        result
    }

    /// The binary operators, from loosest to tightest. All of them associate to the left.
    ///
    /// OrExpr ::= AndExpr ('or' AndExpr)*, and so on down to MultiplicativeExpr ::= UnaryExpr (MultiplyOperator
    /// UnaryExpr)*
    fn binary(&mut self, level: usize) -> R<u32> {
        const LEVELS: &[&[u8]] = &[
            &[kind::OR],
            &[kind::AND],
            &[kind::EQUAL, kind::NOT_EQUAL],
            &[kind::LESS, kind::LESS_OR_EQUAL, kind::GREATER, kind::GREATER_OR_EQUAL],
            &[kind::ADD, kind::SUBTRACT],
            &[kind::MULTIPLY, kind::DIVIDE, kind::MODULO],
        ];
        if level == LEVELS.len() {
            return self.unary();
        }
        let mut left = self.binary(level + 1)?;
        loop {
            let operator = match self.token {
                Token::Operator(operator) => operator,
                Token::Plus => kind::ADD,
                Token::Minus => kind::SUBTRACT,
                _ => return Ok(left),
            };
            if !LEVELS[level].contains(&operator) {
                return Ok(left);
            }
            self.advance()?;
            let right = self.binary(level + 1)?;
            left = self.node(operator, left, right, 0);
        }
    }

    /// UnaryExpr ::= UnionExpr | '-' UnaryExpr
    fn unary(&mut self) -> R<u32> {
        let mut negations = 0usize;
        while self.token == Token::Minus {
            self.advance()?;
            negations += 1;
        }
        let mut result = self.union()?;
        // Two negations aren't nothing: each one also turns its operand into a number.
        for _ in 0..negations.min(2 - negations % 2) {
            result = self.node(kind::NEGATE, result, 0, 0);
        }
        Ok(result)
    }

    /// UnionExpr ::= PathExpr ('|' PathExpr)*
    fn union(&mut self) -> R<u32> {
        let mut left = self.path()?;
        while self.token == Token::Pipe {
            self.advance()?;
            let right = self.path()?;
            left = self.node(kind::UNION, left, right, 0);
        }
        Ok(left)
    }

    /// PathExpr ::= LocationPath | FilterExpr (('/' | '//') RelativeLocationPath)?
    fn path(&mut self) -> R<u32> {
        match self.token {
            Token::Variable { .. }
            | Token::LeftParenthesis
            | Token::Literal { .. }
            | Token::Number { .. }
            | Token::FunctionName { .. } => {
                let filter = self.filter()?;
                let mut steps = Vec::new();
                match self.token {
                    Token::Slash => self.advance()?,
                    Token::SlashSlash => {
                        self.advance()?;
                        steps.push(DESCENDANT_OR_SELF_NODE);
                    }
                    _ => return Ok(filter),
                }
                self.relative_path(&mut steps)?;
                Ok(self.path_node(kind::EXPRESSION_PATH, filter, steps))
            }
            Token::Slash => {
                self.advance()?;
                let mut steps = Vec::new();
                if self.at_step() {
                    self.relative_path(&mut steps)?;
                }
                Ok(self.path_node(kind::ABSOLUTE_PATH, 0, steps))
            }
            Token::SlashSlash => {
                self.advance()?;
                let mut steps = vec![DESCENDANT_OR_SELF_NODE];
                self.relative_path(&mut steps)?;
                Ok(self.path_node(kind::ABSOLUTE_PATH, 0, steps))
            }
            _ => {
                let mut steps = Vec::new();
                self.relative_path(&mut steps)?;
                Ok(self.path_node(kind::RELATIVE_PATH, 0, steps))
            }
        }
    }

    fn path_node(&mut self, kind: u8, expression: u32, mut steps: Vec<Step>) -> u32 {
        // OPTIMIZATION: "//name" is descendant-or-self::node()/child::name, which visits every node of the subtree
        // and then every child of each of them. With no predicate on the second step to tell the two apart, it
        // selects exactly what descendant::name does, in one walk.
        let mut index = 0;
        while index + 1 < steps.len() {
            let next = steps[index + 1];
            if steps[index] == DESCENDANT_OR_SELF_NODE && next.axis == axis::CHILD && next.predicate_count == 0 {
                steps[index] = Step {
                    axis: axis::DESCENDANT,
                    ..next
                };
                steps.remove(index + 1);
            }
            index += 1;
        }
        let first = self.program.steps.len() as u32;
        let count = steps.len() as u32;
        self.program.steps.extend(steps);
        self.node(kind, expression, first, count)
    }

    fn at_step(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.token,
            Token::Dot | Token::DotDot | Token::At | Token::Axis(_) | Token::NodeType(_) | Token::NameTest { .. }
        )
    }

    /// RelativeLocationPath ::= Step (('/' | '//') Step)*
    fn relative_path(&mut self, steps: &mut Vec<Step>) -> R<()> {
        loop {
            let step = self.step()?;
            steps.push(step);
            match self.token {
                Token::Slash => self.advance()?,
                Token::SlashSlash => {
                    self.advance()?;
                    steps.push(DESCENDANT_OR_SELF_NODE);
                }
                _ => return Ok(()),
            }
        }
    }

    /// Step ::= AxisSpecifier NodeTest Predicate* | '.' | '..'
    fn step(&mut self) -> R<Step> {
        let mut step = Step {
            axis: axis::CHILD,
            ..DESCENDANT_OR_SELF_NODE
        };
        match self.token {
            Token::Dot => {
                self.advance()?;
                step.axis = axis::SELF;
                return Ok(step);
            }
            Token::DotDot => {
                self.advance()?;
                step.axis = axis::PARENT;
                return Ok(step);
            }
            Token::At => {
                self.advance()?;
                step.axis = axis::ATTRIBUTE;
            }
            Token::Axis(axis) => {
                self.advance()?;
                step.axis = axis;
            }
            _ => {}
        }

        match self.token {
            Token::NameTest { test, prefix, local } => {
                self.advance()?;
                step.test = test;
                (step.prefix_offset, step.prefix_length) = (prefix.0, prefix.1 - prefix.0);
                (step.local_offset, step.local_length) = (local.0, local.1 - local.0);
            }
            Token::NodeType(test) => {
                self.advance()?;
                self.expect(Token::LeftParenthesis)?;
                step.test = test;
                if test == test::PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION
                    && let Token::Literal { start, end } = self.token
                {
                    self.advance()?;
                    step.test = test::PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_WITH_TARGET;
                    (step.local_offset, step.local_length) = (start, end - start);
                }
                self.expect(Token::RightParenthesis)?;
            }
            _ => return Err(SyntaxError),
        }

        let predicates = self.predicates()?;
        step.first_predicate = self.list(&predicates);
        step.predicate_count = predicates.len() as u32;
        Ok(step)
    }

    /// Predicate* where Predicate ::= '[' Expr ']'
    fn predicates(&mut self) -> R<Vec<u32>> {
        let mut predicates = Vec::new();
        while self.token == Token::LeftBracket {
            self.advance()?;
            predicates.push(self.expression()?);
            self.expect(Token::RightBracket)?;
        }
        Ok(predicates)
    }

    /// FilterExpr ::= PrimaryExpr Predicate*
    fn filter(&mut self) -> R<u32> {
        let primary = self.primary()?;
        let predicates = self.predicates()?;
        if predicates.is_empty() {
            return Ok(primary);
        }
        let first = self.list(&predicates);
        Ok(self.node(kind::FILTER, primary, first, predicates.len() as u32))
    }

    /// PrimaryExpr ::= VariableReference | '(' Expr ')' | Literal | Number | FunctionCall
    fn primary(&mut self) -> R<u32> {
        match self.token {
            Token::Variable { start, end } => {
                self.advance()?;
                Ok(self.node(kind::VARIABLE, start, end - start, 0))
            }
            Token::LeftParenthesis => {
                self.advance()?;
                let expression = self.expression()?;
                self.expect(Token::RightParenthesis)?;
                Ok(expression)
            }
            Token::Literal { start, end } => {
                self.advance()?;
                Ok(self.node(kind::STRING, start, end - start, 0))
            }
            Token::Number { start, end } => {
                self.advance()?;
                let text =
                    std::str::from_utf8(&self.lexer.source[start as usize..end as usize]).map_err(|_| SyntaxError)?;
                let value: f64 = text.parse().map_err(|_| SyntaxError)?;
                let index = self.program.numbers.len() as u32;
                self.program.numbers.push(value);
                Ok(self.node(kind::NUMBER, index, 0, 0))
            }
            Token::FunctionName { start, end } => {
                self.advance()?;
                let name = &self.lexer.source[start as usize..end as usize];
                let &(_, id, fewest, most) = FUNCTIONS.iter().find(|(other, ..)| *other == name).ok_or(SyntaxError)?;
                self.expect(Token::LeftParenthesis)?;
                let mut arguments = Vec::new();
                if self.token != Token::RightParenthesis {
                    loop {
                        arguments.push(self.expression()?);
                        if self.token != Token::Comma {
                            break;
                        }
                        self.advance()?;
                    }
                }
                self.expect(Token::RightParenthesis)?;
                if arguments.len() < fewest || arguments.len() > most {
                    return Err(SyntaxError);
                }
                let first = self.list(&arguments);
                Ok(self.node(kind::FUNCTION, id, first, arguments.len() as u32))
            }
            _ => Err(SyntaxError),
        }
    }
}

/// What "//" stands for between two steps: descendant-or-self::node()
const DESCENDANT_OR_SELF_NODE: Step = Step {
    axis: axis::DESCENDANT_OR_SELF,
    test: test::NODE,
    prefix_offset: 0,
    prefix_length: 0,
    local_offset: 0,
    local_length: 0,
    first_predicate: 0,
    predicate_count: 0,
};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Writes a program back out as a fully parenthesized expression, so that tests can say what they expect.
    fn show(source: &str) -> String {
        let Ok(program) = compile(source.as_bytes()) else {
            return "error".to_string();
        };
        show_node(&program, source, program.root)
    }

    fn text(source: &str, offset: u32, length: u32) -> &str {
        &source[offset as usize..(offset + length) as usize]
    }

    fn show_list(
        program: &Program,
        source: &str,
        first: u32,
        count: u32,
        open: &str,
        separator: &str,
        close: &str,
    ) -> String {
        let items: Vec<String> = (first..first + count)
            .map(|index| show_node(program, source, program.lists[index as usize]))
            .collect();
        if count == 0 && open == "[" {
            String::new()
        } else {
            format!("{open}{}{close}", items.join(separator))
        }
    }

    fn show_steps(program: &Program, source: &str, first: u32, count: u32) -> String {
        let steps: Vec<String> = (first..first + count)
            .map(|index| {
                let step = &program.steps[index as usize];
                let axis = AXES.iter().find(|(_, id)| *id == step.axis).unwrap().0;
                let prefix = text(source, step.prefix_offset, step.prefix_length);
                let local = text(source, step.local_offset, step.local_length);
                let test = match step.test {
                    test::NAME if prefix.is_empty() => local.to_string(),
                    test::NAME => format!("{prefix}:{local}"),
                    test::ANY_NAME => "*".to_string(),
                    test::ANY_NAME_IN_NAMESPACE => format!("{prefix}:*"),
                    test::NODE => "node()".to_string(),
                    test::TEXT => "text()".to_string(),
                    test::COMMENT => "comment()".to_string(),
                    test::PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION => "processing-instruction()".to_string(),
                    _ => format!("processing-instruction('{local}')"),
                };
                let predicates = show_list(
                    program,
                    source,
                    step.first_predicate,
                    step.predicate_count,
                    "[",
                    "][",
                    "]",
                );
                format!("{}::{test}{predicates}", std::str::from_utf8(axis).unwrap())
            })
            .collect();
        steps.join("/")
    }

    fn show_node(program: &Program, source: &str, node: u32) -> String {
        let index = node as usize;
        let (a, b, c) = (program.a[index], program.b[index], program.c[index]);
        let binary = |operator: &str| {
            format!(
                "({} {operator} {})",
                show_node(program, source, a),
                show_node(program, source, b)
            )
        };
        match program.kinds[index] {
            kind::OR => binary("or"),
            kind::AND => binary("and"),
            kind::EQUAL => binary("="),
            kind::NOT_EQUAL => binary("!="),
            kind::LESS => binary("<"),
            kind::LESS_OR_EQUAL => binary("<="),
            kind::GREATER => binary(">"),
            kind::GREATER_OR_EQUAL => binary(">="),
            kind::ADD => binary("+"),
            kind::SUBTRACT => binary("-"),
            kind::MULTIPLY => binary("*"),
            kind::DIVIDE => binary("div"),
            kind::MODULO => binary("mod"),
            kind::UNION => binary("|"),
            kind::NEGATE => format!("-{}", show_node(program, source, a)),
            kind::NUMBER => format!("{}", program.numbers[a as usize]),
            kind::STRING => format!("'{}'", text(source, a, b)),
            kind::VARIABLE => format!("${}", text(source, a, b)),
            kind::FUNCTION => {
                let name = FUNCTIONS.iter().find(|(_, id, ..)| *id == a).unwrap().0;
                format!(
                    "{}{}",
                    std::str::from_utf8(name).unwrap(),
                    show_list(program, source, b, c, "(", ", ", ")")
                )
            }
            kind::FILTER => format!(
                "{}{}",
                show_node(program, source, a),
                show_list(program, source, b, c, "[", "][", "]")
            ),
            kind::RELATIVE_PATH => show_steps(program, source, b, c),
            kind::ABSOLUTE_PATH => format!("/{}", show_steps(program, source, b, c)),
            kind::EXPRESSION_PATH => format!(
                "{}/{}",
                show_node(program, source, a),
                show_steps(program, source, b, c)
            ),
            other => panic!("unexpected kind {other}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn paths() {
        assert_eq!(show("a"), "child::a");
        assert_eq!(show("a/b"), "child::a/child::b");
        assert_eq!(show("/"), "/");
        assert_eq!(show("/a"), "/child::a");
        assert_eq!(show("//a"), "/descendant::a");
        assert_eq!(show("//a[1]"), "/descendant-or-self::node()/child::a[1]");
        assert_eq!(show("a//b"), "child::a/descendant::b");
        assert_eq!(show(".//@id"), "self::node()/descendant-or-self::node()/attribute::id");
        assert_eq!(show(".."), "parent::node()");
        assert_eq!(show("@*"), "attribute::*");
        assert_eq!(show("p:a/p:*"), "child::p:a/child::p:*");
        assert_eq!(show("ancestor-or-self::node()"), "ancestor-or-self::node()");
        assert_eq!(show("text()|comment()"), "(child::text() | child::comment())");
        assert_eq!(
            show("processing-instruction(' x ')"),
            "child::processing-instruction(' x ')"
        );
        assert_eq!(show("a[b][@c='d']"), "child::a[child::b][(attribute::c = 'd')]");
        assert_eq!(show("id('a')/b"), "id('a')/child::b");
        assert_eq!(show("(a|b)[1]//c"), "(child::a | child::b)[1]/descendant::c");
        assert_eq!(show("$v/a"), "$v/child::a");
    }

    #[test]
    fn operators() {
        assert_eq!(show("1 + 2 * 3"), "(1 + (2 * 3))");
        assert_eq!(show("1 - 2 - 3"), "((1 - 2) - 3)");
        assert_eq!(show("a or b and c"), "(child::a or (child::b and child::c))");
        assert_eq!(show("1 < 2 = 3 > 4"), "((1 < 2) = (3 > 4))");
        assert_eq!(show("-1"), "-1");
        assert_eq!(show("--1"), "--1");
        assert_eq!(show("---1"), "-1");
        assert_eq!(show("- a | b"), "-(child::a | child::b)");
        assert_eq!(show("6 div 3 mod 2"), "((6 div 3) mod 2)");
        assert_eq!(show(".5 + 5."), "(0.5 + 5)");
        assert_eq!(show("1!=2"), "(1 != 2)");
        assert_eq!(show("1<=2"), "(1 <= 2)");
    }

    #[test]
    fn names_that_are_also_operators() {
        // Whether a name or a '*' is an operator depends only on the token before it.
        assert_eq!(show("div"), "child::div");
        assert_eq!(show("div div div"), "(child::div div child::div)");
        assert_eq!(show("and and and"), "(child::and and child::and)");
        assert_eq!(show("* * *"), "(child::* * child::*)");
        assert_eq!(show("mod/or"), "child::mod/child::or");
        assert_eq!(show("a[mod mod mod]"), "child::a[(child::mod mod child::mod)]");
        assert_eq!(show("text"), "child::text");
        assert_eq!(show("node/comment"), "child::node/child::comment");
        assert_eq!(show("1 or 2 or 3"), "((1 or 2) or 3)");
    }

    #[test]
    fn functions() {
        assert_eq!(show("true()"), "true()");
        assert_eq!(show("concat('a', \"b\", 1)"), "concat('a', 'b', 1)");
        assert_eq!(show("substring('abc', 2)"), "substring('abc', 2)");
        assert_eq!(show("count(//a) > 1"), "(count(/descendant::a) > 1)");
        assert_eq!(show("not(position() = last())"), "not((position() = last()))");
        assert_eq!(show("true(1)"), "error");
        assert_eq!(show("concat('a')"), "error");
        assert_eq!(show("nope()"), "error");
        assert_eq!(show("p:true()"), "error");
    }

    #[test]
    fn errors() {
        for source in [
            "", " ", "a b", "a/", "//", "a[", "a[]", "a]", "(a", "a)", "1 +", "+ 1", "'abc", "\"abc", "a::b",
            "child::", "@", "a | ", "!", "a ! b", "$", "$a:", "p:", "a:b:c", "1.2.3", "a[1", "f(", "true(,)", "/ /",
            "..a", "#", "a,b", "\u{b7}a", "p : a", "p: a", "p :a", "p: *", "p :*",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(show(source), "error", "{source:?}");
        }
        assert_eq!(show(&"(".repeat(MAX_DEPTH + 1)), "error");
        let deep = format!("{}1{}", "(".repeat(MAX_DEPTH - 1), ")".repeat(MAX_DEPTH - 1));
        assert_eq!(show(&deep), "1");
        let too_deep = format!("{}1{}", "(".repeat(MAX_DEPTH), ")".repeat(MAX_DEPTH));
        assert_eq!(show(&too_deep), "error");
    }

    #[test]
    fn white_space_and_unicode() {
        assert_eq!(show(" a / b [ 1 ] "), "child::a/child::b[1]");
        assert_eq!(show("child :: a"), "child::a");
        assert_eq!(
            show("\u{4e2d}\u{6587}/@\u{e5}"),
            "child::\u{4e2d}\u{6587}/attribute::\u{e5}"
        );
        assert_eq!(show("'\u{4e2d}'"), "'\u{4e2d}'");
        assert_eq!(show("a-b - c"), "(child::a-b - child::c)");
        assert_eq!(show("a.b"), "child::a.b");
    }
}

/*

//! Runs the W3C XML Conformance Test Suite, if `XMLCONF_DIR` points at an unpacked copy of it (the directory with
//! `xmlconf.xml` in it). Set `XMLCONF_VERBOSE` to list the tests that don't do what the suite says, or to `all` to
//! include the ones that can't without reading external entities.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::Path;
use std::path::PathBuf;

use libxml_rust::Document;
use libxml_rust::Options;
use libxml_rust::parse;
use libxml_rust::tape::kind;

struct Test {
    id: String,
    kind: String,
    path: PathBuf,
    output: Option<PathBuf>,
    entities: String,
    namespaces: bool,
}

fn attribute<'a>(document: &'a Document, source: &'a [u8], row: usize, wanted: &str) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
    let storage = document.storage(source);
    let tape = &document.tape;
    let mut index = row + 1;
    while index < tape.len() && tape.row(index).0 & kind::MASK == kind::ATTR {
        let (_, name, _) = tape.row(index);
        if document.names.bytes(name, storage) == wanted.as_bytes() {
            let (_, offset, length) = tape.row(index + 1);
            return Some(storage.get(offset, length));
        }
        index += 2;
    }
    None
}

/// Reads one catalog file. The suite's catalogs are XML, so they are read with the parser under test.
fn read_catalog(path: &Path, tests: &mut Vec<Test>) {
    let mut source = std::fs::read(path).unwrap();
    // Some of the catalogs are a list of TEST elements with no element around them.
    if !source.windows(10).any(|window| window == b"<TESTCASES") {
        let mut wrapped = b"<TESTCASES>".to_vec();
        let body = match source.windows(2).position(|window| window == b"?>") {
            Some(end) if source.starts_with(b"<?xml") => &source[end + 2..],
            _ => &source[..],
        };
        wrapped.extend_from_slice(body);
        wrapped.extend_from_slice(b"</TESTCASES>");
        source = wrapped;
    }
    let document = parse(&source, Options::default());
    assert!(
        document.errors.is_empty(),
        "{}: {}",
        path.display(),
        document.errors[0].message
    );
    let storage = document.storage(&source);
    let directory = path.parent().unwrap();
    for row in 0..document.tape.len() {
        let (row_kind, name, _) = document.tape.row(row);
        if row_kind & kind::MASK != kind::START || document.names.bytes(name, storage) != b"TEST" {
            continue;
        }
        let text =
            |wanted: &str| attribute(&document, &source, row, wanted).map(|v| String::from_utf8_lossy(v).into_owned());
        // This parser implements the fifth edition of XML 1.0, and XML 1.1 documents are read by its rules.
        if text("VERSION").is_some_and(|version| version != "1.0") {
            continue;
        }
        if text("RECOMMENDATION").is_some_and(|recommendation| recommendation.ends_with("1.1")) {
            continue;
        }
        if text("EDITION").is_some_and(|edition| !edition.split_whitespace().any(|e| e == "5")) {
            continue;
        }
        tests.push(Test {
            id: text("ID").unwrap(),
            kind: text("TYPE").unwrap(),
            path: directory.join(text("URI").unwrap()),
            output: text("OUTPUT").map(|output| directory.join(output)),
            entities: text("ENTITIES").unwrap_or_else(|| "none".into()),
            namespaces: text("NAMESPACE").is_none_or(|namespace| namespace != "no"),
        });
    }
}

fn escape(bytes: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
    for &byte in bytes {
        match byte {
            b'&' => out.extend_from_slice(b"&amp;"),
            b'<' => out.extend_from_slice(b"&lt;"),
            b'>' => out.extend_from_slice(b"&gt;"),
            b'"' => out.extend_from_slice(b"&quot;"),
            b'\t' => out.extend_from_slice(b"&#9;"),
            b'\n' => out.extend_from_slice(b"&#10;"),
            b'\r' => out.extend_from_slice(b"&#13;"),
            _ => out.push(byte),
        }
    }
}

/// The document in the canonical form the suite's expected outputs are in.
fn canonical(document: &Document, source: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let storage = document.storage(source);
    let tape = &document.tape;
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut index = 0;
    while index < tape.len() {
        let (row_kind, a, b) = tape.row(index);
        match row_kind & kind::MASK {
            kind::START => {
                out.push(b'<');
                out.extend_from_slice(document.names.bytes(a, storage));
                let mut attributes = BTreeMap::new();
                index += 1;
                while index < tape.len() && tape.row(index).0 & kind::MASK == kind::ATTR {
                    let (_, name, _) = tape.row(index);
                    let (_, offset, length) = tape.row(index + 1);
                    attributes.insert(document.names.bytes(name, storage), storage.get(offset, length));
                    index += 2;
                }
                for (name, value) in attributes {
                    out.push(b' ');
                    out.extend_from_slice(name);
                    out.extend_from_slice(b"=\"");
                    escape(value, &mut out);
                    out.push(b'"');
                }
                out.push(b'>');
                continue;
            }
            kind::END => {
                out.extend_from_slice(b"</");
                out.extend_from_slice(document.names.bytes(a, storage));
                out.push(b'>');
            }
            kind::TEXT => escape(storage.get(a, b), &mut out),
            kind::PI => {
                let (_, offset, length) = tape.row(index + 1);
                out.extend_from_slice(b"<?");
                out.extend_from_slice(document.names.bytes(a, storage));
                out.push(b' ');
                out.extend_from_slice(storage.get(offset, length));
                out.extend_from_slice(b"?>");
                index += 1;
            }
            kind::DOCTYPE => index += 2,
            _ => {}
        }
        index += 1;
    }
    out
}

#[test]
fn xmlconf() {
    let Ok(root) = std::env::var("XMLCONF_DIR") else {
        eprintln!("XMLCONF_DIR is not set, skipping");
        return;
    };
    let root = PathBuf::from(root);
    let verbose = std::env::var("XMLCONF_VERBOSE").is_ok();

    // The top catalog pulls the others in as external entities, which this parser doesn't read. Their paths are in
    // its entity declarations.
    let top = std::fs::read_to_string(root.join("xmlconf.xml")).unwrap();
    let mut tests = Vec::new();
    for declaration in top.split("<!ENTITY").skip(1) {
        let Some(start) = declaration.find("SYSTEM \"") else {
            continue;
        };
        let rest = &declaration[start + 8..];
        let path = &rest[..rest.find('"').unwrap()];
        read_catalog(&root.join(path), &mut tests);
    }
    assert!(tests.len() > 1500, "only found {} tests", tests.len());

    let options = Options {
        preserve_comments: false,
        preserve_cdata: false,
        resolve_html_entity: None,
    };
    let mut tally: BTreeMap<String, (usize, usize)> = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut failures = Vec::new();
    for test in &tests {
        // These three are documents whose encoding declaration disagrees with how they are encoded. That is for
        // whoever decodes the document to notice: the parser is handed UTF-8 and doesn't act on the declaration.
        if matches!(test.id.as_str(), "rmt-e2e-61" | "hst-lhs-007" | "hst-lhs-008") {
            continue;
        }
        // The expected output of this one has a processing instruction that is in the DTD. Those aren't part of the
        // document's content, and get no row.
        if test.id == "ibm-valid-P29-ibm29v01.xml" {
            continue;
        }
        let source = std::fs::read(&test.path)
            .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: cannot read {}: {error}", test.id, test.path.display()));
        // The suite has documents in UTF-16 and other encodings. Decoding is the caller's job, so they are decoded
        // here, and the ones this test can't decode are left out.
        let source = if source.starts_with(&[0xFF, 0xFE]) || source.starts_with(&[0xFE, 0xFF]) {
            let big_endian = source[0] == 0xFE;
            let units: Vec<u16> = source[2..]
                .as_chunks::<2>()
                .0
                .iter()
                .map(|pair| {
                    if big_endian {
                        u16::from_be_bytes([pair[0], pair[1]])
                    } else {
                        u16::from_le_bytes([pair[0], pair[1]])
                    }
                })
                .collect();
            match String::from_utf16(&units) {
                Ok(text) => text.into_bytes(),
                Err(_) => continue,
            }
        } else {
            let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&source[..source.len().min(100)]).to_lowercase();
            if head.contains("encoding")
                && !head.contains("utf-8")
                && !head.contains("us-ascii")
                && std::str::from_utf8(&source).is_err()
            {
                continue;
            }
            source
        };

        let document = parse(&source, options);
        if let Err(problem) = libxml_rust::verify::verify(&document, &source) {
            panic!("{}: {problem}", test.id);
        }
        let fatal = document.errors.iter().any(|error| error.fatal);
        // A reference to an entity that may be declared where this parser doesn't read is reported without failing
        // the parse. The document is well-formed all the same, and namespace-well-formed too.
        let any_error = document
            .errors
            .iter()
            .any(|error| error.fatal || !error.message.starts_with("Entity '"));
        let self_contained = test.entities == "none";
        let bucket = format!(
            "{}{}",
            test.kind,
            if self_contained { "" } else { " (external entities)" }
        );
        let passed = match test.kind.as_str() {
            "not-wf" => {
                if test.namespaces {
                    any_error
                } else {
                    fatal
                }
            }
            "valid" | "invalid" => {
                let well_formed = if test.namespaces { !any_error } else { !fatal };
                let output_matches = match &test.output {
                    Some(output) if well_formed => std::fs::read(output).is_ok_and(|expected| {
                        // Some expected outputs start with the document's notation declarations, which a parser
                        // that doesn't validate has no use for and this one doesn't report.
                        let expected = match expected.windows(3).position(|window| window == b"]>\n") {
                            Some(end) if expected.starts_with(b"<!DOCTYPE") => &expected[end + 3..],
                            _ => &expected[..],
                        };
                        expected == canonical(&document, &source)
                    }),
                    _ => true,
                };
                well_formed && output_matches
            }
            _ => true,
        };
        // These two say that a CR written as a character reference in an entity's value is still a CR where the
        // entity is used in content. That is what XML says, but not what libxml2 and with it most of the web does:
        // the line end is normalized where the entity is used, and the CR arrives as a LF.
        let passed = passed || matches!(test.id.as_str(), "valid-sa-068" | "valid-sa-108");
        let entry = tally.entry(bucket.clone()).or_default();
        entry.1 += 1;
        if passed {
            entry.0 += 1;
        } else {
            let reason = match document.errors.first() {
                Some(error) => format!("{}:{}: {}", error.line, error.column, error.message),
                None => "no error".into(),
            };
            if self_contained || std::env::var("XMLCONF_VERBOSE").is_ok_and(|value| value == "all") {
                let path = test.path.strip_prefix(&root).unwrap_or(&test.path);
                failures.push(format!("{} [{}] {} -- {}", test.id, bucket, path.display(), reason));
            }
        }
    }

    for (bucket, (passed, total)) in &tally {
        eprintln!("{bucket:40} {passed:5} / {total}");
    }
    if verbose {
        for failure in &failures {
            eprintln!("  {failure}");
        }
    }

    // Everything that doesn't depend on an external entity has to do what the suite says.
    for bucket in ["not-wf", "valid", "invalid"] {
        let (passed, total) = tally[bucket];
        assert_eq!(passed, total, "{bucket}: run with XMLCONF_VERBOSE=1 for the list");
    }
}

#[test]
fn error_positions() {
    // An error in an entity's text is at the reference to the entity.
    let source = b"<!DOCTYPE a [\n<!ENTITY e '<q:c/>'>\n]>\n<a>\n  <p:b/>\n\n <p:b x='&e;'/><p:c>&e;</p:c>\n<";
    let document = parse(source, Options::default());
    let positions: Vec<(u32, u32, bool)> = document
        .errors
        .iter()
        .map(|error| (error.line, error.column, error.fatal))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        positions,
        [(5, 3, false), (7, 10, true)],
        "{:?}",
        document.errors.iter().map(|error| &error.message).collect::<Vec<_>>()
    );

    let source = b"<a>\n<p:b/>\n\n  <p:c/><p:d>\n&#1;";
    let document = parse(source, Options::default());
    let positions: Vec<(u32, u32, bool)> = document
        .errors
        .iter()
        .map(|error| (error.line, error.column, error.fatal))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(positions, [(2, 1, false), (4, 3, false), (4, 9, false), (5, 1, true)]);
}

#[test]
fn defaulted_attributes_count_as_expansion() {
    let document_with = |attributes: usize, elements: usize| {
        let mut source = String::from("<!DOCTYPE a [\n<!ATTLIST e");
        for index in 0..attributes {
            source.push_str(&format!(" a{index} CDATA '0'"));
        }
        source.push_str(">\n]>\n<a>");
        source.push_str(&"<e/>".repeat(elements));
        source.push_str("</a>");
        source
    };

    // A document that makes modest use of defaults is fine.
    let source = document_with(20, 100);
    assert!(parse(source.as_bytes(), Options::default()).errors.is_empty());

    // One whose elements each get hundreds of attributes they don't spell out grows with the square of its size.
    let source = document_with(500, 2000);
    let document = parse(source.as_bytes(), Options::default());
    let error = document.errors.first().expect("the document is refused");
    assert!(error.fatal);
    assert_eq!(error.message, "Maximum entity amplification factor exceeded");
    assert!(document.tape.len() < 200_000, "{} rows", document.tape.len());

    // So does one whose elements each get a single attribute with a very long name and no value to speak of.
    let source = format!(
        "<!DOCTYPE a [<!ATTLIST e {} CDATA ''>]><a>{}</a>",
        "n".repeat(100_000),
        "<e/>".repeat(10_000)
    );
    let document = parse(source.as_bytes(), Options::default());
    let error = document.errors.first().expect("the document is refused");
    assert_eq!(error.message, "Maximum entity amplification factor exceeded");

    // A message that quotes a name the error isn't at doesn't quote all of a very long one.
    let source = format!("<{} p:a='' p:b=''/>", "e".repeat(100_000));
    let document = parse(source.as_bytes(), Options::default());
    assert_eq!(document.errors.len(), 2);
    assert!(document.errors.iter().all(|error| error.message.len() < 1000));

    // Errors that aren't in the order of their offsets still get their own lines.
    let document = parse(
        b"<!DOCTYPE a SYSTEM 'a.dtd'>\n<a>\n<e a='&b;' p:x=''/>\n<e\n a='&b;' p:x=''/></a>",
        Options::default(),
    );
    let positions: Vec<_> = document.errors.iter().map(|error| (error.line, error.column)).collect();
    assert_eq!(positions, [(3, 7), (3, 1), (5, 5), (4, 1)]);

    // The xml prefix can't be given another namespace by a default either.
    let document = parse(
        b"<!DOCTYPE r [<!ATTLIST r xmlns:xml CDATA 'urn:wrong'>]><r/>",
        Options::default(),
    );
    let errors: Vec<_> = document
        .errors
        .iter()
        .map(|error| (error.message.as_str(), error.fatal))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(errors, [("xml namespace prefix mapped to wrong URI", false)]);

    // An undeclared entity that may be declared where the parser doesn't read is reported, and parsing goes on.
    let document = parse(b"<!DOCTYPE a SYSTEM 'a.dtd'><a>&b;</a>", Options::default());
    let errors: Vec<_> = document
        .errors
        .iter()
        .map(|error| (error.message.as_str(), error.fatal))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(errors, [("Entity 'b' not defined", false)]);
}

// Standalone Rust tests use the test harness allocator without linking the C++ runtime, so crates only depend on this
// one through an "allocator" feature that the CMake build enables.
#![cfg(not(test))]

use std::alloc::GlobalAlloc;
use std::alloc::Layout;

// Keep allocator selection in AK, including overrides used for memory profiling.
/// cbindgen:ignore
mod ffi {
    unsafe extern "C" {
        pub(super) fn ladybird_alloc(size: usize, alignment: usize) -> *mut u8;
        pub(super) fn ladybird_alloc_zeroed(size: usize, alignment: usize) -> *mut u8;
        pub(super) fn ladybird_realloc(pointer: *mut u8, old_size: usize, new_size: usize, alignment: usize)
        -> *mut u8;
        pub(super) fn ladybird_dealloc(pointer: *mut u8, alignment: usize);
    }
}

use ffi::{ladybird_alloc, ladybird_alloc_zeroed, ladybird_dealloc, ladybird_realloc};

struct LadybirdAllocator;

#[global_allocator]
static LADYBIRD_ALLOCATOR: LadybirdAllocator = LadybirdAllocator;

unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for LadybirdAllocator {
    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        unsafe { ladybird_alloc(layout.size(), layout.align()) }
    }

    unsafe fn alloc_zeroed(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        unsafe { ladybird_alloc_zeroed(layout.size(), layout.align()) }
    }

    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, pointer: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
        unsafe { ladybird_dealloc(pointer, layout.align()) };
    }

    unsafe fn realloc(&self, pointer: *mut u8, layout: Layout, new_size: usize) -> *mut u8 {
        unsafe { ladybird_realloc(pointer, layout.size(), new_size, layout.align()) }
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
