# The members of an interface implemented in Rust, as the Rust bindings handle them: which attributes and operations
# the implementation has methods for and what those methods are called. Everything that asks about the members of such
# an interface asks here, so that what the checks accept, what the definitions are collected from and what the writer
# emits cannot differ. A member that the Rust bindings do not handle is an error that names it.

import re

from dataclasses import dataclass
from dataclasses import field
from typing import List
from typing import Optional
from typing import Union

from Generators.libweb_bindings.overload_resolution import operation_length
from Generators.libweb_bindings.overload_resolution import operation_overload_sets
from Generators.libweb_bindings.overload_resolution import parameter_list_length
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_names import rust_identifier
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import INTEGER_TYPES
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import UnsupportedByRustBindings
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import idl_integer_value
from Utils.webidl_parser import Attribute
from Utils.webidl_parser import Constructor
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLType
from Utils.webidl_parser import Interface
from Utils.webidl_parser import Operation
from Utils.webidl_parser import OperationParameter
from Utils.webidl_parser import SpecialOperation

RUST_METHOD_NAME = re.compile(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_]*")

# The extended attributes of the members of an interface that the Rust bindings handle.
# NB: The context of an attribute or an operation that is [NeedsCallerRealm] has the current realm, not the realm of
#     the object.
SUPPORTED_ATTRIBUTE_EXTENDED_ATTRIBUTES = {
    "AttributeCallbackName",
    "CachedAccessor",
    "CEReactions",
    "Exposed",
    "FIXME",
    "ImplementedAs",
    "LegacyNullToEmptyString",
    "NeedsCallerRealm",
    "NewObject",
    "PutForwards",
    "ReturnsJSValue",
    "SameObject",
    "SecureContext",
}
SUPPORTED_OPERATION_EXTENDED_ATTRIBUTES = {
    "CreatesPromise",
    "CEReactions",
    "Default",
    "Exposed",
    "FIXME",
    "ImplementedAs",
    "NeedsCallerRealm",
    "NewObject",
    "SameObject",
    "SecureContext",
}
SUPPORTED_STRINGIFIER_EXTENDED_ATTRIBUTES = {"Exposed"}

# The values of [Exposed] that the Rust bindings handle on a member, without spaces, with the condition on the realm
# under which the member is exposed.
MEMBER_EXPOSURE_CONDITIONS = {
    "Window": "realm_is_window(realm)",
    "(Window,Worker)": "window_or_worker_global_scope_from_global_object(realm.global_object()).is_some()",
}


def member_exposure_condition(extended_attributes: dict) -> Optional[str]:
    """The condition on the realm under which a member is exposed, if it names the globals that expose it."""
    exposure = extended_attributes.get("Exposed")
    if exposure is None:
        return None
    return MEMBER_EXPOSURE_CONDITIONS.get(exposure.replace(" ", ""))


def generated_function_stem(method: str) -> str:
    """What the names of the generated functions of a member start with: the method without what makes a reserved
    name usable as an identifier, which a longer name does not need."""
    return method.removeprefix("r#").removesuffix("_")


@dataclass
class RustAttribute:
    attribute: Attribute
    # The method of the implementation that the getter calls.
    getter_method: str
    # The method of the implementation that the setter calls, for an attribute that is not read only. An event handler
    # IDL attribute has one only when the IDL names it with [ImplementedAs]: the setter of an interface that does more
    # than set the event handler, which the method does itself.
    setter_method: Optional[str]
    # The event type of an event handler IDL attribute, whose getter and setter work on the C++ EventTarget that the
    # object owns: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#event-handler-idl-attributes
    event_type: Optional[str] = None

    @property
    def put_forwards(self) -> Optional[str]:
        """The attribute of the attribute's value that the setter of a read only attribute forwards to: [PutForwards],
        https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#PutForwards"""
        return self.attribute.extended_attributes.get("PutForwards")

    @property
    def is_cached(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the getter returns the same value for as long as the object lives, which the engine then caches on
        the object: [CachedAccessor]."""
        return "CachedAccessor" in self.attribute.extended_attributes

    @property
    def returns_js_value(self) -> bool:
        return "ReturnsJSValue" in self.attribute.extended_attributes

    @property
    def exposure_condition(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return member_exposure_condition(self.attribute.extended_attributes)

    @property
    def function_stem(self) -> str:
        """What the generated native functions are named after. [AttributeCallbackName] tells apart the attributes that
        name the same methods."""
        callback_name = self.attribute.extended_attributes.get("AttributeCallbackName")
        return callback_name or generated_function_stem(self.getter_method)

    @property
    def getter_function(self) -> str:
        """The generated native function of the getter."""
        return f"{self.function_stem}_getter"

    @property
    def setter_function(self) -> str:
        """The generated native function of the setter."""
        return f"{self.function_stem}_setter"


@dataclass
class RustOperation:
    operation: Operation
    # The method of the implementation that the steps of the operation call, which the implementation does not define
    # for a [Default] toJSON operation: the bindings run the default toJSON steps instead,
    # https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#default-tojson-steps
    method: str
    omitted_parameter: Optional[OperationParameter] = None
    omitted_parameter_index: Optional[int] = None
    implementation_parameters: Optional[List[OperationParameter]] = None

    @property
    def length(self) -> int:
        return operation_length(self.operation)

    @property
    def is_default_to_json(self) -> bool:
        return "Default" in self.operation.extended_attributes

    @property
    def steps_function(self) -> str:
        """The generated function of the steps of the operation, when the operation is one of several overloads that
        the function of the prototype chooses between."""
        suffix = f"_{len(self.operation.parameters)}" if self.omitted_parameter is not None else ""
        return f"{generated_function_stem(self.method)}{suffix}_steps"


@dataclass
class RustOperationSet:
    """The operations of an interface that share an identifier, which are one function of the prototype."""

    name: str
    overloads: List[RustOperation]

    @property
    def function(self) -> str:
        """The generated native function that the prototype holds."""
        return f"{generated_function_stem(rust_identifier(self.name))}_function"

    @property
    def length(self) -> int:
        return min(overload.length for overload in self.overloads)

    @property
    def is_secure_context_only(self) -> bool:
        return "SecureContext" in self.overloads[0].operation.extended_attributes

    @property
    def exposure_condition(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return member_exposure_condition(self.overloads[0].operation.extended_attributes)


@dataclass
class RustStringifier:
    """The stringifier of an interface, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-stringifier: an operation, which the
    implementation runs through its method to_string, or an attribute, whose getter method it runs."""

    # The condition on the realm under which the stringifier is exposed, if it names the globals that expose it.
    exposure_condition: Optional[str]
    # The getter method of the attribute, for a stringifier that is an attribute.
    attribute_getter_method: Optional[str] = None

    function = "to_string_function"

    @property
    def method(self) -> str:
        return self.attribute_getter_method or "to_string"

    @property
    def defines_method(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the implementation has a method for the stringifier of its own, rather than an attribute getter."""
        return self.attribute_getter_method is None


@dataclass
class RustIndexedPropertyGetter:
    """The indexed property getter of an interface, which has an identifier: the operation of that identifier, whose
    method the getter steps of a supported property index call as well, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-indexed-properties
    An index for which a nullable method returns nothing is not a supported property index, nor is an index that is not
    less than the length attribute of an interface whose method does not return a nullable type. An unnamed getter
    defines no operation, and the method of the implementation is item() unless the IDL names it."""

    operation: RustOperation
    # The getter of the length attribute of the interface.
    length_method: str
    # Whether the interface declares a value iterator, which it implements through the indexed properties,
    # https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-value-iterator
    has_value_iterator: bool


@dataclass
class RustIndexedPropertySetter:
    """The unnamed indexed property setter of an interface, whose steps the implementation defines as the methods
    set_value_of_new_indexed_property() and set_value_of_existing_indexed_property(),
    https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#legacy-platform-object-set"""

    value_parameter: OperationParameter


@dataclass
class RustNamedProperties:
    """The named property getter of an interface and its named property setter and deleter, if it has them,
    https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-named-properties. One declared with an identifier is the operation of that
    identifier, whose method the legacy platform object algorithms call as well. The implementation defines the steps of
    one declared without an identifier as the methods determine_value_of_named_property(),
    set_value_of_new_named_property() and set_value_of_existing_named_property(), or delete_existing_named_property().
    The implementation gives its supported property names through its method supported_property_names()."""

    getter: RustOperation
    setter: Optional[RustOperation]
    deleter: Optional[RustOperation]

    @property
    def operations(self) -> List[RustOperation]:
        """The operations declared with an identifier, which the interface prototype object holds as well."""
        return [
            operation
            for operation in (self.getter, self.setter, self.deleter)
            if operation is not None and operation.operation.name
        ]


@dataclass
class RustPairIterator:
    """The pair iterator of an interface, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-pair-iterator, whose value pairs to
    iterate over the implementation gives through its implementation of PairIterable."""

    key_type: IDLType
    value_type: IDLType

    # The names of the functions that the interface prototype object holds, in the order of the C++ bindings.
    function_names = ["entries", "forEach", "keys", "values"]


@dataclass
class RustSetlike:
    """The setlike declaration of an interface, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-setlike. The names say which
    operations of a read-write declaration the bindings define, as the interface can declare them itself."""

    value_type: IDLType
    writable_operations: list[str]

    function_names = ["size", "entries", "values", "keys", "forEach", "has"]


@dataclass
class RustMaplike:
    """The maplike declaration of an interface, whose keys are strings, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-maplike.
    The names say which operations of a read-write declaration the bindings define, as the interface can declare them
    itself."""

    value_type: IDLType
    writable_operations: list[str]

    function_names = ["size", "entries", "keys", "values", "forEach", "get", "has"]


@dataclass
class RustAsyncIterator:
    """The value asynchronously iterable declaration of an interface, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-async-iterable,
    whose asynchronous iterator initialization steps the implementation runs through its method
    asynchronous_iterator_initialization_steps, and whose other steps it gives through its implementation of
    AsyncIterable."""

    parameters: List[OperationParameter]
    # Whether the asynchronous iterator prototype object has a "return" method: [DefinesAsyncIteratorReturn].
    defines_return: bool

    function = "values_function"
    method = "asynchronous_iterator_initialization_steps"

    @property
    def length(self) -> int:
        return parameter_list_length(self.parameters)


@dataclass
class RustConstant:
    name: str
    value: int


@dataclass
class RustConstructor:
    constructor: Constructor
    # The method of the implementation that the steps of the constructor call. The constructors of an overloaded set
    # name theirs in the IDL.
    method: str
    # The generated function of the steps of the constructor. The function `construct` is what the entry point of a
    # construction calls: the steps of the only constructor, or the choice between the overloads.
    steps_function: str

    @property
    def length(self) -> int:
        return parameter_list_length(self.constructor.parameters)


@dataclass
class RustMembers:
    # The attributes and the operations that the implementation has methods for.
    attributes: List[RustAttribute] = field(default_factory=list)
    # The static attributes, which the interface object has.
    static_attributes: List[RustAttribute] = field(default_factory=list)
    operation_sets: List[RustOperationSet] = field(default_factory=list)
    # The static operations, which the interface object has.
    static_operation_sets: List[RustOperationSet] = field(default_factory=list)
    stringifier: Optional[RustStringifier] = None
    indexed_property_getter: Optional[RustIndexedPropertyGetter] = None
    indexed_property_setter: Optional[RustIndexedPropertySetter] = None
    named_properties: Optional[RustNamedProperties] = None
    pair_iterator: Optional[RustPairIterator] = None
    setlike: Optional[RustSetlike] = None
    maplike: Optional[RustMaplike] = None
    async_iterator: Optional[RustAsyncIterator] = None
    constructors: List[RustConstructor] = field(default_factory=list)
    constants: List[RustConstant] = field(default_factory=list)
    # The regular attributes in the order of the IDL, as the prototype defines them: an attribute of `attributes`, or
    # the identifier of one marked [FIXME].
    attributes_in_order: List[Union[RustAttribute, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    # The identifiers of the operations marked [FIXME] that have no implemented overload, each once.
    unimplemented_operation_names: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def constructor_length(self) -> int:
        if not self.constructors:
            return 0
        return min(constructor.length for constructor in self.constructors)

    def property_names(self) -> List[str]:
        """The identifiers of the members that the interface prototype object has a property for, in the order of
        their definition."""
        names = [attribute.attribute.name for attribute in self.attributes]
        names.extend(operation_set.name for operation_set in self.operation_sets)
        if self.stringifier is not None:
            names.append("toString")
        if self.indexed_property_getter is not None and self.indexed_property_getter.operation.operation.name:
            names.append(self.indexed_property_getter.operation.operation.name)
        if self.pair_iterator is not None:
            names.extend(self.pair_iterator.function_names)
        if self.setlike is not None:
            names.extend(self.setlike.function_names + self.setlike.writable_operations)
        if self.maplike is not None:
            names.extend(self.maplike.function_names + self.maplike.writable_operations)
        if self.async_iterator is not None:
            names.append("values")
        names.extend(constant.name for constant in self.constants)
        return names

    def unimplemented_property_names(self) -> List[str]:
        """The identifiers of the members that the interface prototype object records as not implemented."""
        names = [attribute for attribute in self.attributes_in_order if isinstance(attribute, str)]
        names.extend(self.unimplemented_operation_names)
        return names


def rust_members(interface: Interface) -> RustMembers:
    """Raises an error that names the member for every member that the Rust bindings do not handle yet."""

    def fail(message: str) -> None:
        raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(f"{interface.path}: {interface.name} is [ImplementedIn=Rust], but {message}")

    def check_extended_attributes(member_name: str, extended_attributes: dict, supported: set) -> None:
        unsupported = set(extended_attributes) - supported
        if unsupported:
            fail(f"the Rust bindings do not handle the extended attributes {sorted(unsupported)} of {member_name}")

    def method_of(member_name: str, extended_attributes: dict) -> str:
        """The method of the implementation for a member, which the IDL can name with [ImplementedAs]."""
        method = extended_attributes.get("ImplementedAs")
        if method is None:
            return rust_identifier(member_name)
        if not RUST_METHOD_NAME.fullmatch(method):
            fail(f"[ImplementedAs={method}] of {member_name} does not name a Rust method")
        return rust_identifier(method)

    def event_handler_attribute(attribute: Attribute) -> RustAttribute:
        """An event handler IDL attribute, which the bindings get and set on the EventTarget that the object owns. The
        IDL names the method of its setter with [ImplementedAs] when the interface's setter does more than set the
        event handler."""
        if attribute.readonly or not attribute.name.startswith("on"):
            fail(f"its event handler IDL attribute {attribute.name} is not a plain attribute named on<event type>")
        check_extended_attributes(
            attribute.name, attribute.extended_attributes, {"Exposed", "ImplementedAs", "SecureContext"}
        )
        check_exposure(attribute.name, attribute.extended_attributes)
        setter_method = None
        if "ImplementedAs" in attribute.extended_attributes:
            setter_method = method_of(attribute.name, attribute.extended_attributes)
        event_type = attribute.name.removeprefix("on")
        return RustAttribute(attribute, rust_identifier(attribute.name), setter_method, event_type)

    if interface.async_iterable is not None and interface.async_iterable.key_type is not None:
        fail("it has a pair asynchronously iterable declaration")
    has_value_iterator = interface.iterable is not None and interface.iterable.key_type is None

    members = RustMembers()
    if interface.async_iterable is not None:
        members.async_iterator = RustAsyncIterator(
            interface.async_iterable.parameters, "DefinesAsyncIteratorReturn" in interface.extended_attributes
        )
    if interface.iterable is not None and interface.iterable.key_type is not None:
        members.pair_iterator = RustPairIterator(interface.iterable.key_type, interface.iterable.value_type)

    def writable_operations(declaration, names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        """The operations of a read-write declaration that the interface does not declare itself."""
        if declaration.readonly:
            return []
        declared = set(operation_overload_sets(interface))
        return [name for name in names if name not in declared]

    if interface.setlike is not None:
        members.setlike = RustSetlike(
            interface.setlike.value_type, writable_operations(interface.setlike, ["add", "delete", "clear"])
        )
    if interface.maplike is not None:
        if interface.maplike.key_type.name not in ("DOMString", "CSSOMString"):
            fail("its maplike declaration has keys that are not strings")
        members.maplike = RustMaplike(
            interface.maplike.value_type, writable_operations(interface.maplike, ["set", "delete", "clear"])
        )

    getter = interface.indexed_property_getter
    if has_value_iterator and getter is None:
        fail("it declares a value iterator and supports no indexed properties")
    if getter is not None:
        length_attribute = next(
            (attribute for attribute in interface.regular_attributes if attribute.name == "length"), None
        )
        if length_attribute is None:
            fail("it supports indexed properties and has no length attribute")
        assert length_attribute is not None
        check_extended_attributes(getter.name, getter.extended_attributes, {"ImplementedAs"})
        getter_operation = Operation(getter.name, getter.return_type, getter.parameters, getter.extended_attributes)
        members.indexed_property_getter = RustIndexedPropertyGetter(
            RustOperation(getter_operation, method_of(getter.name or "item", getter.extended_attributes)),
            method_of(length_attribute.name, length_attribute.extended_attributes),
            has_value_iterator,
        )

    setter = interface.indexed_property_setter
    if setter is not None:
        if getter is None:
            fail("it has an indexed property setter and no indexed property getter")
        if setter.name:
            fail("its indexed property setter has an identifier, which the Rust bindings do not handle yet")
        members.indexed_property_setter = RustIndexedPropertySetter(setter.parameters[1])

    def named_property_operation(
        special_operation: Optional[SpecialOperation], kind: str, anonymous_method: str
    ) -> Optional[RustOperation]:
        if special_operation is None:
            return None
        operation = Operation(
            special_operation.name,
            special_operation.return_type,
            special_operation.parameters,
            special_operation.extended_attributes,
        )
        if not special_operation.name:
            supported = set() if kind == "getter" else {"CEReactions"}
            check_extended_attributes(f"its named property {kind}", special_operation.extended_attributes, supported)
            return RustOperation(operation, anonymous_method)
        check_extended_attributes(special_operation.name, special_operation.extended_attributes, {"ImplementedAs"})
        return RustOperation(operation, method_of(special_operation.name, special_operation.extended_attributes))

    named_getter = named_property_operation(
        interface.named_property_getter, "getter", "determine_value_of_named_property"
    )
    # NB: An anonymous setter has two methods, set_value_of_new_named_property() and
    #     set_value_of_existing_named_property(), which the bindings name themselves.
    named_setter = named_property_operation(interface.named_property_setter, "setter", "")
    named_deleter = named_property_operation(
        interface.named_property_deleter, "deleter", "delete_existing_named_property"
    )
    if named_getter is None and (named_setter is not None or named_deleter is not None):
        fail("it has a named property setter or deleter and no named property getter")
    if named_getter is not None:
        if getter is not None:
            fail("it supports both indexed and named properties, which the Rust bindings do not handle yet")
        if interface.parent_name:
            fail("it supports named properties and inherits from another interface")
        if named_getter.operation.name and not named_getter.operation.return_type.nullable:
            fail(
                "its named property getter has an identifier and does not return a nullable type, by which the Rust "
                "bindings tell the names that are not supported property names"
            )
        if named_deleter is not None and named_deleter.operation.return_type.name != "undefined":
            fail("its named property deleter returns a value, which the Rust bindings do not handle yet")
        members.named_properties = RustNamedProperties(named_getter, named_setter, named_deleter)

    def check_exposure(member_name: str, extended_attributes: dict) -> None:
        exposure = extended_attributes.get("Exposed")
        interface_exposure = interface.extended_attributes.get("Exposed", "")
        if exposure is None or exposure.replace(" ", "") == interface_exposure.replace(" ", ""):
            return
        if exposure.replace(" ", "") not in MEMBER_EXPOSURE_CONDITIONS:
            fail(
                f"{member_name} is [Exposed={exposure}], and the Rust bindings only handle [Exposed=Window], "
                "[Exposed=(Window,Worker)], or the exposure of the interface on members"
            )

    if interface.stringifier is not None:
        stringifier = interface.stringifier
        supported_attributes = SUPPORTED_STRINGIFIER_EXTENDED_ATTRIBUTES
        if stringifier.attribute is not None:
            # The attribute setter handles [CEReactions], including for a stringifier attribute.
            supported_attributes = supported_attributes | {"CEReactions"}
        check_extended_attributes("its stringifier", stringifier.extended_attributes, supported_attributes)
        check_exposure("its stringifier", stringifier.extended_attributes)
        attribute_getter_method = None
        if stringifier.attribute is not None:
            attribute_getter_method = method_of(stringifier.attribute.name, stringifier.attribute.extended_attributes)
        members.stringifier = RustStringifier(
            member_exposure_condition(stringifier.extended_attributes), attribute_getter_method
        )

    constructor_attributes = {"ImplementedAs"} if len(interface.constructors) > 1 else set()
    for constructor in interface.constructors:
        unsupported_attributes = set(constructor.extended_attributes) - constructor_attributes
        if unsupported_attributes:
            fail(
                "the Rust bindings do not handle the extended attributes "
                f"{sorted(unsupported_attributes)} of its constructor"
            )
    if len(interface.constructors) > 1:
        # NB: Rust has no overloading, and a name made up from the position of a constructor in the IDL would swap
        #     two overloads silently when the IDL is reordered, so the IDL names the method of every overload.
        methods = [constructor.extended_attributes.get("ImplementedAs") for constructor in interface.constructors]
        if not all(method is not None and RUST_METHOD_NAME.fullmatch(method) for method in methods):
            fail("its constructors are overloaded, and not all of them name their Rust method with [ImplementedAs]")
        if len(set(methods)) != len(methods):
            fail(f"its constructors name the same Rust method with [ImplementedAs] more than once: {methods}")
        for constructor in interface.constructors:
            method = constructor.extended_attributes["ImplementedAs"]
            members.constructors.append(RustConstructor(constructor, method, f"{method}_steps"))
    else:
        for constructor in interface.constructors:
            members.constructors.append(RustConstructor(constructor, "construct", "construct"))

    for attribute in interface.regular_attributes:
        check_extended_attributes(
            attribute.name, attribute.extended_attributes, SUPPORTED_ATTRIBUTE_EXTENDED_ATTRIBUTES
        )
        check_exposure(attribute.name, attribute.extended_attributes)
        if "FIXME" in attribute.extended_attributes:
            members.attributes_in_order.append(attribute.name)
            continue
        if "CachedAccessor" in attribute.extended_attributes and not attribute.readonly:
            fail(f"its attribute {attribute.name} is [CachedAccessor] and not read only")
        if "PutForwards" in attribute.extended_attributes and not attribute.readonly:
            fail(f"its attribute {attribute.name} is [PutForwards] and not read only")
        if attribute.type.name in ("EventHandler", "EventHandlerNonNull"):
            rust_attribute = event_handler_attribute(attribute)
        else:
            getter_method = method_of(attribute.name, attribute.extended_attributes)
            setter_method = None if attribute.readonly else f"set_{generated_function_stem(getter_method)}"
            rust_attribute = RustAttribute(attribute, getter_method, setter_method)
        members.attributes.append(rust_attribute)
        members.attributes_in_order.append(rust_attribute)

    for attribute in interface.static_attributes:
        check_extended_attributes(
            attribute.name, attribute.extended_attributes, SUPPORTED_ATTRIBUTE_EXTENDED_ATTRIBUTES - {"FIXME"}
        )
        check_exposure(attribute.name, attribute.extended_attributes)
        if not attribute.readonly:
            fail(f"its static attribute {attribute.name} is not read only, which the Rust bindings do not handle yet")
        members.static_attributes.append(
            RustAttribute(attribute, method_of(attribute.name, attribute.extended_attributes), None)
        )

    def operation_sets(static: bool) -> List[RustOperationSet]:
        operations_of_interface = interface.static_operations if static else interface.regular_operations
        for operation in operations_of_interface:
            check_extended_attributes(
                operation.name, operation.extended_attributes, SUPPORTED_OPERATION_EXTENDED_ATTRIBUTES
            )
            if "CreatesPromise" in operation.extended_attributes and (
                not operation.return_type_is_promise() or operation.return_type.nullable
            ):
                fail(f"its operation {operation.name} is [CreatesPromise] but does not return a non-nullable promise")
            check_exposure(operation.name, operation.extended_attributes)
            if "Default" in operation.extended_attributes and (
                static or operation.name != "toJSON" or operation.return_type.name != "object" or operation.parameters
            ):
                fail(
                    f"its operation {operation.name} is [Default], which only a regular toJSON() that returns an object can be"
                )

        sets = []
        # NB: operation_overload_sets() leaves out the operations marked [FIXME], which the prototype records as not
        #     implemented unless another overload of theirs is.
        overload_sets = operation_overload_sets(interface, static=static)
        for name, operations in overload_sets.items():
            if len(operations) > 1:
                # NB: As for constructors, the IDL names the Rust method of every overload.
                if not all("ImplementedAs" in operation.extended_attributes for operation in operations):
                    fail(
                        f"its operation {name} is overloaded, and not all of the overloads name their Rust method with "
                        "[ImplementedAs]"
                    )
                if len({operation.return_type_is_promise() for operation in operations}) > 1:
                    fail(f"some overloads of its operation {name} return a promise type and others do not")
                exposure = {
                    (operation.extended_attributes.get("Exposed"), "SecureContext" in operation.extended_attributes)
                    for operation in operations
                }
                if len(exposure) > 1:
                    fail(f"the overloads of its operation {name} are exposed differently")
            overloads = [
                RustOperation(operation, method_of(name, operation.extended_attributes)) for operation in operations
            ]
            for method in {overload.method for overload in overloads}:
                shared = [overload for overload in overloads if overload.method == method]
                if len(shared) == 1:
                    continue
                if static or len(shared) != 2:
                    fail(f"the overloads sharing the Rust method {method} must differ by one required parameter")
                shorter, longer = sorted(shared, key=lambda overload: len(overload.operation.parameters))
                short_parameters = shorter.operation.parameters
                long_parameters = longer.operation.parameters
                if len(long_parameters) != len(short_parameters) + 1:
                    fail(f"the overloads sharing the Rust method {method} must differ by one required parameter")
                indices = [
                    index
                    for index, parameter in enumerate(long_parameters)
                    if not parameter.optional
                    and not parameter.variadic
                    and long_parameters[:index] + long_parameters[index + 1 :] == short_parameters
                ]
                if len(indices) != 1 or shorter.operation.return_type != longer.operation.return_type:
                    fail(f"the overloads sharing the Rust method {method} must differ by one required parameter")
                index = indices[0]
                for overload in shared:
                    overload.omitted_parameter = long_parameters[index]
                    overload.omitted_parameter_index = index
                    overload.implementation_parameters = long_parameters
            sets.append(RustOperationSet(name, overloads))
        if static and any("FIXME" in operation.extended_attributes for operation in operations_of_interface):
            fail("it has static operations marked [FIXME], which the Rust bindings do not record yet")
        if not static:
            for operation in operations_of_interface:
                is_unimplemented = "FIXME" in operation.extended_attributes and operation.name not in overload_sets
                if is_unimplemented and operation.name not in members.unimplemented_operation_names:
                    members.unimplemented_operation_names.append(operation.name)
        return sets

    members.operation_sets = operation_sets(static=False)
    if members.named_properties is not None:
        members.operation_sets.extend(
            RustOperationSet(operation.operation.name, [operation]) for operation in members.named_properties.operations
        )
    members.static_operation_sets = operation_sets(static=True)

    for constant in interface.constants:
        value = idl_integer_value(constant.value, constant.type.name) if constant.type.name in INTEGER_TYPES else None
        if value is None:
            fail(f"its constant {constant.name} is not an integer of the type {constant.type}")
        else:
            members.constants.append(RustConstant(constant.name, value))

    # NB: The spellings of a CSS descriptor or property are attributes with the same steps, which name the same methods.
    attribute_methods = {attribute.getter_method for attribute in members.attributes if attribute.event_type is None}
    attribute_methods.update(attribute.getter_method for attribute in members.static_attributes)
    attribute_methods.update(
        attribute.setter_method for attribute in members.attributes if attribute.setter_method is not None
    )
    methods = sorted(attribute_methods)
    methods.extend(
        method
        for operation_set in members.operation_sets + members.static_operation_sets
        for method in {overload.method for overload in operation_set.overloads if not overload.is_default_to_json}
    )
    if members.stringifier is not None and members.stringifier.defines_method:
        methods.append(members.stringifier.method)
    if members.indexed_property_getter is not None:
        methods.append(members.indexed_property_getter.operation.method)
    if members.indexed_property_setter is not None:
        methods.extend(["set_value_of_new_indexed_property", "set_value_of_existing_indexed_property"])
    methods.extend(constructor.method for constructor in members.constructors)
    repeated_methods = sorted({method for method in methods if methods.count(method) > 1})
    if repeated_methods:
        fail(f"more than one of its members has the Rust method {repeated_methods}")

    return members

# Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

# The Rust names of IDL identifiers, for the Rust bindings of the interfaces implemented in Rust.

from Utils.utils import title_case_to_snake_case

RUST_KEYWORDS = {
    "as", "async", "await", "break", "const", "continue", "crate", "dyn", "else", "enum", "extern", "false", "fn", "for",
    "if", "impl", "in", "let", "loop", "match", "mod", "move", "mut", "pub", "ref", "return", "self", "static",
    "struct", "super", "trait", "true", "type", "unsafe", "use", "where", "while", "abstract", "become", "box", "do",
    "final", "gen", "macro", "override", "priv", "try", "typeof", "unsized", "virtual", "yield",
}  # fmt: skip

# Names that Rust does not accept as raw identifiers either.
RUST_RESERVED_NAMES = {"self", "Self", "crate", "super"}


def rust_identifier(name: str) -> str:
    identifier = title_case_to_snake_case(name).replace("-", "_")
    if identifier in RUST_RESERVED_NAMES:
        return f"{identifier}_"
    if identifier in RUST_KEYWORDS:
        return f"r#{identifier}"
    return identifier


def rust_local_name(name: str) -> str:
    """The local variable that holds the IDL value of a parameter, which never clashes with the generated ones."""
    return f"idl_{rust_identifier(name).removeprefix('r#')}"

FILE: Meta/Generators/libweb_bindings/rust_overloads.py
# Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

# The choice between the overloads of a constructor or of an operation of an interface implemented in Rust, with the
# overload resolution algorithm, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-overload-resolution-algorithm
#
# The C++ bindings pass the effective overload set to WebIDL::resolve_overload() of
# Libraries/LibWeb/WebIDL/OverloadResolution.cpp, which tests the argument at the distinguishing index against the
# types of the overloads when it runs. The types are known here, so the Rust bindings get only the tests that can
# select an overload, in the order of that function and with its results, including where it differs from the
# algorithm. The steps below follow it one by one; a change to either has to be made to both.

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Callable
from typing import List
from typing import Optional
from typing import Sequence
from typing import TextIO
from typing import Union

from Generators.libweb_bindings.context import GenerationContext
from Generators.libweb_bindings.overload_resolution import EffectiveOverloadItem
from Generators.libweb_bindings.overload_resolution import Optionality
from Generators.libweb_bindings.overload_resolution import compute_the_effective_overload_set
from Generators.libweb_bindings.overload_resolution import resolve_distinguishing_argument_index
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import TYPED_ARRAY_NAMES
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import UnsupportedByRustBindings
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import cpp_interface
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import cpp_interface_name_constant
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_interface
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_interface_path
from Utils.webidl_parser import Constructor
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLParameterizedType
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLType
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLUnionType
from Utils.webidl_parser import Interface
from Utils.webidl_parser import Operation

STRING_TYPES = {"ByteString", "CSSOMString", "DOMString", "USVString"}
INTEGER_TYPES = {
    "byte",
    "octet",
    "short",
    "unsigned short",
    "long",
    "unsigned long",
    "long long",
    "unsigned long long",
}
FLOATING_POINT_TYPES = {"float", "double", "unrestricted float", "unrestricted double"}


# What an entry of the effective overload set makes a step do: nothing, select the entry, or select it if a
# condition on the argument holds, which is a Rust expression.
NO_MATCH = None
ALWAYS = ""


@dataclass
class OverloadResolutionStep:
    description: str
    # The test of the argument at the distinguishing index, or None for a step that every argument reaches.
    argument_test: Optional[str]
    # Whether an entry of the effective overload set with the type and the optionality at the distinguishing index
    # makes the step select the entry: NO_MATCH, ALWAYS, or the condition on the argument under which it does.
    entry_condition: Callable[[IDLType, Optionality], Optional[str]]


def is_plain(idl_type: IDLType) -> bool:
    return not isinstance(idl_type, (IDLUnionType, IDLParameterizedType))


def is_sequence(idl_type: IDLType) -> bool:
    return isinstance(idl_type, IDLParameterizedType) and idl_type.name == "sequence"


def type_and_flattened_members(idl_type: IDLType) -> List[IDLType]:
    """The types that has_overload_with_argument_type_or_subtype_matching() of OverloadResolution.cpp tests for one
    entry."""
    if isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType):
        return [idl_type, *idl_type.flattened_member_types()]
    return [idl_type]


def type_or_flattened_member_matches(idl_type: IDLType, matches: Callable[[IDLType], bool]) -> bool:
    return any(matches(member_type) for member_type in type_and_flattened_members(idl_type))


def overload_resolution_steps(context: GenerationContext) -> List[OverloadResolutionStep]:
    """The sub-steps of step 12 of the algorithm that resolve_overload() runs, in its order."""

    def is_dictionary(idl_type: IDLType) -> bool:
        return is_plain(idl_type) and context.dictionary(idl_type) is not None

    def is_string(idl_type: IDLType) -> bool:
        return is_plain(idl_type) and (idl_type.name in STRING_TYPES or context.enumeration(idl_type) is not None)

    def is_numeric(idl_type: IDLType) -> bool:
        return is_plain(idl_type) and idl_type.name in INTEGER_TYPES | FLOATING_POINT_TYPES

    def is_named(name: str) -> Callable[[IDLType], bool]:
        return lambda idl_type: is_plain(idl_type) and idl_type.name == name

    is_object = is_named("object")

    def nullable_or_dictionary(idl_type: IDLType) -> bool:
        if idl_type.nullable or is_dictionary(idl_type):
            return True
        # NB: resolve_overload() asks whether the union is a dictionary for each of its members, where the algorithm
        #     asks whether the member is one, so a dictionary inside a union does not match here.
        if isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType):
            return any(member_type.nullable for member_type in idl_type.flattened_member_types())
        return False

    def when(matches: bool) -> Optional[str]:
        return ALWAYS if matches else NO_MATCH

    def with_members(matches: Callable[[IDLType], bool]) -> Callable[[IDLType, Optionality], Optional[str]]:
        return lambda idl_type, _: when(type_or_flattened_member_matches(idl_type, matches))

    def implemented_interface(idl_type: IDLType, _: Optionality) -> Optional[str]:
        """The condition under which the platform object that the argument is implements an interface of the type."""
        if type_or_flattened_member_matches(idl_type, is_object):
            return ALWAYS
        tests = []
        for member_type in type_and_flattened_members(idl_type):
            if not is_plain(member_type):
                continue
            interface = cpp_interface(member_type, context)
            if interface is not None:
                tests.append(f"implements_cpp_interface(value.as_object(), {cpp_interface_name_constant(interface)})")
            interface = rust_interface(member_type, context)
            if interface is not None:
                wrapper_class = f"<{rust_interface_path(interface)}>::wrapper_class()"
                tests.append(f"is_host_instance_of(&value.as_object(), {wrapper_class})")
        return "\n                        || ".join(tests) if tests else NO_MATCH

    def typed_array_of_kind(idl_type: IDLType, _: Optionality) -> Optional[str]:
        """The condition under which the typed array that the argument is has the name of a typed array type of the
        type."""
        if type_or_flattened_member_matches(idl_type, is_object):
            return ALWAYS
        names = [
            member_type.name
            for member_type in type_and_flattened_members(idl_type)
            if is_plain(member_type) and member_type.name in TYPED_ARRAY_NAMES
        ]
        if not names:
            return NO_MATCH
        if set(names) == TYPED_ARRAY_NAMES:
            return ALWAYS
        kinds = " | ".join(f"TypedArrayKind::{name}" for name in names)
        return (
            "value.as_object().downcast::<TypedArrayBase>()"
            f".is_some_and(|typed_array| matches!(typed_array.kind(), {kinds}))"
        )

    return [
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "The argument is undefined, and an overload has an optional argument there.",
            "value.is_undefined()",
            lambda _, optionality: when(optionality == Optionality.Optional),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "The argument is null or undefined, and an overload takes a nullable type or a dictionary there.",
            "value.is_nullish()",
            lambda idl_type, _: when(nullable_or_dictionary(idl_type)),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "The argument is a platform object, and an overload takes object or an interface that it implements there.",
            "value.is_object() && value.as_object().is_platform_object()",
            implemented_interface,
        ),
        # NB: resolve_overload() takes a SharedArrayBuffer for an ArrayBuffer here, which the conversion of the
        #     argument then rejects.
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "The argument is an ArrayBuffer, and an overload takes that type or object there.",
            "value.is_object() && value.as_object().downcast::<ArrayBuffer>().is_some()",
            with_members(lambda idl_type: is_named("ArrayBuffer")(idl_type) or is_object(idl_type)),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "The argument is a DataView, and an overload takes that type or object there.",
            "value.is_object() && value.as_object().downcast::<DataView>().is_some()",
            with_members(lambda idl_type: is_named("DataView")(idl_type) or is_object(idl_type)),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "The argument is a typed array, and an overload takes a typed array with its name or object there.",
            "value.is_object() && value.as_object().downcast::<TypedArrayBase>().is_some()",
            typed_array_of_kind,
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "The argument is callable, and an overload takes object there.",
            "value.is_function()",
            with_members(is_object),
        ),
        # NB: resolve_overload() takes an argument whose @@iterator getter throws for one without the method, where
        #     the algorithm rethrows.
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "The argument is an object with an @@iterator method, and an overload takes a sequence there.",
            "value.is_object() && iterator_method(vm, value).is_ok_and(|method| method.is_some())",
            with_members(is_sequence),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "The argument is an object, and an overload takes a dictionary or object there.",
            "value.is_object()",
            with_members(lambda idl_type: is_dictionary(idl_type) or is_object(idl_type)),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "The argument is a Boolean, and an overload takes a boolean there.",
            "value.is_boolean()",
            with_members(is_named("boolean")),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "The argument is a Number, and an overload takes a numeric type there.",
            "value.is_number()",
            with_members(is_numeric),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "The argument is a BigInt, and an overload takes a bigint there.",
            "value.is_bigint()",
            with_members(is_named("bigint")),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "An overload takes a string type there.",
            None,
            with_members(is_string),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "An overload takes a numeric type there.",
            None,
            with_members(is_numeric),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "An overload takes a boolean there.",
            None,
            with_members(is_named("boolean")),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "An overload takes a bigint there.",
            None,
            with_members(is_named("bigint")),
        ),
        OverloadResolutionStep(
            "An overload takes any there.",
            None,
            lambda idl_type, _: when(is_named("any")(idl_type)),
        ),
    ]


def check_type_at_distinguishing_index(idl_type: IDLType, context: GenerationContext, what: str) -> None:
    """Rejects the types that the steps of resolve_overload() which are not written out here would take an argument
    for."""
    member_types = idl_type.flattened_member_types() if isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType) else [idl_type]
    for member_type in member_types:
        handled = (
            is_sequence(member_type)
            or is_plain(member_type)
            and (
                context.dictionary(member_type) is not None
                or context.enumeration(member_type) is not None
                or cpp_interface(member_type, context) is not None
                or rust_interface(member_type, context) is not None
                or member_type.name in STRING_TYPES | INTEGER_TYPES | FLOATING_POINT_TYPES | TYPED_ARRAY_NAMES
                or member_type.name in ("boolean", "bigint", "any", "object", "ArrayBuffer", "DataView")
            )
        )
        if not handled:
            raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(
                f"{what} are told apart by an argument of the type {idl_type}, and the Rust bindings do not resolve "
                f"overloads by the type {member_type} yet"
            )


def write_resolution_at_distinguishing_index(
    out: TextIO,
    context: GenerationContext,
    interface: Interface,
    entries: List[EffectiveOverloadItem],
    argument_count: int,
    call_for: Callable[[int], str],
    what: str,
) -> None:
    index = resolve_distinguishing_argument_index(interface, entries, argument_count, context)
    for entry in entries:
        check_type_at_distinguishing_index(entry.types[index], context, what)
    out.write(f"                let value = vm.argument({index});\n")
    for step in overload_resolution_steps(context):
        # NB: The first entry that a step matches is the one that it keeps. An entry that only matches under a
        #     condition on the argument leaves the entries after it to the step when the condition does not hold.
        selections = []
        for entry in entries:
            condition = step.entry_condition(entry.types[index], entry.optionality_values[index])
            if condition is NO_MATCH:
                continue
            selections.append((condition, call_for(entry.callable_id)))
            if condition == ALWAYS:
                break
        if not selections:
            continue
        if step.argument_test is None:
            assert selections[0][0] == ALWAYS
            out.write(f"                // {step.description}\n                {selections[0][1]}\n")
            return
        if selections[0][0] == ALWAYS:
            out.write(
                f"""                // {step.description}
                if {step.argument_test} {{
                    return {selections[0][1]};
                }}
"""
            )
            continue
        if len(selections) == 1:
            condition, call = selections[0]
            condition = f"({condition})" if "||" in condition else condition
            out.write(
                f"""                // {step.description}
                if {step.argument_test} && {condition} {{
                    return {call};
                }}
"""
            )
            continue
        out.write(f"                // {step.description}\n                if {step.argument_test} {{\n")
        for condition, call in selections:
            if condition == ALWAYS:
                out.write(f"                    return {call};\n")
            else:
                out.write(
                    f"""                    if {condition} {{
                        return {call};
                    }}
"""
                )
        out.write("                }\n")
    out.write("                vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::OverloadResolutionFailed, &[])\n")


def write_overload_resolution(
    out: TextIO,
    context: GenerationContext,
    interface: Interface,
    overloads: Sequence[Union[Constructor, Operation]],
    signature: str,
    documentation: str,
    call_for: Callable[[int], str],
    what: str,
) -> None:
    """Writes the function with the signature that chooses between the overloads for the arguments of a call.
    `call_for` gives the call of the steps of the overload at a position among the overloads."""
    maximum_argument_count = 0
    entries_by_argument_count: dict[int, List[EffectiveOverloadItem]] = {}
    for entry in compute_the_effective_overload_set(overloads):
        maximum_argument_count = max(maximum_argument_count, len(entry.types))
        entries_by_argument_count.setdefault(len(entry.types), []).append(entry)

    out.write(
        f"""
{documentation}    {signature} {{
        match vm.argument_count().min({maximum_argument_count}) {{
"""
    )
    for argument_count, entries in sorted(entries_by_argument_count.items()):
        if len(entries) == 1:
            out.write(f"            {argument_count} => {call_for(entries[0].callable_id)},\n")
            continue
        out.write(f"            {argument_count} => {{\n")
        write_resolution_at_distinguishing_index(out, context, interface, entries, argument_count, call_for, what)
        out.write("            }\n")
    out.write(
        """            _ => vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::OverloadResolutionFailed, &[]),
        }
    }
"""
    )


def write_constructor_overload_resolution(
    out: TextIO, context: GenerationContext, interface: Interface, steps_functions: List[str]
) -> None:
    """Writes the function that chooses the constructor for the arguments of a construction. The function of the
    steps of each constructor is named in the order of the constructors of the interface."""
    write_overload_resolution(
        out,
        context,
        interface,
        interface.constructors,
        "fn construct(vm: &Vm, new_target: Gc<Object>) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value>",
        """    /// Chooses the constructor for the arguments of a construction, with the steps of the overload resolution
    /// algorithm that can select one of the constructors of the interface,
    /// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-overload-resolution-algorithm
""",
        lambda callable_id: f"{steps_functions[callable_id]}(vm, new_target)",
        f"The constructors of {interface.name}",
    )


def write_operation_overload_resolution(
    out: TextIO,
    context: GenerationContext,
    interface: Interface,
    name: str,
    function: str,
    operations: List[Operation],
    steps_functions: List[str],
) -> None:
    """Writes the native function of an overloaded operation, which chooses the overload for the arguments of a call.
    The function of the steps of each overload is named in the order of the overloads. Like the C++ bindings, it does
    not look at the this value, which the steps of the chosen overload check."""
    write_overload_resolution(
        out,
        context,
        interface,
        operations,
        f"fn {function}(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value>",
        f"""    /// Chooses the overload of {name}() for the arguments of a call, with the steps of the overload resolution
    /// algorithm that can select one of them, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-overload-resolution-algorithm
""",
        lambda callable_id: f"{steps_functions[callable_id]}(vm)",
        f"The overloads of {interface.name}.{name}()",
    )

from typing import Dict
from typing import List
from typing import TextIO

from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import is_implemented_in_rust
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_interface_path
from Utils.webidl_parser import Interface

# These strings are persisted in storage records. IDL decoration alone does not mean the wire format supports an interface.
STORAGE_IDENTIFIERS = (
    "Blob",
    "CryptoKey",
    "DOMException",
    "DOMMatrix",
    "DOMMatrixReadOnly",
    "DOMPoint",
    "DOMPointReadOnly",
    "DOMQuad",
    "DOMRect",
    "DOMRectReadOnly",
    "File",
    "FileList",
    "ImageBitmap",
    "ImageData",
    "Module",
    "QuotaExceededError",
)

# The serializable interfaces implemented in C++ whose steps run in Rust.
CPP_INTERFACES_WITH_RUST_STEPS = ("DOMException", "QuotaExceededError", "RTCEncodedAudioFrame")


def write_rust_serializable_dispatch(out: TextIO, interfaces: List[Interface], values: Dict[str, int]) -> None:
    serializable = sorted(
        (interface for interface in interfaces if "Serializable" in interface.extended_attributes),
        key=lambda interface: interface.name,
    )
    rust_interfaces = [interface for interface in serializable if is_implemented_in_rust(interface)]
    out.write(
        """
pub(crate) mod serializable_objects {
    use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Object, Value};
    use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
    use crate::bindings::interface::is_exact_wrapper;
    use crate::bindings::structured_data::{self, SerializationReader, SerializationWriter};
    use crate::html::structured_serialize::serializable::{SerializableRegistryEntry, SerializableSteps};

    const CPP_INTERFACES: &[u16] = &["""
        + ", ".join(str(values[name]) for name in CPP_INTERFACES_WITH_RUST_STEPS)
        + """];

    pub(crate) fn rust_interface_name(object: Gc<Object>) -> Option<u16> {
"""
    )
    for interface in rust_interfaces:
        out.write(
            f"""        if is_exact_wrapper::<{rust_interface_path(interface)}>(object) {{
            return Some({values[interface.name]});
        }}
"""
        )
    out.write(
        """        None
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_cpp_serializable_interface(interface_name: u16) -> bool {
        CPP_INTERFACES.contains(&interface_name)
    }

    pub(crate) fn serialization_steps(
        interface_name: u16,
        cx: &CallContext,
        object: Gc<Object>,
        serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
        for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        match interface_name {
"""
    )
    for interface in rust_interfaces:
        out.write(
            f"            {values[interface.name]} => structured_data::serialization_steps::<{rust_interface_path(interface)}>(cx, object, serialized, for_storage),\n"
        )
    out.write(
        """            _ => unreachable!("the interface is a Rust serializable interface"),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn deserialization_steps(
        interface_name: u16,
        cx: &CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationReader,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        match interface_name {
"""
    )
    for interface in rust_interfaces:
        out.write(
            f"            {values[interface.name]} => structured_data::deserialization_steps::<{rust_interface_path(interface)}>(cx, serialized),\n"
        )
    out.write(
        """            _ => unreachable!("the interface is a Rust serializable interface"),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) const STORAGE_INTERFACES: &[SerializableRegistryEntry] = &[
"""
    )
    for name in STORAGE_IDENTIFIERS:
        out.write(f'        SerializableRegistryEntry {{ interface_name: {values[name]}, identifier: b"{name}" }},\n')
    out.write(
        f"""    ];

    pub(crate) fn serializable_interface_storage_identifier(interface_name: u16) -> Option<&'static [u8]> {{
        STORAGE_INTERFACES.iter().find(|entry| entry.interface_name == interface_name).map(|entry| entry.identifier)
    }}

    pub(crate) fn serializable_interface_name_from_storage_identifier(identifier: &[u8]) -> Option<u16> {{
        STORAGE_INTERFACES.iter().find(|entry| entry.identifier == identifier).map(|entry| entry.interface_name)
    }}

    pub(crate) fn is_ipc_interface(interface_name: u16) -> bool {{
        interface_name == {values["RTCEncodedAudioFrame"]} || serializable_interface_storage_identifier(interface_name).is_some()
    }}

    pub(crate) fn serializable_steps(interface_name: u16) -> SerializableSteps {{
        match interface_name {{
"""
    )
    for name in CPP_INTERFACES_WITH_RUST_STEPS:
        out.write(f"            {values[name]} => SerializableSteps::{name},\n")
    for interface in rust_interfaces:
        out.write(f"            {values[interface.name]} => SerializableSteps::Rust,\n")
    out.write(
        """            _ => unreachable!("the interface has serialization steps"),
        }
    }
}
"""
    )

FILE: Meta/Generators/libweb_bindings/rust_to_idl_value.py
# Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

# The Rust expressions that convert JS values to IDL values, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-type-mapping, for the
# Rust bindings of the interfaces implemented in Rust, as to_idl_value.py writes the C++ ones. The conversions run in
# the order of the C++ bindings and throw their errors, so that an interface behaves the same in either language.

from dataclasses import dataclass
from dataclasses import field
from typing import List
from typing import Optional
from typing import TextIO
from typing import Union

from Generators.libweb_bindings.context import GenerationContext
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_names import rust_identifier
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_names import rust_local_name
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import DECIMAL_LITERAL
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import FLOATING_POINT_TYPES
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import INTEGER_TYPES
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import TYPED_ARRAY_NAMES
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import UnsupportedByRustBindings
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import cpp_interface
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import cpp_interface_name_constant
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import dictionary_holds_sequence_of_cells
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import holds_cells
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import inheriting_interfaces
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import is_callback_interface
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import is_named_union
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import is_promise_type
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import is_record_of_cells
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import is_sequence_of_cells
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import is_unnamed_union_of_cpp_interfaces
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import is_window_proxy
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import member_other_than_undefined
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import resolved_dictionary
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import runtime_union_type
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_any_interface_path
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_dictionary_path
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_enumeration_path
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_enumeration_variant
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_integer_literal
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_interface
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_interface_path
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_type
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_union_path
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import rust_union_variant
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import union_holds_sequence_of_cells
from Generators.libweb_bindings.rust_types import union_member_types
from Utils.webidl_parser import Dictionary
from Utils.webidl_parser import DictionaryMember
from Utils.webidl_parser import Enumeration
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLParameterizedType
from Utils.webidl_parser import IDLType

# NB: CSSOMString is a string type that an implementation chooses, https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#cssomstring-type,
#     and it is a DOMString here, as it is in the C++ bindings.
DOM_STRING_TYPES = ("CSSOMString", "DOMString")
STRING_TYPES = ("ByteString", *DOM_STRING_TYPES, "USVString")


def buffer_source_rules(idl_type: IDLType, parameter_attributes: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    attributes = {**idl_type.extended_attributes, **parameter_attributes}
    allow_shared = "true" if "AllowShared" in attributes else "false"
    allow_resizable = "true" if "AllowResizable" in attributes else "false"
    return f"&BufferSourceRules {{ allow_shared: {allow_shared}, allow_resizable: {allow_resizable} }}"


def optional_buffer_source_rules(idl_type: Optional[IDLType]) -> str:
    return f"Some({buffer_source_rules(idl_type, {})})" if idl_type is not None else "None"


def rust_to_idl_value(
    idl_type: IDLType,
    parameter_attributes: dict[str, str],
    value: str,
    identifier: str,
    context: GenerationContext,
    what: str,
    keeps_cells_alive: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """An expression of type ThrowCompletionOr<T> that converts the JS value to the IDL value. The identifier is the
    name of the parameter or member that the value is of, which the errors of some conversions name. The value can be
    a sequence of values that are or can hold cells, or a dictionary that holds one, when what receives it keeps the
    sequence alive in a MarkedVec for as long as the reference to the VM lives: a parameter, rust_parameter_type(), or
    a member of such a dictionary, dictionary_holds_sequence_of_cells()."""
    rust_type(idl_type, context, what)
    name = idl_type.name
    attributes = {**idl_type.extended_attributes, **parameter_attributes}
    for integer_attribute in ("Clamp", "EnforceRange"):
        if integer_attribute in attributes and name not in INTEGER_TYPES:
            raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(
                f"{what} has the type {idl_type} with [{integer_attribute}], which the Rust bindings only handle on "
                "integer types"
            )
    if "LegacyNullToEmptyString" in attributes and (idl_type.nullable or name not in DOM_STRING_TYPES):
        raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(
            f"{what} has the type {idl_type} with [LegacyNullToEmptyString], which applies to DOMString only"
        )
    # https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-nullable-type
    if idl_type.nullable:
        inner_type = idl_type.without_nullable()
        if member_other_than_undefined(inner_type) is not None:
            raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(
                f"{what} has the type {idl_type}, whose inner type includes undefined, which the Rust bindings do "
                "not convert to yet"
            )
        inner = rust_to_idl_value(inner_type, parameter_attributes, value, identifier, context, what)
        return f"if {value}.is_nullish() {{ Ok(None) }} else {{ {inner}.map(Some) }}"
    if isinstance(idl_type, IDLParameterizedType) and idl_type.name == "sequence":
        if keeps_cells_alive and is_sequence_of_cells(idl_type, context):
            element = rust_to_idl_value(idl_type.parameters[0], {}, "value", identifier, context, what)
            return f"sequence_from_js(vm, {value}, MarkedVec::new(vm), |value| {element})"
        element = rust_sequence_element_to_idl_value(idl_type, identifier, context, what)
        return f"sequence_from_js(vm, {value}, Vec::new(), |value| {element})"
    if isinstance(idl_type, IDLParameterizedType) and idl_type.name == "record":
        if keeps_cells_alive and is_record_of_cells(idl_type, context):
            key = rust_to_idl_value(idl_type.parameters[0], {}, "key", identifier, context, what)
            record_value = rust_to_idl_value(idl_type.parameters[1], {}, "value", identifier, context, what)
            return f"record_from_js(vm, {value}, MarkedVec::new(vm), |key| {key}, |value| {record_value})"
        return rust_record_to_idl_value(idl_type, value, identifier, context, what)
    if isinstance(idl_type, IDLParameterizedType) and idl_type.name == "Promise":
        return f"to_promise(vm, {value})"
    if isinstance(idl_type, IDLParameterizedType):
        raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(
            f"{what} has the type {idl_type}, which the Rust bindings do not convert to yet"
        )
    if name in DOM_STRING_TYPES:
        if "LegacyNullToEmptyString" in attributes:
            return f"to_dom_string_treating_null_as_empty(vm, {value})"
        return f"to_dom_string(vm, {value})"
    if name == "USVString":
        return f"to_usv_string(vm, {value})"
    if name == "ByteString":
        return f"to_byte_string(vm, {value})"
    if name == "boolean":
        return f"to_boolean({value})"
    if name == "any":
        return f"ThrowCompletionOr::<Value>::Ok({value})"
    if name == "object":
        return f"to_object(vm, {value})"
    if name in INTEGER_TYPES:
        if "EnforceRange" in attributes:
            return f"to_{name.replace(' ', '_')}_enforcing_range(vm, {value})"
        if "Clamp" in attributes:
            return f"to_{name.replace(' ', '_')}_clamping(vm, {value})"
        return f"to_{name.replace(' ', '_')}(vm, {value})"
    if name == "float":
        return f'to_float(vm, {value}, "{identifier}")'
    if name == "unrestricted float":
        return f"to_unrestricted_float(vm, {value})"
    if name == "double":
        return f'to_double(vm, {value}, "{identifier}")'
    if name == "unrestricted double":
        return f"to_unrestricted_double(vm, {value})"
    if name == "ArrayBuffer":
        if "AllowShared" in attributes:
            raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(f"{what} has [AllowShared] ArrayBuffer, which Rust does not convert yet")
        return f"crate::bindings::conversions::to_array_buffer(vm, {value}, {buffer_source_rules(idl_type, parameter_attributes)})"
    if name == "SharedArrayBuffer":
        return f"to_shared_array_buffer(vm, {value}, {buffer_source_rules(idl_type, parameter_attributes)})"
    if name in TYPED_ARRAY_NAMES:
        rules = buffer_source_rules(idl_type, parameter_attributes)
        return f'to_typed_array(vm, {value}, TypedArrayKind::{name}, "{name}", {rules})'
    if runtime_union_type(idl_type, context) == "BufferSource":
        return f"to_buffer_source(vm, {value}, {buffer_source_rules(idl_type, parameter_attributes)})"
    if runtime_union_type(idl_type, context) == "ArrayBufferView":
        return f"to_array_buffer_view(vm, {value}, {buffer_source_rules(idl_type, parameter_attributes)})"
    enumeration = context.enumeration(idl_type)
    if enumeration is not None:
        return f"<{rust_enumeration_path(enumeration, context)}>::from_js(vm, {value})"
    callback_function = context.callback_function(idl_type)
    if callback_function is not None:
        if is_promise_type(callback_function.return_type):
            return f"PromiseCallbackFunction::from_js(vm, {value})"
        return f"CallbackFunction::from_js(vm, {value})"
    if is_callback_interface(idl_type, context):
        return f"CallbackInterface::from_js(vm, {value})"
    interface = rust_interface(idl_type, context)
    if interface is not None:
        if inheriting_interfaces(interface, context):
            return f"<{rust_any_interface_path(interface)}>::from_js(vm, {value})"
        return f"to_interface::<{rust_interface_path(interface)}>(vm, {value})"
    if is_window_proxy(idl_type):
        return f"to_window_proxy(vm, {value})"
    interface = cpp_interface(idl_type, context)
    if interface is not None:
        return f'to_cpp_interface(vm, {value}, {cpp_interface_name_constant(interface)}, "{interface.name}")'
    if is_unnamed_union_of_cpp_interfaces(idl_type, context):
        interface_names = ", ".join(
            cpp_interface_name_constant(context.interfaces[member_type.name])
            for member_type in idl_type.flattened_member_types()
        )
        return f"to_cpp_interface_in_union(vm, {value}, &[{interface_names}])"
    dictionary = resolved_dictionary(idl_type, context)
    if dictionary is not None:
        if dictionary_holds_sequence_of_cells(dictionary, context) and not keeps_cells_alive:
            raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(
                f"{what} has the type {idl_type}, a dictionary that holds a sequence of values that are or can hold "
                "cells, which the Rust bindings only convert to as a parameter yet"
            )
        return f"<{rust_dictionary_path(dictionary, context)}>::from_js(vm, {value})"
    if isinstance(idl_type, IDLUnionType) and is_named_union(idl_type, context):
        members = union_members_by_kind(idl_type, context, what)
        # NB: The conversion of a named union is written once, for every parameter of its type.
        allowances = sorted(set(parameter_attributes) & {"AllowShared", "AllowResizable"})
        if allowances:
            raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(
                f"{what} has the extended attributes {allowances} on the union type {idl_type}, which the Rust "
                "bindings only handle on the members of the union"
            )
        path = rust_union_path(idl_type, context, what)
        if members.names_numeric_argument:
            return f'<{path}>::from_js_with_identifier(vm, {value}, "{identifier}")'
        return f"<{path}>::from_js(vm, {value})"
    raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(f"{what} has the type {idl_type}, which the Rust bindings do not convert to yet")


def rust_sequence_element_to_idl_value(
    sequence_type: IDLParameterizedType, identifier: str, context: GenerationContext, what: str
) -> str:
    """The conversion of the JS value `value` to an element of the sequence type."""
    element_type = sequence_type.parameters[0]
    if holds_cells(element_type, context):
        # NB: The elements are gathered in a Vec, which hides cells from the collector while the rest are converted.
        raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(
            f"{what} has the type {sequence_type}, a sequence of values that are or can hold cells, which the Rust "
            "bindings do not convert to yet"
        )
    return rust_to_idl_value(element_type, {}, "value", identifier, context, what)


def rust_record_to_idl_value(
    record_type: IDLParameterizedType, value: str, identifier: str, context: GenerationContext, what: str
) -> str:
    """The conversion of the JS value to the record type."""
    key_type, value_type = record_type.parameters
    if holds_cells(value_type, context):
        # NB: The entries are gathered in a Vec, which hides cells from the collector while the rest are converted.
        raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(
            f"{what} has the type {record_type}, a record of values that are or can hold cells, which the Rust "
            "bindings do not convert to yet"
        )
    key = rust_to_idl_value(key_type, {}, "key", identifier, context, what)
    record_value = rust_to_idl_value(value_type, {}, "value", identifier, context, what)
    return f"record_from_js(vm, {value}, Vec::new(), |key| {key}, |value| {record_value})"


@dataclass
class UnionMembers:
    """The members of a union by the kinds that the Rust bindings distinguish between when they convert a JS value to
    the union."""

    object_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    dictionary_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    string_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    numeric_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    sequence_type: Optional[IDLParameterizedType] = None
    record_type: Optional[IDLParameterizedType] = None
    buffer_source_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    array_buffer_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    shared_array_buffer_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    array_buffer_view_type: Optional[IDLType] = None
    typed_array_types: List[IDLType] = field(default_factory=list)
    enumeration_types: List[IDLType] = field(default_factory=list)
    # The interfaces, implemented in either language, in the order of the union.
    interface_types: List[IDLType] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def names_numeric_argument(self) -> bool:
        return (
            bool(self.enumeration_types)
            and self.numeric_type is not None
            and self.numeric_type.name
            in (
                "float",
                "double",
            )
        )


def union_members_by_kind(union_type: IDLUnionType, context: GenerationContext, what: str) -> UnionMembers:
    members = UnionMembers()
    for member_type in union_member_types(union_type, context):
        if runtime_union_type(member_type, context) == "BufferSource" and members.buffer_source_type is None:
            members.buffer_source_type = member_type
        elif runtime_union_type(member_type, context) == "ArrayBufferView":
            members.array_buffer_view_type = member_type
        elif member_type.name == "ArrayBuffer":
            members.array_buffer_type = member_type
        elif member_type.name == "SharedArrayBuffer":
            members.shared_array_buffer_type = member_type
        elif member_type.name == "object" and members.object_type is None:
            members.object_type = member_type
        elif resolved_dictionary(member_type, context) is not None and members.dictionary_type is None:
            members.dictionary_type = member_type
        elif member_type.name in STRING_TYPES and members.string_type is None:
            members.string_type = member_type
        elif (
            member_type.name in INTEGER_TYPES or member_type.name in FLOATING_POINT_TYPES
        ) and members.numeric_type is None:
            members.numeric_type = member_type
        elif context.enumeration(member_type) is not None:
            members.enumeration_types.append(member_type)
        elif member_type.name in TYPED_ARRAY_NAMES:
            members.typed_array_types.append(member_type)
        elif (
            is_window_proxy(member_type)
            or cpp_interface(member_type, context) is not None
            or rust_interface(member_type, context) is not None
        ):
            members.interface_types.append(member_type)
        elif (
            isinstance(member_type, IDLParameterizedType)
            and member_type.name == "sequence"
            and members.sequence_type is None
        ):
            members.sequence_type = member_type
        elif (
            isinstance(member_type, IDLParameterizedType)
            and member_type.name == "record"
            and members.record_type is None
        ):
            members.record_type = member_type
        else:
            raise UnsupportedByRustBindings(
