#pragma once

#include <AK/Noncopyable.h>
#include <AK/NonnullRefPtr.h>
#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/Variant.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <AK/kmalloc.h>
#include <Compositor/PresentableSurface.h>
#include <Compositor/RemoteSublayer.h>
#include <LibCompositing/Types.h>
#include <LibGfx/Forward.h>
#include <LibGfx/Size.h>
#include <LibMediaCodecs/VideoFrame.h>

namespace Compositor {

// A layer that this process commits frames into, and that the UI shows in a view of its own by the layer's host handle.
// Frames then reach the screen without passing through the UI.
class RemoteLayer {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(RemoteLayer);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(RemoteLayer);

public:
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    virtual ~RemoteLayer() = default;

    virtual Compositing::RemoteLayerHostHandle host_handle() const = 0;

    using Content = Variant<NonnullRefPtr<Media::VideoFrame>, NonnullRefPtr<PresentableSurface>>;
    virtual bool can_show(WindowServerPlacement const&, Content const&, double device_pixel_ratio) const = 0;

    struct Frame {
        // Without a store, the store shown before stays, and only the sublayers change, unless the frame shows no store.
        Optional<PresentableSurface::Lease> store;
        // Whether the sublayers are all of the frame, which then shows no store below them.
        bool shows_no_store { false };
        Gfx::IntSize painted_size;
        double device_pixel_ratio { 1.0 };
        Optional<Gfx::IntSize> fit_within;
        Vector<RemoteSublayer> sublayers;
    };
    // Shows the part of the store that the frame was painted into, at the top left of the layer at its own size, or
    // scaled to fit within the size of the view given, in device pixels, with the sublayers above it, bottom to top,
    // each group with the sublayers in it.
    [[nodiscard]] virtual bool show_frame(Frame) = 0;
    // Places the frame on display again, as when the view that it is scaled into changes size.
    virtual void place_frame(Optional<Gfx::IntSize> fit_within) = 0;

protected:
    RemoteLayer() = default;
};

}

FILE: Services/Compositor/RemoteSublayer.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/Array.h>
#include <AK/NonnullRefPtr.h>
#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/Types.h>
#include <AK/Variant.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <Compositor/PresentableSurface.h>
#include <LibGfx/AffineTransform.h>
#include <LibGfx/Color.h>
#include <LibGfx/CornerRadii.h>
#include <LibGfx/PathData.h>
#include <LibGfx/Point.h>
#include <LibGfx/Rect.h>
#include <LibGfx/ScalingMode.h>
#include <LibGfx/Size.h>
#include <LibGfx/WindingRule.h>
#include <LibMediaCodecs/VideoFrame.h>

namespace Compositor {

// Content that the window server shows of a frame by itself: a video frame or a surface placed and clipped as drawing it
// into the frame would have placed and clipped it, or a tile or a fill of a painted layer in a group that places and
// clips every sublayer in it. Geometry is in device pixels.
struct RemoteSublayer {
    struct RoundedClip {
        Gfx::FloatRect rect;
        float radius { 0 };
        bool rounds_top_left { false };
        bool rounds_top_right { false };
        bool rounds_bottom_right { false };
        bool rounds_bottom_left { false };
    };

    // A path that clips the content, with a copy of its contours, as the path the copy is of may be gone by the time
    // the frame is shown. The contours are in a space of their own, which the transform maps into the frame.
    struct PathClip {
        // Tells the path apart from every other path of the process, so that a frame that clips by the same path as
        // the one before does not make its outline again.
        u64 path_identity { 0 };
        Vector<Gfx::PathVerb> verbs;
        Vector<Gfx::FloatPoint> points;
        Vector<float> conic_weights;
        Gfx::WindingRule winding_rule { Gfx::WindingRule::Nonzero };
        Gfx::AffineTransform path_to_frame;
    };

    // Holds the sublayers that name it as their group.
    struct Group {
        // From the pixels of the group to those of the group it is in, or to those of the frame.
        Gfx::AffineTransform to_parent;
        // Clips the sublayers of the group to this rect of its own pixels, with its corners rounded by the radii.
        Optional<Gfx::FloatRect> clip_rect;
        Gfx::CornerRadii corner_radii;
        // Composites the sublayers of the group at this opacity, once they are composited with each other.
        float opacity { 1 };
    };

    struct Tile {
        PresentableSurface::Lease surface;
        bool every_pixel_is_opaque { false };
    };

    // What the window server shows below the sublayer, within a rect of the pixels of its group, run through filters.
    struct Backdrop {
        struct Filter {
            enum class Kind : u8 {
                Blur,
                ColorMatrix,
            };
            Kind kind { Kind::Blur };
            // In device pixels.
            float blur_standard_deviation { 0 };
            // Row-major, with the offsets in the fifth column, for unpremultiplied colors from 0 to 1.
            Array<float, 20> color_matrix {};

            bool operator==(Filter const&) const = default;
        };

        Gfx::FloatRect region;
        // Applied in order.
        Vector<Filter, 3> filters;

        bool operator==(Backdrop const&) const = default;
    };

    // Tells a sublayer apart from the others from one frame to the next, so that a frame changes only what moved.
    u64 identity { 0 };
    // The index, among the sublayers of the frame, of the group the sublayer is in, which comes before it. Sublayers of
    // one group, and those of the frame itself, which have none, are shown bottom to top.
    Optional<size_t> group_index;
    Variant<NonnullRefPtr<Media::VideoFrame>, PresentableSurface::Lease, Group, Tile, Gfx::Color, Backdrop> content;
    // Where a video frame or a surface is drawn, in its own space, which the transform maps into the frame. Where a
    // tile or a color is shown, in the pixels of its group.
    Gfx::IntRect content_rect;
    // The transform, the clips and the scaling mode place a video frame or a surface only.
    Gfx::AffineTransform content_to_frame;
    Gfx::FloatRect clip_rect;
    Optional<RoundedClip> rounded_clip;
    Optional<PathClip> path_clip;
    Gfx::ScalingMode scaling_mode { Gfx::ScalingMode::Bilinear };
};

// Where the window server can show the content of a media layer by itself, in viewport pixels.
struct WindowServerPlacement {
    Gfx::IntRect content_rect;
    Gfx::AffineTransform content_to_viewport;
    Gfx::FloatRect clip_rect;
    Optional<RemoteSublayer::RoundedClip> rounded_clip;
    bool is_clipped_by_path { false };
    Gfx::ScalingMode scaling_mode { Gfx::ScalingMode::Bilinear };
};

}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

use std::env;
use std::error::Error;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

#[allow(dead_code, reason = "the model is for the generators of the other crates as well")]
#[path = "../../../Libraries/LibCompositing/Rust/generate/webgl_wire_model.rs"]
mod webgl_wire_model;

#[path = "generate/webgl_replayer.rs"]
mod webgl_replayer;

/// The GL functions that the replayer of WebGL calls, which src/webgl/gl.rs includes, and the methods of the replayer,
/// which src/webgl/replay.rs includes.
fn generate_webgl_replayer(manifest_dir: &Path, out_dir: &Path) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    let libraries = manifest_dir.join("../../../Libraries");
    let functions_path = libraries.join("LibCompositing/WebGL/GLFunctions.json");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", functions_path.display());
    println!(
        "cargo:rerun-if-changed={}",
        libraries.join("LibCompositing/Rust/generate").display()
    );
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=generate");
    let json = std::fs::read_to_string(&functions_path)?;
    let generate = |json: &str| -> Result<(String, String), String> {
        let functions = webgl_wire_model::parse_functions(json)?;
        Ok((
            webgl_replayer::write_gl_functions(&functions)?,
            webgl_replayer::write_replayer(&functions)?,
        ))
    };
    let (gl_functions, replayer) = generate(&json).map_err(|error| format!("{}: {error}", functions_path.display()))?;
    std::fs::write(out_dir.join("webgl_gl.rs"), gl_functions)?;
    std::fs::write(out_dir.join("webgl_replayer.rs"), replayer)?;
    Ok(())
}

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    let manifest_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")?);
    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("OUT_DIR")?);

    generate_webgl_replayer(&manifest_dir, &out_dir)?;

    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=cbindgen.toml");

    let mut config = cbindgen::Config::from_file(manifest_dir.join("cbindgen.toml"))?;
    config.namespaces = Some(vec!["Compositor".to_string(), "RustFFI".to_string()]);
    // An ak::Span is laid out as an AK ReadonlySpan, which C++ passes it as.
    for (rust_name, cpp_name) in [
        ("Span", "AK::ReadonlySpan"),
        ("Color", "Gfx::Color"),
        ("CornerRadii", "Gfx::CornerRadii"),
        ("FloatPoint", "Gfx::FloatPoint"),
        ("FloatRect", "Gfx::FloatRect"),
        ("IntRect", "Gfx::IntRect"),
        ("IntSize", "Gfx::IntSize"),
        ("ScalingMode", "Gfx::ScalingMode"),
        ("WindingRule", "Gfx::WindingRule"),
        ("PathGeometryData", "Gfx::FFI::PathGeometryData"),
        ("SpatialNodeIndex", "Compositing::SpatialNodeIndex"),
        ("RawAttachment", "IPC::RawAttachment"),
        ("RawMessage", "IPC::FfiRawMessage"),
        ("EncodedValue", "AK::ReadonlyBytes"),
        ("FfiRasterPainter", "Compositing::RustFFI::FfiRasterPainter"),
        ("CanvasId", "Compositing::CanvasId"),
        ("DisplayListCommandType", "Compositing::DisplayListCommandType"),
        (
            "Web_Bindings_PredefinedColorSpace",
            "Web::Bindings::PredefinedColorSpace",
        ),
        ("ImageFrameResourceId", "Compositing::ImageFrameResourceId"),
        ("PaintingSurface", "Gfx::PaintingSurface"),
        ("PresentableSurface", "Compositor::PresentableSurface"),
        ("WeakPresentableSurface", "Compositor::FfiWeakPresentableSurface"),
        ("PresentableSurfacePool", "Compositor::FfiPresentableSurfacePool"),
    ] {
        config.export.rename.insert(rust_name.to_string(), cpp_name.to_string());
    }
    // The surfaces are the C++ classes that stand for them, and the C++ declares the rest, so they are only named.
    config.export.exclude.extend(
        [
            "PaintingSurface",
            "PresentableSurface",
            "WeakPresentableSurface",
            "PresentableSurfacePool",
        ]
        .map(String::from),
    );
    config.includes.extend(
        [
            "AK/Span.h",
            "Compositor/PaintingSurface.h",
            "Compositor/PresentableSurface.h",
            "LibCompositing/DisplayList/ContextRef.h",
            "LibCompositing/DisplayList/DisplayListCommandsGenerated.h",
            "LibCompositing/DisplayList/DisplayListResourceIds.h",
            "LibGfx/Color.h",
            "LibGfx/CornerRadii.h",
            "LibGfx/Point.h",
            "LibGfx/Rect.h",
            "LibGfx/RustFFI.h",
            "LibGfx/ScalingMode.h",
            "LibGfx/Size.h",
            "LibGfx/WindingRule.h",
            "LibIPC/RawAttachment.h",
            "LibCompositing/RustFFI.h",
            "LibIPC/RawMessage.h",
            "LibWebCommon/Bindings/PredefinedColorSpace.h",
        ]
        .map(String::from),
    );

    let mut builder = cbindgen::Builder::new().with_config(config);
    for source in [
        "src/ffi.rs",
        "src/host.rs",
        "src/frame_inputs.rs",
        "src/raster_host.rs",
        "src/core/presenting.rs",
        "src/core/mod.rs",
        "src/backing_stores.rs",
        "src/cpp_object.rs",
        "src/surfaces/painting_surface.rs",
        "src/surfaces/presentable_surface.rs",
        "src/webgl/host.rs",
    ] {
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={source}");
        builder = builder.with_src(manifest_dir.join(source));
    }
    builder
        .generate()?
        .write_to_file(out_dir.join("CompositorCoreRustFFI.h"));
    Ok(())
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Writes the replaying side of the WebGL command stream from GLFunctions.json: the table of the GL functions that
//! the Compositor calls, which src/webgl/gl.rs includes, and a method of the replayer for every command and every
//! synchronous call that follows from the signature of its GL function, which src/webgl/generated.rs includes.

use std::fmt::Write;

use crate::webgl_wire_model::{
    Argument, Category, DefaultObject, Function, PayloadFactor, WireType, rust_identifier, title_case_to_snake_case,
    wire_struct,
};

fn unsupported(function: &Function, what: &str) -> String {
    format!("the replayer cannot replay {}: {what}", function.name)
}

/// The Rust type of a GL type in the signature of a GL function.
fn gl_rust_type(cpp_type: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    Some(match cpp_type {
        "void" => "()",
        "GLenum" | "GLuint" | "GLbitfield" => "u32",
        "GLint" | "GLsizei" => "i32",
        "GLfloat" => "f32",
        "GLboolean" => "u8",
        "GLintptr" | "GLsizeiptr" => "isize",
        "GLuint64" => "u64",
        "GLint64" => "i64",
        "GLsync" | "void*" => "*mut c_void",
        "void const*" => "*const c_void",
        "void**" => "*mut *mut c_void",
        "GLubyte const*" => "*const u8",
        "GLchar const*" => "*const c_char",
        "GLchar*" => "*mut c_char",
        "GLchar const* const*" => "*const *const c_char",
        "GLfloat const*" => "*const f32",
        "GLfloat*" => "*mut f32",
        "GLint const*" => "*const i32",
        "GLint*" | "GLsizei*" => "*mut i32",
        "GLuint const*" | "GLenum const*" => "*const u32",
        "GLuint*" | "GLenum*" => "*mut u32",
        "GLboolean*" => "*mut u8",
        "GLint64*" => "*mut i64",
        _ => return None,
    })
}

fn field_name(argument: &Argument) -> String {
    rust_identifier(&title_case_to_snake_case(&argument.name))
}

/// A scalar argument as GL takes it, from the field of the struct that carries it.
fn scalar_argument(argument: &Argument, holder: &str) -> String {
    let field = field_name(argument);
    if matches!(argument.cpp_type.as_str(), "GLintptr" | "GLsizeiptr") {
        format!("{holder}.{field} as isize")
    } else {
        format!("{holder}.{field}")
    }
}

fn has_gl_signature(function: &Function) -> bool {
    function.category != Category::BuiltinCommand
}

fn parameter_types(function: &Function) -> Result<Vec<&'static str>, String> {
    function
        .arguments
        .iter()
        .map(|argument| {
            gl_rust_type(&argument.cpp_type).ok_or_else(|| {
                unsupported(
                    function,
                    &format!("{} has the type {}", argument.name, argument.cpp_type),
                )
            })
        })
        .collect()
}

fn return_type(function: &Function) -> Result<&'static str, String> {
    let cpp_type = function.return_type.as_deref().unwrap_or("void");
    gl_rust_type(cpp_type).ok_or_else(|| unsupported(function, &format!("it returns {cpp_type}")))
}

fn function_pointer_type(function: &Function) -> Result<String, String> {
    let parameters = parameter_types(function)?.join(", ");
    let return_type = return_type(function)?;
    Ok(if return_type == "()" {
        format!("unsafe extern \"system\" fn({parameters})")
    } else {
        format!("unsafe extern \"system\" fn({parameters}) -> {return_type}")
    })
}

fn zero_of(rust_type: &str) -> &'static str {
    match rust_type {
        "()" => "()",
        "f32" => "0.0",
        "c_char" | "u8" | "u32" | "i32" | "isize" | "u64" | "i64" => "0",
        _ if rust_type.starts_with("*mut") => "core::ptr::null_mut()",
        _ => "core::ptr::null()",
    }
}

/// The table of GL functions, with a loader, and the functions that the tests of the crate replay against, which
/// record what is called.
pub fn write_gl_functions(functions: &[Function]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let functions: Vec<&Function> = functions.iter().filter(|function| has_gl_signature(function)).collect();
    let mut out = String::from("// Generated by build.rs from Libraries/LibCompositing/WebGL/GLFunctions.json.\n\n");
    out.push_str("use core::ffi::{CStr, c_char, c_void};\n\n");

    out.push_str("/// The GL functions that the replayer calls.\npub struct GlFunctions {\n");
    for function in &functions {
        writeln!(
            out,
            "    pub {}: {},",
            function.method_name(),
            function_pointer_type(function)?
        )
        .unwrap();
    }
    out.push_str("}\n\n");

    out.push_str(
        "impl GlFunctions {\n    /// Answers the name of a function that `get_proc_address` does not know.\n    ///\n    /// # Safety\n    ///\n    /// `get_proc_address` answers the address of the GL function of a name, or null.\n    pub unsafe fn load(mut get_proc_address: impl FnMut(&CStr) -> *const c_void) -> Result<Self, &'static CStr> {\n        // SAFETY: Each field has the type of the function of its name.\n        unsafe {\n            Ok(Self {\n",
    );
    for function in &functions {
        writeln!(
            out,
            "                {}: load_function(&mut get_proc_address, c\"{}\")?,",
            function.method_name(),
            function.name
        )
        .unwrap();
    }
    out.push_str("            })\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n");
    out.push_str(
        "/// # Safety\n///\n/// `F` is the type of a pointer to the GL function of the name.\nunsafe fn load_function<F: Copy>(\n    get_proc_address: &mut impl FnMut(&CStr) -> *const c_void,\n    name: &'static CStr,\n) -> Result<F, &'static CStr> {\n    const { assert!(size_of::<F>() == size_of::<*const c_void>()) };\n    let address = get_proc_address(name);\n    if address.is_null() {\n        return Err(name);\n    }\n    // SAFETY: The address is that of the function, whose type the caller names.\n    Ok(unsafe { core::mem::transmute_copy::<*const c_void, F>(&address) })\n}\n\n",
    );

    out.push_str("#[cfg(test)]\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\npub mod recording {\n");
    out.push_str("    use super::*;\n\n");
    out.push_str("    fn pointer_text<T>(pointer: *const T) -> &'static str {\n        if pointer.is_null() { \"null\" } else { \"ptr\" }\n    }\n\n");
    for function in &functions {
        let types = parameter_types(function)?;
        let return_type = return_type(function)?;
        let parameters: Vec<String> = function
            .arguments
            .iter()
            .zip(&types)
            .map(|(argument, rust_type)| format!("{}: {rust_type}", field_name(argument)))
            .collect();
        let arguments: Vec<String> = function
            .arguments
            .iter()
            .zip(&types)
            .map(|(argument, rust_type)| {
                let name = field_name(argument);
                if rust_type.starts_with("*mut") {
                    format!("pointer_text({name}.cast_const())")
                } else if rust_type.starts_with('*') {
                    format!("pointer_text({name})")
                } else {
                    format!("&{name}")
                }
            })
            .collect();
        let format_string = vec!["{:?}"; arguments.len()].join(", ");
        let signature_return = if return_type == "()" {
            String::new()
        } else {
            format!(" -> {return_type}")
        };
        writeln!(
            out,
            "    pub unsafe extern \"system\" fn {}({}){signature_return} {{",
            function.method_name(),
            parameters.join(", ")
        )
        .unwrap();
        writeln!(
            out,
            "        crate::webgl::testing::record(format!(\"{}({format_string})\"{}));",
            function.name,
            arguments
                .iter()
                .map(|argument| format!(", {argument}"))
                .collect::<String>()
        )
        .unwrap();
        let is_gen = function.category == Category::Gen;
        if is_gen && function.returns_void() {
            let count = field_name(&function.arguments[0]);
            let names = field_name(&function.arguments[1]);
            writeln!(
                out,
                "        for index in 0..usize::try_from({count}).unwrap_or(0) {{\n            // SAFETY: The replayer passes room for as many names.\n            unsafe {{ {names}.add(index).write(crate::webgl::testing::next_name()) }};\n        }}"
            )
            .unwrap();
        } else if is_gen && return_type == "u32" {
            out.push_str("        crate::webgl::testing::next_name()\n");
        } else if is_gen {
            out.push_str("        crate::webgl::testing::next_name() as usize as *mut c_void\n");
        } else if return_type != "()" {
            writeln!(out, "        {}", zero_of(return_type)).unwrap();
        }
        out.push_str("    }\n\n");
    }
    out.push_str("    pub fn functions() -> GlFunctions {\n        GlFunctions {\n");
    for function in &functions {
        writeln!(
            out,
            "            {}: {},",
            function.method_name(),
            function.method_name()
        )
        .unwrap();
    }
    out.push_str("        }\n    }\n}\n");
    Ok(out)
}

fn wire_type_of(function: &Function, argument: &Argument) -> Result<WireType, String> {
    WireType::of(&argument.cpp_type)
        .ok_or_else(|| unsupported(function, &format!("{} has no wire type", argument.name)))
}

/// The factors of the size that the JSON gives for the data of an argument, as `i64` expressions of the fields of
/// `holder`.
fn size_factors(function: &Function, argument: &Argument, holder: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let mut factors = Vec::new();
    for factor in function.payload_size(argument)? {
        factors.push(match factor {
            PayloadFactor::Constant(constant) => format!("{constant}_i64"),
            PayloadFactor::Argument(index) => {
                let counted_by = &function.arguments[index];
                let field = format!("{holder}.{}", field_name(counted_by));
                match wire_type_of(function, counted_by)? {
                    WireType::I64 => field,
                    WireType::I32 | WireType::U32 => format!("i64::from({field})"),
                    _ => {
                        return Err(unsupported(
                            function,
                            &format!("{} counts with {}", argument.name, counted_by.name),
                        ));
                    }
                }
            }
            PayloadFactor::ColorBufferComponents(index) => format!(
                "if {holder}.{} == GL_COLOR {{ 4 }} else {{ 1 }}",
                field_name(&function.arguments[index])
            ),
        });
    }
    Ok(format!("&[{}]", factors.join(", ")))
}

fn element_type(argument: &Argument) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let pointee = argument.pointee_cpp_type().replace("const", "");
    match pointee.trim() {
        "void" | "GLchar" => None,
        "GLfloat" => Some("f32"),
        "GLint" | "GLsizei" => Some("i32"),
        "GLuint" | "GLenum" => Some("u32"),
        "GLboolean" => Some("u8"),
        "GLint64" => Some("i64"),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn data_pointer(argument: &Argument, bytes: &str) -> String {
    match element_type(argument) {
        Some(element) => format!("typed_data::<{element}>({bytes})?"),
        None => format!("{bytes}.as_ptr().cast()"),
    }
}

fn opaque_data_pointer(argument: &Argument, data: &str) -> String {
    match element_type(argument) {
        Some(element) => format!("typed_opaque_data::<{element}>({data})?"),
        None => format!("{data}.pointer.cast()"),
    }
}

/// Resolves the data of an argument that points at some, and answers what the GL function is passed for it.
fn write_data_resolution(out: &mut String, function: &Function, argument: &Argument) -> Result<String, String> {
    let field = field_name(argument);
    let name = function.command_name();
    let mismatch = format!(
        "ReplayError(\"the data of {name}.{} has another size than its arguments give\")",
        argument.name
    );
    let factors = size_factors(function, argument, "command")?;
    if argument.is_nullable {
        writeln!(
            out,
            "        let {field}_data = if command.has_{field} {{
            let data = if command.{field}.size != 0 {{ self.opaque_data(payload, command.{field})? }} else {{ OpaqueData::EMPTY }};
            if !size_matches(data.size, {factors}) {{
                return Err({mismatch});
            }}
            if command.{field}.size != 0 {{ {} }} else {{ core::ptr::null() }}
        }} else {{
            if command.{field}.size != 0 {{
                return Err(ReplayError(\"{name}.{} has data although it has none\"));
            }}
            core::ptr::null()
        }};",
            opaque_data_pointer(argument, "data"),
            argument.name
        )
        .unwrap();
    } else {
        writeln!(
            out,
            "        let {field}_opaque_data = self.opaque_data(payload, command.{field})?;
        if !size_matches({field}_opaque_data.size, {factors}) {{
            return Err({mismatch});
        }}
        let {field}_data = {};",
            opaque_data_pointer(argument, &format!("{field}_opaque_data"))
        )
        .unwrap();
    }
    Ok(format!("{field}_data"))
}

fn write_command(out: &mut String, function: &Function) -> Result<(), String> {
    let name = function.command_name();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "    fn replay_{}(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {{",
        function.method_name()
    )
    .unwrap();
    if function.arguments.is_empty() {
        writeln!(out, "        decode::<commands::{name}>(payload)?;").unwrap();
    } else {
        writeln!(out, "        let command: commands::{name} = decode(payload)?;").unwrap();
    }
    let mut arguments = Vec::new();
    for argument in &function.arguments {
        let field = field_name(argument);
        let take_or_lookup = if function.deletes_objects { "take" } else { "lookup" };
        if argument.is_string {
            writeln!(
                out,
                "        let {field}_data = string_data(payload, command.{field})?;"
            )
            .unwrap();
            arguments.push(format!("{field}_data"));
        } else if argument.is_offset {
            arguments.push(format!("command.{field} as isize as *const c_void"));
        } else if argument.is_object && !argument.is_pointer() {
            if argument.cpp_type == "GLsync" {
                writeln!(
                    out,
                    "        let {field} = self.objects.{take_or_lookup}_sync(command.{field});"
                )
                .unwrap();
            } else if let Some(default) = argument.zero_means_default {
                let default = match default {
                    DefaultObject::Framebuffer => "framebuffer",
                    DefaultObject::Renderbuffer => "renderbuffer",
                };
                writeln!(
                    out,
                    "        let {field} = if command.{field} == 0 {{ self.defaults.{default} }} else {{ self.objects.lookup(command.{field}) }};"
                )
                .unwrap();
            } else {
                writeln!(
                    out,
                    "        let {field} = self.objects.{take_or_lookup}(command.{field});"
                )
                .unwrap();
            }
            arguments.push(field);
        } else if argument.is_object && argument.is_const_pointer() {
            let factors = size_factors(function, argument, "command")?;
            writeln!(
                out,
                "        let {field}_bytes = data_span(payload, command.{field})?;
        if !size_matches({field}_bytes.len(), {factors}) {{
            return Err(ReplayError(\"the objects of {name}.{} have another size than its arguments give\"));
        }}
        let {field}: Vec<u32> = object_ids({field}_bytes)?.map(|id| self.objects.{take_or_lookup}(id)).collect();",
                argument.name
            )
            .unwrap();
            arguments.push(format!("{field}.as_ptr()"));
        } else if argument.payload.is_some() {
            arguments.push(write_data_resolution(out, function, argument)?);
        } else if argument.is_pointer() {
            return Err(unsupported(
                function,
                &format!("{} points at what has no size", argument.name),
            ));
        } else {
            arguments.push(scalar_argument(argument, "command"));
        }
    }
    writeln!(
        out,
        "        // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and every pointer is valid for what GL reads of it.\n        unsafe {{ (self.gl.{})({}) }};\n        Ok(())\n    }}\n",
        function.method_name(),
        arguments.join(", ")
    )
    .unwrap();
    Ok(())
}

fn write_gen(out: &mut String, function: &Function) {
    let name = function.command_name();
    let method = function.method_name();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "    fn replay_{method}(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {{\n        let command: commands::{name} = decode(payload)?;"
    )
    .unwrap();
    if function.returns_void() {
        let count = field_name(&function.arguments[0]);
        let ids = field_name(&function.arguments[1]);
        writeln!(
            out,
            "        let ids = object_ids(data_span(payload, command.{ids})?)?;
        if i64::try_from(ids.len()) != Ok(i64::from(command.{count})) {{
            return Err(ReplayError(\"{name} has another number of objects than it creates\"));
        }}
        for id in ids {{
            let mut name = 0;
            // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and the name is room for one.
            unsafe {{ (self.gl.{method})(1, &raw mut name) }};
            self.objects.add(id, name)?;
        }}
        Ok(())
    }}
"
        )
        .unwrap();
        return;
    }
    let arguments: Vec<String> = function
        .arguments
        .iter()
        .map(|argument| scalar_argument(argument, "command"))
        .collect();
    let add = if function.return_type.as_deref() == Some("GLsync") {
        "add_sync"
    } else {
        "add"
    };
    writeln!(
        out,
        "        // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current.\n        let object = unsafe {{ (self.gl.{method})({}) }};\n        self.objects.{add}(command.id, object)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }}\n",
        arguments.join(", ")
    )
    .unwrap();
}

fn write_sync_call(out: &mut String, function: &Function) -> Result<(), String> {
    let name = function.command_name();
    let method = function.method_name();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "    fn handle_{method}(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ReplayError> {{"
    )
    .unwrap();
    if function.arguments.iter().any(|argument| !argument.is_out) {
        writeln!(
            out,
            "        let request: sync_calls::{name}Request = decode(payload)?;"
        )
        .unwrap();
    } else {
        writeln!(out, "        let _: sync_calls::{name}Request = decode(payload)?;").unwrap();
    }
    let mut arguments = Vec::new();
    let mut blobs = Vec::new();
    let mut reply_fields = Vec::new();
    for argument in &function.arguments {
        let field = field_name(argument);
        if let Some(value) = &argument.host_override {
            arguments.push(value.clone());
        } else if argument.is_out {
            if argument.payload.is_some() {
                let element = gl_rust_type(&argument.cpp_type)
                    .and_then(|pointer| pointer.strip_prefix("*mut "))
                    .ok_or_else(|| unsupported(function, &format!("{} is no buffer", argument.name)))?;
                let factors = size_factors(function, argument, "request")?;
                writeln!(
                    out,
                    "        let mut {field} = vec![{}; out_data_size({factors})? / size_of::<{element}>()];",
                    zero_of(element)
                )
                .unwrap();
                arguments.push(format!("{field}.as_mut_ptr()"));
                blobs.push((field.clone(), element));
                reply_fields.push(format!("{field}: spans[{}]", blobs.len() - 1));
            } else {
                let element = gl_rust_type(&argument.pointee_cpp_type())
                    .ok_or_else(|| unsupported(function, &format!("{} has no value type", argument.name)))?;
                writeln!(out, "        let mut {field}: {element} = {};", zero_of(element)).unwrap();
                arguments.push(format!("&raw mut {field}"));
                reply_fields.push(field);
            }
        } else if argument.is_object && !argument.is_pointer() {
            let lookup = if argument.cpp_type == "GLsync" {
                "lookup_sync"
            } else {
                "lookup"
            };
            writeln!(out, "        let {field} = self.objects.{lookup}(request.{field});").unwrap();
            arguments.push(field);
        } else if argument.is_string {
            writeln!(
                out,
                "        let {field}_data = string_data(payload, request.{field})?;"
            )
            .unwrap();
            arguments.push(format!("{field}_data"));
        } else if argument.payload.is_some() {
            let factors = size_factors(function, argument, "request")?;
            writeln!(
                out,
                "        let {field}_bytes = data_span(payload, request.{field})?;
        if !size_matches({field}_bytes.len(), {factors}) {{
            return Err(ReplayError(\"the data of {name}.{} has another size than its arguments give\"));
        }}",
                argument.name
            )
            .unwrap();
            arguments.push(data_pointer(argument, &format!("{field}_bytes")));
        } else if argument.is_pointer() {
            return Err(unsupported(
                function,
                &format!("{} points at what has no size", argument.name),
            ));
        } else {
            arguments.push(scalar_argument(argument, "request"));
        }
    }

    let invocation = if function.name == "glGetError" {
        "self.get_error()".to_string()
    } else {
        out.push_str(
            "        // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and every pointer is valid for what GL reads and\n        //         writes of it.\n",
        );
        format!("unsafe {{ (self.gl.{method})({}) }}", arguments.join(", "))
    };
    if function.returns_void() {
        writeln!(out, "        {invocation};").unwrap();
    } else {
        writeln!(out, "        let return_value = {invocation};").unwrap();
        reply_fields.insert(0, "return_value".into());
    }

    if !blobs.is_empty() {
        let blob_sizes: Vec<String> = blobs
            .iter()
            .map(|(field, element)| format!("{field}.len() * size_of::<{element}>()"))
            .collect();
        writeln!(
            out,
            "        let spans = reply_data_spans::<sync_calls::{name}Reply, {}>([{}]);",
            blobs.len(),
            blob_sizes.join(", ")
        )
        .unwrap();
    }
    let reply_layout = wire_struct(format!("SyncCalls::{name}::Reply"), function.sync_reply_fields())?;
    let rest_of_reply = if reply_layout.has_unused_bytes() {
        format!("..sync_calls::{name}Reply::ZEROED")
    } else {
        String::new()
    };
    writeln!(
        out,
        "        let reply = sync_calls::{name}Reply {{ {}{rest_of_reply} }};",
        reply_fields.join(", ")
            + if reply_fields.is_empty() || rest_of_reply.is_empty() {
                ""
            } else {
                ", "
            }
    )
    .unwrap();
    let blob_bytes: Vec<String> = blobs
        .iter()
        .map(|(field, _)| format!("bytes_of_slice(&{field})"))
        .collect();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "        Ok(encode_reply(&reply, &[{}]))\n    }}\n",
        blob_bytes.join(", ")
    )
    .unwrap();
    Ok(())
}

/// The methods of the replayer that follow from the signatures of GL functions, and the dispatch of every command
/// and every synchronous call to its method. The others are written by hand, under the name of their function.
pub fn write_replayer(functions: &[Function]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let mut out = String::from("// Generated by build.rs from Libraries/LibCompositing/WebGL/GLFunctions.json.\n\n");
    out.push_str("impl<H: WebGLHost> Replayer<'_, H> {\n");

    out.push_str(
        "    pub fn replay_record(&mut self, command_type: CommandType, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {\n        match command_type {\n",
    );
    for function in functions.iter().filter(|function| function.is_command_stream_entry()) {
        let name = function.command_name();
        let method = function.method_name();
        if matches!(function.category, Category::Command | Category::Gen) {
            writeln!(out, "            CommandType::{name} => self.replay_{method}(payload),").unwrap();
        } else {
            writeln!(out, "            CommandType::{name} => self.{method}(payload),").unwrap();
        }
    }
    out.push_str("        }\n    }\n\n");

    out.push_str(
        "    pub fn handle_sync_call(&mut self, call_type: SyncCallType, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ReplayError> {\n        match call_type {\n",
    );
    for function in functions.iter().filter(|function| function.is_sync_call()) {
        let name = function.command_name();
        let method = function.method_name();
        if function.category == Category::Sync {
            writeln!(
                out,
                "            SyncCallType::{name} => self.handle_{method}(payload),"
            )
            .unwrap();
        } else {
            writeln!(out, "            SyncCallType::{name} => self.{method}(payload),").unwrap();
        }
    }
    out.push_str("        }\n    }\n\n");

    for function in functions {
        match function.category {
            Category::Command => write_command(&mut out, function)?,
            Category::Gen => write_gen(&mut out, function),
            Category::Sync => write_sync_call(&mut out, function)?,
            Category::Custom | Category::BuiltinCommand => {}
        }
    }
    out.push_str("}\n\n");

    let commands_with_only_opaque_data: Vec<String> = functions
        .iter()
        .filter(|function| function.category == Category::Command && has_only_opaque_data(function))
        .map(|function| format!("CommandType::{}", function.command_name()))
        .collect();
    out.push_str("pub fn only_gl_reads_the_data_of(command_type: CommandType) -> bool {\n");
    if commands_with_only_opaque_data.is_empty() {
        out.push_str("    let _ = command_type;\n    false\n");
    } else {
        writeln!(
            out,
            "    matches!(command_type, {})",
            commands_with_only_opaque_data.join(" | ")
        )
        .unwrap();
    }
    out.push_str("}\n");
    Ok(out)
}

fn has_only_opaque_data(function: &Function) -> bool {
    let reads_its_data = function
        .arguments
        .iter()
        .any(|argument| argument.is_string || (argument.is_object && argument.is_const_pointer()));
    let has_data_that_write_data_resolution_resolves = function.arguments.iter().any(|argument| {
        !argument.is_string && !argument.is_offset && !argument.is_object && argument.payload.is_some()
    });
    has_data_that_write_data_resolution_resolves && !reads_its_data
}

/*

use libcompositing_rust::scrolling::{
    AppliedScrollRequest, AsyncScrollNodeStableID, AsyncScrollOffset, AsyncScrollOperationID,
    PendingAsyncScrollUpdates, StartedUserScroll,
};

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct AsyncScrollUpdateOutbox {
    pending_scroll_offsets: Vec<AsyncScrollOffset>,
    last_publication_sequence: u64,
    last_allocated_operation_id: AsyncScrollOperationID,
    completed_operation_ids: Vec<AsyncScrollOperationID>,
    operation_ids_taken_over_by_user_input: Vec<AsyncScrollOperationID>,
    started_user_scrolls: Vec<StartedUserScroll>,
    applied_scroll_requests: Vec<AppliedScrollRequest>,
    boxes_whose_user_scroll_gesture_ended: Vec<AsyncScrollNodeStableID>,
    published_user_scroll_gesture_state: UserScrollGestureState,
}

// What the compositor holds on to, published whenever it changes.
#[derive(Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct UserScrollGestureState {
    pub boxes_in_user_scroll_gesture: Vec<AsyncScrollNodeStableID>,
    pub wheel_latched_scroller: Option<AsyncScrollNodeStableID>,
}

impl AsyncScrollUpdateOutbox {
    pub fn allocate_operation_id(&mut self) -> AsyncScrollOperationID {
        self.last_allocated_operation_id = self.last_allocated_operation_id.wrapping_add(1);
        self.last_allocated_operation_id
    }

    pub fn complete_operation(&mut self, operation_id: AsyncScrollOperationID) {
        self.completed_operation_ids.push(operation_id);
    }

    pub fn note_operation_taken_over_by_user_input(&mut self, operation_id: AsyncScrollOperationID) {
        self.operation_ids_taken_over_by_user_input.push(operation_id);
    }

    pub fn record_started_user_scroll(&mut self, started_user_scroll: StartedUserScroll) {
        self.started_user_scrolls.push(started_user_scroll);
    }

    pub fn note_scroll_request_applied(&mut self, applied_scroll_request: AppliedScrollRequest) {
        self.applied_scroll_requests.push(applied_scroll_request);
    }
}

fn set_or_append_pending_scroll_offset(
    pending_scroll_offsets: &mut Vec<AsyncScrollOffset>,
    scroll_offset: &AsyncScrollOffset,
) {
    for existing in &mut *pending_scroll_offsets {
        if existing.stable_node_id == scroll_offset.stable_node_id {
            existing.merge_later_scroll(scroll_offset);
            return;
        }
    }
    pending_scroll_offsets.push(scroll_offset.clone());
}

impl AsyncScrollUpdateOutbox {
    pub fn record_scroll_offsets(&mut self, scroll_offsets: &[AsyncScrollOffset]) {
        for scroll_offset in scroll_offsets {
            set_or_append_pending_scroll_offset(&mut self.pending_scroll_offsets, scroll_offset);
        }
    }

    pub fn note_user_scroll_gesture_ended(&mut self, stable_node_ids: &[AsyncScrollNodeStableID]) {
        for &stable_node_id in stable_node_ids {
            if !self.boxes_whose_user_scroll_gesture_ended.contains(&stable_node_id) {
                self.boxes_whose_user_scroll_gesture_ended.push(stable_node_id);
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn has_updates(&self, user_scroll_gesture_state: &UserScrollGestureState) -> bool {
        !self.pending_scroll_offsets.is_empty()
            || !self.completed_operation_ids.is_empty()
            || !self.operation_ids_taken_over_by_user_input.is_empty()
            || !self.started_user_scrolls.is_empty()
            || !self.applied_scroll_requests.is_empty()
            || !self.boxes_whose_user_scroll_gesture_ended.is_empty()
            || *user_scroll_gesture_state != self.published_user_scroll_gesture_state
    }

    pub fn take_updates(&mut self, user_scroll_gesture_state: UserScrollGestureState) -> PendingAsyncScrollUpdates {
        self.last_publication_sequence = self.last_publication_sequence.wrapping_add(1);
        let updates = PendingAsyncScrollUpdates {
            document_id: None,
            sequence: self.last_publication_sequence,
            scroll_offsets: std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_scroll_offsets),
            completed_operation_ids: std::mem::take(&mut self.completed_operation_ids),
            operation_ids_taken_over_by_user_input: std::mem::take(&mut self.operation_ids_taken_over_by_user_input),
            started_user_scrolls: std::mem::take(&mut self.started_user_scrolls),
            applied_scroll_requests: std::mem::take(&mut self.applied_scroll_requests),
            boxes_whose_user_scroll_gesture_ended: std::mem::take(&mut self.boxes_whose_user_scroll_gesture_ended),
            boxes_in_user_scroll_gesture: user_scroll_gesture_state.boxes_in_user_scroll_gesture.clone(),
            wheel_latched_scroller: user_scroll_gesture_state.wheel_latched_scroller,
        };
        self.published_user_scroll_gesture_state = user_scroll_gesture_state;
        updates
    }
}

/*

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! The backing stores of a context: the surfaces its frames are rendered into, each of which is in turn rendered into,
//! shown, and free again. The surfaces and the images they share with the presentation are made by the raster host.

use crate::surfaces::painting_surface::PaintingSurface;
use crate::surfaces::presentable_surface::PresentableSurface;
use libgfx_rust::IntSize;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::ptr::NonNull;
use std::rc::Rc;

/// Who shows the backing stores of a context.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum StorePublication {
    #[default]
    Unpublished,
    /// The presentation shows the stores, and releases each when it shows another.
    Published,
    /// The compositor shows the stores itself, in a remote layer, so a store is replaced on screen by the next one.
    ShownInRemoteLayer,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum StoreResizeOutcome {
    Unchanged,
    /// The stores were reallocated, and nothing that shows them was given them.
    ReallocatedOffscreen,
    /// The presentation or the remote layer that shows the stores was given the new ones.
    ReallocatedForViewer,
    /// The stores of a remote layer could not be allocated.
    Failed,
}

/// How a store is made.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum StoreKind {
    /// A surface nobody else sees.
    Offscreen,
    /// A bitmap in memory shared with the presentation, which a GPU surface is copied into on flush where there is one.
    SharedBitmap,
    /// A GPU image shared with the presentation, where the platform has those.
    SharedGpuImage,
    /// A surface the window server of the remote layer that shows the context shows by itself.
    ShownByWindowServer,
}

/// The memory of a store that is shared with the presentation, which is C++ and which the store owns.
pub struct SharedImageBuffer {
    buffer: NonNull<c_void>,
    is_in_use: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void) -> bool,
    destroy: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
}

impl SharedImageBuffer {
    fn is_in_use(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The buffer is live for as long as this.
        unsafe { (self.is_in_use)(self.buffer.as_ptr()) }
    }
}

impl Drop for SharedImageBuffer {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This owns the buffer.
        unsafe { (self.destroy)(self.buffer.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

/// An image of a store for the presentation to import, which is C++, and which is destroyed unless it is handed over.
pub struct SharedImageToPublish {
    image: NonNull<c_void>,
    destroy: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
}

impl SharedImageToPublish {
    /// Hands the image over to whoever publishes it.
    pub fn into_raw(self) -> *mut c_void {
        let image = self.image.as_ptr();
        std::mem::forget(self);
        image
    }
}

impl Drop for SharedImageToPublish {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This owns the image.
        unsafe { (self.destroy)(self.image.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

/// A store the raster host made, as it hands it over: one reference to each surface, and the C++ objects with the
/// functions that answer for and destroy them.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct FfiNewStore {
    pub surface: *const PaintingSurface,
    /// Null for a store the window server does not show by itself.
    pub window_server_surface: *const PresentableSurface,
    /// Null for a store whose memory is not shared with the presentation.
    pub shared_image_buffer: *mut c_void,
    pub shared_image_buffer_is_in_use: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void) -> bool>,
    pub destroy_shared_image_buffer: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void)>,
    /// Null for a store the presentation does not import.
    pub shared_image: *mut c_void,
    pub destroy_shared_image: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void)>,
}

impl Default for FfiNewStore {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            surface: std::ptr::null(),
            window_server_surface: std::ptr::null(),
            shared_image_buffer: std::ptr::null_mut(),
            shared_image_buffer_is_in_use: None,
            destroy_shared_image_buffer: None,
            shared_image: std::ptr::null_mut(),
            destroy_shared_image: None,
        }
    }
}

pub struct NewStore {
    pub surface: Rc<PaintingSurface>,
    pub window_server_surface: Option<Rc<PresentableSurface>>,
    pub shared_image_buffer: Option<SharedImageBuffer>,
    pub shared_image: Option<SharedImageToPublish>,
}

impl NewStore {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Every pointer of the store must be live and handed over, with the functions that go with it.
    pub unsafe fn adopt(store: FfiNewStore) -> Option<NewStore> {
        // SAFETY: The caller hands over one reference to each surface, or null.
        let (surface, window_server_surface) = unsafe {
            (
                PaintingSurface::adopted_from_ffi(store.surface),
                PresentableSurface::adopted_from_ffi(store.window_server_surface),
            )
        };
        let shared_image_buffer = NonNull::new(store.shared_image_buffer).map(|buffer| SharedImageBuffer {
            buffer,
            is_in_use: store
                .shared_image_buffer_is_in_use
                .expect("a shared buffer comes with its use check"),
            destroy: store
                .destroy_shared_image_buffer
                .expect("a shared buffer comes with its destroy function"),
        });
        let shared_image = NonNull::new(store.shared_image).map(|image| SharedImageToPublish {
            image,
            destroy: store
                .destroy_shared_image
                .expect("a shared image comes with its destroy function"),
        });
        Some(NewStore {
            surface: surface?,
            window_server_surface,
            shared_image_buffer,
            shared_image,
        })
    }
}

/// Makes the stores of a context, or answers none where one could not be made.
pub trait StoreFactory {
    fn create_store(&mut self, kind: StoreKind, size: IntSize) -> Option<NewStore>;
}

impl<F: FnMut(StoreKind, IntSize) -> Option<NewStore>> StoreFactory for F {
    fn create_store(&mut self, kind: StoreKind, size: IntSize) -> Option<NewStore> {
        self(kind, size)
    }
}

/// Stores that were allocated or added, with the images the presentation imports, if it shows the stores.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Publication {
    pub bitmap_ids: Vec<i32>,
    pub shared_images: Vec<SharedImageToPublish>,
}

pub enum AllocationOutcome {
    /// Nothing that shows the stores was given them.
    Offscreen,
    /// The presentation or the remote layer that shows the stores is to be given the new ones.
    ForViewer(Publication),
    /// The stores of a remote layer could not be made.
    Failed,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum StoreState {
    Available,
    Rendering,
    Presented,
}

struct BackingStore {
    surface: Rc<PaintingSurface>,
    shared_image_buffer: Option<SharedImageBuffer>,
    window_server_surface: Option<Rc<PresentableSurface>>,
    bitmap_id: i32,
    state: StoreState,
    was_shown_on_screen: bool,
    was_rendered_into_since_last_retirement_check: bool,
}

impl BackingStore {
    fn new(store: NewStore, bitmap_id: i32, state: StoreState) -> (BackingStore, Option<SharedImageToPublish>) {
        (
            BackingStore {
                surface: store.surface,
                shared_image_buffer: store.shared_image_buffer,
                window_server_surface: store.window_server_surface,
                bitmap_id,
                state,
                was_shown_on_screen: false,
                was_rendered_into_since_last_retirement_check: false,
            },
            store.shared_image,
        )
    }

    fn shared_surface_is_in_use(&self) -> bool {
        if let Some(window_server_surface) = &self.window_server_surface {
            return window_server_surface.is_read_by_window_server();
        }
        // The share exported to the presentation counts as use too, so a store published a moment ago reads as in use
        // until the presentation imported it.
        self.shared_image_buffer
            .as_ref()
            .is_some_and(SharedImageBuffer::is_in_use)
    }

    fn can_be_rendered_into(&self) -> bool {
        if self.state != StoreState::Available {
            return false;
        }
        // Only a store shown on screen is handed to the window server, so whatever uses a store that never was is the
        // share on its way to the presentation.
        if !self.was_shown_on_screen {
            return true;
        }
        !self.shared_surface_is_in_use()
    }
}

const MAXIMUM_BACKING_STORE_COUNT: usize = 8;
const RESIZE_PADDING: i32 = 256;

// A store shown on screen is let go of when the next one is shown, but on macOS the window server is handed the surface
// itself, and keeps reading it until it has composited the replacement. A third store lets the compositor keep
// rendering through that window instead of waiting for it.
fn backing_store_count_for(publication: StorePublication) -> usize {
    if cfg!(target_os = "macos") && publication != StorePublication::Unpublished {
        return 3;
    }
    2
}

// Whether the memory of a 32-bit bitmap of the size could not be addressed.
fn bitmap_size_would_overflow(size: IntSize) -> bool {
    if size.width < 0 || size.height < 0 || size.width > i32::from(u16::MAX) || size.height > i32::from(u16::MAX) {
        return true;
    }
    (size.width * 4).checked_mul(size.height).is_none()
}

/// An allocation of new stores of the size, which replaces the stores there are.
pub struct Allocation {
    size: IntSize,
    bitmap_ids: Vec<i32>,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct BackingStores {
    next_bitmap_id: i32,
    // What the stores were allocated for, which a new allocation replaces. Empty when the stores need allocating.
    allocated_size: IntSize,
    store_size: IntSize,
    publication: StorePublication,
    initial_store_count: usize,
    stores: Vec<BackingStore>,
    rendering_store_index: Option<usize>,
    latest_rendered_store_index: Option<usize>,
}

impl BackingStores {
    pub fn invalidate(&mut self) {
        self.allocated_size = IntSize::default();
    }

    pub fn publication(&self) -> StorePublication {
        self.publication
    }

    pub fn is_valid(&self) -> bool {
        !self.stores.is_empty()
    }

    pub fn is_rendering(&self) -> bool {
        self.rendering_store_index.is_some()
    }

    pub fn has_available_store(&self) -> bool {
        self.stores.iter().any(BackingStore::can_be_rendered_into)
    }

    pub fn has_surplus_stores(&self) -> bool {
        self.stores.len() > self.initial_store_count
    }

    pub fn resize_if_needed(
        &mut self,
        viewport_size: IntSize,
        window_resize_in_progress: bool,
        publication: StorePublication,
    ) -> Option<Allocation> {
        if viewport_size.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let mut allocation_size = viewport_size;
        let mut needs_allocation = self.allocated_size.is_empty();
        if window_resize_in_progress {
            // The stores are padded so that they need not be reallocated while the window is resized. Ones that still
            // hold the viewport are kept.
            allocation_size = IntSize {
                width: viewport_size.width + RESIZE_PADDING,
                height: viewport_size.height + RESIZE_PADDING,
            };
            needs_allocation |= !(self.allocated_size.width >= viewport_size.width
                && self.allocated_size.height >= viewport_size.height);
        } else {
            needs_allocation |= self.allocated_size != viewport_size;
        }
        if !needs_allocation {
            return None;
        }
        self.allocated_size = allocation_size;
        let bitmap_ids = (0..backing_store_count_for(publication))
            .map(|_| self.take_bitmap_id())
            .collect();
        Some(Allocation {
            size: allocation_size,
            bitmap_ids,
        })
    }

    fn take_bitmap_id(&mut self) -> i32 {
        let bitmap_id = self.next_bitmap_id;
        self.next_bitmap_id += 1;
        bitmap_id
    }

    pub fn allocate(
        &mut self,
        allocation: Allocation,
        publication: StorePublication,
        shares_gpu_images: bool,
        factory: &mut dyn StoreFactory,
    ) -> AllocationOutcome {
        self.stores.clear();
        self.rendering_store_index = None;
        self.latest_rendered_store_index = None;
        self.publication = publication;
        if bitmap_size_would_overflow(allocation.size) {
            return AllocationOutcome::Offscreen;
        }
        self.store_size = allocation.size;
        self.initial_store_count = allocation.bitmap_ids.len();

        match publication {
            StorePublication::Unpublished => {
                for &bitmap_id in &allocation.bitmap_ids {
                    let Some(store) = factory.create_store(StoreKind::Offscreen, allocation.size) else {
                        self.stores.clear();
                        self.invalidate();
                        break;
                    };
                    self.stores
                        .push(BackingStore::new(store, bitmap_id, StoreState::Available).0);
                }
                AllocationOutcome::Offscreen
            }
            StorePublication::ShownInRemoteLayer => {
                for &bitmap_id in &allocation.bitmap_ids {
                    let Some(store) = factory.create_store(StoreKind::ShownByWindowServer, allocation.size) else {
                        self.stores.clear();
                        self.invalidate();
                        return AllocationOutcome::Failed;
                    };
                    self.stores
                        .push(BackingStore::new(store, bitmap_id, StoreState::Available).0);
                }
                AllocationOutcome::ForViewer(Publication {
                    bitmap_ids: allocation.bitmap_ids,
                    shared_images: Vec::new(),
                })
            }
            StorePublication::Published => {
                if shares_gpu_images
                    && let Some(publication) = self.allocate_published(&allocation, StoreKind::SharedGpuImage, factory)
                {
                    return AllocationOutcome::ForViewer(publication);
                }
                match self.allocate_published(&allocation, StoreKind::SharedBitmap, factory) {
                    Some(publication) => AllocationOutcome::ForViewer(publication),
                    None => {
                        self.invalidate();
                        AllocationOutcome::Offscreen
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // The presentation installs the first published store as its first front store, and keeps it until it presents
    // another one.
    fn allocate_published(
        &mut self,
        allocation: &Allocation,
        kind: StoreKind,
        factory: &mut dyn StoreFactory,
    ) -> Option<Publication> {
        let mut shared_images = Vec::with_capacity(allocation.bitmap_ids.len());
        for (index, &bitmap_id) in allocation.bitmap_ids.iter().enumerate() {
            let state = if index == 0 {
                StoreState::Presented
            } else {
                StoreState::Available
            };
            let Some(store) = factory.create_store(kind, allocation.size) else {
                self.stores.clear();
                return None;
            };
            let (store, shared_image) = BackingStore::new(store, bitmap_id, state);
            self.stores.push(store);
            shared_images.push(shared_image.expect("a published store has an image for the presentation"));
        }
        Some(Publication {
            bitmap_ids: allocation.bitmap_ids.clone(),
            shared_images,
        })
    }

    // GPU stores shared with the presentation are only ever allocated together, as the presentation installs them.
    fn stores_can_be_added_one_at_a_time(&self) -> bool {
        let Some(first) = self.stores.first() else {
            return false;
        };
        self.publication != StorePublication::Published || first.shared_image_buffer.is_some()
    }

    fn kind_of_added_stores(&self) -> StoreKind {
        match self.publication {
            StorePublication::Unpublished => StoreKind::Offscreen,
            StorePublication::Published => StoreKind::SharedBitmap,
            StorePublication::ShownInRemoteLayer => StoreKind::ShownByWindowServer,
        }
    }

    fn add_store(&mut self, factory: &mut dyn StoreFactory, publication: &mut Publication) -> bool {
        let Some(store) = factory.create_store(self.kind_of_added_stores(), self.store_size) else {
            return false;
        };
        let bitmap_id = self.take_bitmap_id();
        let (store, shared_image) = BackingStore::new(store, bitmap_id, StoreState::Available);
        self.stores.push(store);
        publication.bitmap_ids.push(bitmap_id);
        if self.publication == StorePublication::Published {
            publication
                .shared_images
                .push(shared_image.expect("a published store has an image for the presentation"));
        }
        true
    }

    /// The window server lets go of a store some time after the presentation replaced it on screen, which at high
    /// refresh rates can be later than the next frame is due. Rather than hold that frame back, it is given a store of
    /// its own. While the presentation has yet to take a frame, or to release a store, there is no telling what the
    /// window server holds, and the frame waits as it always did.
    pub fn add_store_if_window_server_still_reads_every_released_store(
        &mut self,
        factory: &mut dyn StoreFactory,
    ) -> Option<Publication> {
        let latest_rendered_store_index = self.latest_rendered_store_index?;
        if self.is_rendering() || self.stores.len() >= MAXIMUM_BACKING_STORE_COUNT {
            return None;
        }
        for (index, store) in self.stores.iter().enumerate() {
            if store.shared_image_buffer.is_none() && store.window_server_surface.is_none() {
                return None;
            }
            let presentation_shows_store = index == latest_rendered_store_index;
            if presentation_shows_store && store.state != StoreState::Presented {
                return None;
            }
            if !presentation_shows_store && (store.state != StoreState::Available || store.can_be_rendered_into()) {
                return None;
            }
        }
        let mut publication = Publication::default();
        self.add_store(factory, &mut publication).then_some(publication)
    }

    fn remove_store(&mut self, index: usize) -> i32 {
        let store = self.stores.remove(index);
        if let Some(latest) = self.latest_rendered_store_index
            && latest > index
        {
            self.latest_rendered_store_index = Some(latest - 1);
        }
        store.bitmap_id
    }

    /// A store added for a burst of frames is given back once a whole interval between two checks went by without it
    /// being rendered into. The stores that stay are the ones first in line for the next frame. Answers the stores
    /// that were retired.
    pub fn retire_idle_surplus_stores(&mut self) -> Vec<i32> {
        let mut retired_bitmap_ids = Vec::new();
        if self.is_rendering() {
            return retired_bitmap_ids;
        }
        for index in (0..self.stores.len()).rev() {
            if !self.has_surplus_stores() {
                break;
            }
            let store = &self.stores[index];
            if self.latest_rendered_store_index == Some(index)
                || store.state != StoreState::Available
                || store.was_rendered_into_since_last_retirement_check
                || store.shared_surface_is_in_use()
            {
                continue;
            }
            retired_bitmap_ids.push(self.remove_store(index));
        }
        for store in &mut self.stores {
            store.was_rendered_into_since_last_retirement_check = false;
        }
        retired_bitmap_ids
    }

    /// A hidden context keeps only the store that holds its latest frame, which is what shows it until it is shown
    /// again, and what a snapshot of it is taken from. Before any frame, the store reserved as the presentation's first
    /// front store stays too. Answers the stores that were retired.
    pub fn retire_stores_except_the_latest_rendered(&mut self) -> Vec<i32> {
        let mut retired_bitmap_ids = Vec::new();
        if self.is_rendering() {
            return retired_bitmap_ids;
        }
        for index in (0..self.stores.len()).rev() {
            let store = &self.stores[index];
            if self.latest_rendered_store_index == Some(index)
                || store.state != StoreState::Available
                || store.shared_surface_is_in_use()
            {
                continue;
            }
            retired_bitmap_ids.push(self.remove_store(index));
        }
        // Stores that never held a frame are allocated anew when the context is shown.
        if self.stores.is_empty() {
            self.invalidate();
        }
        retired_bitmap_ids
    }

    /// Whether a store that the hidden context does not keep is still rendered into, shown, or read by the window
    /// server, and can be retired once it no longer is.
    pub fn has_stores_left_to_retire_while_hidden(&self) -> bool {
        self.stores.iter().enumerate().any(|(index, store)| {
            if self.latest_rendered_store_index == Some(index) {
                return false;
            }
            match store.state {
                StoreState::Rendering => true,
                // Before any frame, a presented store is the one reserved as the presentation's first front store,
                // which the presentation holds until it is shown a frame.
                StoreState::Presented => self.latest_rendered_store_index.is_some(),
                StoreState::Available => store.shared_surface_is_in_use(),
            }
        })
    }

    /// Gives a context that was shown again the stores it had before it was hidden. Answers none where they can't be
    /// added to the ones it kept, or one could not be made, as the context then needs a whole new allocation.
    pub fn add_stores_up_to_initial_count(&mut self, factory: &mut dyn StoreFactory) -> Option<Publication> {
        if !self.stores_can_be_added_one_at_a_time() {
            return None;
        }
        let mut publication = Publication::default();
        while self.stores.len() < self.initial_store_count {
            if !self.add_store(factory, &mut publication) {
                return None;
            }
        }
        Some(publication)
    }

    pub fn acquire_render_target(&mut self) -> Option<(i32, Rc<PaintingSurface>)> {
        assert!(
            self.rendering_store_index.is_none(),
            "one store is rendered into at a time"
        );
        let index = self.stores.iter().position(BackingStore::can_be_rendered_into)?;
        let store = &mut self.stores[index];
        store.state = StoreState::Rendering;
        store.was_rendered_into_since_last_retirement_check = true;
        self.rendering_store_index = Some(index);
        Some((store.bitmap_id, store.surface.clone()))
    }

    pub fn complete_rendering(&mut self, bitmap_id: i32) {
        let index = self.rendering_store_index.take().expect("a store is rendered into");
        assert_eq!(
            self.stores[index].bitmap_id, bitmap_id,
            "the store rendered into completes"
        );
        assert_eq!(self.stores[index].state, StoreState::Rendering);
        let presentation_releases_presented_stores = self.publication == StorePublication::Published;
        if !presentation_releases_presented_stores && let Some(latest) = self.latest_rendered_store_index {
            self.stores[latest].state = StoreState::Available;
        }
        let store = &mut self.stores[index];
        store.state = StoreState::Presented;
        if self.publication != StorePublication::Unpublished {
            store.was_shown_on_screen = true;
        }
        self.latest_rendered_store_index = Some(index);
    }

    /// Answers whether a store that was presented became available.
    pub fn release_store(&mut self, bitmap_id: i32) -> bool {
        let Some(store) = self
            .stores
            .iter_mut()
            .find(|store| store.bitmap_id == bitmap_id && store.state == StoreState::Presented)
        else {
            return false;
        };
        store.state = StoreState::Available;
        true
    }

    pub fn release_all_presented_stores(&mut self) {
        for store in &mut self.stores {
            if store.state == StoreState::Presented {
                store.state = StoreState::Available;
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn latest_rendered_surface(&self) -> Option<Rc<PaintingSurface>> {
        Some(self.stores[self.latest_rendered_store_index?].surface.clone())
    }

    pub fn window_server_surface_of_latest_rendered_store(&self) -> Option<&Rc<PresentableSurface>> {
        self.stores[self.latest_rendered_store_index?]
            .window_server_surface
            .as_ref()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::surfaces::painting_surface::testing::surface_for_testing;
    use std::cell::Cell;

    unsafe extern "C" fn destroy_nothing(_: *mut c_void) {}

    thread_local! {
        static SHARED_BUFFERS_IN_USE: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) };
    }

    unsafe extern "C" fn shared_buffer_in_use(_: *mut c_void) -> bool {
        SHARED_BUFFERS_IN_USE.with(Cell::get)
    }

    fn factory(fail_kind: Option<StoreKind>) -> impl FnMut(StoreKind, IntSize) -> Option<NewStore> {
        move |kind, size| {
            if Some(kind) == fail_kind {
                return None;
            }
            let shares_memory = kind == StoreKind::SharedBitmap;
            let published = matches!(kind, StoreKind::SharedBitmap | StoreKind::SharedGpuImage);
            Some(NewStore {
                surface: surface_for_testing(size, 0),
                window_server_surface: None,
                shared_image_buffer: shares_memory.then(|| SharedImageBuffer {
                    buffer: NonNull::dangling(),
                    is_in_use: shared_buffer_in_use,
                    destroy: destroy_nothing,
                }),
                shared_image: published.then(|| SharedImageToPublish {
                    image: NonNull::dangling(),
                    destroy: destroy_nothing,
                }),
            })
        }
    }

    const VIEWPORT: IntSize = IntSize { width: 100, height: 50 };

    // Each store completes its frame before the next is rendered into, as many as the platform allocates.
    fn render_into_every_available_store(stores: &mut BackingStores) -> Vec<i32> {
        let mut rendered = Vec::new();
        while let Some((bitmap_id, _)) = stores.acquire_render_target() {
            stores.complete_rendering(bitmap_id);
            rendered.push(bitmap_id);
        }
        rendered
    }

    fn allocated(publication: StorePublication, shares_gpu_images: bool) -> (BackingStores, AllocationOutcome) {
        let mut stores = BackingStores::default();
        let allocation = stores.resize_if_needed(VIEWPORT, false, publication).unwrap();
        let outcome = stores.allocate(allocation, publication, shares_gpu_images, &mut factory(None));
        (stores, outcome)
    }

    #[test]
    fn stores_are_reallocated_only_when_the_viewport_changes() {
        let (mut stores, _) = allocated(StorePublication::Unpublished, false);
        assert!(
            stores
                .resize_if_needed(VIEWPORT, false, StorePublication::Unpublished)
                .is_none()
        );
        let larger = IntSize { width: 120, height: 50 };
        assert!(
            stores
                .resize_if_needed(larger, false, StorePublication::Unpublished)
                .is_some()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn stores_are_padded_while_the_window_is_resized() {
        let mut stores = BackingStores::default();
        let allocation = stores
            .resize_if_needed(VIEWPORT, true, StorePublication::Unpublished)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            allocation.size,
            IntSize {
                width: 356,
                height: 306
            }
        );
        stores.allocate(allocation, StorePublication::Unpublished, false, &mut factory(None));
        let a_bit_larger = IntSize { width: 150, height: 80 };
        assert!(
            stores
                .resize_if_needed(a_bit_larger, true, StorePublication::Unpublished)
                .is_none()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_first_published_store_is_held_by_the_presentation() {
        let (mut stores, outcome) = allocated(StorePublication::Published, false);
        let AllocationOutcome::ForViewer(publication) = outcome else {
            panic!("published stores go to the presentation");
        };
        assert_eq!(publication.bitmap_ids.len(), publication.shared_images.len());
        let (bitmap_id, _) = stores.acquire_render_target().unwrap();
        assert_ne!(bitmap_id, publication.bitmap_ids[0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shared_gpu_images_fall_back_to_shared_bitmaps() {
        let mut stores = BackingStores::default();
        let allocation = stores
            .resize_if_needed(VIEWPORT, false, StorePublication::Published)
            .unwrap();
        let outcome = stores.allocate(
            allocation,
            StorePublication::Published,
            true,
            &mut factory(Some(StoreKind::SharedGpuImage)),
        );
        assert!(matches!(outcome, AllocationOutcome::ForViewer(_)));
        assert!(stores.stores_can_be_added_one_at_a_time());
    }

    #[test]
    fn stores_of_a_remote_layer_that_cannot_be_made_fail_the_allocation() {
        let mut stores = BackingStores::default();
        let allocation = stores
            .resize_if_needed(VIEWPORT, false, StorePublication::ShownInRemoteLayer)
            .unwrap();
        let outcome = stores.allocate(
            allocation,
            StorePublication::ShownInRemoteLayer,
            false,
            &mut factory(Some(StoreKind::ShownByWindowServer)),
        );
        assert!(matches!(outcome, AllocationOutcome::Failed));
        assert!(!stores.is_valid());
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unpublished_store_becomes_available_once_the_next_frame_completes() {
        let (mut stores, _) = allocated(StorePublication::Unpublished, false);
        let (first, _) = stores.acquire_render_target().unwrap();
        stores.complete_rendering(first);
        let (second, _) = stores.acquire_render_target().unwrap();
        assert_ne!(first, second);
        stores.complete_rendering(second);
        let (third, _) = stores.acquire_render_target().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(third, first);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_published_store_waits_for_the_presentation_to_release_it() {
        let (mut stores, _) = allocated(StorePublication::Published, false);
        let rendered = render_into_every_available_store(&mut stores);
        assert!(!stores.has_available_store());
        let latest = *rendered.last().unwrap();
        assert!(stores.release_store(latest));
        assert!(!stores.release_store(latest));
        assert!(stores.has_available_store());
    }

    #[test]
    fn surplus_stores_are_retired_after_an_idle_interval() {
        let (mut stores, _) = allocated(StorePublication::Published, false);
        let (rendered, _) = stores.acquire_render_target().unwrap();
        stores.complete_rendering(rendered);
        let first_front_store_bitmap_id = 0;
        assert!(stores.release_store(first_front_store_bitmap_id));
        // A store that is not shown is free, so no store is added.
        assert!(
            stores
                .add_store_if_window_server_still_reads_every_released_store(&mut factory(None))
                .is_none()
        );
        // Every store that is not shown was shown before, and the window server still reads it.
        SHARED_BUFFERS_IN_USE.with(|in_use| in_use.set(true));
        let latest_rendered_store_index = stores.latest_rendered_store_index;
        for (index, store) in stores.stores.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            if Some(index) != latest_rendered_store_index {
                store.was_shown_on_screen = true;
            }
        }
        let added = stores
            .add_store_if_window_server_still_reads_every_released_store(&mut factory(None))
            .unwrap();
        SHARED_BUFFERS_IN_USE.with(|in_use| in_use.set(false));
        assert_eq!(added.bitmap_ids.len(), 1);
        assert!(stores.has_surplus_stores());
        // The added store was not rendered into since it was added, so it goes at the next check.
        assert_eq!(stores.retire_idle_surplus_stores(), added.bitmap_ids);
        assert!(!stores.has_surplus_stores());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_hidden_context_keeps_only_its_latest_frame_and_gets_its_stores_back() {
        let (mut stores, _) = allocated(StorePublication::Unpublished, false);
        let (rendered, _) = stores.acquire_render_target().unwrap();
        stores.complete_rendering(rendered);
        assert_eq!(stores.retire_stores_except_the_latest_rendered().len(), 1);
        assert!(!stores.has_stores_left_to_retire_while_hidden());
        let restored = stores.add_stores_up_to_initial_count(&mut factory(None)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(restored.bitmap_ids.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            stores.latest_rendered_surface().map(|surface| surface.size()),
            Some(VIEWPORT)
        );
    }
}

/*
