}

/// The entry points of the host and the object they are called on: `Compositor::RustFFI::FfiCompositorCoreHost`.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FfiCompositorCoreHost {
    pub host: *mut c_void,
    pub post_message_to_web_content:
        unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u64, ak::Span<'_, u8>, ak::Span<'_, RawAttachment>),
    pub post_message_to_render_clock_of_web_content:
        unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u64, ak::Span<'_, u8>, ak::Span<'_, RawAttachment>),
    pub post_message_to_presentation:
        unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u64, ak::Span<'_, u8>, ak::Span<'_, RawAttachment>),
    /// Arguments: the number of the timer, and the delay in nanoseconds. Setting a timer again replaces its delay, and
    /// a timer that fires calls `compositor_core_timer_fired` with its number.
    pub set_timer: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u64, i64),
    pub cancel_timer: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u64),
    /// The timer is not set again, so the host forgets it.
    pub destroy_timer: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u64),
    /// Arguments: the context, whether a font family is given, the font family, the font size in points, the device
    /// pixel ratio, the text, and what receives the shaped label, which is not called where no font draws the label.
    pub shape_overlay_label: unsafe extern "C" fn(
        *mut c_void,
        u64,
        bool,
        ak::Span<'_, u8>,
        f32,
        f64,
        ak::Span<'_, u8>,
        *mut c_void,
        unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const FfiOverlayLabel<'_>),
    ),
}

type PostEncodedMessage = unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u64, ak::Span<'_, u8>, ak::Span<'_, RawAttachment>);

pub struct Host {
    ffi: FfiCompositorCoreHost,
    display_tick_requests: RefCell<Vec<CompositorContextId>>,
    timer_numbers: RefCell<TimerNumbers>,
}

impl Host {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `ffi.host` must outlive the `Host`, and none of its entry points may call back into the core.
    pub unsafe fn new(ffi: FfiCompositorCoreHost) -> Self {
        Self {
            ffi,
            display_tick_requests: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            timer_numbers: RefCell::default(),
        }
    }

    fn post<M: EndpointMessage>(&self, post_encoded_message: PostEncodedMessage, receiver_id: u64, message: M) {
        let (bytes, attachments) = message
            .encode_message()
            .expect("a message of the compositor fits an IPC message");
        let raw_attachments: Vec<RawAttachment> = attachments.into_iter().map(RawAttachment::from_attachment).collect();
        // SAFETY: The host outlives this, copies the bytes and takes every attachment over.
        unsafe {
            post_encoded_message(
                self.ffi.host,
                receiver_id,
                ak::Span::new(&bytes),
                ak::Span::new(&raw_attachments),
            );
        }
    }

    /// A message for a client that is gone is dropped.
    pub fn post_to_web_content<M: EndpointMessage>(&self, client_id: WebContentClientId, message: M) {
        self.post(self.ffi.post_message_to_web_content, client_id.0, message);
    }

    /// A client without a render clock channel hears nothing.
    pub fn post_to_render_clock_of_web_content<M: EndpointMessage>(&self, client_id: WebContentClientId, message: M) {
        self.post(
            self.ffi.post_message_to_render_clock_of_web_content,
            client_id.0,
            message,
        );
    }

    /// A message for a presentation that is gone is dropped.
    pub fn post_to_presentation<M: EndpointMessage>(&self, presentation_id: PresentationId, message: M) {
        self.post(self.ffi.post_message_to_presentation, presentation_id.0, message);
    }

    /// Display ticks reach a context whose scroll and input logic says it needs animation frames, while it is visible.
    /// The core asks for them once the call that wants them is done.
    pub fn request_display_ticks(&self, context_id: CompositorContextId) {
        self.display_tick_requests.borrow_mut().push(context_id);
    }

    /// The contexts that asked for display ticks since the last call.
    pub fn take_display_tick_requests(&self) -> Vec<CompositorContextId> {
        std::mem::take(&mut *self.display_tick_requests.borrow_mut())
    }

    /// Each timer of a context fires once after the delay, and setting it again replaces the delay.
    pub fn set_timer(&self, context_id: CompositorContextId, timer: ContextTimer, delay: Duration) {
        self.schedule(Timer::Context(context_id, timer), delay);
    }

    pub fn cancel_timer(&self, context_id: CompositorContextId, timer: ContextTimer) {
        self.unschedule(Timer::Context(context_id, timer));
    }

    pub fn schedule(&self, timer: Timer, delay: Duration) {
        let number = {
            let mut numbers = self.timer_numbers.borrow_mut();
            match numbers.number_of_timer.get(&timer) {
                Some(&number) => number,
                None => {
                    numbers.next_number += 1;
                    let number = numbers.next_number;
                    numbers.number_of_timer.insert(timer, number);
                    numbers.timer_of_number.insert(number, timer);
                    number
                }
            }
        };
        // SAFETY: The host outlives this.
        unsafe { (self.ffi.set_timer)(self.ffi.host, number, delay.nanoseconds()) };
    }

    pub fn unschedule(&self, timer: Timer) {
        let Some(number) = self.timer_numbers.borrow().number_of_timer.get(&timer).copied() else {
            return;
        };
        // SAFETY: The host outlives this.
        unsafe { (self.ffi.cancel_timer)(self.ffi.host, number) };
    }

    /// Forgets the timers that match, which are not set again.
    pub fn destroy_timers(&self, matches: impl Fn(&Timer) -> bool) {
        let numbers: Vec<u64> = {
            let mut timer_numbers = self.timer_numbers.borrow_mut();
            let TimerNumbers {
                number_of_timer,
                timer_of_number,
                ..
            } = &mut *timer_numbers;
            let numbers: Vec<u64> = timer_of_number
                .iter()
                .filter(|(_, timer)| matches(timer))
                .map(|(&number, _)| number)
                .collect();
            for number in &numbers {
                if let Some(timer) = timer_of_number.remove(number) {
                    number_of_timer.remove(&timer);
                }
            }
            numbers
        };
        for number in numbers {
            // SAFETY: The host outlives this.
            unsafe { (self.ffi.destroy_timer)(self.ffi.host, number) };
        }
    }

    pub fn timer_of_number(&self, number: u64) -> Option<Timer> {
        self.timer_numbers.borrow().timer_of_number.get(&number).copied()
    }

    pub fn overlay_label_shaper(&self, context_id: CompositorContextId) -> ContextOverlayLabelShaper<'_> {
        ContextOverlayLabelShaper { host: self, context_id }
    }
}

pub struct ContextOverlayLabelShaper<'a> {
    host: &'a Host,
    context_id: CompositorContextId,
}

impl OverlayLabelShaper for ContextOverlayLabelShaper<'_> {
    fn shape_overlay_label(
        &self,
        font_family: Option<&str>,
        font_size_in_points: f32,
        device_pixel_ratio: f64,
        text: &str,
    ) -> Option<OverlayLabel> {
        unsafe extern "C" fn receive(receiver: *mut c_void, label: *const FfiOverlayLabel<'_>) {
            // SAFETY: The receiver is the label below, and the host lends the shaped label for the call.
            let (receiver, label) = unsafe { (&mut *receiver.cast::<Option<OverlayLabel>>(), &*label) };
            *receiver = Some(OverlayLabel {
                font_id: label.font_id,
                glyph_ids: label.glyph_ids.as_slice().to_vec(),
                glyph_x_positions: label.glyph_x_positions.as_slice().to_vec(),
                width: label.width,
                ascent: label.ascent,
                descent: label.descent,
                font_ascent: label.font_ascent,
            });
        }
        let mut label: Option<OverlayLabel> = None;
        // SAFETY: The host outlives this, shapes synchronously and never calls back into the core.
        unsafe {
            (self.host.ffi.shape_overlay_label)(
                self.host.ffi.host,
                self.context_id.0,
                font_family.is_some(),
                ak::Span::new(font_family.unwrap_or_default().as_bytes()),
                font_size_in_points,
                device_pixel_ratio,
                ak::Span::new(text.as_bytes()),
                (&raw mut label).cast(),
                receive,
            );
        }
        label
    }
}

/*

use libcompositing_rust::scrolling::{KeyCode, KeyModifier, WheelDeltaPrecision};

pub fn is_keyboard_scroll_key(key: KeyCode, modifiers: u32) -> bool {
    match key {
        KeyCode::Key_Space => {
            modifiers & !(KeyModifier::Mod_Shift | KeyModifier::Mod_Keypad).0 == KeyModifier::Mod_None.0
        }
        KeyCode::Key_Up | KeyCode::Key_Down => {
            let modifiers = modifiers & !KeyModifier::Mod_Keypad.0;
            modifiers == KeyModifier::Mod_None.0 || modifiers == KeyModifier::Mod_PlatformCtrl.0
        }
        KeyCode::Key_PageUp
        | KeyCode::Key_PageDown
        | KeyCode::Key_Left
        | KeyCode::Key_Right
        | KeyCode::Key_Home
        | KeyCode::Key_End => modifiers & !KeyModifier::Mod_Keypad.0 == KeyModifier::Mod_None.0,
        _ => false,
    }
}

// Besides its pixel delta, wheel input counts how far the wheel turned in 120ths of a tick, the unit of the legacy
// wheelDelta. A tick is a wheel notch, or one line on platforms that accelerate the wheel by whole lines. Input that
// reports only a pixel delta counts its ticks from that: a notch scrolls three 40-pixel lines, and precise input has
// no notches, so it counts one tick per 40-pixel line step.
// INTEROP: For macOS touchpad scrolling, Blink, WebKit, and Gecko all report 3 units per pixel; Blink and WebKit
//          truncate, Gecko rounds. For the ctrl-wheel events of a pinch, WebKit and Gecko also report 3 units per
//          pixel, while Blink reports 120 units per event.
pub fn wheel_tick_120ths_from_pixel_delta(pixel_delta: f64, precision: WheelDeltaPrecision) -> f64 {
    const TICK_120THS_PER_TICK: f64 = 120.0;
    const PIXELS_PER_NOTCH: f64 = 3.0 * 40.0;
    const PIXELS_PER_PRECISE_TICK: f64 = 40.0;
    if precision == WheelDeltaPrecision::Precise {
        return pixel_delta * (TICK_120THS_PER_TICK / PIXELS_PER_PRECISE_TICK);
    }
    pixel_delta * (TICK_120THS_PER_TICK / PIXELS_PER_NOTCH)
}

FILE: Services/Compositor/Rust/src/keyboard_scroll_controller.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

use libcompositing_rust::css_pixels::{CssPixelPoint, CssPixels};
use libcompositing_rust::scrolling::scroll_snap_selection::SnapSelectionStrategyType;
use libcompositing_rust::scrolling::{
    AsyncScrollNodeStableID, AsyncScrollTree, KeyCode, KeyEvent, KeyModifier, KeyboardScrollState,
};
use libgfx_rust::FloatPoint;

pub struct KeyboardScrollController {
    state: KeyboardScrollState,
    held_keys: Vec<KeyCode>,
}

pub struct KeyStep {
    // Where the scroller chain the key scrolls starts.
    pub keyboard_scroll_target: AsyncScrollNodeStableID,
    pub delta: FloatPoint,
    pub scrolls_to_extent: bool,
    pub snap_selection_intent: SnapSelectionStrategyType,
}

impl Default for KeyStep {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            keyboard_scroll_target: AsyncScrollNodeStableID {
                node_id: Default::default(),
                kind: libcompositing_rust::scrolling::AsyncScrollNodeKind::Element,
                pseudo_element_type: 0,
            },
            delta: Default::default(),
            scrolls_to_extent: false,
            snap_selection_intent: SnapSelectionStrategyType::EndPositionAndDirection,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum KeyRelease {
    Ignored,
    ReleasedWhileOtherKeysAreHeld,
    ReleasedLastHeldKey,
}

impl Default for KeyboardScrollController {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            state: KeyboardScrollState {
                generation: 0,
                visual_context_tree_structural_epoch: 0,
                target: None,
                page_scroll_distance: 0.0,
                arrow_scroll_distance: 0.0,
            },
            held_keys: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}

impl KeyboardScrollController {
    pub fn invalidate_state(&mut self, generation: u64) {
        if generation < self.state.generation {
            return;
        }
        self.state.generation = generation;
        self.state.target = None;
    }

    // Returns whether the state is not older than the one already adopted.
    pub fn adopt_state(&mut self, state: KeyboardScrollState) -> bool {
        if state.generation < self.state.generation {
            return false;
        }
        self.state = state;
        true
    }

    pub fn forget_target(&mut self) {
        self.state.target = None;
    }
    pub fn has_target(&self) -> bool {
        self.state.target.is_some()
    }
    pub fn state_matches_visual_context_tree_epoch(&self, visual_context_tree_structural_epoch: u64) -> bool {
        self.state.visual_context_tree_structural_epoch == visual_context_tree_structural_epoch
    }

    pub fn step_for_key(&self, event: &KeyEvent, async_scroll_tree: &AsyncScrollTree) -> Option<KeyStep> {
        assert!(self.state.target.is_some());
        let modifiers_without_keypad = event.modifiers.0 & !KeyModifier::Mod_Keypad.0;
        let scrolls_to_start = event.key == KeyCode::Key_Home
            || (event.key == KeyCode::Key_Up && modifiers_without_keypad == KeyModifier::Mod_PlatformCtrl.0);
        let scrolls_to_end = event.key == KeyCode::Key_End
            || (event.key == KeyCode::Key_Down && modifiers_without_keypad == KeyModifier::Mod_PlatformCtrl.0);
        let scrolls_to_extent = scrolls_to_start || scrolls_to_end;
        let is_arrow = !scrolls_to_extent
            && matches!(
                event.key,
                KeyCode::Key_Up | KeyCode::Key_Down | KeyCode::Key_Left | KeyCode::Key_Right
            );
        let delta = if scrolls_to_extent {
            async_scroll_tree.device_offset_from_css_pixels(CssPixelPoint {
                x: CssPixels::default(),
                y: if scrolls_to_start {
                    -CssPixels::from_raw(i32::MAX)
                } else {
                    CssPixels::from_raw(i32::MAX)
                },
            })
        } else {
            let mut distance = if is_arrow {
                self.state.arrow_scroll_distance
            } else {
                self.state.page_scroll_distance
            };
            if !distance.is_finite() || distance <= 0.0 {
                return None;
            }
            if matches!(event.key, KeyCode::Key_PageUp | KeyCode::Key_Up | KeyCode::Key_Left)
                || (event.key == KeyCode::Key_Space && !(event.modifiers & KeyModifier::Mod_Shift).is_empty())
            {
                distance = -distance;
            }
            let is_horizontal = matches!(event.key, KeyCode::Key_Left | KeyCode::Key_Right);
            if is_horizontal {
                FloatPoint { x: distance, y: 0.0 }
            } else {
                FloatPoint { x: 0.0, y: distance }
            }
        };

        let mut snap_selection_intent = SnapSelectionStrategyType::EndPositionAndDirection;
        if scrolls_to_extent {
            snap_selection_intent = SnapSelectionStrategyType::EndPosition;
        } else if is_arrow {
            snap_selection_intent = SnapSelectionStrategyType::Direction;
        }

        Some(KeyStep {
            keyboard_scroll_target: self.state.target.unwrap(),
            delta,
            scrolls_to_extent,
            snap_selection_intent,
        })
    }

    pub fn hold_key(&mut self, key: KeyCode) {
        if !self.held_keys.contains(&key) {
            self.held_keys.push(key);
        }
    }

    pub fn release_key(&mut self, event: &KeyEvent) -> KeyRelease {
        if event.repeat {
            return KeyRelease::Ignored;
        }
        let Some(index) = self.held_keys.iter().position(|&key| key == event.key) else {
            return KeyRelease::Ignored;
        };
        self.held_keys.remove(index);
        if self.held_keys.is_empty() {
            return KeyRelease::ReleasedLastHeldKey;
        }
        KeyRelease::ReleasedWhileOtherKeysAreHeld
    }

    // Returns whether any key was held.
    pub fn release_all_keys(&mut self) -> bool {
        if self.held_keys.is_empty() {
            return false;
        }
        self.held_keys.clear();
        true
    }

    pub fn has_held_keys(&self) -> bool {
        !self.held_keys.is_empty()
    }
}

//! What the compositor draws over the page of a context: the overlays the browser asks for. They are recorded as display
//! list records and played through the same painter as the page.

use libcompositing_rust::display_list::builder::{DisplayListBuilder, HEADER_SIZE, PendingInlineClip};
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::commands::{
    ContextRef, DisplayListCommand, DisplayListDataSpan, DisplayListGlyph, DisplayListPaintStyle, DrawGlyphRun,
    FillPath, FillRect, FontResourceId, OptionalFloatRect, PathPaintKind, ReplayLayer, StrokePath,
};
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::ffi_bytes::FfiBytes;
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::replay::{RecordsContext, ReplayFrame, ReplayPainter, replay_records};
use libcompositing_rust::overlays::{
    PausedDebuggerOverlayGeometry, paused_debugger_overlay_geometry, picture_in_picture_controls_geometry,
    scaled_overlay_length,
};
use libcompositing_rust::scrolling::overlay_fade::OverlayFade;
use libcompositing_rust::time::MonotonicTime;
use libcompositing_rust::visual_context::{TransformData, TransformDataRole, VisualContextTree};
use libgfx_rust::path::Path;
use libgfx_rust::{
    CapStyle, Color, CompositingAndBlendingOperator, FloatMatrix4x4, FloatPoint, FloatRect, GlyphRunOrientation,
    IntRect, IntSize, JoinStyle, ShouldAntiAlias, WindingRule, enclosing_int_rect,
};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PausedDebuggerOverlayAction {
    StepOver,
    Continue,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PictureInPictureControl {
    BackToTab,
    Close,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct PausedDebuggerOverlayState {
    pub font_family: Option<String>,
    pub hovered_action: Option<PausedDebuggerOverlayAction>,
}

/// The controls stay present while they are hidden, so that they fade out.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct PictureInPictureControlsState {
    pub shown: bool,
    pub hovered_control: Option<PictureInPictureControl>,
}

/// The layers the frames are composited from and the tiles each holds, drawn by the compositor that knows them.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct CompositorLayersOverlayState {
    pub font_family: Option<String>,
    /// The layers the frames leave out, by the ids the descriptions the compositor publishes give them.
    pub hidden_layer_ids: Vec<u64>,
    /// The layers the overlay shows the tiles of.
    pub selected_layer_ids: Vec<u64>,
    /// The layer the overlay marks out, as the pointer is over it in the window or on the page.
    pub hovered_layer_id: Option<u64>,
    /// Each new value zeroes the counts of tiles rastered.
    pub raster_count_reset_generation: u64,
}

/// What the browser draws over a context's page, with each overlay the view has present.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct UIOverlays {
    pub paused_debugger: Option<PausedDebuggerOverlayState>,
    pub picture_in_picture_controls: Option<PictureInPictureControlsState>,
    pub compositor_layers: Option<CompositorLayersOverlayState>,
}

/// What a new set of overlays changes of the frames.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum UIOverlaysChange {
    Nothing,
    /// The compositor layers overlay is drawn over tiles that stay as they are, so the frame rasters nothing for it.
    OnlyCompositorLayers,
    RepaintsEverything,
}

/// A label of an overlay as the host shapes it: the font it resolved, in the overlays' resources, and where each glyph
/// goes along the line, in device pixels.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct OverlayLabel {
    pub font_id: u64,
    pub glyph_ids: Vec<u32>,
    pub glyph_x_positions: Vec<f32>,
    pub width: f32,
    /// Of the font at the size the label is shaped at: the ascent above the baseline, which is negative, and the
    /// descent.
    pub ascent: f32,
    pub descent: f32,
    /// The ascent the painter places glyphs below, at the font's own size.
    pub font_ascent: f32,
}

/// Shapes the label of an overlay, in the font family given or the default one, at a font size and a device pixel
/// ratio.
pub trait OverlayLabelShaper {
    fn shape_overlay_label(
        &self,
        font_family: Option<&str>,
        font_size_in_points: f32,
        device_pixel_ratio: f64,
        text: &str,
    ) -> Option<OverlayLabel>;
}

const PAUSED_DEBUGGER_LABEL: &str = "Paused in debugger";
const PAUSED_DEBUGGER_LABEL_FONT_SIZE_IN_POINTS: f32 = 12.0;

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct ContextOverlays {
    ui_overlays: UIOverlays,
    picture_in_picture_controls_fade: OverlayFade,
    // The label of the paused debugger overlay, for the font family and device pixel ratio it was shaped for.
    paused_debugger_label: Option<(Option<String>, f64, Option<OverlayLabel>)>,
    compositor_layers_overlay_needs_frames_until: Option<MonotonicTime>,
}

impl ContextOverlays {
    pub fn ui_overlays(&self) -> &UIOverlays {
        &self.ui_overlays
    }

    pub fn set_ui_overlays(&mut self, ui_overlays: UIOverlays, now: MonotonicTime) -> UIOverlaysChange {
        if self.ui_overlays == ui_overlays {
            return UIOverlaysChange::Nothing;
        }
        let only_compositor_layers_changed = UIOverlays {
            compositor_layers: self.ui_overlays.compositor_layers.clone(),
            ..ui_overlays.clone()
        } == self.ui_overlays;
        self.ui_overlays = ui_overlays;
        if only_compositor_layers_changed {
            return UIOverlaysChange::OnlyCompositorLayers;
        }
        let shows_picture_in_picture_controls = self
            .ui_overlays
            .picture_in_picture_controls
            .is_some_and(|controls| controls.shown);
        self.picture_in_picture_controls_fade
            .fade_to(if shows_picture_in_picture_controls { 1.0 } else { 0.0 }, now);
        UIOverlaysChange::RepaintsEverything
    }

    pub fn set_compositor_layers_overlay_needs_frames_until(&mut self, until: Option<MonotonicTime>) {
        self.compositor_layers_overlay_needs_frames_until = until;
    }

    pub fn fades_or_compositor_layers_overlay_need_frame(&self) -> bool {
        self.picture_in_picture_controls_fade.is_fading() || self.compositor_layers_overlay_needs_frames_until.is_some()
    }

    /// Answers whether the compositor layers overlay needs a frame: until one is presented at the end of the time it
    /// needs them for, which no longer shows a highlight.
    pub fn compositor_layers_overlay_needs_frame(&mut self, frame_time: MonotonicTime) -> bool {
        let Some(until) = self.compositor_layers_overlay_needs_frames_until else {
            return false;
        };
        if frame_time >= until {
            self.compositor_layers_overlay_needs_frames_until = None;
        }
        true
    }

    /// Advances the fades to a frame, answering what of the viewport they repaint.
    pub fn advance_fades(
        &mut self,
        frame_time: MonotonicTime,
        viewport_size: IntSize,
        device_pixel_ratio: f64,
    ) -> Option<IntRect> {
        if !self.picture_in_picture_controls_fade.advance_to(frame_time) {
            return None;
        }
        Some(picture_in_picture_controls_geometry(viewport_size, device_pixel_ratio).buttons_bounds())
    }

    /// What the overlays draw over a frame of the page.
    pub fn picture_of_frame(
        &mut self,
        viewport_size: IntSize,
        device_pixel_ratio: f64,
        label_shaper: &dyn OverlayLabelShaper,
    ) -> OverlayPicture {
        let viewport_rect = IntRect::new(0, 0, viewport_size.width, viewport_size.height);
        let mut bounds = IntRect::default();

        let mut ui_overlay_records = DisplayListBuilder::new();
        if let Some(paused_debugger) = self.ui_overlays.paused_debugger.clone() {
            let label = self.paused_debugger_label(&paused_debugger, device_pixel_ratio, label_shaper);
            record_paused_debugger_overlay(
                &mut ui_overlay_records,
                viewport_size,
                device_pixel_ratio,
                &paused_debugger,
                label,
            );
        }

        let mut picture_in_picture_controls = None;
        let opacity = self.picture_in_picture_controls_fade.opacity();
        if let Some(controls) = &self.ui_overlays.picture_in_picture_controls
            && opacity > 0.0
        {
            let mut records = DisplayListBuilder::new();
            let controls_bounds =
                record_picture_in_picture_controls(&mut records, viewport_size, device_pixel_ratio, controls);
            picture_in_picture_controls = Some(PictureInPictureControlsPicture {
                opacity,
                bounds: controls_bounds,
                records: AlignedRecords::new(&records.finish().bytes),
            });
        }

        if self.ui_overlays.paused_debugger.is_some() || picture_in_picture_controls.is_some() {
            bounds = viewport_rect;
        }
        OverlayPicture {
            ui_overlay_records: AlignedRecords::new(&ui_overlay_records.finish().bytes),
            picture_in_picture_controls,
            bounds: bounds.intersected(viewport_rect),
            compositor_layers: self.ui_overlays.compositor_layers.clone(),
        }
    }

    fn paused_debugger_label(
        &mut self,
        paused_debugger: &PausedDebuggerOverlayState,
        device_pixel_ratio: f64,
        label_shaper: &dyn OverlayLabelShaper,
    ) -> Option<&OverlayLabel> {
        let is_cached = self
            .paused_debugger_label
            .as_ref()
            .is_some_and(|(font_family, ratio, _)| {
                *font_family == paused_debugger.font_family && *ratio == device_pixel_ratio
            });
        if !is_cached {
            let label = label_shaper.shape_overlay_label(
                paused_debugger.font_family.as_deref(),
                PAUSED_DEBUGGER_LABEL_FONT_SIZE_IN_POINTS,
                device_pixel_ratio,
                PAUSED_DEBUGGER_LABEL,
            );
            self.paused_debugger_label = Some((paused_debugger.font_family.clone(), device_pixel_ratio, label));
        }
        self.paused_debugger_label
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|(_, _, label)| label.as_ref())
    }
}

// Records in memory aligned for every command and payload object they hold, which the painter checks and a Vec<u8>
// does not promise.
struct AlignedRecords {
    words: Vec<u64>,
    size: usize,
}

impl AlignedRecords {
    fn new(bytes: &[u8]) -> Self {
        let mut words = vec![0u64; bytes.len().div_ceil(8)];
        for (word, chunk) in words.iter_mut().zip(bytes.chunks(8)) {
            let mut word_bytes = [0u8; 8];
            word_bytes[..chunk.len()].copy_from_slice(chunk);
            *word = u64::from_ne_bytes(word_bytes);
        }
        Self {
            words,
            size: bytes.len(),
        }
    }

    fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        // SAFETY: The words hold `size` initialized bytes.
        unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.words.as_ptr().cast(), self.size) }
    }
}

struct PictureInPictureControlsPicture {
    opacity: f32,
    bounds: IntRect,
    records: AlignedRecords,
}

/// What the overlays draw over one frame, in the order they are drawn, and the part of the viewport they cover.
pub struct OverlayPicture {
    ui_overlay_records: AlignedRecords,
    picture_in_picture_controls: Option<PictureInPictureControlsPicture>,
    pub bounds: IntRect,
    /// The compositor records that overlay once it has rastered the frame's tiles, which it shows.
    pub compositor_layers: Option<CompositorLayersOverlayState>,
}

thread_local! {
    // The overlays are recorded in the space of the viewport, which no node of a tree transforms.
    static OVERLAY_TREE: VisualContextTree = VisualContextTree::create(TransformData {
        matrix: FloatMatrix4x4::identity(),
        origin: FloatPoint::default(),
        sorting_context_root_index: None,
        flattens_inherited_transform: false,
        role: TransformDataRole::CssTransform,
        synthetic_plane: false,
        establishes_sorting_context: false,
        bounds: FloatRect::default(),
    });
}

/// Records drawn over a frame in the space of the viewport, as the overlays of the browser are.
pub struct OverlayRecords(AlignedRecords);

impl OverlayRecords {
    pub(crate) fn record(record: impl FnOnce(&mut OverlayRecorder<'_>)) -> Self {
        let mut builder = DisplayListBuilder::new();
        record(&mut OverlayRecorder {
            builder: &mut builder,
            clip_of_appended_commands: None,
        });
        Self(AlignedRecords::new(&builder.finish().bytes))
    }

    pub fn paint(&self, painter: &mut impl ReplayPainter) {
        replay_overlay_records(&self.0, painter);
    }
}

fn replay_overlay_records(records: &AlignedRecords, painter: &mut impl ReplayPainter) {
    OVERLAY_TREE.with(|tree| {
        let frame = ReplayFrame::unscrolled(0);
        let context = RecordsContext {
            tree,
            frame: &frame,
            to_root_matrix_of_inline_clip_space: &|_| None,
        };
        replay_records(records.as_bytes(), &context, painter);
    });
}

impl OverlayPicture {
    /// Whether the overlays draw over a frame what `other` draws over its frame, but for the overlay of the compositor's
    /// layers.
    pub fn draws_same_as(&self, other: &OverlayPicture) -> bool {
        let picture_in_picture_controls_draw_the_same =
            match (&self.picture_in_picture_controls, &other.picture_in_picture_controls) {
                (Some(controls), Some(other_controls)) => {
                    controls.opacity == other_controls.opacity
                        && controls.bounds == other_controls.bounds
                        && controls.records.as_bytes() == other_controls.records.as_bytes()
                }
                (None, None) => true,
                _ => false,
            };
        self.bounds == other.bounds
            && self.ui_overlay_records.as_bytes() == other.ui_overlay_records.as_bytes()
            && picture_in_picture_controls_draw_the_same
    }

    /// Paints the overlays over a frame.
    pub fn paint(&self, painter: &mut impl ReplayPainter) {
        replay_overlay_records(&self.ui_overlay_records, painter);
        if let Some(controls) = &self.picture_in_picture_controls {
            painter.push_layer(&ReplayLayer {
                can_draw_directly_for_lcd_text: false,
                opacity: controls.opacity,
                blend_mode: CompositingAndBlendingOperator::Normal,
                filter_bytes: std::ptr::null(),
                filter_bytes_size: 0,
                backdrop_filter_bytes: std::ptr::null(),
                backdrop_filter_bytes_size: 0,
                backdrop_region: IntRect::default(),
                backdrop_corner_radii: Default::default(),
                backdrop_base_color: Color::TRANSPARENT,
                backdrop_blur_edge: OptionalFloatRect::none(),
                filter_cache_key: 0,
                content_bounds: OptionalFloatRect::from(Some(controls.bounds.to_float())),
            });
            replay_overlay_records(&controls.records, painter);
            painter.pop();
        }
    }
}

/// The records of one overlay, with the payload of each command laid out after the command as the painter reads it.
pub(crate) struct OverlayRecorder<'a> {
    builder: &'a mut DisplayListBuilder,
    clip_of_appended_commands: Option<IntRect>,
}

impl OverlayRecorder<'_> {
    fn append<C: DisplayListCommand>(&mut self, command: &C, inline_data: &[u8]) {
        match self.clip_of_appended_commands {
            Some(clip) => self.builder.append_with_inline_clips(
                command,
                inline_data,
                ContextRef::default(),
                &[PendingInlineClip::intersecting_device_rect(clip)],
            ),
            None => self.builder.append(command, inline_data, ContextRef::default()),
        }
    }

    /// Clips what `record` appends to `clip`.
    pub(crate) fn clipped_to(&mut self, clip: IntRect, record: impl FnOnce(&mut Self)) {
        let outer_clip = self.clip_of_appended_commands;
        self.clip_of_appended_commands = Some(outer_clip.map_or(clip, |outer_clip| outer_clip.intersected(clip)));
        record(self);
        self.clip_of_appended_commands = outer_clip;
    }

    // The span of `data` placed after a command of type `C`, at an offset aligned for the data, with the padding
    // that takes put in front of it.
    fn data_after_command<C: DisplayListCommand>(
        &self,
        data: &[u8],
        alignment: usize,
    ) -> (DisplayListDataSpan, Vec<u8>) {
        let payload_start = self.builder.byte_size() + HEADER_SIZE;
        let command_end = payload_start + std::mem::size_of::<C>();
        let padding = command_end.next_multiple_of(alignment) - command_end;
        let mut inline_data = vec![0u8; padding];
        inline_data.extend_from_slice(data);
        let span = DisplayListDataSpan {
            offset: (std::mem::size_of::<C>() + padding) as u32,
            size: data.len() as u32,
        };
        (span, inline_data)
    }

    pub(crate) fn fill_rect(&mut self, rect: IntRect, color: Color) {
        self.append(
            &FillRect {
                rect,
                color,
                compositing_and_blending_operator: CompositingAndBlendingOperator::Normal,
                background_color_animation_effect: libcompositing_rust::display_list::commands::EffectNodeIndex::NONE,
            },
            &[],
        );
    }

    fn fill_rect_clipped_to(&mut self, rect: IntRect, color: Color, clip: &Path) {
        self.builder.append_with_inline_clips(
            &FillRect {
                rect,
                color,
                compositing_and_blending_operator: CompositingAndBlendingOperator::Normal,
                background_color_animation_effect: libcompositing_rust::display_list::commands::EffectNodeIndex::NONE,
            },
            &[],
            ContextRef::default(),
            &[PendingInlineClip::intersecting_path(clip, WindingRule::Nonzero)],
        );
    }

    fn fill_path(&mut self, path: &Path, color: Color) {
        let path_bounding_rect = FloatRect::from_array(path.bounding_box());
        if path_bounding_rect.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let (path_data, inline_data) =
            self.data_after_command::<FillPath>(&path.serialize_to_bytes(), std::mem::align_of::<u32>());
        self.append(
            &FillPath {
                path_bounding_rect,
                path_data,
                opacity: 1.0,
                paint_kind: PathPaintKind::Color,
                color,
                paint_style: DisplayListPaintStyle::default(),
                winding_rule: WindingRule::Nonzero,
                should_anti_alias: ShouldAntiAlias::Yes,
                compositing_and_blending_operator: CompositingAndBlendingOperator::Normal,
            },
            &inline_data,
        );
    }

    fn stroke_path(&mut self, path: &Path, color: Color, thickness: f32, cap_style: CapStyle, join_style: JoinStyle) {
        let path_bounding_rect = FloatRect::from_array(path.bounding_box()).inflated(thickness, thickness);
        if path_bounding_rect.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let (path_data, inline_data) =
            self.data_after_command::<StrokePath>(&path.serialize_to_bytes(), std::mem::align_of::<u32>());
        self.append(
            &StrokePath {
                cap_style,
                join_style,
                miter_limit: 4.0,
                dash_array: DisplayListDataSpan::default(),
                dash_offset: 0.0,
                path_bounding_rect,
                path_data,
                opacity: 1.0,
                paint_kind: PathPaintKind::Color,
                color,
                paint_style: DisplayListPaintStyle::default(),
                thickness,
                should_anti_alias: ShouldAntiAlias::Yes,
            },
            &inline_data,
        );
    }

    pub(crate) fn draw_label(&mut self, label: &OverlayLabel, baseline_origin: FloatPoint, color: Color, scale: f32) {
        if label.glyph_ids.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let glyphs: Vec<DisplayListGlyph> = label
            .glyph_ids
            .iter()
            .zip(&label.glyph_x_positions)
            .map(|(glyph_id, x)| DisplayListGlyph {
                position: FloatPoint {
                    x: (baseline_origin.x + x) / scale,
                    y: baseline_origin.y / scale - label.font_ascent,
                },
                glyph_id: *glyph_id,
            })
            .collect();
        let mut glyph_bytes = vec![0u8; glyphs.len() * std::mem::size_of::<DisplayListGlyph>()];
        for (index, glyph) in glyphs.iter().enumerate() {
            let start = index * std::mem::size_of::<DisplayListGlyph>();
            glyph.write_ffi_bytes(&mut glyph_bytes[start..start + std::mem::size_of::<DisplayListGlyph>()]);
        }
        let (glyph_span, inline_data) =
            self.data_after_command::<DrawGlyphRun>(&glyph_bytes, std::mem::align_of::<DisplayListGlyph>());
        let rect = enclosing_int_rect(FloatRect::new(
            baseline_origin.x,
            baseline_origin.y + label.ascent,
            label.width,
            label.descent - label.ascent,
        ))
        .inflated(2, 2);
        self.append(
            &DrawGlyphRun {
                stroke_width: 0.0,
                font_id: FontResourceId(label.font_id),
                glyphs: glyph_span,
                rect,
                glyph_bounding_rect: rect,
                translation: FloatPoint::default(),
                scale,
                color,
                orientation: GlyphRunOrientation::Horizontal,
                font_smoothing: 0,
            },
            &inline_data,
        );
    }
}

fn rounded_rect_path(rect: FloatRect, radius: f32) -> Path {
    let radius = radius.min(rect.width / 2.0).min(rect.height / 2.0);
    let (left, top, right, bottom) = (rect.x, rect.y, rect.right(), rect.bottom());
    let mut path = Path::new();
    path.move_to(FloatPoint {
        x: left + radius,
        y: top,
    });
    path.line_to(FloatPoint {
        x: right - radius,
        y: top,
    });
    path.arc_to(
        FloatPoint {
            x: right,
            y: top + radius,
        },
        radius,
        false,
        true,
    );
    path.line_to(FloatPoint {
        x: right,
        y: bottom - radius,
    });
    path.arc_to(
        FloatPoint {
            x: right - radius,
            y: bottom,
        },
        radius,
        false,
        true,
    );
    path.line_to(FloatPoint {
        x: left + radius,
        y: bottom,
    });
    path.arc_to(
        FloatPoint {
            x: left,
            y: bottom - radius,
        },
        radius,
        false,
        true,
    );
    path.line_to(FloatPoint {
        x: left,
        y: top + radius,
    });
    path.arc_to(
        FloatPoint {
            x: left + radius,
            y: top,
        },
        radius,
        false,
        true,
    );
    path.close();
    path
}

fn circle_path(center: FloatPoint, radius: f32) -> Path {
    let mut path = Path::new();
    path.move_to(FloatPoint {
        x: center.x + radius,
        y: center.y,
    });
    path.arc_to(
        FloatPoint {
            x: center.x - radius,
            y: center.y,
        },
        radius,
        false,
        true,
    );
    path.arc_to(
        FloatPoint {
            x: center.x + radius,
            y: center.y,
        },
        radius,
        false,
        true,
    );
    path.close();
    path
}

fn rect_center(rect: IntRect) -> FloatPoint {
    // An odd size centers on the pixel below and to the right of the middle, as the integer rects of the painter do.
    FloatPoint {
        x: (rect.x + rect.width / 2) as f32,
        y: (rect.y + rect.height / 2) as f32,
    }
}

// These colors are equivalent to those produced by UI/Qt/ChromeStyle.cpp in light mode. The compositor cannot use
// those colors directly because it does not depend on Qt, so their resolved values are copied here.
const DEBUGGER_OVERLAY_COLOR: Color = Color::from_rgba(0xee, 0xee, 0xef, 168);
const DEBUGGER_TOOLBAR_COLOR: Color = Color::from_rgba(0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 255);
const DEBUGGER_TOOLBAR_BORDER_COLOR: Color = Color::from_rgba(0xce, 0xce, 0xcf, 255);
const DEBUGGER_BUTTON_HOVER_COLOR: Color = Color::from_rgba(0xf1, 0xf1, 0xf2, 255);
const DEBUGGER_TEXT_COLOR: Color = Color::from_rgba(0x18, 0x1d, 0x24, 255);
const DEBUGGER_SHADOW_COLOR: Color = Color::from_rgba(0x18, 0x1d, 0x24, 66);

fn record_paused_debugger_overlay(
    builder: &mut DisplayListBuilder,
    viewport_size: IntSize,
    device_pixel_ratio: f64,
    state: &PausedDebuggerOverlayState,
    label: Option<&OverlayLabel>,
) {
    let mut recorder = OverlayRecorder {
        builder,
        clip_of_appended_commands: None,
    };
    let geometry: PausedDebuggerOverlayGeometry = paused_debugger_overlay_geometry(viewport_size, device_pixel_ratio);
    let radius = 1.0f32.max((4.0 * device_pixel_ratio) as f32);

    recorder.fill_rect(
        IntRect::new(0, 0, viewport_size.width, viewport_size.height),
        DEBUGGER_OVERLAY_COLOR,
    );

    let mut shadow_rect = geometry.toolbar;
    shadow_rect.y += scaled_overlay_length(2, device_pixel_ratio);
    recorder.fill_path(
        &rounded_rect_path(shadow_rect.to_float(), radius),
        DEBUGGER_SHADOW_COLOR,
    );

    let toolbar_path = rounded_rect_path(geometry.toolbar.to_float(), radius);
    recorder.fill_path(&toolbar_path, DEBUGGER_TOOLBAR_COLOR);

    if let Some(hovered_action) = state.hovered_action {
        let hovered_button = match hovered_action {
            PausedDebuggerOverlayAction::StepOver => geometry.step_over_button,
            PausedDebuggerOverlayAction::Continue => geometry.continue_button,
        };
        recorder.fill_rect_clipped_to(hovered_button, DEBUGGER_BUTTON_HOVER_COLOR, &toolbar_path);
    }

    let line_thickness = 1.0f64.max(device_pixel_ratio) as f32;
    recorder.stroke_path(
        &toolbar_path,
        DEBUGGER_TOOLBAR_BORDER_COLOR,
        line_thickness,
        CapStyle::Butt,
        JoinStyle::Miter,
    );

    let divider_inset = scaled_overlay_length(10, device_pixel_ratio) as f32;
    let divider_x = geometry.step_over_button.x as f32;
    let mut divider = Path::new();
    divider.move_to(FloatPoint {
        x: divider_x,
        y: geometry.toolbar.y as f32 + divider_inset,
    });
    divider.line_to(FloatPoint {
        x: divider_x,
        y: geometry.toolbar.bottom() as f32 - divider_inset,
    });
    recorder.stroke_path(
        &divider,
        DEBUGGER_TOOLBAR_BORDER_COLOR,
        line_thickness,
        CapStyle::Butt,
        JoinStyle::Miter,
    );

    if let Some(label) = label {
        let message = geometry.message;
        let label_x = message.x as f32 + (message.width as f32 - label.width) / 2.0;
        let label_y = rect_center(message).y - (label.ascent + label.descent) / 2.0;
        recorder.draw_label(
            label,
            FloatPoint { x: label_x, y: label_y },
            DEBUGGER_TEXT_COLOR,
            device_pixel_ratio as f32,
        );
    }

    let icon_size = 8.0f64.max(16.0 * device_pixel_ratio) as f32;

    // Step over: an arc over a dot, with an arrow at its end.
    let center = rect_center(geometry.step_over_button);
    let left = center.x - icon_size / 2.0;
    let top = center.y - icon_size / 2.0;
    let right = center.x + icon_size / 2.0;
    let mut arc = Path::new();
    arc.move_to(FloatPoint {
        x: left + icon_size / 8.0,
        y: top + icon_size * 0.55,
    });
    arc.cubic_bezier_curve_to(
        FloatPoint {
            x: left + icon_size / 8.0,
            y: top + icon_size * 0.15,
        },
        FloatPoint {
            x: right - icon_size / 5.0,
            y: top + icon_size * 0.15,
        },
        FloatPoint {
            x: right - icon_size / 5.0,
            y: top + icon_size * 0.55,
        },
    );
    recorder.stroke_path(
        &arc,
        DEBUGGER_TEXT_COLOR,
        line_thickness,
        CapStyle::Round,
        JoinStyle::Round,
    );
    let arrow_width = icon_size / 2.5;
    let mut arrow = Path::new();
    arrow.move_to(FloatPoint {
        x: right - arrow_width,
        y: top + icon_size * 0.55,
    });
    arrow.line_to(FloatPoint {
        x: right,
        y: top + icon_size * 0.55,
    });
    arrow.line_to(FloatPoint {
        x: right - arrow_width / 2.0,
        y: top + icon_size * 0.8,
    });
    arrow.close();
    recorder.fill_path(&arrow, DEBUGGER_TEXT_COLOR);
    let dot_size = 2.0f32.max(line_thickness * 2.0);
    recorder.fill_path(
        &circle_path(
            FloatPoint {
                x: center.x,
                y: center.y + icon_size / 3.0,
            },
            dot_size / 2.0,
        ),
        DEBUGGER_TEXT_COLOR,
    );

    // Continue: a triangle pointing along the line.
    let center = rect_center(geometry.continue_button);
    let icon_left = center.x - icon_size / 2.0;
    let icon_top = center.y - icon_size / 2.0;
    let mut triangle = Path::new();
    triangle.move_to(FloatPoint {
        x: icon_left + icon_size / 4.0,
        y: icon_top + icon_size / 8.0,
    });
    triangle.line_to(FloatPoint {
        x: icon_left + icon_size / 4.0,
        y: icon_top + icon_size - icon_size / 8.0,
    });
    triangle.line_to(FloatPoint {
        x: icon_left + icon_size - icon_size / 8.0,
        y: icon_top + icon_size / 2.0,
    });
    triangle.close();
    recorder.fill_path(&triangle, DEBUGGER_TEXT_COLOR);
}

// A step of an icon's outline, on its grid of 16 units.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum IconStep {
    Move(f32, f32),
    Line(f32, f32),
    Quadratic(f32, f32, f32, f32),
}

const PICTURE_IN_PICTURE_BUTTON_COLOR: Color = Color::from_rgba(0, 0, 0, 115);
const PICTURE_IN_PICTURE_ICON_COLOR: Color = Color::from_rgba(0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 255);
const PICTURE_IN_PICTURE_HOVERED_ICON_COLOR: Color = Color::from_rgba(0xe0, 0xd4, 0xff, 255);

// Records the controls, answering the rect that holds them.
fn record_picture_in_picture_controls(
    builder: &mut DisplayListBuilder,
    viewport_size: IntSize,
    device_pixel_ratio: f64,
    state: &PictureInPictureControlsState,
) -> IntRect {
    let mut recorder = OverlayRecorder {
        builder,
        clip_of_appended_commands: None,
    };
    let geometry = picture_in_picture_controls_geometry(viewport_size, device_pixel_ratio);

    // The icons are stroked on a grid of 16 units, and drawn at the given size in points.
    let mut record_button =
        |button: IntRect, control: PictureInPictureControl, icon: &[IconStep], icon_points: f32, stroke_units: f32| {
            let center = FloatPoint {
                x: button.x as f32 + button.width as f32 / 2.0,
                y: button.y as f32 + button.height as f32 / 2.0,
            };
            recorder.fill_path(
                &circle_path(center, button.width as f32 / 2.0),
                PICTURE_IN_PICTURE_BUTTON_COLOR,
            );

            let icon_size = icon_points * device_pixel_ratio as f32;
            let unit = icon_size / 16.0;
            let at = |x: f32, y: f32| FloatPoint {
                x: center.x - icon_size / 2.0 + x * unit,
                y: center.y - icon_size / 2.0 + y * unit,
            };
            let mut path = Path::new();
            for step in icon {
                match *step {
                    IconStep::Move(x, y) => path.move_to(at(x, y)),
                    IconStep::Line(x, y) => path.line_to(at(x, y)),
                    IconStep::Quadratic(control_x, control_y, x, y) => {
                        path.quadratic_bezier_curve_to(at(control_x, control_y), at(x, y));
                    }
                }
            }
            let color = if state.hovered_control == Some(control) {
                PICTURE_IN_PICTURE_HOVERED_ICON_COLOR
            } else {
                PICTURE_IN_PICTURE_ICON_COLOR
            };
            recorder.stroke_path(&path, color, stroke_units * unit, CapStyle::Round, JoinStyle::Round);
        };

    // An arrow out of a box, toward its top right corner.
    let back_to_tab_icon = [
        IconStep::Move(9.5, 2.5),
        IconStep::Line(13.5, 2.5),
        IconStep::Line(13.5, 6.5),
        IconStep::Move(13.5, 2.5),
        IconStep::Line(8.0, 8.0),
        IconStep::Move(12.0, 9.5),
        IconStep::Line(12.0, 12.5),
        IconStep::Quadratic(12.0, 13.5, 11.0, 13.5),
        IconStep::Line(3.5, 13.5),
        IconStep::Quadratic(2.5, 13.5, 2.5, 12.5),
        IconStep::Line(2.5, 5.0),
        IconStep::Quadratic(2.5, 4.0, 3.5, 4.0),
        IconStep::Line(6.5, 4.0),
    ];
    record_button(
        geometry.back_to_tab_button,
        PictureInPictureControl::BackToTab,
        &back_to_tab_icon,
        14.0,
        1.6,
    );

    let close_icon = [
        IconStep::Move(4.0, 4.0),
        IconStep::Line(12.0, 12.0),
        IconStep::Move(12.0, 4.0),
        IconStep::Line(4.0, 12.0),
    ];
    record_button(
        geometry.close_button,
        PictureInPictureControl::Close,
        &close_icon,
        11.0,
        2.0,
    );

    geometry.buttons_bounds()
}

//! What a frame repaints of the frame painted before it, and of what each backing store holds.

use super::layers::{LayerUpdate, PaintedLayers};
use super::{ContextPresenting, FrameToPaint, PresentingEnvironment, rect_of_size};
use crate::frame_inputs::FrameInputs;
use crate::host::PendingFrame;
use crate::raster_host::LiveContent;
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::commands::CompositorContextId;
use libcompositing_rust::scrolling::DisplayList;
use libgfx_rust::{IntRect, IntSize};
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use std::rc::Rc;

/// The frame painted last: its display list and inputs, what it did with its layers, and the version of each live
/// content it drew, which comparing lists cannot see change.
pub struct PaintedFrame {
    pub display_list: Rc<DisplayList>,
    pub frame_inputs: FrameInputs,
    pub layers: PaintedLayers,
    pub viewport_size: IntSize,
    allows_lcd_text: bool,
    canvas_content_generations: HashMap<u64, u64>,
    video_frame_ids: HashMap<u64, Option<u64>>,
    image_frame_pixel_generations: HashMap<u64, u64>,
    nested_context_frame_generations: HashMap<u64, Option<u64>>,
}

impl PaintedFrame {
    pub fn draws_canvas(&self, canvas_id: u64) -> bool {
        self.canvas_content_generations.contains_key(&canvas_id)
    }
}

/// What each backing store misses of the frames painted since it was last painted into, by its id, which new stores
/// never repeat. The stores painted into least recently are forgotten first, as retired stores are never painted into
/// again, and a store that is forgotten is painted in full.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct StoreDamage {
    missed_damage_by_store_least_recently_painted_first: Vec<(i32, IntRect)>,
}

// Twice as many as a context ever has at once.
const MAXIMUM_REMEMBERED_STORE_COUNT: usize = 16;

impl StoreDamage {
    pub fn forget_every_store(&mut self) {
        self.missed_damage_by_store_least_recently_painted_first.clear();
    }

    /// What painting a frame into the store repaints: the frame's damage, and what the store missed since it was last
    /// painted, all of it for a store never painted into.
    pub fn take(&mut self, bitmap_id: i32, frame_damage: IntRect, store_rect: IntRect) -> IntRect {
        let mut repaint_rect = store_rect;
        for (store_bitmap_id, missed_damage) in &mut self.missed_damage_by_store_least_recently_painted_first {
            if *store_bitmap_id == bitmap_id {
                repaint_rect = missed_damage.united(frame_damage);
            }
            *missed_damage = missed_damage.united(frame_damage);
        }
        self.missed_damage_by_store_least_recently_painted_first
            .retain(|(store_bitmap_id, _)| *store_bitmap_id != bitmap_id);
        self.missed_damage_by_store_least_recently_painted_first
            .push((bitmap_id, IntRect::default()));
        if self.missed_damage_by_store_least_recently_painted_first.len() > MAXIMUM_REMEMBERED_STORE_COUNT {
            self.missed_damage_by_store_least_recently_painted_first.remove(0);
        }
        repaint_rect
    }

    /// Damage discovered while painting the current store is still owed to the other stores.
    pub fn add_damage_to_other_stores(&mut self, bitmap_id: i32, damage: IntRect) {
        for (store_bitmap_id, missed_damage) in &mut self.missed_damage_by_store_least_recently_painted_first {
            if *store_bitmap_id != bitmap_id {
                *missed_damage = missed_damage.united(damage);
            }
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn a_late_full_repaint_is_owed_to_the_other_stores() {
        let mut damage = StoreDamage::default();
        let full_rect = IntRect::new(0, 0, 100, 100);
        let partial_rect = IntRect::new(10, 10, 20, 20);
        damage.take(1, full_rect, full_rect);
        damage.take(2, full_rect, full_rect);
        assert_eq!(damage.take(1, partial_rect, full_rect), full_rect);
        assert_eq!(damage.take(2, partial_rect, full_rect), partial_rect);

        damage.add_damage_to_other_stores(2, full_rect);
        assert_eq!(damage.take(2, partial_rect, full_rect), partial_rect);
        assert_eq!(damage.take(1, partial_rect, full_rect), full_rect);
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct LiveContentChangesSinceLastPaint {
    pub canvas_or_video_changed: bool,
    pub repaints_everything: bool,
}

pub struct FrameDamage {
    pub rect_in_raster_device_pixels: IntRect,
    pub layers: LayerUpdate,
    pub live_media_changed: bool,
}

impl ContextPresenting {
    /// The live content of the context as it is now, with the canvases that the list and the frame painted last draw.
    pub(super) fn live_content(&self, env: &PresentingEnvironment<'_>, display_list: &DisplayList) -> LiveContent {
        let mut canvas_ids = display_list.storage().summary().canvas_ids.clone();
        if let Some(painted_frame) = &self.painted_frame {
            let canvas_ids_of_list: HashSet<u64> = canvas_ids.iter().copied().collect();
            canvas_ids.extend(
                painted_frame
                    .canvas_content_generations
                    .keys()
                    .filter(|id| !canvas_ids_of_list.contains(id)),
            );
        }
        env.raster.live_content(env.context_id, &canvas_ids)
    }

    /// Remembers a frame that is painted, or that shows nothing new: what it draws, and what it did with its layers.
    pub(super) fn remember_painted_frame(
        &mut self,
        env: &PresentingEnvironment<'_>,
        viewport_rect: IntRect,
        display_list: &Rc<DisplayList>,
        frame_inputs: FrameInputs,
        live_content: &LiveContent,
        layer_update: LayerUpdate,
    ) {
        let allows_lcd_text = layer_update.frame_allows_lcd_text;
        let layers = self.commit_layer_update(env, layer_update);
        let canvas_generation = |id: u64| {
            live_content
                .canvases
                .get(&id)
                .map_or(0, |canvas| canvas.content_generation)
        };
        let summary = display_list.storage().summary();
        let canvas_content_generations = summary
            .canvas_ids
            .iter()
            .map(|&id| (id, canvas_generation(id)))
            .collect();
        // The host reports the video sinks that the list draws.
        let video_frame_ids = live_content
            .video_sinks
            .values()
            .map(|sink| (sink.handle, sink.has_frame.then_some(sink.frame_id)))
            .collect();
        let image_frame_pixel_generations = live_content.image_frames.clone();
        let nested_context_frame_generations = summary
            .composited_context_ids
            .iter()
            .map(|&id| (id, env.nested_contexts.frame_generation_of(CompositorContextId(id))))
            .collect();
        self.painted_frame = Some(PaintedFrame {
            display_list: display_list.clone(),
            frame_inputs,
            layers,
            viewport_size: IntSize {
                width: viewport_rect.width,
                height: viewport_rect.height,
            },
            allows_lcd_text,
            canvas_content_generations,
            video_frame_ids,
            image_frame_pixel_generations,
            nested_context_frame_generations,
        });
    }

    fn live_content_changes_since_last_paint(
        &self,
        env: &PresentingEnvironment<'_>,
        viewport_size: IntSize,
        display_list: &DisplayList,
        allows_lcd_text: bool,
        live_content: &LiveContent,
    ) -> LiveContentChangesSinceLastPaint {
        let mut changes = LiveContentChangesSinceLastPaint::default();
        let Some(painted_frame) = &self.painted_frame else {
            changes.repaints_everything = true;
            return changes;
        };
        if painted_frame.viewport_size != viewport_size
            || painted_frame.display_list.surface_clear_color() != display_list.surface_clear_color()
            || painted_frame.allows_lcd_text != allows_lcd_text
        {
            changes.repaints_everything = true;
        }

        // Live content that no command of this list draws, such as an image that a filter of the visual context tree
        // draws, has no command in this list to damage.
        let canvas_ids_of_list: HashSet<u64> = display_list.storage().summary().canvas_ids.iter().copied().collect();
        for (canvas_id, content_generation) in &painted_frame.canvas_content_generations {
            let current_content_generation = live_content
                .canvases
                .get(canvas_id)
                .map_or(0, |canvas| canvas.content_generation);
            if current_content_generation == *content_generation {
                continue;
            }
            if !canvas_ids_of_list.contains(canvas_id) {
                changes.repaints_everything = true;
            }
            changes.canvas_or_video_changed = true;
        }
        let summary = display_list.storage().summary();
        let image_frame_ids_of_list: HashSet<u64> = summary.image_frame_ids.iter().copied().collect();
        let video_sink_handles_of_list: HashSet<u64> = summary.video_sink_handles.iter().copied().collect();
        for (video_sink_handle, frame_id) in &painted_frame.video_frame_ids {
            let current_frame_id = live_content
                .video_sinks
                .get(video_sink_handle)
                .and_then(|sink| sink.has_frame.then_some(sink.frame_id));
            if current_frame_id == *frame_id {
                continue;
            }
            if !video_sink_handles_of_list.contains(video_sink_handle) {
                changes.repaints_everything = true;
            }
            changes.canvas_or_video_changed = true;
        }
        for (&image_frame_id, &pixel_generation) in &live_content.image_frames {
            if painted_frame.image_frame_pixel_generations.get(&image_frame_id) == Some(&pixel_generation) {
                continue;
            }
            if !image_frame_ids_of_list.contains(&image_frame_id) {
                changes.repaints_everything = true;
            }
        }
        let nested_context_ids_of_list: HashSet<u64> = summary.composited_context_ids.iter().copied().collect();
        for (&nested_context_id, &frame_generation) in &painted_frame.nested_context_frame_generations {
            let nested_context = CompositorContextId(nested_context_id);
            if env.nested_contexts.frame_generation_of(nested_context) == frame_generation {
                continue;
            }
            if !nested_context_ids_of_list.contains(&nested_context_id) {
                changes.repaints_everything = true;
            }
        }
        changes
    }

    pub(super) fn frame_damage_for(
        &mut self,
        env: &PresentingEnvironment<'_>,
        pending_frame: &PendingFrame,
        frame: &FrameToPaint<'_>,
        live_content: &LiveContent,
    ) -> FrameDamage {
        let viewport_size = IntSize {
            width: pending_frame.viewport_rect.width,
            height: pending_frame.viewport_rect.height,
        };
        let viewport_rect = rect_of_size(viewport_size);
        let raster_rect = self.raster_rect();
        let forced_damage_rect = pending_frame.forced_damage_rect.intersected(viewport_rect);
        let allows_lcd_text = self.allows_lcd_text(frame.display_list, frame.frame_inputs);
        let changes = self.live_content_changes_since_last_paint(
            env,
            viewport_size,
            frame.display_list,
            allows_lcd_text,
            live_content,
        );
        let invalidates_every_tile = changes.repaints_everything;
        let (layer_update, stale_rect) = self.layer_update_for(
            env,
            frame,
            raster_rect,
            live_content,
            invalidates_every_tile,
            allows_lcd_text,
        );
        let live_media_changed = changes.canvas_or_video_changed;

        let forced_damage_rect = self.raster_rect_of(forced_damage_rect);
        let damage_of_layers_moved_by_animated_transforms =
            self.damage_of_layers_moved_by_animated_transforms(&layer_update, raster_rect);
        let repaints_everything = invalidates_every_tile
            || damage_of_layers_moved_by_animated_transforms.is_none()
            || self.layer_overlay.repaints_everything();
        let stale_rect = stale_rect.united(damage_of_layers_moved_by_animated_transforms.unwrap_or_default());
        FrameDamage {
            rect_in_raster_device_pixels: if repaints_everything {
                raster_rect
            } else {
                layer_update.damage_grown_over_what_composited_effects_read(forced_damage_rect.united(stale_rect))
            },
            layers: layer_update,
            live_media_changed,
        }
    }
}

/*
