use libcompositing_rust::display_list::replay::{ScrollbarShownByFrame, thumb_rect_kept_inside_track};
use libcompositing_rust::scrolling::overlay_fade::OverlayFade;
use libcompositing_rust::scrolling::{
    AccumulatedVisualContextTree, AsyncScrollNodeStableID, AsyncScrollTree, AsyncScrollbar, ClipBehavior,
    CompositorContextId, OverlayScrollbarVisibility, ScrollStateSnapshot, ScrollbarDraggedByCompositor,
    SpatialNodeIndex,
};
use libcompositing_rust::time::{Duration, MonotonicTime};
use libgfx_rust::{FloatPoint, FloatRect, IntRect, Orientation};

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct ScrollbarController {
    scrollbars: Vec<AsyncScrollbar>,
    // One for each scrollbar, in the same order.
    visibilities: Vec<Visibility>,
    hovered_scrollbar_index: Option<usize>,
    captured_scrollbar_index: Option<usize>,
    thumb_grab_position: f32,
    last_primary_position_of_captured_drag: f32,
    scrollbars_always_shown: bool,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Drag {
    pub scrollbar_index: usize,
    pub primary_position: f32,
    pub thumb_grab_position: f32,
    // Whether this is the press that began the drag, beside the thumb rather than on it.
    pub is_press_beside_thumb: bool,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct ScrollOffset {
    pub scroll_node_index: SpatialNodeIndex,
    pub scroll_offset: FloatPoint,
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct Visibility {
    fade: OverlayFade,
    // The scroll offset of the scroller as of the last update, which a scroll changes.
    scroll_offset: Option<FloatPoint>,
    is_held_shown: bool,
    fade_out_time: Option<MonotonicTime>,
    // How far the scrollbar has grown from its thin geometry to its expanded one.
    expansion: OverlayFade,
    // Whether the main thread was last told that the scrollbar has faded out.
    reported_hidden: bool,
}

impl Clone for Visibility {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            fade: self.fade,
            scroll_offset: self.scroll_offset,
            is_held_shown: self.is_held_shown,
            fade_out_time: self.fade_out_time,
            expansion: self.expansion,
            reported_hidden: self.reported_hidden,
        }
    }
}

fn orientation_for_scrollbar(scrollbar: &AsyncScrollbar) -> Orientation {
    if scrollbar.vertical {
        Orientation::Vertical
    } else {
        Orientation::Horizontal
    }
}

// A scroll node index can be given to another scroller by the next display list, so a scrollbar is recognized by the
// stable id of its scroller wherever both display lists name one.
struct ScrollbarIdentity {
    scroller_stable_node_id: Option<AsyncScrollNodeStableID>,
    scroll_node_index: SpatialNodeIndex,
    vertical: bool,
}

fn scrollbar_identity(scrollbar: &AsyncScrollbar) -> ScrollbarIdentity {
    ScrollbarIdentity {
        scroller_stable_node_id: scrollbar.scroller_stable_node_id,
        scroll_node_index: scrollbar.scroll_node_index,
        vertical: scrollbar.vertical,
    }
}

fn scrollbar_identity_at(scrollbars: &[AsyncScrollbar], scrollbar_index: Option<usize>) -> Option<ScrollbarIdentity> {
    Some(scrollbar_identity(scrollbars.get(scrollbar_index?)?))
}

fn scrollbar_has_identity(scrollbar: &AsyncScrollbar, identity: &ScrollbarIdentity) -> bool {
    if scrollbar.vertical != identity.vertical {
        return false;
    }
    if let (Some(scroller), Some(identity)) = (scrollbar.scroller_stable_node_id, identity.scroller_stable_node_id) {
        return scroller == identity;
    }
    scrollbar.scroll_node_index == identity.scroll_node_index
}

fn find_scrollbar_index(scrollbars: &[AsyncScrollbar], identity: &ScrollbarIdentity) -> Option<usize> {
    scrollbars
        .iter()
        .position(|scrollbar| scrollbar_has_identity(scrollbar, identity))
}

// The rects of a scrollbar are in the space of the context it is painted in.
fn position_in_space_of_scrollbar(
    scrollbar: &AsyncScrollbar,
    visual_context_tree: &AccumulatedVisualContextTree,
    scroll_state_snapshot: &ScrollStateSnapshot,
    position: FloatPoint,
    clip_behavior: ClipBehavior,
) -> Option<FloatPoint> {
    if !visual_context_tree.context_is_valid(scrollbar.context) {
        return None;
    }
    visual_context_tree.transform_point_for_hit_test(scrollbar.context, position, scroll_state_snapshot, clip_behavior)
}

fn scrollbar_scroll_size(scrollbar: &AsyncScrollbar, expanded: bool) -> f64 {
    if expanded {
        scrollbar.expanded_scroll_size
    } else {
        scrollbar.scroll_size
    }
}

fn translated_thumb_rect(scrollbar: &AsyncScrollbar, scroll_offset: FloatPoint, expanded: bool) -> IntRect {
    let orientation = orientation_for_scrollbar(scrollbar);
    let mut thumb_rect = if expanded {
        scrollbar.expanded_thumb_rect
    } else {
        scrollbar.thumb_rect
    };
    thumb_rect.translate_primary_offset_for_orientation(
        orientation,
        (scroll_offset.primary_offset_for_orientation(orientation) as f64 * scrollbar_scroll_size(scrollbar, expanded))
            as i32,
    );
    thumb_rect
}

fn translated_thumb_rect_with_snapshot(
    scrollbar: &AsyncScrollbar,
    scroll_state_snapshot: &ScrollStateSnapshot,
    expanded: bool,
) -> IntRect {
    let mut thumb_rect = if expanded {
        scrollbar.expanded_thumb_rect
    } else {
        scrollbar.thumb_rect
    };
    let scroll_size = scrollbar_scroll_size(scrollbar, expanded);
    let device_offset = scroll_state_snapshot.device_offset_for_index(scrollbar.scroll_node_index);
    if scrollbar.vertical {
        thumb_rect.y += ((-device_offset.y) as f64 * scroll_size) as i32;
    } else {
        thumb_rect.x += ((-device_offset.x) as f64 * scroll_size) as i32;
    }
    thumb_rect
}

impl ScrollbarController {
    // Overlay scrollbars are hidden until their scroller scrolls. A scrollbar stays shown for this long after its
    // scroller last scrolled or the pointer left it, and then fades out.
    pub const SHOWN_DURATION_AFTER_ACTIVITY: Duration = Duration::from_milliseconds(1000);

    // Tests see every scrollbar at all times, as when it is shown depends on the time.
    pub fn new(scrollbars_always_shown: bool) -> Self {
        Self {
            scrollbars_always_shown,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.scrollbars.clear();
        self.visibilities.clear();
        self.hovered_scrollbar_index = None;
        self.captured_scrollbar_index = None;
        self.thumb_grab_position = 0.0;
        self.last_primary_position_of_captured_drag = 0.0;
    }

    pub fn set_scrollbars(&mut self, scrollbars: &[AsyncScrollbar]) {
        let hovered_scrollbar_identity = scrollbar_identity_at(&self.scrollbars, self.hovered_scrollbar_index);
        let captured_scrollbar_identity = scrollbar_identity_at(&self.scrollbars, self.captured_scrollbar_index);

        let mut visibilities = Vec::with_capacity(scrollbars.len());
        for scrollbar in scrollbars {
            let previous_index = find_scrollbar_index(&self.scrollbars, &scrollbar_identity(scrollbar));
            visibilities
                .push(previous_index.map_or_else(Visibility::default, |index| self.visibilities[index].clone()));
        }

        self.scrollbars = scrollbars.to_vec();
        self.visibilities = visibilities;
        self.hovered_scrollbar_index =
            hovered_scrollbar_identity.and_then(|identity| find_scrollbar_index(&self.scrollbars, &identity));
        self.captured_scrollbar_index =
            captured_scrollbar_identity.and_then(|identity| find_scrollbar_index(&self.scrollbars, &identity));
        if self.captured_scrollbar_index.is_none() {
            self.thumb_grab_position = 0.0;
        }
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.scrollbars.is_empty()
    }
    pub fn scrollbars(&self) -> &[AsyncScrollbar] {
        &self.scrollbars
    }
    pub fn has_captured_scrollbar(&self) -> bool {
        self.captured_scrollbar_index.is_some()
    }
    pub fn captured_scrollbar_index(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        self.captured_scrollbar_index
    }
    // Whether the scrollbar is shown, rather than hidden until its scroller next scrolls.
    pub fn is_shown(&self, scrollbar_index: usize) -> bool {
        self.opacity(scrollbar_index) > 0.0
    }

    // The main thread still takes the mouse events of a drag that holds a scrollbar of an element, but none of a drag that
    // holds a scrollbar of the viewport. The context is the one this controller belongs to.
    pub fn captured_scrollbar_the_page_takes(
        &self,
        context_id: CompositorContextId,
    ) -> Option<ScrollbarDraggedByCompositor> {
        let scrollbar = self.scrollbars.get(self.captured_scrollbar_index?)?;
        if scrollbar.scrolls_viewport || scrollbar.scroller_stable_node_id.is_none() {
            return None;
        }
        Some(ScrollbarDraggedByCompositor {
            context_id,
            scroller_stable_node_id: scrollbar.scroller_stable_node_id?,
        })
    }

    // A scrollbar takes the pointer inside the rect of the scrollbar as it is presented now, and only with nothing that
    // takes pointer input painted over it there. A scrollbar that has faded out takes none, as the main thread passes it
    // by.
    pub fn hit_test_scrollbar(
        &self,
        async_scroll_tree: &AsyncScrollTree,
        visual_context_tree: &AccumulatedVisualContextTree,
        scroll_state_snapshot: &ScrollStateSnapshot,
        position: FloatPoint,
    ) -> Option<usize> {
        for (i, scrollbar) in self.scrollbars.iter().enumerate().rev() {
            if scrollbar.scroller_stable_node_id.is_none() || !self.is_shown(i) {
                continue;
            }
            if async_scroll_tree
                .scroll_offset_for_node(scrollbar.scroll_node_index, scroll_state_snapshot)
                .is_none()
            {
                continue;
            }

            let Some(position_in_scrollbar_space) = position_in_space_of_scrollbar(
                scrollbar,
                visual_context_tree,
                scroll_state_snapshot,
                position,
                ClipBehavior::Respect,
            ) else {
                continue;
            };
            let presented_scrollbar_rect = if self.expansion(i) > 0.0 {
                scrollbar.expanded_gutter_rect
            } else {
                scrollbar.track_rect
            };
            if !presented_scrollbar_rect
                .to_float()
                .contains_point(position_in_scrollbar_space)
            {
                continue;
            }

            if async_scroll_tree.is_covered_by_hit_test_target_painted_after(
                scrollbar.paint_order_index,
                visual_context_tree,
                position,
            ) {
                return None;
            }
            return Some(i);
        }
        None
    }

    pub fn begin_drag(
        &mut self,
        async_scroll_tree: &AsyncScrollTree,
        visual_context_tree: &AccumulatedVisualContextTree,
        scroll_state_snapshot: &ScrollStateSnapshot,
        position: FloatPoint,
    ) -> Option<Drag> {
        let scrollbar_index =
            self.hit_test_scrollbar(async_scroll_tree, visual_context_tree, scroll_state_snapshot, position)?;
        // INTEROP: A scrollbar that has faded out takes no press, as in Chromium.
        if self.opacity(scrollbar_index) <= 0.0 {
            return None;
        }

        let scrollbar = &self.scrollbars[scrollbar_index];
        let scroll_offset =
            async_scroll_tree.scroll_offset_for_node(scrollbar.scroll_node_index, scroll_state_snapshot);
        assert!(scroll_offset.is_some());
        let position_in_scrollbar_space = position_in_space_of_scrollbar(
            scrollbar,
            visual_context_tree,
            scroll_state_snapshot,
            position,
            ClipBehavior::Respect,
        );
        assert!(position_in_scrollbar_space.is_some());

        let orientation = orientation_for_scrollbar(scrollbar);
        // A successful press captures and expands the scrollbar before its drag delta is applied.
        let expanded = true;
        let thumb_rect = translated_thumb_rect(scrollbar, scroll_offset.unwrap(), expanded);
        let thumb_hit_rect = thumb_rect.to_float();

        let primary_position = position_in_scrollbar_space
            .unwrap()
            .primary_offset_for_orientation(orientation);
        let position_is_along_thumb = if orientation == Orientation::Vertical {
            thumb_hit_rect.contains_vertically(primary_position)
        } else {
            thumb_hit_rect.contains_horizontally(primary_position)
        };
        let thumb_grab_position = if position_is_along_thumb {
            primary_position - thumb_rect.primary_offset_for_orientation(orientation) as f32
        } else {
            let gutter_rect = scrollbar.expanded_gutter_rect;
            let thumb_size = thumb_rect.primary_size_for_orientation(orientation) as f32;
            let gutter_start = gutter_rect.primary_offset_for_orientation(orientation) as f32;
            let gutter_size = gutter_rect.primary_size_for_orientation(orientation) as f32;
            let offset_relative_to_gutter = primary_position - gutter_start;
            max(
                min(offset_relative_to_gutter, thumb_size / 2.0),
                offset_relative_to_gutter - gutter_size + thumb_size,
            )
        };

        self.captured_scrollbar_index = Some(scrollbar_index);
        self.hovered_scrollbar_index = Some(scrollbar_index);
        self.thumb_grab_position = thumb_grab_position;
        self.last_primary_position_of_captured_drag = primary_position;
        Some(Drag {
            scrollbar_index,
            primary_position,
            thumb_grab_position,
            is_press_beside_thumb: !position_is_along_thumb,
        })
    }

    // A drag usually leaves the clip of its scrollbar, and the spaces above the scrollbar may move while it lasts, so the
    // position is mapped anew for every event without regard to clips. A position that cannot be mapped moves nothing.
    fn primary_position_of_captured_drag(
        &mut self,
        visual_context_tree: &AccumulatedVisualContextTree,
        scroll_state_snapshot: &ScrollStateSnapshot,
        position: FloatPoint,
    ) -> f32 {
        if let Some(scrollbar) = self
            .captured_scrollbar_index
            .and_then(|index| self.scrollbars.get(index))
            && let Some(position_in_scrollbar_space) = position_in_space_of_scrollbar(
                scrollbar,
                visual_context_tree,
                scroll_state_snapshot,
                position,
                ClipBehavior::Ignore,
            )
        {
            self.last_primary_position_of_captured_drag =
                position_in_scrollbar_space.primary_offset_for_orientation(orientation_for_scrollbar(scrollbar));
        }
        self.last_primary_position_of_captured_drag
    }

    pub fn captured_drag(
        &mut self,
        visual_context_tree: &AccumulatedVisualContextTree,
        scroll_state_snapshot: &ScrollStateSnapshot,
        position: FloatPoint,
    ) -> Option<Drag> {
        let scrollbar_index = self.captured_scrollbar_index?;
        let primary_position =
            self.primary_position_of_captured_drag(visual_context_tree, scroll_state_snapshot, position);
        Some(Drag {
            scrollbar_index,
            primary_position,
            thumb_grab_position: self.thumb_grab_position,
            ..Default::default()
        })
    }

    pub fn release_captured_drag(
        &mut self,
        visual_context_tree: &AccumulatedVisualContextTree,
        scroll_state_snapshot: &ScrollStateSnapshot,
        position: FloatPoint,
    ) -> Option<Drag> {
        let scrollbar_index = self.captured_scrollbar_index?;
        let thumb_grab_position = self.thumb_grab_position;
        let primary_position =
            self.primary_position_of_captured_drag(visual_context_tree, scroll_state_snapshot, position);
        self.captured_scrollbar_index = None;
        self.thumb_grab_position = 0.0;
        Some(Drag {
            scrollbar_index,
            primary_position,
            thumb_grab_position,
            ..Default::default()
        })
    }

    pub fn set_hovered_scrollbar(&mut self, scrollbar_index: Option<usize>) -> bool {
        if self.hovered_scrollbar_index == scrollbar_index {
            return false;
        }
        self.hovered_scrollbar_index = scrollbar_index;
        true
    }

    pub fn scroll_offset_for_drag(
        &self,
        async_scroll_tree: &AsyncScrollTree,
        scroll_state_snapshot: &ScrollStateSnapshot,
        drag: &Drag,
    ) -> Option<ScrollOffset> {
        let scrollbar = self.scrollbars.get(drag.scrollbar_index)?;
        let expanded = self.is_expanded(drag.scrollbar_index);
        let scroll_size = scrollbar_scroll_size(scrollbar, expanded);
        if scroll_size == 0.0 {
            return None;
        }

        let current_scroll_offset =
            async_scroll_tree.scroll_offset_for_node(scrollbar.scroll_node_index, scroll_state_snapshot)?;
        let orientation = orientation_for_scrollbar(scrollbar);
        let thumb_rect = if expanded {
            scrollbar.expanded_thumb_rect
        } else {
            scrollbar.thumb_rect
        };
        let zero_offset_thumb_position = thumb_rect.primary_offset_for_orientation(orientation) as f32;
        let min_thumb_position = zero_offset_thumb_position + scrollbar.min_scroll_offset * scroll_size as f32;
        let max_thumb_position = zero_offset_thumb_position + scrollbar.max_scroll_offset * scroll_size as f32;
        if min_thumb_position.is_nan() || max_thumb_position.is_nan() || max_thumb_position < min_thumb_position {
            return None;
        }
        let target_thumb_position = clamp(
            drag.primary_position - drag.thumb_grab_position,
            min_thumb_position,
            max_thumb_position,
        );
        let mut target_scroll_offset = (target_thumb_position - zero_offset_thumb_position) / scroll_size as f32;
        // A thumb at either end of its track scrolls exactly to that end, whatever rounding the division above suffers.
        if target_thumb_position == min_thumb_position {
            target_scroll_offset = scrollbar.min_scroll_offset;
        } else if target_thumb_position == max_thumb_position {
            target_scroll_offset = scrollbar.max_scroll_offset;
        }

        let mut scroll_offset = current_scroll_offset;
        scroll_offset.set_primary_offset_for_orientation(orientation, target_scroll_offset);
        Some(ScrollOffset {
            scroll_node_index: scrollbar.scroll_node_index,
            scroll_offset,
        })
    }

    // Which way a press beside the thumb pages: -1 or 1 toward the pointer from where the thumb is at the given scroll
    // offset, or 0 when the thumb is under the pointer.
    pub fn paging_direction(&self, scrollbar_index: usize, primary_position: f32, scroll_offset: FloatPoint) -> i32 {
        let Some(scrollbar) = self.scrollbars.get(scrollbar_index) else {
            return 0;
        };
        let orientation = orientation_for_scrollbar(scrollbar);
        let thumb_rect = translated_thumb_rect(scrollbar, scroll_offset, self.is_expanded(scrollbar_index));
        if primary_position < thumb_rect.primary_offset_for_orientation(orientation) as f32 {
            return -1;
        }
        if primary_position
            >= (thumb_rect.primary_offset_for_orientation(orientation)
                + thumb_rect.primary_size_for_orientation(orientation)) as f32
        {
            return 1;
        }
        0
    }

    // Shows each scrollbar whose scroller scrolled since the last call, keeps a shown scrollbar that is hovered or
    // dragged shown, and starts the wait before a scrollbar that is no longer hovered or dragged fades out. A hovered or
    // dragged scrollbar that is shown grows to its expanded geometry, and keeps it until it has faded out.
    pub fn update_visibility(&mut self, scroll_state_snapshot: &ScrollStateSnapshot, now: MonotonicTime) {
        for i in 0..self.scrollbars.len() {
            let expanded = self.is_expanded(i);
            let visibility = &mut self.visibilities[i];
            let scrollbar = &self.scrollbars[i];
            let scroll_offset = scroll_state_snapshot.device_offset_for_index(scrollbar.scroll_node_index);
            let scrolled = visibility.scroll_offset.is_some_and(|offset| offset != scroll_offset);
            visibility.scroll_offset = Some(scroll_offset);

            let was_held_shown = visibility.is_held_shown;
            // Hovering a hidden scrollbar does not show it. Only a scroll does.
            visibility.is_held_shown = expanded && (scrolled || visibility.fade.opacity() > 0.0);
            if visibility.is_held_shown {
                visibility.fade.jump_to(1.0);
                visibility.fade_out_time = None;
                visibility.expansion.fade_to(1.0, now);
                continue;
            }
            if scrolled {
                visibility.fade.jump_to(1.0);
            }
            if scrolled || was_held_shown {
                visibility.fade_out_time = Some(now + Self::SHOWN_DURATION_AFTER_ACTIVITY);
            }
        }
    }

    // When the next scrollbar starts to fade out.
    pub fn next_fade_out_time(&self) -> Option<MonotonicTime> {
        let mut next_fade_out_time = None;
        for visibility in &self.visibilities {
            if let Some(time) = visibility.fade_out_time
                && next_fade_out_time.is_none_or(|next| time < next)
            {
                next_fade_out_time = Some(time);
            }
        }
        next_fade_out_time
    }

    // The scrollbars that faded out or were shown again since the last call. The main thread hit tests the scrollbars
    // too, and passes by the ones that have faded out.
    pub fn take_visibility_changes(&mut self) -> Vec<OverlayScrollbarVisibility> {
        let mut changes = Vec::new();
        for i in 0..self.scrollbars.len() {
            let hidden = self.opacity(i) <= 0.0;
            let scrollbar = &self.scrollbars[i];
            let visibility = &mut self.visibilities[i];
            let Some(scroller_stable_node_id) = scrollbar.scroller_stable_node_id else {
                continue;
            };
            if hidden == visibility.reported_hidden {
                continue;
            }
            visibility.reported_hidden = hidden;
            changes.push(OverlayScrollbarVisibility {
                scroller_stable_node_id,
                vertical: scrollbar.vertical,
                hidden,
            });
        }
        changes
    }

    pub fn fades_need_frame(&self, now: MonotonicTime) -> bool {
        for visibility in &self.visibilities {
            if visibility.fade.is_fading()
                || visibility.expansion.is_fading()
                || visibility.fade_out_time.is_some_and(|time| time <= now)
            {
                return true;
            }
        }
        false
    }

    // Advances the fades to a frame, and answers whether any scrollbar changed. The frame finds what changed in the
    // content hashes of the records of the scrollbars.
    pub fn advance_fades(&mut self, frame_time: MonotonicTime) -> bool {
        let mut some_scrollbar_changed = false;
        for visibility in &mut self.visibilities {
            if visibility.fade_out_time.is_some_and(|time| time <= frame_time) {
                visibility.fade_out_time = None;
                visibility.fade.fade_to(0.0, frame_time);
            }
            let mut changed = visibility.fade.advance_to(frame_time);
            // A scrollbar that has faded out is thin again when it is next shown.
            if visibility.fade.opacity() <= 0.0 {
                visibility.expansion.jump_to(0.0);
            }
            changed |= visibility.expansion.advance_to(frame_time);
            some_scrollbar_changed |= changed;
        }
        some_scrollbar_changed
    }
}

fn interpolated_rect(from: IntRect, to: IntRect, progress: f32) -> FloatRect {
    let interpolate = |from: i32, to: i32| from as f32 + (to - from) as f32 * progress;
    FloatRect::new(
        interpolate(from.x, to.x),
        interpolate(from.y, to.y),
        interpolate(from.width, to.width),
        interpolate(from.height, to.height),
    )
}

impl ScrollbarController {
    pub fn scrollbars_of_frame(&self, scroll_state_snapshot: &ScrollStateSnapshot) -> Vec<ScrollbarShownByFrame> {
        let mut scrollbars_of_frame = Vec::with_capacity(self.scrollbars.len());
        for (i, scrollbar) in self.scrollbars.iter().enumerate() {
            let progress = self.expansion(i);
            let mut thin_thumb_rect = thumb_rect_kept_inside_track(
                translated_thumb_rect_with_snapshot(scrollbar, scroll_state_snapshot, false),
                scrollbar.track_rect,
                scrollbar.vertical,
            );
            let mut expanded_thumb_rect = thumb_rect_kept_inside_track(
                translated_thumb_rect_with_snapshot(scrollbar, scroll_state_snapshot, true),
                scrollbar.expanded_gutter_rect,
                scrollbar.vertical,
            );
            // An empty thumb has nothing to grow from or to.
            if thin_thumb_rect.is_empty() {
                thin_thumb_rect = expanded_thumb_rect;
            }
            if expanded_thumb_rect.is_empty() {
                expanded_thumb_rect = thin_thumb_rect;
            }

            scrollbars_of_frame.push(ScrollbarShownByFrame {
                scroll_node_index: scrollbar.scroll_node_index,
                vertical: scrollbar.vertical,
                gutter_rect: interpolated_rect(scrollbar.track_rect, scrollbar.expanded_gutter_rect, progress),
                thumb_rect: interpolated_rect(thin_thumb_rect, expanded_thumb_rect, progress),
                expansion: progress,
                opacity: self.opacity(i),
            });
        }
        scrollbars_of_frame
    }

    fn is_expanded(&self, scrollbar_index: usize) -> bool {
        self.hovered_scrollbar_index == Some(scrollbar_index) || self.captured_scrollbar_index == Some(scrollbar_index)
    }

    fn opacity(&self, scrollbar_index: usize) -> f32 {
        if self.scrollbars_always_shown {
            return 1.0;
        }
        self.visibilities
            .get(scrollbar_index)
            .map_or(0.0, |visibility| visibility.fade.opacity())
    }

    fn expansion(&self, scrollbar_index: usize) -> f32 {
        if self.scrollbars_always_shown {
            return if self.is_expanded(scrollbar_index) { 1.0 } else { 0.0 };
        }
        self.visibilities
            .get(scrollbar_index)
            .map_or(0.0, |visibility| visibility.expansion.opacity())
    }
}

fn min(a: f32, b: f32) -> f32 {
    if b < a { b } else { a }
}
fn max(a: f32, b: f32) -> f32 {
    if a < b { b } else { a }
}
fn clamp(value: f32, min: f32, max: f32) -> f32 {
    assert!(max >= min);
    if value > max {
        max
    } else if value < min {
        min
    } else {
        value
    }
}

/*

//! A surface the Compositor paints into, which the core and the C++ around it share by reference counting: a pointer to
//! a `Gfx::PaintingSurface` is the `PaintingSurface` of an `Rc`. The Skia part of the surface is C++, and the surface
//! owns it. Only the Compositor's main thread may retain, release or read a surface.

use libgfx_rust::IntSize;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::ptr::NonNull;
use std::rc::Rc;

pub struct PaintingSurface {
    size: IntSize,
    gpu_backend_context: *const c_void,
    skia_surface: NonNull<c_void>,
    destroy_skia_surface: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
}

impl PaintingSurface {
    pub fn size(&self) -> IntSize {
        self.size
    }

    pub fn uses_gpu(&self) -> bool {
        !self.gpu_backend_context.is_null()
    }

    pub fn shares_backend_with(&self, other: &PaintingSurface) -> bool {
        self.gpu_backend_context == other.gpu_backend_context
    }

    /// Null for a surface in memory.
    pub fn gpu_backend_context(&self) -> *const c_void {
        self.gpu_backend_context
    }

    pub fn as_ffi(self: &Rc<Self>) -> *const PaintingSurface {
        Rc::as_ptr(self)
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `surface` must be a live surface, which then has one more owner.
    pub unsafe fn retained_from_ffi(surface: *const PaintingSurface) -> Rc<PaintingSurface> {
        assert!(!surface.is_null(), "the C++ side passes a surface");
        // SAFETY: The caller passes the PaintingSurface of a live Rc.
        unsafe {
            Rc::increment_strong_count(surface);
            Rc::from_raw(surface)
        }
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `surface` must be a surface whose one reference the caller hands over, or null.
    pub unsafe fn adopted_from_ffi(surface: *const PaintingSurface) -> Option<Rc<PaintingSurface>> {
        if surface.is_null() {
            return None;
        }
        // SAFETY: The caller hands over one reference to the PaintingSurface of a live Rc.
        Some(unsafe { Rc::from_raw(surface) })
    }

    pub fn into_ffi(surface: Rc<PaintingSurface>) -> *const PaintingSurface {
        Rc::into_raw(surface)
    }
}

impl Drop for PaintingSurface {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: The surface owns its Skia part, which nothing uses once the last reference is gone.
        unsafe { (self.destroy_skia_surface)(self.skia_surface.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

/// A new surface whose one reference the caller owns and gives up with `compositor_painting_surface_release()`. It
/// takes over the Skia part, which it destroys with `destroy_skia_surface` once the last reference is gone. A GPU
/// surface names the backend context it renders with, which surfaces that can be drawn into each other share.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `skia_surface` must be a live Skia part that `destroy_skia_surface` destroys.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn compositor_painting_surface_create(
    size: IntSize,
    gpu_backend_context: *const c_void,
    skia_surface: *mut c_void,
    destroy_skia_surface: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
) -> *const PaintingSurface {
    let skia_surface = NonNull::new(skia_surface).expect("the C++ side passes the Skia part of the surface");
    PaintingSurface::into_ffi(Rc::new(PaintingSurface {
        size,
        gpu_backend_context,
        skia_surface,
        destroy_skia_surface,
    }))
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `surface` must be a live surface.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn compositor_painting_surface_retain(surface: *const PaintingSurface) {
    assert!(!surface.is_null(), "the C++ side passes a surface");
    // SAFETY: The caller passes the PaintingSurface of a live Rc.
    unsafe { Rc::increment_strong_count(surface) };
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `surface` must be a live surface of which the caller owns a reference.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn compositor_painting_surface_release(surface: *const PaintingSurface) {
    assert!(!surface.is_null(), "the C++ side passes a surface");
    // SAFETY: The caller gives up one of its references to the PaintingSurface of a live Rc.
    unsafe { Rc::decrement_strong_count(surface) };
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn compositor_painting_surface_skia_surface(surface: &PaintingSurface) -> *mut c_void {
    surface.skia_surface.as_ptr()
}

/// NB: A C++ function returns Gfx::IntSize in memory rather than in a register on Windows, so the size is written.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn compositor_painting_surface_size(surface: &PaintingSurface, size: &mut IntSize) {
    *size = surface.size;
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub mod testing {
    use super::*;
    use std::cell::Cell;

    thread_local! {
        pub static DESTROYED_SKIA_SURFACES: Cell<usize> = const { Cell::new(0) };
    }

    unsafe extern "C" fn count_destroyed_skia_surface(_: *mut c_void) {
        DESTROYED_SKIA_SURFACES.with(|count| count.set(count.get() + 1));
    }

    pub fn surface_for_testing(size: IntSize, gpu_backend_context: usize) -> Rc<PaintingSurface> {
        // SAFETY: The Skia part is a dangling pointer that only the counting destroy function sees.
        let surface = unsafe {
            compositor_painting_surface_create(
                size,
                gpu_backend_context as *const c_void,
                NonNull::<u8>::dangling().as_ptr().cast(),
                count_destroyed_skia_surface,
            )
        };
        // SAFETY: The surface was just made with one reference, which this takes over.
        unsafe { PaintingSurface::adopted_from_ffi(surface) }.expect("a new surface")
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::testing::*;
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn skia_part_is_destroyed_with_the_last_reference_from_either_side() {
        let before = DESTROYED_SKIA_SURFACES.with(|count| count.get());
        let surface = surface_for_testing(IntSize { width: 4, height: 3 }, 0);
        let pointer = surface.as_ffi();
        // SAFETY: The surface is live, and the reference taken here is given up below.
        unsafe { compositor_painting_surface_retain(pointer) };
        drop(surface);
        assert_eq!(DESTROYED_SKIA_SURFACES.with(|count| count.get()), before);
        // SAFETY: The reference taken above is given up.
        unsafe { compositor_painting_surface_release(pointer) };
        assert_eq!(DESTROYED_SKIA_SURFACES.with(|count| count.get()), before + 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn surfaces_share_a_backend_by_its_context() {
        let size = IntSize { width: 1, height: 1 };
        let gpu = surface_for_testing(size, 0x10);
        let same_gpu = surface_for_testing(size, 0x10);
        let cpu = surface_for_testing(size, 0);
        assert!(gpu.uses_gpu());
        assert!(!cpu.uses_gpu());
        assert!(gpu.shares_backend_with(&same_gpu));
        assert!(!gpu.shares_backend_with(&cpu));
    }
}

/*

//! A surface whose content the window server can show as it is, instead of after it is composited into a frame, which
//! the core and the C++ around it share by reference counting: a pointer to a `Compositor::PresentableSurface` is the
//! `PresentableSurface` of an `Rc`. While a lease of it is held, as by a frame on its way to the window server and by
//! the layer that shows it, or while the window server still reads it, the surface is busy, and its content must stay
//! as it is. Only the Compositor's main thread may use a surface.

use crate::surfaces::painting_surface::PaintingSurface;
use libgfx_rust::IntSize;
use std::cell::Cell;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::ptr::NonNull;
use std::rc::{Rc, Weak};

/// The part of a presentable surface that the window server shows, which is C++ and which the surface owns.
pub struct WindowServerSurface {
    surface: NonNull<c_void>,
    may_be_read_by_window_server: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void) -> bool,
    destroy: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
}

impl Drop for WindowServerSurface {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: The presentable surface owns the window server's part, which nothing uses once it is gone.
        unsafe { (self.destroy)(self.surface.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

pub struct PresentableSurface {
    painting_surface: Rc<PaintingSurface>,
    content_is_upside_down: bool,
    window_server_surface: Option<WindowServerSurface>,
    was_handed_to_window_server: Cell<bool>,
    lease_count: Cell<usize>,
}

impl PresentableSurface {
    pub fn painting_surface(&self) -> &Rc<PaintingSurface> {
        &self.painting_surface
    }

    pub fn size(&self) -> IntSize {
        self.painting_surface.size()
    }

    pub fn as_ffi(self: &Rc<Self>) -> *const PresentableSurface {
        Rc::as_ptr(self)
    }

    /// A surface over the painting surface that draws into memory the window server cannot read.
    pub fn shown_by_no_window_server(painting_surface: Rc<PaintingSurface>) -> Rc<PresentableSurface> {
        Rc::new(PresentableSurface {
            painting_surface,
            content_is_upside_down: false,
            window_server_surface: None,
            was_handed_to_window_server: Cell::new(false),
            lease_count: Cell::new(0),
        })
    }

    pub fn can_be_shown_by_window_server(&self) -> bool {
        self.window_server_surface.is_some()
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `surface` must be a surface whose one reference the caller hands over, or null.
    pub unsafe fn adopted_from_ffi(surface: *const PresentableSurface) -> Option<Rc<PresentableSurface>> {
        if surface.is_null() {
            return None;
        }
        // SAFETY: The caller hands over one reference to the PresentableSurface of a live Rc.
        Some(unsafe { Rc::from_raw(surface) })
    }

    // GPU work in flight on a surface counts as use too, so only a surface handed to the window server is checked.
    pub fn is_read_by_window_server(&self) -> bool {
        self.was_handed_to_window_server.get()
            && self
                .window_server_surface
                .as_ref()
                .is_some_and(|window_server_surface| {
                    // SAFETY: The window server's part is live for as long as the surface.
                    unsafe {
                        (window_server_surface.may_be_read_by_window_server)(window_server_surface.surface.as_ptr())
                    }
                })
    }

    pub fn is_busy(&self) -> bool {
        self.lease_count.get() > 0 || self.is_read_by_window_server()
    }

    pub fn lease(self: &Rc<Self>) -> PresentableSurfaceLease {
        self.lease_count.set(self.lease_count.get() + 1);
        PresentableSurfaceLease(self.clone())
    }
}

impl Drop for PresentableSurface {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        assert_eq!(self.lease_count.get(), 0, "a lease holds the surface");
    }
}

/// Keeps the content of the surface as it is for as long as it is held. Holding the surface itself does not.
pub struct PresentableSurfaceLease(Rc<PresentableSurface>);

impl PresentableSurfaceLease {
    pub fn surface(&self) -> &Rc<PresentableSurface> {
        &self.0
    }
}

impl Clone for PresentableSurfaceLease {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        self.0.lease()
    }
}

impl Drop for PresentableSurfaceLease {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let count = self.0.lease_count.get();
        assert!(count > 0, "the lease counts towards the surface");
        self.0.lease_count.set(count - 1);
    }
}

/// The surfaces that one piece of content, such as a canvas, is presented from in turn. The content goes into its
/// latest surface again unless that one is busy, so content that is only ever composited into frames keeps a single
/// surface.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct PresentableSurfacePool {
    // In the order the content went into them, the latest last.
    surfaces: Vec<Rc<PresentableSurface>>,
}

// A surface is only added while every other one is busy, so a pool holds about as many as are on their way to the
// window server or still read by it at once, which is a few. The limit only stops a pool whose surfaces never stop being
// busy from growing without end.
const MAXIMUM_SURFACE_COUNT_OF_POOL: usize = 8;

impl PresentableSurfacePool {
    /// A surface of the size for the next content, rendered with the GPU backend context given, which is never one that
    /// is busy. None when every surface is busy and the pool is full, or when `create` makes none, and the content then
    /// has to wait for a later turn.
    pub fn surface_for_next_content(
        &mut self,
        size: IntSize,
        gpu_backend_context: *const c_void,
        create: impl FnOnce() -> Option<Rc<PresentableSurface>>,
    ) -> Option<Rc<PresentableSurface>> {
        let fits = |surface: &PresentableSurface| {
            surface.size() == size && surface.painting_surface.gpu_backend_context() == gpu_backend_context
        };
        self.surfaces.retain(|surface| fits(surface) || surface.is_busy());

        let can_take_next_content = |surface: &PresentableSurface| fits(surface) && !surface.is_busy();
        if let Some(latest) = self.surfaces.last()
            && can_take_next_content(latest)
        {
            return Some(latest.clone());
        }
        if let Some(index) = self.surfaces.iter().position(|surface| can_take_next_content(surface)) {
            let surface = self.surfaces.remove(index);
            self.surfaces.push(surface.clone());
            return Some(surface);
        }

        if self.surfaces.len() >= MAXIMUM_SURFACE_COUNT_OF_POOL {
            return None;
        }
        let surface = create()?;
        self.surfaces.push(surface.clone());
        Some(surface)
    }
}

/// A new surface over the painting surface, whose one reference the caller owns and gives up with
/// `compositor_presentable_surface_release()`. It takes over the window server's part, if there is one, which it
/// destroys with `destroy_window_server_surface`.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `painting_surface` must be a live surface. A window server's part must be live and destroyed by
/// `destroy_window_server_surface`, and `may_be_read_by_window_server` must answer for it.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_create(
    painting_surface: *const PaintingSurface,
    content_is_upside_down: bool,
    window_server_surface: *mut c_void,
    may_be_read_by_window_server: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void) -> bool,
    destroy_window_server_surface: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
) -> *const PresentableSurface {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live surface, which the presentable surface holds.
    let painting_surface = unsafe { PaintingSurface::retained_from_ffi(painting_surface) };
    let window_server_surface = NonNull::new(window_server_surface).map(|surface| WindowServerSurface {
        surface,
        may_be_read_by_window_server,
        destroy: destroy_window_server_surface,
    });
    Rc::into_raw(Rc::new(PresentableSurface {
        painting_surface,
        content_is_upside_down,
        window_server_surface,
        was_handed_to_window_server: Cell::new(false),
        lease_count: Cell::new(0),
    }))
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `surface` must be a live surface.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_retain(surface: *const PresentableSurface) {
    assert!(!surface.is_null(), "the C++ side passes a surface");
    // SAFETY: The caller passes the PresentableSurface of a live Rc.
    unsafe { Rc::increment_strong_count(surface) };
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `surface` must be a live surface of which the caller owns a reference.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_release(surface: *const PresentableSurface) {
    assert!(!surface.is_null(), "the C++ side passes a surface");
    // SAFETY: The caller gives up one of its references to the PresentableSurface of a live Rc.
    unsafe { Rc::decrement_strong_count(surface) };
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_painting_surface(
    surface: &PresentableSurface,
) -> *const PaintingSurface {
    surface.painting_surface.as_ffi()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_content_is_upside_down(surface: &PresentableSurface) -> bool {
    surface.content_is_upside_down
}

/// The window server's part of the surface, or null for a surface that draws into memory the window server cannot read.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_window_server_surface(surface: &PresentableSurface) -> *mut c_void {
    surface
        .window_server_surface
        .as_ref()
        .map_or(std::ptr::null_mut(), |window_server_surface| {
            window_server_surface.surface.as_ptr()
        })
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_did_hand_to_window_server(surface: &PresentableSurface) {
    surface.was_handed_to_window_server.set(true);
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_is_read_by_window_server(surface: &PresentableSurface) -> bool {
    surface.is_read_by_window_server()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_is_busy(surface: &PresentableSurface) -> bool {
    surface.is_busy()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_add_lease(surface: &PresentableSurface) {
    surface.lease_count.set(surface.lease_count.get() + 1);
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_remove_lease(surface: &PresentableSurface) {
    let count = surface.lease_count.get();
    assert!(count > 0, "the lease counts towards the surface");
    surface.lease_count.set(count - 1);
}

pub struct WeakPresentableSurface(Weak<PresentableSurface>);

/// A weak reference to the surface, which `compositor_weak_presentable_surface_destroy()` gives up.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `surface` must be a live surface.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_downgrade(
    surface: *const PresentableSurface,
) -> *mut WeakPresentableSurface {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes the PresentableSurface of a live Rc, which this borrows only to downgrade it.
    let surface = std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(unsafe { Rc::from_raw(surface) });
    Box::into_raw(Box::new(WeakPresentableSurface(Rc::downgrade(&surface))))
}

/// A reference to the surface that the caller owns, or null once the surface is gone.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn compositor_weak_presentable_surface_upgrade(
    weak: &WeakPresentableSurface,
) -> *const PresentableSurface {
    weak.0.upgrade().map_or(std::ptr::null(), Rc::into_raw)
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `weak` must be null or a weak reference from `compositor_presentable_surface_downgrade()` that nothing uses
/// afterwards.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn compositor_weak_presentable_surface_destroy(weak: *mut WeakPresentableSurface) {
    if !weak.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: The caller hands over the weak reference.
        drop(unsafe { Box::from_raw(weak) });
    }
}

/// A pool of surfaces for C++ that presents content from one, which `compositor_presentable_surface_pool_destroy()`
/// destroys.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_pool_create() -> *mut PresentableSurfacePool {
    Box::into_raw(Box::default())
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `pool` must be null or a pool from `compositor_presentable_surface_pool_create()` that nothing uses afterwards.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_pool_destroy(pool: *mut PresentableSurfacePool) {
    if !pool.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: The caller hands over the pool.
        drop(unsafe { Box::from_raw(pool) });
    }
}

/// A surface of the pool for the next content, with one reference that the caller takes over, or null when the content
/// has to wait. A new surface comes from `create`, which hands over one reference to it or answers null.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `create` must answer as described while the call runs, and must not use the pool.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn compositor_presentable_surface_pool_surface_for_next_content(
    pool: &mut PresentableSurfacePool,
    size: IntSize,
    gpu_backend_context: *const c_void,
    create: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void) -> *const PresentableSurface,
    create_context: *mut c_void,
) -> *const PresentableSurface {
    pool.surface_for_next_content(size, gpu_backend_context, || {
        // SAFETY: The caller's `create` hands over a new surface or answers null.
        unsafe { PresentableSurface::adopted_from_ffi(create(create_context)) }
    })
    .map_or(std::ptr::null(), Rc::into_raw)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::surfaces::painting_surface::testing::surface_for_testing;

    unsafe extern "C" fn never_read(_: *mut c_void) -> bool {
        false
    }

    unsafe extern "C" fn destroy_nothing(_: *mut c_void) {}

    fn presentable_surface(size: IntSize) -> Rc<PresentableSurface> {
        let painting_surface = surface_for_testing(size, 0x10);
        // SAFETY: The painting surface is live, and there is no window server's part.
        let surface = unsafe {
            compositor_presentable_surface_create(
                painting_surface.as_ffi(),
                false,
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                never_read,
                destroy_nothing,
            )
        };
        // SAFETY: The surface was just made with one reference, which this takes over.
        unsafe { PresentableSurface::adopted_from_ffi(surface) }.expect("a new surface")
    }

    const SIZE: IntSize = IntSize { width: 8, height: 8 };
    const BACKEND: *const c_void = 0x10 as *const c_void;

    #[test]
    fn pool_reuses_its_latest_surface_while_nothing_holds_it() {
        let mut pool = PresentableSurfacePool::default();
        let first = pool
            .surface_for_next_content(SIZE, BACKEND, || Some(presentable_surface(SIZE)))
            .unwrap();
        let again = pool
            .surface_for_next_content(SIZE, BACKEND, || panic!("no new surface"))
            .unwrap();
        assert!(Rc::ptr_eq(&first, &again));
    }

    #[test]
    fn pool_adds_a_surface_while_the_others_are_leased() {
        let mut pool = PresentableSurfacePool::default();
        let first = pool
            .surface_for_next_content(SIZE, BACKEND, || Some(presentable_surface(SIZE)))
            .unwrap();
        let lease = first.lease();
        let second = pool
            .surface_for_next_content(SIZE, BACKEND, || Some(presentable_surface(SIZE)))
            .unwrap();
        assert!(!Rc::ptr_eq(&first, &second));
        drop(lease);
        let reused = pool
            .surface_for_next_content(SIZE, BACKEND, || panic!("no new surface"))
            .unwrap();
        assert!(Rc::ptr_eq(&second, &reused));
    }

    #[test]
    fn pool_stops_growing_when_every_surface_is_busy() {
        let mut pool = PresentableSurfacePool::default();
        let mut leases = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..MAXIMUM_SURFACE_COUNT_OF_POOL {
            let surface = pool
                .surface_for_next_content(SIZE, BACKEND, || Some(presentable_surface(SIZE)))
                .unwrap();
            leases.push(surface.lease());
        }
        assert!(
            pool.surface_for_next_content(SIZE, BACKEND, || panic!("no new surface"))
                .is_none()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn pool_drops_idle_surfaces_of_another_size() {
        let mut pool = PresentableSurfacePool::default();
        let small = pool
            .surface_for_next_content(SIZE, BACKEND, || Some(presentable_surface(SIZE)))
            .unwrap();
        let weak = Rc::downgrade(&small);
        drop(small);
        let larger = IntSize { width: 16, height: 16 };
        pool.surface_for_next_content(larger, BACKEND, || Some(presentable_surface(larger)))
            .unwrap();
        assert!(weak.upgrade().is_none());
    }
}

//! Stand-ins for the LibGfx process-wide counters, which the unit tests link without the C++ runtime.

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

// One counter stands in for each of LibGfx's process-wide counters: their values only need to be unique.
static NEXT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(1);

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
extern "C" fn ladybird_gfx_process_next_structural_epoch() -> u64 {
    NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
}

//! The commands and the synchronous calls whose structs GLFunctions.json spells out, which the replayer handles by
//! hand: those of the strings that GL takes as arrays, of the drawing buffer, and of the images that a texture upload
//! takes its pixels from.

use core::ffi::{CStr, c_char, c_void};

use libcompositing_rust::webgl::ImageSource;
use libcompositing_rust::webgl::texture_upload::texture_export_format;
use libcompositing_rust::webgl::vocabulary::{commands, sync_calls};
use libcompositing_rust::webgl::wire::{encode_reply, reply_data_spans};
use libgfx_rust::IntSize;

use super::gl::GlFunctions;
use super::gl_constants::*;
use super::host::{DefaultBuffers, ImageConversion, ImageConversionOutcome, VideoFrameCopy, WebGLHost};
use super::replay::{ReplayError, Replayer, bytes_of_slice, data_span, decode, split_packed_strings, string_data};

const MAX_DRAWING_BUFFER_DIMENSION: i32 = 16384;

fn copy_can_write_internal_format(internalformat: i32) -> bool {
    u32::try_from(internalformat).is_ok_and(|internalformat| {
        matches!(
            internalformat,
            GL_ALPHA
                | GL_LUMINANCE
                | GL_LUMINANCE_ALPHA
                | GL_RGB
                | GL_RGBA
                | GL_SRGB_EXT
                | GL_SRGB_ALPHA_EXT
                | GL_R8
                | GL_RG8
                | GL_RGB8
                | GL_RGBA8
                | GL_SRGB8
                | GL_SRGB8_ALPHA8
                | GL_RGB565
                | GL_RGBA4
                | GL_RGB5_A1
                | GL_RGB10_A2
                | GL_RGB9_E5
                | GL_R11F_G11F_B10F
                | GL_R16F
                | GL_RG16F
                | GL_RGB16F
                | GL_RGBA16F
                | GL_R32F
                | GL_RG32F
                | GL_RGB32F
                | GL_RGBA32F
        )
    })
}

fn format_is_integer(format: u32) -> bool {
    matches!(
        format,
        GL_RED_INTEGER | GL_RG_INTEGER | GL_RGB_INTEGER | GL_RGBA_INTEGER
    )
}

fn upload_size(
    frame_size: IntSize,
    has_explicit_destination_size: bool,
    destination_width: i32,
    destination_height: i32,
) -> Option<IntSize> {
    if !has_explicit_destination_size {
        return Some(frame_size);
    }
    (destination_width >= 0 && destination_height >= 0).then_some(IntSize {
        width: destination_width,
        height: destination_height,
    })
}

/// The extensions that GL has enabled, or that ANGLE can enable on request.
pub fn supported_extensions(gl: &GlFunctions) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut extensions = Vec::new();
    for list in [GL_EXTENSIONS, GL_REQUESTABLE_EXTENSIONS_ANGLE] {
        // SAFETY: A context is current, and GL answers a string or null.
        let names = unsafe { (gl.get_string)(list) };
        if names.is_null() {
            continue;
        }
        // SAFETY: GL answers a NUL-terminated string.
        let names = unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(names.cast()) }.to_string_lossy();
        extensions.extend(names.split(' ').filter(|name| !name.is_empty()).map(String::from));
    }
    extensions
}

fn extension_is_enabled(gl: &GlFunctions, extension: &[u8]) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: A context is current, and GL answers a string or null.
    let names = unsafe { (gl.get_string)(GL_EXTENSIONS) };
    // SAFETY: GL answers a NUL-terminated string.
    !names.is_null()
        && unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(names.cast()) }
            .to_bytes()
            .split(|&byte| byte == b' ')
            .any(|name| name == extension)
}

/// Clears the drawing buffer to the values that WebGL clears it to between frames, and restores the clear values and the
/// bindings of the page.
pub fn clear_buffer_to_default_values(gl: &GlFunctions, webgl2: bool, defaults: DefaultBuffers) {
    let (framebuffer_target, framebuffer_binding) = if webgl2 {
        (GL_DRAW_FRAMEBUFFER, GL_DRAW_FRAMEBUFFER_BINDING)
    } else {
        (GL_FRAMEBUFFER, GL_FRAMEBUFFER_BINDING)
    };
    let mut original_framebuffer = 0;
    let mut original_renderbuffer = 0;
    let mut clear_color = [0.0_f32; 4];
    let mut clear_depth = 0.0_f32;
    let mut clear_stencil = 0;
    // SAFETY: A context is current, and every pointer is room for what GL writes.
    unsafe {
        (gl.get_integerv)(framebuffer_binding, &raw mut original_framebuffer);
        (gl.get_integerv)(GL_RENDERBUFFER_BINDING, &raw mut original_renderbuffer);
        (gl.bind_framebuffer)(framebuffer_target, defaults.framebuffer);
        (gl.bind_renderbuffer)(GL_RENDERBUFFER, defaults.renderbuffer);
        (gl.get_floatv)(GL_COLOR_CLEAR_VALUE, clear_color.as_mut_ptr());
        (gl.get_floatv)(GL_DEPTH_CLEAR_VALUE, &raw mut clear_depth);
        (gl.get_integerv)(GL_STENCIL_CLEAR_VALUE, &raw mut clear_stencil);
        (gl.clear_color)(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
        (gl.clear_depthf)(1.0);
        (gl.clear_stencil)(0);
        (gl.clear)(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT | GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT | GL_STENCIL_BUFFER_BIT);
        (gl.clear_color)(clear_color[0], clear_color[1], clear_color[2], clear_color[3]);
        (gl.clear_depthf)(clear_depth);
        (gl.clear_stencil)(clear_stencil);
        (gl.bind_framebuffer)(framebuffer_target, original_framebuffer as u32);
        (gl.bind_renderbuffer)(GL_RENDERBUFFER, original_renderbuffer as u32);
    }
}

/// The pixels of an image as a texture upload takes them, or the negative size that GL is to reject.
struct ConvertedImage<P> {
    pixels: Option<P>,
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
}

/// What an upload from an image asks for, whatever kind of upload it is.
struct ImageUpload {
    bitmap_index: u32,
    format: u32,
    r#type: u32,
    has_explicit_destination_size: bool,
    destination_width: i32,
    destination_height: i32,
    flip_y: bool,
    premultiply_alpha: bool,
}

macro_rules! image_upload {
    ($command:expr) => {
        ImageUpload {
            bitmap_index: $command.bitmap_index,
            format: $command.format,
            r#type: $command.r#type,
            has_explicit_destination_size: $command.has_explicit_destination_size,
            destination_width: $command.destination_width,
            destination_height: $command.destination_height,
            flip_y: $command.flip_y,
            premultiply_alpha: $command.premultiply_alpha,
        }
    };
}

fn pixels_of<P: AsRef<[u8]>>(image: &ConvertedImage<P>) -> Result<(i32, *const c_void), ReplayError> {
    let bytes = image.pixels.as_ref().map_or(&[][..], AsRef::as_ref);
    let size = i32::try_from(bytes.len()).map_err(|_| ReplayError("WebGL image upload is too big"))?;
    Ok((size, bytes.as_ptr().cast()))
}

impl<H: WebGLHost> Replayer<'_, H> {
    pub(super) fn shader_source(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
        let command: commands::ShaderSource = decode(payload)?;
        let source = string_data(payload, command.source)?;
        let shader = self.objects.lookup(command.shader);
        let length =
            i32::try_from(command.source.size - 1).map_err(|_| ReplayError("WebGL shader source is too long"))?;
        // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and the source has the length.
        unsafe { (self.gl.shader_source)(shader, 1, &raw const source, &raw const length) };
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(super) fn transform_feedback_varyings(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
        let command: commands::TransformFeedbackVaryings = decode(payload)?;
        let varyings = split_packed_strings(data_span(payload, command.varyings)?, command.count)?;
        let program = self.objects.lookup(command.program);
        // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and every string is NUL-terminated.
        unsafe {
            (self.gl.transform_feedback_varyings)(program, command.count, varyings.as_ptr(), command.buffer_mode);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(super) fn set_drawing_buffer_size(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
        let command: commands::SetDrawingBufferSize = decode(payload)?;
        let dimensions = 1..=MAX_DRAWING_BUFFER_DIMENSION;
        if !dimensions.contains(&command.width) || !dimensions.contains(&command.height) {
            return Err(ReplayError("WebGL drawing buffer size is out of range"));
        }
        let size = IntSize {
            width: command.width,
            height: command.height,
        };
        self.host
            .set_webgl_drawing_buffer_size(self.client, self.canvas_id, size);
        self.defaults = self.host.make_webgl_context_current(self.client, self.canvas_id);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(super) fn read_pixels_into_pixel_pack_buffer(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
        let command: commands::ReadPixelsIntoPixelPackBuffer = decode(payload)?;
        // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and GL writes into the bound pixel pack buffer at the offset.
        unsafe {
            (self.gl.read_pixels_robust_angle)(
                command.x,
                command.y,
                command.width,
                command.height,
                command.format,
                command.r#type,
                0,
                core::ptr::null_mut(),
                core::ptr::null_mut(),
                core::ptr::null_mut(),
                command.offset as isize as *mut c_void,
            );
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn image_source_at(&self, bitmap_index: u32) -> Result<ImageSource, ReplayError> {
        self.image_sources
            .get(bitmap_index as usize)
            .copied()
            .ok_or(ReplayError("WebGL image upload references an out-of-range bitmap"))
    }

    /// None where the image could not be converted, which leaves the texture as it is.
    fn converted_image(&self, upload: &ImageUpload) -> Result<Option<ConvertedImage<H::Pixels>>, ReplayError> {
        let source = self.image_source_at(upload.bitmap_index)?;
        let export_format = texture_export_format(upload.format, upload.r#type).ok_or(ReplayError(
            "WebGL image upload has an unsupported format and type combination",
        ))?;
        let mut target_size = None;
        if upload.has_explicit_destination_size {
            if upload.destination_width < 0 || upload.destination_height < 0 {
                return Ok(Some(ConvertedImage {
                    pixels: None,
                    width: upload.destination_width,
                    height: upload.destination_height,
                }));
            }
            target_size = Some(IntSize {
                width: upload.destination_width,
                height: upload.destination_height,
            });
        }
        let conversion = ImageConversion {
            export_format,
            flip_y: upload.flip_y,
            premultiply_alpha: upload.premultiply_alpha,
            target_size,
        };
        match self.host.convert_image_source(self.client, source, conversion) {
            ImageConversionOutcome::Converted { pixels, width, height } => Ok(Some(ConvertedImage {
                pixels: Some(pixels),
                width,
                height,
            })),
            ImageConversionOutcome::UnknownImageFrame => Err(ReplayError(
                "WebGL image upload names an image frame that is not registered",
            )),
            ImageConversionOutcome::Failed => {
                eprintln!("Compositor: Could not convert an image for a WebGL texture upload");
                Ok(None)
            }
        }
    }

    fn supports_pixel_buffer_objects(&self) -> bool {
        self.webgl2 || extension_is_enabled(self.gl, b"GL_NV_pixel_buffer_object")
    }

    fn supports_unpack_subimage_parameters(&self) -> bool {
        self.webgl2 || extension_is_enabled(self.gl, b"GL_EXT_unpack_subimage")
    }

    fn with_pixel_unpack_buffer_unbound(&self, upload: impl FnOnce()) {
        let has_pixel_buffer_objects = self.supports_pixel_buffer_objects();
        let mut bound_buffer = 0;
        if has_pixel_buffer_objects {
            // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and the binding is room for one value.
            unsafe {
                (self.gl.get_integerv_robust_angle)(
                    GL_PIXEL_UNPACK_BUFFER_BINDING,
                    1,
                    core::ptr::null_mut(),
                    &raw mut bound_buffer,
                );
                (self.gl.bind_buffer)(GL_PIXEL_UNPACK_BUFFER, 0);
            }
        }
        upload();
        if has_pixel_buffer_objects {
            // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current.
            unsafe { (self.gl.bind_buffer)(GL_PIXEL_UNPACK_BUFFER, bound_buffer as u32) };
        }
    }

    /// The pixels of a converted image are tightly packed, row after row and image after image, so the unpack
    /// parameters that the page set for its own data are reset for the upload, and restored after it.
    fn with_packed_unpack_state(&self, upload: impl FnOnce()) {
        let mut saved_parameters = Vec::with_capacity(6);
        let mut reset = |parameter: u32, value: i32| {
            let mut saved_value = 0;
            // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and the saved value is room for one value.
            unsafe {
                (self.gl.get_integerv)(parameter, &raw mut saved_value);
                (self.gl.pixel_storei)(parameter, value);
            }
            saved_parameters.push((parameter, saved_value));
        };
        reset(GL_UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 1);
        if self.supports_unpack_subimage_parameters() {
            reset(GL_UNPACK_ROW_LENGTH, 0);
            reset(GL_UNPACK_SKIP_PIXELS, 0);
            reset(GL_UNPACK_SKIP_ROWS, 0);
        }
        if self.webgl2 {
            reset(GL_UNPACK_IMAGE_HEIGHT, 0);
            reset(GL_UNPACK_SKIP_IMAGES, 0);
        }
        upload();
        for (parameter, saved_value) in saved_parameters {
            // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current.
            unsafe { (self.gl.pixel_storei)(parameter, saved_value) };
        }
    }

    /// Defines the level of the texture with the call that an upload of pixels would make, so that WebGL sees the same
    /// errors, and copies the frame into it on the GPU. False where the frame has to be uploaded as pixels instead.
    fn define_texture_image_from_video_frame(
        &mut self,
        command: &commands::TexImage2DFromBitmap,
        frame: &H::VideoFrame,
        frame_size: IntSize,
    ) -> bool {
        if !self
            .host
            .webgl_can_copy_images_into_textures(self.client, self.canvas_id)
            || !copy_can_write_internal_format(command.internalformat)
        {
            return false;
        }
        let Some(size) = upload_size(
            frame_size,
            command.has_explicit_destination_size,
            command.destination_width,
            command.destination_height,
        ) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(image) = self.host.video_frame_image(frame) else {
            return false;
        };

        self.stash_errors();
        self.with_pixel_unpack_buffer_unbound(|| {
            // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and GL reads no pixels.
            unsafe {
                (self.gl.tex_image2d_robust_angle)(
                    command.target,
                    command.level,
                    command.internalformat,
                    size.width,
                    size.height,
                    0,
                    command.format,
                    command.r#type,
                    0,
                    core::ptr::null(),
                );
            }
        });
        if self.stash_errors() || size.is_empty() {
            return true;
        }
        let copy = VideoFrameCopy {
            source_size: frame_size,
            size,
            target: command.target,
            level: command.level,
            xoffset: 0,
            yoffset: 0,
            flip_y: command.flip_y,
            premultiply_alpha: command.premultiply_alpha,
        };
        if !self
            .host
            .copy_video_frame_image_into_bound_texture(self.client, self.canvas_id, &image, copy)
        {
            return false;
        }
        self.discard_errors();
        true
    }

    fn update_texture_image_from_video_frame(
        &mut self,
        command: &commands::TexSubImage2DFromBitmap,
        frame: &H::VideoFrame,
        frame_size: IntSize,
    ) -> bool {
        if !self
            .host
            .webgl_can_copy_images_into_textures(self.client, self.canvas_id)
            || format_is_integer(command.format)
        {
            return false;
        }
        let Some(size) = upload_size(
            frame_size,
            command.has_explicit_destination_size,
            command.destination_width,
            command.destination_height,
        ) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(image) = self.host.video_frame_image(frame) else {
            return false;
        };

        self.stash_errors();
        self.with_pixel_unpack_buffer_unbound(|| {
            // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and GL reads no pixels.
            unsafe {
                (self.gl.tex_sub_image2d_robust_angle)(
                    command.target,
                    command.level,
                    command.xoffset,
                    command.yoffset,
                    0,
                    0,
                    command.format,
                    command.r#type,
                    0,
                    core::ptr::null(),
                );
            }
        });
        if self.stash_errors() || size.is_empty() {
            return true;
        }
        let copy = VideoFrameCopy {
            source_size: frame_size,
            size,
            target: command.target,
            level: command.level,
            xoffset: command.xoffset,
            yoffset: command.yoffset,
            flip_y: command.flip_y,
            premultiply_alpha: command.premultiply_alpha,
        };
        if !self
            .host
            .copy_video_frame_image_into_bound_texture(self.client, self.canvas_id, &image, copy)
        {
            return false;
        }
        // NB: A region beyond the level is the caller's error, as it would be for an upload of pixels.
        self.stash_errors();
        true
    }

    fn held_video_frame_of(&self, source: ImageSource) -> Option<(H::VideoFrame, IntSize)> {
        let ImageSource::HeldVideoFrame {
            sink_handle,
            generation,
        } = source
        else {
            return None;
        };
        self.host.held_video_frame(self.client, sink_handle, generation)
    }

    pub(super) fn tex_image2d_from_bitmap(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
        let command: commands::TexImage2DFromBitmap = decode(payload)?;
        let source = self.image_source_at(command.bitmap_index)?;
        if let Some((frame, frame_size)) = self.held_video_frame_of(source)
            && self.define_texture_image_from_video_frame(&command, &frame, frame_size)
        {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let Some(image) = self.converted_image(&image_upload!(command))? else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        let (pixels_size, pixels) = pixels_of(&image)?;
        self.with_packed_unpack_state(|| {
            // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and the pixels have the size.
            unsafe {
                (self.gl.tex_image2d_robust_angle)(
                    command.target,
                    command.level,
                    command.internalformat,
                    image.width,
                    image.height,
                    0,
                    command.format,
                    command.r#type,
                    pixels_size,
                    pixels,
                );
            }
        });
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(super) fn tex_sub_image2d_from_bitmap(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
        let command: commands::TexSubImage2DFromBitmap = decode(payload)?;
        let source = self.image_source_at(command.bitmap_index)?;
        if let Some((frame, frame_size)) = self.held_video_frame_of(source)
            && self.update_texture_image_from_video_frame(&command, &frame, frame_size)
        {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let Some(image) = self.converted_image(&image_upload!(command))? else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        let (pixels_size, pixels) = pixels_of(&image)?;
        self.with_packed_unpack_state(|| {
            // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and the pixels have the size.
            unsafe {
                (self.gl.tex_sub_image2d_robust_angle)(
                    command.target,
                    command.level,
                    command.xoffset,
                    command.yoffset,
                    image.width,
                    image.height,
                    command.format,
                    command.r#type,
                    pixels_size,
                    pixels,
                );
            }
        });
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(super) fn tex_image3d_from_bitmap(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
        let command: commands::TexImage3DFromBitmap = decode(payload)?;
        let Some(image) = self.converted_image(&image_upload!(command))? else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        let (pixels_size, pixels) = pixels_of(&image)?;
        self.with_packed_unpack_state(|| {
            // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and the pixels have the size.
            unsafe {
                (self.gl.tex_image3d_robust_angle)(
                    command.target,
                    command.level,
                    command.internalformat,
                    image.width,
                    image.height,
                    command.depth,
                    0,
                    command.format,
                    command.r#type,
                    pixels_size,
                    pixels,
                );
            }
        });
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(super) fn tex_sub_image3d_from_bitmap(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
        let command: commands::TexSubImage3DFromBitmap = decode(payload)?;
        let Some(image) = self.converted_image(&image_upload!(command))? else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        let (pixels_size, pixels) = pixels_of(&image)?;
        self.with_packed_unpack_state(|| {
            // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and the pixels have the size.
            unsafe {
                (self.gl.tex_sub_image3d_robust_angle)(
                    command.target,
                    command.level,
                    command.xoffset,
                    command.yoffset,
                    command.zoffset,
                    image.width,
                    image.height,
                    command.depth,
                    command.format,
                    command.r#type,
                    pixels_size,
                    pixels,
                );
            }
        });
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(super) fn get_string(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ReplayError> {
        let request: sync_calls::GetStringRequest = decode(payload)?;
        // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and GL answers a string or null.
        let value = unsafe { (self.gl.get_string)(request.name) };
        let value: &[u8] = if value.is_null() {
            b"\0"
        } else {
            // SAFETY: GL answers a NUL-terminated string.
            unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(value.cast::<c_char>()) }.to_bytes_with_nul()
        };
        let [value_span] = reply_data_spans::<sync_calls::GetStringReply, 1>([value.len()]);
        let reply = sync_calls::GetStringReply { value: value_span };
        Ok(encode_reply(&reply, &[value]))
    }

    pub(super) fn get_vertex_attrib_pointerv_robust_angle(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ReplayError> {
        let request: sync_calls::GetVertexAttribPointervRobustANGLERequest = decode(payload)?;
        let mut pointer = core::ptr::null_mut();
        let mut length = 0;
        // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, and the pointer is room for one.
        unsafe {
            (self.gl.get_vertex_attrib_pointerv_robust_angle)(
                request.index,
                request.pname,
                1,
                &raw mut length,
                &raw mut pointer,
            );
        }
        let reply = sync_calls::GetVertexAttribPointervRobustANGLEReply {
            pointer: pointer as usize as i64,
        };
        Ok(encode_reply(&reply, &[]))
    }

    pub(super) fn get_uniform_indices(&mut self, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ReplayError> {
        let request: sync_calls::GetUniformIndicesRequest = decode(payload)?;
        let names = split_packed_strings(data_span(payload, request.uniform_names)?, request.uniform_count)?;
        let program = self.objects.lookup(request.program);
        let mut indices = vec![0_u32; names.len()];
        // SAFETY: The context of the replayer is current, every name is NUL-terminated, and there is room for an index
        //         of each.
        unsafe {
            (self.gl.get_uniform_indices)(program, request.uniform_count, names.as_ptr(), indices.as_mut_ptr());
        }
        let indices = bytes_of_slice(&indices);
        let [indices_span] = reply_data_spans::<sync_calls::GetUniformIndicesReply, 1>([indices.len()]);
        let reply = sync_calls::GetUniformIndicesReply {
            uniform_indices: indices_span,
        };
        Ok(encode_reply(&reply, &[indices]))
    }
}
