#include <AK/ScopeGuard.h>
#include <AK/Time.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibCore/System.h>
#include <LibGC/BlockAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapBlock.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapRegion.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>

TEST_CASE(all_blocks_share_one_reserved_region)
{
    GC::BlockAllocator first_allocator;
    GC::BlockAllocator second_allocator;

    auto* first_block = first_allocator.allocate_block("first");
    auto* second_block = second_allocator.allocate_block("second");

    auto region_start = GC::BlockAllocator::heap_region_start();
    auto region_end = GC::BlockAllocator::heap_region_end();
    EXPECT(region_start < region_end);
    EXPECT_EQ(region_start, js_heap_region_base);
    EXPECT_EQ(region_start % GC::HEAP_REGION_SIZE, 0u);

    auto first_address = reinterpret_cast<FlatPtr>(first_block);
    auto second_address = reinterpret_cast<FlatPtr>(second_block);
    EXPECT(first_address >= region_start);
    EXPECT(first_address + GC::HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE <= region_end);
    EXPECT(second_address >= region_start);
    EXPECT(second_address + GC::HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE <= region_end);

    first_allocator.deallocate_block(first_block, GC::DeferDecommit::No);
    second_allocator.deallocate_block(second_block, GC::DeferDecommit::No);
}

TEST_CASE(blocks_stay_out_of_the_region_guards)
{
    GC::BlockAllocator allocator;
    auto region_start = GC::BlockAllocator::heap_region_start();
    auto region_end = GC::BlockAllocator::heap_region_end();

    // Enough blocks to take several fresh chunks.
    static constexpr size_t BLOCK_COUNT = 1024;
    Vector<void*> blocks;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < BLOCK_COUNT; ++i)
        blocks.append(allocator.allocate_block("guards"));

    auto committed_end = GC::BlockAllocator::heap_region_committed_end();
    EXPECT(committed_end >= region_start + GC::HEAP_REGION_LOW_GUARD_SIZE + BLOCK_COUNT * GC::HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE);
    EXPECT(committed_end <= region_end - GC::HEAP_REGION_HIGH_GUARD_SIZE);

    for (auto* block : blocks) {
        auto address = reinterpret_cast<FlatPtr>(block);
        EXPECT(address >= region_start + GC::HEAP_REGION_LOW_GUARD_SIZE);
        EXPECT(address + GC::HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE <= committed_end);
    }

    for (auto* block : blocks)
        allocator.deallocate_block(block, GC::DeferDecommit::No);
}

TEST_CASE(decommitted_block_can_be_reused)
{
    GC::BlockAllocator allocator;

    auto* block = static_cast<u8*>(allocator.allocate_block("decommit"));
    for (size_t i = 0; i < GC::HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE; ++i)
        block[i] = 0xab;
    auto block_count_before_free = allocator.block_count();

    allocator.deallocate_block(block, GC::DeferDecommit::Yes);
    GC::BlockAllocator::wake_decommit_worker_async();

    // The decommit worker returns the block to the reusable pool once it has released the block's pages.
    auto deadline = MonotonicTime::now() + AK::Duration::from_seconds(10);
    while (allocator.block_count() == block_count_before_free && MonotonicTime::now() < deadline)
        (void)Core::System::sleep_ms(10);
    EXPECT_EQ(allocator.block_count(), block_count_before_free + 1);

    auto* reused_block = static_cast<u8*>(allocator.allocate_block("decommit"));
    EXPECT_EQ(reused_block, block);

    for (size_t i = 0; i < GC::HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE; ++i)
        reused_block[i] = static_cast<u8>(i);
    bool contents_match = true;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < GC::HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE; ++i) {
        if (reused_block[i] != static_cast<u8>(i))
            contents_match = false;
    }
    EXPECT(contents_match);

    allocator.deallocate_block(reused_block, GC::DeferDecommit::No);
}

#if defined(AK_OS_LINUX) && !defined(HAS_ADDRESS_SANITIZER)
TEST_CASE(pages_of_a_block_that_stays_unused_go_back_to_the_system)
{
    auto cold_block_age = GC::BlockAllocator::set_cold_block_age_for_testing(AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(10));
    ScopeGuard restore_cold_block_age = [&] { GC::BlockAllocator::set_cold_block_age_for_testing(cold_block_age); };

    GC::BlockAllocator allocator;

    auto* block = static_cast<u8 volatile*>(allocator.allocate_block("cold"));
    block[0] = 0xab;
    allocator.deallocate_block(const_cast<u8*>(block), GC::DeferDecommit::Yes);
    GC::BlockAllocator::wake_decommit_worker_async();

    // NB: MADV_FREE leaves the contents until the system runs short of memory, so only a real return zeroes the page.
    //     Nothing has to collect garbage for this to happen.
    // The worker zeroes the pages before it puts the block back in the pool, so wait until the block is back: An
    // allocation before then would get a fresh slot.
    auto deadline = MonotonicTime::now() + AK::Duration::from_seconds(30);
    while (allocator.returned_block_count_for_testing() == 0 && MonotonicTime::now() < deadline)
        (void)Core::System::sleep_ms(1);
    EXPECT_EQ(allocator.returned_block_count_for_testing(), 1u);
    u8 first_byte = block[0];
    EXPECT_EQ(first_byte, 0);

    auto* reused_block = allocator.allocate_block("cold");
    EXPECT_EQ(reused_block, const_cast<u8*>(block));
    allocator.deallocate_block(reused_block, GC::DeferDecommit::No);
}
#endif

FILE: Tests/LibGC/TestCompressedPointer.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <AK/NeverDestroyed.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/CellAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/CompressedPointer.h>
#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibGC/Testing.h>
#include <LibGC/Weak.h>
#include <LibGC/WeakInlines.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>

namespace {

class TestCell final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(TestCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(TestCell);

    u8 m_padding[32] {};
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(TestCell);

static GC::Heap& test_heap()
{
    static AK::NeverDestroyed<GC::Heap> heap([](auto&) { });
    return *heap;
}

TEST_SETUP
{
    GC::Heap::set_default_heap_for_testing(test_heap());
}

TEST_CASE(compressed_pointer_round_trips)
{
    auto cell = test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();
    auto compressed = GC::compress(cell.ptr());

    EXPECT(compressed >= GC::MIN_COMPRESSED_CELL_POINTER);
    EXPECT_EQ(GC::decompress(compressed), reinterpret_cast<FlatPtr>(cell.ptr()));
    EXPECT_EQ(GC::decompress_nonnull(compressed), reinterpret_cast<FlatPtr>(cell.ptr()));
}

TEST_CASE(null_compresses_to_zero)
{
    EXPECT_EQ(GC::compress(nullptr), 0u);
    EXPECT_EQ(GC::decompress(0), 0u);
}

TEST_CASE(every_compressed_pointer_decodes_inside_the_heap_region)
{
    auto start = js_heap_region_base;
    for (u32 compressed : { 1u, GC::MIN_COMPRESSED_CELL_POINTER, 0x8000'0000u, 0xffff'ffffu }) {
        auto address = GC::decompress_nonnull(compressed);
        EXPECT(address >= start);
        EXPECT(address + sizeof(FlatPtr) <= start + GC::HEAP_REGION_SIZE);
    }
}

using MakeWord = u64 (*)(u32 compressed);

// Allocates a cell that nothing refers to but the word made from its compressed pointer.
static NEVER_INLINE void allocate_cell_into_word(GC::Weak<TestCell>& weak_cell, u64 volatile& word, MakeWord make_word)
{
    auto cell = test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();
    weak_cell = cell.ptr();
    word = make_word(GC::compress(cell.ptr()));
}

// Keeps a cell alive through the given word only, then drops the word and collects again.
static void expect_word_keeps_cell_alive(MakeWord make_word)
{
    auto& heap = test_heap();
    GC::Weak<TestCell> weak_cell;
    u64 volatile word = 0;
    allocate_cell_into_word(weak_cell, word, make_word);

    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT(weak_cell);

    word = 0;
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage(GC::Heap::CollectionType::CollectEverything);
    EXPECT(!weak_cell);
}

TEST_CASE(conservative_scanner_finds_compressed_pointer_in_low_half)
{
    expect_word_keeps_cell_alive([](u32 compressed) -> u64 { return 0xdead'beef'0000'0000ULL | compressed; });
}

TEST_CASE(conservative_scanner_finds_compressed_pointer_in_high_half)
{
    expect_word_keeps_cell_alive([](u32 compressed) -> u64 { return (static_cast<u64>(compressed) << 32) | 0x1234; });
}

TEST_CASE(conservative_scanner_ignores_compressed_pointer_into_a_cell)
{
    auto& heap = test_heap();
    GC::Weak<TestCell> weak_cell;
    u64 volatile word = 0;
    // One unit past the cell's start points into the cell, which no compressed pointer does.
    allocate_cell_into_word(weak_cell, word, [](u32 compressed) -> u64 { return compressed + 1; });

    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT(!weak_cell);
    EXPECT(word != 0);
}

}

#include <AK/Array.h>
#include <LibGC/ExternalEntityTable.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>

class TestExternalEntityTable final : private GC::ExternalEntityTable {
public:
    using ExternalEntityTable::allocate_entry;
    using ExternalEntityTable::free_entry;
    using ExternalEntityTable::is_valid;
};

TEST_CASE(balanced_tags_are_unique_and_have_equal_hamming_weight)
{
    constexpr size_t tag_count_to_test = 256;
    Array<GC::ExternalEntityTableTag, tag_count_to_test> tags;

    for (u16 ordinal = 0; ordinal < tags.size(); ++ordinal) {
        auto tag = GC::balanced_external_entity_table_tag(ordinal);
        EXPECT(tag.is_balanced());
        EXPECT_EQ(popcount(tag.value), GC::ExternalEntityTableTag::set_bit_count);
        for (u16 previous = 0; previous < ordinal; ++previous)
            EXPECT(tag != tags[previous]);
        tags[ordinal] = tag;
    }
}

TEST_CASE(entries_validate_their_type_and_generation)
{
    TestExternalEntityTable table;
    constexpr auto first_tag = GC::balanced_external_entity_table_tag(0);
    constexpr auto second_tag = GC::balanced_external_entity_table_tag(1);

    auto first_handle = table.allocate_entry(first_tag);
    EXPECT(table.is_valid(first_handle, first_tag));
    EXPECT(!table.is_valid(first_handle, second_tag));

    table.free_entry(first_handle, second_tag);
    EXPECT(table.is_valid(first_handle, first_tag));

    table.free_entry(first_handle, first_tag);
    EXPECT(!table.is_valid(first_handle, first_tag));

    auto second_handle = table.allocate_entry(second_tag);
    EXPECT_EQ(second_handle.index, first_handle.index);
    EXPECT_NE(second_handle.generation, first_handle.generation);
    EXPECT(table.is_valid(second_handle, second_tag));
    EXPECT(!table.is_valid(second_handle, first_tag));
}

class TestCell : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(TestCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(TestCell);

    // Padding to satisfy minimum cell size (must be >= sizeof(FreelistEntry)).
    u8 m_padding[16] {};
};

class FinalizerObservingCell : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(FinalizerObservingCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(FinalizerObservingCell);

public:
    GC::Weak<TestCell> weak_cell;
    bool* weak_cell_was_null_while_finalizing { nullptr };
    bool* weak_to_self_was_null_while_finalizing { nullptr };

private:
    virtual void finalize() override
    {
        Base::finalize();
        *weak_cell_was_null_while_finalizing = !weak_cell;
        *weak_to_self_was_null_while_finalizing = !GC::Weak<FinalizerObservingCell> { *this };
    }
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(FinalizerObservingCell);

static GC::Heap& test_heap()
{
    static AK::NeverDestroyed<GC::Heap> heap([](auto&) { });
    return *heap;
}

{
    GC::Heap::set_default_heap_for_testing(test_heap());
}

class TestVisitor : public GC::Cell::Visitor {
    virtual void visit_impl(GC::Cell& cell) override { visited_cells.set(&cell); }
    virtual void visit_impl(ReadonlySpan<GC::NanBoxedValue>) override { }

public:
    HashTable<GC::Cell*> visited_cells;
};

TEST_CASE(root_vector_native_member_survives_relocation)
{
    auto& heap = test_heap();
    struct NativeState {
        GC::RootVector<GC::Ref<TestCell>> cells;
    };
    Vector<NativeState> states;
    states.append(NativeState {});
    auto cell = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    states[0].cells.append(cell);

    // Moving the enclosing native storage must transfer the member's registration in the heap's root list.
    states.ensure_capacity(states.capacity() + 1);
    heap.collect_garbage();

    HashMap<GC::Cell*, GC::HeapRoot> roots;
    states[0].cells.gather_roots(roots);
    EXPECT(roots.contains(cell.ptr()));
    EXPECT_EQ(roots.size(), 1u);

    // Destruction must unregister the member before the collector next walks its root list.
    states.clear();
    heap.collect_garbage();
}

struct TracedRecord {
    GC::Ref<TestCell> cell;
    GC::Ptr<TestCell> other_cell;
    int payload { 0 };

    void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor)
    {
        visitor.visit(cell);
        visitor.visit(other_cell);
    }
};

struct PlainRecord {
    int payload { 0 };
};

static_assert(GC::Detail::IsRootableValue<GC::Ref<TestCell>>);
static_assert(GC::Detail::IsRootableValue<TracedRecord>);
static_assert(GC::Detail::IsRootableValue<Variant<GC::Ref<TestCell>, Empty>>);
static_assert(GC::Detail::IsRootableValue<Optional<TracedRecord>>);
static_assert(GC::Detail::IsRootableValue<Array<GC::Ref<TestCell>, 2>>);
static_assert(!GC::Detail::IsRootableValue<int>);
static_assert(!GC::Detail::IsRootableValue<PlainRecord>);

TEST_CASE(root_vector_of_traced_values_reports_their_cells)
{
    auto& heap = test_heap();
    GC::RootVector<TracedRecord> vector;

    auto cell = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    auto other_cell = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    vector.append({ cell, other_cell, 1 });
    vector.append({ cell, nullptr, 2 });

    HashMap<GC::Cell*, GC::HeapRoot> roots;
    vector.gather_roots(roots);

    EXPECT(roots.contains(cell.ptr()));
    EXPECT(roots.contains(other_cell.ptr()));
    EXPECT_EQ(roots.size(), 2u);
    EXPECT_EQ(roots.get(cell.ptr())->type, GC::HeapRoot::Type::RootVector);
}

template<typename Container, typename AddCell, typename Transfer>
static void expect_transferred_container_keeps_cell_alive(AddCell add_cell, Transfer transfer)
{
    auto& heap = test_heap();
    GC::Weak<TestCell> weak_cell;
    Optional<Container> destination;

    {
        Container source;
        auto cell = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
        weak_cell = cell.ptr();
        add_cell(source, cell);
        transfer(destination, source);
    }

    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT(weak_cell);
}

    auto cell = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    table.set(cell);
    GC::RootHashTable<GC::Ref<TestCell>> root_table { move(table) };

    HashMap<GC::Cell*, GC::HeapRoot> roots;
    root_table.gather_roots(roots);

    EXPECT(roots.contains(cell.ptr()));
    EXPECT_EQ(roots.size(), 1u);
}

TEST_CASE(copied_and_moved_root_hash_maps_keep_cells_alive)
{
    using Map = GC::RootHashMap<int, GC::Ref<TestCell>>;
    auto add_cell = [](Map& map, GC::Ref<TestCell> cell) { map.set(42, cell); };
    expect_transferred_container_keeps_cell_alive<Map>(add_cell, [](Optional<Map>& destination, Map& source) { destination = source; });
    expect_transferred_container_keeps_cell_alive<Map>(add_cell, [](Optional<Map>& destination, Map& source) { destination = move(source); });
    expect_transferred_container_keeps_cell_alive<Map>(add_cell, [](Optional<Map>& destination, Map& source) {
        destination.emplace();
        *destination = source;
    });
    expect_transferred_container_keeps_cell_alive<Map>(add_cell, [](Optional<Map>& destination, Map& source) {
        destination.emplace();
        *destination = move(source);
    });
}

TEST_CASE(copied_and_moved_root_hash_tables_keep_cells_alive)
{
    using Table = GC::RootHashTable<GC::Ref<TestCell>>;
    auto add_cell = [](Table& table, GC::Ref<TestCell> cell) { table.set(cell); };
    expect_transferred_container_keeps_cell_alive<Table>(add_cell, [](Optional<Table>& destination, Table& source) { destination = source; });
    expect_transferred_container_keeps_cell_alive<Table>(add_cell, [](Optional<Table>& destination, Table& source) { destination = move(source); });
    expect_transferred_container_keeps_cell_alive<Table>(add_cell, [](Optional<Table>& destination, Table& source) {
        destination.emplace();
        *destination = source;
    });
    expect_transferred_container_keeps_cell_alive<Table>(add_cell, [](Optional<Table>& destination, Table& source) {
        destination.emplace();
        *destination = move(source);
    });
}

{
    auto& heap = test_heap();
    GC::WeakHashMap<int, TestCell> map;

    auto cell = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    map.set(1, *cell);

    bool called = false;

        called = true;
        return heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    });

    EXPECT(!called);
    EXPECT_EQ(&value, cell.ptr());

TEST_CASE(weak_hash_map_ensure_replaces_collected_cell_value)
{
    auto& heap = test_heap();
    GC::WeakHashMap<int, TestCell> map;

    {
        auto cell = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
        map.set(1, *cell);
    }

    heap.collect_garbage(GC::Heap::CollectionType::CollectEverything);
    EXPECT_EQ(map.get(1), static_cast<TestCell*>(nullptr));

    auto replacement = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    bool called = false;
    auto& value = map.ensure(1, [&] {
        called = true;
        return replacement;
    });

    EXPECT(called);
    EXPECT_EQ(&value, replacement.ptr());
    EXPECT_EQ(map.get(1), replacement.ptr());
}

TEST_CASE(weak_hash_map_ensure_handles_non_cell_value)
{
    auto& heap = test_heap();
    GC::WeakHashMap<TestCell, int> map;

    auto key = heap.allocate<TestCell>();

    bool called = false;
    auto& value = map.ensure(*key, [&] {
        called = true;
        return 7;
    });

    EXPECT(called);
    EXPECT_EQ(value, 7);

    value = 9;
    called = false;
    auto& existing_value = map.ensure(*key, [&] {
        called = true;
        return 11;
    });

    EXPECT(!called);
    EXPECT_EQ(existing_value, 9);

    auto default_key = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    auto& default_value = map.ensure(*default_key);
    EXPECT_EQ(default_value, 0);

    default_value = 13;
    EXPECT_EQ(map.get(*default_key).value(), 13);
}

TEST_CASE(weak_pointers_to_dead_cells_are_null_while_finalizing)
{
    auto& heap = test_heap();
    bool weak_cell_was_null_while_finalizing = false;
    bool weak_to_self_was_null_while_finalizing = false;

    {
        auto cell = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
        auto observer = heap.allocate<FinalizerObservingCell>();
        observer->weak_cell = cell.ptr();
        observer->weak_cell_was_null_while_finalizing = &weak_cell_was_null_while_finalizing;
        observer->weak_to_self_was_null_while_finalizing = &weak_to_self_was_null_while_finalizing;
    }

    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage(GC::Heap::CollectionType::CollectEverything);
    EXPECT(weak_cell_was_null_while_finalizing);
    EXPECT(weak_to_self_was_null_while_finalizing);
}

FILE: Tests/LibGC/TestGCEphemeron.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/CellAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibGC/NanBoxedValue.h>
#include <LibGC/Ptr.h>
#include <LibGC/Root.h>
#include <LibGC/Testing.h>
#include <LibGC/WeakContainer.h>
#include <LibGC/WeakInlines.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>

namespace {

class TestNanBox : public GC::NanBoxedValue {
public:
    static TestNanBox from_cell(GC::Cell& cell)
    {
        TestNanBox box;
        box.m_value.encoded = GC::SHIFTED_IS_CELL_PATTERN | GC::NanBoxedValue::encode_pointer_bits(&cell);
        return box;
    }

    static TestNanBox from_double(double value)
    {
        TestNanBox box;
        box.m_value.as_double = value;
        return box;
    }

    double as_double() const { return m_value.as_double; }
};

class TestCell final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(TestCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(TestCell);

public:
    GC::Ptr<GC::Cell> edge;

private:
    TestCell() = default;

    virtual void visit_edges(Visitor& visitor) override
    {
        Base::visit_edges(visitor);
        visitor.visit(edge);
    }
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(TestCell);

// Holds its values as ephemerons of their keys, and drops the entries whose key died, as WeakMap does.
class EphemeronTable final
    : public GC::Cell
    , public GC::WeakContainer {
    GC_CELL(EphemeronTable, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(EphemeronTable);

public:
    struct Entry {
        GC::RawPtr<GC::Cell> key;
        TestNanBox value;
    };

    void add(GC::Cell& key, TestNanBox value) { entries.append({ &key, value }); }

    Vector<Entry> entries;

private:
    EphemeronTable()
        : GC::WeakContainer(heap())
    {
    }

    virtual void visit_edges(Visitor& visitor) override
    {
        Base::visit_edges(visitor);
        for (auto& entry : entries)
            visitor.visit_ephemeron(*entry.key, entry.value);
    }

    virtual GC::Cell const& owner_cell(Badge<GC::Heap>) const override { return *this; }

    virtual void remove_dead_cells(Badge<GC::Heap>) override
    {
        entries.remove_all_matching([](auto const& entry) { return !entry.key->is_marked(); });
    }
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(EphemeronTable);

struct Weaks {
    GC::Weak<TestCell> key;
    GC::Weak<TestCell> value;
};

NEVER_INLINE Weaks add_value_referring_to_its_key(GC::Heap& heap, EphemeronTable& table)
{
    auto key = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    auto value = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    value->edge = key.ptr();
    table.add(*key, TestNanBox::from_cell(*value));
    return { key.ptr(), value.ptr() };
}

// The entry of the second key comes first, so marking visits it before the entry of the first key marks the second.
NEVER_INLINE Weaks add_chain_from(GC::Heap& heap, EphemeronTable& table, TestCell& first_key)
{
    auto second_key = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    auto value = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    table.add(*second_key, TestNanBox::from_cell(*value));
    table.add(first_key, TestNanBox::from_cell(*second_key));
    return { second_key.ptr(), value.ptr() };
}

NEVER_INLINE GC::Weak<TestCell> add_value_of_foreign_key(GC::Heap& heap, GC::Heap& foreign_heap, EphemeronTable& table)
{
    auto key = foreign_heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    auto value = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    table.add(*key, TestNanBox::from_cell(*value));
    return value.ptr();
}

NEVER_INLINE void add_double_of_dead_key(GC::Heap& heap, EphemeronTable& table)
{
    table.add(*heap.allocate<TestCell>(), TestNanBox::from_double(2.5));
}

}

static NEVER_INLINE void value_referring_to_its_key_dies_with_it()
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    auto table = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<EphemeronTable>());

    auto weaks = add_value_referring_to_its_key(heap, *table);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage();

    EXPECT(!weaks.key);
    EXPECT(!weaks.value);
    EXPECT(table->entries.is_empty());
}

static NEVER_INLINE void value_survives_when_its_key_is_marked_later()
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    auto table = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<EphemeronTable>());
    auto first_key = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<TestCell>());

    auto weaks = add_chain_from(heap, *table, *first_key);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage();

    EXPECT(weaks.key);
    EXPECT(weaks.value);
    EXPECT_EQ(table->entries.size(), 2u);
}

static NEVER_INLINE void value_of_key_outside_domain_survives_local_collection()
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    GC::Heap foreign_heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    foreign_heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    auto table = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<EphemeronTable>());

    auto value = add_value_of_foreign_key(heap, foreign_heap, *table);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage();

    // NB: A collection of this heap alone never marks the key, so the table drops its entry.
    EXPECT(value);
    EXPECT(table->entries.is_empty());
}

static NEVER_INLINE void non_cell_value_is_ignored()
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    auto table = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<EphemeronTable>());
    auto key = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<TestCell>());
    table->add(*key, TestNanBox::from_double(1.5));

    add_double_of_dead_key(heap, *table);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage();

    EXPECT_EQ(table->entries.size(), 1u);
    EXPECT_EQ(table->entries[0].value.as_double(), 1.5);
}

// Under ASan with detect_stack_use_after_return, a function's locals live on a fake stack, but its frame on the real
// stack still reserves room for them — room it never writes, so it keeps whatever earlier calls left there, and the
// conservative scan reads it. A stale pointer there can keep a dropped cell alive. So each case runs in a frame of its
// own, on stack that scrub_stack_for_testing() has just cleared.
TEST_CASE(value_referring_to_its_key_dies_with_it)
{
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    value_referring_to_its_key_dies_with_it();
}

TEST_CASE(value_survives_when_its_key_is_marked_later)
{
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    value_survives_when_its_key_is_marked_later();
}

TEST_CASE(value_of_key_outside_domain_survives_local_collection)
{
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    value_of_key_outside_domain_survives_local_collection();
}

TEST_CASE(non_cell_value_is_ignored)
{
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    non_cell_value_is_ignored();
}

#include <AK/OwnPtr.h>
#include <AK/RefCounted.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/CellAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/CompressedPointer.h>

#include <LibGC/Root.h>
#include <LibGC/Testing.h>
#include <LibGC/WeakInlines.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>

namespace {

class TestCell final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(TestCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(TestCell);

public:
    i64 value { 0 };

private:
    TestCell() = default;
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(TestCell);

class CellWithFunction final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(CellWithFunction, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(CellWithFunction);

public:
    GC::Ptr<GC::Function<void()>> function;

private:
    CellWithFunction() = default;

    virtual void visit_edges(Visitor& visitor) override
    {
        Base::visit_edges(visitor);
        visitor.visit(function);
    }
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(CellWithFunction);

class CellCallingFunctionWhenFinalized final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(CellCallingFunctionWhenFinalized, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(CellCallingFunctionWhenFinalized);

public:
    GC::Ptr<GC::Function<void()>> function;

private:
    CellCallingFunctionWhenFinalized() = default;

    virtual void visit_edges(Visitor& visitor) override
    {
        Base::visit_edges(visitor);
        visitor.visit(function);
    }

    virtual void finalize() override
    {
        Base::finalize();
        function->function()();
    }
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(CellCallingFunctionWhenFinalized);

struct DestructionFlag {
    GC_HOLDS_NO_CELL_EDGES;

    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    explicit DestructionFlag(bool& destroyed)
        : destroyed(destroyed)
    {
    }
    ~DestructionFlag() { destroyed = true; }

    bool& destroyed;
};

struct RunState : RefCounted<RunState> {
    GC_HOLDS_NO_CELL_EDGES;

    GC::Weak<GC::Function<void()>> function;
    bool survived_collection { false };
};

struct CalledFlag : RefCounted<CalledFlag> {
    GC_HOLDS_NO_CELL_EDGES;

    explicit CalledFlag(bool& called)
        : called(called)
    {
    }

    bool& called;
};

struct CountedWithCell : RefCounted<CountedWithCell> {
    GC::Ptr<TestCell> cell;
};

struct CountedWithoutCells : RefCounted<CountedWithoutCells> {
    GC_HOLDS_NO_CELL_EDGES;
};

struct CountedAndTraced : RefCounted<CountedAndTraced> {
    GC::Ptr<TestCell> cell;

    void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor) { visitor.visit(cell); }
};

// Nothing can reach a capture without saying how it is traced, also not through a counted or owning pointer.
static_assert(!GC::IsCapturable<CountedWithCell>);
static_assert(!GC::IsCapturable<NonnullRefPtr<CountedWithCell>>);
static_assert(!GC::IsCapturable<RefPtr<CountedWithCell>>);
static_assert(!GC::IsCapturable<OwnPtr<CountedWithCell>>);
static_assert(!GC::IsCapturable<NonnullOwnPtr<CountedWithCell>>);
static_assert(!GC::IsCapturable<Vector<NonnullRefPtr<CountedWithCell>>>);
static_assert(!GC::IsCapturable<AK::Function<void()>>);
static_assert(!GC::IsCapturable<int*>);
static_assert(GC::IsCapturable<NonnullRefPtr<CountedWithoutCells>>);
static_assert(GC::IsCapturable<NonnullRefPtr<CountedWithoutCells const>>);
static_assert(GC::IsCapturable<OwnPtr<CountedWithoutCells>>);
static_assert(GC::IsCapturable<NonnullRefPtr<CountedAndTraced>>);
static_assert(GC::IsCapturable<Optional<RefPtr<CountedAndTraced>>>);

// A root is only capturable on its own, which holds it as a pointer, so that a function never keeps a root.
static_assert(!GC::IsCapturable<GC::Root<TestCell>>);
static_assert(!GC::IsCapturable<Optional<GC::Root<TestCell>>>);
static_assert(!GC::IsCapturable<Vector<GC::Root<TestCell>>>);
static_assert(IsSame<GC::Detail::CaptureStorage<GC::Root<TestCell>&>::Type, GC::Detail::CapturedRoot<TestCell>>);

struct Holders {
    GC::Root<GC::Function<int()>> function;
    GC::Weak<TestCell> cell;
};

NEVER_INLINE Holders make_function_capturing_cell(GC::Heap& heap)
{
    auto cell = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    cell->value = 42;
    auto function = GC::create_function(heap, GC::captures(*cell), [](TestCell& cell) { return static_cast<int>(cell.value); });
    return { GC::make_root(function), cell.ptr() };
}

NEVER_INLINE Holders make_function_capturing_cell_address_as_integers(GC::Heap& heap)
{
    auto cell = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
    auto address = bit_cast<FlatPtr>(cell.ptr());
    auto compressed = GC::compress(cell.ptr());
    auto function = GC::create_function(heap, GC::captures(address, compressed), [](FlatPtr address, u32 compressed) {
        return static_cast<int>(address != 0) + static_cast<int>(compressed != 0);
    });
    return { GC::make_root(function), cell.ptr() };
}

NEVER_INLINE GC::Weak<CellWithFunction> make_cycle_through_captured_root(GC::Heap& heap)
{
    auto cell = heap.allocate<CellWithFunction>();
    auto root = GC::make_root(cell);
    cell->function = GC::create_function(heap, GC::captures(root), [](GC::Ptr<CellWithFunction>&) { });
    return cell.ptr();
}

NEVER_INLINE GC::Weak<GC::Function<void()>> make_unrooted_function_owning(GC::Heap& heap, bool& destroyed)
{
    auto function = GC::create_function(heap, GC::captures(make<DestructionFlag>(destroyed)), [](NonnullOwnPtr<DestructionFlag>&) { });
    return function.ptr();
}

NEVER_INLINE void make_unrooted_cell_calling_function_when_finalized(GC::Heap& heap, bool& called)
{
    // NB: Finalizers run in no particular order. The function is made first, which here finalizes it first.
    auto function = GC::create_function(heap, GC::captures(make_ref_counted<CalledFlag>(called)), [](NonnullRefPtr<CalledFlag>& flag) {
        flag->called = true;
    });
    heap.allocate<CellCallingFunctionWhenFinalized>()->function = function;
}

}

TEST_CASE(captured_cell_is_traced)
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);

    auto holders = make_function_capturing_cell(heap);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage();

    EXPECT(holders.cell);
    EXPECT_EQ(holders.function->function()(), 42);
}

TEST_CASE(captured_integers_are_not_cell_pointers)
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);

    auto holders = make_function_capturing_cell_address_as_integers(heap);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage();

    EXPECT(!holders.cell);
    EXPECT_EQ(holders.function->function()(), 2);
}

TEST_CASE(captures_take_arguments_after_them_and_keep_state)
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);

    auto function = GC::create_function(heap, GC::captures(0), [](int& calls, int argument) {
        ++calls;
        return calls * 100 + argument;
    });

    EXPECT_EQ(function->function()(1), 101);
    EXPECT_EQ(function->function()(2), 202);
}

    auto function = GC::create_function(heap, [](int argument) { return argument * 2; });
    EXPECT_EQ(function->function()(21), 42);
}

}

TEST_CASE(captures_taken_as_auto_with_a_named_function_type)

    });

TEST_CASE(captures_taken_as_auto_with_a_deduced_function_type)

    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    auto cell = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<TestCell>());
    cell->value = 5;

    auto function = GC::create_function(heap, GC::captures(*cell, 10), [](auto& cell, auto& offset, int argument) {
        return static_cast<int>(cell.value) + offset + argument;
    });
    static_assert(IsSame<decltype(function), GC::Ref<GC::Function<int(int)>>>);
    EXPECT_EQ(function->function()(1), 16);

    heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);

    auto cell = make_cycle_through_captured_root(heap);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();

    EXPECT(!cell);

TEST_CASE(captured_root_vector_is_traced_as_a_vector)
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::Yes);
    heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);

    GC::RootVector<GC::Ref<TestCell>> cells;
    cells.append(heap.allocate<TestCell>());
    cells[0]->value = 3;
    auto function = GC::make_root(GC::create_function(heap, GC::captures(move(cells)), [](Vector<GC::Ref<TestCell>>& cells) {
        return static_cast<int>(cells[0]->value);
    }));
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage();

    EXPECT_EQ(function->function()(), 3);
}

TEST_CASE(function_with_captures_stays_alive_while_it_runs)
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);

    auto state = adopt_ref(*new RunState);
    auto holder = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<CellWithFunction>());
    holder->function = GC::create_function(heap, GC::captures(*holder, state), [](CellWithFunction& holder, NonnullRefPtr<RunState>& state) {
        holder.function = nullptr;
        holder.heap().collect_garbage();
        state->survived_collection = static_cast<bool>(state->function);
    });
    state->function = holder->function;

    holder->function->function()();
    EXPECT(state->survived_collection);
}

TEST_CASE(captures_too_large_for_their_entry_keep_their_address_as_the_table_grows)
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::Yes);

    Array<u64, 8> values { 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 };
    auto function = GC::make_root(GC::create_function(heap, GC::captures(values, 0), [](Array<u64, 8>& values, int& padding) {
        auto const* before = values.data();
        for (size_t i = 0; i < 1000; ++i)
            (void)GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), [] { });
        VERIFY(values.data() == before);
        u64 sum = 0;
        for (auto value : values)
            sum += value;
        return static_cast<int>(sum) + padding;
    }));
    EXPECT_EQ(function->function()(), 36);
}

FILE: Tests/LibGC/TestGCHeapGroup.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026, Ali Mohammad Pur <ali@ladybird.org>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/CellAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/CrossHeapMember.h>
#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapGroup.h>
#include <LibGC/Ptr.h>
#include <LibGC/Root.h>
#include <LibGC/Testing.h>
#include <LibGC/WeakInlines.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>

namespace {

size_t s_live_linked_cells = 0;

class LinkedCell final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(LinkedCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(LinkedCell);

public:
    virtual ~LinkedCell() override { --s_live_linked_cells; }

    GC::CrossHeapMember<LinkedCell>& foreign() { return m_foreign; }
    GC::Ptr<LinkedCell>& local() { return m_local; }

private:
    LinkedCell() { ++s_live_linked_cells; }

    virtual void visit_edges(Visitor& visitor) override
    {
        Base::visit_edges(visitor);
        visitor.visit(m_local);
        m_foreign.visit(visitor);
    }

    GC::CrossHeapMember<LinkedCell> m_foreign;
    GC::Ptr<LinkedCell> m_local;
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(LinkedCell);

Optional<bool> s_weak_to_dead_foreign_cell_was_null_while_finalizing;

class WeakCreatingCell final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(WeakCreatingCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(WeakCreatingCell);

public:
    // Not visited, so that the foreign cell dies whether or not we do.
    GC::RawPtr<LinkedCell> foreign_cell;

private:
    WeakCreatingCell() = default;

    virtual void finalize() override
    {
        Base::finalize();
        s_weak_to_dead_foreign_cell_was_null_while_finalizing = !GC::Weak<LinkedCell> { foreign_cell.ptr() };
    }
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(WeakCreatingCell);

NEVER_INLINE GC::Root<LinkedCell> allocate_holder_and_foreign_target(GC::Heap& holder_heap, GC::Heap& target_heap)
{
    auto holder = GC::make_root(holder_heap.allocate<LinkedCell>());
    auto target = target_heap.allocate<LinkedCell>();
    holder->foreign() = target.ptr();
    return holder;
}

NEVER_INLINE void allocate_cross_heap_cycle(GC::Heap& heap_a, GC::Heap& heap_b)
{
    auto cell_on_a = heap_a.allocate<LinkedCell>();
    auto cell_on_b = heap_b.allocate<LinkedCell>();
    cell_on_a->foreign() = cell_on_b.ptr();
    cell_on_b->foreign() = cell_on_a.ptr();
}

NEVER_INLINE GC::Root<LinkedCell> allocate_cross_heap_chain(GC::Heap& heap_a, GC::Heap& heap_b)
{
    // root -> A -> B -> A(second)
    auto holder = GC::make_root(heap_a.allocate<LinkedCell>());
    auto middle = heap_b.allocate<LinkedCell>();
    auto tail = heap_a.allocate<LinkedCell>();
    middle->foreign() = tail.ptr();
    holder->foreign() = middle.ptr();
    return holder;
}

NEVER_INLINE void allocate_weak_creating_cell_and_foreign_garbage(GC::Heap& heap_a, GC::Heap& heap_b)
{
    auto cell = heap_a.allocate<WeakCreatingCell>();
    cell->foreign_cell = heap_b.allocate<LinkedCell>().ptr();
}

NEVER_INLINE void allocate_garbage(GC::Heap& heap)
{
    (void)heap.allocate<LinkedCell>();
}

}

static NEVER_INLINE void sanity_single_heap_frees_garbage()
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);

    allocate_garbage(heap);
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 1u);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 0u);
}

static NEVER_INLINE void incoming_cross_heap_member_roots_local_collection()
{
    GC::Heap heap_a([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    GC::Heap heap_b([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    // No event loop runs during this test; sweep synchronously so frees are observable.
    heap_a.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    heap_b.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    GC::HeapGroup group;
    group.add(heap_a);
    group.add(heap_b);

    auto holder = allocate_holder_and_foreign_target(heap_a, heap_b);
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 2u);

    // The only thing keeping the target alive is the incoming cross-heap member; B's local collection cannot see the holder on A, so the member registration must root it.
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap_b.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 2u);

    // Once the edge is dropped, B's next local collection should free the target.
    holder->foreign() = nullptr;
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap_b.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 1u);

    holder = {};
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap_a.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 0u);

    group.remove(heap_a);
    group.remove(heap_b);
}

static NEVER_INLINE void group_collection_breaks_cross_heap_cycles()
{
    GC::Heap heap_a([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    GC::Heap heap_b([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);

    heap_a.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    heap_b.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    GC::HeapGroup group;
    group.add(heap_a);
    group.add(heap_b);

    allocate_cross_heap_cycle(heap_a, heap_b);
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 2u);

    // Local collections see the incoming members as roots, so the boundary cycle should survive collection.
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap_a.collect_garbage();
    heap_b.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 2u);

    // The unified mark should not reach the cycle, so both cells should be freed by the group collection.
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    group.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 0u);

    group.remove(heap_a);
    group.remove(heap_b);
}

static NEVER_INLINE void group_collection_traces_live_cross_heap_chains()
{
    GC::Heap heap_a([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    GC::Heap heap_b([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);

    heap_a.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    heap_b.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    GC::HeapGroup group;
    group.add(heap_a);
    group.add(heap_b);

    auto holder = allocate_cross_heap_chain(heap_a, heap_b);
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 3u);

    // The whole chain must survive a group collection, including the second A cell that is only reachable through the B cell.
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    group.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 3u);

    holder = {};
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    group.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 0u);

    group.remove(heap_a);
    group.remove(heap_b);
}

static NEVER_INLINE void group_collection_finalizer_creates_null_weak_to_dead_foreign_cell()
{
    GC::Heap heap_a([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    GC::Heap heap_b([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);

    heap_a.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    heap_b.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    GC::HeapGroup group;
    group.add(heap_a);
    group.add(heap_b);

    // The finalizer runs while heap B's weak pointers have already been cleared, whether or not B has run its own
    // finalizers yet, so a weak pointer that it creates to B's dead cell must be null.
    s_weak_to_dead_foreign_cell_was_null_while_finalizing = {};
    allocate_weak_creating_cell_and_foreign_garbage(heap_a, heap_b);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    group.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT_EQ(s_weak_to_dead_foreign_cell_was_null_while_finalizing, true);
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_linked_cells, 0u);

    group.remove(heap_a);
    group.remove(heap_b);
}

// Under ASan with detect_stack_use_after_return, a function's locals live on a fake stack, but its frame on the real
// stack still reserves room for them — room it never writes, so it keeps whatever earlier calls left there, and the
// conservative scan reads it. A stale pointer there can keep a dropped cell alive. So each case runs in a frame of its
// own, on stack that GC::scrub_stack_for_testing() has just cleared.
TEST_CASE(sanity_single_heap_frees_garbage)
{

FILE: Tests/LibGC/TestGCIdleCollection.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <LibCore/EventLoop.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/CellAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibGC/IdleCollectionPolicy.h>
#include <LibGC/Testing.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>

using Decision = GC::IdleCollectionPolicy::Decision;

namespace {

bool s_abandoned_cell_was_destroyed = false;

class AbandonedCell final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(AbandonedCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(AbandonedCell);

public:
    virtual ~AbandonedCell() override { s_abandoned_cell_was_destroyed = true; }

private:
    AbandonedCell() = default;

    [[maybe_unused]] FlatPtr m_room_for_a_freelist_entry[2] {};
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(AbandonedCell);

NEVER_INLINE void allocate_abandoned_cell(GC::Heap& heap)
{
    (void)heap.allocate<AbandonedCell>();
}

}

TEST_CASE(collects_once_the_allocation_rate_drops)
{
    GC::IdleCollectionPolicy policy;
    policy.reset(0);

    // A burst establishes the episode's peak rate; a single tick is never itself a rate drop.
    EXPECT(policy.evaluate(16 * MiB, 16 * MiB, 8 * MiB) == Decision::KeepWaiting);

    // No further allocation: the rate has collapsed and there is plenty of garbage, so collect.
    EXPECT(policy.evaluate(16 * MiB, 16 * MiB, 8 * MiB) == Decision::Collect);
}

TEST_CASE(rate_drop_is_gated_on_having_enough_garbage)
{
    GC::IdleCollectionPolicy policy;
    policy.reset(0);

    // A burst far below the minimum-garbage gate (threshold / 16, i.e. 0.5 MiB here).
    EXPECT(policy.evaluate(64 * KiB, 64 * KiB, 8 * MiB) == Decision::KeepWaiting);

    // The rate has dropped, but there still isn't enough garbage to be worth marking the whole live heap.
    EXPECT(policy.evaluate(64 * KiB, 64 * KiB, 8 * MiB) == Decision::KeepWaiting);
}

TEST_CASE(a_quiet_tick_collects_a_few_mib_of_garbage_below_the_rate_drop_gate)
{
    GC::IdleCollectionPolicy policy;
    policy.reset(0);

    // A burst far below the rate-drop gate of a large heap (threshold / 16, i.e. 16 MiB here).
    EXPECT(policy.evaluate(3 * MiB, 3 * MiB, 256 * MiB) == Decision::KeepWaiting);
    EXPECT(!policy.last_tick_was_quiet());

    // Next to no allocation since: the heap went quiet, and a few MiB of garbage are enough.
    EXPECT(policy.evaluate(3 * MiB + 64 * KiB, 3 * MiB + 64 * KiB, 256 * MiB) == Decision::Collect);
    EXPECT(policy.last_tick_was_quiet());
}

TEST_CASE(watchdog_collects_when_the_rate_never_drops)
{
    GC::IdleCollectionPolicy policy;
    policy.reset(0);

    // Steady allocation every tick never looks like a rate drop, so only the watchdog can fire.
    u64 total = 0;
    for (u32 tick = 1; tick < GC::IdleCollectionPolicy::watchdog_ticks; ++tick) {
        total += MiB;
        EXPECT(policy.evaluate(total, 1 * MiB, 8 * MiB) == Decision::KeepWaiting);
    }

    // The watchdog fires on the final tick regardless of the rate or the gate.
    total += MiB;
    EXPECT(policy.evaluate(total, 1 * MiB, 8 * MiB) == Decision::Collect);
}

TEST_CASE(parks_when_there_is_nothing_to_collect)
{
    GC::IdleCollectionPolicy policy;
    policy.reset(0);
    EXPECT(policy.evaluate(4 * MiB, 0, 8 * MiB) == Decision::Park);
}

TEST_CASE(an_abandoned_object_graph_is_collected_without_further_allocation)
{
    Core::EventLoop event_loop;
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);

    s_abandoned_cell_was_destroyed = false;
    allocate_abandoned_cell(heap);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();

    heap.did_abandon_object_graph();
    event_loop.spin_until([] { return s_abandoned_cell_was_destroyed; });
}

FILE: Tests/LibGC/TestGCIncrementalSweep.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <AK/JsonObject.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/CellAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/DeferGC.h>
#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapBlock.h>
#include <LibGC/Root.h>
#include <LibGC/Testing.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>

namespace {

bool s_cell_that_allocates_when_destroyed_was_destroyed = false;
bool s_reachable_cell_was_destroyed = false;

class CellOfAnotherType final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(CellOfAnotherType, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(CellOfAnotherType);

private:
    CellOfAnotherType() = default;

    [[maybe_unused]] FlatPtr m_room_for_a_freelist_entry[2] {};
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(CellOfAnotherType);

CellOfAnotherType* s_cell_of_another_type_allocated_by_a_destructor = nullptr;

class SweptCell final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(SweptCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(SweptCell);

public:
    enum class Role : u8 {
        AllocatesWhenDestroyed,
        AllocatesCellOfAnotherTypeWhenDestroyed,
        Reachable,
        AllocatedByADestructor,
    };

    virtual ~SweptCell() override
    {
        switch (m_role) {
        case Role::AllocatesWhenDestroyed:
            s_cell_that_allocates_when_destroyed_was_destroyed = true;
            (void)heap().allocate<SweptCell>(Role::AllocatedByADestructor);
            break;
        case Role::AllocatesCellOfAnotherTypeWhenDestroyed:
            s_cell_of_another_type_allocated_by_a_destructor = heap().allocate<CellOfAnotherType>().ptr();
            break;
        case Role::Reachable:
            s_reachable_cell_was_destroyed = true;
            break;
        case Role::AllocatedByADestructor:
            break;
        }
    }

private:
    explicit SweptCell(Role role)
        : m_role(role)
    {
    }

    Role m_role;
    [[maybe_unused]] FlatPtr m_room_for_a_freelist_entry[2] {};
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(SweptCell);

// NB: Both cells come from the same block of a fresh heap, the unreachable one first, so the sweep of that block
//     destroys it before it reaches the reachable one.
NEVER_INLINE GC::Root<SweptCell> allocate_unreachable_then_reachable_cell(GC::Heap& heap)
{
    (void)heap.allocate<SweptCell>(SweptCell::Role::AllocatesWhenDestroyed);
    return GC::make_root(heap.allocate<SweptCell>(SweptCell::Role::Reachable));
}

NEVER_INLINE GC::Root<CellOfAnotherType> allocate_reachable_cell_of_another_type_then_unreachable_cell(GC::Heap& heap)
{
    auto reachable_cell = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<CellOfAnotherType>());
    (void)heap.allocate<SweptCell>(SweptCell::Role::AllocatesCellOfAnotherTypeWhenDestroyed);
    return reachable_cell;
}

}

TEST_CASE(allocating_from_a_destructor_during_a_sweep_does_not_free_reachable_cells_of_the_block)
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);

    auto reachable_cell = allocate_unreachable_then_reachable_cell(heap);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();

    // This collection marks the reachable cell and leaves the destruction of the other one to the incremental sweep.
    heap.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT(heap.is_incremental_sweep_active());
    EXPECT(!s_cell_that_allocates_when_destroyed_was_destroyed);

    // Finishing that sweep destroys the unreachable cell, and its allocation starts another collection.
    heap.set_should_collect_on_every_allocation(true);
    heap.collect_garbage();
    heap.set_should_collect_on_every_allocation(false);

    EXPECT(s_cell_that_allocates_when_destroyed_was_destroyed);
    EXPECT(!s_reachable_cell_was_destroyed);
}

TEST_CASE(ending_a_deferral_from_a_destructor_during_a_sweep_does_not_start_a_collection)
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    heap.enable_stats();
    s_cell_that_allocates_when_destroyed_was_destroyed = false;
    s_reachable_cell_was_destroyed = false;

    auto reachable_cell = allocate_unreachable_then_reachable_cell(heap);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();

    // This collection marks the reachable cell and leaves the destruction of the other one to the incremental sweep.
    heap.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT(heap.is_incremental_sweep_active());
    EXPECT(!s_cell_that_allocates_when_destroyed_was_destroyed);

    // A collection requested under a deferral runs once the deferral ends, and finishes that sweep first. That destroys
    // the unreachable cell, and its allocation ends the deferral that the construction of the new cell starts.
    {
        GC::DeferGC defer_gc { heap };
        heap.collect_garbage();
    }

    EXPECT(s_cell_that_allocates_when_destroyed_was_destroyed);
    EXPECT(!s_reachable_cell_was_destroyed);

    AK::JsonObject stats;
    heap.add_stats(stats);
    EXPECT_EQ(stats.get_u64("gc.collections"sv), 2u);
}

TEST_CASE(free_cells_that_a_destructor_takes_while_a_collection_finishes_the_sweep_go_back_to_their_block)
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);

    auto reachable_cell = allocate_reachable_cell_of_another_type_then_unreachable_cell(heap);
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();

    // This collection leaves the destruction of the unreachable cell to the incremental sweep.
    heap.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT(heap.is_incremental_sweep_active());

    // The next collection finishes that sweep. The destructor takes the free cells of the block that holds the
    // reachable cell, and the cell it allocates there is unreachable.
    heap.collect_garbage();
    auto* cell_allocated_by_the_destructor = s_cell_of_another_type_allocated_by_a_destructor;
    EXPECT(cell_allocated_by_the_destructor);
    auto& block = *GC::HeapBlock::from_cell(cell_allocated_by_the_destructor);
    EXPECT_EQ(&block, GC::HeapBlock::from_cell(reachable_cell.ptr()));
    EXPECT(block.is_pending_sweep());

    // Sweeping the block, as the sweep timer would, frees that cell. Once no allocator holds free cells of the block,
    // the next cell comes from the free list of the block.
    heap.sweep_block(block);
    auto next_cell = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<CellOfAnotherType>());
    EXPECT_EQ(next_cell.ptr(), cell_allocated_by_the_destructor);
}

TEST_CASE(cells_allocated_into_blocks_pending_sweep_do_not_count_as_live)
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    heap.enable_stats();

    auto reachable_cell = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<CellOfAnotherType>());
    auto& block = *GC::HeapBlock::from_cell(reachable_cell.ptr());
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();

    heap.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT(heap.is_incremental_sweep_active());

    // Under a deferral the allocator takes cells from the block without sweeping it, and they get marked to survive.
    {
        GC::DeferGC defer_gc { heap };
        for (size_t i = 0; i < 16; ++i) {
            auto cell = heap.allocate<CellOfAnotherType>();
            EXPECT_EQ(GC::HeapBlock::from_cell(cell.ptr()), &block);
            EXPECT(block.is_pending_sweep());
        }
    }

    // The next collection finishes that sweep, which records what the collection before it found alive.
    heap.collect_garbage();
    AK::JsonObject stats;
    heap.add_stats(stats);
    EXPECT_EQ(stats.get_u64("gc.live_cell_bytes"sv), block.cell_size());
}

TEST_CASE(collect_everything_leaves_no_live_cell_bytes)
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    heap.enable_stats();

    {
        auto reachable_cell = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<CellOfAnotherType>());
        GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
        heap.collect_garbage();
    }

    heap.collect_garbage(GC::Heap::CollectionType::CollectEverything);
    AK::JsonObject stats;
    heap.add_stats(stats);
    EXPECT_EQ(stats.get_u64("gc.live_cell_bytes"sv), 0u);
}

FILE: Tests/LibGC/TestGCThreads.cpp
/*

#include <AK/AssertionFailure.h>
#include <AK/Atomic.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibGC/BlockAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/CellAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibGC/Ptr.h>
#include <LibGC/Root.h>
#include <LibGC/Testing.h>
#include <LibGC/Weak.h>
#include <LibGC/WeakInlines.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>
#include <LibThreading/Thread.h>

#if !defined(AK_OS_WINDOWS)
#    include <sys/wait.h>
#    include <unistd.h>
#endif

namespace {

Atomic<size_t> s_live_cells { 0 };

class ThreadTestCell final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(ThreadTestCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(ThreadTestCell);

public:
    virtual ~ThreadTestCell() override { s_live_cells.fetch_sub(1); }

    GC::Ptr<ThreadTestCell>& next() { return m_next; }

private:
    ThreadTestCell() { s_live_cells.fetch_add(1); }

    virtual void visit_edges(Visitor& visitor) override
    {
        Base::visit_edges(visitor);
        visitor.visit(m_next);
    }

    GC::Ptr<ThreadTestCell> m_next;
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(ThreadTestCell);

template<typename Callback>
void run_on_threads(size_t thread_count, IGNORE_USE_IN_ESCAPING_LAMBDA Callback callback)
{
    Vector<NonnullRefPtr<Threading::Thread>> threads;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < thread_count; ++i) {
        auto thread = Threading::Thread::construct("GCThreadTest"sv, [&callback] {
            callback();
            return static_cast<intptr_t>(0);
        });
        thread->start();
        threads.append(move(thread));
    }
    for (auto& thread : threads)
        MUST(thread->join());
}

void churn_cells()
{
    GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { });
    heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
    EXPECT_EQ(&GC::Heap::the(), &heap);

    // More than one block of cells, and enough weak pointers for a weak block.
    auto list = GC::make_root(heap.allocate<ThreadTestCell>());
    Vector<GC::Weak<ThreadTestCell>> weak_pointers;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) {
        auto cell = heap.allocate<ThreadTestCell>();
        cell->next() = list.cell();
        list = GC::make_root(cell);
        weak_pointers.append(cell);
    }
    heap.collect_garbage();
    for (auto& weak : weak_pointers)
        EXPECT(weak.ptr());
    list = {};
}

}

TEST_CASE(heaps_on_several_threads_do_not_share_their_allocators)
{
    run_on_threads(8, [] {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < 10; ++i)
            churn_cells();
    });
    EXPECT_EQ(s_live_cells.load(), 0u);
}

TEST_CASE(heap_blocks_come_back_when_a_heap_goes_away)
{
    auto churn = [] {
        run_on_threads(4, [] {
            for (size_t i = 0; i < 10; ++i)
                churn_cells();
        });
    };

    churn();
    auto committed_end = GC::BlockAllocator::heap_region_committed_end();
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 20; ++i)
        churn();
    // NB: The decommit worker may have one chunk prepared ahead of the blocks that are in use.
    EXPECT(GC::BlockAllocator::heap_region_committed_end() <= committed_end + 2 * MiB);
}

TEST_CASE(a_new_heap_can_become_the_default_of_a_thread)
{
    run_on_threads(1, [] {
        {
            GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { });
            EXPECT_EQ(&GC::Heap::the(), &heap);
        }
        GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { });
        EXPECT_EQ(&GC::Heap::the(), &heap);
    });
}

TEST_CASE(null_weak_pointers_can_be_copied_on_several_threads)
{
    run_on_threads(8, [] {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < 1'000'000; ++i) {
            GC::Weak<ThreadTestCell> weak;
            auto copy = weak;
            EXPECT(!copy);
        }
    });
}

TEST_CASE(weak_pointer_can_outlive_its_heap)
{
    GC::Weak<ThreadTestCell> weak;
    {
        GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
        auto cell = heap.allocate<ThreadTestCell>();
        weak = cell;
        EXPECT(weak);
    }
    EXPECT(!weak);
    auto copy = weak;
    EXPECT(!copy);
    weak = nullptr;
    EXPECT(!copy);
}

#if !defined(AK_OS_WINDOWS)
static constexpr int verification_failure_exit_code = 42;

template<typename Callback>
static bool crashes(Callback callback)
{
    auto pid = fork();
    VERIFY(pid >= 0);
    if (pid == 0) {
        // NB: A failed check would print a symbolized backtrace before it crashes, which takes about a second.
        AK::set_assertion_failure_callback([](auto, auto) { _exit(verification_failure_exit_code); });
        callback();
        _exit(0);
    }
    int status = 0;
    VERIFY(waitpid(pid, &status, 0) == pid);
    return WIFEXITED(status) && WEXITSTATUS(status) == verification_failure_exit_code;
}

TEST_CASE(a_heap_must_go_away_on_its_own_thread)
{
    EXPECT(crashes([] {
        auto* heap = new GC::Heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
        run_on_threads(1, [heap] { delete heap; });
    }));
}

TEST_CASE(a_heap_must_collect_on_its_own_thread)
{
    EXPECT(crashes([] {
        auto* heap = new GC::Heap([](auto&) { }, GC::Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
        run_on_threads(1, [heap] { heap->collect_garbage(); });
    }));
}
#endif

FILE: Tests/LibGC/TestGCTypeIsolation.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <AK/Atomic.h>
#include <AK/HashTable.h>
#include <LibGC/CAPI.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/CellAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/DeferGC.h>
#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapBlock.h>
#include <LibGC/Testing.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>
#include <LibThreading/Thread.h>

namespace {

Atomic<size_t> s_live_cells { 0 };

// Each test uses types of its own, so that it starts out with empty pools.
template<int Tag>
class TaggedCell final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(TaggedCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(TaggedCell);

public:
    virtual ~TaggedCell() override { s_live_cells.fetch_sub(1); }

private:
    TaggedCell() { s_live_cells.fetch_add(1); }

    [[maybe_unused]] FlatPtr m_room_for_a_freelist_entry[2] {};
};

template<int Tag>
GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(TaggedCell<Tag>);

using Blocks = HashTable<FlatPtr>;

static constexpr size_t BLOCK_COUNT = 64;

// Fills cells until they are in BLOCK_COUNT blocks, and returns those.
template<typename T>
NEVER_INLINE Blocks allocate_blocks(GC::Heap& heap)
{
    GC::DeferGC defer_gc { heap };
    Blocks blocks;
    while (blocks.size() < BLOCK_COUNT)
        blocks.set(bit_cast<FlatPtr>(GC::HeapBlock::from_cell(heap.allocate<T>().ptr())));
    return blocks;
}

bool have_a_block_in_common(Blocks const& first, Blocks const& second)
{
    for (auto block : first) {
        if (second.contains(block))
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

template<typename Callback>
void run_on_a_new_thread(IGNORE_USE_IN_ESCAPING_LAMBDA Callback callback)
{
    auto thread = Threading::Thread::construct("TypeIsolationTest"sv, [&callback] {
        callback();
        return static_cast<intptr_t>(0);
    });
    thread->start();
    MUST(thread->join());
}

}

TEST_CASE(blocks_stay_with_their_type_after_their_heap_dies)
{
    using A = TaggedCell<0>;
    using B = TaggedCell<1>;

    Blocks blocks_of_a;
    run_on_a_new_thread([&] {
        GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { });
        blocks_of_a = allocate_blocks<A>(heap);
    });
    EXPECT_EQ(blocks_of_a.size(), BLOCK_COUNT);

#if defined(AK_OS_LINUX) && !defined(HAS_ADDRESS_SANITIZER)
    // The pages went back with the heap: a page that is still there holds the block's header.
    for (auto block : blocks_of_a) {
        FlatPtr first_word = *bit_cast<FlatPtr volatile*>(block);
        EXPECT_EQ(first_word, 0u);
    }
#endif

    run_on_a_new_thread([&] {
        GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { });
        EXPECT(!have_a_block_in_common(blocks_of_a, allocate_blocks<B>(heap)));

        // The new heap reuses the blocks of the type it needs, and so takes no others.
        auto blocks_of_a_again = allocate_blocks<A>(heap);
        EXPECT_EQ(blocks_of_a_again.size(), blocks_of_a.size());
        for (auto block : blocks_of_a_again)
            EXPECT(blocks_of_a.contains(block));
    });
}

TEST_CASE(blocks_stay_with_their_type_after_a_collection_frees_them)
{
    using A = TaggedCell<2>;
    using B = TaggedCell<3>;

    run_on_a_new_thread([] {
        GC::Heap heap([](auto&) { });
        heap.set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);

        auto live_cells_before = s_live_cells.load();
        auto blocks_of_a = allocate_blocks<A>(heap);
        auto allocated_cells = s_live_cells.load() - live_cells_before;

        GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
        heap.collect_garbage();
        // NB: A value left in a register can keep a cell, and its block, alive. Nearly all of them have to go, or
        //     this proves nothing.
        EXPECT(s_live_cells.load() - live_cells_before < allocated_cells / 8);

        EXPECT(!have_a_block_in_common(blocks_of_a, allocate_blocks<B>(heap)));

        auto blocks_of_a_again = allocate_blocks<A>(heap);
        for (auto block : blocks_of_a_again)
            EXPECT(blocks_of_a.contains(block));
    });
}

TEST_CASE(a_foreign_type_has_the_same_pool_in_every_heap)
{
    static GCCellTypeInfo const small_cell_info {
        .cell_size = 64,
        .alignment = 8,
        .kind = 0,
        .visit_edges = [](GCCell*, GCVisitor*) { },
        .finalize = nullptr,
        .destroy = nullptr,
        .external_memory_size = nullptr,
        .class_name = nullptr,
    };
    static GCCellTypeInfo const large_cell_info { [] {
        auto info = small_cell_info;
        info.cell_size = 128;
        return info;
    }() };
    static int first_type;
    static int second_type;

    auto pool_of = [](GCCellTypeInfo const& info, void const* foreign_type) {
        auto* allocator = gc_allocator_create(&info, "Foreign", 7, foreign_type);
        auto* pool = &reinterpret_cast<GC::CellAllocatorDescriptorBase*>(allocator)->block_allocator();
        if (foreign_type)
            gc_allocator_destroy(allocator);
        return pool;
    };

    auto* pool = pool_of(small_cell_info, &first_type);
    EXPECT_EQ(pool_of(small_cell_info, &first_type), pool);
    EXPECT_NE(pool_of(small_cell_info, &second_type), pool);
    EXPECT_NE(pool_of(large_cell_info, &first_type), pool);

    // NB: Allocators without a foreign type live as long as the process.
    EXPECT_NE(pool_of(small_cell_info, nullptr), pool_of(small_cell_info, nullptr));
}

class TestVisitor : public GC::Cell::Visitor {
    virtual void visit_impl(GC::Cell& cell) override { visited_cells.set(&cell); }
    virtual void visit_impl(ReadonlySpan<GC::NanBoxedValue> span) override { last_nan_span_size = span.size(); }

public:

class TestNanBox : public GC::NanBoxedValue {
public:
    static TestNanBox from_cell(GC::Cell* cell)
    {
        TestNanBox box;
        box.m_value.encoded = GC::SHIFTED_IS_CELL_PATTERN | GC::NanBoxedValue::encode_pointer_bits(cell);
        return box;
    }

    static TestNanBox from_double(double value)
    {
        TestNanBox box;
        box.m_value.as_double = value;
        return box;
    }

#include <AK/HashMap.h>

class TestCell : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(TestCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(TestCell);

public:
    GC::Member<TestCell> next;
    u32 value { 0 };

private:
    virtual void visit_edges(Visitor& visitor) override
    {
        Base::visit_edges(visitor);
        visitor.visit(next);
    }
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(TestCell);

class DerivedTestCell final : public TestCell {
    GC_CELL(DerivedTestCell, TestCell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(DerivedTestCell);
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(DerivedTestCell);

static GC::Heap& test_heap()
{
    static AK::NeverDestroyed<GC::Heap> heap([](auto&) { });
    return *heap;
}

TEST_SETUP
{
    GC::Heap::set_default_heap_for_testing(test_heap());
}

static_assert(sizeof(GC::Member<TestCell>) == sizeof(u32));
static_assert(sizeof(GC::NonnullMember<TestCell>) == sizeof(u32));
static_assert(IsTriviallyCopyConstructible<GC::Member<TestCell>> && IsTriviallyMoveConstructible<GC::Member<TestCell>>);
static_assert(IsTriviallyDestructible<GC::Member<TestCell>>);
static_assert(IsTriviallyCopyConstructible<GC::NonnullMember<TestCell>> && IsTriviallyMoveConstructible<GC::NonnullMember<TestCell>>);
static_assert(IsTriviallyDestructible<GC::NonnullMember<TestCell>>);

TEST_CASE(base_copy_matches_the_heap_region)
{
    // NB: The first cell reserves the region, if nothing has yet.
    (void)test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();
    EXPECT_EQ(GC::heap_region_base(), js_heap_region_base);
    EXPECT_EQ(GC::heap_region_base() % GC::HEAP_REGION_SIZE, 0u);
}

TEST_CASE(base_copy_registered_after_the_region_exists_gets_the_base)
{
    (void)test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();
    // NB: Registrations are never undone, so this one is for the rest of the process.
    static FlatPtr copy;
    static GC::HeapRegionBaseCopyRegistration registration { copy };
    EXPECT_NE(copy, 0u);
    EXPECT_EQ(copy, js_heap_region_base);
}

TEST_CASE(member_round_trips_and_null_is_zero)
{
    auto cell = test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();

    GC::Member<TestCell> member;
    EXPECT(!member);
    EXPECT_EQ(member.compressed(), 0u);
    EXPECT_EQ(member.ptr(), nullptr);
    EXPECT(member == nullptr);

    member = cell;
    EXPECT(member);
    EXPECT_EQ(member.ptr(), cell.ptr());
    EXPECT_EQ(member.compressed(), GC::compress(cell.ptr()));
    EXPECT_EQ(&*member, cell.ptr());
    EXPECT_EQ(member->value, 0u);

    member = nullptr;
    EXPECT(!member);

    GC::NonnullMember<TestCell> nonnull = *cell;
    EXPECT_EQ(nonnull.ptr(), cell.ptr());
    EXPECT_EQ(nonnull.compressed(), GC::compress(cell.ptr()));
}

TEST_CASE(members_convert_to_and_from_stack_pointers)
{
    auto derived = test_heap().allocate<DerivedTestCell>();

    GC::Member<DerivedTestCell> member = derived;
    GC::Ptr<TestCell> base_ptr = member;
    EXPECT_EQ(base_ptr.ptr(), derived.ptr());
    GC::Ptr<GC::Cell> cell_ptr = member;
    EXPECT_EQ(cell_ptr.ptr(), derived.ptr());
    EXPECT_EQ(member.as_nonnull().ptr(), derived.ptr());

    GC::NonnullMember<DerivedTestCell> nonnull = derived;
    GC::Ref<TestCell> base_ref = nonnull;
    EXPECT_EQ(base_ref.ptr(), derived.ptr());
    GC::Ptr<TestCell> base_ptr_from_nonnull = nonnull;
    EXPECT_EQ(base_ptr_from_nonnull.ptr(), derived.ptr());
    TestCell& reference = nonnull;
    EXPECT_EQ(&reference, derived.ptr());

    GC::Member<TestCell> widened = nonnull;
    EXPECT_EQ(widened.ptr(), derived.ptr());
    GC::Member<TestCell> from_ptr = GC::Ptr<DerivedTestCell> { derived };
    EXPECT_EQ(from_ptr.ptr(), derived.ptr());
    GC::NonnullMember<TestCell> from_ref = derived;
    EXPECT_EQ(from_ref.ptr(), derived.ptr());
}

TEST_CASE(members_compare_like_pointers)
{
    auto a = test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();
    auto b = test_heap().allocate<DerivedTestCell>();

    GC::Member<TestCell> member_a = a;
    GC::Member<TestCell> member_b = b;
    GC::NonnullMember<DerivedTestCell> nonnull_b = b;

    EXPECT(member_a != member_b);
    EXPECT(member_b == nonnull_b);
    EXPECT(nonnull_b == member_b);
    EXPECT(member_a == a);
    EXPECT(a == member_a);
    EXPECT(member_a != GC::Ptr<TestCell> { b });
    EXPECT(member_b == GC::Ref<DerivedTestCell> { *b });
    EXPECT(member_a == a.ptr());
    EXPECT(b.ptr() == nonnull_b);
    EXPECT(member_a != nullptr);
    EXPECT(GC::Member<TestCell> {} == GC::Ptr<TestCell> {});

    GC::Cell* as_cell = b.ptr();
    EXPECT(member_b == as_cell);
    EXPECT(nonnull_b == as_cell);
}

TEST_CASE(members_hash_like_pointers)
{
    auto a = test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();
    auto b = test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();

    EXPECT_EQ(Traits<GC::Member<TestCell>>::hash(a), Traits<GC::Ptr<TestCell>>::hash(a));
    EXPECT_EQ(Traits<GC::NonnullMember<TestCell>>::hash(*a), Traits<GC::Ref<TestCell>>::hash(a));

    HashTable<GC::Member<TestCell>> table;
    table.set(a);
    EXPECT(table.contains(GC::Ptr<TestCell> { a }));
    EXPECT(!table.contains(GC::Ptr<TestCell> { b }));

    HashMap<GC::NonnullMember<TestCell>, int> map;
    map.set(*a, 1);
    map.set(*b, 2);
    EXPECT_EQ(map.get(GC::Ref<TestCell> { a }), 1);
    EXPECT_EQ(map.get(GC::Ref<TestCell> { b }), 2);
}

class TestVisitor : public GC::Cell::Visitor {
    virtual void visit_impl(GC::Cell& cell) override { visited_cells.append(&cell); }
    virtual void visit_impl(ReadonlySpan<GC::NanBoxedValue>) override { }

public:
    Vector<GC::Cell*> visited_cells;
};

TEST_CASE(visitor_visits_member_slots)
{
    auto a = test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();
    auto b = test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();

    GC::Member<TestCell> member = a;
    GC::Member<TestCell> null_member;
    GC::NonnullMember<TestCell> nonnull = *b;
    Vector<GC::Member<TestCell>> vector { a, nullptr, b };
    Optional<GC::NonnullMember<TestCell>> optional = GC::NonnullMember<TestCell> { *a };

    TestVisitor visitor;
    visitor.visit(member);
    visitor.visit(null_member);
    visitor.visit(nonnull);
    visitor.visit(vector);
    visitor.visit(optional);

    Vector<GC::Cell*> expected { a.ptr(), b.ptr(), a.ptr(), b.ptr(), a.ptr() };
    EXPECT_EQ(visitor.visited_cells, expected);
}

TEST_CASE(members_keep_cells_alive)
{
    auto head = GC::make_root(test_heap().allocate<TestCell>());
    head->next = test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();
    head->next->value = 42;

    test_heap().collect_garbage(GC::Heap::CollectionType::CollectGarbage);

    EXPECT_EQ(head->next->value, 42u);
}

class FinalizationTrackingCell final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(FinalizationTrackingCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(FinalizationTrackingCell);

public:
    explicit FinalizationTrackingCell(bool& finalized)
        : m_finalized(finalized)
    {
    }

private:
    virtual void finalize() override
    {
        Base::finalize();
        m_finalized = true;
    }

    bool& m_finalized;
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(FinalizationTrackingCell);

// Keeps nothing on the stack that points at the cell the function captures, other than the root of the function.
static NEVER_INLINE GC::Root<GC::Function<size_t()>> make_function_capturing_a_member(bool& finalized)
{
    GC::Member<FinalizationTrackingCell> member = test_heap().allocate<FinalizationTrackingCell>(finalized);
    return GC::make_root(GC::create_function(test_heap(), GC::captures(member), [](GC::Ptr<FinalizationTrackingCell>& cell) {
        return reinterpret_cast<size_t>(cell.ptr());
    }));
}

static NEVER_INLINE void clobber_the_stack()
{
    u8 volatile scratch[16 * KiB];
    for (auto& byte : scratch)
        byte = 0;
}

TEST_CASE(function_capturing_a_member_keeps_its_cell_alive)
{
    // NB: Static, since the cell outlives the test once nothing holds it anymore.
    static bool finalized;
    finalized = false;
    auto function = make_function_capturing_a_member(finalized);
    clobber_the_stack();

    test_heap().collect_garbage(GC::Heap::CollectionType::CollectGarbage);

    EXPECT(!finalized);
    EXPECT_NE(function->function()(), 0u);
}

FILE: Tests/LibGC/TestNanBoxedValue.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

#include <AK/NeverDestroyed.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/CellAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapRegion.h>
#include <LibGC/NanBoxedValue.h>
#include <LibGC/Testing.h>
#include <LibGC/Weak.h>
#include <LibGC/WeakInlines.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>

namespace {

class TestCell final : public GC::Cell {
    GC_CELL(TestCell, GC::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(TestCell);

    u8 m_padding[16] {};
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(TestCell);

static GC::Heap& test_heap()
{
    static AK::NeverDestroyed<GC::Heap> heap([](auto&) { });
    return *heap;
}

TEST_SETUP
{
    GC::Heap::set_default_heap_for_testing(test_heap());
}

// Every payload bit above the heap region offset.
static constexpr u64 JUNK_PAYLOAD_BITS = 0x0000'ffff'ffff'ffffULL & ~static_cast<u64>(GC::HEAP_REGION_OFFSET_MASK);

class TestNanBox final : public GC::NanBoxedValue {
public:
    static TestNanBox from_payload(u64 payload)
    {
        TestNanBox value;
        value.m_value.encoded = GC::SHIFTED_IS_CELL_PATTERN | payload;
        return value;
    }

    static TestNanBox from_cell(GC::Cell const* cell)
    {
        return from_payload(GC::NanBoxedValue::encode_pointer_bits(cell));
    }
};

TEST_CASE(cell_payload_round_trips_through_heap_region)
{
    auto cell = test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();
    auto value = TestNanBox::from_cell(cell.ptr());

    EXPECT(value.is_cell());
    EXPECT_EQ(value.extract_pointer<GC::Cell>(), cell.ptr());
}

TEST_CASE(cell_payload_masks_junk_high_bits)
{
    auto cell = test_heap().allocate<TestCell>();
    auto offset = GC::NanBoxedValue::encode_pointer_bits(cell.ptr());
    auto value = TestNanBox::from_payload(offset | JUNK_PAYLOAD_BITS);
    auto decoded = value.extract_pointer<GC::Cell>();
    auto base = js_heap_region_base;

    EXPECT(reinterpret_cast<FlatPtr>(decoded) >= base);
    EXPECT(reinterpret_cast<FlatPtr>(decoded) < base + GC::HEAP_REGION_SIZE);
    EXPECT_EQ(decoded, cell.ptr());
}

TEST_CASE(conservative_scanner_decodes_caged_value)
{
    auto& heap = test_heap();
    GC::Weak<TestCell> weak_cell;
    u64 volatile boxed_value = 0;

    {
        auto cell = heap.allocate<TestCell>();
        weak_cell = cell.ptr();
        boxed_value = GC::SHIFTED_IS_CELL_PATTERN
            | GC::NanBoxedValue::encode_pointer_bits(cell.ptr())
            | JUNK_PAYLOAD_BITS;
        EXPECT(boxed_value != 0);
    }

    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage();
    EXPECT(weak_cell);

    boxed_value = 0;
    GC::scrub_stack_for_testing();
    heap.collect_garbage(GC::Heap::CollectionType::CollectEverything);
    EXPECT(!weak_cell);
}
