// A message that arrives immediately before EOF must be delivered to the consumer — even when the consumer drains in
// the narrow window between the IO thread observing EOF and that message becoming available. Otherwise, the consumer
// (e.g. a MessagePort) can tear itself down on the EOF, and drop the final message. See the EOF/message ordering in
// read_incoming_messages and read_as_many_messages_as_possible_without_blocking.
TEST_CASE(message_arriving_just_before_eof_is_not_dropped_on_shutdown)
{
    Core::EventLoop loop;

    int fds[2] = {};
    MUST(Core::System::socketpair(AF_LOCAL, SOCK_STREAM, 0, fds));

    // Queue one message and hang up the peer before the reading transport (and its IO thread) exists — so the IO
    // thread's first read sees the message bytes and EOF together.
    {
        auto peer_socket = TRY_OR_FAIL(Core::LocalSocket::adopt_fd(fds[1]));
        MUST(peer_socket->set_blocking(false));
        IPC::TransportSocket peer(move(peer_socket));

        auto hello = "hello"sv.bytes();
        IPC::MessageDataType payload;
        payload.append(hello.data(), hello.size());
        Vector<IPC::Attachment> no_attachments;
        MUST(peer.post_message(move(payload), no_attachments));
        peer.close_after_sending_all_pending_messages();
    }

    // Force the IO thread to wake the consumer and pause on EOF before it parses and appends the message it read — so
    // the consumer's first drain falls inside the window that would otherwise drop the message.
    IPC::TransportSocket::set_eof_drain_window_for_test(200);
    ScopeGuard reset_window = [] { IPC::TransportSocket::set_eof_drain_window_for_test(0); };

    auto reader_socket = TRY_OR_FAIL(Core::LocalSocket::adopt_fd(fds[0]));
    MUST(reader_socket->set_blocking(false));
    IPC::TransportSocket transport(move(reader_socket));

    IGNORE_USE_IN_ESCAPING_LAMBDA Atomic<u32> delivered = 0;
    IGNORE_USE_IN_ESCAPING_LAMBDA Atomic<bool> observed_shutdown = false;

    transport.set_up_read_hook([&] {
        // Model a consumer that tears itself down once it observes shutdown (as MessagePort does): A message not
        // delivered before shutdown is observed is lost for good.
        if (observed_shutdown.load(AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed))
            return;
        auto should_shutdown = transport.read_as_many_messages_as_possible_without_blocking([&](auto&&) {
            delivered.fetch_add(1, AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed);
        });
        if (should_shutdown == IPC::TransportSocket::ShouldShutdown::Yes)
            observed_shutdown.store(true, AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed);
    });

    spin_until(loop, [&] {
        return observed_shutdown.load(AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed);
    });

    EXPECT_EQ(delivered.load(AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed), 1u);
}

// A message already buffered on the socket when the IO thread stops must still be delivered — even if the loop stops on
// a path that doesn't run its in-loop read. That happens when a send fails because the peer closed (transfer_data
// returns SocketClosed): The loop ends without draining the receive side. The loop-exit drain is the backstop. Without
// it, the message is lost, and a consumer that tears down on EOF (like MessagePort, e.g. a cross-realm transform stream
// receiving a final "error") hangs its peer forever.
TEST_CASE(buffered_message_is_drained_when_io_thread_stops_without_reading_it)
{
    Core::EventLoop loop;

    int fds[2] = {};
    MUST(Core::System::socketpair(AF_LOCAL, SOCK_STREAM, 0, fds));

    // Queue one message, and hang up the peer before the reading transport exists — so the reader's first poll sees the
    // message bytes and EOF together.
    {
        auto peer_socket = TRY_OR_FAIL(Core::LocalSocket::adopt_fd(fds[1]));
        MUST(peer_socket->set_blocking(false));
        IPC::TransportSocket peer(move(peer_socket));

        auto hello = "hello"sv.bytes();
        IPC::MessageDataType payload;
        payload.append(hello.data(), hello.size());
        Vector<IPC::Attachment> no_attachments;
        MUST(peer.post_message(move(payload), no_attachments));
        peer.close_after_sending_all_pending_messages();
    }

    // Model a stop path that doesn't run the in-loop read (e.g. SocketClosed from a failed send): The loop reaches its
    // exit with the message still buffered on the socket — so only the loop-exit drain can deliver it.
    IPC::TransportSocket::set_skip_inloop_read_for_test(true);
    ScopeGuard reset_skip = [] { IPC::TransportSocket::set_skip_inloop_read_for_test(false); };

    auto reader_socket = TRY_OR_FAIL(Core::LocalSocket::adopt_fd(fds[0]));
    MUST(reader_socket->set_blocking(false));
    IPC::TransportSocket transport(move(reader_socket));

    // The receive barrier must include the loop-exit drain, even after the IO thread stops.
    transport.wait_until_incoming_is_current();

    IGNORE_USE_IN_ESCAPING_LAMBDA Atomic<u32> delivered = 0;
    IGNORE_USE_IN_ESCAPING_LAMBDA Atomic<bool> observed_shutdown = false;

    transport.set_up_read_hook([&] {
        if (observed_shutdown.load(AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed))
            return;
        auto should_shutdown = transport.read_as_many_messages_as_possible_without_blocking([&](auto&&) {
            delivered.fetch_add(1, AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed);
        });
        if (should_shutdown == IPC::TransportSocket::ShouldShutdown::Yes)
            observed_shutdown.store(true, AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed);
    });

    spin_until(loop, [&] {
        return observed_shutdown.load(AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed);
    });

    EXPECT_EQ(delivered.load(AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed), 1u);
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/AST/input/arguments-object.js
// Accessing `arguments` in a non-strict function.
function uses_arguments() {
    return arguments[0];
}

// Naming a parameter `arguments` shadows the arguments object.
function arguments_as_param(arguments) {
    return arguments;
}

// `arguments` as the second parameter gets [argument:1].
function arguments_as_second_param(x, arguments) {
    return x + arguments;
}

// `arguments` in an arrow function refers to the enclosing function.
function arrow_arguments() {
    let f = () => arguments[0];
    return f();
}

// Destructuring parameter still allows `arguments` access.
function destructured_with_arguments({ x }) {
    return arguments[0];
}

// Rest parameter + arguments.
function rest_and_arguments(...args) {
    return arguments.length;
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/AST/input/arrow-this-in-nested-function.js
// An arrow function takes `this` from the nearest function that is not an arrow function.
// Functions further out must not be marked as reading `this` through the environment.
function outer_of_function() {
    function inner() {
        return () => this;
    }
    return inner;
}

function outer_of_class() {
    class C {
        m() {
            return () => this;
        }
    }
    return C;
}

function outer_of_object_method() {
    return {
        m() {
            return () => this;
        }
    };
}

function outer_of_arrow() {
    return () => () => this;
}

// Assignment targets: the LHS of assignments should still resolve
// as local or global correctly.
var g = 1;

function assign_local() {
    let x = 1;
    x = 2;
    x += 3;
    return x;
}

function assign_global() {
    g = 2;
    g += 3;
    return g;
}

// Destructuring assignment (not declaration).
function destruct_assign() {
    let a, b;
    [a, b] = [1, 2];
    return a + b;
}

// Assignment to a variable not declared anywhere (implicit global).
function assign_undeclared() {
    undeclared = 1;
    return undeclared;
}

// Increment/decrement targets.
function update_targets() {
    let x = 0;
    x++;
    ++x;
    x--;
    --x;
    return x;
}

// Identifiers inside a binding pattern should carry their own start
// position. Previously they inherited the pattern's opening `[` or `{`
// position, which made source maps and devtools point at the bracket
// rather than the binding name.

let { foo, bar } = {};

FILE: Tests/LibJS/AST/input/catch-param-scope.js
// Catch parameter is scoped to the catch block.
function basic_catch() {
    try {
        throw 1;
    } catch (err) {
        return err;
    }
}

// Catch with destructuring.
function catch_destruct() {
    try {
        throw { msg: "oops", code: 42 };
    } catch ({ msg, code }) {
        return msg + code;
    }
}

// Catch parameter shadows outer variable.
function catch_shadow() {
    let err = "outer";
    try {
        throw "inner";
    } catch (err) {
        err;
    }
    return err;
}

// No catch parameter (catch without binding).
function catch_no_param() {
    try {
        throw 1;
    } catch {
        return 2;
    }
}

// Multiple catch clauses with destructuring patterns.
// Tests that pattern_bound_names don't leak between catch clauses.
function multiple_catch_destruct() {
    try {
        try {
            throw { a: 1 };
        } catch ({ a }) {
            a;
        }
        throw { b: 2 };
    } catch ({ b }) {
        return b;
    }
}

// Catch with eval: poisons the catch block.
function catch_with_eval() {
    try {
        throw 1;
    } catch (err) {
        eval("");
        return err;
    }
}

// Class name is visible inside the class body but not outside (for class expressions).

    method() {
        return MyClass;
    }

// Class declaration name IS visible in the enclosing scope.
function uses_class() {
    class Foo {
        method() {
            return new Foo();
        }
    }
    return new Foo();
}

// Computed property keys are evaluated in the class scope.
function computed_key() {
    let key = "hello";

        }
    }
    return new Bar();
}

        static x = 1;
        static method() {
            return Baz.x;
        }
    }
    return Baz.method();
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/AST/input/closure-captures.js
// Inner function captures a variable from the outer function.
// Both should mark their own locals correctly.
function outer() {
    let captured = 1;
    let not_captured = 2;
    function inner() {
        return captured;
    }
    return inner() + not_captured;
}

// Capture across two levels of nesting.
function level0() {
    let a = 1;
    function level1() {
        let b = 2;
        function level2() {
            return a + b;
        }
        return level2();
    }
    return level1();
}

// Closure created in a loop -- each iteration captures the same
// variable binding (with var) or different ones (with let).
function loop_closure_var() {
    var fns = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        fns.push(function () {
            return i;
        });
    }
    return fns;
}

function loop_closure_let() {
    var fns = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        fns.push(function () {
            return i;
        });
    }
    return fns;
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/AST/input/eval-scope-chain-deep.js
// eval in the middle of a deep nesting chain.
// Functions ABOVE the eval should keep their locals.
// The function WITH eval loses locals.
// Functions BELOW don't directly lose locals, but references to
// variables in the eval-poisoned scope become [in-eval-scope].
function clean_outer() {
    let a = 1;
    function middle() {
        let b = 2;
        eval("");
        function inner() {
            let c = 3;
            return a + b + c;
        }
        return inner();
    }
    return middle();
}

// eval at the top level of a nested chain.
function eval_at_top() {
    let x = 1;
    eval("");
    function level1() {
        let y = 2;
        function level2() {
            return x + y;
        }
        return level2();
    }
    return level1();
}

        b;

// eval in one branch, with in another -- both poison the function.
function branched_poison(flag, obj) {
    let c = 1;
    if (flag) {
        eval("");
    } else {
        with (obj) {
            c;
        }
    }
    return c;
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/AST/input/property-key-arguments.js
// `arguments` as a non-computed property key is just a name token,
// not a reference. The function should NOT be marked might-need-arguments.
function plain_arguments_key() {
    return { arguments: 1 };
}

// Same for `eval` as a non-computed property key.
function plain_eval_key() {
    return { eval: 1 };
}

// Shorthand `{ arguments }` IS a reference to the binding. The parser
// doesn't fire its conservative might-need-arguments flag here (the
// shorthand path doesn't go through the eval/arguments check on
// consume), but scope analysis still allocates a local for `arguments`
// and the bytecode generator falls back to that signal so the
// arguments object IS materialized at runtime.
function shorthand_arguments() {
    return { arguments };
}

// Computed `[arguments]` is a real identifier reference inside the
// computed-key expression, so the function is marked might-need-arguments.
function computed_arguments_key() {
    return { [arguments]: 1 };
}

// Computed `[eval]` similarly.
function computed_eval_key() {
    return { [eval]: 1 };
}

// Binding-pattern non-computed key with name `arguments`. The key
// is a property name, not a reference; the alias `x` is the bound
// name. Should NOT mark might-need-arguments on its own.
function binding_pattern_arguments_key() {
    let { arguments: x } = { arguments: 1 };
    return x;
}

// Method named `arguments` is again a property-key context.
function method_named_arguments() {
    return { arguments() { return 1; } }.arguments();
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/AST/input/var-shadow-in-default-param.js
// A body `var` that shadows a name referenced in a default parameter
// expression must NOT be optimized to a local -- the default expression
// must resolve the name from the outer scope via the environment chain.
var shadow = "outer";
function shadow_in_default(x = shadow) {
    var shadow = "inner";
    return x;
}

// Body vars whose names are NOT referenced in any default parameter
// expression should still be optimized to locals.
function no_conflict(x = 1) {
    var y = 2;
    return y;
}

// A parameter that is also var-declared in the body (var a) keeps its
// argument slot -- the IsForbiddenLexical flag prevents the deopt.
function param_redeclared(a = 10) {
    var a;
    return a;
}

// Multiple defaults with shadowing -- both body vars should be deoptimized.
function multi_shadow(x = shadow, y = shadow) {
    var shadow = "inner";
    return x;
}

// A var that shadows something referenced in a *destructuring* default
// should also be deoptimized.
function destruct_shadow({ x } = shadow) {
    var shadow = {};
    return x;
}

// An arrow function inside a default expression captures through the
// environment; `shadow` in the arrow is in its own scope and propagates
// up as captured_by_nested_function, which already prevents locals.
function arrow_in_default(x = (() => shadow)()) {
    var shadow = "inner";
    return x;
}

// Body function declarations whose names are NOT referenced in any
// default parameter expression should remain locals.
function func_decl_no_conflict(x = 1) {
    var y = 42;
    function inner() { return y; }
    return inner();
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/AST/input/with-defeats-locals.js
// `with` makes identifiers ambiguous -- they might come from the
// with-object or from the enclosing scope.
function basic_with(obj) {
    let x = 1;
    with (obj) {
        x;
    }
}

// Variables declared INSIDE a with block are still local to the function.
function var_in_with(obj) {
    with (obj) {
        var y = 2;
    }
    return y;
}

// Nested function inside with inherits the ambiguity.
function nested_in_with(obj) {
    let z = 10;
    with (obj) {
        (function () {
            return z;
        });
    }
}

// with + eval: double poison.
function with_and_eval(obj) {
    let a = 1;
    with (obj) {
        eval("");
        a;
    }
}

    }
}

        }
    }
}

    }
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Bytecode/input/arguments-from-frame.js
function count(a, b) {
    return arguments.length;
}
function sloppy(a) {
    a = 1;
    let s = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < arguments.length; ++i) s += arguments[i];
    return s + arguments[0];
}
function strict(a) {
    "use strict";
    return arguments[0] + arguments.length;
}
function writesParameter(a) {
    "use strict";
    a = 1;
    return arguments[0];
}
function beforeArrow(a) {
    const count = arguments.length;
    return () => count;
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Bytecode/input/block-scoping.js
function closureOverBlockScope() {
    let fns = [];
    {
        let x = 1;
        fns.push(() => x);
    }
    {
        let y = 2;
        fns.push(() => y);
    }
    return fns[0]() + fns[1]();
}
console.log(closureOverBlockScope());

function breakThroughBlockScopes() {
    let result;
    outer: for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        {
            let x = i;
            let f = () => x;
            if (x > 1) {
                result = f;
                break outer;
            }
        }
    }
    return result();
}
console.log(breakThroughBlockScopes());

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Bytecode/input/catch-scope-boundary.js
function throwInCatch() {
    let result = "bad";
    try {
        throw 1;
    } catch (e) {
        try {
            throw 2;
        } catch (e2) {
            result = "good";
        }
    }
    return result;
}
console.log(throwInCatch());

function throwInCatchWithLocals() {
    let outerVar = "outer";
    try {
        throw "first";
    } catch (e) {
        let catchLocal = "local:" + e;
        try {
            throw "second";
        } catch (inner) {
            return outerVar + "," + catchLocal + "," + inner;
        }
    }
}
console.log(throwInCatchWithLocals());

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Bytecode/input/computed-destructuring-key-registers.js
function without_rest(source, key) {
    const { [key]: first, [key]: second, [key]: third, [key]: fourth } = source;
    return [first, second, third, fourth];
}

function with_rest(source, key) {
    const { [key]: first, [key]: second, ...rest } = source;
    return [first, second, rest];
}

without_rest({ value: 1 }, "value");
with_rest({ value: 1, other: 2 }, "value");

// after saving it), and that register free order is consistent across
// sequential statements.

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Bytecode/input/condition-dead-code-elim.js
function alive() {
    return "alive";
}
function dead() {
    return "dead";
}

function ternary_true() {
    return true ? 1 : dead();
}
function ternary_truthy() {
    return 1 ? 1 : dead();
}
function ternary_false() {
    return false ? dead() : 1;
}
function ternary_falsey() {
    return undefined ? dead() : 1;
}

function while_falsey() {
    while (false) {
        dead();
    }
    while (null) {
        dead();
    }
    while (undefined) {
        dead();
    }

    // ensure blocks after eliminated blocks run
    alive();
}
function do_while_falsey() {
    do {
        alive();
    } while (false);
    do {
        alive();
    } while (null);
    do {
        alive();
    } while (undefined);

    // ensure blocks after eliminated blocks run
    alive();
}

function if_falsely() {
    if (false) {
        dead();
    }
    if (null) {
        dead();
    }
    if (undefined) {
        dead();
    }

    // ensure blocks after eliminated blocks run
    alive();
}
function if_truthy() {
    if (true) {
        alive();
    } else {
        dead();
    }
    if ("abc") {
        alive();
    } else {
        dead();
    }
    if (123) {
        alive();
    } else {
        dead();
    }

    // ensure blocks after eliminated blocks run
    alive();
}
function if_exhausted() {
    if (false) {
        dead();
    } else if (false) {
        dead();
    } else {
        alive();
    }
    if (true) {
        alive();
    } else if (true) {
        dead();
    } else {
        dead();
    }

    // ensure blocks after eliminated blocks run
    alive();
}

function call_this() {
    return 1;
}

function for_false() {
    for (; false; ) {
        dead();
    }
    for (; null; ) {
        dead();
    }
    for (; undefined; ) {
        dead();
    }
    // ensure that `call_this()` is still called
    for (let x = call_this(); false; ) {
        dead();
    }

    // ensure blocks after eliminated blocks run
    alive();
}
function for_true(x) {
    // Block should not be optimized away here
    for (; true; ) {
        alive();
        if (x) break;
    }
    for (; 1; ) {
        alive();
        if (x) break;
    }

    // ensure blocks after eliminated blocks run
    alive();
}

ternary_true();
ternary_truthy();
ternary_false();
ternary_falsey();

while_falsey();
do_while_falsey();

if_falsely();
if_truthy();
if_exhausted();

for_false();
for_true(true);

    }

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Bytecode/input/indexed-append-guards.js
"use strict";

function expect_type_error(callback) {
    let did_throw = false;
    try {
        callback();
    } catch (error) {
        if (!(error instanceof TypeError))
            throw error;
        did_throw = true;
    }
    if (!did_throw)
        throw new Error("Expected TypeError");
}

let object = Object.preventExtensions({ 0: 1 });
expect_type_error(() => {
    object[1] = 2;
});
if (object[1] !== undefined)
    throw new Error("Indexed object append mutated");

let array = [1, 2];
Object.defineProperty(array, "length", { writable: false });
expect_type_error(() => {
    array[array.length] = 3;
});
if (array.length !== 2)
    throw new Error("Array length changed");
if (array[2] !== undefined)
    throw new Error("Array append mutated");

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Bytecode/input/int32-comparison-specializations.js
function comparison_results(value) {
    return [
        value < 2,
        value <= 2,
        value > 2,
        value >= 2,
        value === 2,
        value !== 2,
        value == 2,
        value != 2,
    ];
}

function comparison_jumps(value) {
    let result = 0;
    if (value < 2)
        result += 1;
    if (value <= 2)
        result += 2;
    if (value > 2)
        result += 4;
    if (value >= 2)
        result += 8;
    if (value === 2)
        result += 16;
    if (value !== 2)
        result += 32;
    if (value == 2)
        result += 64;
    if (value != 2)
        result += 128;
    return result;
}

comparison_jumps(1);

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Bytecode/input/lexical-env-teardown.js
// Tests that lexical environment teardown works correctly for
// all code paths: with, block scope, for-in/of, catch, and
// named function expressions.

// 1. with statement restores outer environment
function withTeardown() {
    let outer = 1;
    with ({ x: 10 }) {
        let inner = x + outer;
    }
    return outer;
}
console.log(withTeardown());

// 2. Block scope with let restores environment
function blockTeardown() {
    let outer = 2;
    {
        let inner = 3;
        outer;
    }
    return outer;
}
console.log(blockTeardown());

// 3. for-in with lexical binding restores environment
function forInTeardown() {
    let outer = 4;
    for (let k in { a: 1, b: 2 }) {
        k;
    }
    return outer;
}
console.log(forInTeardown());

// 4. for-of with lexical binding restores environment
function forOfTeardown() {
    let outer = 5;
    for (let v of [10, 20]) {
        v;
    }
    return outer;
}
console.log(forOfTeardown());

// 5. try-catch restores environment after catch scope
function catchTeardown() {
    let outer = 6;
    try {
        throw new Error("test");
    } catch (e) {
        e;
    }
    return outer;
}
console.log(catchTeardown());

// 6. Named function expression scope teardown
var namedFn = function myName() {
    return typeof myName;
};
console.log(namedFn());

function recover() {}

    } catch {

        } catch {

                work();
            } catch {
                try {
                    work();

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Bytecode/input/tdz-reset-in-loop.js
// A local that a TDZ check reads is emptied at the start of each iteration of the innermost
// loop around its scope. A local without such a check costs nothing.

function checked(list) {
    for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
        list[i](() => 0, typeof value);
        let value = i;
        let plain = value + 1;
        list[i](plain);
    }
}

function nested(list) {
    while (list.length) {
        {
            for (const item of list) item(typeof value);
            let value = list.pop();
        }
    }
}

checked([]);
nested([]);

    var x = 1;
    // Capture x to prevent local optimization.
    (function () {
        x;
    });
    return x;
}

function let_access() {
    let x = 1;
    // Capture x to prevent local optimization.
    (function () {
        x;
    });
    return x;
}

var_access();
let_access();

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/coverage.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
#
# Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
#

"""Reports which IR ops, speculations and exits the JIT's tests reach.

Runs with LIBJS_JIT=...,coverage=DIRECTORY write what the code they compiled contained (one key per node, like
"Int32Binary.Add" or "LoadElementAt.TypedArray(Int8)", and per place it can exit, like "exit-site.BadShape") and what
happened to it ("exit.Overflow", "stress-exit.BadShape", "osr-entry", "discard", ...) into that directory. This adds
them up and compares them with every op and kind there is, read from the compiler's source, so that new ops and exit
kinds show up as not covered until a test reaches them.

Usage: coverage.py DIRECTORY... [--json report.json] [--baseline report.json]
With --baseline, fails if a key the baseline covered is not covered anymore.
"""

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys

from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict
from typing import List

SOURCE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
JIT_SOURCE = SOURCE_DIR / "Libraries/LibJS/JIT/Rust/src"

# Keys that cannot be covered, with the reason.
IMPOSSIBLE = {
    "Int32Binary.Div": "Div is not an int32 operation",
    "Constant": "constants are in no block",
    "VirtualObject": "virtual objects are in no block",
    "exit.Leave": "leaves are not exits",
    "exit.LeaveMaterialized": "leaves are not exits",
    "stress-exit.Leave": "leaves are not exits",
    "stress-exit.LeaveMaterialized": "leaves are not exits",
    "exit-site.Leave": "leaves are not exits",
    "exit-site.LeaveMaterialized": "leaves are not exits",
    "stress-exit.NoFeedback": "unconditional exits are not forced",
    "exit.InlinedCall": "calls in inlined code are not exits",
    "exit-site.InlinedCall": "calls in inlined code are not exits",
    "stress-exit.InlinedCall": "calls in inlined code are not exits",
}


def enum_variants(path: Path, name: str) -> List[str]:
    """The variants of `pub enum name` in a Rust source file."""
    text = path.read_text()
    match = re.search(rf"pub enum {name} \{{\n(.*?)\n\}}", text, re.DOTALL)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError(f"No enum {name} in {path}")
    return re.findall(r"^    ([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)\b", match.group(1), re.MULTILINE)


def universe() -> Dict[str, List[str]]:
    """Every coverage key there is, by category."""
    ops = enum_variants(JIT_SOURCE / "ir/mod.rs", "Op")
    exit_kinds = enum_variants(JIT_SOURCE / "code.rs", "ExitKind")
    binary_ops = enum_variants(JIT_SOURCE / "ir/mod.rs", "BinaryOp")
    comparisons = enum_variants(JIT_SOURCE / "ir/mod.rs", "Comparison")
    typed_array_elements = enum_variants(JIT_SOURCE / "ir/mod.rs", "TypedArrayElement")
    elements_kinds = ["Packed", "Holey"] + [f"TypedArray({element})" for element in typed_array_elements]

    refined = {
        "Int32Binary": binary_ops,
        "Int32Compare": comparisons,
        "CheckElements": elements_kinds,
        "LoadElementAt": elements_kinds,
        "StoreElementAt": elements_kinds,
    }
    # NB: Other ops come in kinds too (Generic and CallSlowPath by opcode, Exit by exit kind, ...), but not all of
    #     their kinds are expected to be compiled, so only the op is.
    op_keys = []
    for op in ops:
        op_keys += [f"{op}.{kind}" for kind in refined[op]] if op in refined else [op]
    return {
        "ops": op_keys,
        "exit sites": [f"exit-site.{kind}" for kind in exit_kinds],
        "exits taken": [f"exit.{kind}" for kind in exit_kinds],
        "stress exits taken": [f"stress-exit.{kind}" for kind in exit_kinds],
        "branches": ["Branch.Bool", "Branch.Nullish", "Branch.Undefined", "Branch.TaggedEquals"]
        + [f"Branch.Int32.{comparison}" for comparison in comparisons],
        "events": [
            "compile",
            "discard",
            "refuse",
            "osr-entry",
            "stress-invalidate",
            "exit.from-inlined-code",
            "graph.loop",
            "graph.osr-entry",
        ]
        + [f"graph.inlined-depth.{depth}" for depth in range(1, 6)],
    }


def covered_keys(counts: Counter) -> Counter:
    """The counts, with the counts of refined keys also counted for their unrefined op (Generic.Call counts for
    Generic), so that ops covered in any kind count as covered."""
    result = Counter(counts)
    for key, count in counts.items():
        if "." in key and not key.startswith(("exit", "stress-exit", "graph", "compile-failure")):
            result[key.split(".", 1)[0]] += count
    return result


def load(directories: List[Path]) -> Counter:
    counts: Counter = Counter()
    for directory in directories:
        for path in directory.rglob("coverage-*.json"):
            try:
                counts.update(json.loads(path.read_text()))
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                print(f"Skipping unreadable {path}", file=sys.stderr)
    return counts


def report(counts: Counter) -> dict:
    counts = covered_keys(counts)
    categories = {}
    for category, keys in universe().items():
        possible = [key for key in keys if key not in IMPOSSIBLE]
        covered = [key for key in possible if counts.get(key)]
        categories[category] = {
            "covered": len(covered),
            "total": len(possible),
            "missing": [key for key in possible if not counts.get(key)],
        }
    others = sorted(key for key in counts if key.startswith(("Generic.", "CallSlowPath.", "compile-failure.")))
    return {
        "categories": categories,
        "generic and slow path opcodes": {key: counts[key] for key in others},
        "counts": dict(sorted(counts.items())),
    }


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("directories", type=Path, nargs="+")
    parser.add_argument("--json", type=Path, help="write the report as JSON")
    parser.add_argument("--baseline", type=Path, help="a report whose covered keys must stay covered")
    parser.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true", help="list the counts of every key")
    arguments = parser.parse_args()

    counts = load(arguments.directories)
    if not counts:
        print("No coverage files found")
        return 1
    result = report(counts)
    for category, data in result["categories"].items():
        percent = 100 * data["covered"] / max(data["total"], 1)
        print(f"{category}: {data['covered']}/{data['total']} ({percent:.0f}%)")
        if data["missing"]:
            print(f"  not covered: {', '.join(data['missing'])}")
    generic = [key for key in result["generic and slow path opcodes"] if key.startswith("Generic.")]
    print(f"opcodes compiled generically: {len(generic)}")
    if arguments.verbose:
        for key, count in result["counts"].items():
            print(f"  {key}: {count}")
    if arguments.json:
        arguments.json.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")

    if arguments.baseline:
        baseline = json.loads(arguments.baseline.read_text())
        lost = [key for key, count in baseline["counts"].items() if count and not result["counts"].get(key)]
        if lost:
            print(f"No longer covered: {', '.join(lost)}")
            return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/fuzz.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
#
# Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
#

"""Differential fuzzing of the JIT: random programs (generator.py) run in the interpreter and under JIT stress modes,
and every crash or difference in their output is a bug.

Each program runs in the interpreter and in a few of the modes, chosen by its number. Failures are saved in the output
directory with a command that reproduces them, reduced (reduce.py) and deduplicated by their crash signature or, for
output differences, by their reduced program. findings.md there lists one line per distinct failure.

The campaign pauses while the machine is needed idle (see machine.py). Program N of seed S is generator.py's program
S * 1000000 + N, so every failure reproduces from its number.
"""

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys
import threading
import time

from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from generator import generate  # noqa: E402
from machine import wait_until_machine_is_free  # noqa: E402
from modes import INTERPRETER  # noqa: E402
from modes import MODES_BY_NAME  # noqa: E402
from reduce import reduce_program  # noqa: E402
from reduce import run_program  # noqa: E402

SOURCE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
FUZZ_MODES = [
    "warm",
    "exits",
    "eager",
    "osr",
    "registers",
    "deep-inline",
    "random",
    "exits-always",
    "no-inline",
    "async",
    "invalidate",
]
IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r"\b(v|p|f)[0-9_]+\b")


class Campaign:
    def __init__(self, arguments):
        self.arguments = arguments
        self.js = arguments.build / "bin/js"
        self.out = arguments.out
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.signatures = {}
        self.counts = {"programs": 0, "runs": 0, "skipped": 0, "failures": 0, "distinct": 0}
        self.started = time.monotonic()
        findings = self.out / "findings.json"
        if findings.exists():
            self.signatures = json.loads(findings.read_text())
            self.counts["distinct"] = len(self.signatures)

    def modes_for(self, number: int):
        modes = self.arguments.modes
        count = min(self.arguments.modes_per_program, len(modes))
        return [MODES_BY_NAME[modes[(number * count + k) % len(modes)]] for k in range(count)]

    def run_one(self, number: int) -> None:
        wait_until_machine_is_free()
        seed = self.arguments.seed * 1000000 + number
        source = generate(seed)
        work = self.out / "work" / f"{seed}.js"
        work.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        work.write_text(source)
        expected = run_program(self.js, work, INTERPRETER, seed, self.arguments.timeout)
        with self.lock:
            self.counts["programs"] += 1
            self.counts["runs"] += 1
        if expected.timed_out or expected.crash_signature():
            with self.lock:
                self.counts["skipped"] += 1
            work.unlink()
            return
        for mode in self.modes_for(number):
            actual = run_program(self.js, work, mode, seed, self.arguments.timeout * 3)
            with self.lock:
                self.counts["runs"] += 1
            crash = actual.crash_signature()
            if crash:
                self.record_failure(seed, mode, source, f"crash: {crash}", actual.output)
            elif actual.timed_out:
                self.record_failure(seed, mode, source, "timeout", "")
            elif (actual.exit_code, actual.output) != (expected.exit_code, expected.output):
                self.record_failure(seed, mode, source, "mismatch", actual.output)
        work.unlink()

    def record_failure(self, seed: int, mode, source: str, signature: str, output: str) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            self.counts["failures"] += 1
            known = signature.startswith("crash") and signature in self.signatures
        directory = self.out / "failures" / f"{seed}-{mode.name}"
        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (directory / "program.js").write_text(source)
        # NB: Panics come first and the verifiers' dumps after them.
        (directory / "output.txt").write_text(
            output if len(output) < 40000 else output[:20000] + "\n...\n" + output[-20000:]
        )
        repro = (
            f"python3 {Path(__file__).parent / 'generator.py'} {seed} > p.js && "
            f"LIBJS_JIT={mode.environment_value(seed)} {self.js} --expose-jit-testing p.js"
        )
        (directory / "repro.txt").write_text(repro + "\n")
        if known:
            return
        reduced, reduced_signature = source, signature
        if self.arguments.reduce:
            reduced, reduced_signature = reduce_program(
                self.js, source, mode, seed, directory / "reduced.js", self.arguments.timeout, log=lambda _: None
            )
            if reduced_signature is None:
                reduced_signature = signature
        key = reduced_signature
        if not key.startswith("crash"):
            key = f"{reduced_signature}: {hashlib.sha1(IDENTIFIER.sub('x', reduced).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]}"
        with self.lock:
            if key in self.signatures:
                return
            self.signatures[key] = {
                "seed": seed,
                "mode": mode.name,
                "jit": mode.environment_value(seed),
                "directory": str(directory),
                "lines": len(reduced.splitlines()),
                "found": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
            }
            self.counts["distinct"] = len(self.signatures)
            (self.out / "findings.json").write_text(json.dumps(self.signatures, indent=2))
            with open(self.out / "findings.md", "a") as findings:
                findings.write(
                    f"- {key}: seed {seed}, mode {mode.name}, {len(reduced.splitlines())} lines, {directory}\n"
                )
            print(f"NEW {key} (seed {seed}, mode {mode.name}) in {directory}", flush=True)

    def report(self) -> None:
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - self.started
        with self.lock:
            counts = dict(self.counts)
        print(
            f"[{elapsed / 60:.1f} min] {counts['programs']} programs ({counts['programs'] / max(elapsed, 1):.1f}/s), "
            f"{counts['runs']} runs, {counts['skipped']} skipped, {counts['failures']} failures, "
            f"{counts['distinct']} distinct",
            flush=True,
        )


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--build", type=Path, default=SOURCE_DIR / "Build/release")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1, help="campaign seed")
    parser.add_argument("--start", type=int, default=0, help="number of the first program")
    parser.add_argument("--count", type=int, default=0, help="programs to run (default: until --seconds)")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=int, default=0, help="how long to run (default: until --count)")
    parser.add_argument("-j", "--jobs", type=int, default=4)
    parser.add_argument("--modes", default=",".join(FUZZ_MODES), help="modes to run programs in")
    parser.add_argument("--modes-per-program", type=int, default=3)
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=5.0, help="seconds for the interpreter run of a program")
    parser.add_argument("--no-reduce", dest="reduce", action="store_false", help="keep failures unreduced")
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=Path("/tmp/jit-fuzz"))
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    arguments.modes = arguments.modes.split(",")
    arguments.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    campaign = Campaign(arguments)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + arguments.seconds if arguments.seconds else None
    number = arguments.start
    last_report = time.monotonic()
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(arguments.jobs) as executor:
        pending = set()
        while True:
            done = deadline is not None and time.monotonic() > deadline
            done = done or (arguments.count and number >= arguments.start + arguments.count)
            while not done and len(pending) < arguments.jobs * 2:
                pending.add(executor.submit(campaign.run_one, number))
                number += 1
                done = arguments.count and number >= arguments.start + arguments.count
            if not pending:
                break
            finished, pending = concurrent.futures.wait(pending, timeout=5, return_when="FIRST_COMPLETED")
            for future in finished:
                future.result()
            if time.monotonic() - last_report > 60:
                campaign.report()
                last_report = time.monotonic()
            if done and not pending:
                break
    campaign.report()
    return 1 if campaign.signatures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/generator.py

"""A generator of random JavaScript programs for differential testing of the JIT.

The programs are made to give the JIT a hard time where it speculates: their functions warm up with arguments of stable
types and shapes, get compiled (by the tier-up thresholds, and at random points by jit.compile()), and then see other
types, other shapes, prototype changes, accessors, proxies, frozen objects, holes, callee changes and exceptions. They
call each other, so that the JIT inlines them, and loop, so that it enters them on the stack.

A program prints a running hash of everything its calls returned or threw, after each phase, and nothing else that
could differ between runs. The same program must print the same in the interpreter and in every JIT mode.

Every statement is on its own line and blocks close on lines of their own, so that the reducer can drop lines.
"""

import random

from typing import List

PRELUDE = """\
"use strict";
let __seed = SEED;
Math.random = () => {
    __seed = (__seed * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648;
    return __seed / 2147483648;
};
let __hash = 0;
function __describe(value, depth) {
    if (typeof value === "number") return Object.is(value, -0) ? "-0" : String(value);
    if (typeof value === "bigint") return value + "n";
    if (typeof value === "string") return JSON.stringify(value);
    if (typeof value === "symbol") return value.toString();
    if (typeof value === "function") return "function";
    if (value === null || value === undefined) return String(value);
    if (typeof value !== "object") return String(value);
    if (depth > 2) return "...";
    if (Array.isArray(value)) {
        let text = "[";
        for (let i = 0; i < value.length && i < 8; ++i) text += (i in value ? __describe(value[i], depth + 1) : "_") + ",";
        return text + "]";
    }
    let text = "{";
    let count = 0;
    for (const key in value) {
        if (++count > 8) break;
        text += key + ":" + __describe(value[key], depth + 1) + ",";
    }
    return text + "}";
}
function __record(value) {
    const text = __describe(value, 0);
    __hash = (Math.imul(__hash, 31) + text.length) | 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < text.length && i < 256; ++i) __hash = (Math.imul(__hash, 31) + text.charCodeAt(i)) | 0;
}
function __call(f) {
    try {
        __record(f());
    } catch (e) {
        __record("threw " + (e instanceof Error ? e.constructor.name + ": " + e.message : __describe(e, 0)));
    }
}
function __phase(name) {
    print(name + " " + __hash);
}
const __jit = typeof jit === "object" ? jit : { compile() {}, prepare() {}, discard() {} };
"""


class Context:
    """What the statements generated in one function can refer to."""

    def __init__(self, generator: "Generator", parameters: List[str], depth: int):
        self.generator = generator
        self.parameters = parameters
        self.locals: List[str] = []
        # NB: Loop counters are read but never assigned, so that every loop ends.
        self.counters: List[str] = []
        self.depth = depth
        self.loop_depth = 0

    def variables(self) -> List[str]:
        return self.parameters + self.locals + self.counters

    def assignable(self) -> List[str]:
        return self.parameters + self.locals


class Generator:
    def __init__(self, seed: int):
        self.random = random.Random(seed)
        self.seed = seed
        self.lines: List[str] = []
        self.functions: List[tuple] = []
        self.next_local = 0

    # Values -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def int_literal(self) -> str:
        r = self.random
        return str(r.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 31, 100, 255, 1000, -1, -7, 2147483647, -2147483648, 1073741824]))

    def double_literal(self) -> str:
        return self.random.choice(["0.5", "1.5", "-2.25", "0.1", "1e300", "-0", "NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity", "3.0"])

    def string_literal(self) -> str:
        return self.random.choice(['""', '"a"', '"abc"', '"12"', '" 7 "', '"x"', '"length"', '"0"', '"\\u00e9"'])

    def literal(self) -> str:
        r = self.random.random()
        if r < 0.45:
            return f"({self.int_literal()})"
        if r < 0.6:
            return f"({self.double_literal()})"
        if r < 0.75:
            return self.string_literal()
        return self.random.choice(["true", "false", "undefined", "null", "1n", "[]", "{}", "[1, 2]"])

    def shape_literal(self, context: Context) -> str:
        r = self.random
        properties = r.sample(["x", "y", "z", "w", "length", "0"], r.randint(1, 3))
        # NB: Values that are often plain operands give the JIT literals it can initialize from constants.
        parts = [f"{json_key(p)}: {self.property_value(context)}" for p in properties]
        extra = r.random()
        if extra < 0.1:
            parts.append(f"{json_key(properties[0])}: {self.property_value(context)}")
        elif extra < 0.2:
            parts.insert(0, f"...{self.receiver(context)}")
        elif extra < 0.25:
            parts.append(f"get g() {{ return {self.operand(context)}; }}")
        elif extra < 0.3:
            parts.append(f"[{self.string_literal()}]: {self.operand(context)}")
        elif extra < 0.33:
            parts.append("__proto__: shared")
        return "{ " + ", ".join(parts) + " }"

    def property_value(self, context: Context) -> str:
        return self.operand(context) if self.random.random() < 0.6 else self.expression(context, 1)

    # Expressions ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def operand(self, context: Context) -> str:
        variables = context.variables()
        if variables and self.random.random() < 0.75:
            return self.random.choice(variables)
        return self.literal()

    def expression(self, context: Context, depth: int = 0) -> str:
        r = self.random
        if depth > 2:
            return self.operand(context)
        choice = r.random()
        a = self.expression(context, depth + 1)
        if choice < 0.30:
            op = r.choice(["+", "-", "*", "/", "%", "&", "|", "^", "<<", ">>", ">>>", "**"])
            return f"({a} {op} {self.expression(context, depth + 1)})"
        if choice < 0.42:
            op = r.choice(["<", "<=", ">", ">=", "==", "!=", "===", "!=="])
            return f"({a} {op} {self.expression(context, depth + 1)})"
        if choice < 0.47:
            return f"({r.choice(['-', '+', '~', '!', 'typeof '])}{a})"
        if choice < 0.52:
            return f"({a} | 0)"
        if choice < 0.60:
            return f"{self.receiver(context)}.{r.choice(['x', 'y', 'z', 'length', 'w'])}"
        if choice < 0.66:
            return f"{self.receiver(context)}[{self.index(context)}]"
        if choice < 0.74 and self.functions and context.loop_depth == 0:
            return self.call(context, depth)
        if choice < 0.77:
            return f"({a} ? {self.expression(context, depth + 1)} : {self.expression(context, depth + 1)})"
        if choice < 0.80:
            return f"({a} ?? {self.expression(context, depth + 1)})"
        if choice < 0.83:
            return f"`${{{a}}}-${{{self.expression(context, depth + 1)}}}`"
        if choice < 0.86:
            kind = r.choice(["number", "string", "object", "undefined"])
            return f'(typeof {a} === "{kind}")'
        if choice < 0.88:
            return f"({self.string_literal()} in Object({a}))"
        if choice < 0.90:
            return f"({a} instanceof {r.choice(['Object', 'Array', 'Shape0', 'Number'])})"
        if choice < 0.92:
            return f"String({a}).length"
        if choice < 0.94:
            return (
                f"Math.{r.choice(['max', 'min', 'imul', 'floor', 'abs'])}({a}, {self.expression(context, depth + 1)})"
            )
        if choice < 0.96:
            return f"[{a}, {self.expression(context, depth + 1)}]"
        return r.choice(
            [
                f"String({a}).charCodeAt({self.index(context)})",
                f"String({a}).slice(1)",
                f"[1, , {a}][{self.index(context)}]",
                f"{self.receiver(context)}?.x",
                f"Object.keys(Object({a})).length",
                f"(({a}) instanceof Shape1 ? 1 : 2)",
                f'(typeof {a} === "object" && {a} !== null ? {a}.method?.() : {a})',
                f"Number({a})",
                f"({a}, {self.expression(context, depth + 1)})",
                f"{a}?.length",
                a,
            ]
        )

    def receiver(self, context: Context) -> str:
        r = self.random
        variables = context.variables()
        if variables and r.random() < 0.8:
            return r.choice(variables)
        return r.choice(["globalObject", "globalArray", "shared"])

    def index(self, context: Context) -> str:
        r = self.random
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.5:
            return str(r.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 0, 1]))
        if choice < 0.7 and context.variables():
            return f"({r.choice(context.variables())} & 3)"
        if choice < 0.8:
            return self.random.choice(["-1", "100", "1.5", '"1"', '"x"', "i"]) if context.loop_depth else "-1"
        return self.operand(context)

    def call(self, context: Context, depth: int) -> str:
        r = self.random
        name, arity = r.choice(self.functions)
        arguments = [
            self.expression(context, depth + 1) for _ in range(r.choice([arity, arity, arity, arity - 1, arity + 1]))
        ]
        style = r.random()
        if style < 0.7:
            return f"{name}({', '.join(arguments)})"
        if style < 0.8:
            return f"{name}.call({self.operand(context)}, {', '.join(arguments)})"
        if style < 0.9:
            return f"{name}.apply(undefined, [{', '.join(arguments)}])"
        return f"{name}(...[{', '.join(arguments)}])"

    # Statements -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def new_local(self, context: Context) -> str:
        name = f"v{self.next_local}"
        self.next_local += 1
        context.locals.append(name)
        return name

    def statements(self, context: Context, count: int, indent: str) -> None:
        for _ in range(count):
            self.statement(context, indent)

    def statement(self, context: Context, indent: str) -> None:
        r = self.random
        emit = self.lines.append
        variables = context.variables()
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.18 or not variables:
            value = self.expression(context)
            emit(f"{indent}let {self.new_local(context)} = {value};")
        elif choice < 0.33 and context.assignable():
            emit(f"{indent}{r.choice(context.assignable())} = {self.expression(context)};")
        elif choice < 0.40 and context.assignable():
            op = r.choice(["+=", "-=", "*=", "|=", "&=", "<<=", "++", "--"])
            target = r.choice(context.assignable())
            emit(
                f"{indent}{target}{op};" if op in ("++", "--") else f"{indent}{target} {op} {self.expression(context)};"
            )
        elif choice < 0.48:
            receiver = self.receiver(context)
            emit(
                f'{indent}if ({receiver} !== null && typeof {receiver} === "object") {receiver}.{r.choice(["x", "y", "z", "w"])} = {self.expression(context)};'
            )
        elif choice < 0.53:
            receiver = self.receiver(context)
            emit(
                f"{indent}if (Array.isArray({receiver})) {receiver}[{self.index(context)}] = {self.expression(context)};"
            )
        elif choice < 0.58:
            value = self.shape_literal(context)
            emit(f"{indent}let {self.new_local(context)} = {value};")
        elif choice < 0.61:
            value = f"new Shape{r.randint(0, 1)}({self.expression(context)}, {self.expression(context)})"
            emit(f"{indent}let {self.new_local(context)} = {value};")
        elif choice < 0.64:
            value = f"[{', '.join(self.expression(context, 1) for _ in range(r.randint(0, 4)))}]"
            emit(f"{indent}let {self.new_local(context)} = {value};")
        elif choice < 0.72 and context.depth < 3:
            emit(f"{indent}if ({self.expression(context)}) {{")
            context.depth += 1
            saved = list(context.locals)
            self.statements(context, r.randint(1, 3), indent + "    ")
            context.locals = list(saved)
            if r.random() < 0.5:
                emit(f"{indent}}} else {{")
                self.statements(context, r.randint(1, 3), indent + "    ")
                context.locals = saved
            context.depth -= 1
            emit(f"{indent}}}")
        elif choice < 0.79 and context.depth < 3 and context.loop_depth < 2:
            counter = "i" if context.loop_depth == 0 else "j"
            emit(f"{indent}for (let {counter} = 0; {counter} < {r.choice([2, 3, 5, 8])}; ++{counter}) {{")
            context.loop_depth += 1
            context.depth += 1
            saved = list(context.locals)
            context.counters.append(counter)
            self.statements(context, r.randint(1, 4), indent + "    ")
            context.counters.pop()
            context.locals = saved
            context.depth -= 1
            context.loop_depth -= 1
            emit(f"{indent}}}")
        elif choice < 0.84 and context.depth < 3:
            emit(f"{indent}try {{")
            context.depth += 1
            saved = list(context.locals)
            self.statements(context, r.randint(1, 3), indent + "    ")
            if r.random() < 0.4:
                emit(
                    f'{indent}    if ({self.expression(context)}) throw new RangeError("thrown " + {self.operand(context)});'
                )
            context.locals = saved
            emit(f"{indent}}} catch (e) {{")
            emit(f"{indent}    __record(e instanceof Error ? e.message : e);")
            if r.random() < 0.3:
                emit(f"{indent}}} finally {{")
                emit(f"{indent}    __record({self.operand(context)});")
            context.depth -= 1
            emit(f"{indent}}}")
        elif choice < 0.88 and self.functions and context.loop_depth == 0:
            emit(f"{indent}__record({self.call(context, 0)});")
        elif choice < 0.90:
            emit(f"{indent}__record({self.expression(context)});")
        elif choice < 0.92:
            emit(f'{indent}if ({self.expression(context)}) throw new TypeError("bail " + {self.operand(context)});')
        elif choice < 0.94:
            body = f"p {r.choice(['+', '*', '-'])} {self.operand(context)}"
            argument = self.expression(context)
            name = self.new_local(context)
            emit(f"{indent}let {name} = (p) => {body};")
            emit(f"{indent}__record({name}({argument}));")
        elif choice < 0.96:
            emit(
                f"{indent}for (const element of [{self.operand(context)}, {self.operand(context)}]) __record(typeof element);"
            )
        elif choice < 0.97:
            emit(f"{indent}__record(arguments.length + {self.int_literal()});")
        elif choice < 0.975 and context.assignable():
            a, b = r.choice(context.assignable()), r.choice(context.assignable())
            emit(f"{indent}[{a}, {b}] = [{b}, {a}];")
        elif choice < 0.98:
            receiver = self.receiver(context)
            emit(f"{indent}for (const key in Object({receiver})) __record(key);")
        else:
            receiver = self.receiver(context)
            emit(
                f'{indent}if ({receiver} !== null && typeof {receiver} === "object") delete {receiver}.{r.choice(["x", "y", "z"])};'
            )

    def function(self, index: int) -> None:
        r = self.random
        arity = r.randint(1, 3)
        parameters = [f"p{index}_{k}" for k in range(arity)]
        name = f"f{index}"
        self.lines.append(f"function {name}({', '.join(parameters)}) {{")
        context = Context(self, parameters, 0)
        # NB: Small functions get inlined into their callers.
        self.statements(context, r.randint(0, 2) if r.random() < 0.5 else r.randint(3, 10), "    ")
        self.lines.append(f"    return {self.expression(context)};")
        self.lines.append("}")
        self.functions.append((name, arity))

    # Values that warm up functions with stable types, and those that come later ------------------------------

    STABLE_ARGUMENTS = [
        "i",
        "i * 2 + 1",
        "(i & 7) - 3",
        "i + 0.5",
        '"s" + (i & 3)',
        "objects[i & 1]",
        "arrays[i & 1]",
        "i & 1 ? 3 : 4",
        "new Shape0(i, i + 1)",
    ]

    LATER_ARGUMENTS = [
        "2147483647",
        "-2147483648",
        "-0",
        "NaN",
        "1.5",
        '"7"',
        '"abc"',
        "undefined",
        "null",
        "true",
        "3n",
        "Symbol.iterator",
        "[1, , 3]",
        '[1.5, "two"]',
        "{ y: 1, x: 2 }",
        "Object.create({ x: 5 })",
        "Object.freeze({ x: 1, y: 2 })",
        "new Proxy({ x: 1 }, {})",
        "{ get x() { return 9; }, y: 1 }",
        "{ valueOf() { return 4; } }",
        '{ valueOf() { throw new Error("valueOf"); } }',
        "new Shape1(1, 2)",
        "new Int32Array([1, 2, 3])",
        "new Float64Array([0.5, NaN])",
        '""',
        "function () {}",
    ]

    PERTURBATIONS = [
        'Object.defineProperty(Shape0.prototype, "z", { get() { return 42; }, configurable: true });',
        "Shape0.prototype.method = function () { return -1; };",
        "Object.setPrototypeOf(objects[0], { x: 100, w: 3 });",
        'objects[1] = { w: 1, x: "string", y: 2.5 };',
        "arrays[0][10] = 1;",
        'arrays[1].push("tail");',
        "Object.freeze(arrays[1]);",
        "Object.freeze(objects[0]);",
        "delete globalObject.x;",
        "globalObject.x = 1.5;",
        "globalArray.length = 0;",
        'Array.prototype[1] = "from Array.prototype";',
        'Object.prototype.y = "from Object.prototype";',
        "shared.x = { nested: true };",
        "objects[0] = new Proxy(objects[0], {});",
    ]

    def program(self) -> str:
        r = self.random
        self.lines = [PRELUDE.replace("SEED", str(r.randint(1, 1 << 30)))]
        emit = self.lines.append
        emit("class Shape0 {")
        emit("    constructor(a, b) {")
        emit("        this.x = a;")
        emit("        this.y = b;")
        emit("    }")
        emit("    method() {")
        emit("        return this.x;")
        emit("    }")
        emit("}")
        emit("class Shape1 extends Shape0 {")
        emit("    constructor(a, b) {")
        emit("        super(b, a);")
        emit("        this.z = a;")
        emit("    }")
        emit("}")
        emit("const objects = [{ x: 1, y: 2 }, { x: 3, y: 4 }];")
        emit("const arrays = [[1, 2, 3, 4], [5, 6, 7, 8]];")
        emit("const globalObject = { x: 1, y: 2, z: 3 };")
        emit("const globalArray = [1, 2, 3];")
        emit("const shared = new Shape0(1, 2);")
        function_count = r.randint(2, 6)
        for index in range(function_count):
            self.function(index)

        def call_line(index: int, arguments_pool: List[str], indent: str) -> str:
            name, arity = self.functions[index]
            arguments = ", ".join(r.choice(arguments_pool) for _ in range(arity))
            return f"{indent}__call(() => {name}({arguments}));"

        warm_iterations = r.choice([5, 20, 50, 100])
        for phase in range(r.randint(2, 4)):
            emit(f"for (let i = 0; i < {warm_iterations}; ++i) {{")
            for index in range(function_count):
                if r.random() < 0.8:
                    emit(call_line(index, self.STABLE_ARGUMENTS[: r.randint(1, len(self.STABLE_ARGUMENTS))], "    "))
            emit("}")
            for index in range(function_count):
                if r.random() < 0.3:
                    emit(f"__jit.compile(f{index});")
            emit(f'__phase("warm {phase}");')
            for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
                if r.random() < 0.6:
                    emit(f"try {{ {r.choice(self.PERTURBATIONS)} }} catch (e) {{ __record(e.message); }}")
            if r.random() < 0.2:
                index = r.randrange(function_count)
                name, arity = self.functions[index]
                emit(f"f{index} = function (...rest) {{ return rest.length; }};")
            # NB: The stable arguments use the loop variable, which the calls after the loop need too.
            emit(f"{{ let i = {r.randrange(warm_iterations)};")
            for _ in range(r.randint(2, 8)):
                emit(call_line(r.randrange(function_count), self.LATER_ARGUMENTS + self.STABLE_ARGUMENTS, "    "))
            emit("}")
            emit(f'__phase("changed {phase}");')
        emit("delete Array.prototype[1];")
        emit("delete Object.prototype.y;")
        return "\n".join(self.lines) + "\n"


def json_key(key: str) -> str:
    return key if key.isidentifier() else f'"{key}"'


def generate(seed: int) -> str:
    return Generator(seed).program()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys

    print(generate(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1), end="")

// Once %Array.prototype%[@@iterator] was replaced, the realm's arrays may be iterated observably for good, and for-of
// loops over them take the slow path of GetIterator, which calls the iterator method.

const values = Array.prototype.values;
let iteratorMethodCalls = 0;
Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator] = function () {
    ++iteratorMethodCalls;
    return values.call(this);
};

function sum(array) {
    let total = 0;
    for (const value of array) total += value;
    return total;
}

// Array length uses receiver feedback and guards, with no fallback call.
// In a pure scan this lets the length and the target property leave the loop.

function lengthOf(array) {
    return array.length;
}
function find(array, target) {
    for (let i = 0; i < array.length; ++i) {
        if (array[i].pos == target.pos) return array[i];
    }
    return false;
}

}

// An async function runs from its start into its body, which has no initial suspension. It suspends at an await in
// compiled code like the interpreter's Await: it writes the slots live at the continuation to its frame, records the
// continuation and that the value is awaited, and returns the value. It resumes at an entry block of the continuation,

// Bitwise operations on booleans, like `(a < b) & (c < d)` and `(a < b) | 0` in asm.js code, take the booleans as the
// int32 values 0 and 1 instead of calling the generic operation.

function bothLess(a, b, c, d) {
    a = +a;
    b = +b;
    c = +c;
    d = +d;
    return ((a < b) & (c < d)) ^ true ^ ((a > d) | 0) ^ ~(b > c);
}

// OPTIONS: stress-osr
// Bounds checks of indices that a counted loop's induction variable keeps within the count go away. The counter that
// an on-stack replacement entry brings is checked against the loop's bound once where it enters instead.

const heap = new Int32Array(4096);
function fill(value) {

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/catch-entries.js
// An exception thrown in compiled code leaves it, and the interpreter runs the Catch of the handler, which continues
// the frame in compiled code at an entry block after it. The entry loads the slots live there from the frame, like the
// resume entry of a generator, and jumps to the block that continues the handler. A handler that never caught an
// exception gets no entry, and its blocks are not built.

function thrower(x) {
    if (x & 1) throw x;
    return x;
}

function sum(n) {
    let total = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        try {
            total += thrower(i);
        } catch (e) {
            total -= e;
        }
        try {
            total += thrower(0);
        } catch (e) {
            total -= e;
        }
    }
    return total;
}
jit.prepare(sum);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) sum(10);
jit.compile(sum);

// CHECK-FUNCTION: sum
// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK: {{^}}b0:
// CHECK: {{^}}[[ENTRY:b[0-9]+]]:{{$}}
// CHECK-NEXT: LoadSlot
// CHECK: Jump [[HANDLER:b[0-9]+]]
// CHECK: {{^}}[[HANDLER]] (pc [[PC:[0-9]+]]) <- [[ENTRY]]:
// CHECK-NEXT: CheckInt32
// CHECK: Int32Sub
// CHECK: osr entry at pc [[PC]]: [[ENTRY]]
// CHECK-COUNT-1: osr entry at pc
// CHECK-COUNT-1: Int32Sub

console.log(sum(100));

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/check-elimination-branch-outcomes.js
// A branch on values alone, like a comparison, goes the way a branch on the same values went before, where only one
// edge of that branch leads, and becomes a jump there.

function nested(a, b) {
    if (a < b) {
        if (a < b) return 1;
        return 2;
    }
    if (a < b) return 3;
    return 4;
}
jit.prepare(nested);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) nested(i, 5);
jit.compile(nested);

// CHECK-FUNCTION: nested
// CHECK-PASS: check elimination
// CHECK-COUNT-1: BranchBool
// CHECK: Return (#4)
// CHECK: Return (#1)

// Where both edges meet again, neither outcome is known.

function merged(a, b, c) {
    let s = 0;
    if (a < b) s = c;
    if (a < b) s = (s + 1) | 0;
    return s;
}
jit.prepare(merged);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) merged(i, 5, 7);
jit.compile(merged);

// CHECK-FUNCTION: merged
// CHECK-PASS: check elimination
// CHECK-COUNT-2: BranchBool

console.log(nested(1, 2), nested(2, 1), merged(1, 2, 3), merged(2, 1, 3));

function total(object, count) {

        if (i > 0) {

// A closure of a sloppy function, arrow functions included, which shows its frames as the legacy caller of the
// functions they call, is allocated when an inlined call of it calls a function without the frames of inlined calls.

function callee() {
    return 1;
}

    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++)
        sum += apply(function (x) {
            return callee() + x;
        }, i);
    return sum;
}
function sloppyArrowCaller(n) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) sum += apply(x => callee() + x, i);
    return sum;
}
function strictCaller(n) {
    "use strict";
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) sum += apply(x => callee() + x, i);
    return sum;
}

    sloppyCaller(10);
    sloppyArrowCaller(10);
    strictCaller(10);
}

jit.compile(strictCaller);

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/dead-code-after-refinement-removal.js
// REQUIRES: inline-allocation
//
// The multiplication's check of value is the last user of the frame state that refers to the object escape analysis
// removed, and so of the phi of its property. Only the value numbering after loop invariant code motion merges it with
// the check hoisted out of the loop, which leaves the phi unused. It must not stay in a register across the call.

function phiOfVirtualObjectProperty(flag, value) {
    let number = 1;
    for (let i = 0; i < 4; ++i) number = value;
    const object = { a: 1 };

    object.b = value * number;
    return flag / flag;
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/exit-unboxing.js
// Frame states take int32 values unboxed where only exits read their boxings, so that the boxings go away. The builder
// boxes the sum for the loop phi it flows into, and once representation selection unboxes the phi, only the exit of

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/generators.js
// A generator suspends in compiled code like the interpreter's Yield: it writes the slots live at the continuation to
// its frame, records the continuation, and returns the value. It resumes at an entry block of the continuation, which
// loads those slots from the frame like an on-stack replacement entry, and reads the completion it resumed with from

function* counter(limit) {

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/global-constants.js
// A property of the global object that holds an object, such as a function a script declares or a `var` initializes,
// is a constant while it is never assigned, on which the code depends: calling it needs no lookup. One that was
// assigned is loaded from the global object and checked for the object it held.

function add(a, b) {
    return a + b;
}
var subtract = function (a, b) {
    return a - b;
};
function replaced(a) {
    return a;
}
replaced = function (a) {
    return a + 1;
};

function sum(n) {
    let s = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) s = add(i, s) + subtract(1, 1) + replaced(0);
    return s;
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/hole-filling-stores.js
// Stores into holes of holey arrays fill them inline where the array can get
// a new element without running any code. Stores that need more storage, and
// stores to the last index, which may make the elements packed, call the
// runtime in cold blocks, which runs no code for such arrays either. Holes of
// other objects exit, so no path through the store runs other code.

function fill(n) {
    const a = new Array(n);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) a[i] = i;
    return a;
}
jit.prepare(fill);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) fill(20);

// REQUIRES: inline-allocation
// Inlined callees keep their arguments objects virtual: forwarding them with apply inlines the call with the values
// the inlined call passed, and their length and constant indices are those values.

const Class = {
    create() {
        return function () {
            this.initialize.apply(this, arguments);
        };
    },
};
const Point = Class.create();
Point.prototype = {
    initialize(x, y) {
        this.x = x;
        this.y = y;
    },
};

Color.prototype = {
    initialize(r, g, b) {
        this.r = r;
        this.g = g;
        this.b = b;
    },
};
function second() {
    return arguments.length + arguments[1];
}
function make(i) {
    return new Point(i, 2).x + second(i, 3);
}

for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
    new Color(1, 2, 3);
    make(i);
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/inlined-exception-handlers.js
// Callees with exception handlers, like the handler that closes the iterator of a for-of loop, are inlined if none of
// their handlers caught an exception before the compile. Their handlers get no blocks. Callees whose handler caught
// stay calls.

class Writer {
    constructor() {
        this.values = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0];
        this.position = 0;
    }
    write(list) {
        for (const value of list) this.values[this.position++] = value;
    }
}
function writeAll(writer, list) {
    writer.position = 0;
    writer.write(list);
    return writer.position;
}
const writer = new Writer();
jit.prepare(Writer.prototype.write);
jit.prepare(writeAll);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) writeAll(writer, [1, 2, 3]);
jit.compile(writeAll);

// reads them, like stores to an Int32Array, they become wrapping int32 arithmetic: doubles hold such sums exactly.

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/int32-number-round-trips.js
// Number checks of boxed int32 values, which representation selection leaves where an int32 phi meets a user of
// numbers (like a store to an Int32Array), become conversions, which then cancel out with the conversion back.

const heap = new Int32Array(64);
function storeEither(a, b) {
    a = a | 0;
    b = b | 0;
    let x = 0;
    if ((a | 0) > (b | 0)) x = (a - b) | 0;
    else x = (b + 1) | 0;
    heap[a & 15] = x;
    return 0;
}
jit.prepare(storeEither);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) storeEither(i, 3);
jit.compile(storeEither);

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/interrupt-checks.js
// Every loop checks for interrupts where it jumps back, and keeps the check in the loop. Loops that count to an end lose
// theirs if they have a loop around them to stop at, or end soon by themselves.

function untilZero(object) {
    while (object.value !== 0) object.value = object.next;
}
function counts(object, count) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) sum = (sum + object.value) | 0;
    return sum;
}
function wraps(object) {
    let i = 0;
    while (object.value-- > 0) i = (i + 2) | 0;
    return i;
}
function short(object) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 4000; ++i) sum = (sum + object.value) | 0;
    return sum;
}
function notShort(object) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 6000; ++i) sum = (sum + object.value) | 0;
    return sum;
}
function nested(count) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        for (let j = 0; j < 10; ++j) sum = (sum + j) | 0;
    }
    return sum;
}

jit.prepare(untilZero);
jit.prepare(counts);
jit.prepare(wraps);
jit.prepare(short);
jit.prepare(notShort);
jit.prepare(nested);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
    untilZero({ value: 1, next: 0 });
    counts({ value: i }, 10);
    wraps({ value: 2 });
    short({ value: i });
    notShort({ value: i });
    nested(2);
}
jit.compile(untilZero);
jit.compile(counts);
jit.compile(wraps);
jit.compile(short);
jit.compile(notShort);
jit.compile(nested);

// CHECK-FUNCTION: untilZero
// CHECK-PASS: loop invariant code motion
// CHECK: loop:
// CHECK: CheckInterrupt
// CHECK-PASS: interrupt check elimination
// CHECK: CheckInterrupt

// CHECK-FUNCTION: counts
// CHECK-PASS: interrupt check elimination
// CHECK: CheckInterrupt

// CHECK-FUNCTION: short
// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK: CheckInterrupt
// CHECK-PASS: interrupt check elimination
// CHECK-COUNT-0: CheckInterrupt

// CHECK-FUNCTION: notShort
// CHECK-PASS: interrupt check elimination
// CHECK: CheckInterrupt

// CHECK-FUNCTION: wraps
// CHECK-PASS: interrupt check elimination
// CHECK: CheckInterrupt

// CHECK-FUNCTION: nested
// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK-COUNT-2: CheckInterrupt
// CHECK-PASS: interrupt check elimination
// CHECK-COUNT-1: CheckInterrupt

// access know. Other concatenations make rope strings.

// CHECK-PASS: branch fusion
// CHECK: [[KEY:v[0-9]+]] = ConcatenateStrings
// CHECK-PASS: key strings
// CHECK-NOT: ConcatenateStrings
// CHECK: [[KEY]] = ConcatenateKeyStrings
// CHECK: ProbeKeyedCache

// The key is a local variable that a loop assigns, and the store and the `in` take it too.
function count(object, names) {
    let key = "";
    let found = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < names.length; ++i) {
        key = "data-" + names[i];
        if (key in object) ++found;
        object[key] = i;
    }
    return found;
}

// A string that a loop puts together is a key once, and its pieces are rope strings.
function lookUp(object, names) {
    let path = "";
    for (let i = 0; i < names.length; ++i) path = path + names[i];
    return object[path];
}
jit.prepare(lookUp);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) lookUp({}, ["first_piece", "second_piece", "third_piece"]);
jit.compile(lookUp);

// CHECK-FUNCTION: lookUp
// CHECK-PASS: key strings
// CHECK-COUNT-1: = ConcatenateStrings
// CHECK-COUNT-0: ConcatenateKeyStrings

// The same goes for a loop that has more than one way out.
function lookUpUntil(object, names, last) {
    let path = "";
    for (let i = 0; i < names.length; ++i) {
        path = path + names[i];
        if (i === last) break;
    }
    return object[path];
}
jit.prepare(lookUpUntil);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) lookUpUntil({}, ["first_piece", "second_piece", "third_piece"], i & 1 ? 1 : 5);
jit.compile(lookUpUntil);

// CHECK-FUNCTION: lookUpUntil
// CHECK-PASS: key strings
// CHECK-COUNT-1: = ConcatenateStrings
// CHECK-COUNT-0: ConcatenateKeyStrings

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/keyed-access.js
// Keyed accesses are made of small nodes: a check of the elements kind,
// the element counts, bounds checks against them, the load or store, and
// for holey elements a check for a hole. Sites that speculation does not
// cover branch on the elements kinds and keys their feedback saw, and take
// the slow path, in cold blocks, for anything else.

function sum(a) {
    let s = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i <= a.length; i++) {
        const v = a[i];
        if (v !== undefined) s += v;
    }
    return s;
}
jit.prepare(sum);

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/legacy-arguments-eligibility.js
// Calls in inlined functions with legacy arguments properties may run code that reads the function's arguments through
// them. Objects among them that the code never allocated stay unallocated: the runtime creates them for code that reads
// them, and the code exits after the call (AssumeValid). Where code read them before, recompiles allocate them there.

function opaque(read) {
    // A debugger statement keeps this function from being inlined.
    debugger;
    if (read) return ordinary.arguments[0].x;
}
const arrow = object => {
    opaque(false);
    return object.x;
};
const holder = {
    method(object) {
        opaque(false);
        return object.x;
    },
};
function ordinary(object, read) {
    opaque(read);
    return object.x;
}
function throughArrow(x) {
    return arrow({ x });
}
function throughMethod(x) {
    return holder.method({ x });
}
function throughOrdinary(x) {
    return ordinary({ x }, false);
}
function throughOrdinaryAfterRead(x, read) {
    return ordinary({ x }, read);
}
for (const fn of [
    opaque,
    arrow,
    holder.method,
    ordinary,
    throughArrow,
    throughMethod,
    throughOrdinary,
    throughOrdinaryAfterRead,
])
    jit.prepare(fn);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
    throughArrow(i);
    throughMethod(i);
    throughOrdinary(i);
    throughOrdinaryAfterRead(i, false);
}
jit.compile(throughArrow);
jit.compile(throughMethod);
jit.compile(throughOrdinary);
jit.compile(throughOrdinaryAfterRead);
throughOrdinaryAfterRead(1, true);
jit.compile(throughOrdinaryAfterRead);

// CHECK-FUNCTION: throughArrow
// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK: AllocateObject
// CHECK-NOT: AssumeLegacyArgumentsUnread
// CHECK-PASS: escape analysis
// CHECK-NOT: AllocateObject

// CHECK-FUNCTION: throughMethod
// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK: AllocateObject
// CHECK-NOT: AssumeLegacyArgumentsUnread
// CHECK-PASS: escape analysis
// CHECK-NOT: AllocateObject

// CHECK-FUNCTION: throughOrdinary
// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK: AllocateObject
// CHECK: CallDirect
// CHECK-NEXT: AssumeLegacyArgumentsUnread
// CHECK-PASS: escape analysis
// CHECK-NOT: AllocateObject
// CHECK: CallDirect
// CHECK-NEXT: AssumeValid

// CHECK-FUNCTION: throughOrdinaryAfterRead
// CHECK-PASS: escape analysis
// CHECK: AllocateObject
// CHECK: CallDirect

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/licm-osr-entries.js
// OPTIONS: stress-osr
// Loops with their test at the bottom are entered at their header by on-stack replacement entries too, and loop
// invariant code motion merges the entries in a preheader, here hoisting the check of the loop bound. Checks every
// iteration runs, like the lookup of the inlined callee, move there as well.

// NB: The callee is assigned after its variable held another value, so that the loop looks it up rather than
