FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/licm-runtime-helper-calls.js
// Calls of runtime helpers that run no code, like ToBoolean for the truthiness
// of a value that may be an object, write only what they say they do, so loads
// they do not write move out of loops around them.

function weighNodes(node, object) {
    let total = 0;
    for (; node; node = node.next) total = (total + object.weight) | 0;
    return total;
}
jit.prepare(weighNodes);

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/licm-speculative-hoists.js
// Checks in blocks that not every iteration runs move out of the loop too, speculatively. One that fails there exits
// with its own reason, Hoisted, so the code compiled next keeps such checks in the loop, and still moves those that
// every iteration runs.

function sum(object, other, n) {
    let total = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        total = (total + object.x) | 0;
        if (i === 7) total = (total + other.y) | 0;
    }
    return total;
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/licm-trivial-header-phis.js
// OPTIONS: stress-osr
// Where an on-stack replacement entry also enters an inner loop, loop invariant code motion merges the entries in a
// preheader, after which the header phis of values the inner loop leaves as they are take only what the preheader
// brings. They go away, so that what the inner loop computes from them moves to the preheader.

const heap = new Int32Array(4096);
function fill(value) {
    value = value | 0;
    for (let row = 0; row < 4; row = (row + 1) | 0) {
        for (let column = 0; column < 16; column = (column + 1) | 0) heap[((row << 6) + (column << 2)) >> 2] = value;
    }
}
jit.prepare(fill);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) fill(i);
jit.compile(fill);

// CHECK-FUNCTION: fill
// CHECK-PASS: loop invariant code motion
// CHECK: Int32LeftShift ({{v[0-9]+}}, #i32:6)
// CHECK: loop:
// CHECK-NOT: #i32:6
// CHECK: StoreElementAt

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/loop-rotation.js
// OPTIONS: stress-osr
// An on-stack replacement entry at the test at the bottom of a loop that reads the bound from a property runs the
// test's branch itself and enters the loop's body, while the code before the loop enters it at the test. Loop rotation
// copies the test for the way in from before the loop, so that the body becomes the loop's only entry, and loop
// invariant code motion moves the loads of `this` out of it.

function Holder(values) {
    this.values = values;
    this.count = values.length;
}
Holder.prototype.sum = function sum() {
    let total = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < this.count; ++i) total += this.values[i];
    return total;
};
const holder = new Holder([1, 2, 3, 4]);
jit.prepare(Holder.prototype.sum);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) holder.sum();
jit.compile(Holder.prototype.sum);

// CHECK-PASS: loop rotation
// CHECK: osr entry at pc
// CHECK-PASS: loop invariant code motion
// CHECK: CheckShape
// CHECK: CheckShape
// CHECK: CheckShape
// CHECK: loop:
// CHECK-NOT: CheckShape
// CHECK-NOT: LoadNamed
// CHECK: LoadElementAt Packed
// CHECK-NOT: CheckShape
// CHECK-NOT: LoadNamed
// CHECK: osr entry at pc

// which decline (with the empty value) for receivers that are no Map, so that the slow path calls the builtin.

// Int32 arguments take int32 paths: the absolute value of an int32 is the
// larger of it and its negation (which overflows, and exits, for the
// smallest), and its square root is that of its double.

function absAndSqrt(n) {
    const i = n | 0;
    return Math.abs(i) + Math.sqrt(i) + Math.ceil(i * 0.5) + Math.round(i * 0.25);
}
jit.prepare(absAndSqrt);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) absAndSqrt(i - 5);
jit.compile(absAndSqrt);

// Math.exp, log, sin, cos, tan and pow of numbers call the runtime's functions
// of doubles, which only compute: the code after them keeps what it knew, and
// a call of loop invariant numbers moves out of the loop.

function bias(base, values) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < values.length; ++i) sum += Math.pow(values[i], Math.log(1 - base * 0.5) / Math.LN2);
    return sum;
}
jit.prepare(bias);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) bias(0.25, [0.5, 0.75]);
jit.compile(bias);

// CHECK-FUNCTION: bias
// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK: CallFloat64Log
// CHECK: CallFloat64Pow
// CHECK-NOT: CallSlowPath Call @
// CHECK-PASS: loop invariant code motion
// CHECK: CallFloat64Log
// CHECK: loop:
// CHECK-NOT: CallFloat64Log
// CHECK: CallFloat64Pow

function trigonometry(x) {
    return Math.sin(x) + Math.cos(x) + Math.tan(x) + Math.exp(x);
}
jit.prepare(trigonometry);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) trigonometry(i * 0.5);
jit.compile(trigonometry);

// CHECK: CallFloat64Exp
// CHECK-NOT: CallSlowPath

console.log(bias(0.25, [0.5, 0.75]), trigonometry(0.5), trigonometry(2));

// REQUIRES: inline-allocation
// A constructor that many classes share reads their methods through a megamorphic cache. Inlined into a construct,
// whose object has a known shape, it reads the method of that shape as a constant and inlines its call.

function makeClass(scale) {
    const constructor = function (value) {
        this.initialize(value);
    };
    constructor.prototype = {
        initialize(value) {
            this.value = value * scale;
        },
    };
    return constructor;
}
const classes = [];
for (let scale = 1; scale <= 8; ++scale) classes.push(makeClass(scale));
const First = classes[0];
function make(i) {
    return new First(i).value;
}
jit.prepare(make);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
    for (const Class of classes) new Class(i);
    make(i);
}
jit.compile(make);

// CHECK-FUNCTION: make
// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK-NOT: CallSlowPath GetById
// CHECK-NOT: CallSlowPath Call @
// CHECK: Return

// Arithmetic that exited for another operand takes one path per kind of operand once recompiled: int32 values (with
// int32 operations that exit where results do not fit), then numbers as doubles. Other operands go to one slow path.
// The next operation, whose feedback only saw numbers, checks the joined result to be a number once.

// Compiles `f`, makes it exit with `args`, and compiles it again.
function recompileAfterExit(f, ...args) {
    jit.compile(f);
    f(...args);
    jit.discard(f);
    jit.compile(f);
}

const notANumber = { valueOf: () => 2 };

function mixed(a, b) {
    return a * b + 0.5;
}
jit.prepare(mixed);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
    mixed(i, 2.5);
    mixed(i, 3);
}
recompileAfterExit(mixed, notANumber, 3);

// CHECK-PASS: dead code elimination

// CHECK-NEXT: [[SUM:v[0-9]+]]:float64 = Float64Add ([[NUMBER]], #0x3fe0000000000000)
// CHECK-NEXT: BoxFloat64 ([[SUM]])
// CHECK-NOT: CallSlowPath Add

function find(nodes, target) {

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/osr-exits-into-loop.js
// Code that keeps exiting into a loop without an OSR entry is discarded after fewer exits than elsewhere, and
// compiled again with an entry at that loop.

function exitsIntoLoop(cold) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) sum += i;
    if (cold) {
        for (let j = 0; j < 5000; ++j) {
            if (jit.inCompiledCode()) return -1;
            sum += j;
        }
    }
    return sum;
}
jit.prepare(exitsIntoLoop);
exitsIntoLoop(false);
jit.compile(exitsIntoLoop);
let calls = 0;
while (exitsIntoLoop(true) !== -1) {
    if (++calls === 7) throw new Error("The loop never continued in recompiled code");
}
if (jit.discardCount(exitsIntoLoop) !== 1) throw new Error("The code was not discarded once");

// CHECK-FUNCTION: exitsIntoLoop
// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK: osr entry at pc

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/osr-exits-once-into-loop.js
// A call that exits once into a long loop that never ran before its code was compiled, like a driver that runs one
// loop after another, does not run the rest of that loop in the interpreter: once it keeps looping where no entry is
// reachable, the code is discarded and compiled again with an entry at that loop.

function runsLoopsInTurn(warm) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) sum += i;
    if (warm) return sum;
    for (let j = 0; j < 100000; ++j) {
        if (jit.inCompiledCode()) return -1;
        sum += j;
    }
    return sum;
}
jit.prepare(runsLoopsInTurn);
runsLoopsInTurn(true);
jit.compile(runsLoopsInTurn);
if (runsLoopsInTurn(false) !== -1) throw new Error("The loop never continued in recompiled code");
if (jit.discardCount(runsLoopsInTurn) !== 1) throw new Error("The code was not discarded once");

// CHECK-FUNCTION: runsLoopsInTurn
// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK: osr entry at pc

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/osr-installed-from-callee.js
// Installing code from a callee must give the suspended interpreted caller a chance to discard it when its next
// loop cannot reach an OSR entry. The caller has never entered the code, so no JIT exit can give it that budget.

function installCaller() {
    if (!jit.compile(runsLoopsAcrossInstall)) throw new Error("The caller was not compiled");
}
jit.neverCompile(installCaller);

function runsLoopsAcrossInstall(warm) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) sum += i;
    if (warm) return sum;
    installCaller();
    for (let j = 0; j < 1000000; ++j) {
        if (jit.inCompiledCode()) return -1;
        sum += j & 1;
    }
    return sum;
}
jit.prepare(runsLoopsAcrossInstall);
runsLoopsAcrossInstall(true);
if (runsLoopsAcrossInstall(false) !== -1) throw new Error("The caller stayed in the interpreter after installation");
const discards = jit.discardCount(runsLoopsAcrossInstall);
if (discards !== 1) throw new Error(`The caller code was discarded ${discards} times instead of once`);

// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK: osr entry at pc

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/osr-installed-in-recursive-callee.js
// Installing code in an inner recursive frame must also give the suspended outer frame a discard budget.
// The inner frame returns without using its budget, while the outer frame continues past the code's OSR entry.

function installRecursiveCaller() {
    if (!jit.compile(recursiveLoopsAcrossInstall)) throw new Error("The recursive caller was not compiled");
}
jit.neverCompile(installRecursiveCaller);

function recursiveLoopsAcrossInstall(warm, depth) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) sum += i;
    if (warm) return sum;
    if (depth === 0) {
        installRecursiveCaller();
        return sum;
    }
    recursiveLoopsAcrossInstall(false, depth - 1);
    for (let j = 0; j < 1000000; ++j) {
        if (jit.inCompiledCode()) return -1;
        sum += j & 1;
    }
    return sum;
}
jit.prepare(recursiveLoopsAcrossInstall);
recursiveLoopsAcrossInstall(true, 0);
if (recursiveLoopsAcrossInstall(false, 1) !== -1)
    throw new Error("The outer recursive caller stayed in the interpreter after installation");
const discards = jit.discardCount(recursiveLoopsAcrossInstall);
if (discards !== 1) throw new Error(`The recursive caller code was discarded ${discards} times instead of once`);

// CHECK-FUNCTION: recursiveLoopsAcrossInstall
// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK: osr entry at pc

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/osr-intermediate-inlined-frame.js
// An exit from outer -> middle -> leaf must give the materialized middle frame its own discard budget.
// Only middle has a long loop after the exit; neither the compiled root nor the innermost frame can use its budget.

function leafForLoop(value) {
    return value + 1;
}
function middleWithLoop(warm, value) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) sum += i;
    leafForLoop(value);
    if (warm) return sum;
    for (let j = 0; j < 1000000; ++j) {
        if (jit.inCompiledCode()) return -1;
        sum += j & 1;
    }
    return sum;
}
function outerWithLoop(warm, value) {
    return middleWithLoop(warm, value);
}
jit.prepare(leafForLoop);
jit.prepare(middleWithLoop);
jit.prepare(outerWithLoop);
outerWithLoop(true, 1);
if (!jit.compile(middleWithLoop) || !jit.compile(outerWithLoop)) throw new Error("The call chain was not compiled");
if (outerWithLoop(false, "different type") !== -1)
    throw new Error("The intermediate inlined frame stayed in the interpreter");
if (jit.discardCount(middleWithLoop) !== 1) throw new Error("The intermediate code was not discarded once");

// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK: Int32Add
// CHECK: fs[[MIDDLE:[0-9]+]]: e1 pc {{[0-9]+}} after
// CHECK: e2 pc {{.*}} in fs[[MIDDLE]]

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/osr-nested-loop-polling.js
// OPTIONS: stress-osr,threshold=400
// A cold loop shifts tier-up checks to an inner back edge that has no OSR entry. The interpreter must still find
// the outer loop's entry, even when its regular polling budget is a multiple of the number of back edges.

function nestedLoops(inner) {
    if (inner) {
        let i = 0;
        do {
            ++i;
        } while (i < 1);
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) {
        if (jit.inCompiledCode()) return true;
        if (inner) {
            let j = 0;
            do {
                ++j;
            } while (j < 1);
        }
    }
    return false;
}
jit.prepare(nestedLoops);
nestedLoops(false);
jit.compile(nestedLoops);
if (!nestedLoops(true)) throw new Error("The outer loop's OSR entry was never entered");

// CHECK-PASS: graph building
// CHECK: osr entry at pc

// OPTIONS: stress-osr
// On-stack replacement entries at unconditional back edges jump to the loop header, so that the loop has one header
// and loop invariant code motion can hoist the check of the loop bound to its preheader.

function countUp(n) {

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/osr-update-step.js
// OPTIONS: stress-osr
// A continue reaches the update step of a loop going forward, like the end of the body, so that the loop has one back
// edge and one on-stack replacement entry, at its test. That gives it one header, and loop invariant code motion can
// hoist the loads of the loop bound and of the object's property.

function sumOf(object, n) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        const x = object.x;
        if (i === 2) continue;
        sum = (sum + x) | 0;
    }
    return sum;
}

// CHECK-NOT: LoadNamed
// CHECK: osr entry at pc

// A loop whose test is a constant ends in a back edge that jumps to the start of the body. A body of one block leads
// to the test, which is the loop's header, so the on-stack replacement entry at that back edge runs the body itself
// and continues at the header, and the loop stays reducible.

function stopAt(i, n) {
    if (i === n) throw 0;
}
function spin(object, n) {
    let sum = 0;
    try {
        for (let i = 0; true; ++i) {
            sum = (sum + object.x) | 0;
            stopAt(i, n);
        }
    } catch {
        return sum;
    }
}
jit.prepare(spin);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) spin({ x: i }, 5);
jit.compile(spin);

// CHECK-FUNCTION: spin
// CHECK-PASS: graph building

// CHECK-NEXT: BoxInt32

// CHECK: [[SPIN_HEADER]] (pc {{[0-9]+}}) <- {{b[0-9]+}}, {{b[0-9]+}}, {{b[0-9]+}} loop:

console.log(spin({ x: 3 }, 5));

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/overflow-check-elimination.js
// Additions, subtractions and multiplications whose operands' ranges keep the result an int32, and multiplications
// that cannot make -0, stop checking for overflow. The ranges come from masks and shifts, and an index that a bounds
// check made below the elements' count can be incremented.

function multiplyDigits(x, y) {
    return (x & 0x3fff) * (y & 0x3fff) + ((x >> 14) - (y >> 14));
}

for (let k = 0; k < 10; ++k) multiplyDigits(k * 1000, k * 7000);

// The product of a value that may be negative and one that may be zero could be -0, and products of unknown ranges
// could overflow, so they stay checked.

function products(x, y) {

// Every bounds check of an operand narrows its range: a typed array's length has no known range, but the array's
// count below it keeps `j + 1` from overflowing.

function afterBothAccesses(ta, a, i) {

// check take its refined value, so that passes only move or share them with

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/representation-checked-entries.js
// OPTIONS: stress-osr
// A loop invariant value that the loop entry and an on-stack replacement entry bring in tagged becomes an int32 phi
// where the code checks it to be an int32, even only on some iterations: its tagged values are checked where they
// enter, once, instead of in the loop.

function addOnOddIterations(n, k) {
    const step = k | 0;
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i = (i + 1) | 0) {

// Loop variables that start as uint32 typed array elements (doubles, since they may not fit an int32) are checked to
// be int32 values where they enter the loop, also where no instruction at the loop header has a frame state of its own.

const states = new Uint32Array(60);
const data = new Uint16Array(1000);
for (let s = 0; s < 10; ++s) states[s * 6 + 1] = s * 30;
for (let k = 0; k < 1000; ++k) data[k] = k % 7;

    return states[s * 6 + slot];
}

    let index = 0;
    for (let i = stateSlot(state, 1); ; i += 3) {
        if (data[i] == 65535) break;
        if (data[i] == token) index++;
    }
    return index;
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir/scaled-index-arithmetic.js
// The heap index arithmetic of asm.js code, `(base + (i << 2)) >> 2`, is `i + base / 4` where the range of `i` keeps the
// shift and the addition from overflowing and the base is a multiple of 4.

const heap = new Int32Array(4096);
function sum() {
    let i = 0;
    let total = 0;
    do {
        total = (total + heap[(400 + (i << 2)) >> 2]) | 0;
        i = (i + 1) | 0;
    } while ((i | 0) != 1024);
    return total;
}
jit.prepare(sum);

// Additions whose results only reach ToInt32 (the `| 0` of asm.js code, shifts, integer typed array stores) wrap
// instead of exiting on overflow, while sums something reads in full keep checking: the returned sum, and the stored
// one, which the checks of the typed array before the store exit with.

const heap = new Int32Array(16);
function asmStyle(a, b) {
    a = a | 0;
    b = b | 0;
    const index = (a + b) | 0;
    heap[(index + 4) >> 2] = a + 1;
    return a + b;
}

// The rare cases of the length (an empty, detached or out-of-bounds typed array) exit instead of running the slow
// path, so a loop bounded by the length runs no code that could change it, and its checks move out of the loop.
function countEqual(left, right) {

// Comparisons of uint32 values compare the bits of the shifted int32 values unsigned, so that the `>>> 0` shifts
// neither exit for values above 2^31 nor make the comparison one of doubles.

function compareUnsigned(a, b) {
    a = a | 0;
    b = b | 0;
    let result = 0;
    if (a >>> 0 < b >>> 0) result = 1;
    if (((a - 8) | 0) >>> 0 < 20) result = (result + 2) | 0;
    return result;
}
jit.prepare(compareUnsigned);
for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
    compareUnsigned(i, 3);
    compareUnsigned(-i, 3);
}
jit.compile(compareUnsigned);

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/irtest.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
#
# Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
#

"""Runs the IR tests in Tests/LibJS/JIT/ir: JavaScript programs that compile functions with the jit object, whose IR
after building and after each pass (LIBJS_JIT=dump-passes) must match the CHECK lines in their comments, in the
manner of LLVM's FileCheck.

Directives, in // comments:
  OPTIONS: <LIBJS_JIT options>  added to "on,sync,dump-passes,verify-ir"
  REQUIRES: inline-allocation   skip the test in builds whose JIT code cannot allocate cells itself (AddressSanitizer)
  CHECK-FUNCTION: <name>        the checks below are about the last code compiled for the function of that name
  CHECK-PASS: <pass>[#N]        ...in its IR after that pass (the Nth time it ran; "graph building" is before any)
  CHECK: <pattern>              a line matches, after the line the previous check matched
  CHECK-NEXT: <pattern>         the line right after the previous match matches
  CHECK-SAME: <pattern>         the rest of the previously matched line matches
  CHECK-NOT: <pattern>          no line between the previous match and the next one (or the end) matches
  CHECK-COUNT-<N>: <pattern>    exactly N lines of the IR after the pass match
Patterns are literal text, except for {{regex}}, [[NAME:regex]] (which binds NAME to what the regex matched, for the
rest of the file) and [[NAME]] (what NAME was bound to).

Usage: irtest.py [--build Build/release] [-f FILTER] [--dump]
"""

import argparse
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

from dataclasses import dataclass
from dataclasses import field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict
from typing import List
from typing import Optional
from typing import Tuple

SOURCE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
TESTS_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "ir"
DIRECTIVE = re.compile(
    r"//\s*(OPTIONS|REQUIRES|CHECK-FUNCTION|CHECK-PASS|CHECK-NEXT|CHECK-SAME|CHECK-NOT|CHECK-COUNT-\d+|CHECK):\s?(.*)$"
)
FUNCTION_HEADER = re.compile(r"^JIT code for (\S+?)(?: \((?:.+:)?\d+:\d+\))?:$")
PASS_HEADER = re.compile(r"^=== after (.+)$")


@dataclass
class Check:
    kind: str
    pattern: str
    line: int


@dataclass
class Section:
    function: str
    pass_name: str
    checks: List[Check] = field(default_factory=list)


def parse_test(path: Path) -> Tuple[str, List[Section]]:
    options = ""
    sections: List[Section] = []
    function = None
    for number, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
        match = DIRECTIVE.search(line)
        if not match:
            continue
        kind, argument = match.group(1), match.group(2).rstrip()
        if kind == "OPTIONS":
            options = argument
        elif kind == "REQUIRES":
            if argument != "inline-allocation":
                raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: unknown requirement {argument}")
        elif kind == "CHECK-FUNCTION":
            function = argument
        elif kind == "CHECK-PASS":
            if function is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: CHECK-PASS before CHECK-FUNCTION")
            sections.append(Section(function, argument))
        else:
            if not sections:
                raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: {kind} before CHECK-PASS")
            sections[-1].checks.append(Check(kind, argument, number))
    return options, sections


def requires_inline_allocation(path: Path) -> bool:
    return re.search(r"^//\s*REQUIRES:\s*inline-allocation\s*$", path.read_text(), re.MULTILINE) is not None


def has_inline_allocation(build: Path) -> bool:
    """Whether JIT code of this build allocates cells itself: AddressSanitizer builds give no addresses of free lists."""
    try:
        cache = (build / "CMakeCache.txt").read_text()
    except OSError:
        return True
    return re.search(r"^ENABLE_ADDRESS_SANITIZER:BOOL=ON$", cache, re.MULTILINE) is None


def compile_pattern(pattern: str, variables: Dict[str, str]) -> Tuple[re.Pattern, List[str]]:
    """A regex for a check pattern, and the names of the variables it binds, in group order."""
    regex = ""
    bound = []
    position = 0
    for match in re.finditer(r"\{\{(.*?)\}\}|\[\[(\w+):(.*?)\]\]|\[\[(\w+)\]\]", pattern):
        regex += re.escape(pattern[position : match.start()])
        if match.group(1) is not None:
            regex += f"(?:{match.group(1)})"
        elif match.group(2) is not None:
            regex += f"({match.group(3)})"
            bound.append(match.group(2))
        else:
            name = match.group(4)
            if name not in variables:
                raise ValueError(f"[[{name}]] is not bound")
            regex += re.escape(variables[name])
        position = match.end()
    regex += re.escape(pattern[position:])
    return re.compile(regex), bound


def split_dump(text: str) -> Dict[str, List[Tuple[str, List[str]]]]:
    """The pass dumps of each function's last compile: function name -> [(pass, lines)]."""
    functions: Dict[str, List[Tuple[str, List[str]]]] = {}
    current: Optional[List[Tuple[str, List[str]]]] = None
    for line in text.splitlines():
        header = FUNCTION_HEADER.match(line)
        if header:
            current = []
            functions[header.group(1)] = current
            continue
        pass_header = PASS_HEADER.match(line)
        if pass_header and current is not None:
            current.append((pass_header.group(1), []))
            continue
        if current:
            current[-1][1].append(line)
    return functions


def pass_lines(passes: List[Tuple[str, List[str]]], pass_name: str) -> Optional[List[str]]:
    name, _, occurrence = pass_name.partition("#")
    matching = [lines for pass_, lines in passes if pass_ == name]
    index = int(occurrence) - 1 if occurrence else 0
    if index >= len(matching):
        return None
    return matching[index]


def run_checks(lines: List[str], section: Section, path: Path, variables: Dict[str, str]) -> List[str]:
    failures = []
    position = 0  # The line after the previous match.
    previous_line = -1
    previous_end = 0
    pending_nots: List[Tuple[Check, re.Pattern]] = []

    def check_nots(end: int):
        for check, regex in pending_nots:
            for index in range(position, end):
                if regex.search(lines[index]):
                    failures.append(f"{path.name}:{check.line}: CHECK-NOT matched {lines[index].strip()!r}")
                    break
        pending_nots.clear()

    for check in section.checks:
        try:
            regex, bound = compile_pattern(check.pattern, variables)
        except ValueError as error:
            failures.append(f"{path.name}:{check.line}: {error}")
            return failures
        if check.kind == "CHECK-NOT":
            pending_nots.append((check, regex))
            continue
        if check.kind.startswith("CHECK-COUNT-"):
            expected = int(check.kind.split("-")[-1])
            count = sum(1 for line in lines if regex.search(line))
            if count != expected:
                failures.append(f"{path.name}:{check.line}: expected {expected} lines matching, found {count}")
            continue
        match = None
        matched_line = -1
        if check.kind == "CHECK-SAME":
            if previous_line >= 0:
                match = regex.search(lines[previous_line], previous_end)
                matched_line = previous_line
        elif check.kind == "CHECK-NEXT":
            if previous_line + 1 < len(lines):
                match = regex.search(lines[previous_line + 1])
                matched_line = previous_line + 1
        else:
            for index in range(position, len(lines)):
                match = regex.search(lines[index])
                if match:
                    matched_line = index
                    break
        if not match:
            failures.append(f"{path.name}:{check.line}: {check.kind}: {check.pattern!r} did not match")
            return failures
        check_nots(matched_line)
        for name, value in zip(bound, match.groups()):
            variables[name] = value
        previous_line, previous_end = matched_line, match.end()
        position = matched_line + 1
    check_nots(len(lines))
    return failures


def run_test(js: Path, path: Path) -> List[str]:
    options, sections = parse_test(path)
    environment = dict(os.environ)
    jit = "on,sync,dump-passes,verify-ir"
    environment["LIBJS_JIT"] = f"{jit},{options}" if options else jit
    try:
        process = subprocess.run(
            [str(js), "--expose-jit-testing", str(path)],
            env=environment,
            capture_output=True,
            timeout=120,
            check=False,
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return [f"{path.name}: js did not finish in 120 seconds"]
    stderr = process.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    if process.returncode != 0:
        output = process.stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        return [f"{path.name}: js exited with {process.returncode}: {(output + stderr)[-500:]}"]
    functions = split_dump(stderr)
    failures = []
    # NB: Variables bound in the IR after one pass may be used in the IR after a later one.
    variables: Dict[str, str] = {}
    for section in sections:
        passes = functions.get(section.function)
        if passes is None:
            failures.append(f"{path.name}: no code was compiled for {section.function}")
            continue
        lines = pass_lines(passes, section.pass_name)
        if lines is None:
            failures.append(f"{path.name}: {section.function} has no IR after {section.pass_name}")
            continue
        failures += run_checks(lines, section, path, variables)
    return failures


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--build", type=Path, default=SOURCE_DIR / "Build/release")
    parser.add_argument("-f", "--filter", default="", help="only tests whose path contains this")
    parser.add_argument("--dump", action="store_true", help="print the IR of the tests' functions")
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    js = arguments.build / "bin/js"

    tests = sorted(path for path in TESTS_DIR.glob("*.js") if arguments.filter in str(path))
    failed = 0
    skipped = 0
    inline_allocation = has_inline_allocation(arguments.build)
    for path in tests:
        if not inline_allocation and requires_inline_allocation(path):
            print(f"SKIP {path.relative_to(SOURCE_DIR)}: JIT code of this build cannot allocate cells")
            skipped += 1
            continue
        if arguments.dump:
            environment = dict(os.environ)
            options, _ = parse_test(path)
            environment["LIBJS_JIT"] = "on,sync,dump-passes" + (f",{options}" if options else "")
            subprocess.run([str(js), "--expose-jit-testing", str(path)], env=environment, check=False)
            continue
        failures = run_test(js, path)
        if failures:
            failed += 1
            print(f"FAIL {path.relative_to(SOURCE_DIR)}")
            for failure in failures:
                print(f"  {failure}")
        else:
            print(f"PASS {path.relative_to(SOURCE_DIR)}")
    print(f"{len(tests) - failed - skipped} of {len(tests) - skipped} IR tests passed ({skipped} skipped)")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/machine.py
#
# Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
#

"""Sharing the machine with work that needs it idle, like benchmarks.

While one of the pause files exists, the test tools start nothing new. LIBJS_JIT_TEST_PAUSE_FILES lists them,
separated by colons.
"""

import os
import time

from pathlib import Path


def pause_files():
    return [Path(path) for path in os.environ.get("LIBJS_JIT_TEST_PAUSE_FILES", "").split(":") if path]


def wait_until_machine_is_free():
    """Returns once none of the pause files exists."""
    while any(path.exists() for path in pause_files()):
        time.sleep(20)

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/matrix.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
#
# Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
#

"""Runs JavaScript test suites under a matrix of JIT stress modes and compares every result with the interpreter's.

Suites:
  test-js   The LibJS runtime tests (Tests/LibJS/Runtime), one process per file, each test run LIBJS_TEST_REPEAT
            times so that the functions it calls get compiled with feedback. The per-test results must match the
            interpreter's with the same repeat count.
  test262   The whole test262 suite through libjs-test262's main.py; the per-file results must match the
            interpreter's.
  programs  Every .js file (and .mjs file, as a module) in the --programs directories (Tests/LibJS/JIT/programs by
            default), run with js; the exit code and the output must match the interpreter's (lines with timings are
            ignored).

Every mismatch is printed with a command that reproduces it. The exit code is 1 if there were any.
"""

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict
from typing import List
from typing import Optional
from typing import Tuple

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from machine import wait_until_machine_is_free  # noqa: E402
from modes import INTERPRETER  # noqa: E402
from modes import Mode  # noqa: E402
from modes import modes_for  # noqa: E402

SOURCE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
TIMING_LINE = re.compile(r"\btimes?\b|[0-9] ?ms\b|\bscore\b|[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ?s\b", re.IGNORECASE)
ANSI_ESCAPE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m")


def environment_for(mode: Mode, seed: int, extra: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None) -> Dict[str, str]:
    environment = dict(os.environ)
    environment.pop("LIBJS_JIT", None)
    environment["LADYBIRD_SOURCE_DIR"] = str(SOURCE_DIR)
    if mode.jit:
        environment["LIBJS_JIT"] = mode.environment_value(seed)
    if extra:
        environment.update(extra)
    return environment


def command_line(environment_changes: Dict[str, str], command: List, cwd: Optional[Path] = None) -> str:
    """A shell command line that runs `command` with the environment changes."""
    parts = [f"{name}={value}" for name, value in environment_changes.items() if value]
    parts += [str(part) for part in command]
    line = " ".join(parts)
    return f"(cd {cwd} && {line})" if cwd else line


class Suite:
    name = ""

    def __init__(self, arguments):
        self.arguments = arguments

    def run(self, mode: Mode) -> Dict[str, str]:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def repro(self, mode: Mode, key: str) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError


class TestJsSuite(Suite):
    name = "test-js"

    def __init__(self, arguments):
        super().__init__(arguments)
        self.root = SOURCE_DIR / "Tests/LibJS/Runtime"
        self.runner = arguments.build / "bin/test-js-runtime"
        self.files = sorted(
            path
            for path in self.root.rglob("*.js")
            if path.name != "test-common.js" and all(f in str(path) for f in arguments.filter)
        )

    def environment_changes(self, mode: Mode) -> Dict[str, str]:
        return {
            "LIBJS_JIT": mode.environment_value(self.arguments.seed),
            "LIBJS_TEST_REPEAT": str(self.arguments.repeat),
        }

    def test_filter(self, relative: str) -> str:
        """The runner's filter for the test file at `relative`, which it matches against paths with forward slashes. A
        backslash in it would escape the next character."""
        return f"{self.root.name}/{relative}"

    def run_file(self, mode: Mode, path: Path) -> Dict[str, str]:
        wait_until_machine_is_free()
        relative = path.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()
        environment = environment_for(mode, self.arguments.seed, {"LIBJS_TEST_REPEAT": str(self.arguments.repeat)})
        try:
            process = subprocess.run(
                [self.runner, "--per-file", "-f", self.test_filter(relative)],
                env=environment,
                capture_output=True,
                timeout=self.arguments.timeout,
                check=False,
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return {f"{relative}/(process)": "TIMEOUT"}
        results = {}
        try:
            output = json.loads(process.stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
            for test, result in output.get("results", {}).items():
                results[test] = result
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            pass
        # NB: test-js exits with 1 when a test fails, but a crash is a signal or another exit code.
        if process.returncode not in (0, 1) or not results and process.returncode != 0:
            stderr = process.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip().splitlines()
            reason = stderr[-1][:200] if stderr else ""
            results[f"{relative}/(process)"] = f"CRASH {process.returncode} {reason}"
        return results

    def run(self, mode: Mode) -> Dict[str, str]:
        results = {}
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(self.arguments.jobs) as executor:
            for file_results in executor.map(lambda path: self.run_file(mode, path), self.files):
                results.update(file_results)
        return results

    def repro(self, mode: Mode, key: str) -> str:
        relative = key.split(".js/", 1)[0] + ".js"
        return command_line(
            self.environment_changes(mode) | {"LADYBIRD_SOURCE_DIR": str(SOURCE_DIR)},
            [self.runner, "-f", self.test_filter(relative)],
        )


class Test262Suite(Suite):
    name = "test262"

    def __init__(self, arguments):
        super().__init__(arguments)
        self.directory = arguments.test262
        self.runner = arguments.build / "bin/test262-runner"
        # NB: The runner scripts run with this Python, which needs their requirements.
        self.python = Path(sys.executable)
        self.pattern = arguments.test262_pattern

    def run(self, mode: Mode) -> Dict[str, str]:
        wait_until_machine_is_free()
        output = self.arguments.results / f"test262-{mode.name}.json"
        output.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        command = [
            self.python,
            self.directory / "main.py",
            "-j",
            self.runner,
            "-c",
            str(self.arguments.jobs),
            "--per-file",
            output,
            "-s",
        ]
        if self.pattern:
            command += ["-p", self.pattern]
        subprocess.run(
            command,
            cwd=self.directory,
            env=environment_for(mode, self.arguments.seed),
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            check=False,
        )
        try:
            return json.loads(output.read_text())["results"]
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError):
            return {"(test262)": "NO RESULTS"}

    def repro(self, mode: Mode, key: str) -> str:
        return command_line(
            {"LIBJS_JIT": mode.environment_value(self.arguments.seed)},
            [self.python, "main.py", "-j", self.runner, "-v", "-p", key],
            cwd=self.directory,
        )


class ProgramsSuite(Suite):
    name = "programs"

    def __init__(self, arguments):
        super().__init__(arguments)
        self.js = arguments.build / "bin/js"
        directories = arguments.programs or [SOURCE_DIR / "Tests/LibJS/JIT/programs"]
        self.files = sorted(
            path
            for directory in directories
            for pattern in ("*.js", "*.mjs")
            for path in Path(directory).rglob(pattern)
            if all(f in str(path) for f in arguments.filter)
        )

    def run_file(self, mode: Mode, path: Path) -> tuple[str, str]:
        wait_until_machine_is_free()
        try:
            process = subprocess.run(
                self.command(path),
                cwd=path.parent,
                env=environment_for(mode, self.arguments.seed),
                stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                timeout=self.arguments.timeout,
                check=False,
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return str(path), "TIMEOUT"
        text = ANSI_ESCAPE.sub("", process.stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
        lines = [line for line in text.splitlines() if not TIMING_LINE.search(line)]
        return str(path), f"exit {process.returncode}\n" + "\n".join(lines)

    def run(self, mode: Mode) -> Dict[str, str]:
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(self.arguments.jobs) as executor:
            return dict(executor.map(lambda path: self.run_file(mode, path), self.files))

    def repro(self, mode: Mode, key: str) -> str:
        path = Path(key)
        return command_line(
            {"LIBJS_JIT": mode.environment_value(self.arguments.seed)},
            self.command(path),
            cwd=path.parent,
        )

    def command(self, path: Path) -> List:
        """The js command line that runs the program at `path`, as a module if it is a .mjs file."""
        module = ["--as-module"] if path.suffix == ".mjs" else []
        return [self.js, "--expose-jit-testing", *module, path.name]


SUITES = {suite.name: suite for suite in (TestJsSuite, Test262Suite, ProgramsSuite)}

KNOWN_MISMATCHES = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "known-mismatches.txt"


def load_known_mismatches() -> Dict[Tuple[str, str], str]:
    """The mismatches of open bugs, which do not fail a run: (suite, key) -> the bug, from lines of
    "<suite> <key> # <bug>" in known-mismatches.txt."""
    known = {}
    for line in KNOWN_MISMATCHES.read_text().splitlines():
        if not line.strip() or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        entry, _, bug = line.partition(" # ")
        suite, _, key = entry.partition(" ")
        known[(suite, key.strip())] = bug.strip()
    return known


def describe_difference(expected: str, actual: str) -> str:
    if "\n" not in expected and "\n" not in actual:
        return f"interpreter: {expected}, got: {actual}"
    expected_lines, actual_lines = expected.splitlines(), actual.splitlines()
    for index, (expected_line, actual_line) in enumerate(zip(expected_lines, actual_lines)):
        if expected_line != actual_line:
            return f"line {index + 1}: interpreter: {expected_line[:160]!r}, got: {actual_line[:160]!r}"
    return f"interpreter printed {len(expected_lines)} lines, got {len(actual_lines)}"


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description=__doc__,
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    parser.add_argument("--build", type=Path, default=SOURCE_DIR / "Build/release", help="build directory")
    parser.add_argument("--modes", default="fast", help="comma-separated modes and tiers (see modes.py)")
    parser.add_argument("--suites", default="test-js,programs", help="comma-separated suites: " + ", ".join(SUITES))
    parser.add_argument("-j", "--jobs", type=int, default=4, help="processes to run at once")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1, help="seed of the modes that make random choices")
    parser.add_argument("--repeat", type=int, default=3, help="how often test-js runs each test")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=300, help="seconds per test file or program")
    parser.add_argument("-f", "--filter", action="append", default=[], help="only paths containing this")
    parser.add_argument("--programs", action="append", type=Path, help="directories of programs to run")
    parser.add_argument("--test262", type=Path, help="checkout of libjs-test262, for the test262 suite")
    parser.add_argument("--test262-pattern", help="glob of test262 tests to run (default: all)")
    parser.add_argument("--results", type=Path, help="directory for the results (default: a new one in /tmp)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--coverage", action="store_true", help="collect what compiled code contained and did, and report it"
    )
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    if "test262" in arguments.suites.split(",") and arguments.test262 is None:
        parser.error("the test262 suite needs --test262")

    arguments.build = arguments.build.resolve()
    if arguments.test262 is not None:
        arguments.test262 = arguments.test262.resolve()
    if arguments.results is None:
        arguments.results = Path(f"/tmp/jit-matrix-{os.getpid()}")
    arguments.results = arguments.results.resolve()
    arguments.results.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    modes = modes_for(arguments.modes.split(","))
    if arguments.coverage:
        coverage = arguments.results / "coverage"
        modes = [Mode(mode.name, f"{mode.jit},coverage={coverage / mode.name}", mode.description) for mode in modes]
    suites = [SUITES[name](arguments) for name in arguments.suites.split(",")]

    known = load_known_mismatches()
    mismatch_count = 0
    known_seen = set()
    known_run = set()
    summary = {}
    for suite in suites:
        start = time.monotonic()
        expected = suite.run(INTERPRETER)
        print(f"{suite.name} [interpreter]: {len(expected)} results in {time.monotonic() - start:.1f} s", flush=True)
        summary[suite.name] = {"interpreter": {"results": len(expected)}}
        if not expected or "(test262)" in expected:
            print(f"{suite.name} [interpreter]: no results, so nothing to compare with")
            return 1
        for mode in modes:
            start = time.monotonic()
            actual = suite.run(mode)
            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
            mismatches = []
            for key in sorted(set(expected) | set(actual)):
                expected_result = expected.get(key, "MISSING")
                actual_result = actual.get(key, "MISSING")
                if expected_result != actual_result:
                    mismatches.append((key, expected_result, actual_result))
            print(
                f"{suite.name} [{mode.name}]: {len(actual)} results, {len(mismatches)} mismatches in {elapsed:.1f} s",
                flush=True,
            )
            known_run |= {(suite.name, key) for key in expected if (suite.name, key) in known}
            for key, expected_result, actual_result in mismatches:
                if (suite.name, key) in known:
                    known_seen.add((suite.name, key))
                    print(f"  KNOWN ({known[(suite.name, key)]}) {key}")
                    continue
                print(f"  MISMATCH {key}: {describe_difference(expected_result, actual_result)}")
                print(f"    repro: {suite.repro(mode, key)}")
                mismatch_count += 1
            summary[suite.name][mode.name] = {
                "jit": mode.environment_value(arguments.seed),
                "results": len(actual),
                "mismatches": [{"key": key, "interpreter": e, "actual": a} for key, e, a in mismatches],
                "seconds": round(elapsed, 1),
            }
            (arguments.results / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))

    if arguments.coverage:
        subprocess.run(
            [
                sys.executable,
                Path(__file__).parent / "coverage.py",
                arguments.results / "coverage",
                "--json",
                arguments.results / "coverage.json",
            ],
            check=False,
        )
    fixed = sorted(known_run - known_seen)
    for suite_name, key in fixed:
        print(
            f"FIXED? {suite_name} {key} did not mismatch in these modes; remove it from known-mismatches.txt if fixed"
        )
    print(f"{mismatch_count} new mismatches, {len(known_seen)} known; results in {arguments.results}")
    return 1 if mismatch_count else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#
# Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

"""The JIT stress modes the test tools run code under, as LIBJS_JIT values.

Every mode is compared with the interpreter (LIBJS_JIT=off): whatever runs in a mode must behave exactly like it does
in the interpreter. Modes with "sync" compile at the same points in every run, so their failures reproduce with the
same command. "{seed}" in a mode is replaced by the run's seed.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Mode:
    name: str
    jit: str
    description: str

    def environment_value(self, seed: int) -> str:
        return self.jit.replace("{seed}", str(seed))


INTERPRETER = Mode("interpreter", "off", "The interpreter alone: the reference every other mode is compared with.")

# NB: "warmup=0,threshold=2" profiles every function from its first call and compiles it after about two more, so that
#     even code that runs a handful of times (like a test repeated a few times) gets compiled with real feedback.
WARM = "on,warmup=0,threshold=2,sync"

MODES = [
    Mode(
        "eager", "on,warmup=0,threshold=0,sync,verify-ir", "Compile every function at its first call, without feedback."
    ),
    Mode("warm", f"{WARM},verify-ir", "Compile every function after a few calls, from the feedback they collected."),
    Mode("exits", f"{WARM},stress-exits=5,verify-ir", "Like warm, and exit from compiled code at every few checks."),
    Mode("exits-always", f"{WARM},stress-exits=1", "Like warm, and exit from compiled code at every check."),
    Mode("osr", f"{WARM},stress-osr,verify-ir", "Like warm, with an on-stack replacement entry at every loop."),
    Mode(
        "invalidate",
        f"{WARM},stress-invalidate=5,verify-ir",
        "Like warm, and invalidate code as if what it depends on stopped holding, every few tier-up checks.",
    ),
    Mode("registers", f"{WARM},stress-registers,verify-ir", "Like warm, with very few registers for values."),
    Mode("no-inline", f"{WARM},inline-depth=0", "Like warm, without inlining."),
    Mode(
        "deep-inline",
        f"{WARM},inline-depth=10,inline-max-size=2000,inline-budget=100000,verify-ir",
        "Like warm, inlining every call it can, as deep as it can.",
    ),
    Mode(
        "random",
        "on,warmup=2,threshold=10,random-thresholds,sync,stress-exits=50,seed={seed}",
        "Compile each function after a random number of calls, and exit at random checks.",
    ),
    Mode(
        "async",
        "on,warmup=1,threshold=4,stress-install,seed={seed}",
        "Compile on the compile threads, installing the code after a random number of tier-up checks.",
    ),
    Mode("default", "on", "The JIT with its default options, as the browser runs it."),
]

MODES_BY_NAME = {mode.name: mode for mode in [INTERPRETER] + MODES}

TIERS = {
    # Every commit: minutes.
    "fast": ["eager", "warm", "exits"],
    # Nightly: every mode.
    "full": [mode.name for mode in MODES],
}


def modes_for(names: List[str]) -> List[Mode]:
    """The modes of a list of mode and tier names."""
    modes = []
    for name in names:
        for mode_name in TIERS.get(name, [name]):
            if mode_name not in MODES_BY_NAME:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown mode or tier '{mode_name}'")
            mode = MODES_BY_NAME[mode_name]
            if mode not in modes:
                modes.append(mode)
    return modes

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/programs/bound-calls-with-many-bound-arguments.js
// Calls of bound functions with more bound arguments than the old limit of four are inlined, and calls of bound
// functions with more bound arguments than the inlining limit are not: both must see every bound argument.
function sum(...values) {
    let total = 0;
    for (const value of values) total += value;
    return total + values.length * 1000;
}
const count = n => Array.from({ length: n }, (_, index) => index + 1);
for (const n of [5, 16, 64, 65, 200]) {
    const bound = sum.bind(null, ...count(n));
    // NB: Each caller has its own executable, so its call site sees only one bound function.
    const call = Function("bound", "return argument => bound(argument);")(bound);
    let result = 0;
    for (let k = 0; k < 200; k++) result = call(k);
    print(n, result);
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/programs/closures-of-inlined-callees.js
// Closures that inlined callees create must be what the interpreter would have created, when code exits in them or
// after them, when they escape, and when the stack is walked through them.

function apply(f, x) {
    return f(x);
}

// The inlined callee creates a closure that captures a binding of the environment the callee was created in.
function makeScaled() {
    let factor = 2;
    function scaled(x) {
        return apply(y => y * factor, x);
    }
    return {
        scaled,
        grow() {
            factor++;
        },
    };
}

// Exits in the closure of the inlined callee once the values stop being int32.
function sumScaled(scaler, values) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (const value of values) sum += scaler.scaled(value);
    return sum;
}

// The closure of the inlined callee escapes into an array.
function collect(values) {
    const closures = [];
    for (const value of values) closures.push(wrap(value));
    return closures.map(f => f()).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
}
function wrap(value) {
    return () => value;
}

// The closure of the inlined callee is held across a call that exits.
function twice(x) {
    const f = y => y + 1;
    return apply(f, x) + apply(f, x * 2);
}
function sumTwice(values) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (const value of values) sum += twice(value);
    return sum;
}

// Sloppy closures of inlined callees show their frames as the legacy caller.
function whoCalled() {
    return whoCalled.caller;
}
function sloppyInner(x) {
    return apply(function (y) {
        return [whoCalled(), whoCalled(), y];
    }, x);
}
function legacyCaller(count) {
    let same = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const result = sloppyInner(i);
        if (result[0] === result[1] && typeof result[0] === "function") same++;
    }
    return same;
}

// Stack traces through the frames of closures of inlined callees name the closures.
function tracedInner(x, last) {
    return apply(function named(y) {
        return y === last ? new Error().stack : "";
    }, x);
}
function traced(count) {
    let names = "";
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const stack = tracedInner(i, count - 1);
        if (stack)
            names = stack
                .split("\n")
                .slice(1, 4)
                .join(" | ")
                .replace(/\(.*?\)/g, "");
    }
    return names;
}

// Methods of classes with private names have a private environment, which their closures keep.
class Counter {
    #step = 3;
    scaled(x) {
        return apply(y => y * this.#step, x);
    }
}
function sumCounter(counter, values) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (const value of values) sum += counter.scaled(value);
    return sum;
}

const ints = Array.from({ length: 50 }, (_, i) => i);
const mixed = ints.concat([1.5, 2.5, "3", 4]);
const scaler = makeScaled();
const counter = new Counter();
for (let i = 0; i < 300; i++) {
    sumScaled(scaler, ints);
    collect(ints);
    sumTwice(ints);
    sumCounter(counter, ints);
}
print(sumScaled(scaler, ints), sumScaled(scaler, mixed));
scaler.grow();
print(sumScaled(scaler, ints), sumScaled(scaler, mixed));
print(collect(ints), collect(mixed));
print(sumTwice(ints), sumTwice(mixed));
print(sumCounter(counter, ints), sumCounter(counter, mixed));
for (let i = 0; i < 300; i++) legacyCaller(5);
print(legacyCaller(10));
for (let i = 0; i < 300; i++) traced(3);
print(traced(3));

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/programs/closures-the-code-never-allocated.js
// Closures that compiled code never allocates, because nothing but the frames of inlined calls of them refers to them,
// must be created as they were when code exits in them, or after them, or walks the stack through them.

function apply(f, x) {
    return f(x);
}

// Exits in the inlined closure, which reads a binding it captured, once the values stop being int32.
function capturing(values) {
    let offset = 1;
    let sum = 0;
    for (const value of values) {
        sum += apply(x => x * 2 + offset, value);
        offset++;
    }
    return sum;
}

// Exits with the closure in a local slot, before it is called again.
function heldInLocal(values) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (const value of values) {
        const f = x => x + 1;
        sum += apply(f, value);
        sum += value * 3;
        sum += apply(f, value);
    }
    return sum;
}

// Exits in a closure created in a method of a class, which has a private environment.
class Counter {
    #step = 2;
    total(values) {
        let sum = 0;
        for (const value of values) sum += apply(x => x * this.#step, value);
        return sum;
    }
}

// Sloppy functions show the frames of inlined calls of them as the legacy caller of the functions they call.
function whoCalled() {
    return whoCalled.caller;
}
function legacyCaller(count) {
    let same = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const caller = apply(function (x) {
            return [whoCalled(), whoCalled(), x];
        }, i);
        if (caller[0] === caller[1] && typeof caller[0] === "function") same++;
    }
    return same;
}

// Sloppy arrow functions are legacy callers too, which must stay the same object across the calls they make.
function countCalls() {
    const caller = countCalls.caller;
    caller.calls = (caller.calls | 0) + 1;
    // NB: Too large to inline, so that it runs without the frames of inlined calls.
    let padding = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) padding += i * 2 + 1;
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) padding -= i * 2 + 1;
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) padding += i % 2;
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) padding -= i % 2;
    return caller.calls + padding;
}
function arrowCaller() {
    const arrow = () => countCalls();
    apply(arrow, 0);
    return apply(arrow, 0);
}

// Stack traces through the frames of inlined calls name the closures.
function traced(count) {
    let names = "";
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const stack = apply(function named(x) {
            return x === count - 1 ? new Error().stack : "";
        }, i);
        if (stack)
            names = stack
                .split("\n")
                .slice(1, 3)
                .join(" | ")
                .replace(/\(.*?\)/g, "");
    }
    return names;
}

const ints = Array.from({ length: 50 }, (_, i) => i);
const mixed = ints.concat([1.5, 2.5, "3", 4]);
for (let i = 0; i < 300; i++) {
    capturing(ints);
    heldInLocal(ints);
    new Counter().total(ints);
}
print(capturing(ints), capturing(mixed));
print(heldInLocal(ints), heldInLocal(mixed));
print(new Counter().total(ints), new Counter().total(mixed));
for (let i = 0; i < 300; i++) legacyCaller(5);
print(legacyCaller(10));
let arrowCalls = 0;
for (let i = 0; i < 300; i++) arrowCalls += arrowCaller();
print(arrowCalls);
for (let i = 0; i < 300; i++) traced(3);
print(traced(3));

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/programs/exits-from-frames-not-initialized-yet.js
// Exits from compiled code before it initialized its frame must not keep the registers the frame state lists as held in
// the frame, which are left over from earlier frames: with an exit at every check (stress-exits=1), the garbage
// collector visited one of them as a cell and crashed.
"use strict";
let __hash = 0;
function __describe(value, depth) {
    if (typeof value === "string") return JSON.stringify(value);
    if (typeof value !== "object") return String(value);
    let text = "[";
    for (let i = 0; i < value.length && i < 8; ++i) text += (i in value ? __describe(value[i], depth + 1) : "_") + ",";
    return text + "]";
}
function __record(value) {
    const text = __describe(value, 0);

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/programs/for-in-loops-that-change-their-objects.js
// For-in loops exit where the property iterator cache stops holding their object's keys, and the keys their bodies
// read come straight from the cache. These loops change the shape of the object they iterate over while they run,
// leave early, nest, read keys after the loop, read keys of other objects, and iterate over objects with accessors,
// indices and dictionary shapes.
function keysAddingProperties(o) {
    let s = "";
    for (const k in o) {
        s += k;
        if (k === "b") o["added" + s.length] = 1;
    }
    return s;
}

function keysDeletingProperties(o) {
    let s = "";
    for (const k in o) {
        s += k + o[k];
        delete o.c;
    }
    return s;
}

function nested(a, b) {
    let n = 0;
    for (const x in a) for (const y in b) if (a.hasOwnProperty(x) && b[y] !== a[x]) n += x.length + y.length;
    return n;
}

function lastKey(o) {
    let last;
    for (var k in o) {
        if (k === "stop") break;
        last = k;
    }
    return [last, k];
}

function inherited(o) {
    let s = "";
    for (const k in o) s += k + (o.hasOwnProperty(k) ? "!" : "?") + o[k];
    return s;
}

function valuesHere(o, other) {
    let s = "";
    for (const k in o) s += k + o[k] + other[k] + o.hasOwnProperty(k) + other.hasOwnProperty(k) + ",";
    return s;
}

function withAccessors(i) {
    return {
        a: i,
        get b() {
            if (i % 4 === 0) delete this.c;
            else this.c = "set" + i;
            return "got";
        },
        c: 3,
        d: 4,
    };
}

function dictionary(i) {
    const o = { a: 1, b: 2, c: 3, d: i };
    delete o.b;
    o.e = 5;
    return o;
}

const proto = { p: 1 };
let out = [];
for (let i = 0; i < 300; i++) {
    out.push(keysAddingProperties({ a: 1, b: 2, c: 3 }));
    out.push(keysDeletingProperties({ a: 1, b: 2, c: 3, d: 4 }));
    out.push(nested({ a: 1, bb: 2 }, { a: 1, c: i }));
    out.push(lastKey(i % 3 ? { x: 1, y: 2 } : { x: 1, stop: 2, y: 3 }).join());
    const child = Object.create(proto);
    child.q = i;
    out.push(inherited(i % 2 ? child : { q: i }));
    const array = [i, 2, 3];
    array.x = "named";
    const others = [{ a: 9, b: 8, c: 7, d: 6 }, { d: 6, c: 7 }, withAccessors(i + 1), array, dictionary(i + 2)];
    const objects = [{ a: i, b: 2, c: 3, d: 4 }, withAccessors(i), array, dictionary(i), child];
    out.push(valuesHere(objects[i % objects.length], others[(i >> 2) % others.length]));
}

print(out.slice(-10).join("|"));
print(out.length);

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/programs/large-native-stack-frames.js
// JIT code passes the arguments of some calls on the native stack, and keeps the operands of some slow paths in its
// native stack frame. Neither may skip over the guard pages that Windows keeps below the committed part of a thread's
// stack, which fault when skipped. The second use is larger than the first, so that it also goes beyond what was ever
// used by more than the guard pages.
function operands(count) {
    return Array.from({ length: count }, () => "value").join(", ");
}

// NB: A call of a native function goes through the call stub, which takes its arguments on the native stack.
const callWithManyArguments = Function("callee", "value", `return callee(${operands(24000)});`);

// NB: An array literal has its elements in the operand record of its slow path, in the frame. The frames also have to
//     get past each other, and are larger than what JIT code leaves of the native stack when it stops calling
//     deeper, so that a frame that recursing runs into the end of the stack with must not be touched at all.
const createLargeArray = Function(
    "value",
    "depth",
    `
    const below = depth > 0 ? createLargeArray(value, depth - 1) : 0;
    const array = [${operands(64000)}];
    return below + array.length;
`
);

for (let warmup = 0; warmup < 500; warmup++) {
    callWithManyArguments(Math.max, warmup);
    createLargeArray(warmup, 0);
}

print(callWithManyArguments(Math.max, 1));
for (const depth of [1, 2, 4, 8]) print(createLargeArray(1, depth));

try {
    createLargeArray(1, Infinity);
} catch (error) {
    print(error instanceof InternalError);
}

// creates, and exceptions it throws and catches, and leaves to the interpreter for what it had not seen.

FILE: Tests/LibJS/JIT/reduce.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
#
# Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
#

"""Reduces a JavaScript program that behaves differently under a JIT mode than in the interpreter.

The program keeps "failing the same way" while lines are removed: it crashes with the same signature, or its output
still differs from the interpreter's. Lines are removed in chunks of halving size (delta debugging), then blocks are
unwrapped (an `if`, loop or `try` replaced by its body), until nothing more can go.

Usage: reduce.py program.js --mode warm [--build Build/release] [-o reduced.js]
"""

import argparse
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable
from typing import List
from typing import Optional

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from machine import wait_until_machine_is_free  # noqa: E402
from modes import INTERPRETER  # noqa: E402
from modes import MODES_BY_NAME  # noqa: E402
from modes import Mode  # noqa: E402

SOURCE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
PANIC_LOCATION = re.compile(r"panicked at ([^\s:]+:\d+)")
ANSI_ESCAPE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m")
NUMBERED_NAME = re.compile(r"\b(v|b|fs|s|r|l|a)[0-9]+\b|\b[0-9]+\b")


@dataclass
class Run:
    exit_code: int
    output: str
    timed_out: bool

    def crash_signature(self) -> Optional[str]:
        """What identifies the crash, if the run crashed: where Rust panicked, or the signal."""
        match = PANIC_LOCATION.search(self.output)
        if match:
            # NB: The verifiers panic in one place for every invariant, so the first violation they name tells
            #     failures apart, with its value, block and frame state numbers left out.
            lines = self.output[match.end() :].splitlines()[1:3]
            detail = " / ".join(NUMBERED_NAME.sub("_", line.strip()) for line in lines)
            return f"panic at {match.group(1)}: {detail[:160]}"
        if self.exit_code < 0:
            return f"signal {-self.exit_code}"
        if self.exit_code >= 128:
            return f"signal {self.exit_code - 128}"
        if "VERIFICATION FAILED" in self.output or "ASSERTION FAILED" in self.output:
            line = next(line for line in self.output.splitlines() if "FAILED" in line)
            return f"assertion {line.strip()[:120]}"
        return None


def run_program(js: Path, path: Path, mode: Mode, seed: int, timeout: float) -> Run:
    wait_until_machine_is_free()
    environment = dict(os.environ)
    environment.pop("LIBJS_JIT", None)
    if mode.jit:
        environment["LIBJS_JIT"] = mode.environment_value(seed)
    try:
        process = subprocess.run(
            [str(js), "--expose-jit-testing", str(path)],
            env=environment,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            timeout=timeout,
            check=False,
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return Run(0, "", True)
    output = ANSI_ESCAPE.sub("", process.stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
    return Run(process.returncode, output, False)


def failure_signature(js: Path, path: Path, mode: Mode, seed: int, timeout: float) -> Optional[str]:
    """How the program fails under `mode`: a crash signature, "mismatch" if its output differs from the
    interpreter's, or None if it does not fail (or the interpreter does not finish)."""
    actual = run_program(js, path, mode, seed, timeout)
    crash = actual.crash_signature()
    if crash:
        return f"crash: {crash}"
    expected = run_program(js, path, INTERPRETER, seed, timeout)
    if expected.timed_out or expected.crash_signature():
        return None
    if actual.timed_out:
        return "timeout"
    if (actual.exit_code, actual.output) != (expected.exit_code, expected.output):
        return "mismatch"
    return None


def reduce_lines(lines: List[str], is_interesting: Callable[[List[str]], bool], log=print) -> List[str]:
    """Removes chunks of lines, then single block openers and their closers, while the program stays interesting."""
    chunk = max(1, len(lines) // 2)
    while True:
        index = 0
        removed_any = False
        while index < len(lines):
            candidate = lines[:index] + lines[index + chunk :]
            if candidate and is_interesting(candidate):
                lines = candidate
                removed_any = True
                log(f"  {len(lines)} lines")
            else:
                index += chunk
        if chunk > 1:
            chunk //= 2
        elif not removed_any:
            break

    # Unwrap blocks: drop a line opening a block together with the line closing it.
    index = 0
    while index < len(lines):
        if lines[index].rstrip().endswith("{"):
            closer = matching_closer(lines, index)
            if closer is not None:
                candidate = lines[:index] + lines[index + 1 : closer] + lines[closer + 1 :]
                if is_interesting(candidate):
                    lines = candidate
                    log(f"  {len(lines)} lines")
                    continue
        index += 1
    return lines


def matching_closer(lines: List[str], opener: int) -> Optional[int]:
    """The line closing the block `lines[opener]` opens, by indentation."""
    indent = len(lines[opener]) - len(lines[opener].lstrip())
    for index in range(opener + 1, len(lines)):
        line = lines[index]
        if line.strip() and len(line) - len(line.lstrip()) == indent:
            return index if line.strip().startswith("}") else None
    return None


def reduce_program(
    js: Path, source: str, mode: Mode, seed: int, scratch: Path, timeout: float = 10.0, log=print
) -> tuple:
    """Reduces `source`, which fails under `mode`. Returns the reduced source and its failure signature."""
    scratch.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    scratch.write_text(source)
    signature = failure_signature(js, scratch, mode, seed, timeout)
    if signature is None:
        return source, None

    def is_interesting(lines: List[str]) -> bool:
        scratch.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
        return failure_signature(js, scratch, mode, seed, timeout) == signature

    lines = reduce_lines(source.splitlines(), is_interesting, log)
    reduced = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    scratch.write_text(reduced)
    return reduced, signature


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("program", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--mode", required=True, help="the JIT mode it fails in (see modes.py)")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1, help="seed of the mode")
    parser.add_argument("--build", type=Path, default=SOURCE_DIR / "Build/release")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=10.0)
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", type=Path, help="where to write the result (default: <program>.reduced.js)")
    arguments = parser.parse_args()

    mode = MODES_BY_NAME[arguments.mode]
    output = arguments.output or arguments.program.with_suffix(".reduced.js")
    reduced, signature = reduce_program(
        arguments.build / "bin/js",
        arguments.program.read_text(),
        mode,
        arguments.seed,
        output,
        arguments.timeout,
    )
    if signature is None:
        print("The program does not fail in that mode.")
        return 1
    print(f"{signature}: {len(reduced.splitlines())} lines in {output}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

function assertEquals(expected, actual, msg) {

        expect(actual.source).toBe(expected.source);
        expect(actual.flags).toBe(expected.flags);
    } else if (expected !== null && typeof expected === "object" && actual !== null && typeof actual === "object") {
        expect(actual).toEqual(expected);
    } else {
        expect(actual).toBe(expected);
    }
}

}

function assertFalse(val, msg) {

    if (typeof fn === "string") {
        expect(() => eval(fn)).toThrow();
    } else {
        expect(fn).toThrow();
    }
}

function assertDoesNotThrow(fn, msg) {
    if (typeof fn === "string") {
        eval(fn);
    } else {
        fn();

}

    assertThrows(f, type_opt);
}

function assertArrayEquals(expected, actual) {
    expect(actual).toEqual(expected);
}

test("es6/array-concat-spreadable-regexp", () => {
    "use strict";
    var re = /abc/;
    // RegExps are not concat-spreadable by default
    assertEquals([re], [].concat(re));

    // RegExps may be individually concat-spreadable
    re[Symbol.isConcatSpreadable] = true;
    ((re[0] = 1), (re[1] = 2), (re[2] = 3), (re.length = 3));
    assertEquals([1, 2, 3], [].concat(re));

    // RegExps may be concat-spreadable
    RegExp.prototype[Symbol.isConcatSpreadable] = true;
    RegExp.prototype.length = 3;

    assertEquals(new Array(3), [].concat(/abc/));
    RegExp.prototype[0] = 1;
    RegExp.prototype[1] = 2;
    RegExp.prototype[2] = 3;
    assertEquals([1, 2, 3], [].concat(/abc/));
});

test("es6/regexp-constructor", () => {
    "use strict";

    function should_not_be_called() {
        throw new Error("should not be called");
    }

    (function () {
        var r = new RegExp("biep");
        assertTrue(r === RegExp(r));
        assertFalse(r === new RegExp(r));
        r[Symbol.match] = false;
        Object.defineProperty(r, "source", { get: should_not_be_called });
        Object.defineProperty(r, "flags", { get: should_not_be_called });
        assertFalse(r === RegExp(r));
    })();

    (function () {
        let allow = false;
        class A extends RegExp {
            get source() {
                if (!allow) throw new Error("should not be called");
                return super.source;
            }
            get flags() {
                if (!allow) throw new Error("should not be called");
                return super.flags;
            }
        }

        var r = new A("biep");
        var r2 = RegExp(r);

        assertFalse(r === r2);
        allow = true;
        assertEquals(r, r2);
        allow = false;
        assertTrue(A.prototype === r.__proto__);
        assertTrue(RegExp.prototype === r2.__proto__);

        var r3 = RegExp(r);
        assertFalse(r3 === r);
        allow = true;
        assertEquals(r3, r);
        allow = false;

        var r4 = new A(r2);
        assertFalse(r4 === r2);
        allow = true;
        assertEquals(r4, r2);
        allow = false;
        assertTrue(A.prototype === r4.__proto__);

        r[Symbol.match] = false;
        var r5 = new A(r);
        assertFalse(r5 === r);
        allow = true;
        assertEquals(r5, r);
        allow = false;
        assertTrue(A.prototype === r5.__proto__);
    })();

    (function () {
        var log = [];
        var match = {
            get source() {
                log.push("source");
                return "biep";
            },
            get flags() {
                log.push("flags");
                return "i";
            },
        };
        Object.defineProperty(match, Symbol.match, {
            get() {
                log.push("match");
                return true;
            },
        });
        var r = RegExp(match);
        assertEquals(["match", "source", "flags"], log);
        assertFalse(r === match);
        assertEquals(/biep/i, r);
    })();

    (function () {
        var log = [];
        var match = {
            get source() {
                log.push("source");
                return "biep";
            },
            get flags() {
                log.push("flags");
                return "i";
            },
        };
        Object.defineProperty(match, Symbol.match, {
            get() {
                log.push("match");
                return true;
            },
        });
        match.constructor = RegExp;
        var r = RegExp(match);
        assertEquals(["match"], log);
        assertTrue(r === match);
    })();

    (function () {
        var r = RegExp("biep", "i");
        r[Symbol.match] = false;
        var r2 = RegExp(r, "g");
        assertFalse(r === r2);
        assertEquals(/biep/i, r);
        assertEquals(/biep/g, r2);
    })();

    (function () {
        class A extends RegExp {
            get ["constructor"]() {
                log.push("constructor");
                return RegExp;
            }
        }
        var r = new A("biep");
        var log = [];
        var r2 = RegExp(r);
        assertEquals(["constructor"], log);
        assertTrue(r === r2);
    })();
});
