        new A();
    }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Super constructor is not a constructor");
});

test("extending String", () => {
    class MyString extends String {}

    const ms = new MyString("abc");
    expect(ms).toBeInstanceOf(MyString);
    expect(ms).toBeInstanceOf(String);
    expect(ms.charAt(1)).toBe("b");

    class MyString2 extends MyString {
        charAt(i) {
            return `#${super.charAt(i)}`;
        }
    }

    const ms2 = new MyString2("abc");
    expect(ms2.charAt(1)).toBe("#b");
});

test("class extends value is invalid", () => {
    expect(() => {
        class A extends 123 {}
    }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Class extends value 123 is not a constructor or null");
});

test("class extends value has invalid prototype", () => {
    function f() {}
    f.prototype = 123;
    expect(() => {
        class A extends f {}
    }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Class extends value has an invalid prototype 123");
});

test("class heritage rejects unparenthesized arrows", () => {
    expect(() => eval("class A extends () => {} {}")).toThrow(SyntaxError);
    expect(() => eval("class A extends async () => {} {}")).toThrow(SyntaxError);
    expect(() => eval("const A = class extends () => {} {};")).toThrow(SyntaxError);
    expect(() => eval("const A = class extends async () => {} {};")).toThrow(SyntaxError);

    expect(() => eval("class A extends (() => {}) {}")).toThrow(TypeError);

    function mixin(callback) {
        expect(callback()).toBe(1);
        return class {};
    }
    class A extends mixin(() => 1) {}
    expect(new A()).toBeInstanceOf(A);
});

        };
    }).toThrow(TypeError);

    expect(() => {
        class A {
            [(Object.preventExtensions({}).prop = 1)];
        }
    }).toThrow(TypeError);

    expect(() => {
        class A extends (Object.preventExtensions({}).prop = 1) {}
    }).toThrow(TypeError);

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/classes/class-constructor-this.js
// Base class constructors bind `this` like other functions, while derived
// ones bind it when super() returns.

test("this in base class constructors", () => {
    class Base {
        constructor(value) {
            this.value = value;
            this.self = this;
        }
    }
    const object = new Base(1);
    expect(object.value).toBe(1);
    expect(object.self).toBe(object);
    expect(object).toBeInstanceOf(Base);
});

test("arrow functions and eval in base class constructors see its this", () => {
    class Arrow {
        constructor() {
            this.getThis = () => this;
        }
    }
    class Eval {
        constructor() {
            this.evaluated = eval("this");
        }
    }
    const arrow = new Arrow();
    expect(arrow.getThis()).toBe(arrow);
    const evaluated = new Eval();
    expect(evaluated.evaluated).toBe(evaluated);
});

test("new.target and super properties in base class constructors", () => {
    class Base {
        constructor() {
            this.target = new.target;
            this.description = super.toString.call(this);
        }
    }
    class Derived extends Base {}
    expect(new Base().target).toBe(Base);
    expect(new Derived().target).toBe(Derived);
    expect(new Base().description).toBe("[object Object]");
});

test("this in derived class constructors", () => {
    class Base {
        constructor() {
            this.base = true;
        }
    }
    class Derived extends Base {
        constructor() {
            expect(() => this).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "|this| has not been initialized");
            super();
            this.derived = true;
        }
    }
    const object = new Derived();
    expect(object.base).toBeTrue();
    expect(object.derived).toBeTrue();
});

test("base class constructors returning objects", () => {
    class Replaced {
        constructor(replacement) {
            this.ignored = true;
            if (replacement) return replacement;
        }
    }
    const replacement = { replaced: true };
    expect(new Replaced(replacement)).toBe(replacement);
    expect(new Replaced(null).ignored).toBeTrue();
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/classes/class-definition-evaluation-order.js
describe("class definition evaluation order", () => {
    test("a computed key is converted to a property key before the next key is evaluated", () => {
        const log = [];
        const key = {
            toString() {
                log.push("first toString");
                return "first";
            },
        };

        class C {
            [key]() {}
            [(log.push("second key"), "second")]() {}
        }

        expect(log).toEqual(["first toString", "second key"]);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(C.prototype)).toEqual(["constructor", "first", "second"]);
    });

    test("a later computed key can't change an earlier one", () => {
        function defineClass() {
            let key = "first";
            class C {
                [key]() {}
                static [((key = "changed"), "second")] = 1;
            }
            return C;
        }

        const C = defineClass();
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(C.prototype)).toEqual(["constructor", "first"]);
        expect(C.second).toBe(1);
    });

    test("the superclass is the value the heritage evaluated to", () => {
        function reassignToNonConstructor() {
            let Base = class {};
            const Original = Base;
            const C = class extends Base {
                [((Base = 1), "m")]() {}
            };
            return Object.getPrototypeOf(C) === Original;
        }

        function reassignToOtherConstructor() {
            class First {}
            class Second {}
            let Base = First;
            const C = class extends Base {
                [((Base = Second), "m")]() {}
            };
            return [Object.getPrototypeOf(C) === First, Object.getPrototypeOf(C.prototype) === First.prototype];
        }

        expect(reassignToNonConstructor()).toBeTrue();
        expect(reassignToOtherConstructor()).toEqual([true, true]);
    });

    test("the heritage is checked before computed keys are evaluated", () => {
        const log = [];
        expect(() => {
            class C extends (0, 1) {
                [(log.push("key"), "m")]() {}
            }
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Class extends value 1 is not a constructor or null");
        expect(log).toEqual([]);

        const Base = new Proxy(function () {}, {
            get(target, property) {
                log.push(`get ${String(property)}`);
                return target[property];
            },
        });
        class D extends Base {
            [(log.push("key"), "m")]() {}
        }
        expect(log).toEqual(["get prototype", "key"]);
    });

    test("a class named by a computed property key has its name while its static elements are evaluated", () => {
        const key = "named";
        const symbol = Symbol("description");
        const object = {
            [key]: class {
                static seenName = this.name;
            },
            [symbol]: class {
                static seenName = this.name;
            },
        };

        expect(object.named.seenName).toBe("named");
        expect(object.named.name).toBe("named");
        expect(object[symbol].seenName).toBe("[description]");
    });

    test("a static method named prototype throws before the next key is evaluated", () => {
        const log = [];
        expect(() => {
            class C {
                static ["prototype"]() {}
                [(log.push("method key"), "x")]() {}
            }
        }).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(() => {
            class C {
                static set ["prototype"](value) {}
                static [(log.push("static key"), "y")] = 1;
            }
        }).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(() => {
            class C {
                static get ["prototype"]() {}
                [(() => {
                    throw new RangeError();
                })()]() {}
            }
        }).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(log).toEqual([]);

        function* generator() {
            class C {
                static ["prototype"]() {}
                [yield "reached"]() {}
            }
        }
        expect(() => generator().next()).toThrow(TypeError);

        class D {
            ["prototype"]() {
                return "instance";
            }
        }
        expect(D.prototype.prototype()).toBe("instance");
    });
});

    });

    class A {
      set foo() {
      }
    }`).not.toEval();
    });

    test("setter with more than one argument", () => {
        expect(`
    class A {
      set foo(bar, baz) {
      }
    }`).not.toEval();
        expect(`
    class A {
      set foo(...bar) {
      }
    }`).not.toEval();
    });

    test("super reference inside different |this| scope", () => {
        expect(`
    class Parent {}

    class Child extends Parent {
      foo() {

      }
    }`).not.toEval();
    });

        expect(`
    class A {
      constructor() {
        super();
      }
    }`).not.toEval();
    });

        expect("class A {} class B extends A { constructor() { (() => new super())(); } }").not.toEval();

        expect("class A {} class B extends A { constructor() { new super; } }").not.toEval();

        expect("class A {} class B extends A { constructor() { super(); new super.x; } }").toEval();

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/classes/class-field-closures-in-functions.js
test("a closure in a field captures a local of a function with a using declaration", () => {
    function run() {
        using resource = null;
        let base = 1;
        class C {
            static fromField = base + 1;
            field = () => base + C.fromField;
            static {
                this.fromBlock = () => base;
            }
        }
        base = 10;
        return [new C().field(), C.fromBlock()];
    }
    expect(run()).toEqual([12, 10]);
});

test("a closure nested deeper in a field captures a local as well", () => {
    function run() {
        using resource = null;
        const value = 1;
        class C {
            field = () => () => {
                try {
                    value++;
                } catch {
                    return value;
                }
            };
        }
        return new C().field()();
    }
    expect(run()).toBe(1);
});

test("can access super via direct eval", () => {
    let superCalled = false;
    const aObject = { a: 1 };
    const bObject = { b: 2 };

    class A {
        constructor() {
            superCalled = true;
        }

        foo() {
            return aObject;
        }

        bar() {
            return bObject;
        }
    }

    class B extends A {
        constructor() {
            eval("super()");
        }
    }

    expect(() => {
        new B();
    }).not.toThrow();

    expect(superCalled).toBeTrue();
    superCalled = false;

    class C extends A {
        constructor() {
            eval("super()");
            return eval("super.foo()");
        }
    }

    expect(() => {
        new C();
    }).not.toThrow();

    expect(superCalled).toBeTrue();
    superCalled = false;

    expect(new C()).toBe(aObject);

    expect(superCalled).toBeTrue();
    superCalled = false;

    class D extends A {
        constructor() {
            eval("super()");
            return eval("super['bar']()");
        }
    }

    expect(() => {
        new D();
    }).not.toThrow();

    expect(superCalled).toBeTrue();
    superCalled = false;

    expect(new D()).toBe(bObject);

    expect(superCalled).toBeTrue();
});

test("cannot access super via indirect eval", () => {
    const indirect = eval;
    let superCalled = false;

    const aObject = { a: 1 };
    const bObject = { b: 1 };

    class A {
        constructor() {
            superCalled = true;
            this.a = aObject;
            this.c = bObject;
        }
    }

    class B extends A {
        constructor() {
            indirect("super()");
        }
    }

    expect(() => {
        new B();
    }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "'super' keyword unexpected here");

    expect(superCalled).toBeFalse();

    class C extends A {
        constructor() {
            super();
            return indirect("super.a");
        }
    }

    expect(() => {
        new C();
    }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "'super' keyword unexpected here");

    expect(superCalled).toBeTrue();
    superCalled = false;

    class D extends A {
        constructor() {
            super();
            return indirect("super['b']");
        }
    }

    expect(() => {
        new D();
    }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "'super' keyword unexpected here");

    expect(superCalled).toBeTrue();
});

test("When no constructor on deriving class @@iterator of %Array.prototype% is not visibly called", () => {
    const oldIterator = Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator];
    var calls = 0;
    Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator] = function () {
        ++calls;
        expect().fail("Called @@iterator");
    };

    class Base {
        constructor(value1, value2) {
            this.value1 = value1;
            this.value2 = value2;
        }
    }

    class Derived extends Base {}

    const noArgumentsDerived = new Derived();
    expect(noArgumentsDerived.value1).toBeUndefined();
    expect(noArgumentsDerived.value2).toBeUndefined();
    expect(noArgumentsDerived).toBeInstanceOf(Base);
    expect(noArgumentsDerived).toBeInstanceOf(Derived);

    const singleArgumentDerived = new Derived(1);
    expect(singleArgumentDerived.value1).toBe(1);
    expect(singleArgumentDerived.value2).toBeUndefined();

    const singleArrayArgumentDerived = new Derived([1, 2]);
    expect(singleArrayArgumentDerived.value1).toEqual([1, 2]);
    expect(singleArrayArgumentDerived.value2).toBeUndefined();

    const doubleArgumentDerived = new Derived(1, 2);
    expect(doubleArgumentDerived.value1).toBe(1);
    expect(doubleArgumentDerived.value2).toBe(2);

    expect(calls).toBe(0);

    class Derived2 extends Base {
        constructor(...args) {
            super(...args);
        }
    }

    expect(() => {
        new Derived2();
    }).toThrowWithMessage(ExpectationError, "Called @@iterator");

    expect(calls).toBe(1);

    Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator] = oldIterator;

    // Now Derived2 is fine again.
    expect(new Derived2()).toBeInstanceOf(Derived2);

    expect(calls).toBe(1);
});

test("constructor return value overrides inheritance and property initialization", () => {
    let calls = 0;
    class Base {
        constructor() {
            this.prop = 1;
            calls++;
        }
    }

    class Derived extends Base {
        constructor() {
            super();

            // Return an empty object instead of Derived/Base object
            return {};
        }
    }

    let object = new Derived();

    expect(calls).toBe(1);
    expect(typeof object.prop).toBe("undefined");
    expect(object instanceof Derived).toBe(false);
    expect(object instanceof Base).toBe(false);
});

test("can call other private methods from methods", () => {
    class A {
        #a() {
            return 1;
        }

        async #b() {
            return 2;
        }

        syncA() {
            return this.#a();
        }

        async asyncA() {
            return this.#a();
        }

        syncB() {
            return this.#b();
        }

        async asyncB() {
            return this.#b();
        }
    }

    var called = false;

    async function check() {
        called = true;
        const a = new A();

        expect(a.syncA()).toBe(1);
        expect(await a.asyncA()).toBe(1);
        expect(await a.syncB()).toBe(2);
        expect(await a.asyncB()).toBe(2);
        return 3;
    }

    var error = null;
    var failed = false;

    check().then(
        value => {
            expect(called).toBeTrue();
            expect(value).toBe(3);
        },
        thrownError => {
            failed = true;
            error = thrownError;
        }
    );

    runQueuedPromiseJobs();

    expect(called).toBeTrue();

    if (failed) throw error;

    expect(failed).toBeFalse();
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/classes/class-private-elements-on-objects.js
// Private elements live in the storage of the objects they are added to, as properties nothing outside the engine sees.

class Stamper extends class {
    constructor(object) {
        return object;
    }
} {
    #field = 1;
    #method() {
        return "method";
    }
    get #accessor() {
        return this.#field;
    }
    set #accessor(value) {
        this.#field = value;
    }

    static has(object) {
        return #field in object;
    }

    static field(object) {
        return object.#field;
    }

    static setField(object, value) {
        object.#field = value;
    }

    static callMethod(object) {
        return object.#method();
    }

    static setMethod(object) {
        object.#method = null;
    }

    static setAccessor(object, value) {
        object.#accessor = value;
        return object.#accessor;
    }
}

test("private elements are not properties", () => {
    const object = new Stamper({ visible: 1 });
    expect(Stamper.has(object)).toBeTrue();
    expect(Reflect.ownKeys(object)).toEqual(["visible"]);
    expect({ ...object }).toEqual({ visible: 1 });
    expect(Object.assign({}, object)).toEqual({ visible: 1 });
    expect(JSON.stringify(object)).toBe('{"visible":1}');
});

test("fields stay writable on frozen objects", () => {
    const object = new Stamper({});
    Object.freeze(object);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(object)).toBeTrue();
    Stamper.setField(object, 2);
    expect(Stamper.field(object)).toBe(2);
    expect(Stamper.setAccessor(object, 3)).toBe(3);
});

test("methods are read-only", () => {
    const object = new Stamper({});
    expect(Stamper.callMethod(object)).toBe("method");
    expect(() => Stamper.setMethod(object)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Cannot set private method");
});

test("proxies keep private elements without calling traps", () => {
    const proxy = new Proxy(
        {},
        new Proxy(
            {},
            {
                get() {
                    throw new Error("trap called");
                },
            }
        )
    );
    new Stamper(proxy);
    Stamper.setField(proxy, 2);
    expect(Stamper.field(proxy)).toBe(2);
});

test("private elements survive dictionary objects losing properties", () => {
    const object = {};
    for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) object[`property${i}`] = i;
    new Stamper(object);
    for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) delete object[`property${i}`];
    expect(Stamper.field(object)).toBe(1);
    expect(Stamper.setAccessor(object, 4)).toBe(4);
    expect(Reflect.ownKeys(object)).toEqual([]);
});

test("each evaluation of a class has private names of its own", () => {
    const makeClass = () =>
        class {
            #field;
            static has(object) {
                return #field in object;
            }
        };
    const A = makeClass();
    const B = makeClass();
    const a = new A();
    expect(A.has(a)).toBeTrue();
    expect(B.has(a)).toBeFalse();
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/classes/class-private-environment-frames.js
test("classes that a function makes see their own private names", () => {
    function makeClass(value) {
        return class {
            #value = value;
            static read(object) {
                return object.#value;
            }
        };
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) {
        const A = makeClass(i);
        const B = makeClass(-i);
        expect(A.read(new A())).toBe(i);
        expect(() => A.read(new B())).toThrow(TypeError);
    }
});

test("methods, arrows and nested functions of a class read its private names", () => {
    class A {
        #x = 1;
        method() {
            const arrow = () => this.#x;
            function nested(object) {
                return object.#x;
            }
            return arrow() + nested(this);
        }
        static make() {
            return new A();
        }
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) expect(A.make().method()).toBe(2);
});

test("nested classes in one function", () => {
    function outer() {
        class A {
            #a = "a";
            inner() {
                class B {
                    #b = "b";
                    read(a) {
                        return a.#a + this.#b;
                    }
                }
                return new B().read(this);
            }
            read() {
                return this.#a;
            }
        }
        const after = new A().read();
        return new A().inner() + after;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) expect(outer()).toBe("aba");
});

test("a function keeps the private environment around it after its class is done", () => {
    class Outer {
        #o = 5;
        test() {
            class Inner {
                #i = 1;
            }
            new Inner();
            return this.#o;
        }
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) expect(new Outer().test()).toBe(5);
});

test("an exception in a class body leaves its private environment", () => {
    class Outer {
        #o = 7;
        test() {
            try {
                class Inner {
                    #i = 1;
                    static [(() => {
                        throw new Error("thrown");
                    })()] = 1;
                }
            } catch {}
            return this.#o;
        }
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) expect(new Outer().test()).toBe(7);
});

test("direct eval in a class method sees its private names", () => {
    class A {
        #x = 3;
        read() {
            return eval("this.#x");
        }
        makeInEval() {
            return eval("class B { #y = 4; static read(b) { return b.#y; } }; B.read(new B()) + this.#x");
        }
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
        expect(new A().read()).toBe(3);
        expect(new A().makeInEval()).toBe(7);
    }
});

test("generators and async functions of a class", async () => {
    function make() {
        return class {
            #v = 2;
            *values() {
                yield this.#v;
                class Inner {
                    #w = 3;
                    static read(inner) {
                        return inner.#w;
                    }
                }
                yield Inner.read(new Inner());
                yield this.#v;
            }
            async value() {
                await null;
                return this.#v;
            }
        };
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 50; ++i) {
        const C = make();
        expect([...new C().values()]).toEqual([2, 3, 2]);
    }
    const C = make();
    let total = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i) total += await new C().value();
    expect(total).toBe(40);
});

test("private identifier not followed by 'in' throws", () => {
    expect(`class A { #field = 2; method() { return #field instanceof 1; }}`).not.toEval();
    expect(`class A { #field = 2; method() { return #field < 1; }}`).not.toEval();
    expect(`class A { #field = 2; method() { return #field + 1; }}`).not.toEval();
    expect(`class A { #field = 2; method() { return #field ** 1; }}`).not.toEval();
    expect(`class A { #field = 2; method() { return !#field; } }`).not.toEval();
    expect(`class A { #field = 2; method() { return ~#field; } }`).not.toEval();
    expect(`class A { #field = 2; method() { return ++#field; } }`).not.toEval();

    expect(`class A { #field = 2; method() { return #field in 1; }}`).toEval();
});

test("private identifier followed by 'in' with invalid grammar throws", () => {
    expect(`
class C {
  #field;

  constructor() {
    #field in () => {};
  }
}
    `).not.toEval();

    expect(`
class C {
  #field;

  constructor() {
    #field in #field in this;
  }
}
    `).not.toEval();

    expect(`
class C {
  #field;

  *gen() {
    #field in yield;
  }
}
    `).not.toEval();

    expect(`
class C {
  #field;

  *gen() {
    #field in yield this;
  }
}
    `).not.toEval();
});

test("private identifier followed by 'in' with parenthesized yield is valid", () => {
    class C {
        #field = 42;

        *gen(obj) {

        }
    }

    const c = new C();
    const it = c.gen({ "#field": true });
    it.next();

    expect(result.value).toBe(true);

});

test("unknown private name gives SyntaxError", () => {

    expect(`obj.#n`).not.toEval();
    expect(`this.#n`).not.toEval();
    expect(`if (#n) 1;`).not.toEval();

    expect(`1?.n.#n`).not.toEval();

describe("private names refer to the outer class after an inner class definition ends abruptly", () => {
    const thrower = () => {
        throw new Error();
    };

    test("exception from a computed key", () => {
        class Outer {
            #x = 1;
            static read(object) {
                try {
                    class Inner {
                        #x = 2;
                        [thrower()] = 1;
                    }
                } catch {}
                return object.#x;
            }
        }
        expect(Outer.read(new Outer())).toBe(1);
    });

    test("exception from a static initialization block", () => {
        class Outer {
            #x = 1;
            static read(object) {
                try {
                    class Inner {
                        #x = 2;
                        static {
                            thrower();
                        }
                    }
                } catch {}
                return object.#x;
            }
        }
        expect(Outer.read(new Outer())).toBe(1);
    });

    test("exception from the heritage", () => {
        class Outer {
            #x = 1;
            static read(object) {
                try {
                    class Inner extends thrower() {
                        #x = 2;
                    }
                } catch {}
                return object.#x;
            }
        }
        expect(Outer.read(new Outer())).toBe(1);
    });

    test("exception from a computed key of a class in a computed key", () => {
        class Outer {
            #x = 1;
            static read(object) {
                try {
                    class Middle {
                        #x = 2;
                        [(class {
                            #x = 3;
                            [thrower()] = 1;
                        },
                        "key")] = 1;
                    }
                } catch {}
                return object.#x;
            }
        }
        expect(Outer.read(new Outer())).toBe(1);
    });

    test("generator return from a computed key", () => {
        const seen = [];
        class Outer {
            #x = 1;
            static *read(object) {
                try {
                    class Inner {
                        #x = 2;
                        [yield] = 1;
                    }
                } finally {
                    seen.push(object.#x);
                }
            }
        }
        const generator = Outer.read(new Outer());
        generator.next();
        expect(generator.return("r")).toEqual({ value: "r", done: true });
        expect(seen).toEqual([1]);
    });
});

test("anonymous function initializer is named by a computed key", () => {

    const symbol = Symbol("description");

        static [symbol] = () => {};
        [key] = () => {};
        static [(0, "notAnonymous")] = (0, function () {});
    }

    expect(A.named.name).toBe("named");
    expect(A.namedClass.name).toBe("namedClass");
    expect(A.namedClass.seenName).toBe("namedClass");
    expect(A[symbol].name).toBe("[description]");
    expect(new A().named.name).toBe("named");
    expect(A.notAnonymous.name).toBe("");
});

test("each evaluation of a class names initializers by its own computed keys", () => {
    function makeClass(key) {
        return class {
            [key] = function () {};
        };
    }

    const First = makeClass("first");
    const Second = makeClass("second");
    expect(new First().first.name).toBe("first");
    expect(new Second().second.name).toBe("second");
});

describe("class fields with a 'special' name", () => {
    test("static", () => {
        class A {
            static;
        }
        expect("static" in new A()).toBeTrue();

        class B {
            static;
        }
        expect("static" in new B()).toBeTrue();

        class C {
            static a;
        }
        expect("static" in new C()).toBeFalse();
        expect("a" in new C()).toBeFalse();

        expect("a" in C).toBeTrue();
        expect("static" in C).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("async", () => {
        class A {
            async;
        }
        expect("async" in new A()).toBeTrue();

        class B {
            async;
        }
        expect("async" in new B()).toBeTrue();

        class C {
            async;
            a;
        }
        expect("async" in new C()).toBeTrue();
        expect("a" in new C()).toBeTrue();
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/classes/class-static-block-function-declarations.js
test("function declarations of a static block are not bindings of the block around the class", () => {
    function inBlock() {
        var b = "outer";
        {
            class C {
                static {
                    function b() {}
                }
            }
            return typeof b;
        }
    }
    function inCatch() {
        try {
            throw 0;
        } catch (e) {
            class C {
                static {
                    function e() {}
                }
            }
            return typeof e;
        }
    }
    function inSwitch() {
        switch (1) {
            case 1:
                class C {
                    static {
                        function b() {}
                    }
                }
                return typeof b;
        }
    }
    expect(inBlock()).toBe("string");
    expect(inCatch()).toBe("number");
    expect(inSwitch()).toBe("undefined");
});

test("function declarations of a static block can use private names", () => {
    let result;
    {
        class C {
            static #p = 7;
            static {
                function read(o) {
                    return o.#p;
                }
                result = read(C);
            }
        }
        expect(() => read(C)).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "'read' is not defined");
    }
    expect(result).toBe(7);
});

                }
                result = b();
            }

        static {
            const makeGenerator = function* await(await) {
                yield await;
            };

            expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: 42, done: false });
            expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: undefined, done: true });

                expect(await).toBe(42);

                    static {
                        let [b] = [];
                    }
                },
            ] = [];
            return typeof a;
        }
        expect(f()).toBe("function");
    });

    test("destructuring declaration with the same name", () => {
        expect("const [a = class { static { let [a] = []; } }] = [];").toEval();
    });

    test("destructured catch parameter", () => {
        function f() {
            const {
                a,
                b = class {
                    static {
                        try {
                        } catch ({ message }) {}
                    }
                },
            } = { a: 1 };
            return a;
        }
        expect(f()).toBe(1);
    });
});

test("a direct eval in a static block sees the block's own arguments object", () => {
    class A {
        static {
            this.result = eval("typeof arguments + ',' + arguments.length");
        }
    }
    expect(A.result).toBe("object,0");

    class B {
        static {
            this.result = (() => eval("arguments.length"))();
        }
    }
    expect(B.result).toBe(0);

    function outer() {
        class C {
            static {
                this.result = eval("arguments.length");
            }
        }
        return [C.result, arguments.length];
    }
    expect(outer(1, 2, 3)).toEqual([0, 3]);
});
