FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/functions/function-declaration-scoping-with-destructured-params.js
// This test covers a bug where function declarations inside functions with
// destructured parameters were not visible in nested closures. The issue was
// that CreateVariableEnvironment (which holds function declarations) was not
// properly chained as the parent of the subsequent lexical environment.

describe("function declarations accessible from closures with destructured object params", () => {
    test("basic: aliased destructured param with default", () => {
        function go({ tz: o = 420 }) {
            let s = 69;
            function y() {
                return s;
            }
            return {
                _foo: y,
                _bar: function () {
                    return y();
                },
            };
        }
        let result = go({});
        expect(result._foo()).toBe(69);
        expect(result._bar()).toBe(69);
    });

    test("simple destructured param, no default", () => {
        function go({ x }) {
            let val = 42;
            function inner() {
                return val + x;
            }
            return function () {
                return inner();
            };
        }
        expect(go({ x: 8 })()).toBe(50);
    });

    test("multiple destructured params", () => {
        function go({ a }, { b }) {
            function inner() {
                return a + b;
            }
            return function () {
                return inner();
            };
        }
        expect(go({ a: 10 }, { b: 20 })()).toBe(30);
    });

    test("destructured param with default value used", () => {
        function go({ x = 100 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            return function () {
                return inner();
            };
        }
        expect(go({})()).toBe(100);
        expect(go({ x: 5 })()).toBe(5);
    });

    test("destructured param with default value, plus let binding", () => {
        function go({ x = 100 }) {
            let y = x + 1;
            function inner() {
                return y;
            }
            return function () {
                return inner();
            };
        }
        expect(go({})()).toBe(101);
        expect(go({ x: 5 })()).toBe(6);
    });

    test("nested destructured param", () => {
        function go({ a: { b } }) {
            function inner() {
                return b;
            }
            return function () {
                return inner();
            };
        }
        expect(go({ a: { b: 99 } })()).toBe(99);
    });

    test("rest element in destructured param", () => {
        function go({ x, ...rest }) {
            function inner() {
                return rest.y;
            }
            return function () {
                return inner();
            };
        }
        expect(go({ x: 1, y: 2 })()).toBe(2);
    });

    test("arrow function closure over function declaration", () => {
        function go({ x = 1 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            return () => inner();
        }
        expect(go({})()).toBe(1);
    });

    test("multiple function declarations", () => {
        function go({ x = 10 }) {
            let y = 20;
            function a() {
                return x;
            }
            function b() {
                return y;
            }
            return function () {
                return a() + b();
            };
        }
        expect(go({})()).toBe(30);
    });

    test("function declaration references another function declaration", () => {
        function go({ x = 5 }) {
            function a() {
                return x;
            }
            function b() {
                return a() * 2;
            }
            return function () {
                return b();
            };
        }
        expect(go({})()).toBe(10);
    });

    test("closure in object literal method shorthand", () => {
        function go({ x = 7 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            return {
                get() {
                    return inner();
                },
            };
        }
        expect(go({}).get()).toBe(7);
    });

    test("closure in computed property value", () => {
        function go({ x = 3 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            let key = "result";
            return {
                [key]: function () {
                    return inner();
                },
            };
        }
        expect(go({}).result()).toBe(3);
    });

    test("closure in getter", () => {
        function go({ x = 11 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            return {
                get value() {
                    return inner();
                },
            };
        }
        expect(go({}).value).toBe(11);
    });

    test("closure in setter", () => {
        function go({ x = 0 }) {
            let captured = x;
            function inner(v) {
                captured = v;
            }
            function get() {
                return captured;
            }
            return {
                set value(v) {
                    inner(v);
                },
                read() {
                    return get();
                },
            };
        }
        let obj = go({});
        obj.value = 42;
        expect(obj.read()).toBe(42);
    });

    test("IIFE closure over function declaration", () => {
        function go({ x = 5 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            return (function () {
                return inner();
            })();
        }
        expect(go({})).toBe(5);
    });

    test("deeply nested closure", () => {
        function go({ x = 1 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            return function () {
                return function () {
                    return function () {
                        return inner();
                    };
                };
            };
        }
        expect(go({})()()()).toBe(1);
    });

    test("function declaration with same name as destructured binding", () => {
        function go({ x = 1 }) {
            function x() {
                return 42;
            }
            return function () {
                return x();
            };
        }
        expect(go({})()).toBe(42);
    });

    test("var and function declaration coexist", () => {
        function go({ x = 1 }) {
            var z = 100;
            function inner() {
                return x + z;
            }
            return function () {
                return inner();
            };
        }
        expect(go({})()).toBe(101);
    });

    test("let, const, var, and function declaration all present", () => {
        function go({ x = 1 }) {
            let a = 10;
            const b = 20;
            var c = 30;
            function inner() {
                return x + a + b + c;
            }
            return function () {
                return inner();
            };
        }
        expect(go({})()).toBe(61);
    });

    test("function declaration mutates closed-over let", () => {
        function go({ x = 0 }) {
            let counter = x;
            function increment() {
                counter++;
                return counter;
            }
            return function () {
                return increment();
            };
        }
        let inc = go({});
        expect(inc()).toBe(1);
        expect(inc()).toBe(2);
        expect(inc()).toBe(3);
    });

    test("multiple closures share same function declaration", () => {
        function go({ x = 0 }) {
            let state = x;
            function get() {
                return state;
            }
            function set(v) {
                state = v;
            }
            return {
                reader: function () {
                    return get();
                },
                writer: function (v) {
                    set(v);
                },
            };
        }
        let obj = go({});
        expect(obj.reader()).toBe(0);
        obj.writer(42);
        expect(obj.reader()).toBe(42);
    });
});

describe("function declarations in arrow functions with destructured params", () => {
    // Arrow functions don't have their own `arguments` or `this`,
    // but they still create variable environments for function declarations
    // (well, arrow functions can't have function declarations in their body
    // unless using a block, but let's test the block form)

    test("block-body arrow with destructured param", () => {
        let go = ({ x = 1 }) => {
            let y = x + 1;
            // Arrow functions can't have function declarations in non-strict mode
            // but they can have them in blocks... let's use a let-bound function instead
            let inner = function () {
                return y;
            };
            return function () {
                return inner();
            };
        };
        expect(go({})()).toBe(2);
    });
});

describe("edge cases", () => {
    test("empty destructuring pattern with default triggers separate var env", () => {
        function go({} = {}) {
            function inner() {
                return 42;
            }
            return function () {
                return inner();
            };
        }
        expect(go()()).toBe(42);
    });

    test("deeply nested destructuring with defaults", () => {
        function go({
            a: {
                b: { c = 99 },
            },
        }) {
            function inner() {
                return c;
            }
            return function () {
                return inner();
            };
        }
        expect(go({ a: { b: {} } })()).toBe(99);
    });

    test("destructured param shadows outer variable", () => {
        let x = "outer";
        function go({ x = "default" }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            return function () {
                return inner();
            };
        }
        expect(go({})()).toBe("default");
        expect(go({ x: "passed" })()).toBe("passed");
        expect(x).toBe("outer");
    });

    test("function declaration called during object construction in return", () => {
        function go({ x = 1 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            return {
                a: inner(),
                b: (function () {
                    return inner();
                })(),
                c: (() => inner())(),
            };
        }
        let result = go({ x: 7 });
        expect(result.a).toBe(7);
        expect(result.b).toBe(7);
        expect(result.c).toBe(7);
    });

    test("function declaration used in array literal", () => {
        function go({ x = 1 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            return [
                inner,
                function () {
                    return inner();
                },
                () => inner(),
            ];
        }
        let result = go({ x: 3 });
        expect(result[0]()).toBe(3);
        expect(result[1]()).toBe(3);
        expect(result[2]()).toBe(3);
    });

    test("function declaration used as callback", () => {
        function go({ x = 1 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            return [1, 2, 3].map(function () {
                return inner();
            });
        }
        expect(go({ x: 5 })).toEqual([5, 5, 5]);
    });

    test("function declaration in try/catch inside function with destructured params", () => {
        function go({ x = 1 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            try {
                return function () {
                    return inner();
                };
            } catch (e) {
                return null;
            }
        }
        expect(go({})()).toBe(1);
    });

    test("function declaration in for loop inside function with destructured params", () => {
        function go({ x = 1 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            let results = [];
            for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
                results.push(function () {
                    return inner() + i;
                });
            }
            return results;
        }
        let fns = go({});
        // let i creates a new binding per iteration
        expect(fns[0]()).toBe(1);
        expect(fns[1]()).toBe(2);
        expect(fns[2]()).toBe(3);
    });

    test("function declaration in switch inside function with destructured params", () => {
        function go({ x = 1 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            switch (x) {
                case 1:
                    return function () {
                        return inner();
                    };
                default:
                    return function () {
                        return inner() * 2;
                    };
            }
        }
        expect(go({})()).toBe(1);
        expect(go({ x: 5 })()).toBe(10);
    });

    test("function declaration referenced via eval", () => {
        function go({ x = 1 }) {
            function inner() {
                return x;
            }
            return function () {
                return eval("inner()");
            };
        }
        expect(go({ x: 77 })()).toBe(77);
    });

    test("multiple independent closures each see the same function declaration", () => {
        function go({ x = 0 }) {
            let state = x;
            function inc() {
                return ++state;
            }
            let a = function () {
                return inc();
            };
            let b = function () {
                return inc();
            };
            return { a, b };
        }
        let obj = go({});
        expect(obj.a()).toBe(1);
        expect(obj.b()).toBe(2);
        expect(obj.a()).toBe(3);
    });

    test("recursive function declaration inside function with destructured params", () => {
        function go({ n }) {
            function factorial(x) {
                if (x <= 1) return 1;
                return x * factorial(x - 1);
            }
            return function () {
                return factorial(n);
            };
        }
        expect(go({ n: 5 })()).toBe(120);
    });

    test("mutually recursive function declarations", () => {
        function go({ x = true }) {
            function isEven(n) {
                if (n === 0) return true;
                return isOdd(n - 1);
            }
            function isOdd(n) {
                if (n === 0) return false;
                return isEven(n - 1);
            }
            return function (n) {
                return x ? isEven(n) : isOdd(n);
            };
        }
        let checkEven = go({});
        expect(checkEven(4)).toBeTrue();
        expect(checkEven(5)).toBeFalse();
        let checkOdd = go({ x: false });
        expect(checkOdd(3)).toBeTrue();
        expect(checkOdd(4)).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("the original tumblr bug repro", () => {
        function go({ tz: o = 420 }) {
            let s = 69;
            function y() {
                return s;
            }
            return {
                _foo: y,
                _bar: function () {
                    y();
                },
            };
        }
        expect(() => go({})).not.toThrow();
        let result = go({});
        expect(result._foo()).toBe(69);
        expect(() => result._bar()).not.toThrow();
    });
});

test("single default parameter", () => {
    function func(a = 6) {
        return typeof a;
    }

    const arrowFunc = (a = 6) => typeof a;

    expect(func()).toBe("number");
    expect(func(5)).toBe("number");
    expect(func(undefined)).toBe("number");
    expect(func(false)).toBe("boolean");
    expect(func(null)).toBe("object");
    expect(func({})).toBe("object");

    expect(arrowFunc()).toBe("number");
    expect(arrowFunc(5)).toBe("number");
    expect(arrowFunc(undefined)).toBe("number");
    expect(arrowFunc(false)).toBe("boolean");
    expect(arrowFunc(null)).toBe("object");
    expect(arrowFunc({})).toBe("object");
});

test("two parameters, second one is default", () => {
    function func(a, b = 1) {
        return a + b;
    }

    const arrowFunc = (a, b = 1) => a + b;

    expect(func(4, 5)).toBe(9);
    expect(func(4)).toBe(5);
    expect(func(4, undefined)).toBe(5);
    expect(func()).toBeNaN();

    expect(arrowFunc(4, 5)).toBe(9);
    expect(arrowFunc(4)).toBe(5);
    expect(arrowFunc(4, undefined)).toBe(5);
    expect(arrowFunc()).toBeNaN();
});

test("two parameters, first one is default", () => {

    expect(arrowFunc(undefined, 4)).toBe(9);

test("parameter default values allow the in operator", () => {
    function func(object, present = "present" in object) {
        return present;
    }

    const arrowFunc = (object, present = "present" in object) => present;
    const object = {
        method(object, present = "present" in object) {
            return present;
        },
    };

    for (const callback of [func, arrowFunc, object.method]) {
        expect(callback({ present: true })).toBeTrue();
        expect(callback({})).toBeFalse();
        expect(callback(null, "explicit")).toBe("explicit");
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/functions/function-destructuring-parameters.js
describe("parsing", () => {
    test("single parameter, single name", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction({ a }) { }`).toEval();
    });

    test("single parameter, single name with rest values", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction({ a, ...b }) { }`).toEval();
    });

    test("single parameter, single aliased name", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction({ a: b }) { }`).toEval();
    });

    test("single parameter, single aliased name with rest values", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction({ a: b, ...c }) { }`).toEval();
    });

    test("multiple parameters, single destructuring parameter", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction(a, { b }) { }`).toEval();
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction({ a }, { b }) { }`).toEval();
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters with rest parameters", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction({ a }, { bar, ...b }) { }`).toEval();
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters with rest parameters 2", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction({ bar, ...a }, { baz, ...b }) { }`).toEval();
    });

    test("duplicate names across destructuring parameters are not allowed", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction({ bar, ...a }, { bar, ...b }) { }`).not.toEval();
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters, array patterns", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction({ bar, ...a }, [ b ]) { }`).toEval();
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters with rest parameters, array patterns", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction({ bar, ...a }, [ b, ...rest ]) { }`).toEval();
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters with rest parameters, array patterns with recursive patterns", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction({ bar, ...a }, [ b, [ c ] ]) { }`).toEval();
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters with rest parameters, array patterns with recursive patterns 2", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction({ bar, ...a }, [ b, [ c, ...{ d } ] ]) { }`).toEval();
    });

    test("eval and arguments are allowed in sloppy destructuring parameters", () => {
        expect(`function testFunction([eval]) { }`).toEval();
        expect(`function testFunction({ value: arguments }) { }`).toEval();
        expect(`({ method([eval]) { } });`).toEval();
        expect(`({ set value({ value: arguments }) { } });`).toEval();
    });

    test("eval and arguments are not allowed in strict destructuring parameters", () => {
        for (const source of [
            `"use strict"; function testFunction([eval]) { }`,
            `"use strict"; function testFunction({ value: eval }) { }`,
            `"use strict"; function testFunction([arguments]) { }`,
            `"use strict"; function testFunction({ value: arguments }) { }`,
            `"use strict"; ({ method([eval]) { } });`,
            `"use strict"; ({ set value({ value: arguments }) { } });`,
            `class C { method([eval]) { } }`,
            `class C { set value({ value: arguments }) { } }`,
        ]) {
            expect(source).not.toEval();
        }
    });
});

describe("evaluating", () => {
    test("single parameter, single name", () => {
        function testFunction({ a }) {
            return a;
        }

        expect(testFunction({ a: 42 })).toBe(42);
    });

    test("single parameter, single name with rest values", () => {
        function testFunction({ a, ...b }) {
            return b.foo;
        }

        expect(testFunction({ a: 42, foo: "yoinks" })).toBe("yoinks");
    });

    test("single parameter, single aliased name", () => {
        function testFunction({ a: b }) {
            return b;
        }

        expect(testFunction({ a: 42, foo: "yoinks" })).toBe(42);
    });

    test("single parameter, single aliased name with rest values", () => {
        function testFunction({ a: b, ...c }) {
            return b + c.foo;
        }

        expect(testFunction({ a: 42, foo: "yoinks" })).toBe("42yoinks");
    });

    test("multiple parameters, single destructuring parameter", () => {
        function testFunction(a, { b }) {
            return a + b;
        }

        expect(testFunction("27", { b: 42 })).toBe("2742");
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters", () => {
        function testFunction({ a }, { b }) {
            return a + b;
        }

        expect(testFunction({ a: "27" }, { b: 42 })).toBe("2742");
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters with rest parameters", () => {
        function testFunction({ a }, { bar, ...b }) {
            return bar;
        }

        expect(testFunction({ a: "27" }, { b: 42 })).toBeUndefined();
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters with rest parameters 2", () => {
        function testFunction({ bar, ...a }, { baz, ...b }) {
            return a.foo + b.foo;
        }

        expect(testFunction({ foo: "27" }, { foo: 42 })).toBe("2742");
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters, array patterns", () => {
        function testFunction({ bar, ...a }, [b]) {
            return a.foo + b;
        }

        expect(testFunction({ foo: "27" }, [42])).toBe("2742");
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters with rest parameters, array patterns", () => {
        function testFunction({ bar, ...a }, [b, ...rest]) {
            return rest.length + a.foo;
        }

        expect(testFunction({ foo: "20" }, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4])).toBe("420");
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters with rest parameters, array patterns with recursive patterns", () => {
        function testFunction({ bar, ...a }, [b, [c]]) {
            return a.foo + b + c;
        }

        expect(testFunction({ foo: "20" }, [0, [1, 2, 3, 4]])).toBe("2001");
    });

    test("multiple destructuring parameters with rest parameters, array patterns with recursive patterns 2", () => {
        function testFunction({ bar, ...a }, [b, [c, ...{ length }]]) {
            return a.foo + b + c + length;
        }

        expect(testFunction({ foo: "20" }, [0, [1, 2, 3, 4]])).toBe("20013");
    });

    test("patterns with default", () => {
        function testFunction({ a = "27", b: bar }) {
            return a + bar;
        }

        expect(testFunction({ b: 42 })).toBe("2742");
    });
});

describe("names of a parameter's binding pattern are uninitialized until they are bound", () => {
    test("read by an initializer", () => {
        function arrayPattern([a = b, b]) {}
        function objectPattern({ a = b, b }) {}
        function earlierPattern([a = b], [b]) {}
        function plainParameter(a = b, [b]) {}
        function typeofName([a = typeof b, b]) {}
        const arrow = ([a = b, b]) => {};

        expect(() => arrayPattern([])).toThrow(ReferenceError);
        expect(() => objectPattern({})).toThrow(ReferenceError);
        expect(() => earlierPattern([], [])).toThrow(ReferenceError);
        expect(() => plainParameter(undefined, [])).toThrow(ReferenceError);
        expect(() => typeofName([])).toThrow(ReferenceError);
        expect(() => arrow([])).toThrow(ReferenceError);
    });

    test("assigned by an initializer", () => {
        function assigned([a = (b = 1), b]) {}
        function updated([a = b++, b]) {}

        expect(() => assigned([])).toThrow(ReferenceError);
        expect(() => updated([])).toThrow(ReferenceError);
    });

    test("read once they are bound", () => {
        function arrayPattern([a, b = a]) {
            return b;
        }
        function objectPattern({ a, b = a }, c = b) {
            return c;
        }

        expect(arrayPattern([1])).toBe(1);
        expect(objectPattern({ a: 2 })).toBe(2);
    });
});

test("function with duplicate parameter names", () => {
    function foo(bar, _, bar) {
        return bar;
    }
    expect(foo(1, 2, 3)).toBe(3);
});

test("syntax errors", () => {
    // Regular function in strict mode
    expect(`
        "use strict";
        function foo(bar, bar) {}
    `).not.toEval();

    // Arrow function in strict mode
    expect(`
        "use strict";
        const foo = (bar, bar) => {};
    `).not.toEval();

    // Arrow function in non-strict mode
    expect(`
        const foo = (bar, bar) => {};
    `).not.toEval();

    // Regular function with rest parameter
    expect(`
        function foo(bar, ...bar) {}
    `).not.toEval();

    // Regular function with duplicate parameters before rest parameter
    expect(`
        function foo(bar, bar, ...baz) {}
    `).not.toEval();

    // Arrow function with rest parameter
    expect(`
        const foo = (bar, ...bar) => {};
    `).not.toEval();

    // Regular function with default parameter
    expect(`
        function foo(bar, bar = 1) {}
    `).not.toEval();

    // Arrow function with default parameter
    expect(`
        const foo = (bar, bar = 1) => {};
    `).not.toEval();

    // Duplicate across destructuring parameters
    expect(`
        function foo({ bar }, { bar }) {}
    `).not.toEval();

    // Duplicate between identifier and destructuring parameter
    expect(`
        function foo(bar, { bar }) {}
    `).not.toEval();

    // Duplicate between destructuring and identifier parameter
    expect(`
        function foo({ bar }, bar) {}
    `).not.toEval();

    // Object method with duplicate parameters
    expect(`
        ({ foo(bar, bar) {} });
    `).not.toEval();

    // Object method with rest parameter
    expect(`
        ({ foo(bar, ...bar) {} });
    `).not.toEval();
});

test("sloppy generators and async functions with a simple parameter list may repeat a parameter name", () => {
    expect("function* g(a, a) {}").toEval();
    expect("async function f(a, a) {}").toEval();
    expect("async function* h(a, a) {}").toEval();
    expect("(function* (a, a) {})").toEval();
    expect("(async function (a, a) {})").toEval();
    expect("(async function* (a, a) {})").toEval();

    function* generator(a, a) {
        yield a;
    }
    expect(generator(1, 2).next().value).toBe(2);
});

test("other generators and async functions may not repeat a parameter name", () => {
    expect("'use strict'; function* g(a, a) {}").not.toEval();
    expect("async function f(a, a) { 'use strict'; }").not.toEval();
    expect("function* g(a, [a]) {}").not.toEval();
    expect("async function f(a, a = 1) {}").not.toEval();
    expect("async (a, a) => {}").not.toEval();
    expect("({ *m(a, a) {} })").not.toEval();
    expect("({ async m(a, a) {} })").not.toEval();
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/functions/function-environment-this-binding.js
// Functions whose code never reads `this`, `new.target` or `super` through their environment get a lighter environment
// for their captured bindings. Everything that does read them has to keep working.

const ITERATIONS = 5000;

function repeated(callback) {
    let result;
    for (let i = 0; i < ITERATIONS; ++i) result = callback(i);
    return result;
}

test("closures that do not read this through their environment", () => {
    function counter(start) {
        let count = start;
        return () => ++count;
    }
    const next = repeated(i => counter(i));
    expect(next()).toBe(ITERATIONS);
    expect(next()).toBe(ITERATIONS + 1);
});

test("this read directly next to captured bindings", () => {
    function method(value) {
        const captured = () => value;
        return [this.name, captured()];
    }
    const object = { name: "object", method };
    expect(repeated(i => object.method(i))).toEqual(["object", ITERATIONS - 1]);

    function sloppy() {
        const value = 1;
        const captured = () => value;
        captured();
        return typeof this;
    }
    expect(repeated(() => sloppy.call(1))).toBe("object");
    expect(repeated(() => sloppy())).toBe("object");
});

test("this read through arrow functions", () => {
    function method(value) {
        return () => () => [this.name, value];
    }
    const object = { name: "object", method };
    expect(repeated(i => object.method(i)()())).toEqual(["object", ITERATIONS - 1]);
    expect(object.method(1)()()).toEqual(["object", 1]);
});

test("arrow functions with captured bindings of their own", () => {
    function method() {
        return value => {
            const captured = () => value;
            return [this.name, captured()];
        };
    }
    const object = { name: "object", method };
    expect(repeated(i => object.method()(i))).toEqual(["object", ITERATIONS - 1]);

    const lexical = value => {
        const captured = () => value;
        return captured();
    };
    expect(repeated(i => lexical(i))).toBe(ITERATIONS - 1);
});

test("new.target next to captured bindings", () => {
    function Direct(value) {
        const captured = () => value;
        this.value = captured();
        this.target = new.target;
    }
    expect(repeated(i => new Direct(i)).target).toBe(Direct);
    expect(Direct.call({}, 1)).toBeUndefined();

    function ThroughArrow(value) {
        const captured = () => [new.target, value];
        this.result = captured();
    }
    expect(repeated(i => new ThroughArrow(i)).result).toEqual([ThroughArrow, ITERATIONS - 1]);
});

test("super next to captured bindings", () => {
    class Base {
        constructor(value) {
            this.base = value;
        }
        method() {
            return "base";
        }
    }
    class Derived extends Base {
        constructor(value) {
            const captured = () => value;
            super(captured());
            this.derived = captured();
        }
        method(value) {
            const captured = () => value;
            return [super.method(), captured()];
        }
        arrow(value) {
            return (() => [super.method(), value])();
        }
    }
    class ThroughArrow extends Base {
        constructor(value) {
            const call = () => super(value);
            call();
            this.after = value;
        }
    }
    const object = repeated(i => new Derived(i));
    expect(object.base).toBe(ITERATIONS - 1);
    expect(object.derived).toBe(ITERATIONS - 1);
    expect(repeated(i => object.method(i))).toEqual(["base", ITERATIONS - 1]);
    expect(repeated(i => object.arrow(i))).toEqual(["base", ITERATIONS - 1]);
    expect(repeated(i => new ThroughArrow(i)).base).toBe(ITERATIONS - 1);

    class Uninitialized extends Base {
        constructor() {
            const read = () => this;
            expect(read).toThrow(ReferenceError);
            super(1);
            expect(read().base).toBe(1);
        }
    }
    new Uninitialized();
});

test("direct eval reads everything", () => {
    function evaluates(value) {
        const captured = () => value;
        captured();
        return [eval("this.name"), eval("new.target"), eval("value")];
    }
    expect(evaluates.call({ name: "object" }, 1)).toEqual(["object", undefined, 1]);

    function evaluatesInArrow(value) {
        return (() => [eval("this.name"), eval("new.target"), eval("value")])();
    }
    expect(evaluatesInArrow.call({ name: "object" }, 1)).toEqual(["object", undefined, 1]);

    function nested(value) {
        const inner = () => eval("var added = value + 1; added");
        return inner();
    }
    expect(nested(1)).toBe(2);

    class Base {
        method() {
            return "base";
        }
    }
    class Derived extends Base {
        method() {
            const value = 1;
            return () => eval("super.method()") + value;
        }
    }
    expect(new Derived().method()()).toBe("base1");
});

test("generators and async functions with captured bindings", () => {
    function* generator(value) {
        const captured = () => value;
        yield this.name;
        yield captured();
        yield (() => this.name)();
    }
    expect([...generator.call({ name: "object" }, 1)]).toEqual(["object", 1, "object"]);

    let result;
    async function asynchronous(value) {
        const captured = () => value;
        await null;
        result = [this.name, captured(), (() => this.name)()];
    }
    asynchronous.call({ name: "object" }, 1);
    runQueuedPromiseJobs();
    expect(result).toEqual(["object", 1, "object"]);
});

test("arguments objects and parameter scopes", () => {
    function mapped(a) {
        const captured = () => a;
        arguments[0] = 2;
        return [captured(), arguments.length, this.name];
    }
    expect(repeated(() => mapped.call({ name: "object" }, 1))).toEqual([2, 1, "object"]);

    function defaults(a, b = () => a) {
        var a;
        return b();
    }
    expect(repeated(() => defaults(1))).toBe(1);
});

test("class fields and static blocks", () => {
    class Fields {
        value = 1;
        arrow = () => this.value;
        static captured = (() => this.name)();
        static {
            const value = 2;
            const read = () => [this.name, value];
            this.read = read();
        }
    }
    expect(repeated(() => new Fields().arrow())).toBe(1);
    expect(Fields.captured).toBe("Fields");
    expect(Fields.read).toEqual(["Fields", 2]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/functions/function-evaluation-order.js
describe("CallExpression", () => {
    test("callee is evaluated before arguments", () => {
        function foo() {}
        const values = [];

        [foo][(values.push("callee"), 0)](values.push("args"));

        expect(values).toEqual(["callee", "args"]);
    });

    test("arguments are evaluated in order", () => {
        function foo() {}
        const values = [];

        foo(values.push("arg1"), values.push("arg2"), values.push("arg3"));

        expect(values).toEqual(["arg1", "arg2", "arg3"]);
    });

    test("arguments are evaluated before callee is checked for its type", () => {
        const values = [];

        expect(() => {
            "foo"(values.push("args"));
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "foo is not a function");
        expect(values).toEqual(["args"]);

        expect(() => {
            "foo"(bar);
        }).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "'bar' is not defined");
    });
});

describe("NewExpression", () => {
    test("callee is evaluated before arguments", () => {
        function Foo() {}
        const values = [];

        new [Foo][(values.push("callee"), 0)](values.push("args"));

        expect(values).toEqual(["callee", "args"]);
    });

    test("arguments are evaluated in order", () => {
        function Foo() {}
        const values = [];

        new Foo(values.push("arg1"), values.push("arg2"), values.push("arg3"));

        expect(values).toEqual(["arg1", "arg2", "arg3"]);
    });

    test("arguments are evaluated before callee is checked for its type", () => {
        const values = [];

        expect(() => {
            new "Foo"(values.push("args"));
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Foo is not a constructor");
        expect(values).toEqual(["args"]);

        expect(() => {
            new "Foo"(bar);
        }).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "'bar' is not defined");
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/functions/function-expression-scoping.js
describe("named function expression scoping", () => {
    test("name is visible inside function body", () => {
        const f = function factorial(n) {
            if (n <= 1) return 1;
            return n * factorial(n - 1);
        };
        expect(f(5)).toBe(120);
    });

    test("name is not visible outside function body", () => {
        const f = function inner() {
            return 42;
        };
        expect(() => inner).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "'inner' is not defined");
    });

    test("name binding is immutable inside function", () => {
        const f = function immutableName() {
            immutableName = "changed";
            return typeof immutableName;
        };
        expect(f()).toBe("function");
    });

    test("outer variable with same name is shadowed inside", () => {
        let shadow = "outer";
        const f = function shadow() {
            return typeof shadow;
        };
        expect(shadow).toBe("outer");
        expect(f()).toBe("function");
    });

    test("assignment to outer variable with same name works", () => {
        let outer;
        outer = function outer() {
            return outer.name;
        };
        expect(outer()).toBe("outer");
        expect(typeof outer).toBe("function");
    });

    test("property access on outer variable with same name works", () => {
        let Foo;
        Foo = function Foo() {};
        Foo.bar = 42;
        expect(Foo.bar).toBe(42);
    });

    test("nested named function expressions", () => {
        const outer = function outerFn() {
            const inner = function innerFn() {
                return typeof outerFn + "," + typeof innerFn;
            };
            return inner();
        };
        expect(outer()).toBe("function,function");
    });

    test("same name in nested function expressions", () => {
        const outer = function sameName() {
            const inner = function sameName() {
                return sameName.length;
            };
            return [sameName.length, inner()];
        };
        const result = outer();
        expect(result[0]).toBe(0); // outer sameName
        expect(result[1]).toBe(0); // inner sameName (shadows outer)
    });
});

    function hoisted() {

    }
    expect(hoisted()).toBe("foo");
    expect(callHoisted).toBe("foo");

test("functions are hoisted across non-lexical scopes", () => {
    expect(scopedHoisted).toBeUndefined();
    expect(callScopedHoisted).toBeUndefined();
    {
        var callScopedHoisted = scopedHoisted();
        function scopedHoisted() {
            return "foo";
        }
        expect(scopedHoisted()).toBe("foo");
        expect(callScopedHoisted).toBe("foo");
    }
    expect(scopedHoisted()).toBe("foo");
    expect(callScopedHoisted).toBe("foo");
});

test("functions are not hoisted across lexical scopes", () => {
    const test = () => {
        var iife = (function () {
            return declaredLater();
        })();
        function declaredLater() {
            return "yay";
        }
        return iife;
    };

    expect(() => declaredLater).toThrow(ReferenceError);
    expect(test()).toBe("yay");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/functions/function-indexed-properties.js
describe("indexed properties of functions", () => {
    test("functions keep working with indexed properties", () => {
        const outer = 42;
        function f(a) {
            return a + outer;
        }

        f[0] = "zero";
        f[1] = "one";
        f[1000000] = "sparse";

        expect(f[0]).toBe("zero");
        expect(f[1]).toBe("one");
        expect(f[1000000]).toBe("sparse");
        expect(f[2]).toBeUndefined();
        expect(f(1)).toBe(43);
        expect(new f(1)).toBeInstanceOf(f);
    });

    test("indexed keys come first, in order", () => {
        function f() {}
        f.named = 1;
        f[2] = "two";
        f[0] = "zero";

        expect(Object.keys(f)).toEqual(["0", "2", "named"]);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f).slice(0, 2)).toEqual(["0", "2"]);
    });

    test("dense fills stay readable", () => {
        function f() {
            return "called";
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) f[i] = i * 2;
        let sum = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) sum += f[i];

        expect(sum).toBe(999000);
        expect(f()).toBe("called");
    });

    test("deleting and redefining", () => {
        function f() {}
        f[0] = 1;
        expect(delete f[0]).toBeTrue();
        expect(f[0]).toBeUndefined();
        expect(0 in f).toBeFalse();

        Object.defineProperty(f, 3, { value: "fixed", writable: false, enumerable: false, configurable: false });
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(f, 3).writable).toBeFalse();
        expect(delete f[3]).toBeFalse();
        expect(f[3]).toBe("fixed");
    });

    test("freezing", () => {
        function f() {}
        f[0] = 1;
        Object.freeze(f);
        expect(Object.isFrozen(f)).toBeTrue();
        expect(() => {
            "use strict";
            f[0] = 2;
        }).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(f[0]).toBe(1);
    });

    test("array methods applied to functions", () => {
        function f() {}
        f[0] = "a";
        f[1] = "b";
        // NB: Function length is not writable, so the methods that write it throw.
        expect(Array.prototype.join.call(f)).toBe("");
        expect(() => Array.prototype.push.call(f, "c")).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(f[0]).toBe("c");
        expect(f[1]).toBe("b");
    });

    test("every kind of function, surviving a collection", () => {
        const functions = [
            function () {},
            () => {},
            function* () {},
            async function () {},
            class {},
            class {
                static #x = 1;
                static m() {
                    return this.#x;
                }
            },
        ];
        for (const f of functions) {
            f[0] = { value: "kept" };
            f[100000] = { value: "sparse" };
        }
        gc();
        for (const f of functions) {
            expect(f[0].value).toBe("kept");
            expect(f[100000].value).toBe("sparse");
        }
        expect(functions[5].m()).toBe(1);
    });

    test("the prototype chain reads the elements of a function", () => {
        function f() {}
        f[7] = "inherited";
        const object = Object.create(f);
        expect(object[7]).toBe("inherited");
        expect(7 in object).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("many functions with elements, collected", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) {
            const f = function () {};
            f[0] = i;
        }
        gc();
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/functions/function-lazy-length-and-name.js
describe("own properties of functions that never had them looked at", () => {
    test("length and name come first, whatever is added first", () => {
        function a(x, y) {}
        a.foo = 1;
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(a).slice(0, 2)).toEqual(["length", "name"]);
        expect(a.length).toBe(2);
        expect(a.name).toBe("a");
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(a)).toContain("foo");

        const b = () => {};
        Object.defineProperty(b, "bar", { value: 1 });
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(b)).toEqual(["length", "name", "bar"]);

        const c = async x => {};
        c[Symbol.iterator] = 1;
        c.baz = 1;
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(c)).toEqual(["length", "name", "baz"]);
        expect(c.length).toBe(1);
    });

    test("descriptors", () => {
        const f = function (x) {};
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(f, "length")).toEqual({
            value: 1,
            writable: false,
            enumerable: false,
            configurable: true,
        });
        const g = function named() {};
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(g, "name")).toEqual({
            value: "named",
            writable: false,
            enumerable: false,
            configurable: true,
        });
    });

    test("hasOwn and in", () => {
        expect(Object.hasOwn(() => {}, "length")).toBeTrue();
        expect(Object.hasOwn(() => {}, "name")).toBeTrue();
        expect((() => {}).hasOwnProperty("length")).toBeTrue();
        expect("name" in function () {}).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("deleting them reveals the ones of the prototype", () => {
        const f = function named(x) {};
        expect(delete f.name).toBeTrue();
        expect(Object.hasOwn(f, "name")).toBeFalse();
        expect(f.name).toBe("");
        expect(f.length).toBe(1);
        expect(delete f.length).toBeTrue();
        expect(f.length).toBe(0);
    });

    test("they are not writable", () => {
        const f = function named(x) {};
        f.length = 10;
        f.name = "other";
        expect(f.length).toBe(1);
        expect(f.name).toBe("named");

        const g = function named(x) {};
        expect(() => {
            "use strict";
            g.name = "other";
        }).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(() => Object.assign(function named() {}, { name: "other" })).toThrow(TypeError);
    });

    test("they can be redefined", () => {
        const f = function named() {};
        Object.defineProperty(f, "name", { value: "other" });
        expect(f.name).toBe("other");
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f).slice(0, 2)).toEqual(["length", "name"]);
    });

    test("objects inheriting from a function see them", () => {
        const f = function named(x) {};
        const o = Object.create(f);
        expect(o.name).toBe("named");
        expect(o.length).toBe(1);

        // A non-writable inherited property keeps assignments from adding one.
        const g = function other() {};
        const p = Object.create(g);
        p.name = "mine";
        expect(Object.hasOwn(p, "name")).toBeFalse();
        expect(p.name).toBe("other");
    });

    test("they shadow enumerable properties of the prototype chain", () => {
        Object.prototype.name = 1;
        Function.prototype.length2 = 1;
        try {
            const keys = [];
            for (const key in function () {}) keys.push(key);
            expect(keys).not.toContain("name");
            expect(keys).toContain("length2");
        } finally {
            delete Object.prototype.name;
            delete Function.prototype.length2;
        }
    });

    test("freezing, sealing and preventing extensions", () => {
        const frozen = Object.freeze(function named(x) {});
        expect(Object.isFrozen(frozen)).toBeTrue();
        expect(frozen.name).toBe("named");
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(frozen, "length").configurable).toBeFalse();

        const sealed = Object.seal(() => {});
        expect(Object.isSealed(sealed)).toBeTrue();
        expect(sealed.length).toBe(0);

        const fixed = Object.preventExtensions(function named(x) {});
        expect(fixed.length).toBe(1);
        expect(fixed.name).toBe("named");
        expect(Object.isExtensible(fixed)).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("changing the prototype first", () => {
        const f = function named(x) {};
        Object.setPrototypeOf(f, null);
        expect(f.length).toBe(1);
        expect(f.name).toBe("named");
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f).slice(0, 2)).toEqual(["length", "name"]);
    });

    test("a function that is a prototype, before and after", () => {
        const f = function named(x) {};
        const o = Object.create(f);
        f.foo = 1;
        expect(o.foo).toBe(1);
        expect(o.length).toBe(1);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f).slice(0, 2)).toEqual(["length", "name"]);
    });

    test("bind", () => {
        const f = function named(x, y) {};
        const bound = f.bind(null, 1);
        expect(bound.length).toBe(1);
        expect(bound.name).toBe("bound named");
    });

    test("classes", () => {
        class A {
            static x = 1;
            static m() {}
        }
        expect(A.name).toBe("A");
        expect(A.length).toBe(0);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(A).slice(0, 3)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype"]);
        expect(A.m.name).toBe("m");
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(A.m)).toEqual(["length", "name"]);

        class B extends A {
            constructor(a, b) {
                super();
            }
        }
        expect(B.length).toBe(2);
        expect(B.name).toBe("B");
    });

    test("names set by the context", () => {
        const a = () => {};
        const o = { b: () => {}, ["c" + 1]: function () {}, get d() {} };
        expect(a.name).toBe("a");
        expect(o.b.name).toBe("b");
        expect(o.c1.name).toBe("c1");
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(o, "d").get.name).toBe("get d");
        const k = Symbol("s");
        const p = { [k]: () => {} };
        expect(p[k].name).toBe("[s]");
    });

    test("properties added before the first look at them move behind them", () => {
        const f = function named(x) {};
        f.a = 1;
        f.b = 2;
        Object.defineProperty(f, "c", { value: 3, enumerable: false });
        expect(f.a).toBe(1);
        expect(f.name).toBe("named");
        expect(f.a).toBe(1);
        expect(f.b).toBe(2);
        expect(f.c).toBe(3);
        expect(f.length).toBe(1);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "a", "b", "c"]);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(f, "c").enumerable).toBeFalse();
        expect(Object.keys(f)).toEqual(["a", "b"]);
    });

    test("deleting an added property", () => {
        const f = () => {};
        f.a = 1;
        f.b = 2;
        expect(delete f.a).toBeTrue();
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "b"]);
        expect(f.b).toBe(2);
    });

    test("many added properties", () => {
        const f = () => {};
        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) f["p" + i] = i;
        const names = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f);
        expect(names.length).toBe(102);
        expect(names.slice(0, 3)).toEqual(["length", "name", "p0"]);
        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) expect(f["p" + i]).toBe(i);
    });

    test("accessors and changed attributes of added properties survive", () => {
        const f = () => {};
        let got = 0;
        Object.defineProperty(f, "a", {
            get() {
                return ++got;
            },
            configurable: true,
        });
        f.b = 1;
        Object.defineProperty(f, "b", { writable: false });
        expect(f.name).toBe("f");
        expect(f.a).toBe(1);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(f, "b").writable).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("objects inheriting from a function with added properties", () => {
        const f = function named(x) {};
        f.a = 1;
        const o = Object.create(f);
        expect(o.a).toBe(1);
        expect(o.name).toBe("named");
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "a"]);
    });

    test("the prototype property does not get ahead of them", () => {
        function F(a, b) {}
        F.prototype.x = 1;
        expect(new F().x).toBe(1);
        expect(F.length).toBe(2);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(F)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype"]);
    });

    test("cached additions keep functions apart", () => {
        const addTo = f => {
            f.a = 1;
            f.b = 2;
            return f;
        };
        for (let i = 0; i < 3000; ++i) {
            const f = addTo(x => x);
            if (i % 3 === 0) expect(f.length).toBe(1);
            if (i % 3 === 1) expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "a", "b"]);
            expect(f.a + f.b).toBe(3);
            if (i % 7 === 0) {
                expect(f.name).toBe("");
                expect(f.a + f.b).toBe(3);
            }
        }
    });

    test("inline caches do not mix functions up", () => {
        const lengthOf = f => f.length;
        const nameOf = f => f.name;
        const addTo = f => {
            f.foo = 1;
            return f;
        };
        for (let i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) {
            const f = function named(x, y) {};
            expect(lengthOf(f)).toBe(2);
            expect(nameOf(f)).toBe("named");
            const g = addTo(() => {});
            expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(g)).toEqual(["length", "name", "foo"]);
            expect(g.foo).toBe(1);
            expect(lengthOf(addTo(x => x))).toBe(1);
        }
    });

    test("a closure copied in a loop", () => {
        const make = () => x => x;
        let last;
        for (let i = 0; i < 20000; ++i) {
            last = make();
            if (i % 1000 === 0) {
                expect(last.length).toBe(1);
                expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(last)).toEqual(["length", "name"]);
            }
        }
        expect(last.length).toBe(1);
        expect(last.name).toBe("");
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/functions/function-lazy-prototype.js
describe("the prototype property of normal functions that never had it looked at", () => {
    test("it comes right after length and name, whatever is added first", () => {
        function f() {}
        f.g = 1;
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "g"]);

        function h() {}
        h.prototype;
        h.g = 1;
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(h)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "g"]);
    });

    test("length and name were looked at first", () => {
        function f(a) {}
        expect(f.length).toBe(1);
        f.g = 1;
        f.h = 2;
        expect(f.prototype.constructor).toBe(f);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "g", "h"]);
        expect(f.g + f.h).toBe(3);
    });

    test("length and name are looked at last", () => {
        function f(a, b) {}
        f.g = 1;
        f.prototype.x = 1;
        f.h = 2;
        expect(f.name).toBe("f");
        expect(f.length).toBe(2);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "g", "h"]);
        expect(new f().x).toBe(1);
        expect(f.g + f.h).toBe(3);
    });

    test("it is assigned to first", () => {
        function f() {}
        f.g = 1;
        const prototype = {};
        f.prototype = prototype;
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "g"]);
        expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(new f())).toBe(prototype);
    });

    test("deleting length or name", () => {
        function f() {}
        expect(f.length).toBe(0);
        expect(delete f.name).toBeTrue();
        f.g = 1;
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "prototype", "g"]);

        function h() {}
        h.g = 1;
        expect(delete h.length).toBeTrue();
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(h)).toEqual(["name", "prototype", "g"]);

        function k() {}
        expect(delete k.name).toBeTrue();
        Object.defineProperty(k, "name", { value: "other" });
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(k)).toEqual(["length", "prototype", "name"]);
        expect(k.name).toBe("other");
    });

    test("deleting an added property", () => {
        function f() {}
        f.g = 1;
        f.h = 2;
        expect(delete f.g).toBeTrue();
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "h"]);
        expect(f.h).toBe(2);
    });

    test("preventing extensions", () => {
        function f() {}
        f.g = 1;
        Object.preventExtensions(f);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "g"]);
        expect(f.prototype.constructor).toBe(f);
        expect(Object.isExtensible(f)).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("changing the prototype of the function", () => {
        function f() {}
        f.g = 1;
        Object.setPrototypeOf(f, null);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "g"]);
        expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(f)).toBeNull();
    });

    test("many added properties", () => {
        function f() {}
        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) f["p" + i] = i;
        const names = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f);
        expect(names.length).toBe(103);
        expect(names.slice(0, 4)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "p0"]);
        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) expect(f["p" + i]).toBe(i);
        expect(f.prototype.constructor).toBe(f);

        function g() {}
        expect(g.name).toBe("g");
        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) g["p" + i] = i;
        expect(g.prototype.constructor).toBe(g);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(g).slice(0, 4)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "p0"]);
        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) expect(g["p" + i]).toBe(i);
    });

    test("a function that is a prototype", () => {
        function f() {}
        f.g = 1;
        const o = Object.create(f);
        expect(o.g).toBe(1);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "g"]);
        expect(o.prototype).toBe(f.prototype);

        function A() {}
        A.s = 1;
        class B extends A {}
        expect(B.s).toBe(1);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(A)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "s"]);
        expect(new B()).toBeInstanceOf(A);
    });

    test("functions from the Function constructor", () => {
        const f = new Function("a", "b", "");
        f.g = 1;
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "g"]);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(f, "prototype")).toEqual({
            value: f.prototype,
            writable: true,
            enumerable: false,
            configurable: false,
        });
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(f.prototype, "constructor")).toEqual({
            value: f,
            writable: true,
            enumerable: false,
            configurable: true,
        });
        expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(f.prototype)).toBe(Object.prototype);
        expect(new f()).toBeInstanceOf(f);
    });

    test("it shadows enumerable properties of the prototype chain", () => {
        Object.prototype.prototype = 1;
        try {
            function f() {}
            expect(f.length).toBe(0);
            const keys = [];
            for (const key in f) keys.push(key);
            expect(keys).toEqual([]);

            function g() {}
            g.a = 1;
            expect(g.name).toBe("g");
            const otherKeys = [];
            for (const key in g) otherKeys.push(key);
            expect(otherKeys).toEqual(["a"]);
        } finally {
            delete Object.prototype.prototype;
        }
    });

    test("caches of lookups on arrow functions and methods do not apply to it", () => {
        Function.prototype.prototype = 7;
        try {
            const get = f => f.prototype;
            for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
                expect(get(() => {})).toBe(7);
                expect(get({ m() {} }.m)).toBe(7);
            }
            function f() {}
            expect(get(f).constructor).toBe(f);
        } finally {
            delete Function.prototype.prototype;
        }

        const set = (f, key, value) => {
            f[key] = value;
        };
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
            const arrow = () => {};
            arrow.x = 1;
            set(arrow, "prototype", 1);
        }
        function h() {}
        h.x = 1;
        set(h, "prototype", 1);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(h)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "x"]);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(h, "prototype")).toEqual({
            value: 1,
            writable: true,
            enumerable: false,
            configurable: false,
        });
    });

    test("an inherited prototype setter cached from methods is not called for it", () => {
        const receivers = [];
        Object.defineProperty(Function.prototype, "prototype", {
            configurable: true,
            set() {
                receivers.push(this);
            },
        });
        try {
            const set = (f, value) => {
                f.prototype = value;
            };
            const method = { m() {} }.m;
            for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) set(method, 1);
            function f() {}
            const prototype = {};
            set(f, prototype);
            expect(receivers.length).toBe(10);
            expect(receivers.includes(f)).toBeFalse();
            expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(new f())).toBe(prototype);
        } finally {
            delete Function.prototype.prototype;
        }
    });

    test("functions made in a loop", () => {
        const make = () => {
            function F(x) {}
            F.a = 1;
            F.prototype.b = 2;
            F.c = 3;
            return F;
        };
        for (let i = 0; i < 3000; ++i) {
            const F = make();
            expect(F.a + F.c + new F().b).toBe(6);
            if (i % 100 === 0) {
                expect(F.length).toBe(1);
                expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(F)).toEqual(["length", "name", "prototype", "a", "c"]);
            }
        }
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/functions/function-legacy-caller-arguments.js
test("legacy caller property exposes only sloppy non-generator, non-async callers", () => {
    function getCaller() {
        return getCaller.caller;
    }

    function ordinary() {
        return getCaller();
    }

    const arrow = () => getCaller();

    const object = {
        method() {
            return getCaller();
        },
        get getter() {
            return getCaller();
        },
    };

    function strict() {
        "use strict";
        return getCaller();
    }

    class C {
        method() {
            return getCaller();
        }
    }

    function* generator() {
        yield getCaller();
    }

    expect(ordinary()).toBe(ordinary);
    expect(arrow()).toBe(arrow);
    expect(object.method()).toBe(object.method);
    expect(object.getter).toBe(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(object, "getter").get);
    expect(strict()).toBeNull();
    expect(new C().method()).toBeNull();
    expect(generator().next().value).toBeNull();
    expect([1].map(getCaller)[0]).toBeNull();
});

test("legacy caller property hides async callers", () => {
    function getCaller() {
        return getCaller.caller;
    }

    let result;
    async function asyncFunction() {
        result = getCaller();
    }
    asyncFunction();
    expect(result).toBeNull();
});

test("legacy caller property looks through Function.prototype.call, apply and Reflect.apply", () => {
    function getCaller() {
        return getCaller.caller;
    }

    function viaCall() {
        return getCaller.call(null);
    }

    function viaApply() {
        return getCaller.apply(null, []);
    }

    function viaReflectApply() {
        return Reflect.apply(getCaller, null, []);
    }

    function viaCallOfCall() {
        return Function.prototype.call.call(getCaller, null);
    }

    function viaApplyOfReflectApply() {
        return Reflect.apply.apply(null, [getCaller, null, []]);
    }

    function strictViaCall() {
        "use strict";
        return getCaller.call(null);
    }

    expect(viaCall()).toBe(viaCall);
    expect(viaApply()).toBe(viaApply);
    expect(viaReflectApply()).toBe(viaReflectApply);
    expect(viaCallOfCall()).toBe(viaCallOfCall);
    expect(viaApplyOfReflectApply()).toBe(viaApplyOfReflectApply);
    expect(strictViaCall()).toBeNull();
});

test("legacy arguments property exposes the active arguments object", () => {
    function getArguments(a, b) {
        return getArguments.arguments;
    }

    expect(getArguments.arguments).toBeNull();

    let argumentsObject = getArguments(1, undefined);
    expect(argumentsObject.length).toBe(2);
    expect(argumentsObject[0]).toBe(1);
    expect(argumentsObject[1]).toBeUndefined();
    expect(argumentsObject.callee).toBe(getArguments);

    let calleeDescriptor = Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(argumentsObject, "callee");
    expect(calleeDescriptor.value).toBe(getArguments);
    expect(calleeDescriptor.writable).toBeTrue();
    expect(calleeDescriptor.enumerable).toBeFalse();
    expect(calleeDescriptor.configurable).toBeTrue();

    function getClonedArguments(a) {
        let legacyArguments = getClonedArguments.arguments;
        a = 9;
        return legacyArguments;
    }

    let clonedArguments = getClonedArguments(7);
    expect(clonedArguments[0]).toBe(7);
    expect(clonedArguments.callee).toBe(getClonedArguments);

    function getRestrictedArguments(a = 1) {
        return getRestrictedArguments.arguments;
    }

    expect(() => getRestrictedArguments().callee).toThrow(TypeError);

    expect(getArguments.arguments).toBeNull();
});

test("restricted functions keep the throwing caller and arguments accessors", () => {
    function strict() {
        "use strict";
    }

    let arrow = () => {};

    expect(() => strict.caller).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => strict.arguments).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => arrow.caller).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => arrow.arguments).toThrow(TypeError);
});

test("legacy caller and arguments are not own properties of functions", () => {
    function ordinary() {
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(ordinary, "caller")).toBeUndefined();
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(ordinary, "arguments")).toBeUndefined();
    }
    ordinary();

    expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(ordinary)).not.toContain("caller");
    expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(ordinary)).not.toContain("arguments");
    expect(Reflect.ownKeys(ordinary)).not.toContain("caller");
    expect(Reflect.ownKeys(ordinary)).not.toContain("arguments");
    expect(Object.hasOwn(ordinary, "caller")).toBeFalse();
    expect(Object.hasOwn(ordinary, "arguments")).toBeFalse();
    expect("caller" in ordinary).toBeTrue();
    expect("arguments" in ordinary).toBeTrue();
});

test("walking own properties from inside a function does not reach its caller's arguments", () => {
    const secret = {};

    function walk(root) {
        const seen = [];
        (function visit(object) {
            if (!object || (typeof object !== "object" && typeof object !== "function") || seen.includes(object))
                return;
            seen.push(object);
            for (const name of Object.getOwnPropertyNames(object)) {
                const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(object, name);
                if ("value" in descriptor) visit(descriptor.value);
            }
        })(root);
        return seen;
    }

    function outer(argument) {
        const holder = {
            method: function () {
                return walk(holder);
            },
        };
        return holder.method();
    }

    expect(outer(secret)).not.toContain(secret);
});

test("%Function.prototype% has caller and arguments accessors", () => {
    function strict() {
        "use strict";
    }

    for (const name of ["caller", "arguments"]) {
        const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(Function.prototype, name);
        expect(descriptor.get).toBeInstanceOf(Function);
        expect(descriptor.set).toBeInstanceOf(Function);
        expect(descriptor.enumerable).toBeFalse();
        expect(descriptor.configurable).toBeTrue();

        expect(descriptor.get.call(function () {})).toBeNull();
        expect(descriptor.set.call(function () {}, 1)).toBeUndefined();

        const restricted = [strict, () => {}, class {}, function* () {}, async function () {}, Math.abs, {}, 1];
        restricted.push(function () {}.bind(), { method() {} }.method, Function.prototype, undefined);
        for (const receiver of restricted) {
            expect(() => descriptor.get.call(receiver)).toThrow(TypeError);
            expect(() => descriptor.set.call(receiver, 1)).toThrow(TypeError);
        }
    }
});

test("objects that inherit from sloppy functions cannot use legacy caller and arguments", () => {
    function base() {}
    class Derived extends base {}

    for (const object of [Object.create(base), new Proxy(base, {}), Derived]) {
        expect(() => object.caller).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "ordinary non-strict functions");
        expect(() => object.arguments).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "ordinary non-strict functions");
    }

    const inheriting = Object.create(base);
    expect(() => {
        inheriting.caller = 1;
    }).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => {
        inheriting.arguments = 1;
    }).toThrow(TypeError);
});

        ordinary.arguments = 2;

test("computed property names infer anonymous function names", () => {
    const namedSymbol = Symbol("named");
    const emptySymbol = Symbol("");
    const unnamedSymbol = Symbol();
    const getterSymbol = Symbol("getter");
    const setterSymbol = Symbol("");

    const object = {
        [1]: function () {},
        [2]: class {},
        [namedSymbol]: () => {},
        [emptySymbol]: function* () {},
        [unnamedSymbol]: async function () {},
        [/a/]: function () {},
        get [getterSymbol]() {},
        set [setterSymbol](value) {},
    };

    expect(object[1].name).toBe("1");
    expect(object[2].name).toBe("2");
    expect(object[namedSymbol].name).toBe("[named]");
    expect(object[emptySymbol].name).toBe("[]");
    expect(object[unnamedSymbol].name).toBe("");
    expect(object[/a/].name).toBe("/a/");
    expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(object, getterSymbol).get.name).toBe("get [getter]");
    expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(object, setterSymbol).set.name).toBe("set []");
});

});

        },

    test("direct assignment does name new function expression", () => {
        // prettier-ignore
        let f1 = (function () {});
        expect(f1.name).toBe("f1");

        let f2 = false;
        f2 ||= function () {};
        expect(f2.name).toBe("f2");
    });

    test("assignment from variable does not name", () => {
        const f1 = function () {};
        let f3 = f1;
        expect(f3.name).toBe("f1");
    });

    test("assignment via expression does not name", () => {
        let f4 = false || function () {};
        expect(f4.name).toBe("");
    });

        expect(f5.name).toBe("");

        let f6;
        eval("(f6) ??= function () {};");
        expect(f6.name).toBe("");

        let f7 = false;
        eval("(f7) ||= function () {};");
        expect(f7.name).toBe("");

        let f8 = true;
        eval("(f8) &&= function () {};");
        expect(f8.name).toBe("");
    });
