            configurable: true,
        });
        try {
            const array = [0, 1];
            store(array, 2, 2);
            expect(arraySetterCalls).toBe(1);
            expect(Object.hasOwn(array, 2)).toBeFalse();
        } finally {
            delete Array.prototype[2];
        }

        let objectSetterCalls = 0;
        Object.defineProperty(Object.prototype, 1, {
            set(value) {
                ++objectSetterCalls;
            },
            configurable: true,
        });
        try {
            const array = [0];
            store(array, 1, 1);
            expect(objectSetterCalls).toBe(1);
            expect(array.length).toBe(1);
        } finally {
            delete Object.prototype[1];
        }

        const withOwnPrototype = [0];
        Object.setPrototypeOf(withOwnPrototype, {
            set 1(value) {
                withOwnPrototype.seen = value;
            },
        });
        store(withOwnPrototype, 1, "seen");
        expect(withOwnPrototype.seen).toBe("seen");
        expect(withOwnPrototype.length).toBe(1);

        expect(fill(4)).toEqual([0, 1, 2, 3]);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/array-constructs.js
// JIT code allocates the arrays `new Array(...)` makes of no argument or of
// several arguments itself, and those of a length through the runtime.
// These tests run every function many times, so that with a low JIT
// threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

describe("constructs of Array in JIT code", () => {
    test("no arguments, a length, and several elements", () => {
        function empty() {
            return new Array();
        }
        function ofLength(n) {
            return new Array(n);
        }
        function ofElements(a, b, c) {
            return new Array(a, b, c);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const array = empty();
            expect(Array.isArray(array)).toBeTrue();
            expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(array)).toBe(Array.prototype);
            expect(array.length).toBe(0);
            array.push(i);
            expect(array).toEqual([i]);
            expect(empty()).not.toBe(empty());

            const sized = ofLength(i % 5);
            expect(sized.length).toBe(i % 5);
            expect(0 in sized).toBeFalse();

            const elements = ofElements(i, "x", null);
            expect(elements).toEqual([i, "x", null]);
            expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(elements)).toBe(Array.prototype);
        }
    });

    test("single arguments that are no lengths", () => {
        function ofOne(value) {
            return new Array(value);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(ofOne(3).length).toBe(3);
            expect(ofOne("3")).toEqual(["3"]);
            expect(ofOne(null)).toEqual([null]);
        }
        expect(() => ofOne(-1)).toThrow(RangeError);
        expect(() => ofOne(1.5)).toThrow(RangeError);
        expect(ofOne(2 ** 31).length).toBe(2 ** 31);
    });

    test("constructors other than Array", () => {
        class MyArray extends Array {}
        function construct(C) {
            return new C();
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(Array.isArray(construct(Array))).toBeTrue();
        const mine = construct(MyArray);
        expect(mine).toBeInstanceOf(MyArray);
        expect(construct(Object)).not.toBeInstanceOf(Array);
    });

    test("a replaced global Array", () => {
        const OriginalArray = Array;
        function make() {
            return new Array();
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(Array.isArray(make())).toBeTrue();
        try {
            globalThis.Array = function () {
                this.replaced = true;
            };
            expect(make().replaced).toBeTrue();
        } finally {
            globalThis.Array = OriginalArray;
        }
        expect(Array.isArray(make())).toBeTrue();
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/array-iteration-dependencies.js
// Compiled code starts for-of loops over arrays without asking the runtime while the realm's arrays are iterated with
// the realm's array iterators, whose next method is the builtin one, which it reads from the realm at every loop start.
// Changing either method, also while the code runs, makes the next loop start use the new method.
//
// NB: Every change of an iterator method makes the realm's arrays observably iterated for good, so the test that makes
//     one comes last, and array-iterator-next-dependency.js changes the other method in a realm of its own. The
//     functions come from the Function constructor, so that each run of a test (see LIBJS_TEST_REPEAT) compiles new
//     ones.

function compiled(parameters, body, ...warmUpArguments) {
    const f = new Function(...parameters, body);
    jit.prepare(f);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) f(...warmUpArguments);
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return f;
}

const collectBody = "const values = []; for (const value of iterable) values.push(value); return values;";

describe("for-of loops over arrays in compiled code", () => {
    test("iterables other than plain arrays of the realm take the slow path", () => {
        const collect = compiled(["iterable"], collectBody, [1, 2, 3]);
        expect(collect([4, 5])).toEqual([4, 5]);
        expect(collect([])).toEqual([]);
        expect(collect([1, , 3])).toEqual([1, undefined, 3]);
        const named = [1, 2];
        named.label = "named";
        expect(collect(named)).toEqual([1, 2]);
        const own = [1, 2];
        own[Symbol.iterator] = function* () {
            yield "own";
        };
        expect(collect(own)).toEqual(["own"]);
        class Subclass extends Array {}
        expect(collect(Subclass.of(3, 4))).toEqual([3, 4]);
        const otherPrototype = Object.setPrototypeOf([7, 8], {
            *[Symbol.iterator]() {
                yield "other";
            },
        });
        expect(collect(otherPrototype)).toEqual(["other"]);
        expect(() => collect(Object.setPrototypeOf([9], null))).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(collect(new Map([[1, 2]]))).toEqual([[1, 2]]);
        expect(collect(new Set([9]))).toEqual([9]);
        expect(collect("hi")).toEqual(["h", "i"]);
        expect(collect(new Int8Array([1, 2]))).toEqual([1, 2]);
        expect(collect({ length: 2, 0: "a", 1: "b", [Symbol.iterator]: Array.prototype.values })).toEqual(["a", "b"]);
        expect(
            collect(
                (function* () {
                    yield 1;
                })()
            )
        ).toEqual([1]);
        expect(() => collect({})).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(() => collect(undefined)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(collect([6, 7])).toEqual([6, 7]);
    });

    test("arrays that change while their loop runs", () => {
        const visit = compiled(
            ["array", "change"],
            "const values = []; for (const value of array) { values.push(value); change(array, values.length); } return values;",
            [1, 2, 3],
            () => {}
        );
        const grow = (array, count) => {
            if (count === 1) array.push(4);
        };
        const shrink = array => {
            array.length = 1;
        };
        const name = (array, count) => {
            if (count === 1) array.label = "named";
        };
        const ownIteratorMethod = (array, count) => {
            if (count === 1)
                array[Symbol.iterator] = function* () {
                    yield "own";
                };
        };
        expect(visit([1, 2, 3], grow)).toEqual([1, 2, 3, 4]);
        expect(visit([1, 2, 3], shrink)).toEqual([1]);
        expect(visit([1, 2, 3], name)).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
        const array = [1, 2, 3];
        expect(visit(array, ownIteratorMethod)).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
        expect(visit(array, () => {})).toEqual(["own"]);
    });

    test("loops in inlined callees", () => {
        const sum = new Function("values", "let total = 0; for (const value of values) total += value; return total;");
        jit.prepare(sum);
        const sumBoth = compiled(["sum", "a", "b"], "return sum(a) + sum(b);", sum, [1, 2], [3]);
        expect(sumBoth(sum, [1, 2, 3], [4])).toBe(10);
        const named = [5];
        named.label = "named";
        expect(sumBoth(sum, named, new Set([6]))).toBe(11);
        expect(sumBoth(sum, [], [1, , 2])).toBeNaN();
    });
});

describe("a changed iterator method", () => {
    // NB: The code calls the same function between its loops every time, so that it goes on in compiled code after it.
    let action = () => {};
    const between = () => action();

    test("an iterator method of arrays replaced while compiled code runs is called from the next loop on", () => {
        const originalIteratorMethod = Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator];
        const twoLoops = compiled(
            ["array", "between"],
            "let first = ''; for (const value of array) { first += value; between(); } let second = ''; for (const value of array) second += value; return [first, second];",
            [1, 2],
            between
        );
        action = () => {
            Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator] = function* () {
                yield "replaced";
            };
        };
        try {
            expect(twoLoops([1, 2], between)).toEqual(["12", "replaced"]);
            action = () => {};
            expect(twoLoops([1, 2], between)).toEqual(["replaced", "replaced"]);
        } finally {
            action = () => {};
            Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator] = originalIteratorMethod;
        }
        expect(twoLoops([1, 2], between)).toEqual(["12", "12"]);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/array-iteration.js
function compileIteration(f, ...args) {
    jit.prepare(f);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) f(...args);
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return f;
}

function collect(iterable) {
    const values = [];
    for (const value of iterable) values.push(value);
    return values;
}

function firstTwo(iterable) {
    const [first, second] = iterable;
    return [first, second];
}

test("for-of and destructuring step through packed and holey arrays", () => {
    compileIteration(collect, [1, 2, 3]);
    compileIteration(firstTwo, [1, 2, 3]);
    expect(collect([4, 5, 6])).toEqual([4, 5, 6]);
    expect(collect([])).toEqual([]);
    expect(collect([1, , 3])).toEqual([1, undefined, 3]);
    expect(firstTwo([7])).toEqual([7, undefined]);
    expect(firstTwo([7, 8, 9])).toEqual([7, 8]);
    expect(jit.exitCount(collect)).toBe(0);
});

test("holes read the prototype chain", () => {
    compileIteration(collect, [1, 2, 3]);
    Array.prototype[1] = "from prototype";
    try {
        expect(collect([1, , 3])).toEqual([1, "from prototype", 3]);
    } finally {
        delete Array.prototype[1];
    }
});

test("holey arrays iterate up to their length past their storage", () => {
    const count = compileIteration(new Function("array", "let n = 0; for (const value of array) ++n; return n;"), [
        1,
        ,
        3,
    ]);
    expect(count(new Array(5))).toBe(5);
    const grown = [1, 2, 3];
    grown.length = 40;
    expect(count(grown)).toBe(40);
    expect(collect(Object.assign(new Array(3), { 1: "set" }))).toEqual([undefined, "set", undefined]);
});

test("arrays changed while iterating", () => {
    compileIteration(collect, [1, 2, 3]);
    const growing = [1, 2];
    const seen = [];
    for (const value of growing) {
        seen.push(value);
        if (growing.length < 5) growing.push(value * 10);
    }
    expect(seen).toEqual([1, 2, 10, 20, 100]);

    const shrinking = [1, 2, 3, 4];
    const kept = [];
    const step = new Function("array", "kept", "for (const value of array) { kept.push(value); array.length = 2; }");
    compileIteration(step, [1, 2, 3], []);
    step(shrinking, kept);
    expect(kept).toEqual([1, 2]);
});

test("other iterables and iterators take the slow path", () => {
    compileIteration(collect, [1, 2, 3]);
    expect(collect(new Uint8Array([1, 2]))).toEqual([1, 2]);
    expect(collect("ab")).toEqual(["a", "b"]);
    expect(collect(new Set([3, 4]))).toEqual([3, 4]);
    expect(collect([5, 6].keys())).toEqual([0, 1]);
    expect(collect([5, 6].entries())).toEqual([
        [0, 5],
        [1, 6],
    ]);
    expect(collect(new Proxy([1, 2], {}))).toEqual([1, 2]);
    class MyArray extends Array {}
    expect(collect(MyArray.of(8, 9))).toEqual([8, 9]);
});

test("own and replaced iterator methods are called", () => {
    compileIteration(collect, [1, 2, 3]);
    const own = [1, 2];
    own[Symbol.iterator] = function* () {
        yield "own";
    };
    expect(collect(own)).toEqual(["own"]);

    const values = Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator];
    Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator] = function* () {
        yield "replaced";
    };
    try {
        expect(collect([1, 2])).toEqual(["replaced"]);
    } finally {
        Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator] = values;
    }
    expect(collect([1, 2])).toEqual([1, 2]);

    let getterCalls = 0;
    Object.defineProperty(Array.prototype, Symbol.iterator, {
        get() {
            ++getterCalls;
            return values;
        },
        configurable: true,
    });
    try {
        expect(collect([1, 2])).toEqual([1, 2]);
        expect(getterCalls).toBe(1);
    } finally {
        Object.defineProperty(Array.prototype, Symbol.iterator, {
            value: values,
            writable: true,
            configurable: true,
        });
    }
});

test("a replaced next method is called", () => {
    compileIteration(collect, [1, 2, 3]);
    const iteratorPrototype = Object.getPrototypeOf([][Symbol.iterator]());
    const next = iteratorPrototype.next;
    let calls = 0;
    iteratorPrototype.next = function () {
        ++calls;
        return next.call(this);
    };
    try {
        expect(collect([1, 2])).toEqual([1, 2]);
        expect(calls).toBe(3);
    } finally {
        iteratorPrototype.next = next;
    }
    expect(collect([1, 2])).toEqual([1, 2]);
});

test("array-likes iterate up to their length property", () => {
    compileIteration(collect, [1, 2, 3]);
    const shorter = { 0: "a", 1: "b", length: 1, [Symbol.iterator]: Array.prototype.values };
    expect(collect(shorter)).toEqual(["a"]);
    const longer = { 0: "a", length: 3, [Symbol.iterator]: Array.prototype.values };
    expect(collect(longer)).toEqual(["a", undefined, undefined]);
    const argumentsWithLength = (function () {
        "use strict";
        arguments.length = 1;
        return arguments;
    })(1, 2, 3);
    expect(collect(argumentsWithLength)).toEqual([1]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/array-iterator-next-dependency.js
// Compiled code starts for-of loops over arrays without asking the runtime while the realm's array iterators have
// their builtin next method. Replacing it, also while the code runs, makes the next loop start call the new method
// (see array-iteration-dependencies.js).

function compiled(parameters, body, ...warmUpArguments) {
    const f = new Function(...parameters, body);
    jit.prepare(f);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) f(...warmUpArguments);
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return f;
}

// NB: The code calls the same function between its loops every time, so that it goes on in compiled code after it.
let action = () => {};
const between = () => action();

test("a next method of array iterators replaced while compiled code runs is called from the next loop on", () => {
    const iteratorPrototype = Object.getPrototypeOf([][Symbol.iterator]());
    const originalNext = iteratorPrototype.next;
    let calls = 0;
    const twoLoops = compiled(
        ["array", "between"],
        "let first = 0; for (const value of array) { first += value; between(); } let second = 0; for (const value of array) second += value; return [first, second];",
        [1, 2],
        between
    );
    action = () => {
        iteratorPrototype.next = function () {
            ++calls;
            return originalNext.call(this);
        };
    };
    try {
        expect(twoLoops([1, 2], between)).toEqual([3, 3]);
        expect(calls).toBe(3);
        action = () => {};
        expect(twoLoops([1, 2], between)).toEqual([3, 3]);
        expect(calls).toBe(9);
    } finally {
        action = () => {};
        iteratorPrototype.next = originalNext;
    }
    expect(twoLoops([1, 2], between)).toEqual([3, 3]);
    expect(calls).toBe(9);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/array-length.js
function compileLength() {
    const lengthOf = new Function("array", "return array.length;");
    jit.prepare(lengthOf);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) lengthOf([1, 2, 3]);
    expect(jit.compile(lengthOf)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return lengthOf;
}

test("compiled array length handles every storage kind and the int32 boundary", () => {
    class Subclass extends Array {}
    const arrays = [[], [1, 2, 3], [1, , 3], Object.freeze([1, 2]), new Subclass(4)];
    const sparse = [];
    sparse[10000] = 1;
    arrays.push(sparse);
    const accessor = [1, 2];
    Object.defineProperty(accessor, 0, {
        get() {
            throw new Error("length must not read elements");
        },
    });
    arrays.push(accessor);
    for (const length of [0, 1, 2147483647, 2147483648, 4294967295]) arrays.push(new Array(length));
    for (const array of arrays) {
        const lengthOf = compileLength();
        expect(lengthOf(array)).toBe(array.length);
    }
});

test("compiled array length handles changed receivers and observable property access", () => {
    let getterCalls = 0;
    let proxyCalls = 0;
    const getter = {
        get length() {
            ++getterCalls;
            return 7;
        },
    };
    const proxy = new Proxy([1, 2], {
        get(target, key) {
            ++proxyCalls;
            expect(key).toBe("length");
            return 19;
        },
    });
    for (const [receiver, expected] of [
        [{ length: "ordinary" }, "ordinary"],
        [getter, 7],
        [proxy, 19],
        ["hello", 5],
        [new String("hello"), 5],
        [new Uint16Array(4), 4],
        [42, undefined],
        [function (a, b) {}, 2],
    ]) {
        const lengthOf = compileLength();
        expect(lengthOf(receiver)).toBe(expected);
        expect(lengthOf([1, 2, 3])).toBe(3);
    }
    expect(getterCalls).toBe(1);
    expect(proxyCalls).toBe(1);
    for (const receiver of [null, undefined]) {
        const lengthOf = compileLength();
        expect(() => lengthOf(receiver)).toThrow(TypeError);
    }
});

test("mixed length feedback keeps ordinary property access", () => {
    const lengthOf = new Function("array", "return array.length;");
    let getterCalls = 0;
    const object = {
        get length() {
            ++getterCalls;
            return 9;
        },
    };
    jit.prepare(lengthOf);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
        lengthOf([1, 2]);
        lengthOf(object);
        lengthOf("abc");
    }
    expect(jit.compile(lengthOf)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    getterCalls = 0;
    expect(lengthOf(object)).toBe(9);
    expect(getterCalls).toBe(1);
    expect(lengthOf([1, 2])).toBe(2);
    expect(lengthOf("abc")).toBe(3);
});

test("array length loads observe mutations inside loops", () => {
    for (const mutation of ["array.length = 1;", "array.pop();", "alias.length = 1;"]) {
        const scan = new Function(
            "array",
            "alias",
            `let count = 0; for (let i = 0; i < array.length; ++i) { ++count; ${mutation} } return count;`
        );
        jit.prepare(scan);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
            const array = [1, 2, 3];
            scan(array, array);
        }
        expect(jit.compile(scan)).toBe(jit.enabled);
        const array = [1, 2, 3];
        expect(scan(array, array)).toBe(mutation === "array.pop();" ? 2 : 1);
    }
    const scan = new Function(
        "array",
        "let count = 0; for (let i = 0; i < array.length; ++i) { array[i]; ++count; } return count;"
    );
    jit.prepare(scan);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) scan([1, 2, 3]);
    expect(jit.compile(scan)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    const array = [1, 2, 3];
    Object.defineProperty(array, 0, {
        get() {
            array.length = 1;
            return 1;
        },
    });
    expect(scan(array)).toBe(1);
});

test("hoisted scan guards preserve empty scans and changed target properties", () => {
    const scan = new Function(
        "array",
        "target",
        "for (let i = 0; i < array.length; ++i) if (array[i].pos == target.pos) return array[i]; return false;"
    );
    const position = {};
    const first = { pos: {} };
    const last = { pos: position };
    jit.prepare(scan);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) scan([first, last], { pos: position });
    expect(jit.compile(scan)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(scan([first, last], { pos: position })).toBe(last);
    expect(scan([], null)).toBeFalse();
    let getterCalls = 0;
    const target = {
        get pos() {
            ++getterCalls;
            return position;
        },
    };
    expect(scan([], target)).toBeFalse();
    expect(getterCalls).toBe(0);
    expect(scan([first, last], target)).toBe(last);
    expect(getterCalls).toBe(2);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/array-literals.js
// JIT code allocates the arrays of array literals itself, with their elements
// packed. These tests run every function many times, so that with a low JIT
// threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

describe("array literals in JIT code", () => {
    test("elements, lengths and growth", () => {
        function pair(a, b) {
            return [a, b];
        }
        function empty() {
            return [];
        }
        function constants() {
            return [1, 2.5, "three", null, undefined, true];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const array = pair(i, { value: i });
            expect(Array.isArray(array)).toBeTrue();
            expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(array)).toBe(Array.prototype);
            expect(array.length).toBe(2);
            expect(array[0]).toBe(i);
            expect(array[1].value).toBe(i);
            expect(array[2]).toBeUndefined();
            expect(Object.keys(array)).toEqual(["0", "1"]);

            const grown = empty();
            expect(grown.length).toBe(0);
            for (let j = 0; j < 20; ++j) grown.push(j);
            expect(grown.length).toBe(20);
            expect(grown[19]).toBe(19);

            const literal = constants();
            expect(literal).toEqual([1, 2.5, "three", null, undefined, true]);
            literal[10] = "far";
            expect(literal.length).toBe(11);
            expect(literal[8]).toBeUndefined();
            expect(8 in literal).toBeFalse();
            literal.length = 2;
            const holey = [i, , i + 1, ,];
            expect(holey.length).toBe(4);
            expect(1 in holey).toBeFalse();
            expect(3 in holey).toBeFalse();
            expect(holey[2]).toBe(i + 1);
            expect(literal).toEqual([1, 2.5]);
        }
    });

    test("arrays with more elements than allocate inline, and collections", () => {
        // NB: An array literal of 70 elements.
        const wide = new Function("i", `return [${Array(70).fill("i").join(", ")}];`);
        function nested(i) {
            const inner = [i, [i + 1, [i + 2]]];
            gc();
            return [inner, inner[1]];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const array = wide(i);
            expect(array.length).toBe(70);
            expect(array.every(element => element === i)).toBeTrue();
            const tree = nested(i);
            expect(tree[0][1][1][0]).toBe(i + 2);
            expect(tree[1][0]).toBe(i + 1);
            expect(JSON.stringify(tree[0])).toBe(`[${i},[${i + 1},[${i + 2}]]]`);
        }
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/array-push.js
// JIT code appends to arrays with Array.prototype.push inline, when nothing
// could observe the difference. These tests run every function many times,
// so that with a low JIT threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

function push(array, value) {
    return array.push(value);
}

function fill(count) {
    const array = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) push(array, i);
    return array;
}

describe("Array.prototype.push in JIT code", () => {
    test("appending and growing", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const array = fill(i);
            expect(array.length).toBe(i);
            for (let j = 0; j < i; ++j) expect(array[j]).toBe(j);
        }
        const array = [1, 2];
        expect(push(array, "three")).toBe(3);
        expect(array).toEqual([1, 2, "three"]);
    });

    test("arrays it cannot append to unobservably", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) fill(4);

        const frozen = Object.freeze([1]);
        expect(() => push(frozen, 2)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(frozen).toEqual([1]);

        const fixedLength = [1];
        Object.defineProperty(fixedLength, "length", { writable: false });
        expect(() => push(fixedLength, 2)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(fixedLength.length).toBe(1);

        const holey = [1, , 3];
        expect(push(holey, 4)).toBe(4);
        expect(holey[3]).toBe(4);

        const arrayLike = { length: 2, push: Array.prototype.push };
        expect(push(arrayLike, "x")).toBe(3);
        expect(arrayLike[2]).toBe("x");
        expect(arrayLike.length).toBe(3);

        class Subclass extends Array {}
        const subclass = new Subclass();
        expect(push(subclass, 5)).toBe(1);
        expect(subclass[0]).toBe(5);

        const proxied = new Proxy([], {});
        expect(push(proxied, 1)).toBe(1);
        expect(proxied[0]).toBe(1);
    });

    test("setters on the prototype chain", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) fill(4);
        let setterCalls = 0;
        Object.defineProperty(Array.prototype, 2, {
            set(value) {
                ++setterCalls;
            },
            configurable: true,
        });
        try {
            const array = [0, 1];
            expect(push(array, 2)).toBe(3);
            expect(setterCalls).toBe(1);
            expect(Object.hasOwn(array, 2)).toBeFalse();
        } finally {
            delete Array.prototype[2];
        }
        expect(fill(4)).toEqual([0, 1, 2, 3]);
    });

    test("a push that is not of Array.prototype.push", () => {
        const array = [];
        array.push = function (value) {
            return "own push " + value;
        };
        expect(push(array, 1)).toBe("own push 1");
        expect(array.length).toBe(0);
    });

    test("several values at once", () => {
        const pushThree = (array, a, b, c) => array.push(a, b, c);
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const array = [];
            for (let j = 0; j < i; ++j) expect(pushThree(array, j, -j, "x")).toBe(3 * j + 3);
            expect(array.length).toBe(3 * i);
            for (let j = 0; j < i; ++j) expect(array.slice(3 * j, 3 * j + 3)).toEqual([j, -j, "x"]);
        }
        expect(() => pushThree(Object.freeze([1]), 1, 2, 3)).toThrow(TypeError);
        const holey = [1, , 3];
        expect(pushThree(holey, 4, 5, 6)).toBe(6);
        expect(holey).toEqual([1, undefined, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/array-splice.js
function compiledSplice(itemCount) {
    const parameters = ["array", "start", "count", "x", "y", "z"].slice(0, itemCount + 3);
    const call = parameters.slice(1).join(", ");
    const splice = new Function(...parameters, `return array.splice(${call});`);
    jit.prepare(splice);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) splice([1, 2, 3, 4], 1, 1, 5, 6, 7);
    expect(jit.compile(splice)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return splice;
}

test("packed splices move both overlapping directions and return removed elements", () => {
    for (let itemCount = 0; itemCount <= 3; ++itemCount) {
        const splice = compiledSplice(itemCount);
        const reference = new Function("a", "start", "count", "items", "return a.splice(start, count, ...items);");
        jit.neverCompile(reference);
        const items = [{ name: "one" }, "two", 3.5].slice(0, itemCount);
        for (const length of [1, 2, 4, 7, 64, 1025]) {
            const values = Array.from({ length }, (_, i) => i);
            for (const start of [-0x80000000, -length - 1, -1, 0, 1, length - 1, length, 0x7fffffff]) {
                for (const count of [-0x80000000, -1, 0, 1, 2, length, 0x7fffffff]) {
                    const actual = values.slice();
                    const expected = values.slice();
                    expect(splice(actual, start, count, ...items)).toEqual(reference(expected, start, count, items));
                    expect(actual).toEqual(expected);
                }
            }
        }
    }
});

test("empty and holey arrays keep their ordinary splice behavior", () => {
    const splice = compiledSplice(2);
    const empty = [];
    expect(splice(empty, 0, 10, "a", "b")).toEqual([]);
    expect(empty).toEqual(["a", "b"]);
    const holey = [1, , 3, , 5];
    const removed = splice(holey, 1, 3, "a", "b");
    expect(removed.length).toBe(3);
    expect(0 in removed).toBeFalse();
    expect(removed[1]).toBe(3);
    expect(2 in removed).toBeFalse();
    expect(holey).toEqual([1, "a", "b", 5]);
});

test("argument coercions and changed methods run once", () => {
    const splice = compiledSplice(1);
    let calls = 0;
    const array = [1, 2, 3];
    const start = {
        valueOf() {
            ++calls;
            return 1;
        },
    };
    expect(splice(array, start, 1, "x")).toEqual([2]);
    expect(calls).toBe(1);
    expect(array).toEqual([1, "x", 3]);
    array.splice = function (...args) {
        ++calls;
        return args;
    };
    expect(splice(array, 0, 2, "y")).toEqual([0, 2, "y"]);
    expect(calls).toBe(2);
});

test("custom species is observed before changing the source array", () => {
    const splice = compiledSplice(3);
    const array = [1, 2, 3];
    let calls = 0;
    array.constructor = {
        [Symbol.species]: function (length) {
            ++calls;
            expect(length).toBe(1);
            expect(array).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
            return { created: true };
        },
    };
    expect(splice(array, 1, 1, "a", "b", "c")).toEqual({ 0: 2, length: 1, created: true });
    expect(calls).toBe(1);
    expect([...array]).toEqual([1, "a", "b", "c", 3]);
});

test("non-writable arrays throw through the ordinary call", () => {
    const splice = compiledSplice(1);
    expect(() => splice(Object.freeze([1, 2, 3]), 1, 1, 4)).toThrow(TypeError);
    const array = [1, 2, 3];
    Object.defineProperty(array, "length", { writable: false });
    expect(() => splice(array, 1, 1, 4)).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(array).toEqual([1, 4, 3]);
});

test("objects inserted through stack arguments survive allocation and collection", () => {
    const splice = new Function("array", "i", "return array.splice(0, array.length, { i }, [i + 1], { next: i + 2 });");
    jit.prepare(splice);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) splice([null], i);
    expect(jit.compile(splice)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    const array = [null];
    for (let i = 0; i < 5000; ++i) {
        splice(array, i);
        expect(array).toEqual([{ i }, [i + 1], { next: i + 2 }]);
    }
});

test("values live across a splice keep their registers and spill slots", () => {
    const compute = new Function(
        "array",
        "start",
        "count",
        "x",
        "y",
        "z",
        `const before = start * 11 + count * 7 + x * 5 + y * 3 + z;
        const removed = array.splice(start, count, x, y, z);
        return [before, start, count, x, y, z, removed, array];`
    );
    jit.prepare(compute);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) compute([1, 2, 3, 4], 1, 2, 5, 6, 7);
    expect(jit.compile(compute)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(compute([1, 2, 3, 4], 1, 2, 5, 6, 7)).toEqual([75, 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, [2, 3], [1, 5, 6, 7, 4]]);
});

test("inherited setters see inserted indices", () => {
    const splice = compiledSplice(1);
    const seen = [];
    const prototype = Object.create(Array.prototype);
    Object.defineProperty(prototype, "3", {
        set(value) {
            seen.push(value);
        },
    });
    const array = [1, 2, 3];
    Object.setPrototypeOf(array, prototype);
    expect(splice(array, 3, 0, "x")).toEqual([]);
    expect(seen).toEqual(["x"]);
    expect(Object.hasOwn(array, "3")).toBeFalse();
    expect(array.length).toBe(4);
});

test("changes to the default species are observed by compiled calls", () => {
    const splice = compiledSplice(1);
    class Removed extends Array {}
    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(Array, Symbol.species);
    let calls = 0;
    Object.defineProperty(Array, Symbol.species, {
        configurable: true,
        get() {
            ++calls;
            return Removed;
        },
    });
    try {
        const array = [1, 2, 3];
        const removed = splice(array, 1, 1, "x");
        expect(removed).toBeInstanceOf(Removed);
        expect(removed).toEqual([2]);
        expect(calls).toBe(1);
        expect(array).toEqual([1, "x", 3]);
    } finally {
        Object.defineProperty(Array, Symbol.species, descriptor);
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/async-functions.js
// Async functions and async generators run in compiled code: a call starts one there, and each resumption enters the
// code at the continuation of the await it was suspended at, with the values that the frame kept across the
// suspension.
//
// NB: The functions come from the AsyncFunction and AsyncGeneratorFunction constructors, so that each run of a test
//     (see LIBJS_TEST_REPEAT) compiles new ones.

const AsyncFunction = Object.getPrototypeOf(async function () {}).constructor;
const AsyncGeneratorFunction = Object.getPrototypeOf(async function* () {}).constructor;

function prepared(constructor, ...parameters_and_body) {
    const function_ = new constructor(...parameters_and_body);
    jit.prepare(function_);
    return function_;
}

function settle(promise) {
    let result;
    promise.then(
        value => (result = { value }),
        error => (result = { error })
    );
    runQueuedPromiseJobs();
    return result;
}

function compile(function_, warm_up) {
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) warm_up();
    runQueuedPromiseJobs();
    expect(jit.compile(function_)).toBe(jit.enabled);
}

describe("async functions in compiled code", () => {
    test("resume where they awaited, with the values live across their awaits", () => {
        const count = prepared(
            AsyncFunction,
            "start",
            "step",
            "let total = 0; const steps = []; for (let i = start; i < start + 5; i += step) { total += await i; steps.push([i, total, jit.inCompiledCode()]); } return [total * 2, steps];"
        );
        compile(count, () => count(0, 1));
        const { value } = settle(count(10, 2));
        const [doubled, steps] = value;
        expect(doubled).toBe(72);
        expect(steps.map(([i, total]) => [i, total])).toEqual([
            [10, 10],
            [12, 22],
            [14, 36],
        ]);
        if (jit.enabled && !jit.forcesExits) expect(steps.every(([, , compiled]) => compiled)).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("receive the values of the promises they await", () => {
        const add = prepared(
            AsyncFunction,
            "a",
            "b",
            "const x = await a; const y = await Promise.resolve(b); return x + y + (await { valueOf: () => 0 }).valueOf();"
        );
        compile(add, () => add(1, 2));
        expect(settle(add(3, 4))).toEqual({ value: 7 });
        expect(settle(add(Promise.resolve("x"), "y"))).toEqual({ value: "xy0" });
        expect(settle(add(1.5, Promise.resolve(2)))).toEqual({ value: 3.5 });
    });

    test("wait for pending promises", () => {
        const wait = prepared(
            AsyncFunction,
            "promise",
            "suffix",
            "const value = await promise; return value + suffix;"
        );
        compile(wait, () => wait(Promise.resolve(1), 1));
        let resolve;
        const promise = new Promise(r => (resolve = r));
        let result;
        wait(promise, "!").then(value => (result = value));
        runQueuedPromiseJobs();
        expect(result).toBeUndefined();
        resolve("done");
        runQueuedPromiseJobs();
        expect(result).toBe("done!");
    });

    test("reject when an awaited promise rejects or they throw", () => {
        const rethrow = prepared(
            AsyncFunction,
            "promise",
            "fail",
            "const value = await promise; if (fail) throw new TypeError(value); return value;"
        );
        compile(rethrow, () => rethrow(1, false));
        expect(settle(rethrow(5, false))).toEqual({ value: 5 });
        const rejected = settle(rethrow(Promise.reject(new RangeError("rejected")), false));
        expect(rejected.error).toBeInstanceOf(RangeError);
        expect(rejected.error.message).toBe("rejected");
        const thrown = settle(rethrow("thrown", true));
        expect(thrown.error).toBeInstanceOf(TypeError);
        expect(thrown.error.message).toBe("thrown");
    });

    test("keep this, arguments and captured bindings across awaits", () => {
        const make = new Function(
            "AsyncFunction",
            "jit",
            "let captured = 1; const async_function = async function (a, b) { const x = this.x + (await a); captured += await b; return [x, arguments.length + captured, this.x * b]; }; jit.prepare(async_function); return [async_function, () => captured];"
        );
        const [async_function, captured] = make(AsyncFunction, jit);
        compile(async_function, () => async_function.call({ x: 1 }, 2, 3));
        const before = captured();
        expect(settle(async_function.call({ x: 10 }, 20, 30, 40))).toEqual({ value: [30, 3 + before + 30, 300] });
        expect(captured()).toBe(before + 30);
    });

    test("leave compiled code where a speculation fails, and keep their state", () => {
        const add = prepared(
            AsyncFunction,
            "a",
            "b",
            "let sum = a; const sums = []; for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) { sum = sum + (await b); sums.push(sum); } return sums;"
        );
        compile(add, () => add(1, 2));
        expect(settle(add(1, 2))).toEqual({ value: [3, 5, 7] });
        expect(settle(add(2147483647, 1))).toEqual({ value: [2147483648, 2147483649, 2147483650] });
        expect(settle(add("a", 1))).toEqual({ value: ["a1", "a11", "a111"] });
    });

    test("suspended async functions resume after their code is discarded and compiled again", () => {
        const values = prepared(
            AsyncFunction,
            "promises",
            "const results = []; for (const promise of promises) results.push(await promise); return results;"
        );
        compile(values, () => values([1, 2]));
        const resolvers = [];
        const promises = [0, 1, 2].map(() => new Promise(resolve => resolvers.push(resolve)));
        let result;
        values(promises).then(value => (result = value));
        resolvers[0]("a");
        runQueuedPromiseJobs();
        jit.discard(values);
        resolvers[1]("b");
        runQueuedPromiseJobs();
        expect(jit.compile(values)).toBe(jit.enabled);
        resolvers[2]("c");
        runQueuedPromiseJobs();
        expect(result).toEqual(["a", "b", "c"]);
    });

    test("compile async arrow functions and async methods once they get hot", () => {
        const make = new Function(
            "return [async (x) => (await x) * 2, { async method(x) { return (await x) + this.offset; }, offset: 10 }];"
        );
        const [arrow, object] = make();
        let total = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) {
            arrow(i).then(value => (total += value));
            object.method(i).then(value => (total += value));
        }
        runQueuedPromiseJobs();
        expect(total).toBe(999000 + 499500 + 10000);
    });
});

describe("async functions run in their call until they first await", () => {
    test("reject when evaluating a parameter throws", () => {
        const parameters = prepared(AsyncFunction, "a = (() => { throw new TypeError('parameter'); })()", "return a;");
        compile(parameters, () => parameters(1));
        let promise;
        expect(() => (promise = parameters())).not.toThrow();
        const { error } = settle(promise);
        expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(TypeError);
        expect(error.message).toBe("parameter");
        expect(settle(parameters(5))).toEqual({ value: 5 });
    });

    test("run synchronously up to the first await, and reject when they throw before it", () => {
        const steps = [];
        const make = new Function(
            "steps",
            "jit",
            "const f = async function (fail) { steps.push('body'); if (fail) throw new RangeError('before'); await 0; steps.push('after'); }; jit.prepare(f); return f;"
        );
        const f = make(steps, jit);
        compile(f, () => f(false));
        steps.length = 0;
        const promise = f(false);
        steps.push("returned");
        runQueuedPromiseJobs();
        expect(steps).toEqual(["body", "returned", "after"]);
        let thrown;
        expect(() => (thrown = f(true))).not.toThrow();
        const { error } = settle(thrown);
        expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(RangeError);
        expect(error.message).toBe("before");
        expect(settle(promise)).toEqual({ value: undefined });
    });

    test("resolve when they return without awaiting, adopting returned thenables", () => {
        const identity = prepared(AsyncFunction, "value", "return value;");
        compile(identity, () => identity(1));
        expect(settle(identity(7))).toEqual({ value: 7 });
        expect(settle(identity())).toEqual({ value: undefined });
        const thenable = { then: resolve => resolve("adopted") };
        expect(settle(identity(thenable))).toEqual({ value: "adopted" });
        expect(settle(identity(Promise.resolve("promise")))).toEqual({ value: "promise" });
        const rejected = settle(identity(Promise.reject(new SyntaxError("rejected"))));
        expect(rejected.error).toBeInstanceOf(SyntaxError);
    });

    test("catch a rejection of their first await", () => {
        const guarded = prepared(
            AsyncFunction,
            "promise",
            "try { await promise; return 'resolved'; } catch (error) { return 'caught ' + error; }"
        );
        expect(settle(guarded(Promise.reject("oops")))).toEqual({ value: "caught oops" });
        expect(settle(guarded(Promise.resolve()))).toEqual({ value: "resolved" });
    });

    test("show up once in stack traces before their first await", () => {
        async function listsItselfOnce() {
            const stack = new Error().stack;
            await 0;
            return stack;
        }
        const { value } = settle(listsItselfOnce());
        expect(value.split("\n").filter(line => line.includes("listsItselfOnce"))).toHaveLength(1);
    });
});

describe("async generators in compiled code", () => {
    test("yield and await with the values live across both", () => {
        const values = prepared(
            AsyncGeneratorFunction,
            "count",
            "let total = 0; for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) { total += await i; yield [i, total, jit.inCompiledCode()]; } return total;"
        );
        const collect = async generator => {
            const results = [];
            for await (const value of generator) results.push(value);
            return results;
        };
        compile(values, () => collect(values(3)));
        const { value } = settle(collect(values(4)));
        expect(value.map(([i, total]) => [i, total])).toEqual([
            [0, 0],
            [1, 1],
            [2, 3],
            [3, 6],
        ]);
        if (jit.enabled && !jit.forcesExits) expect(value.every(([, , compiled]) => compiled)).toBeTrue();

        const generator = values(2);
        const first = settle(generator.next()).value;
        expect(first.done).toBeFalse();
        expect(first.value.slice(0, 2)).toEqual([0, 0]);
        settle(generator.next());
        expect(settle(generator.next()).value).toEqual({ value: 1, done: true });
    });

    test("receive the values passed to next and finish through return", () => {
        const accumulate = prepared(
            AsyncGeneratorFunction,
            "let total = 0; while (true) { const value = await (yield total); if (value === undefined) return total; total += value; }"
        );
        compile(accumulate, () => {
            const generator = accumulate();
            generator.next();
            generator.next(1);
            generator.next();
        });
        const generator = accumulate();
        expect(settle(generator.next(100)).value).toEqual({ value: 0, done: false });
        expect(settle(generator.next(Promise.resolve(5))).value).toEqual({ value: 5, done: false });
        expect(settle(generator.next(0.5)).value).toEqual({ value: 5.5, done: false });
        expect(settle(generator.next()).value).toEqual({ value: 5.5, done: true });

        const returned = accumulate();
        settle(returned.next());
        expect(settle(returned.return(7)).value).toEqual({ value: 7, done: true });
        expect(settle(returned.next()).value).toEqual({ value: undefined, done: true });
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/bitwise-booleans.js
test("compiled bitwise operations take booleans as 0 and 1", () => {
    const heap = new Float32Array([1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 1, 0, 7]);
    const combine = new Function(
        "heap",
        "i",
        `return [
            (heap[i] < heap[i + 1]) & (heap[i + 2] < heap[i + 3]) & 1,
            ((heap[i] < 2) | (heap[i] > 5)) ^ true,
            (heap[i] < heap[i + 1]) << 3,
            (heap[i] > heap[i + 1]) >>> 0,
            (heap[i] < heap[i + 2]) | 0,
            ~(heap[i] > heap[i + 3]),
        ];`
    );
    const expected = i => [
        (heap[i] < heap[i + 1]) & (heap[i + 2] < heap[i + 3]) & 1,
        ((heap[i] < 2) | (heap[i] > 5)) ^ true,
        (heap[i] < heap[i + 1]) << 3,
        (heap[i] > heap[i + 1]) >>> 0,
        (heap[i] < heap[i + 2]) | 0,
        ~(heap[i] > heap[i + 3]),
    ];
    jit.prepare(combine);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) combine(heap, i & 3);
    expect(jit.compile(combine)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; ++i) expect(combine(heap, i)).toEqual(expected(i));
    expect(jit.exitCount(combine)).toBe(0);
});

test("compiled bitwise operations take operands that are sometimes booleans", () => {
    // NB: Like compiled asm.js code, where a local holds an int32 or a comparison.
    const combine = new Function(
        "a",
        "b",
        `let mixed = 0;
        mixed = a & 1 ? a >= b : mixed;
        return [mixed | (a < b), (b & 3) ^ mixed, mixed & (a > 2), ~mixed, mixed | 0, mixed >>> 0];`
    );
    const expected = (a, b) => {
        let mixed = 0;
        mixed = a & 1 ? a >= b : mixed;
        return [mixed | (a < b), (b & 3) ^ mixed, mixed & (a > 2), ~mixed, mixed | 0, mixed >>> 0];
    };
    jit.prepare(combine);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) combine(i, 5);
    expect(jit.compile(combine)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) expect(combine(i, 5)).toEqual(expected(i, 5));
    expect(jit.exitCount(combine)).toBe(0);

    // Other values still convert like ToInt32 does.
    for (const value of [1.5, -2.75, 2 ** 32 + 3, undefined, null, "7", {}]) {
        const bitwise = new Function("v", "w", "return [v | w, v & 7, v ^ w, ~v, v | 0];");
        jit.prepare(bitwise);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) bitwise(i & 1 ? i > 4 : i, i < 3);
        jit.compile(bitwise);
        expect(bitwise(value, true)).toEqual([value | true, value & 7, value ^ true, ~value, value | 0]);
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/bounds-check-elimination.js
function compiled(f, ...warmupArguments) {
    jit.prepare(f);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) f(...warmupArguments);
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return f;
}

test("counted loops stay within their bounds without bounds checks", () => {
    const fill = compiled(
        new Function(
            "heap",
            "start",
            "step",
            "end",
            `let i = start | 0, count = 0;
            do {
                heap[i] = (heap[i] | 0) + 1;
                count = (count + 1) | 0;
                i = (i + step) | 0;
            } while ((i | 0) != (end | 0) && count < 100);
            return count;`
        ),
        new Int32Array(16),
        0,
        1,
        16
    );
    const heap = new Int32Array(16);
    expect(fill(heap, 0, 1, 16)).toBe(16);
    expect(Array.from(heap)).toEqual(new Array(16).fill(1));
    // NB: A step that jumps over the bound runs past the array.
    const small = new Int32Array(4);
    expect(fill(small, 1, 2, 4)).toBe(100);
    expect(Array.from(small)).toEqual([0, 1, 0, 1]);
});

test("loops with constant bounds handle every start", () => {
    const sum = compiled(
        new Function(
            "heap",
            "start",
            `let i = start | 0, total = 0;
            do {
                total = (total + (heap[i] | 0)) | 0;
                i = (i + 1) | 0;
            } while ((i | 0) != 8);
            return total;`
        ),
        new Int32Array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]),
        0
    );
    const heap = new Int32Array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]);
    expect(sum(heap, 0)).toBe(36);
    expect(sum(heap, 5)).toBe(21);
    expect(sum(heap, -2)).toBe(36);
    expect(sum(heap, 7)).toBe(8);
});

test("loops entered in the middle by on-stack replacement keep their checks", () => {
    const heap = new Int32Array(64);
    let total = 0;
    for (let round = 0; round < 3; ++round) {
        let i = round === 2 ? 60 : 0;
        do {
            heap[i] = i;
            total = (total + heap[i]) | 0;
            i = (i + 1) | 0;
        } while ((i | 0) != 64);
    }
    expect(total).toBe(2016 + 2016 + (60 + 61 + 62 + 63));
});

test("scaled indices keep their arithmetic where it may overflow", () => {
    const body = `let i = start | 0, n = 0, total = 0;
        do {
            total = (total + (heap[(8 + (i << 2)) >> 2] | 0)) | 0;
            i = (i + 1) | 0;
            n = (n + 1) | 0;
        } while ((n | 0) != 4);
        return total;`;
    const read = compiled(new Function("heap", "start", body), new Int32Array(6), 0);
    const expected = new Function("heap", "start", body);
    const heap = new Int32Array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
    // NB: `i << 2` overflows for some of these starts, and wraps around.
    for (const start of [0, 1, 0x3ffffffe, 0x3fffffff, -0x40000000, -3, 0x7ffffffe])
        expect(read(heap, start)).toBe(expected(heap, start));
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/builtin-inlining.js
// Calls of the Array.prototype iteration builtins from hot functions, which the JIT inlines, with what makes the
// inlined code exit to the interpreter in the middle of a loop.

const ROUNDS = 300;

function sumWithForEach(array) {
    let sum = 0;
    array.forEach(value => {
        sum += value;
    });
    return sum;
}

function doubled(array) {
    return array.map(value => value * 2);
}

function odd(array) {
    return array.filter(value => value % 2 === 1);
}

test("results stay right while the callers get hot", () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) {
        expect(sumWithForEach([1, 2, 3, i])).toBe(6 + i);
        expect(doubled([1, 2, i])).toEqual([2, 4, 2 * i]);
        expect(odd([1, 2, 3, i])).toEqual(i % 2 === 1 ? [1, 3, i] : [1, 3]);
    }
});

test("other values and receivers at a hot site", () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) sumWithForEach([1, 2, 3]);
    expect(sumWithForEach([1.5, 2.5])).toBe(4);
    expect(sumWithForEach(["a", "b"])).toBe("0ab");
    expect(sumWithForEach({ length: 2, 0: 1, 1: 2, forEach: Array.prototype.forEach })).toBe(3);
    expect(sumWithForEach([1, , 3])).toBe(4);
    const withPrototypeElement = [1, , 3];
    Object.setPrototypeOf(withPrototypeElement, Object.create(Array.prototype, { 1: { value: 10 } }));
    expect(sumWithForEach(withPrototypeElement)).toBe(14);
    expect(sumWithForEach(new Proxy([4, 5], {}))).toBe(9);
    expect(doubled({ length: 1, 0: 4, map: Array.prototype.map })).toEqual([8]);
});

test("callbacks that change the array in the middle of the loop", () => {
    function shrinkAndGrow(array) {
        const seen = [];
        array.forEach((value, index) => {
            seen.push(value);
            if (index === 1) {
                array.length = 3;
                array.push(100);
            }
        });
        return seen;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) expect(shrinkAndGrow([1, 2])).toEqual([1, 2]);
    expect(shrinkAndGrow([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])).toEqual([1, 2, 3, 100]);
    expect(shrinkAndGrow([1, 2, 3])).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
});

test("exceptions thrown by callbacks of inlined builtins", () => {
    function throwsAt(array, bad) {
        return array.map(value => {
            if (value === bad) throw new Error(`bad ${value}`);
            return value + 1;
        });
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) expect(throwsAt([1, 2, 3], -1)).toEqual([2, 3, 4]);
    expect(() => throwsAt([1, 2, 3], 2)).toThrowWithMessage(Error, "bad 2");
    expect(() => throwsAt([1, 2, 3], 2)).toThrowWithMessage(Error, "bad 2");
    expect(throwsAt([5], 2)).toEqual([6]);
});

test("stack traces from callbacks of inlined builtins show the builtin", () => {
    function stackFromFilter(array) {
        let stack = null;
        array.filter(() => {
            stack = new Error().stack;
            return true;
        });
        return stack;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) stackFromFilter([1]);
    const stack = stackFromFilter([1]);
    expect(stack.includes("at filter\n")).toBeTrue();
    expect(stack.includes("BuiltinFile")).toBeFalse();
});

test("reduce with and without an initial value at hot sites", () => {
    function sum(array) {
        return array.reduce((a, b) => a + b);
    }
    function sumFrom(array, initial) {
        return array.reduce((a, b) => a + b, initial);
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) {
        expect(sum([1, 2, i])).toBe(3 + i);
        expect(sumFrom([1, 2], i)).toBe(3 + i);
    }
    expect(() => sum([])).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Reduce of empty array with no initial value");
    expect(sumFrom([], undefined)).toBeUndefined();
});

test("thisArg and the replaced builtins", () => {
    function withThis(array, thisArg) {
        return array.some(function (value) {
            "use strict";
            return this === thisArg && value > 1;
        }, thisArg);
    }
    const thisArg = {};
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) expect(withThis([1, 2], thisArg)).toBeTrue();
    expect(withThis([1, 2], 42)).toBeTrue();
    const originalSome = Array.prototype.some;
    Array.prototype.some = function () {
        return "replaced";
    };
    try {
        expect(withThis([1, 2], thisArg)).toBe("replaced");
    } finally {
        Array.prototype.some = originalSome;
    }
    expect(withThis([1, 2], thisArg)).toBeTrue();
});

test("arrays that map and filter create at hot sites", () => {
    function squares(array) {
        return array.map(value => value * value);
    }
    function evens(array) {
        return array.filter(value => value % 2 === 0);
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) {
        expect(squares([1, 2, 3])).toEqual([1, 4, 9]);
        expect(evens([1, 2, 3, 4])).toEqual([2, 4]);
    }
    const holey = squares([1, , 3]);
    expect(holey.length).toBe(3);
    expect(1 in holey).toBeFalse();
    expect(holey[2]).toBe(9);
    const many = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) many.push(i);
    expect(evens(many).length).toBe(500);
    expect(squares(many)[999]).toBe(998001);

    class Frozen extends Array {
        static get [Symbol.species]() {
            return function () {
                return Object.freeze([]);
            };
        }
    }
    const frozenSpecies = Frozen.from([1, 2]);
    expect(() => squares(frozenSpecies)).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => evens(frozenSpecies)).toThrow(TypeError);
});

test("callbacks that hot callers pass on to inlined builtins", () => {
    function isEven(value) {
        return value % 2 === 0;
    }
    function makeAbove(limit) {
        return value => value > limit;
    }
    function countMatching(array, predicate) {
        return array.filter(predicate).length;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) {
        expect(countMatching([1, 2, 3, 4], isEven)).toBe(2);
        expect(countMatching([1, 2, 3, 4], makeAbove(i % 4))).toBe(4 - (i % 4));
    }
    expect(countMatching([1.5, 2, 3.5], makeAbove(1.75))).toBe(2);
    expect(countMatching(["a", "b"], value => value === "b")).toBe(1);
    expect(countMatching([1, 2], Boolean)).toBe(2);
    expect(() => countMatching([1], 42)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "42 is not a function");
    expect(countMatching([1, 2, 3, 4], isEven)).toBe(2);
    expect(countMatching([1, 2, 3, 4], makeAbove(2))).toBe(2);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/call-paths.js
// Calls made from JIT code take fast paths for ECMAScript functions, raw
// native functions, bound functions and Function.prototype.call/apply, and
// constructing ECMAScript functions and classes takes one as well. These
// tests run every caller and callee many times, so that with a low JIT
// threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 50;

describe("calls from JIT code", () => {
    test("direct calls with missing and extra arguments", () => {
        function callee(a, b, c) {
            return [a, b, c, arguments.length];
        }
        function caller(i) {
            return [callee(i), callee(i, 1, 2, 3)];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(caller(i)).toEqual([
                [i, undefined, undefined, 1],
                [i, 1, 2, 4],
            ]);
        }
    });

    test("this values of sloppy and strict callees", () => {
        function sloppy() {
            return this;
        }
        function strict() {
            "use strict";
            return this;
        }
        function caller() {
            return [sloppy(), strict(), sloppy.call(1), strict.call(1)];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const [sloppyThis, strictThis, boxedThis, primitiveThis] = caller();
            expect(sloppyThis).toBe(globalThis);
            expect(strictThis).toBeUndefined();
            expect(boxedThis).toBeInstanceOf(Number);
            expect(primitiveThis).toBe(1);
        }
    });

    test("exceptions reach the caller's handler", () => {
        function thrower(value) {
            if (value % 2) throw new Error(`odd ${value}`);
            return value;
        }
        function middle(value) {
            return thrower(value) + 1;
        }
        function caller(value) {
            try {
                return middle(value);
            } catch (error) {
                return error.message;
            }
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller(i)).toBe(i % 2 ? `odd ${i}` : i + 1);
    });

    test("exceptions from native functions reach the caller's handler", () => {
        function caller(value) {
            try {
                return JSON.parse(value);
            } catch (error) {
                return error.name;
            }
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller(i % 2 ? "{" : `${i}`)).toBe(i % 2 ? "SyntaxError" : i);
    });

    test("native functions with captured state through call, apply, and bind", () => {
        const format = new Intl.NumberFormat("en", { useGrouping: false }).format;
        const bound = format.bind(null);
        const sentinel = {};
        function caller(value) {
            try {
                return [format(value), format.call(null, value), format.apply(null, [value]), bound(value)];
            } catch (error) {
                return error;
            }
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const value = {
                valueOf() {
                    if (i % 2) throw sentinel;
                    // Reenter the native function while it is converting an argument.
                    return Number(format(i));
                },
            };
            expect(caller(value)).toEqual(i % 2 ? sentinel : Array(4).fill(String(i)));
        }
    });

    test("stack traces include callers", () => {
        function inner() {
            return new Error().stack;
        }
        function outer() {
            return inner();
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const stack = outer();
            expect(stack.includes("at inner")).toBeTrue();
            expect(stack.includes("at outer")).toBeTrue();
        }
    });

    test("Function.prototype.call", () => {
        function add(a, b) {
            return this.base + a + b;
        }
        function caller(i) {
            return add.call({ base: i }, 1, 2);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller(i)).toBe(i + 3);
    });

    test("Function.prototype.call of a non-callable value throws", () => {
        const call = Function.prototype.call;
        function caller() {
            return call.call({});
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller).toThrow(TypeError);
    });

    test("Function.prototype.apply with arrays, arguments objects, array-likes and nullish values", () => {
        function collect() {
            return Array.from(arguments);
        }
        function forward() {
            return collect.apply(null, arguments);
        }
        function caller(i) {
            return [
                collect.apply(null, [i, 1]),
                forward(i, 2),
                collect.apply(null, { length: 2, 0: i, 1: 3 }),
                collect.apply(null, null),
                collect.apply(null),
                collect.apply(null, [i, , 4]),
            ];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(caller(i)).toEqual([[i, 1], [i, 2], [i, 3], [], [], [i, undefined, 4]]);
        }
    });

    test("Function.prototype.apply reads array-likes in order and propagates their exceptions", () => {
        function collect() {
            return Array.from(arguments);
        }
        function caller(throwAt) {
            const reads = [];
            const arrayLike = {
                get length() {
                    reads.push("length");
                    return 2;
                },
                get 0() {
                    reads.push(0);
                    if (throwAt === 0) throw new Error("no");
                    return "a";
                },
                get 1() {
                    reads.push(1);
                    return "b";
                },
            };
            try {
                return [collect.apply(null, arrayLike), reads];
            } catch (error) {
                return [error.message, reads];
            }
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(caller(-1)).toEqual([
                ["a", "b"],
                ["length", 0, 1],
            ]);
            expect(caller(0)).toEqual(["no", ["length", 0]]);
        }
    });

    test("Function.prototype.apply with a non-object argument list throws", () => {
        function f() {}
        function caller() {
            return f.apply(null, 1);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller).toThrow(TypeError);
    });

    test("bound functions", () => {
        function add(a, b, c) {
            return this.base + a + b + (c ?? 0);
        }
        const bound = add.bind({ base: 10 });
        const boundWithArguments = add.bind({ base: 20 }, 1);
        const doublyBound = boundWithArguments.bind(null, 2);
        function caller(i) {
            return [
                bound(i, 1),
                boundWithArguments(i),
                doublyBound(i),
                bound.call(null, i, 2),
                bound.apply(null, [i, 3]),
            ];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller(i)).toEqual([11 + i, 21 + i, 23 + i, 12 + i, 13 + i]);
    });

    test("class constructors cannot be called", () => {
        class C {}
        function caller() {
            return C();
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller).toThrow(TypeError);
    });

    test("proxies and native functions", () => {
        const proxy = new Proxy(function (a) {
            return a * 2;
        }, {});
        function caller(i) {
            return [proxy(i), Math.max(i, 3), String.fromCharCode(65 + (i % 26))];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i)
            expect(caller(i)).toEqual([i * 2, Math.max(i, 3), String.fromCharCode(65 + (i % 26))]);
    });

    test("constructing ECMAScript functions", () => {
        function Point(x) {
            this.x = x;
        }
        function ReturnsObject() {
            this.ignored = true;
            return { replaced: true };
        }
        function ReturnsPrimitive() {
            this.kept = true;
            return 1;
        }
        function WithoutObjectPrototype() {}
        WithoutObjectPrototype.prototype = 1;
        function NewTarget() {
            this.target = new.target;
        }
        function caller(i) {
            return [
                new Point(i),
                new ReturnsObject(),
                new ReturnsPrimitive(),
                new WithoutObjectPrototype(),
                new NewTarget(),
            ];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const [point, returnsObject, returnsPrimitive, withoutObjectPrototype, newTarget] = caller(i);
            expect(point).toBeInstanceOf(Point);
            expect(point.x).toBe(i);
            expect(returnsObject).toEqual({ replaced: true });
            expect(returnsPrimitive).toBeInstanceOf(ReturnsPrimitive);
            expect(returnsPrimitive.kept).toBeTrue();
            expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(withoutObjectPrototype)).toBe(Object.prototype);
            expect(newTarget.target).toBe(NewTarget);
        }
    });

    test("constructing classes", () => {
        let initialized = 0;
        class Base {
            field = ++initialized;
            constructor(x) {
                this.x = x;
            }
        }
        class Derived extends Base {
            constructor(x) {
                super(x);
                this.y = x + 1;
            }
        }
        class DerivedReturningObject extends Base {
            constructor() {
                super(0);
                return { replaced: true };
            }
        }
        function caller(i) {
            return [new Base(i), new Derived(i), new DerivedReturningObject()];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const [base, derived, derivedReturningObject] = caller(i);
            expect(base).toBeInstanceOf(Base);
            expect(base.x).toBe(i);
            expect(derived).toBeInstanceOf(Derived);
            expect(derived.x).toBe(i);
            expect(derived.y).toBe(i + 1);
            expect(derived.field).toBe(base.field + 1);
            expect(derivedReturningObject).toEqual({ replaced: true });
        }
        expect(initialized).toBe(3 * iterations);
    });

    test("constructors that throw or return invalid values", () => {
        class ThrowingField {
            field = (() => {
                throw new Error("field");
            })();
        }
        class Base {}
        class DerivedReturningPrimitive extends Base {
            constructor() {
                super();
                return 1;
            }
        }
        class DerivedWithoutSuper extends Base {
            constructor() {}
        }
        function Throwing() {
            throw new Error("body");
        }
        function construct(Constructor) {
            try {
                new Constructor();
                return "no exception";
            } catch (error) {
                return `${error.name}: ${error.message.includes("field") || error.message.includes("body") ? error.message : ""}`;
            }
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(construct(ThrowingField)).toBe("Error: field");
            expect(construct(Throwing)).toBe("Error: body");
            expect(construct(DerivedReturningPrimitive)).toBe("TypeError: ");
            expect(construct(DerivedWithoutSuper)).toBe("ReferenceError: ");
        }
    });

    test("unbounded recursion throws", () => {
        function recurse(depth) {
            return recurse(depth + 1) + 1;
        }
        function recurseThroughCall(depth) {
            return recurseThroughCall.call(null, depth + 1) + 1;
        }
        expect(() => recurse(0)).toThrow(InternalError);
        expect(() => recurseThroughCall(0)).toThrow(InternalError);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/calls-in-inlined-callees.js
// JIT code makes the direct and native calls of strict inlined callees without the frames of the inlined calls they
// are in, which stack walks show from the call site, and which the calls' slow paths materialize: when the callee is
// another function, when it has no JIT code or exits to the interpreter, and when it throws. These tests run every
// function many times, so that with a low JIT threshold they are compiled, and check that what the callees see is
// the same throughout.

const iterations = 200;

function stackFunctionNames(error) {
    return error.stack
        .split("\n")
        .map(line => line.trim())
        .filter(line => line.startsWith("at "))
        .map(line => line.slice(3).split(" ")[0]);
}

describe("calls in inlined callees", () => {
    test("Error.stack shows the inlined callees", () => {
        // NB: The callee is too large to be inlined itself.
        function makeError(value) {
            "use strict";
            if (value === -1) {
                value = (value * 3 + 1) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 7) + 7;
                value = (value * 5 + 2) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 11) + 11;
                value = (value * 7 + 3) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 13) + 13;
                value = (value * 9 + 4) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 17) + 17;
            }
            return new Error(`here ${value}`);
        }
        function middle() {
            "use strict";
            return makeError(1);
        }
        function outer() {
            "use strict";
            return middle();
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const names = stackFunctionNames(outer());
            const start = names.indexOf("makeError");
            expect(names.slice(start, start + 3)).toEqual(["makeError", "middle", "outer"]);
        }
    });

    test("Error.stack of an error thrown by a native function called from an inlined callee", () => {
        function parse(text) {
            "use strict";
            return JSON.parse(text);
        }
        function middle(text) {
            "use strict";
            return parse(text) + 1;
        }
        function outer(text) {
            "use strict";
            return middle(text);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const valid = i % 50 !== 49;
            if (valid) {
                expect(outer(String(i))).toBe(i + 1);
                continue;
            }
            let caught = null;
            try {
                outer("{");
            } catch (error) {
                caught = error;
            }
            expect(caught).toBeInstanceOf(SyntaxError);
            expect(stackFunctionNames(caught)).toContain("middle");
        }
    });

    test("the legacy caller of a function called from a strict inlined callee", () => {
        // NB: The callee is too large to be inlined itself.
        function sloppyCallee(value) {
            if (value === -1) {
                value = (value * 3 + 1) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 7) + 7;
                value = (value * 5 + 2) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 11) + 11;
                value = (value * 7 + 3) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 13) + 13;
                value = (value * 9 + 4) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 17) + 17;
            }
            return sloppyCallee.caller;
        }
        function middle() {
            "use strict";
            return sloppyCallee(1);
        }
        function outer() {
            return middle();
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(outer()).toBeNull();
    });

    test("the legacy caller and arguments of a function called from a non-strict inlined callee", () => {
        // NB: The callee is too large to be inlined itself.
        function sloppyCallee(a, b) {
            if (a === -1) {
                a = (a * 3 + b) | 0;
                b = (b ^ a) + 7;
                a = (a * 5 + b) | 0;
                b = (b ^ a) + 11;
                a = (a * 7 + b) | 0;
                b = (b ^ a) + 13;
                a = (a * 9 + b) | 0;
                b = (b ^ a) + 17;
            }
            return [sloppyCallee.caller, Array.from(sloppyCallee.arguments)];
        }
        function middle(x) {
            return sloppyCallee(x, x + 1);
        }
        function outer(x) {
            return middle(x);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const [caller, args] = outer(i);
            expect(caller).toBe(middle);
            expect(args).toEqual([i, i + 1]);
        }
    });

    test("the legacy caller and arguments of a non-strict inlined callee, from a function it calls", () => {
        // NB: The callee is too large to be inlined itself.
        function inspect(value) {
            if (value === -1) {
                value = (value * 3 + 1) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 7) + 7;
                value = (value * 5 + 2) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 11) + 11;
                value = (value * 7 + 3) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 13) + 13;
                value = (value * 9 + 4) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 17) + 17;
            }
            return [inspect.caller === middle, Array.from(middle.arguments), middle.caller === outer, value];
        }
        // NB: The middle function reads all its arguments, none of which it needs once it calls.
        function middle(a, b, c) {
            if (c === null) return b;
            return inspect(a + 1);
        }
        function outer(a) {
            return middle(a, `b${a}`, { c: a });
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const [callerIsMiddle, middleArguments, middleCallerIsOuter, value] = outer(i);
            expect(callerIsMiddle).toBeTrue();
            expect(middleArguments.length).toBe(3);
            expect(middleArguments[0]).toBe(i);
            expect(middleArguments[1]).toBe(`b${i}`);
            expect(middleArguments[2].c).toBe(i);
            expect(middleCallerIsOuter).toBeTrue();
            expect(value).toBe(i + 1);
        }
    });

    test("the legacy caller of a function called from an inlined closure", () => {
        // NB: The callee is too large to be inlined itself.
        function inspect(value) {
            if (value === -1) {
                value = (value * 3 + 1) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 7) + 7;
                value = (value * 5 + 2) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 11) + 11;
                value = (value * 7 + 3) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 13) + 13;
                value = (value * 9 + 4) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 17) + 17;
            }
            return inspect.caller;
        }
        function makeClosure(offset) {
            return function closure(value) {
                return [inspect(value + offset), closure];
            };
        }
        const closures = [makeClosure(1), makeClosure(2)];
        function outer(closure, value) {
            return closure(value);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const closure = closures[i % 100 === 99 ? 1 : 0];
            const [caller, self] = outer(closure, i);
            expect(caller).toBe(self);
            expect(caller).toBe(closure);
        }
    });

    test("exceptions from callees caught in the inlined callee and further out", () => {
        function thrower(value) {
            "use strict";
            if (value % 7 === 3) throw new Error(`bad ${value}`);
            return value * 2;
        }
        function catchingMiddle(value) {
            "use strict";
            try {
                return thrower(value);
            } catch (error) {
                return error.message;
            }
        }
        function middle(value) {
            "use strict";
            return thrower(value) + 1;
        }
        function outer(value) {
            "use strict";
            let result;
            try {
                result = middle(value);
            } catch (error) {
                result = `outer ${error.message}`;
            }
            return [result, catchingMiddle(value)];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const expected = i % 7 === 3 ? [`outer bad ${i}`, `bad ${i}`] : [i * 2 + 1, i * 2];
            expect(outer(i)).toEqual(expected);
        }
    });

    test("callees that exit to the interpreter or have no JIT code", () => {
        // NB: The callee is too large to be inlined itself.
        function callee(value) {
            "use strict";
            if (value === -1) {
                value = (value * 3 + 1) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 7) + 7;
                value = (value * 5 + 2) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 11) + 11;
                value = (value * 7 + 3) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 13) + 13;
                value = (value * 9 + 4) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 17) + 17;
            }
            return value.x + 1;
        }
        function middle(value, other) {
            "use strict";
            const before = other * 3;
            const result = callee(value);
            return [before, result, other];
        }
        function outer(value, other) {
            "use strict";
            return middle(value, other);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            // NB: The callee sees objects of other shapes, and strings, now and then.
            let value = { x: i };
            if (i % 40 === 39) value = { y: 0, x: i };
            if (i % 60 === 59) value = String(i);
            const [before, result, other] = outer(value, i);
            expect(before).toBe(i * 3);
            expect(other).toBe(i);
            if (typeof value === "string") expect(result).toBeNaN();
            else expect(result).toBe(i + 1);
        }
    });

    test("call sites that see another callee", () => {
        // NB: The callees are too large to be inlined themselves.
        function first(value) {
            "use strict";
            if (value === -1) {
                value = (value * 3 + 1) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 7) + 7;
                value = (value * 5 + 2) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 11) + 11;
