                value = (value * 7 + 3) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 13) + 13;
                value = (value * 9 + 4) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 17) + 17;
            }
            return value + 1;
        }
        function second(value) {
            "use strict";
            if (value === -1) {
                value = (value * 3 + 1) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 7) + 7;
                value = (value * 5 + 2) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 11) + 11;
                value = (value * 7 + 3) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 13) + 13;
                value = (value * 9 + 4) | 0;
                value = (value ^ 17) + 17;
            }
            return value + 2;
        }
        function middle(callee, value) {
            "use strict";
            const kept = value * 5;
            return [callee(value), kept];
        }
        function outer(callee, value) {
            "use strict";
            return middle(callee, value);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const callee = i % 25 === 24 ? second : first;
            expect(outer(callee, i)).toEqual([callee === first ? i + 1 : i + 2, i * 5]);
        }
    });

    test("values of the inlined callees survive garbage collection in their callees", () => {
        function collect(value) {
            "use strict";
            if (value % 50 === 0) gc();
            return value;
        }
        function middle(value) {
            "use strict";
            const object = { value, list: [value, value + 1] };
            const text = `text ${value}`;
            collect(value);
            return object.list[1] + object.value + text.length;
        }
        function outer(value) {
            "use strict";
            return middle(value);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(outer(i)).toBe(2 * i + 1 + `text ${i}`.length);
    });

    test("native functions that call back into JavaScript from inlined callees", () => {
        let names = null;
        function reviver(key, value) {
            "use strict";
            if (key === "") names = stackFunctionNames(new Error());
            return value;
        }
        function middle(text) {
            "use strict";
            return JSON.parse(text, reviver);
        }
        function outer(text) {
            "use strict";
            return middle(text);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            names = null;
            expect(outer(String(i))).toBe(i);
            expect(names).toContain("reviver");
            expect(names).toContain("middle");
            expect(names).toContain("outer");
        }
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/calls-with-target-changes.js
// Calls, compiled (and inlined) after warming up with one callee, then given other callees: other functions, closures
// of the same function, natives, bound functions, proxies, classes, getters, callees that throw or re-enter the
// compiled code, and calls with too few or too many arguments. The compiled code must do what the interpreter does
// (see compareCompiledWithInterpreter in test-common.js).

const callees = {
    "same function": () => (a, b) => a + b,
    "other function": () => (a, b) => a * b,
    "closure with state": log => {
        let calls = 0;
        return (a, b) => {
            log.push(`closure call ${++calls}`);
            return a - b;
        };
    },
    "function using arguments": () =>
        function () {
            return arguments.length + arguments[0];
        },
    "function with rest":
        () =>
        (...rest) =>
            rest.length,
    "function with defaults":
        () =>
        (a, b = 100) =>
            a + b,
    "function returning nothing": () => () => {},
    "throwing function": log => () => {
        log.push("throwing");
        throw new EvalError("callee threw");
    },
    "throwing a primitive": () => () => {
        throw 42;
    },
    "deep recursion": () => {
        const recurse = n => (n <= 0 ? 0 : 1 + recurse(n - 1));
        return a => recurse(a % 50);
    },
    native: () => Math.max,
    "native that throws": () => Object.defineProperty,
    "bound function": () =>
        function (a, b) {
            return [this.tag, a, b];
        }.bind({ tag: "bound" }, "first"),
    proxy: log =>
        new Proxy((a, b) => a + b, {
            apply(target, thisArgument, args) {
                log.push(`apply ${args.length}`);
                return Reflect.apply(target, thisArgument, args);
            },
        }),
    class: () => class {},
    generator: () =>
        function* (a) {
            yield a;
        },
    "async function": () => async a => a,
    "not callable": () => ({}),
    undefined: () => undefined,
    "getter calling": log => {
        const object = {
            get value() {
                log.push("getter");
                return 7;
            },
        };
        return a => object.value + a;
    },
    "callee that calls back": log => (a, b, again) => {
        if (typeof again === "function" && a > 0) {
            log.push("re-entering");
            return again(again, a - 1);
        }
        return a;
    },
    "callee that collects garbage": () => (a, b) => {
        gc();
        return a + b;
    },
    "strict this": () =>
        function () {
            "use strict";
            return this;
        },
    "sloppy this": () =>
        function () {
            return typeof this;
        },
};

const probes = {};
for (const [name, make] of Object.entries(callees)) probes[name] = (log, i) => [make(log), i, log];

describe("calls of changing callees", () => {
    const forms = {
        call: () => (callee, i) => callee(i, 2),
        "call with too few arguments": () => (callee, i) => callee(i),
        "call with too many arguments": () => (callee, i) => callee(i, 2, 3, 4, 5),
        "call with spread": () => (callee, i) => callee(...[i, 2]),
        "method call": () => (callee, i) => {
            const object = { method: callee, tag: "object" };
            return object.method(i, 2);
        },
        "call in a loop": () => (callee, i) => {
            let result = [];
            for (let k = 0; k < 3; ++k) result.push(callee(i + k, k));
            return result;
        },
        "call caught": () => (callee, i) => {
            try {
                return callee(i, 2);
            } catch (e) {
                return `caught ${e}`;
            }
        },
        "call with finally": () => (callee, i, log) => {
            let state = "before";
            try {
                state = "calling";
                return [callee(i, 2), state];
            } finally {
                log.push(`finally saw ${state}`);
            }
        },
        construct: () => (callee, i) => {
            const made = new callee(i, 2);
            return typeof made;
        },
        "call through apply": () => (callee, i) => callee.apply(undefined, [i, 2]),
        "call through call": () => (callee, i) => callee.call({ tag: "this" }, i, 2),
        "re-entrant call": () => {
            const self = (callee, i, log) =>
                typeof callee === "function" ? callee(i % 3, 2, (again, a) => self(callee, a, log)) : "not callable";
            return self;
        },
    };
    for (const [name, factory] of Object.entries(forms)) {
        test(name, () => {
            const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(factory, {
                warmUp: (log, i) => [(a, b) => a + b, i, log],
                probes,
            });
            expect(failures).toEqual([]);
        });
    }
});

describe("inlined calls", () => {
    test("exits at every depth of an inlined chain", () => {
        const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
            () => {
                const leaf = value => value.amount * 2;
                const middle = value => leaf(value) + 1;
                const outer = value => [middle(value), value.amount];
                return value => outer(value);
            },
            {
                warmUp: (log, i) => [{ amount: i }],
                probes: {
                    double: () => [{ amount: 1.5 }],
                    string: () => [{ amount: "3" }],
                    "other shape": () => [{ other: 1, amount: 2 }],
                    getter: log => [
                        {
                            get amount() {
                                log.push("amount getter");
                                return 4;
                            },
                        },
                    ],
                    "throwing getter": () => [
                        {
                            get amount() {
                                throw new Error("amount getter threw");
                            },
                        },
                    ],
                    overflow: () => [{ amount: 2147483647 }],
                    null: () => [null],
                },
            }
        );
        expect(failures).toEqual([]);
    });

    test("locals of the caller survive exceptions in inlined callees", () => {
        const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
            () => {
                const check = value => {
                    if (value > 5) throw new RangeError(`too big: ${value}`);
                    return value;
                };
                return (value, log) => {
                    let local = value * 2;
                    const other = { value };
                    try {
                        local += check(value);
                    } catch (e) {
                        log.push(`caught ${e.message}, local is ${local}, other is ${other.value}`);
                        local = -local;
                    }
                    return [local, other.value];
                };
            },
            {
                warmUp: (log, i) => [i % 5, log],
                probes: { throwing: log => [9, log], double: log => [2.5, log], string: log => ["4", log] },
            }
        );
        expect(failures).toEqual([]);
    });

    test("results of native calls in inlined callees", () => {
        const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
            () => {
                const inner = (a, b) => Math.max(a, b) + Math.min(a, b) * 2;
                return (a, b) => [inner(a, b), inner(b, a)];
            },
            {
                warmUp: (log, i) => [i, 3],
                probes: {
                    doubles: () => [1.5, -0],
                    strings: () => ["7", "2"],
                    objects: () => [{ valueOf: () => 3 }, 1],
                },
            }
        );
        expect(failures).toEqual([]);
    });

    test("arguments objects of inlined callees", () => {
        const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
            () => {
                function inner() {
                    return [arguments.length, arguments[0], arguments[arguments.length - 1]];
                }
                function mapped(a) {
                    arguments[0] = "changed";
                    return a;
                }
                return (a, b) => [inner(a, b), inner(a), mapped(a)];
            },
            {
                warmUp: (log, i) => [i, 2],
                probes: { undefined: () => [undefined, undefined], object: () => [{}, []] },
            }
        );
        expect(failures).toEqual([]);
    });

    test("this of inlined methods", () => {
        const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
            () => {
                const prototype = {
                    total() {
                        return this.a + this.b;
                    },
                    scaled(factor) {
                        return this.total() * factor;
                    },
                };
                return (a, b) => {
                    const object = Object.create(prototype);
                    object.a = a;
                    object.b = b;
                    return object.scaled(2);
                };
            },
            {
                warmUp: (log, i) => [i, 1],
                probes: { strings: () => ["x", "y"], overflow: () => [2147483647, 2147483647] },
            }
        );
        expect(failures).toEqual([]);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/captured-binding-stores.js
function compiled(f, ...warmupArguments) {
    jit.prepare(f);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) f(...warmupArguments);
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return f;
}

test("compiled stores to captured var bindings", () => {
    function outer() {
        var top = 0;
        function store(value) {
            top = value;
            return top;
        }
        return [store, () => top];
    }
    const [store, read] = outer();
    compiled(store, 1);
    expect(store(42)).toBe(42);
    expect(read()).toBe(42);
});

test("compiled stores to captured const bindings still throw", () => {
    function outer() {
        const fixed = 1;
        let calls = 0;
        function store(value) {
            calls = (calls + 1) | 0;
            if (value === "assign") fixed = 2;
            return calls;
        }
        return [store, () => fixed];
    }
    const [store, read] = outer();
    compiled(store, 0);
    expect(() => store("assign")).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Invalid assignment to const variable");
    expect(read()).toBe(1);
});

test("compiled stores to captured let bindings before their initialization still throw", () => {
    function outer(storeFirst) {
        function store(value) {
            late = value;
            return late;
        }
        if (storeFirst) store(1);
        let late = 0;
        return store;
    }
    const store = outer(false);
    compiled(store, 1);
    expect(store(5)).toBe(5);
    expect(() => outer(true)).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "Binding late is not initialized");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/captured-object-bindings.js
function compileCaptured(f, warmUp = f => f()) {
    jit.prepare(f);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) warmUp(f);
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return f;
}

function capturedArray(value) {
    var array = new Int32Array([value]);
    return {
        read: () => array[0],
        replace: value => {
            array = value;
        },
    };
}

test("captured typed arrays keep observing writes to their elements", () => {
    const closure = capturedArray(123);
    const read = compileCaptured(closure.read);
    expect(read()).toBe(123);
    closure.replace(new Int32Array([456]));
    expect(read()).toBe(456);
    closure.replace([789]);
    expect(read()).toBe(789);
    closure.replace(null);
    expect(read).toThrow(TypeError);
});

test("closures sharing compiled code read their own captured objects", () => {
    const first = capturedArray(12);
    const second = capturedArray(34);
    compileCaptured(first.read);
    expect(first.read()).toBe(12);
    expect(second.read()).toBe(34);
    first.replace(new Int32Array([56]));
    expect(second.read()).toBe(34);
    expect(first.read()).toBe(56);
});

test("captured objects are reloaded after calls that replace them", () => {
    var object = { value: 1 };
    function read(callback) {
        const before = object.value;
        callback();
        return [before, object.value];
    }
    compileCaptured(read, f => f(() => {}));
    expect(read(() => (object = { value: 2 }))).toEqual([1, 2]);
    expect(read(() => (object = { value: 3 }))).toEqual([2, 3]);
});

test("captured objects are reloaded after stores in a compiled loop", () => {
    var object = { value: 10 };
    function sum(count, replace) {
        let result = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
            result += object.value;
            if (i === 2 && replace) object = { value: 20 };
        }
        return result;
    }
    compileCaptured(sum, f => f(8, false));
    expect(sum(8, true)).toBe(130);
    expect(sum(8, false)).toBe(160);
});

test("captured functions and outer environments retain their identity", () => {
    function outer(value) {
        var callable = () => value;
        return function middle() {
            return {
                call: () => callable(),
                replace: replacement => {
                    callable = replacement;
                },
            };
        };
    }
    const closure = outer(17)();
    const call = compileCaptured(closure.call);
    expect(call()).toBe(17);
    closure.replace(() => 29);
    expect(call()).toBe(29);
});

test("captured constants survive garbage collection and buffer detachment", () => {
    function factory() {
        var array = new Int32Array([42]);
        return { array, read: () => array[0] };
    }
    const closure = factory();
    compileCaptured(closure.read);
    gc();
    expect(closure.read()).toBe(42);
    detachArrayBuffer(closure.array.buffer);
    expect(closure.read()).toBeUndefined();
});

test("local environments and uninitialized captured bindings preserve their behavior", () => {
    var object = { value: 1 };
    function local(value) {
        {
            let object = { value };
            return (() => object.value)();
        }
    }
    compileCaptured(local, f => f(2));
    expect(local(3)).toBe(3);
    function uninitialized() {
        const read = () => object;
        jit.prepare(read);
        jit.compile(read);
        expect(read).toThrow(ReferenceError);
        let object = { value: 4 };
        return read();
    }
    expect(uninitialized()).toEqual({ value: 4 });
    expect(object.value).toBe(1);
});

// NB: The factories come from new Function, so that each run of a test (see LIBJS_TEST_REPEAT) has new functions
//     whose closures it counts from zero.
function readerFactory() {
    return new Function(
        "value",
        "var array = new Int32Array([value]); return { read: () => array[0], replace: value => { array = value; } };"
    );
}

function exitKinds(f) {
    return jit.exitSites(f).map(site => site.split("@")[0]);
}

test("the only closure of a function speculates on its captured objects once", () => {
    const closure = readerFactory()(5);
    compileCaptured(closure.read);
    expect(closure.read()).toBe(5);
    closure.replace(new Int32Array([6]));
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i) expect(closure.read()).toBe(6);
    if (!jit.enabled || jit.forcesExits) return;
    expect(exitKinds(closure.read)).toContain("UnexpectedValue");
    expect(jit.discardCount(closure.read)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
    expect(jit.compile(closure.read)).toBeTrue();
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i) expect(closure.read()).toBe(6);
    expect(jit.exitCount(closure.read)).toBe(0);
});

test("a captured object that changed is not speculated on at any of its loads", () => {
    const closure = new Function(
        "var object = { value: 1 }; return { read: first => (first ? object.value : object.value * 2), replace: value => { object = value; } };"
    )();
    compileCaptured(closure.read, f => {
        f(true);
        f(false);
    });
    closure.replace({ value: 3 });
    expect(closure.read(true)).toBe(3);
    if (!jit.enabled || jit.forcesExits) return;
    expect(exitKinds(closure.read)).toContain("UnexpectedValue");
    jit.discard(closure.read);
    expect(jit.compile(closure.read)).toBeTrue();
    expect(closure.read(false)).toBe(6);
    expect(jit.exitCount(closure.read)).toBe(0);
});

test("closures of one function do not speculate on each other's captured objects", () => {
    const makeReader = readerFactory();
    const readers = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 32; ++i) readers.push(makeReader(i).read);
    compileCaptured(readers[0], () => readers.forEach(read => read()));
    let sum = 0;
    for (let round = 0; round < 20; ++round) for (const read of readers) sum += read();
    expect(sum).toBe(20 * ((31 * 32) / 2));
    if (!jit.enabled || jit.forcesExits) return;
    expect(jit.exitCount(readers[0])).toBe(0);
    expect(jit.discardCount(readers[0])).toBe(0);
    expect(exitKinds(readers[0])).not.toContain("UnexpectedValue");
});

test("closures created after a compile stop the speculation on captured objects", () => {
    const makeReader = readerFactory();
    const first = makeReader(0).read;
    compileCaptured(first);
    const readers = [first];
    for (let i = 1; i < 32; ++i) readers.push(makeReader(i).read);
    let sum = 0;
    for (let round = 0; round < 20; ++round) for (const read of readers) sum += read();
    expect(sum).toBe(20 * ((31 * 32) / 2));
    if (!jit.enabled || jit.forcesExits) return;
    expect(jit.discardCount(first)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
    expect(jit.compile(first)).toBeTrue();
    for (let round = 0; round < 20; ++round) for (const read of readers) sum += read();
    expect(jit.exitCount(first)).toBe(0);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/capturing-native-calls.js
test("capturing native calls retain their state and guard the target", () => {
    const first = Proxy.revocable({}, {});
    const second = Proxy.revocable({}, {});
    function invoke(revoke) {
        return revoke();
    }
    jit.prepare(invoke);
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i) expect(invoke(first.revoke)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(jit.compile(invoke) || !jit.enabled).toBeTrue();
    gc();
    expect(invoke(first.revoke)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(Reflect.ownKeys(second.proxy)).toEqual([]);
    expect(invoke(second.revoke)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(() => Reflect.ownKeys(second.proxy)).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(invoke(() => 42)).toBe(42);
});

test("exceptions from capturing native calls unwind inlined callers", () => {
    const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
        () => {
            function strictArguments() {
                "use strict";
                return arguments;
            }
            const thrower = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(strictArguments(), "callee").get;
            function inner(value) {
                thrower(value);
            }
            function middle(value) {
                return inner(value);
            }
            return (value, log) => {
                gc();
                try {
                    return middle(value);
                } catch (error) {
                    log.push(error instanceof TypeError);
                    return value;
                } finally {
                    log.push("finally");
                }
            };
        },
        {
            warmUp: (log, i) => [i, log],
            probes: { object: log => [{ marker: 42 }, log] },
        }
    );
    expect(failures).toEqual([]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/checked-doubles.js
test("compiled comparisons of doubles that held int32 values stay exact", () => {
    const keys = new Float64Array([1, 2, 3, 4]);
    const countBelow = new Function(
        "keys",
        "limit",
        `let count = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < keys.length; ++i) {
            if (keys[i] < limit) count = (count + 1) | 0;
        }
        return count;`
    );
    jit.prepare(countBelow);
    for (let k = 0; k < 10; ++k) countBelow(keys, k);
    expect(jit.compile(countBelow)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(countBelow(keys, 2.5)).toBe(2);
    keys.set([0.5, -0, NaN, 3.25]);
    expect(countBelow(keys, 0)).toBe(0);
    expect(countBelow(keys, 1)).toBe(2);
    expect(countBelow(keys, 3.5)).toBe(3);
    expect(countBelow(keys, Infinity)).toBe(3);
});

test("compiled arithmetic on doubles that held int32 values stays exact", () => {
    const values = new Float64Array([1, 2, 3, 4]);
    const sum = new Function(
        "values",
        `let total = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < values.length; ++i) total += values[i];
        return total;`
    );
    jit.prepare(sum);
    for (let k = 0; k < 10; ++k) sum(values);
    expect(jit.compile(sum)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(sum(values)).toBe(10);
    values.set([0.5, 0.25, -0, 1e300]);
    expect(sum(values)).toBe(0.75 + 1e300);
    values.set([NaN, 1, 2, 3]);
    expect(sum(values)).toBeNaN();
});

test("unused int32 arithmetic keeps converting operands with effects", () => {
    const add = new Function("a", "b", "const sum = a + b; return 1;");
    jit.prepare(add);
    for (let k = 0; k < 10; ++k) add(k, 2);
    jit.compile(add);
    let calls = 0;
    expect(add({ valueOf: () => ++calls }, 1)).toBe(1);
    expect(calls).toBe(1);
    expect(() => add(Symbol(), 1)).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => add(1n, 1)).toThrow(TypeError);
});

test("doubles that are both compared and used as indices keep their checks", () => {
    const lookup = new Function(
        "keys",
        "table",
        "limit",
        `let total = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < keys.length; ++i) {
            if (keys[i] < limit) total += table[keys[i]];
        }
        return total;`
    );
    const keys = new Float64Array([0, 1, 2, 3]);
    const table = [10, 20, 30, 40];
    jit.prepare(lookup);
    for (let k = 0; k < 10; ++k) lookup(keys, table, 4);
    jit.compile(lookup);
    expect(lookup(keys, table, 4)).toBe(100);
    // NB: Keys that are no int32 values index no elements.
    keys.set([1, 1, 2.5, 3]);
    expect(lookup(keys, table, 2)).toBe(40);
    expect(lookup(keys, table, 4)).toBeNaN();
});

test("compiled identities of doubles that held int32 values convert them", () => {
    const midpoint = new Function("low", "high", "return ((low + high) / 2) | 0;");
    const plusZero = new Function("values", "return values[0] + 0;");
    const shifted = new Function("values", "return (values[0] << 0) + (values[0] >> 0) + (values[0] ^ 0);");
    const values = new Float64Array([4]);
    for (const f of [midpoint, plusZero, shifted]) jit.prepare(f);
    for (let k = 0; k < 10; ++k) {
        midpoint(k, k + 2);
        plusZero(values);
        shifted(values);
    }
    for (const f of [midpoint, plusZero, shifted]) expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(midpoint(1, 2)).toBe(1);
    expect(midpoint(-1, -2)).toBe(-1);
    expect(midpoint(0, NaN)).toBe(0);
    expect(midpoint(2 ** 32, 2 ** 32 + 6)).toBe(3);
    values[0] = -0;
    expect(Object.is(plusZero(values), 0)).toBeTrue();
    values[0] = 2.5;
    expect(plusZero(values)).toBe(2.5);
    expect(shifted(values)).toBe(6);
    values[0] = -(2 ** 31) - 1.5;
    expect(shifted(values)).toBe(3 * (2 ** 31 - 1));
});

test("folds that give doubles checked to be int32 values int32 users keep the checks", () => {
    const sum = new Function(
        "a",
        "b",
        "count",
        "start",
        `let y = +(a * b);
        let s = start;
        for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            let t = y;
            if (i > 1000) t = y;
            y = t;
            s = s + y;
        }
        return s;`
    );
    jit.prepare(sum);
    for (let k = 0; k < 10; ++k) {
        sum(1.5, 2, 3, 0);
        sum(1.5, 2, 2, "a");
    }
    expect(jit.compile(sum)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(sum(1.5, 2, 3, 0)).toBe(9);
    expect(sum(1.5, 2, 2, "a")).toBe("a33");
    expect(sum(1.25, 2, 2, 1)).toBe(6);
    expect(sum(1.25, 2, 2, "b")).toBe("b2.52.5");
});

test("number conversions of boxed doubles checked to be int32 values keep the checks", () => {
    const keys = new Float64Array([1, 2, 3, 4]);
    const add = new Function("x", "j", "const y = +x; return j + (y | 0);");
    // NB: Math.min() needs the key as an int32, so compiled code checks that it is one.
    //     The inlined `+x` then converts that int32 back, through the loop's copy of the key.
    const addKey = new Function(
        "add",
        "keys",
        "i",
        "n",
        `const key = +keys[i];
        Math.min(key, key);
        let index = key;
        let sum = 0;
        for (let j = 0; j < n; ++j) {
            sum = add(index, j);
            const same = index;
            index = same;
        }
        return sum;`
    );
    jit.prepare(add);
    jit.prepare(addKey);
    for (let k = 0; k < 10; ++k) {
        add(1, k);
        add("5", k);
        add(1.5, k);
    }
    for (let k = 0; k < 10; ++k) addKey(add, keys, k & 3, 2);
    expect(jit.compile(addKey)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(addKey(add, keys, 1, 2)).toBe(3);
    expect(addKey(add, keys, 2, 3)).toBe(5);
    keys.set([0.5, 2.75, -1.5, 2 ** 40]);
    expect(addKey(add, keys, 0, 2)).toBe(1);
    expect(addKey(add, keys, 1, 2)).toBe(3);
    expect(addKey(add, keys, 2, 2)).toBe(0);
    expect(addKey(add, keys, 3, 2)).toBe(1);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/clamped-array-stores.js
test("compiled clamped stores round ties to even and saturate", () => {
    const store = new Function("array", "index", "value", "array[index] = value; return array[index];");
    const array = new Uint8ClampedArray(2);
    jit.prepare(store);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) store(array, 1, 1.25);
    expect(jit.compile(store)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    for (const [value, expected] of [
        [-Infinity, 0],
        [-1e300, 0],
        [-0.5, 0],
        [-0, 0],
        [0, 0],
        [NaN, 0],
        [Number.MIN_VALUE, 0],
        [0.49999999999999994, 0],
        [0.5, 0],
        [0.5000000000000001, 1],
        [1.4999999999999998, 1],
        [1.5, 2],
        [1.5000000000000002, 2],
        [2.5, 2],
        [3.5, 4],
        [254.49999999999997, 254],
        [254.5, 254],
        [254.50000000000003, 255],
        [255, 255],
        [255.5, 255],
        [1e300, 255],
        [Infinity, 255],
    ]) {
        expect(store(array, 1, value)).toBe(expected);
        expect(array[0]).toBe(0);
    }
    expect(jit.exitCount(store)).toBe(0);
});

test("clamped stores preserve coercion and invalid indices", () => {
    const store = new Function("array", "index", "value", "array[index] = value; return array[index];");
    const array = new Uint8ClampedArray(2);
    jit.prepare(store);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) store(array, 0, 2.25);
    jit.compile(store);
    let calls = 0;
    const value = {
        valueOf() {
            ++calls;
            return 3.5;
        },
    };
    expect(store(array, 0, value)).toBe(4);
    expect(calls).toBe(1);
    expect(store(array, 0, "2.5")).toBe(2);
    expect(store(array, 0, undefined)).toBe(0);
    expect(() => store(array, 0, 1n)).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(store(array, -1, 8.5)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(store(array, 2, 8.5)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(store(array, 0.5, 8.5)).toBeUndefined();
});

test("compiled clamped stores handle resizing and detaching buffers", () => {
    const compileStore = array => {
        const store = new Function("array", "index", "value", "array[index] = value; return array[index];");
        jit.prepare(store);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) store(array, 0, 2.25);
        expect(jit.compile(store)).toBe(jit.enabled);
        return store;
    };
    const buffer = new ArrayBuffer(2, { maxByteLength: 8 });
    const resizable = new Uint8ClampedArray(buffer);
    const store = compileStore(resizable);
    expect(store(resizable, 1, 2.5)).toBe(2);
    buffer.resize(1);
    expect(store(resizable, 1, 3.5)).toBeUndefined();
    buffer.resize(4);
    expect(store(resizable, 3, 3.5)).toBe(4);
    const array = new Uint8ClampedArray(2);
    const detachedStore = compileStore(array);
    detachArrayBuffer(array.buffer);
    expect(detachedStore(array, 0, 5.5)).toBeUndefined();
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/closure-inlining.js
// Calls of closures that hot functions create themselves, which the JIT inlines without feedback, as each call of
// the outer function creates a new closure.

const ROUNDS = 300;

test("closures read the variables they capture", () => {
    function addAll(values, offset) {
        let total = 0;
        const add = value => {
            total += value + offset;
        };
        for (const value of values) add(value);
        return total;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) expect(addAll([1, 2], i)).toBe(3 + 2 * i);
    expect(addAll([1.5], 0.25)).toBe(1.75);
    expect(addAll(["a"], "b")).toBe("0ab");
});

test("closures passed to inlined builtins", () => {
    function matching(items, id) {
        return items.filter(item => item.id === id).map(item => ({ id: item.id, title: item.title + "!" }));
    }
    const items = [
        { id: 1, title: "one" },
        { id: 2, title: "two" },
    ];
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) {
        const id = 1 + (i % 2);
        expect(matching(items, id)).toEqual([{ id, title: (id === 1 ? "one" : "two") + "!" }]);
    }
    expect(matching([{ id: 1, title: 5 }], 1)).toEqual([{ id: 1, title: "5!" }]);
    expect(matching([{ id: "1" }], 1)).toEqual([]);
});

test("exits, exceptions and stack traces inside inlined closures", () => {
    function run(values, failAt) {
        const seen = [];
        values.forEach(value => {
            if (value === failAt) throw new Error(`failed at ${value} ${new Error().stack.includes("at forEach\n")}`);
            seen.push(value * 2);
        });
        return seen;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) expect(run([1, 2, 3], -1)).toEqual([2, 4, 6]);
    expect(run([1.5, "x", 3], -1)).toEqual([3, NaN, 6]);
    expect(() => run([1, 2, 3], 2)).toThrowWithMessage(Error, "failed at 2 true");
    expect(run([4], -1)).toEqual([8]);
});

test("closures that change what they captured", () => {
    function counter(values) {
        let count = 0;
        const bump = () => ++count;
        values.forEach(bump);
        values.forEach(() => {
            count *= 2;
        });
        return count;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < ROUNDS; ++i) expect(counter([1, 2])).toBe(8);
    expect(counter([])).toBe(0);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/closures.js
// JIT code creates the function objects of closures itself, by copying one it
// made for the same code before. These tests run every function many times,
// so that with a low JIT threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

describe("closures created in JIT code", () => {
    test("environments, names, lengths and prototypes", () => {
        function makeAdder(x) {
            return function (y) {
                return x + y;
            };
        }
        function makeArrow(x) {
            const multiply = (y, z) => x * y;
            return multiply;
        }
        function makeNamed(i) {
            function inner(a, b, c) {
                return i;
            }
            return inner;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const adder = makeAdder(i);
            expect(adder(1)).toBe(i + 1);
            expect(adder.name).toBe("");
            expect(adder.length).toBe(1);
            expect(typeof adder.prototype).toBe("object");
            expect(adder.prototype.constructor).toBe(adder);
            expect(adder.prototype).not.toBe(makeAdder(i).prototype);
            expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(adder)).toBe(Function.prototype);

            const arrow = makeArrow(i);
            expect(arrow(2)).toBe(2 * i);
            expect(arrow.name).toBe("multiply");
            expect(arrow.length).toBe(2);
            expect(arrow.prototype).toBeUndefined();

            const named = makeNamed(i);
            expect(named()).toBe(i);
            expect(named.name).toBe("inner");
            expect(named.length).toBe(3);
            expect(named.toString()).toBe("function inner(a, b, c) {\n                return i;\n            }");
            named.extra = i;
            expect(named.extra).toBe(i);
            expect(new named()).toBeInstanceOf(named);
        }
    });

    test("closures over mutable bindings, and collections", () => {
        function counter() {
            let count = 0;
            const increment = () => ++count;
            const read = function () {
                return count;
            };
            gc();
            return [increment, read];
        }
        function curry(fun) {
            return function (a) {
                return function (b) {
                    return fun(a, b);
                };
            };
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const [increment, read] = counter();
            increment();
            increment();
            expect(read()).toBe(2);
            expect(curry((a, b) => a - b)(i)(1)).toBe(i - 1);
        }
    });

    test("methods with home objects", () => {
        const base = {
            greet() {
                return "base";
            },
        };
        function make(i) {
            const object = {
                greet() {
                    return super.greet() + i;
                },
            };
            Object.setPrototypeOf(object, base);
            return object;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(make(i).greet()).toBe("base" + i);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/code-flushing.js
// The JIT code of a function that did not run for a while is flushed, and the function runs in the interpreter until
// it gets hot again. flushCode("jit") flushes the JIT code of every function no frame runs, whatever its age.

// NB: The functions the tests declare keep their shared data across the harness's repeated runs of a test, so that each
//     run would add recompiles, which stop the flushes of a function after six. So the body runs once.
function flushingTest(name, body) {
    let ran = false;
    test(name, () => {
        if (ran) return;
        ran = true;
        body();
    });
}

function compileHot(f, warmUp) {
    jit.prepare(f);
    warmUp();
    return jit.compile(f);
}

flushingTest("flushed JIT code compiles again", () => {
    function scale(value) {
        return value * 3 + 1;
    }
    const warmUp = () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) expect(scale(i)).toBe(i * 3 + 1);
    };
    expect(compileHot(scale, warmUp)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(jit.isCompiled(scale)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    flushCode("jit");
    expect(jit.isCompiled(scale)).toBeFalse();
    expect(scale(5)).toBe(16);
    expect(compileHot(scale, warmUp)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(scale(7)).toBe(22);
});

flushingTest("callers of flushed JIT code keep working", () => {
    function callee(value) {
        let result = value;
        for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) result = result * 2 + 1;
        return result;
    }
    function caller(value) {
        return callee(value) + callee(value + 1);
    }
    const warmUp = () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) expect(caller(i)).toBe(16 * i + 22);
    };
    expect(compileHot(callee, warmUp)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(compileHot(caller, warmUp)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    flushCode("jit");
    expect(jit.isCompiled(callee)).toBeFalse();
    expect(jit.isCompiled(caller)).toBeFalse();
    expect(caller(2)).toBe(54);
    expect(compileHot(caller, warmUp)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(caller(3)).toBe(70);
});

flushingTest("running functions keep their JIT code", () => {
    function running(flush) {
        if (flush) flushCode("jit");
        return jit.isCompiled(running);
    }
    jit.prepare(running);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) running(false);
    expect(jit.compile(running)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    // NB: Forced exits can discard the code of the running function on their own.
    const compiled = running(true);
    if (!jit.forcesExits) expect(compiled).toBe(jit.enabled);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/constant-methods.js
// JIT code loads methods from prototypes as the constants they were at
// compile time.
// These tests run every function many times, so that with a low JIT
// threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

describe("methods as constants in JIT code", () => {
    test("methods replaced on the prototype are called", () => {
        class Model {
            value() {
                return 1;
            }
            twice() {
                return this.value() + this.value();
            }
        }
        const model = new Model();
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(model.twice()).toBe(2);
        Model.prototype.value = function () {
            return 5;
        };
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(model.twice()).toBe(10);
        Model.prototype.value = 7;
        expect(() => model.twice()).toThrow(TypeError);
    });

    test("methods replaced while they run", () => {
        class Counter {
            step() {
                if (this.count === 50) {
                    Counter.prototype.step = function () {
                        return 100;
                    };
                }
                ++this.count;
                return 1;
            }
            run() {
                return this.step() + this.step();
            }
        }
        const counter = new Counter();
        counter.count = 0;
        let sum = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) sum += counter.run();
        expect(sum).toBe(51 + 100 * (2 * iterations - 51));
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/control-flow-and-state.js
// Exceptions, loops, closures and globals in compiled code, warmed up with one kind of input and then given others
// that make it exit, throw or take other paths. The compiled code must do what the interpreter does (see
// compareCompiledWithInterpreter in test-common.js).

const values = {
    int32: (log, i) => i,
    double: () => 2.5,
    string: () => "7",
    object: log => ({
        valueOf() {
            log.push("valueOf");
            return 3;
        },
    }),
    throwing: () => ({
        valueOf() {
            throw new SyntaxError("valueOf threw");
        },
    }),
    undefined: () => undefined,
    null: () => null,
    bigint: () => 3n,
    "negative zero": () => -0,
    large: () => 2147483647,
    small: () => -2147483648,
};

const probes = {};
for (const [name, make] of Object.entries(values)) probes[name] = (log, i) => [make(log, i), log];

const warmUp = (log, i) => [i % 10, log];

function check(factory) {
    expect(compareCompiledWithInterpreter(factory, { warmUp, probes })).toEqual([]);
}

describe("exceptions", () => {
    test("throw and catch in the same function", () =>
        check(() => (value, log) => {
            try {
                if (value > 5) throw new Error(`big ${value}`);
                return value * 2;
            } catch (e) {
                log.push(e.message);
                return -1;
            }
        }));

    test("finally overriding the return value", () =>
        check(() => (value, log) => {
            try {
                return value + 1;
            } finally {
                log.push("finally");
                if (value === 3) return "overridden";
            }
        }));

    test("rethrow from catch", () =>
        check(() => (value, log) => {
            try {
                try {
                    return value * value;
                } catch (e) {
                    log.push("inner catch");
                    throw new TypeError(`rethrown ${e.message}`);
                }
            } catch (e) {
                return `outer caught ${e}`;
            }
        }));

    test("loop with try inside", () =>
        check(() => (value, log) => {
            let total = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < 5; ++i) {
                try {
                    total += value * i;
                    if (i === 3) throw i;
                } catch (e) {
                    total -= e;
                }
            }
            return total;
        }));

    test("exception from a native called in a loop", () =>
        check(() => (value, log) => {
            const results = [];
            for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
                try {
                    results.push(BigInt(value) + BigInt(i));
                } catch (e) {
                    results.push(e.constructor.name);
                }
            }
            return results;
        }));
});

describe("loops", () => {
    test("int32 counter with an overflowing sum", () =>
        check(() => value => {
            let sum = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) sum += value * 1000000;
            return sum;
        }));

    test("loop whose phi changes type", () =>
        check(() => value => {
            let x = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < 6; ++i) x = i === 3 ? value : x + 1;
            return x;
        }));

    test("nested loops with breaks and continues", () =>
        check(() => value => {
            let count = 0;
            outer: for (let i = 0; i < 5; ++i) {
                for (let j = 0; j < 5; ++j) {
                    if (j === value) continue outer;
                    if (i * j > 8) break outer;
                    count += i ^ j;
                }
            }
            return count;
        }));

    test("for-in over a changing object", () =>
        check(() => (value, log) => {
            const object = { a: 1, b: 2, c: value };
            const keys = [];
            for (const key in object) {
                keys.push(key);
                if (key === "a") delete object.b;
                if (key === "c") object.d = 4;
            }
            return keys;
        }));

    test("for-of over arrays and strings", () =>
        check(() => value => {
            const seen = [];
            for (const element of [value, value + 1]) seen.push(element);
            for (const character of `${value}`) seen.push(character);
            return seen;
        }));

    test("do-while counting down", () =>
        check(() => value => {
            let n = typeof value === "number" && value === value && Math.abs(value) < 100 ? value : 3;
            let steps = 0;
            do {
                n = n - 1;
                ++steps;
            } while (n > 0 && steps < 200);
            return [n, steps];
        }));
});

describe("closures and environments", () => {
    test("closure created in the compiled function", () =>
        check(() => value => {
            const add = x => x + value;
            return [add(1), add(value)];
        }));

    test("closures in a loop capture their own binding", () =>
        check(() => value => {
            const functions = [];
            for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) functions.push(() => i + value);
            return functions.map(f => f());
        }));

    test("callee changes the caller's variable", () =>
        check(() => {
            let shared = 0;
            const bump = amount => {
                shared += amount;
            };
            return value => {
                shared = value;
                bump(1);
                return shared;
            };
        }));

    test("arguments object and named parameter alias", () =>
        check(
            () =>
                function (value) {
                    arguments[0] = "replaced";
                    return [value, arguments.length];
                }
        ));

    test("eval sees the locals", () =>
        check(() => value => {
            const local = value;
            return eval("local");
        }));
});

describe("globals", () => {
    test("global variable changing type", () =>
        check(() => value => {
            globalThis.jitTestGlobal = value;
            return globalThis.jitTestGlobal;
        }));

    test("global function replaced", () =>
        check(() => (value, log) => {
            const saved = globalThis.parseInt;
            if (value === 7 || value === "7") globalThis.parseInt = () => "replaced";
            try {
                return parseInt("12", 10);
            } finally {
                globalThis.parseInt = saved;
            }
        }));
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/data-property-loads.js
// JIT code loads and stores properties that the checked shape marks writable
// without checking for an accessor, as accessor properties are never
// writable. Properties the shape does not mark writable are still checked.
// These tests run every function many times, so that with a low JIT
// threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

describe("loads and stores of data properties", () => {
    test("accessors with the shape of a read-only data property", () => {
        // NB: Either shape may be the first the property lookup cache lists.
        function loadWritableFirst(object) {
            return object.x;
        }
        function loadReadOnlyFirst(object) {
            return object.x;
        }
        const writable = { x: 1 };
        const readOnly = Object.defineProperty({}, "x", { value: 2, enumerable: true, configurable: true });
        loadWritableFirst(readOnly);
        loadReadOnlyFirst(writable);
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            for (const load of [loadWritableFirst, loadReadOnlyFirst]) {
                expect(load(writable)).toBe(1);
                expect(load(readOnly)).toBe(2);
            }
        }
        const accessor = Object.defineProperty({}, "x", {
            get() {
                return 3;
            },
            enumerable: true,
            configurable: true,
        });
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(loadWritableFirst(accessor)).toBe(3);
            expect(loadReadOnlyFirst(accessor)).toBe(3);
        }
    });

    test("properties redefined as accessors", () => {
        function load(object) {
            return object.x;
        }
        function store(object, value) {
            object.x = value;
        }
        const object = { x: 1 };
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            store(object, i);
            expect(load(object)).toBe(i);
        }
        let stored;
        Object.defineProperty(object, "x", {
            get() {
                return "getter";
            },
            set(value) {
                stored = value;
            },
        });
        store(object, "value");
        expect(stored).toBe("value");
        expect(load(object)).toBe("getter");
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/dense-dictionary-arrays.js
function filledTexture() {
    const values = new Array(16 * 16 * 3 * 16);
    for (let i = 768; i < values.length; ++i) values[i] = i;
    return values;
}

test("mostly filled dictionary arrays preserve holes and promote to holey storage", () => {
    const values = filledTexture();
    expect(values.length).toBe(12288);
    expect(0 in values).toBeFalse();
    expect(767 in values).toBeFalse();
    expect(values[767]).toBeUndefined();
    expect(values[768]).toBe(768);
    expect(values[12287]).toBe(12287);
    expect(Object.keys(values).length).toBe(11520);
    if (jit.enabled) {
        const read = new Function("values", "index", "return values[index];");
        jit.prepare(read);
        read(values, 1000);
        expect(jit.feedback(read).includes("elements=Holey")).toBeTrue();
        jit.compile(read);
        expect(read(values, 12287)).toBe(12287);
        expect(read(values, 0)).toBeUndefined();
        const prototype = Object.create(Array.prototype);
        prototype[0] = 42;
        Object.setPrototypeOf(values, prototype);
        expect(read(values, 0)).toBe(42);
        delete values[1000];
        expect(read(values, 1000)).toBeUndefined();
    }
});

test("dictionary promotion retains indexed attributes and accessors", () => {
    const values = new Array(1024);
    let calls = 0;
    Object.defineProperty(values, 768, {
        get() {
            ++calls;
            return 7;
        },
        enumerable: true,
        configurable: true,
    });
    Object.defineProperty(values, 769, { value: 9, writable: false, enumerable: false, configurable: false });
    for (let i = 770; i < 1024; ++i) values[i] = i;
    for (let i = 0; i < 768; ++i) values[i] = i;
    expect(values[768]).toBe(7);
    expect(calls).toBe(1);
    expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(values, "769")).toEqual({
        value: 9,
        writable: false,
        enumerable: false,
        configurable: false,
    });
    values[769] = 100;
    expect(values[769]).toBe(9);
    expect(Object.keys(values)).not.toContain("769");
});

test("dense promotion preserves shrinking, growing, and sparse lengths", () => {
    const values = filledTexture();
    values.length = 800;
    expect(values[799]).toBe(799);
    expect(values[800]).toBeUndefined();
    expect(0 in values).toBeFalse();
    values.length = 12288;
    expect(800 in values).toBeFalse();
    values[1000] = 42;
    expect(values[1000]).toBe(42);
    expect(999 in values).toBeFalse();
    const sparse = new Array(0xffffffff);
    sparse[1000] = 7;
    expect(sparse.length).toBe(0xffffffff);
    expect(sparse[1000]).toBe(7);
    expect(999 in sparse).toBeFalse();
    expect(Object.keys(sparse)).toEqual(["1000"]);
});

test("dictionary arrays that start above the density threshold keep their elements", () => {
    const values = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 1024; ++i) values[i] = i;
    // NB: A read-only element makes the elements a dictionary, which is
    //     already denser than the promotion threshold.
    Object.defineProperty(values, 900, { value: 900, writable: false, enumerable: true, configurable: true });
    delete values[900];
    delete values[901];
    values[1100] = 1100;
    expect(values.length).toBe(1101);
    expect(900 in values).toBeFalse();
    expect(901 in values).toBeFalse();
    expect(1024 in values).toBeFalse();
    expect(values[899]).toBe(899);
    expect(values[1023]).toBe(1023);
    expect(values[1100]).toBe(1100);
    expect(Object.keys(values).length).toBe(1023);
    values[900] = 900;
    values[901] = 901;
    for (let i = 1024; i < 1100; ++i) values[i] = i;
    expect(Object.keys(values).length).toBe(1101);
    expect(values.every((value, index) => value === index)).toBeTrue();
    const read = new Function("values", "index", "return values[index];");
    jit.prepare(read);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) read(values, i);
    jit.compile(read);
    expect(read(values, 901)).toBe(901);
    expect(read(values, 1100)).toBe(1100);
    expect(read(values, 1101)).toBeUndefined();
});

function elementsKindSeen(values, index) {
    const read = new Function("values", "index", "return values[index];");
    jit.prepare(read);
    read(values, index);
    return jit.feedback(read);
}

test("sparse stores past elements that stay dense enough keep them dense", () => {
    const packed = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 1024; ++i) packed[i] = i;
    packed[1300] = 1300;
    const holey = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 1024; ++i) if (i % 16) holey[i] = i;
    holey[1250] = 1250;
    for (const [values, last, count] of [
        [packed, 1300, 1025],
        [holey, 1250, 961],
    ]) {
        expect(values.length).toBe(last + 1);
        expect(1024 in values).toBeFalse();
        expect(values[last - 1]).toBeUndefined();
        expect(values[last]).toBe(last);
        expect(Object.keys(values).length).toBe(count);
        values[1024] = 1024;
        expect(values[1024]).toBe(1024);
        if (jit.enabled) expect(elementsKindSeen(values, 1000).includes("elements=Holey")).toBeTrue();
    }

    // Stores that would leave the elements sparse make them a dictionary.
    const sparse = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 1024; ++i) sparse[i] = i;
    sparse[1400] = 1400;
    expect(sparse[1400]).toBe(1400);
    expect(Object.keys(sparse).length).toBe(1025);
    if (jit.enabled) expect(elementsKindSeen(sparse, 1000).includes("elements=Other")).toBeTrue();
});

test("repeated sparse stores past holey elements that stay dense keep them dense", () => {
    // NB: Each store lands past the elements' storage, and the gaps fill in
    //     but for one hole, so the elements stay dense. Counting the holes at
    //     every such store would take quadratic time.
    const values = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 1024; ++i) if (i % 16) values[i] = i;
    for (let k = 0; k < 10000; ++k) {
        const start = values.length;
        values[start + 201] = start + 201;
        for (let i = start + 1; i < start + 201; ++i) values[i] = i;
    }
    expect(values.length).toBe(1024 + 10000 * 202);
    expect(0 in values).toBeFalse();
    expect(1024 in values).toBeFalse();
    expect(values[1025]).toBe(1025);
    expect(values[values.length - 1]).toBe(values.length - 1);
    if (jit.enabled) expect(elementsKindSeen(values, 1025).includes("elements=Holey")).toBeTrue();
});

test("stores that each leave few holes but make holey elements sparse make them a dictionary", () => {
    const keys = [50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900, 950];
    const palette = {};
    for (const key of keys) palette[key] = `#${key}`;
    expect(Object.keys(palette)).toEqual(keys.map(String));
    for (const key of keys) expect(palette[key]).toBe(`#${key}`);
    expect(0 in palette).toBeFalse();
    expect(150 in palette).toBeFalse();
    if (jit.enabled) expect(elementsKindSeen(palette, 950).includes("elements=Other")).toBeTrue();

    // Holey elements with few holes, or with many holes but at least an eighth filled, stay dense as they grow.
    const values = [];
    for (let i = 1; i < 1000; ++i) values[i] = i;
    const strided = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 2000; i += 2) strided[i] = i;
    const queue = [];
    let head = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) {
        queue.push(i);
        if (i % 2) delete queue[head++];
    }
    for (const [elements, hole, last] of [
        [values, 0, 999],
        [strided, 1, 1998],
        [queue, 0, 1999],
    ]) {
        expect(hole in elements).toBeFalse();
        expect(elements[last]).toBe(last);
        if (jit.enabled) expect(elementsKindSeen(elements, last).includes("elements=Holey")).toBeTrue();
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/direct-calls.js
// JIT code calls the single callee a call site saw directly when it does not
// inline it. These tests run every caller and callee many times, so that with
// a low JIT threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

describe("direct calls from JIT code", () => {
    test("arguments, missing arguments and return values", () => {
        function callee(a, b, c) {
            if (a < 0) return;
            return [a, b, c, arguments.length];
        }
        function caller(i) {
            return [callee(i), callee(i, 1, 2, 3), callee(-1, 2)];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(caller(i)).toEqual([[i, undefined, undefined, 1], [i, 1, 2, 4], undefined]);
        }
    });

    test("this values of sloppy and strict callees", () => {
        function sloppy() {
            return this;
        }
        function strict() {
            "use strict";
            return this;
        }
        const object = { sloppy, strict };
        function caller(value) {
            return [sloppy(), strict(), object.sloppy(), object.strict(), sloppy.call(value), strict.call(value)];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const [sloppyThis, strictThis, sloppyMethodThis, strictMethodThis, boxedThis, primitiveThis] = caller(i);
            expect(sloppyThis).toBe(globalThis);
            expect(strictThis).toBeUndefined();
            expect(sloppyMethodThis).toBe(object);
            expect(strictMethodThis).toBe(object);
            expect(boxedThis).toBeInstanceOf(Number);
            expect(primitiveThis).toBe(i);
        }
    });

    test("exceptions thrown by callees reach the caller's handler", () => {
        function thrower(value) {
            if (value % 3 === 0) throw new Error(`thrown ${value}`);
            return value;
        }
        function caller(value) {
            try {
                return thrower(value) + 1;
            } catch (error) {
                return error.message;
            }
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller(i)).toBe(i % 3 === 0 ? `thrown ${i}` : i + 1);
    });

    test("deep recursion works and running out of stack throws", () => {
        function depth(n) {
            if (n === 0) return 0;
            return 1 + depth(n - 1);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(depth(i)).toBe(i);
        expect(depth(3000)).toBe(3000);
        expect(() => depth(1e7)).toThrow();
        expect(depth(10)).toBe(10);
    });

    test("callees that change behavior or start throwing late", () => {
        function callee(value) {
            if (value > iterations) return value * 2;
            return value;
        }
        function caller(value) {
            return callee(value) + 1;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller(i)).toBe(i + 1);
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const value = iterations + 1 + i;
            expect(caller(value)).toBe(value * 2 + 1);
        }
    });

    test("call sites that see other callees later", () => {
        function first(value) {
            return value + 1;
        }
        function second(value) {
            return value + 2;
        }
        function caller(f, value) {
            return f(value);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller(first, i)).toBe(i + 1);
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller(second, i)).toBe(i + 2);
        expect(caller(Math.abs, -5)).toBe(5);
        expect(caller(first.bind(null, 10), 0)).toBe(11);
    });

    test("stack traces show directly called frames", () => {
        function inner() {
            return new Error().stack;
        }
        function middle() {
            return inner();
        }
        function outer() {
            return middle();
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const names = outer()
                .split("\n")
                .slice(1)
                .map(line => line.trim().split(" ")[1]);
            expect(names.indexOf("inner")).toBeLessThan(names.indexOf("middle"));
            expect(names.indexOf("middle")).toBeLessThan(names.indexOf("outer"));
        }
    });

    test("call sites that see callees only the generic call can call later", () => {
        function target(value) {
            // NB: Too large to inline.
            let x = value;
            x = x + 1 - 1;
            x = x + 2 - 2;
            x = x + 3 - 3;
            x = x + 4 - 4;
            x = x + 5 - 5;
            x = x + 6 - 6;
            x = x + 7 - 7;
            x = x + 8 - 8;
            x = x + 9 - 9;
            x = x + 10 - 10;
            x = x + 11 - 11;
            x = x + 12 - 12;
            x = x + 13 - 13;
            x = x + 14 - 14;
            x = x + 15 - 15;
            x = x + 16 - 16;
            return x + 1;
        }
        function caller(f, value) {
            return f(value, value);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller(target, i)).toBe(i + 1);
        // NB: The generic call reads the call's operands from the frame.
        const proxy = new Proxy(function (value) {
            return value * 2;
        }, {});
        expect(caller(proxy, 3)).toBe(6);
        expect(() => caller(5, 5)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "5 is not a function");
    });

    test("closures of one function, each with its own environment", () => {
        function makeCounter(start) {
            let count = start;
            return function (step) {
                count += step;
                return [this === undefined ? "undefined" : typeof this, count];
            };
        }
        function call(counter, step) {
            return counter(step);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const counter = makeCounter(i * 100);
            expect(call(counter, 1)).toEqual(["object", i * 100 + 1]);
            expect(call(counter, 2)).toEqual(["object", i * 100 + 3]);
        }
        expect(call(x => x * 2, 21)).toBe(42);
        expect(() => call(makeCounter(0).bind(null), Symbol())).toThrow(TypeError);
    });

    test("recursive named function expressions made for each call", () => {
        function sumTree(tree) {
            let sum = 0;
            (function walk(node) {
                sum += node.value;
                for (const child of node.children) walk(child);
            })(tree);
            return sum;
        }
        const leaf = value => ({ value, children: [] });
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const tree = { value: i, children: [leaf(1), { value: 2, children: [leaf(3), leaf(4)] }] };
            expect(sumTree(tree)).toBe(i + 10);
        }
        expect(() => sumTree({ value: 1, children: [null] })).toThrow(TypeError);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/discarded-code.js
// JIT code that keeps exiting is discarded, and its executable compiled
// again once no frame that may run the old code is live anymore. These tests
// discard code while frames of it run below, through recursion and through
// direct calls.

const iterations = 200;

describe("discarded JIT code", () => {
    test("recursive frames of discarded code keep running", () => {
        function recurse(value, depth) {
            if (depth > 0) return recurse(value, depth - 1) + 1;
            // NB: Changing types make the code exit until it is discarded.
            return typeof value === "number" ? value * 2 : value + "!";
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(recurse(i, 5)).toBe(i * 2 + 5);
            if (i % 3 === 0) expect(recurse(`${i}`, 3)).toBe(`${i}!111`);
        }
    });

    test("directly called callees whose code is discarded while their callers run", () => {
        function callee(value) {
            let result = value;
            for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) result = typeof result === "number" ? result + 1 : result + "?";
            return result;
        }
        function caller(value, depth) {
            if (depth > 0) return caller(value, depth - 1);
            return callee(value);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(caller(i, 2)).toBe(i + 3);
            if (i % 4 === 0) expect(caller({ toString: () => "o" }, 2)).toBe("o???");
        }
    });

    test("loops continue in code installed or exited while they run", () => {
        let total = 0;
        function add(value) {
            total += value;
            // NB: A path the code has not seen makes it exit, inlined or not.
            if (value > 1000) return "big";
            return total & 7;
        }
        function loop(count) {
            let seen = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
                const result = add(i);
                if (result === "big") ++seen;
            }
            return seen;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i) add(1);
        expect(loop(1000)).toBe(0);
        expect(loop(5000)).toBe(3999);
        expect(total).toBe(20 + 499500 + 12497500);
    });
});

describe("recompiles after discarded code", () => {
    test("code that exits where it reaches code that never ran is compiled again", () => {
        // NB: Like the per-frame step of an emulator, which reaches new branches as the program it runs goes on.
        const cases = Array.from(
            { length: 16 },
            (_, phase) => `case ${phase}: x = (x ^ ${phase}) + ${phase} | 0; break;`
        );
        // NB: A debugger statement keeps the function from being inlined, where its exits would teach it the cases
        //     before its own code reaches them.
        const step = new Function("phase", "x", `debugger; switch (phase) { ${cases.join(" ")} } return x;`);
        jit.prepare(step);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) step(0, i);
        expect(jit.compile(step)).toBe(jit.enabled);
        for (let phase = 1; phase < 16; ++phase) {
            for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i) expect(step(phase, i)).toBe(((i ^ phase) + phase) | 0);
            expect(jit.compile(step)).toBe(jit.enabled);
        }
        // NB: Exits forced at random checks may come before the ones at sites that never ran, which then go unrecorded.
        if (!jit.forcesExits) expect(jit.discardCount(step)).toBe(jit.enabled ? 15 : 0);
    });

    test("code that keeps learning is not compiled anymore after many discards", () => {
        const cases = Array.from(
            { length: 80 },
            (_, phase) => `case ${phase}: x = (x ^ ${phase}) + ${phase} | 0; break;`
        );
        const step = new Function("phase", "x", `switch (phase) { ${cases.join(" ")} } return x;`);
        jit.prepare(step);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) step(0, i);
        for (let phase = 0; phase < 80; ++phase) {
            for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i) expect(step(phase, i)).toBe(((i ^ phase) + phase) | 0);
            jit.compile(step);
        }
        if (jit.enabled && !jit.forcesExits) {
            expect(jit.discardCount(step)).toBe(64);
            expect(jit.compile(step)).toBeFalse();
        }
        expect(step(79, 1)).toBe(((1 ^ 79) + 79) | 0);
    });

    test("discards that teach the code something start the count of fruitless discards over", () => {
        const step = new Function(
            "phase",
            "x",
            "switch (phase) { case 0: return x + 1 | 0; case 1: return x ^ 3; } return x;"
        );
        // NB: Exits forced at random checks may come before the one where the code reaches the case that never ran,
        //     which then goes unrecorded and teaches the recompiles nothing.
        const expectCompiled = compiled => {
            if (!jit.forcesExits) expect(compiled).toBe(jit.enabled);
        };
        jit.prepare(step);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) step(0, i);
        for (let i = 0; i < 7; ++i) {
            expectCompiled(jit.compile(step));
            jit.discard(step);
        }
        // The code exits where it reaches the case that never ran, which a recompile learns from.
        expectCompiled(jit.compile(step));
        for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i) expect(step(1, i)).toBe(i ^ 3);
        for (let i = 0; i < 7; ++i) {
            expectCompiled(jit.compile(step));
            jit.discard(step);
        }
        expectCompiled(jit.compile(step));
    });

    test("code discarded again and again without new exits is not compiled anymore", () => {
        const add = new Function("a", "b", "return a + b;");
        jit.prepare(add);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) add(i, 1);
        for (let i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
            expect(jit.compile(add)).toBe(jit.enabled);
            jit.discard(add);
        }
        expect(jit.compile(add)).toBeFalse();
        expect(add(2, 3)).toBe(5);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/element-access-with-kind-changes.js
// Indexed gets and puts, compiled after warming up with packed arrays of int32 values and in-bounds indices, then given
// every other kind of object and index: holes, out-of-bounds and negative indices, doubles, strings, every typed
// array kind, detached buffers, frozen arrays, arrays with accessors, proxies and array-likes. The compiled code must
// do what the interpreter does (see compareCompiledWithInterpreter in test-common.js).

const objects = {
    packed: (log, i) => [i, 1, 2, 3],
    "packed doubles": (log, i) => [i + 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5],
    "packed mixed": (log, i) => [i, "one", { two: 2 }, null],
    holey: (log, i) => [i, , 2, , 4],
    "holey with prototype element": (log, i) => {
        const array = [i, , 2, , 4];
        Object.setPrototypeOf(array, Object.assign(Object.create(Array.prototype), { 1: "from prototype" }));
        return array;
    },
    "with getter element": (log, i) =>
        Object.defineProperty([i, 1, 2, 3], 1, {
            get() {
                log.push("element getter");
                return "got";
            },
            set(value) {
                log.push(`element setter ${value}`);
            },
        }),
    frozen: (log, i) => Object.freeze([i, 1, 2, 3]),
    "non-extensible": (log, i) => Object.preventExtensions([i, 1]),
    empty: () => [],
    long: (log, i) => new Array(100).fill(i),
    "length changed": (log, i) => {
        const array = [i, 1, 2, 3];
        array.length = 1;
        return array;
    },
    sparse: (log, i) => {
        const array = [];
        array[1000] = i;
        return array;
    },
    Int8Array: (log, i) => new Int8Array([i, 127, -128, 3]),
    Uint8Array: (log, i) => new Uint8Array([i, 255, 0, 3]),
    Uint8ClampedArray: (log, i) => new Uint8ClampedArray([i, 255, 0, 3]),
    Int16Array: (log, i) => new Int16Array([i, -32768, 32767, 3]),
    Uint16Array: (log, i) => new Uint16Array([i, 65535, 0, 3]),
    Int32Array: (log, i) => new Int32Array([i, -2147483648, 2147483647, 3]),
    Uint32Array: (log, i) => new Uint32Array([i, 4294967295, 2147483648, 3]),
    Float16Array: (log, i) => new Float16Array([i, 0.5, -0, 3]),
    Float32Array: (log, i) => new Float32Array([i, 0.1, NaN, -0]),
    Float64Array: (log, i) => new Float64Array([i, 0.1, NaN, -0]),
    BigInt64Array: (log, i) => new BigInt64Array([BigInt(i), -1n, 2n, 3n]),
    BigUint64Array: (log, i) => new BigUint64Array([BigInt(i), 1n, 2n, 3n]),
    "detached typed array": () => {
        const array = new Int32Array(4);
        detachArrayBuffer(array.buffer);
        return array;
    },
    "resizable typed array": (log, i) => {
        const buffer = new ArrayBuffer(16, { maxByteLength: 64 });
        const array = new Int32Array(buffer);
        array[0] = i;
        buffer.resize(8);
        return array;
    },
    "typed array subarray": (log, i) => new Int32Array([9, i, 1, 2, 3]).subarray(1),
    proxy: (log, i) =>
        new Proxy([i, 1, 2, 3], {
            get(target, key, receiver) {
                log.push(`proxy get ${String(key)}`);
                return Reflect.get(target, key, receiver);
            },
            set(target, key, value, receiver) {
                log.push(`proxy set ${String(key)}`);
                return Reflect.set(target, key, value, receiver);
            },
        }),
    "array-like": (log, i) => ({ 0: i, 1: 1, length: 2 }),
    arguments: (log, i) =>
        (function () {
            return arguments;
        })(i, 1, 2, 3),
    string: (log, i) => `s${i}xyz`,
    "string object": (log, i) => new String(`s${i}`),
    null: () => null,
    undefined: () => undefined,
    number: () => 42,
};

const indices = {
    "in bounds": (log, i) => i % 4,
    first: () => 0,
    "out of bounds": () => 10,
    "far out of bounds": () => 1e9,
    negative: () => -1,
    "negative zero": () => -0,
    double: () => 1.5,
    "integral double": () => 2.0,
    NaN: () => NaN,
    "numeric string": () => "2",
    "non-numeric string": () => "length",
    "array index string": () => "4294967294",
    symbol: () => Symbol.iterator,
    object: log => ({
        toString() {
            log.push("index toString");
            return "1";
        },
    }),
    "throwing object": () => ({
        toString() {
            throw new TypeError("index toString threw");
        },
    }),
    undefined: () => undefined,
    "max int32": () => 2147483647,
    "min int32": () => -2147483648,
};

const warmUp = (log, i) => [[i, 1, 2, 3], i % 4, log, i];

const probes = {};
for (const [name, make] of Object.entries(objects))
    probes[`object: ${name}`] = (log, i) => [make(log, i), i % 4, log, i];
for (const [name, make] of Object.entries(indices))
    probes[`index: ${name}`] = (log, i) => [[i, 1, 2, 3], make(log, i), log, i];
for (const [objectName, makeObject] of Object.entries(objects)) {
    for (const indexName of ["out of bounds", "negative", "double", "numeric string"])
        probes[`object: ${objectName}, index: ${indexName}`] = (log, i) => [
            makeObject(log, i),
            indices[indexName](log, i),
            log,
            i,
        ];
}

describe("indexed gets", () => {
    const forms = {
        get: () => (object, index) => object[index],
        "get with a constant index": () => object => object[1],
        "sum in a loop": () => object => {
            let sum = 0;
            for (let k = 0; k < 4; ++k) sum = sum + object[k];
            return sum;
        },
        "get, then length": () => (object, index) => [object[index], object.length],
        "nested get": () => (object, index) => object[object[index] % 4],
        in: () => (object, index) =>
            typeof object === "object" && object !== null && typeof index !== "symbol" ? index in object : "skip",
    };
    for (const [name, factory] of Object.entries(forms)) {
        test(name, () => {
            expect(compareCompiledWithInterpreter(factory, { warmUp, probes })).toEqual([]);
        });
    }
});

describe("indexed puts", () => {
    const forms = {
        put: () => (object, index, log, i) => {
            object[index] = i;
            return [object[index], object.length];
        },
        "put of a double": () => (object, index, log, i) => {
            object[index] = i + 0.25;
            return object[index];
        },
        "put of an object": () => (object, index) => {
            object[index] = { boxed: index };
            return object[index];
        },
        append: () => (object, index, log, i) => {
            if (object === null || object === undefined) return "nullish";
            object[object.length] = i;
            return object.length;
        },
        push: () => (object, index, log, i) => {
            if (!Array.isArray(object)) return "not an array";
            return object.push(i);
        },
        increment: () => (object, index) => {
            object[index]++;
            return object[index];
        },
        "strict put": () => (object, index, log, i) => {
            "use strict";
            object[index] = i;
            return object[index];
        },
        "fill loop": () => (object, index, log, i) => {
            for (let k = 0; k < 4; ++k) object[k] = k * i;
            return object;
        },
    };
    for (const [name, factory] of Object.entries(forms)) {
        test(name, () => {
            expect(compareCompiledWithInterpreter(factory, { warmUp, probes })).toEqual([]);
        });
    }
});

describe("typed arrays warmed up by kind", () => {
    const kinds = [
        "Int8Array",
        "Uint8Array",
        "Uint8ClampedArray",
        "Int16Array",
        "Uint16Array",
        "Int32Array",
        "Uint32Array",
        "Float16Array",
        "Float32Array",
        "Float64Array",
    ];
    for (const kind of kinds) {
        test(kind, () => {
            const values = [0, 1, -1, 255, 256, -129, 65536, 2147483648, 4294967296, 0.5, -0.5, 1.5, NaN, -0, Infinity];
            const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
                () => (array, index, value) => {
                    array[index] = value;
                    return [array[index], array[index + 1]];
                },
                {
                    warmUp: (log, i) => [new globalThis[kind](4), i % 3, i],
                    probes: Object.fromEntries(
                        values.map(value => [
                            `store ${describeForComparison(value)}`,
                            () => [new globalThis[kind](4), 1, value],
                        ])
                    ),
                }
            );
            expect(failures).toEqual([]);
        });
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/element-load-elimination.js
function compiled(f, ...warmupArguments) {
    jit.prepare(f);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) f(...warmupArguments);
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return f;
}

test("elements read twice give the same value", () => {
    const digits = compiled(new Function("a", "i", "return (a[i] & 0x3fff) + (a[i] >> 14);"), [1 << 20, 2, 3], 0);
    expect(digits([(5 << 14) | 7, 1], 0)).toBe(12);
    expect(digits([1, (3 << 14) | 2], 1)).toBe(5);
});

test("stores between reads of an element are seen", () => {
