    const update = compiled(
        new Function(
            "a",
            "b",
            "i",
            `const before = a[i];
            b[i] = before + 10;
            return before * 100 + a[i];`
        ),
        [1, 2],
        [3, 4],
        0
    );
    expect(update([1, 2], [3, 4], 1)).toBe(202);
    const shared = [5, 6];
    expect(update(shared, shared, 0)).toBe(515);
    expect(shared).toEqual([15, 6]);
});

test("stores through typed arrays sharing a buffer are seen", () => {
    const read = compiled(
        new Function(
            "bytes",
            "words",
            `const before = bytes[0];
            words[0] = 0x01020304;
            return before * 1000 + bytes[0];`
        ),
        new Uint8Array(4),
        new Uint32Array(4)
    );
    const buffer = new ArrayBuffer(16);
    const bytes = new Uint8Array(buffer);
    bytes[0] = 7;
    expect(read(bytes, new Uint32Array(buffer))).toBe(7004);
});

test("calls between reads of an element are seen", () => {
    const read = compiled(
        new Function(
            "a",
            "f",
            `const before = a[0];
            f(a);
            return before * 100 + a[0];`
        ),
        [1],
        () => {}
    );
    expect(
        read([2], a => {
            a[0] = 3;
        })
    ).toBe(203);
});

test("holes read twice exit for both reads", () => {
    const read = compiled(new Function("a", "i", "return [a[i], a[i]];"), [1, 2], 0);
    expect(read([1, , 3], 1)).toEqual([undefined, undefined]);
    Array.prototype[1] = "inherited";
    try {
        expect(read([1, , 3], 1)).toEqual(["inherited", "inherited"]);
    } finally {
        delete Array.prototype[1];
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/embedded-cells-gc.js
// JIT code may embed the shapes its property accesses saw. These tests drop
// every object of such a shape, collect garbage and allocate objects with new
// shapes, which must never be mistaken for the old ones.

function makeShapes(count, keys) {
    const objects = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        const object = {};
        for (const key of keys) object[key + i] = i;
        object.a = i;
        objects.push(object);
    }
    return objects;
}

describe("JIT code whose embedded cells lose every other reference", () => {
    test("calling again after a collection", () => {
        function read(object) {
            return object.a;
        }

        let warm = [
            { a: 1, b: 2 },
            { a: 3, b: 4 },
        ];
        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) expect(read(warm[i % 2])).toBe(i % 2 ? 3 : 1);
        warm = null;
        gc();

        const others = makeShapes(200, ["x", "y"]);
        for (let i = 0; i < others.length; ++i) expect(read(others[i])).toBe(i);
    });

    test("a collection while the code runs", () => {
        let warm = { a: 1, b: 2 };
        function readAround(object, callback) {
            const before = object.a;
            const next = callback();
            return before + next.a;
        }

        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) expect(readAround(warm, () => ({ a: 10, b: 20 }))).toBe(11);

        const result = readAround(warm, () => {
            warm = null;
            gc();
            return makeShapes(200, ["p", "q", "r"])[123];
        });
        expect(result).toBe(124);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/entries-and-exits.js
// Frames enter JIT code at function entry and at loop back edges, and leave
// it for the interpreter when a speculation fails, when a slow path does not
// continue in the compiled code, and when an exception is thrown. These tests
// run every function many times, so that with a low JIT threshold they are
// compiled, and then make them take every way out.

const iterations = 100;

describe("entering and leaving JIT code", () => {
    test("speculations that stop holding exit to the interpreter", () => {
        function add(a, b) {
            return a + b;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(add(i, 1)).toBe(i + 1);
        expect(add(0.5, 1)).toBe(1.5);
        expect(add("a", 1)).toBe("a1");
        expect(add(2147483647, 1)).toBe(2147483648);
        expect(add(-0, -0)).toBe(-0);
        expect(add({ valueOf: () => 4 }, 1)).toBe(5);
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(add(i, 0.25)).toBe(i + 0.25);
    });

    test("code that keeps exiting is recompiled with what the exits taught", () => {
        function scale(value, factor) {
            return value * factor;
        }
        for (let round = 0; round < 20; ++round) {
            for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(scale(i, 2)).toBe(2 * i);
            expect(scale(round + 0.5, 2)).toBe(2 * round + 1);
            expect(scale(65536 * 65536, 2)).toBe(2 * 65536 * 65536);
        }
    });

    test("loops continue in JIT code at their back edges", () => {
        function sum(count) {
            let total = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) total += i % 13;
            return total;
        }
        let expected = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 100000; ++i) expected += i % 13;
        expect(sum(100000)).toBe(expected);

        function nested(count) {
            let total = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
                for (let j = 0; j < 10; ++j) total += i ^ j;
            }
            return total;
        }
        let nested_expected = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 10000; ++i) {
            for (let j = 0; j < 10; ++j) nested_expected += i ^ j;
        }
        expect(nested(10000)).toBe(nested_expected);
    });

    test("loops that leave JIT code keep their state", () => {
        function collect(count) {
            const values = [];
            let total = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
                total += i;
                if (i === count - 10) total += 0.5;
                values.push(total);
            }
            return values;
        }
        const values = collect(20000);
        expect(values.length).toBe(20000);
        expect(values[9989]).toBe((9989 * 9990) / 2);
        expect(values[19990]).toBe((19990 * 19991) / 2 + 0.5);
        expect(values[19999]).toBe((19999 * 20000) / 2 + 0.5);
    });

    test("stores that fill the holes of new arrays", () => {
        function fill(count, offset) {
            const values = new Array(count);
            for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) values[i] = i + offset;
            return values;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const values = fill(4, i);
            expect(values).toEqual([i, i + 1, i + 2, i + 3]);
        }
        const sparse = new Array(8);
        sparse[2] = "x";
        expect(fill(8, 0)[7]).toBe(7);
        expect(sparse[1]).toBeUndefined();
    });

    test("loops that left JIT code continue in it again", () => {
        function accumulate(count, odd_every) {
            let total = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
                // NB: A path the loop did not take while it was profiled exits from its code each time it runs.
                if (i % odd_every === odd_every - 1) total += 0.5;
                else total += i & 7;
            }
            return total;
        }
        let expected = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 200000; ++i) expected += i % 50000 === 49999 ? 0.5 : i & 7;
        expect(accumulate(200000, 50000)).toBe(expected);
    });

    test("exceptions are caught in the compiled function", () => {
        function check(value) {
            if (value % 7 === 0) throw new Error(`bad ${value}`);
            return value;
        }
        function guarded(value) {
            try {
                return check(value) * 2;
            } catch (error) {
                return error.message;
            } finally {
                ++guarded.calls;
            }
        }
        guarded.calls = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(guarded(i)).toBe(i % 7 === 0 ? `bad ${i}` : 2 * i);
        expect(guarded.calls).toBe(iterations);
    });

    test("exceptions leave the compiled function for its caller", () => {
        function access(object) {
            return object.property.value;
        }
        function caller(object) {
            try {
                return access(object);
            } catch (error) {
                return error instanceof TypeError;
            }
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller({ property: { value: i } })).toBe(i);
        expect(caller({})).toBeTrue();
        expect(caller(null)).toBeTrue();
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller({ property: { value: i } })).toBe(i);
    });

    test("constructors called from JIT code", () => {
        function Point(x, y) {
            this.x = x;
            this.y = y;
        }
        class Pair {
            constructor(first, second) {
                if (first === undefined) throw new RangeError("no first");
                this.first = first;
                this.second = second;
            }
        }
        function make(i) {
            const point = new Point(i, i + 1);
            const pair = new Pair(point, i);
            return pair.first.x + pair.first.y + pair.second;
        }
        function make_or_fail(i) {
            try {
                return new Pair(i === 13 ? undefined : i, i).first;
            } catch (error) {
                return error.name;
            }
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(make(i)).toBe(3 * i + 1);
            expect(make_or_fail(i)).toBe(i === 13 ? "RangeError" : i);
        }
    });

    test("recursion through JIT code", () => {
        function fibonacci(n) {
            return n < 2 ? n : fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2);
        }
        expect(fibonacci(25)).toBe(75025);

        function depth(n) {
            return n === 0 ? 0 : 1 + depth(n - 1);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(depth(i)).toBe(i);
        expect(() => {
            depth(1e6);
        }).toThrowWithMessage(InternalError, "Call stack size limit exceeded");
        expect(depth(100)).toBe(100);
    });

    test("arguments objects of compiled functions", () => {
        function sloppy(a, b) {
            arguments[0] = a * 2;
            return a + b + arguments.length;
        }
        function strict(a, b) {
            "use strict";
            arguments[0] = a * 2;
            return a + b + arguments.length;
        }
        function rest() {
            return Array.prototype.slice.call(arguments, 1).length;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(sloppy(i, 1)).toBe(2 * i + 3);
            expect(strict(i, 1)).toBe(i + 3);
            expect(sloppy(i, 1, 2)).toBe(2 * i + 4);
            expect(rest(i, i, i)).toBe(2);
        }
        expect(sloppy(0.5, 1)).toBe(4);
        expect(strict("x", 1)).toBe("x12");
    });

    test("generators run in the interpreter", () => {
        function* counter(count) {
            for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) yield i;
        }
        function sum_of(count) {
            let total = 0;
            for (const value of counter(count)) total += value;
            return total;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(sum_of(i)).toBe((i * (i - 1)) / 2 + 0);
    });

    test("closures and environments of compiled functions", () => {
        function make_counter() {
            let count = 0;
            return () => ++count;
        }
        function use(counter, times) {
            let last = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < times; ++i) last = counter();
            return last;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(use(make_counter(), i)).toBe(i);

        function shadowing(value) {
            let result = value;
            {
                let value = result + 1;
                result = () => value;
            }
            return result();
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(shadowing(i)).toBe(i + 1);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/environment-bindings.js
// Bindings at static environment coordinates are read and written in place, and their slow paths run where a binding
// is uninitialized or immutable.

test("reading an uninitialized binding throws", () => {
    function readsEarly(early) {
        const read = () => value;
        if (early) return read();
        let value = 1;
        return read();
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; ++i) expect(readsEarly(false)).toBe(1);
    expect(() => readsEarly(true)).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "value");
});

test("reading the truthiness of an uninitialized binding in a loop throws", () => {
    function makeReader(early) {
        const read = () => {
            let result = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < 2; ++i) result = !value;
            return result;
        };
        if (early) return read;
        let value = undefined;
        return read;
    }
    const initialized = makeReader(false);
    const uninitialized = makeReader(true);
    jit.prepare(initialized);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) expect(initialized()).toBeTrue();
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        jit.discard(initialized);
        const compiled = jit.compile(initialized);
        if (!jit.forcesExits) expect(compiled).toBe(jit.enabled);
        expect(uninitialized).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "value");
        expect(initialized()).toBeTrue();
    }
});

test("reading the truthiness of an uninitialized local in a loop throws", () => {
    function read(clause) {
        let result = 0;
        switch (clause) {
            case 0:
                let value = undefined;
            case 1:
                for (let i = 0; i < 2; ++i) result = !value;
        }
        return result;
    }
    jit.prepare(read);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
        expect(read(0)).toBeTrue();
        expect(read(2)).toBe(0);
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        jit.discard(read);
        const compiled = jit.compile(read);
        if (!jit.forcesExits) expect(compiled).toBe(jit.enabled);
        expect(() => read(1)).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "not initialized");
        expect(read(0)).toBeTrue();
    }
});

test("reading the truthiness of an uninitialized local in a branch of a loop throws", () => {
    function read(clause, choose) {
        let result = 0;
        switch (clause) {
            case 0:
                let value = undefined;
            case 1:
                for (let i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {
                    if (choose) result = !value;
                }
        }
        return result;
    }
    jit.prepare(read);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
        expect(read(0, true)).toBeTrue();
        expect(read(0, false)).toBe(0);
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        jit.discard(read);
        const compiled = jit.compile(read);
        if (!jit.forcesExits) expect(compiled).toBe(jit.enabled);
        expect(() => read(1, true)).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "not initialized");
        expect(read(0, true)).toBeTrue();
    }
});

test("reading the truthiness of a local checked in both branches of a loop throws", () => {
    function read(clause, choose) {
        let result = 0;
        let copy = 0;
        switch (clause) {
            case 0:
                let value = undefined;
            case 1:
                for (let i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {
                    if (choose) copy = value;
                    else copy = value;
                    result = !copy;
                }
        }
        return result;
    }
    jit.prepare(read);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
        expect(read(0, true)).toBeTrue();
        expect(read(0, false)).toBeTrue();
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        jit.discard(read);
        const compiled = jit.compile(read);
        if (!jit.forcesExits) expect(compiled).toBe(jit.enabled);
        expect(() => read(1, true)).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "not initialized");
        expect(read(0, true)).toBeTrue();
    }
});

test("assigning a constant binding throws", () => {
    function assigns(assign) {
        const constant = 1;
        const write = () => {
            if (assign) constant = 2;
            return constant;
        };
        return write();
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; ++i) expect(assigns(false)).toBe(1);
    expect(() => assigns(true)).toThrow(TypeError);
});

test("assigning the name of a function expression does nothing in sloppy code", () => {
    const named = function name(assign) {
        const write = () => {
            if (assign) name = 1;
            return typeof name;
        };
        return write();
    };
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; ++i) expect(named(i % 2 === 0)).toBe("function");
});

test("closures in loops see their own bindings", () => {
    function closures() {
        const functions = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < 5; ++i) functions.push(() => i);
        let sum = 0;
        for (const f of functions) sum = sum * 10 + f();
        return sum;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; ++i) expect(closures()).toBe(1234);
});

test("bindings written in loops are read back", () => {
    function counts() {
        let count = 0;
        const increment = () => ++count;
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) increment();
        return count;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; ++i) expect(counts()).toBe(10);
});

test("bindings incremented several times in a row are read back", () => {
    function steps() {
        let top = 0;
        const advance = () => {
            const start = top;
            top = (top + 8) | 0;
            top = (top + 8) | 0;
            top = (top + 8) | 0;
            return top - start;
        };
        let sum = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) sum += advance();
        return sum + top;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; ++i) expect(steps()).toBe(480);
});

test("assigning an uninitialized binding with a number throws", () => {
    function assignEarly(value) {
        const assign = () => {
            binding = (value + 1) | 0;
        };
        assign();
        let binding = 0;
        return binding;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; ++i)
        expect(() => assignEarly(i)).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "Binding binding is not initialized");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/escape-analysis.js
// JIT code never allocates objects that nothing but their property accesses
// see; exits create them. These tests run every function many times, so that
// with a low JIT threshold they are compiled, and then make them exit while
// such objects are live.

const iterations = 100;

describe("objects replaced by their properties in JIT code", () => {
    test("properties updated in loops and branches", () => {
        function count(n, step) {
            const counter = { total: 0, steps: 0 };
            for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
                if (i % 2) counter.total += step;
                else counter.total += 2 * step;
                counter.steps++;
            }
            return counter.total * 1000 + counter.steps;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(count(5, 1)).toBe(8005);
        expect(count(3, 0.5)).toBe(2503);
        expect(count(2, "x")).toBe(NaN);
    });

    test("exits create the objects, once each, with their current properties", () => {
        function live(a, b, reveal) {
            const point = { x: a, y: b };
            const box = { point, z: 1 };
            const sum = a + b;
            point.y = sum;
            // NB: This call never runs before the function is compiled, so it
            //     is an exit, which needs the objects.
            if (reveal) return reveal(box, point);
            return box.z + point.x + point.y;
        }
        function aliased(a, reveal) {
            const object = { x: a };
            const alias = object;
            const doubled = a * 2;
            if (reveal) return reveal(alias, object, doubled);
            return alias.x + object.x + doubled;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(live(i, 1, null)).toBe(2 * i + 2);
            expect(aliased(i, null)).toBe(4 * i);
        }
        const [box, point] = live(2, 3, (...values) => values);
        expect(box.point).toBe(point);
        expect(point).toEqual({ x: 2, y: 5 });
        expect(Object.keys(box)).toEqual(["point", "z"]);
        expect(box.z).toBe(1);
        const [alias, object, doubled] = aliased(4, (...values) => values);
        expect(alias).toBe(object);
        expect(object.x).toBe(4);
        expect(doubled).toBe(8);
        expect(live("s", 1, null)).toBe("1ss1");
    });

    test("objects that escape stay allocated", () => {
        function make(a) {
            const object = { a };
            const total = a + 1;
            return total > 0 ? object : null;
        }
        const seen = new Set();
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const object = make(i);
            expect(object.a).toBe(i);
            expect(seen.has(object)).toBeFalse();
            seen.add(object);
        }
        expect(make(-5)).toBeNull();
        expect(make(0.5).a).toBe(0.5);
    });

    test("slow paths and calls that leave compiled code create the objects", () => {
        function throwsCaught(a, target) {
            const point = { x: a, y: a + 1 };
            let caught = null;
            try {
                target.missing.property;
            } catch (error) {
                caught = error;
            }
            point.y += 10;
            if (caught) return [point.x, point.y, caught instanceof TypeError];
            return point.x + point.y;
        }
        function callsThrow(a, f) {
            const point = { x: a, y: 2 };
            try {
                point.x += f(a);
            } catch (error) {
                return [point.x, point.y, error];
            }
            return point.x * point.y;
        }
        function inlinedThrows(object) {
            return object.missing.property;
        }
        function throwsInInlinedCallee(a, target) {
            const point = { x: a, y: 3 };
            let caught = null;
            try {
                inlinedThrows(target);
            } catch (error) {
                caught = error;
            }
            return caught ? [point.x, point.y] : point.x * point.y;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(throwsCaught(i, { missing: {} })).toBe(2 * i + 11);
            expect(callsThrow(i, value => value + 1)).toBe(2 * (2 * i + 1));
            expect(throwsInInlinedCallee(i, { missing: {} })).toBe(3 * i);
        }
        expect(throwsCaught(3, {})).toEqual([3, 14, true]);
        expect(
            callsThrow(5, () => {
                throw "thrown";
            })
        ).toEqual([5, 2, "thrown"]);
        expect(throwsInInlinedCallee(7, {})).toEqual([7, 3]);
    });

    test("calls and slow paths that continue keep the objects virtual", () => {
        function callsAcross(a, f) {
            const point = { x: a, y: 2 };
            const inner = { point, z: a };
            const result = f(a);
            point.x += result;
            return point.x * point.y + inner.z + inner.point.y;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(callsAcross(i, value => value + 1)).toBe(2 * (2 * i + 1) + i + 2);
        expect(
            callsAcross(3, value => {
                gc();
                return value;
            })
        ).toBe(17);
    });

    test("collections while objects are virtual", () => {
        function churn(n) {
            const state = { values: 0, last: null };
            for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
                state.values += i;
                if (i === n - 1) gc();
            }
            return state.values;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(churn(10)).toBe(45);
        expect(churn(1.5)).toBe(1);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/exception-handlers.js
// Exception handlers run in compiled code: an exception thrown in compiled code leaves it with every value live into
// the handler written to the frame, the interpreter runs the handler's Catch, and the frame continues in compiled code
// after it. Finally blocks are handlers too, and so are the handlers that close iterators.
//
// NB: The functions come from the Function constructor, so that each run of a test (see LIBJS_TEST_REPEAT) compiles
//     new ones.

function prepared(...parameters_and_body) {
    const make = new Function(
        "jit",
        "thrower",
        `const f = function (${parameters_and_body.slice(0, -1).join(", ")}) { ${parameters_and_body.at(-1)} }; jit.prepare(f); return f;`
    );
    return make(jit, thrower);
}

function thrower(value) {
    if (value & 1) throw value;
    return value;
}

function compile(f, warm_up) {
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) warm_up();
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
}

const checksCompiledCode = () => jit.enabled && !jit.forcesExits;

describe("exception handlers in compiled code", () => {
    test("catch exceptions of calls, with the values live into the handler", () => {
        const sum = prepared(
            "n",
            "let total = 0; let caught = 0; let compiled = true; for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) { const before = total; try { total += 100; total += thrower(i); } catch (e) { total = before - e; ++caught; compiled &&= jit.inCompiledCode(); } } return [total, caught, compiled];"
        );
        compile(sum, () => sum(10));
        const [total, caught, compiled] = sum(1000);
        let expected = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) expected = i & 1 ? expected - i : expected + 100 + i;
        expect(total).toBe(expected);
        expect(caught).toBe(500);
        if (checksCompiledCode()) expect(compiled).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("run finally blocks after normal completions, returns, breaks and exceptions", () => {
        const run = prepared(
            "n",
            "const log = []; for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) { try { if (i % 4 === 1) continue; if (i % 4 === 2) break; thrower(i); log.push('try ' + i); } catch (e) { log.push('catch ' + e); } finally { log.push('finally ' + i); } } return log;"
        );
        const returns = prepared(
            "x",
            "let state = 'start'; try { state = 'try'; if (x) return state; thrower(1); } catch (e) { state = 'catch ' + e; return state; } finally { state += ' finally'; } return state;"
        );
        compile(run, () => run(3));
        compile(returns, () => [returns(true), returns(false)]);
        expect(run(2)).toEqual(["try 0", "finally 0", "finally 1"]);
        expect(run(10)).toEqual(["try 0", "finally 0", "finally 1", "finally 2"]);
        expect(returns(true)).toBe("try");
        expect(returns(false)).toBe("catch 1");
    });

    test("rethrow from catch and finally blocks to outer handlers", () => {
        const nested = prepared(
            "n",
            "let log = ''; for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) { try { try { thrower(i); log += 'a'; } catch (e) { log += 'b'; throw e + 1; } finally { log += 'c'; } } catch (e) { log += e; } } return log;"
        );
        const propagates = prepared("x", "try { thrower(x); } finally { if (x === 3) return 'overridden'; }");
        compile(nested, () => nested(4));
        compile(propagates, () => {
            try {
                propagates(1);
            } catch {}
            propagates(2);
        });
        expect(nested(6)).toBe("acbc2acbc4acbc6");
        let thrown;
        try {
            propagates(5);
        } catch (e) {
            thrown = e;
        }
        expect(thrown).toBe(5);
        expect(propagates(3)).toBe("overridden");
        expect(propagates(4)).toBeUndefined();
    });

    test("catch exceptions thrown by property accesses, builtins and checks", () => {
        const access = prepared(
            "values",
            "const results = []; for (const value of values) { try { results.push(value.x.y); } catch (e) { results.push(e.constructor.name); } try { results.push(JSON.parse(value.text)); } catch (e) { results.push(e.constructor.name); } } return results;"
        );
        const getter = {
            get x() {
                throw new RangeError();
            },
        };
        compile(access, () =>
            access([
                { x: { y: 1 }, text: "1" },
                { x: null, text: "{" },
            ])
        );
        expect(access([{ x: { y: 2 }, text: "[3]" }, {}, getter, { x: { y: 4 }, text: "}" }])).toEqual([
            2,
            [3],
            "TypeError",
            "SyntaxError",
            "RangeError",
            "SyntaxError",
            4,
            "SyntaxError",
        ]);
    });

    test("catch exceptions thrown with throw statements in the same function", () => {
        const classify = prepared(
            "values",
            "let total = 0; for (const value of values) { try { if (typeof value !== 'number') throw value; total += value; } catch (e) { total += e.length; } } return total;"
        );
        compile(classify, () => classify([1, "ab", 2]));
        expect(classify([1, 2, "abc", 3, "de", [1, 2, 3, 4]])).toBe(15);
    });

    test("handle exceptions in handlers that first catch after the code was compiled", () => {
        const late = prepared(
            "n, limit",
            "let total = 0; for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) { try { if (i >= limit) throw i; total += i; } catch (e) { total -= e; } } return total;"
        );
        compile(late, () => late(10, 100));
        let expected = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 300; ++i) expected += i < 50 ? i : -i;
        for (let run = 0; run < 20; ++run) expect(late(300, 50)).toBe(expected);
    });

    test("close iterators of loops left by exceptions", () => {
        const closes = prepared(
            "iterable",
            "let total = 0; try { for (const value of iterable) { total += thrower(value); } } catch (e) { total += 1000 * e; } return total;"
        );
        let closed = 0;
        const iterable = values => ({
            [Symbol.iterator]() {
                let index = 0;
                return {
                    next: () => (index < values.length ? { value: values[index++], done: false } : { done: true }),
                    return: () => {
                        ++closed;
                        return {};
                    },
                };
            },
        });
        compile(closes, () => [closes(iterable([2, 4])), closes(iterable([2, 3]))]);
        closed = 0;
        expect(closes(iterable([2, 4, 6]))).toBe(12);
        expect(closes(iterable([2, 4, 5, 6]))).toBe(5006);
        expect(closed).toBe(1);
    });
    test("keep unboxed values live into handlers", () => {
        const mixed = prepared(
            "n",
            "let count = 0; let ratio = 0.5; let flag = false; let log = []; for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) { count += 3; ratio *= 1.5; flag = !flag; try { thrower(i); } catch (e) { log.push([count, ratio, flag, e]); } } return log;"
        );
        compile(mixed, () => mixed(4));
        const expected = [];
        let count = 0;
        let ratio = 0.5;
        let flag = false;
        for (let i = 0; i < 6; ++i) {
            count += 3;
            ratio *= 1.5;
            flag = !flag;
            if (i & 1) expected.push([count, ratio, flag, i]);
        }
        expect(mixed(6)).toEqual(expected);
    });

    test("catch exceptions thrown before the frame was observed", () => {
        const first = prepared("x", "try { return thrower(x); } catch (e) { return -e; }");
        compile(first, () => [first(1), first(2)]);
        const results = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) results.push(first(i));
        expect(results).toEqual(results.map((_, i) => (i & 1 ? -i : i)));
    });

    test("catch exceptions thrown by calls that invalidated the code", () => {
        const make = new Function(
            "jit",
            "class Point { constructor(x) { this.x = x; } } const read = function (point, poison) { let total = 0; try { total += point.x; poison(); total += point.x; } catch (e) { total += point.x * 10 + e; } return total; }; jit.prepare(read); return [read, Point];"
        );
        const [read, Point] = make(jit);
        const harmless = () => {};
        compile(read, () => read(new Point(1), harmless));
        const point = new Point(2);
        const poison = () => {
            Object.defineProperty(Point.prototype, "x", { get: () => 100, configurable: true });
            delete point.x;
            throw 7;
        };
        expect(read(point, poison)).toBe(2 + 100 * 10 + 7);
        expect(read({ x: 3 }, harmless)).toBe(6);
    });
});

describe("exception handlers in compiled generators", () => {
    test("catch exceptions between yields and thrown into them", () => {
        const GeneratorFunction = Object.getPrototypeOf(function* () {}).constructor;
        const generator = new GeneratorFunction(
            "thrower",
            "n",
            "for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) { try { yield thrower(i); } catch (e) { yield 'caught ' + e; } }"
        );
        jit.prepare(generator);
        compile(generator, () => [...generator(thrower, 4)]);
        expect([...generator(thrower, 4)]).toEqual([0, "caught 1", 2, "caught 3"]);
        const resumed = generator(thrower, 2);
        expect(resumed.next()).toEqual({ value: 0, done: false });
        expect(resumed.throw("thrown")).toEqual({ value: "caught thrown", done: false });
        expect(resumed.next()).toEqual({ value: "caught 1", done: false });
        expect(resumed.next()).toEqual({ value: undefined, done: true });
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/for-of-in-inlined-callees.js
// Callees with exception handlers, like the handler that closes the iterator of a for-of loop, are inlined when none
// of their handlers caught an exception before the compile. An exception that one of them catches leaves compiled code,
// and the interpreter runs the handler in the callee's frame.
//
// NB: The functions come from the Function constructor, so that each run of a test (see LIBJS_TEST_REPEAT) compiles
//     new ones, whose handlers never caught anything.

function prepared(source) {
    const functions = new Function(source)();
    for (const f of Object.values(functions)) jit.prepare(f);
    return functions;
}

function compile(f, warm_up) {
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) warm_up();
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
}

function closingIterable(values, log) {
    return {
        [Symbol.iterator]() {
            let index = 0;
            return {
                next: () => (index < values.length ? { value: values[index++], done: false } : { done: true }),
                return: () => {
                    log.push("return");
                    return {};
                },
            };
        },
    };
}

function* closingGenerator(values, log) {
    try {
        yield* values;
    } finally {
        log.push("return");
    }
}

describe("for-of loops in inlined callees", () => {
    test("an exception from the loop body closes the iterator once and reaches the caller's handler", () => {
        const { run } = prepared(`
            function sum(iterable, error) {
                let total = 0;
                for (const value of iterable) {
                    if (value < 0) throw error;
                    total += value;
                }
                return total;
            }
            function run(iterable, error) {
                try {
                    return sum(iterable, error);
                } catch (e) {
                    return e;
                }
            }
            return { sum, run };
        `);
        const error = new Error("negative");
        compile(run, () => {
            run(closingIterable([1, 2], []), error);
            run(closingGenerator([1, 2], []), error);
        });
        for (const iterable of [closingIterable, closingGenerator]) {
            const log = [];
            expect(run(iterable([1, -1, 2], log), error)).toBe(error);
            expect(log).toEqual(["return"]);
        }
        expect(run([1, 2, 3], error)).toBe(6);
        expect(run([1, -2, 3], error)).toBe(error);
    });

    test("break and return close a generator once", () => {
        const { run } = prepared(`
            function firstAbove(iterable, limit) {
                for (const value of iterable) {
                    if (value > limit) return value;
                }
                return -1;
            }
            function countUpTo(iterable, limit) {
                let count = 0;
                for (const value of iterable) {
                    if (value > limit) break;
                    ++count;
                }
                return count;
            }
            function run(make, values, limit, log) {
                return [firstAbove(make(values, log), limit), countUpTo(make(values, log), limit)];
            }
            return { firstAbove, countUpTo, run };
        `);
        compile(run, () => run(closingGenerator, [1, 5, 2], 3, []));
        let log = [];
        expect(run(closingGenerator, [1, 5, 2], 3, log)).toEqual([5, 1]);
        expect(log).toEqual(["return", "return"]);
        log = [];
        expect(run(closingGenerator, [1, 2], 3, log)).toEqual([-1, 2]);
        expect(log).toEqual(["return", "return"]);
        log = [];
        expect(run(closingIterable, [7, 1], 3, log)).toEqual([7, 0]);
        expect(log).toEqual(["return", "return"]);
    });
});

describe("exception handlers in inlined callees", () => {
    test("a handler of an inlined callee gets the exception it caught", () => {
        const { run } = prepared(`
            function doubled(value) {
                try {
                    if (typeof value !== "number") throw value;
                    return value * 2;
                } catch (e) {
                    return "not a number: " + e;
                }
            }
            function run(values) {
                const results = [];
                for (let i = 0; i < values.length; ++i) results.push(doubled(values[i]));
                return results;
            }
            return { doubled, run };
        `);
        compile(run, () => run([1, 2, 3]));
        expect(run([1, "a", 3])).toEqual([2, "not a number: a", 6]);
        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) expect(run([i, "b"])).toEqual([2 * i, "not a number: b"]);
    });

    test("an exception thrown in a nested inlined callee reaches the handler of the callee it is inlined into", () => {
        const { run } = prepared(`
            function checked(value) {
                if (value < 0) throw value;
                return value;
            }
            function sum(values) {
                let total = 0;
                try {
                    for (const value of values) total += checked(value);
                } catch (e) {
                    return [e, total];
                }
                return total;
            }
            function run(values) {
                return sum(values);
            }
            return { checked, sum, run };
        `);
        compile(run, () => run([1, 2, 3]));
        expect(run([1, 2, -3, 4])).toEqual([-3, 3]);
        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) expect(run([i, -i - 1])).toEqual([-i - 1, i]);
        expect(run([4, 5])).toBe(9);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/forwarded-calls.js
// JIT code inlines functions called through Function.prototype.call,
// Function.prototype.apply with the caller's arguments, and bound functions,
// as the interpreter saw them forward their calls. These tests run every
// function many times, so that with a low JIT threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

describe("calls forwarded to inlined functions", () => {
    test("Function.prototype.call", () => {
        const object = {
            base: 1,
            add(a, b) {
                return this.base + a + b;
            },
        };
        function caller(i) {
            return object.add.call(object, i, 2);
        }
        function withoutArguments() {
            return object.add.call();
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(caller(i)).toBe(i + 3);
            expect(withoutArguments()).toBeNaN();
        }
        // Another function, another receiver and a primitive receiver.
        const add = object.add;
        object.add = function (a, b) {
            return a * b;
        };
        expect(caller(5)).toBe(10);
        object.add = add;
        expect(caller.call(null, 5)).toBe(8);
        expect(add.call(3, 1, 1)).toBeNaN();
    });

    test("Function.prototype.apply with the caller's arguments", () => {
        const target = {
            base: 1,
            inner(a, b, c) {
                return this.base + a + b + c;
            },
        };
        function forward() {
            return target.inner.apply(target, arguments);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(forward(i, 2, 3)).toBe(i + 6);
        // Other argument counts than the ones seen.
        expect(forward(1, 2)).toBeNaN();
        expect(forward(1, 2, 3, 4)).toBe(7);
        expect(forward()).toBeNaN();
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(forward(i, 2, 3)).toBe(i + 6);
    });

    test("bound functions", () => {
        const object = { base: 10 };
        function add(a, b, c) {
            return this.base + a + b + c;
        }
        const bound = add.bind(object, 1);
        function caller(i) {
            return bound(i, 2);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller(i)).toBe(i + 13);
        const strictBound = function (a) {
            "use strict";
            return [this, a];
        }.bind(5, 6);
        function strictCaller() {
            return strictBound();
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(strictCaller()).toEqual([5, 6]);
    });

    test("exits in forwarded callees", () => {
        const target = {
            inner(a, b, c) {
                if (a > 1000) {
                    // Never ran while warming up.
                    return [a, b, c, this === target];
                }
                return a + b + c;
            },
        };
        function forward() {
            return target.inner.apply(target, arguments);
        }
        function viaCall(a, b) {
            return target.inner.call(target, a, b, 3);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(forward(i, 2, 3)).toBe(i + 5);
            expect(viaCall(i, 2)).toBe(i + 5);
        }
        expect(forward(2000, 2, 3)).toEqual([2000, 2, 3, true]);
        expect(viaCall(2000, 2)).toEqual([2000, 2, 3, true]);
    });

    test("exceptions and stack traces of forwarded calls", () => {
        const object = {
            check(value) {
                if (value % 5 === 4) throw new Error(`bad ${value}`);
                return value;
            },
        };
        function caller(i) {
            try {
                return object.check.call(object, i);
            } catch (error) {
                return error.message;
            }
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(caller(i)).toBe(i % 5 === 4 ? `bad ${i}` : i);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/frame-initialization.js
test("large frames with many arithmetic slow paths", () => {
    let body = "let result = input;";
    for (let i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) body += `result = result + ${i + 0.123456789};`;
    body += "return result;";
    const sum = new Function("input", body);
    const reference = new Function("input", body);
    jit.neverCompile(reference);
    jit.prepare(sum);
    expect(sum(1)).toBe(reference(1));
    expect(sum("x")).toBe(reference("x"));
    expect(jit.compile(sum)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(sum(1)).toBe(reference(1));
    expect(sum("x")).toBe(reference("x"));
    expect(sum({ valueOf: () => 2 })).toBe(reference(2));
    expect(() => sum(Symbol())).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(sum(3)).toBe(reference(3));
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/function-lazy-properties.js
const triggers = {
    defineName: object => Object.defineProperty(object, "name", { value: "renamed" }),
    deleteLength: object => delete object.length,
    becomePrototype: object => Object.setPrototypeOf({}, object),
    ownKeys: object => Reflect.ownKeys(object),
    getOwnName: object => Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(object, "name"),
};

const factories = {
    normal: () => new Function(""),
    arrow: () => () => {},
    async: () => async function () {},
};

for (const [kind, make] of Object.entries(factories)) {
    for (const [name, trigger] of Object.entries(triggers)) {
        test(`${kind} function reifies lazy properties during a call: ${name}`, () => {
            const victim = make();
            // Give each test a fresh shape, so earlier tests cannot have made it unstable.
            victim[Symbol()] = 0;
            victim.a = 10;
            victim.b = 20;
            let armed = false;
            const poke = object => {
                if (armed) trigger(object);
            };
            const read = new Function(
                "poke",
                "object",
                "const first = object.b; poke(object); return first + object.b;"
            );
            jit.prepare(read);
            for (let i = 0; i < 50; ++i) read(poke, victim);
            expect(jit.compile(read)).toBe(jit.enabled);

            armed = true;
            expect(read(poke, victim)).toBe(40);
            expect(victim.a).toBe(10);
            expect(victim.b).toBe(20);
            expect(read(poke, victim)).toBe(40);
        });
    }
}

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/generators.js
// Generators run in compiled code: a call starts one there, and each resumption enters the code at the continuation
// of the yield it was suspended at, with the values that the frame kept across the suspension.
//
// NB: The functions come from the GeneratorFunction constructor, so that each run of a test (see LIBJS_TEST_REPEAT)
//     compiles new ones.

const GeneratorFunction = Object.getPrototypeOf(function* () {}).constructor;

function prepared(...parameters_and_body) {
    const generator = new GeneratorFunction(...parameters_and_body);
    jit.prepare(generator);
    return generator;
}

function compile(generator, warm_up) {
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) warm_up();
    expect(jit.compile(generator)).toBe(jit.enabled);
}

describe("generators in compiled code", () => {
    test("resume where they yielded, with the values live across their yields", () => {
        const count = prepared(
            "start",
            "step",
            "let total = 0; for (let i = start; i < start + 5; i += step) { total += i; yield [i, total, jit.inCompiledCode()]; } return total * 2;"
        );
        compile(count, () => [...count(0, 1)]);
        const generator = count(10, 2);
        const results = [];
        for (let result = generator.next(); !result.done; result = generator.next()) results.push(result.value);
        expect(results.map(([value, total]) => [value, total])).toEqual([
            [10, 10],
            [12, 22],
            [14, 36],
        ]);
        if (jit.enabled && !jit.forcesExits) expect(results.every(([, , compiled]) => compiled)).toBeTrue();
        const first = count(1, 1).next();
        expect(first.done).toBeFalse();
        expect(first.value.slice(0, 2)).toEqual([1, 1]);
        const finished = count(0, 4);
        finished.next();
        finished.next();
        expect(finished.next()).toEqual({ value: 8, done: true });
        expect(finished.next()).toEqual({ value: undefined, done: true });
    });

    test("receive the values passed to next", () => {
        const accumulate = prepared(
            "let total = 0; while (true) { const value = yield total; if (value === undefined) return total; total += value; }"
        );
        compile(accumulate, () => {
            const generator = accumulate();
            generator.next();
            generator.next(1);
            generator.next(2);
            generator.next();
        });
        const generator = accumulate();
        expect(generator.next(100)).toEqual({ value: 0, done: false });
        expect(generator.next(5)).toEqual({ value: 5, done: false });
        expect(generator.next(0.5)).toEqual({ value: 5.5, done: false });
        expect(generator.next("x")).toEqual({ value: "5.5x", done: false });
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: "5.5x", done: true });
    });

    test("keep this, arguments and captured bindings across yields", () => {
        const make = new Function(
            "GeneratorFunction",
            "jit",
            "let captured = 1; const generator = function* (a, b) { yield this.x + a; captured += b; yield arguments.length + captured; yield this.x * b; }; jit.prepare(generator); return [generator, () => captured];"
        );
        const [generator, captured] = make(GeneratorFunction, jit);
        compile(generator, () => [...generator.call({ x: 1 }, 2, 3)]);
        const before = captured();
        expect([...generator.call({ x: 10 }, 20, 30, 40)]).toEqual([30, 3 + before + 30, 300]);
        expect(captured()).toBe(before + 30);
    });

    test("finish through return and throw", () => {
        const guarded = prepared("let i = 0; while (true) yield i++;");
        compile(guarded, () => {
            const generator = guarded();
            generator.next();
            generator.next();
            generator.return(5);
        });
        const returned = guarded();
        expect(returned.next()).toEqual({ value: 0, done: false });
        expect(returned.next()).toEqual({ value: 1, done: false });
        expect(returned.return(7)).toEqual({ value: 7, done: true });
        expect(returned.next()).toEqual({ value: undefined, done: true });

        const thrown = guarded();
        thrown.next();
        expect(() => thrown.throw(new RangeError("stop"))).toThrowWithMessage(RangeError, "stop");
        expect(thrown.next()).toEqual({ value: undefined, done: true });
    });

    test("delegate with yield*", () => {
        const inner = prepared("value", "const received = yield value; yield received * 2; return value + 1;");
        const outer = prepared(
            "inner",
            "let results = []; for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) results.push(yield* inner(i)); return results;"
        );
        compile(inner, () => [...inner(1)]);
        compile(outer, () => [...outer(inner)]);
        const generator = outer(inner);
        const values = [];
        let result = generator.next();
        for (let i = 0; !result.done; ++i) {
            values.push(result.value);
            result = generator.next(i);
        }
        expect(values).toEqual([0, 0, 1, 4, 2, 8]);
        expect(result).toEqual({ value: [1, 2, 3], done: true });
    });

    test("run in for-of loops and spreads", () => {
        const range = prepared("count", "for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) yield i * i;");
        compile(range, () => [...range(3)]);
        let total = 0;
        for (const value of range(100)) total += value;
        expect(total).toBe(328350);
        expect([...range(4)]).toEqual([0, 1, 4, 9]);
        expect(Array.from(range(0))).toEqual([]);
    });

    test("leave compiled code where a speculation fails, and keep their state", () => {
        const add = prepared("a", "b", "let sum = a; for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) { sum = sum + b; yield sum; }");
        compile(add, () => [...add(1, 2)]);
        expect([...add(1, 2)]).toEqual([3, 5, 7]);
        expect([...add(2147483647, 1)]).toEqual([2147483648, 2147483649, 2147483650]);
        expect([...add("a", 1)]).toEqual(["a1", "a11", "a111"]);
        const generator = add(1, 1);
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: 2, done: false });
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: 3, done: false });
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: 4, done: false });
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: undefined, done: true });
    });

    test("suspended generators resume after their code is discarded and compiled again", () => {
        const values = prepared("for (let i = 0; i < 4; ++i) yield i;");
        compile(values, () => [...values()]);
        const generator = values();
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: 0, done: false });
        jit.discard(values);
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: 1, done: false });
        expect(jit.compile(values)).toBe(jit.enabled);
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: 2, done: false });
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: 3, done: false });
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: undefined, done: true });
    });

    test("loops in generators continue in compiled code at their back edges", () => {
        const sum = prepared(
            "count",
            "let total = 0; for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) total += i % 7; yield total; yield total + 1;"
        );
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) [...sum(10)];
        const generator = sum(100000);
        let expected = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 100000; ++i) expected += i % 7;
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: expected, done: false });
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: expected + 1, done: false });
        expect(generator.next()).toEqual({ value: undefined, done: true });
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/global-property-constants.js
// Properties of the global object that hold an object and were never assigned are constants in compiled code, which
// depends on them staying unassigned. Each case compiles a function that calls such a property, then changes the
// property in another way, from compiled code where it can, and checks that the caller sees the change.

function compile(f, warmUp = () => {}) {
    jit.prepare(f);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) warmUp(f, i);
    jit.compile(f);
    return f;
}

const callEach = f => f();

test("a declared function is assigned by compiled code", () => {
    evaluateSource("function jitConstantAssigned() { return 1; }");
    const caller = compile(() => jitConstantAssigned(), callEach);
    expect(caller()).toBe(1);
    const assign = compile(value => {
        jitConstantAssigned = value;
    });
    assign(() => 2);
    expect(caller()).toBe(2);

    // Once assigned, the property is loaded, and compiled code that stores to it like the caches do is seen too.
    const assignAgain = compile(
        value => {
            jitConstantAssigned = value;
        },
        (f, i) => f(() => 3 + i)
    );
    const callerAgain = compile(() => jitConstantAssigned(), callEach);
    expect(callerAgain()).toBe(12);
    assignAgain(() => 20);
    expect(callerAgain()).toBe(20);
    expect(caller()).toBe(20);
});

test("a function a var initialized is assigned", () => {
    evaluateSource("var jitConstantVar = function () { return 1; };");
    const caller = compile(() => jitConstantVar(), callEach);
    expect(caller()).toBe(1);
    evaluateSource("jitConstantVar = function () { return 2; };");
    expect(caller()).toBe(2);
});

test("compiled code that stores to properties of other objects stores to the global object", () => {
    evaluateSource("function jitConstantNamed() { return 1; }");
    const caller = compile(() => jitConstantNamed(), callEach);
    expect(caller()).toBe(1);
    const store = compile(
        (object, value) => {
            object.jitConstantNamed = value;
        },
        (f, i) => f({ jitConstantNamed: i }, i)
    );
    store(globalThis, () => 2);
    expect(caller()).toBe(2);
});

test("compiled code that stores to keyed properties of other objects stores to the global object", () => {
    evaluateSource("function jitConstantKeyed() { return 1; }");
    const caller = compile(() => jitConstantKeyed(), callEach);
    expect(caller()).toBe(1);
    const store = compile(
        (object, key, value) => {
            object[key] = value;
        },
        (f, i) => f({ jitConstantKeyed: i }, "jitConstantKeyed", i)
    );
    store(globalThis, "jitConstantKeyed", () => 2);
    expect(caller()).toBe(2);
});

test("a declared function is redefined", () => {
    evaluateSource("function jitConstantDefined() { return 1; }");
    const caller = compile(() => jitConstantDefined(), callEach);
    expect(caller()).toBe(1);
    Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "jitConstantDefined", { value: () => 2 });
    expect(caller()).toBe(2);
});

test("a function is replaced by Object.assign()", () => {
    evaluateSource("function jitConstantAssign() { return 1; }");
    const caller = compile(() => jitConstantAssign(), callEach);
    expect(caller()).toBe(1);
    Object.assign(globalThis, { jitConstantAssign: () => 2 });
    expect(caller()).toBe(2);
});

test("a property becomes an accessor", () => {
    globalThis.jitConstantAccessor = () => 1;
    const caller = compile(() => jitConstantAccessor(), callEach);
    expect(caller()).toBe(1);
    Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "jitConstantAccessor", { get: () => () => 2 });
    expect(caller()).toBe(2);
});

test("a property is deleted, and one after it moves", () => {
    globalThis.jitConstantDeleted = () => 1;
    globalThis.jitConstantMoved = () => 2;
    const callDeleted = compile(() => jitConstantDeleted(), callEach);
    const callMoved = compile(() => jitConstantMoved(), callEach);
    expect(callDeleted()).toBe(1);
    expect(callMoved()).toBe(2);
    delete globalThis.jitConstantDeleted;
    expect(callDeleted).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "'jitConstantDeleted' is not defined");
    expect(callMoved()).toBe(2);
    globalThis.jitConstantDeleted = () => 3;
    expect(callDeleted()).toBe(3);
    expect(callMoved()).toBe(2);
});

test("a later script declares a binding that shadows the property", () => {
    globalThis.jitConstantShadowed = () => 1;
    const caller = compile(() => jitConstantShadowed(), callEach);
    expect(caller()).toBe(1);
    evaluateSource("let jitConstantShadowed = () => 2;");
    expect(caller()).toBe(2);
});

test("a variable is initialized and then assigned by the same code", () => {
    evaluateSource("var jitConstantInitialized;");
    const assign = value => {
        jitConstantInitialized = value;
    };
    assign(() => 1);
    const caller = compile(() => jitConstantInitialized(), callEach);
    expect(caller()).toBe(1);
    assign(() => 2);
    expect(caller()).toBe(2);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/global-variables.js
// JIT code reads and writes global variables directly: global `let`, `const`
// and `class` bindings, and properties of the global object. It uses the
// values of `const` bindings as constants, and speculates that globals
// holding objects keep them. These tests run every function many times, so
// that with a low JIT threshold they are compiled, and then change what the
// compiled code relied on.

const iterations = 200;
const constantNumber = 3;
const constantObject = { value: 4 };
let changingLet = 1;
let changingObject = { value: 1 };
var changingVar = 1;
var functionVar = () => "first";
class GlobalClass {
    static value = 5;
}

function readConstants() {
    return constantNumber + constantObject.value + GlobalClass.value;
}

function readLet() {
    return changingLet;
}

function readObjectLet() {
    return changingObject.value;
}

function writeLet(value) {
    changingLet = value;
}

function readVar() {
    return changingVar;
}

function writeVar(value) {
    changingVar = value;
}

function callFunctionVar() {
    return functionVar();
}

describe("Global variables in JIT code", () => {
    test("constants", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(readConstants()).toBe(12);
    });

    test("let bindings that change", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            writeLet(i);
            expect(readLet()).toBe(i);
        }
        writeLet("a string");
        expect(readLet()).toBe("a string");
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(readObjectLet()).toBe(1);
        changingObject = { value: 2 };
        expect(readObjectLet()).toBe(2);
    });

    test("var properties that change", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            writeVar(i);
            expect(readVar()).toBe(i);
        }
        writeVar(undefined);
        expect(readVar()).toBeUndefined();
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(callFunctionVar()).toBe("first");
        functionVar = () => "second";
        expect(callFunctionVar()).toBe("second");
        globalThis.functionVar = () => "third";
        expect(callFunctionVar()).toBe("third");
    });

    test("properties of the global object that become accessors or go away", () => {
        globalThis.configurableGlobal = 1;
        const read = () => configurableGlobal;
        const write = value => {
            configurableGlobal = value;
        };
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            write(i);
            expect(read()).toBe(i);
        }
        let stored;
        Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "configurableGlobal", {
            get: () => "getter",
            set: value => {
                stored = value;
            },
            configurable: true,
        });
        expect(read()).toBe("getter");
        write(7);
        expect(stored).toBe(7);
        delete globalThis.configurableGlobal;
        expect(() => read()).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "'configurableGlobal' is not defined");
    });

    test("bindings that a later script declares shadow properties of the global object", () => {
        globalThis.shadowedGlobal = "property";
        const read = () => shadowedGlobal;
        const values = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            if (i === iterations / 2) evaluateSource("let shadowedGlobal = 'binding';");
            values.push(read());
        }
        expect(values[0]).toBe("property");
        expect(values[iterations / 2 - 1]).toBe("property");
        expect(values[iterations / 2]).toBe("binding");
        expect(values[iterations - 1]).toBe("binding");
        expect(globalThis.shadowedGlobal).toBe("property");
    });

    test("bindings that are not initialized yet", () => {
        evaluateSource(`
            function readEarly() {
                return earlyBinding;
            }
            globalThis.earlyResults = [];
            for (let i = 0; i < ${iterations}; ++i) {
                try {
                    earlyResults.push(readEarly());
                } catch (error) {
                    earlyResults.push(error.constructor.name);
                }
            }
            let earlyBinding = "initialized";
            for (let i = 0; i < ${iterations}; ++i) earlyResults.push(readEarly());
        `);
        expect(earlyResults.length).toBe(2 * iterations);
        expect(earlyResults.slice(0, iterations).every(result => result === "ReferenceError")).toBeTrue();
        expect(earlyResults.slice(iterations).every(result => result === "initialized")).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("constant bindings cannot be assigned", () => {
        const assign = () => {
            constantNumber = 4;
        };
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i)
            expect(assign).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Invalid assignment to const variable");
        expect(readConstants()).toBe(12);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/hole-filling-stores-prototype-setters.js
// JIT code stores into the holes of holey arrays inline only where their
// prototype chain has no indexed properties. Each test compiles the stores
// first, and then gives %Array.prototype% or %Object.prototype% an indexed
// property. Indexed properties of %Object.prototype% stay in effect after they
// are deleted, so that test comes last, and this file is of its own.

const iterations = 100;

function store(array, index, value) {
    array[index] = value;
}

function strictStore(array, index, value) {
    "use strict";
    array[index] = value;
}

function warmUp() {
    for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
        const array = new Array(16);
        for (let j = 0; j < 16; ++j) store(array, j, j);
        const strictArray = new Array(16);
        for (let j = 0; j < 16; ++j) strictStore(strictArray, j, j);
    }
}

// An array with holes inside the capacity of its storage, so that stores into
// them do not need to grow it.
function holeyArray(length) {
    const array = new Array(length);
    array[0] = 0;
    return array;
}

function removeArrayPrototypeElement(index) {
    delete Array.prototype[index];
    Array.prototype.length = 0;
}

describe("Hole-filling stores in JIT code with indexed properties on prototypes", () => {
    test("a setter on Array.prototype", () => {
        warmUp();
        const calls = [];
        Object.defineProperty(Array.prototype, 2, {
            set(value) {
                calls.push([this, value]);
            },
            configurable: true,
        });
        try {
            const array = holeyArray(8);
            store(array, 2, "x");
            strictStore(array, 2, "y");
            expect(calls).toEqual([
                [array, "x"],
                [array, "y"],
            ]);
            expect(Object.hasOwn(array, 2)).toBeFalse();
            store(array, 3, "z");
            expect(array[3]).toBe("z");
        } finally {
            removeArrayPrototypeElement(2);
        }
        const array = holeyArray(8);
        store(array, 2, "x");
        expect(array[2]).toBe("x");
        expect(calls.length).toBe(2);
    });

    test("a read-only element of Array.prototype", () => {
        warmUp();
        Object.defineProperty(Array.prototype, 3, { value: "read-only", configurable: true });
        try {
            const array = holeyArray(8);
            store(array, 3, "x");
            expect(Object.hasOwn(array, 3)).toBeFalse();
            expect(array[3]).toBe("read-only");
            expect(() => strictStore(array, 3, "x")).toThrow(TypeError);
            expect(Object.hasOwn(array, 3)).toBeFalse();
        } finally {
            removeArrayPrototypeElement(3);
        }
        const array = holeyArray(8);
        store(array, 3, "x");
        expect(array[3]).toBe("x");
    });

    test("a setter on Object.prototype", () => {
        warmUp();
        const calls = [];
        Object.defineProperty(Object.prototype, 4, {
            set(value) {
                calls.push([this, value]);
            },
            configurable: true,
        });
        try {
            const array = holeyArray(8);
            store(array, 4, "x");
            strictStore(array, 4, "y");
            expect(calls).toEqual([
                [array, "x"],
                [array, "y"],
            ]);
            expect(Object.hasOwn(array, 4)).toBeFalse();
        } finally {
            delete Object.prototype[4];
        }
        const array = holeyArray(8);
        store(array, 4, "x");
        expect(array[4]).toBe("x");
        expect(calls.length).toBe(2);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/hole-filling-stores.js
// JIT code stores into the holes of holey arrays inline, when nothing could
// observe the difference. These tests run every function many times, so that
// with a low JIT threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

function store(array, index, value) {
    array[index] = value;
}

function strictStore(array, index, value) {
    "use strict";
    array[index] = value;
}

function fill(values) {
    const array = new Array(values.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < values.length; ++i) store(array, i, values[i]);
    return array;
}

function warmUp() {
    const values = Array.from({ length: 16 }, (_, i) => i);
    for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
        fill(values);
        const array = new Array(values.length);
        for (let j = 0; j < values.length; ++j) strictStore(array, j, j);
    }
}

// An array with holes inside the capacity of its storage, so that stores into
// them do not need to grow it.
function holeyArray(length) {
    const array = new Array(length);
    array[0] = 0;
    return array;
}

describe("Hole-filling stores in JIT code", () => {
    test("filling every hole", () => {
        const kinds = [i => i, i => `${i}`, i => ({ i }), () => undefined];
        for (let count = 0; count <= iterations; ++count) {
            for (const kind of kinds) {
                const values = Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => kind(i));
                const array = fill(values);
                expect(array.length).toBe(count);
                for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
                    expect(Object.hasOwn(array, i)).toBeTrue();
                    expect(array[i]).toBe(values[i]);
                }
                expect(array).toEqual(values);
                expect([...array]).toEqual(values);
                expect(Object.keys(array)).toEqual(Object.keys(values));
            }
        }
    });

    test("overwriting elements of holey arrays", () => {
        warmUp();
        const array = holeyArray(8);
        store(array, 2, "a");
        store(array, 2, "b");
        strictStore(array, 3, "c");
        strictStore(array, 3, "d");
        expect(array[2]).toBe("b");
        expect(array[3]).toBe("d");
        expect(Object.keys(array)).toEqual(["0", "2", "3"]);
    });

    test("filling some holes leaves the others", () => {
        warmUp();
        for (let count = 0; count <= 40; ++count) {
            const array = new Array(count);
            for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 2) store(array, i, i);
            expect(array.length).toBe(count);
            for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
                const filled = i % 2 === 0;
                expect(Object.hasOwn(array, i)).toBe(filled);
                expect(i in array).toBe(filled);
                expect(array[i]).toBe(filled ? i : undefined);
            }
            expect(Object.keys(array).length).toBe(Math.ceil(count / 2));
        }
    });

    test("filling in reverse and the last index first", () => {
        warmUp();
        const expected = Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => i);

        const reversed = new Array(20);
        for (let i = 19; i >= 0; --i) store(reversed, i, i);
        expect(reversed).toEqual(expected);

        const lastFirst = holeyArray(20);
        store(lastFirst, 19, 19);
        for (let i = 1; i < 19; ++i) store(lastFirst, i, i);
        expect(lastFirst).toEqual(expected);

        const lastAtEnd = holeyArray(20);
        for (let i = 1; i < 20; ++i) store(lastAtEnd, i, i);
        expect(lastAtEnd).toEqual(expected);

        for (const array of [reversed, lastFirst, lastAtEnd]) {
            expect(array[19]).toBe(19);
            expect(array.indexOf(7)).toBe(7);
            expect(array.indexOf(20)).toBe(-1);
            expect(array.push(20)).toBe(21);
            expect([...array]).toEqual([...expected, 20]);
            expect(Object.keys(array).length).toBe(21);
        }
    });

    test("negative keys of arrays longer than 2^31", () => {
        warmUp();
        const array = new Array(2 ** 32 - 1);
        store(array, -5, "negative");
        strictStore(array, -6, "also negative");
        expect(array[-5]).toBe("negative");
        expect(array[-6]).toBe("also negative");
        expect(array[2 ** 32 - 5]).toBeUndefined();
        expect(array.length).toBe(2 ** 32 - 1);
        expect(Object.keys(array)).toEqual(["-5", "-6"]);
    });

    test("arrays that cannot get new elements", () => {
        warmUp();
        const array = Object.preventExtensions(holeyArray(8));
        store(array, 3, "x");
        expect(Object.hasOwn(array, 3)).toBeFalse();
        expect(array.length).toBe(8);
        expect(() => strictStore(array, 3, "x")).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(Object.hasOwn(array, 3)).toBeFalse();
        store(array, 0, "existing");
        expect(array[0]).toBe("existing");

        const sealed = Object.seal(holeyArray(8));
        store(sealed, 3, "x");
        expect(Object.hasOwn(sealed, 3)).toBeFalse();
        expect(() => strictStore(sealed, 3, "x")).toThrow(TypeError);
    });

    test("arrays with other prototypes", () => {
        warmUp();
        class Subclass extends Array {
            set 3(value) {
                this.seen = value;
            }
        }
        const subclass = new Subclass(8);
        subclass[0] = 0;
        store(subclass, 3, "x");
        expect(subclass.seen).toBe("x");
        expect(Object.hasOwn(subclass, 3)).toBeFalse();
        store(subclass, 4, "y");
        expect(subclass[4]).toBe("y");

        const calls = [];
        const withOwnPrototype = holeyArray(8);
        Object.setPrototypeOf(withOwnPrototype, {
            set 2(value) {
                calls.push([this, value]);
            },
        });
        store(withOwnPrototype, 2, "x");
        strictStore(withOwnPrototype, 2, "y");
        expect(calls).toEqual([
            [withOwnPrototype, "x"],
            [withOwnPrototype, "y"],
        ]);
        expect(Object.hasOwn(withOwnPrototype, 2)).toBeFalse();
        store(withOwnPrototype, 3, "z");
        expect(Object.hasOwn(withOwnPrototype, 3)).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("proxy targets and other objects", () => {
        warmUp();
        const target = holeyArray(8);
        let sets = 0;
        const proxy = new Proxy(target, {
            set(target, key, value) {
                ++sets;
                target[key] = value;
                return true;
            },
        });
        store(target, 3, "x");
        expect(target[3]).toBe("x");
        expect(sets).toBe(0);
        store(proxy, 4, "y");
        expect(target[4]).toBe("y");
        expect(sets).toBe(1);
        expect(Object.keys(target)).toEqual(["0", "3", "4"]);

        const arrayLike = { length: 8, 0: 0, 5: 5 };
        store(arrayLike, 3, "x");
        expect(arrayLike[3]).toBe("x");
        expect(arrayLike.length).toBe(8);
        expect(Object.keys(arrayLike)).toEqual(["0", "3", "5", "length"]);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/inline-construct.js
// JIT code inlines constructs of base constructors. These tests run every
// function many times, so that with a low JIT threshold they are compiled,
// and then make the inlined code exit or throw.

const iterations = 100;

describe("inlined constructs", () => {
    test("objects get their prototype and properties", () => {
        function Point(x, y) {
            this.x = x;
            this.y = y;
        }
        Point.prototype.sum = function () {
            return this.x + this.y;
        };
        function make(i) {
            return new Point(i, i + 1);
        }
        const seen = new Set();
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const point = make(i);
            expect(point).toBeInstanceOf(Point);
            expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(point)).toBe(Point.prototype);
            expect(point.constructor).toBe(Point);
            expect(Object.keys(point)).toEqual(["x", "y"]);
            expect(point.sum()).toBe(2 * i + 1);
            expect(seen.has(point)).toBeFalse();
            seen.add(point);
        }
    });

    test("constructors that return this or a primitive result in this", () => {
        function ReturnsThis(value) {
            this.value = value;
            return this;
        }
        function ReturnsPrimitive(value) {
            this.value = value;
            return 42;
        }
        function make(i) {
            return [new ReturnsThis(i), new ReturnsPrimitive(i)];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const [a, b] = make(i);
            expect(a).toBeInstanceOf(ReturnsThis);
            expect(a.value).toBe(i);
            expect(b).toBeInstanceOf(ReturnsPrimitive);
            expect(b.value).toBe(i);
        }
    });

    test("constructors that return objects", () => {
        function Replaced(value) {
            this.ignored = true;
            if (value > 1000) return { replaced: value };
        }
        function make(i) {
            return new Replaced(i);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(make(i).ignored).toBeTrue();
        expect(make(2000)).toEqual({ replaced: 2000 });
    });

    test("a new prototype is seen", () => {
        function Thing(value) {
            this.value = value;
        }
        function make(i) {
            return new Thing(i);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(make(i))).toBe(Thing.prototype);
        const original = Thing.prototype;
        const replacement = { replacement: true };
        Thing.prototype = replacement;
        const thing = make(1);
        expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(thing)).toBe(replacement);
        expect(thing.replacement).toBeTrue();
        expect(thing.value).toBe(1);
        Thing.prototype = original;
        expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(make(2))).toBe(original);
    });

    test("exits and exceptions inside inlined constructors", () => {
        function Sum(a, b) {
            this.first = a;
            this.sum = a + b;
            this.last = b;
        }
        function Throws(value) {
            this.value = value;
            if (value.missing.property) this.never = true;
        }
        function make(a, b) {
            return new Sum(a, b);
        }
        function makeThrowing(value) {
            try {
                return new Throws(value);
            } catch (error) {
                return error;
            }
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(make(i, 1).sum).toBe(i + 1);
            expect(makeThrowing({ missing: {} }).value).toEqual({ missing: {} });
        }
        const strings = make("a", "b");
        expect(strings).toBeInstanceOf(Sum);
        expect(strings).toEqual({ first: "a", sum: "ab", last: "b" });
        expect(makeThrowing({})).toBeInstanceOf(TypeError);
    });

    test("classes", () => {
        class Vector {
            constructor(x) {
                this.x = x;
            }
            get double() {
                return this.x * 2;
            }
        }
        function make(i) {
            return new Vector(i);
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const vector = make(i);
            expect(vector).toBeInstanceOf(Vector);
            expect(vector.double).toBe(2 * i);
        }
    });

    test("collections during inlined constructs", () => {
        function Node(value, next) {
            this.value = value;
            this.next = next;
            if (value % 50 === 49) gc();
        }
        function build(count) {
            let list = null;
            for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) list = new Node(i, list);
            return list;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
            let list = build(100);
            for (let value = 99; value >= 0; --value, list = list.next) expect(list.value).toBe(value);
            expect(list).toBeNull();
        }
    });

    test("properties added to constructed objects", () => {
        function Pair(first, second) {
            this.first = first;
            this.second = second;
        }
        function sum(first, second) {
            const pair = new Pair(first, second);
            return pair.first + pair.second;
        }
        function keep(first, second, reveal) {
