                for (const object of objects) sum += call(object);
                expect(sum).toBe((phase * (phase + 1)) / 2);
            }
        }
    });

    test("methods replaced on a prototype", () => {
        class A {
            value() {
                return 1;
            }
        }
        class B {
            value() {
                return 2;
            }
        }
        function call(object) {
            return object.value();
        }
        const objects = [new A(), new B()];
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(call(objects[i % 2])).toBe((i % 2) + 1);
        B.prototype.value = function () {
            return 20;
        };
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(call(objects[i % 2])).toBe(i % 2 ? 20 : 1);
        A.prototype.value = 5;
        expect(() => call(objects[0])).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(call(objects[1])).toBe(20);
    });

    test("methods replaced by an inlined method while the caller runs", () => {
        class A {
            value(i) {
                if (i === 150) {
                    B.prototype.value = function () {
                        return 30;
                    };
                }
                return 1;
            }
        }
        class B {
            value() {
                return 2;
            }
        }
        function sum(objects, count) {
            let total = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) total += objects[i % 2].value(i);
            return total;
        }
        const objects = [new A(), new B()];
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) expect(sum(objects, 100)).toBe(150);
        // Up to i = 150, B's calls return 2, and 30 after.
        expect(sum(objects, 300)).toBe(150 + 75 * 2 + 75 * 30);
    });

    test("methods that throw, never return, or are too big to inline", () => {
        class Thrower {
            run(value) {
                throw new Error(`thrown ${value}`);
            }
        }
        class Plain {
            run(value) {
                return value + 1;
            }
        }
        class Big {
            run(value) {
                let a = value,
                    b = 1,
                    c = 2,
                    d = 3;
                for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
                    a += b * c;
                    b += c * d;
                    c += d * a;
                    d += a * b;
                    a %= 1000;
                    b %= 1000;
                    c %= 1000;
                    d %= 1000;
                    if (a > 500) a -= 7;
                    if (b > 500) b -= 11;
                    if (c > 500) c -= 13;
                    if (d > 500) d -= 17;
                }
                return a + b + c + d;
            }
        }
        function bigRun(value) {
            return new Big().run(value);
        }
        function call(object, value) {
            try {
                return object.run(value);
            } catch (error) {
                return error.message;
            }
        }
        const objects = [new Thrower(), new Plain(), new Big()];
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(call(objects[0], i)).toBe(`thrown ${i}`);
            expect(call(objects[1], i)).toBe(i + 1);
            expect(call(objects[2], i)).toBe(bigRun(i));
        }
    });

    test("this, arguments and the results of the inlined methods", () => {
        class A {
            constructor() {
                this.name = "a";
            }
            describe(x, y) {
                return `${this.name}:${x}:${y}:${arguments.length}`;
            }
        }
        class B {
            constructor() {
                this.label = "b";
            }
            describe(x) {
                return [this.label, x];
            }
        }
        function call(object, i) {
            return object.describe(i, i + 1);
        }
        const objects = [new A(), new B()];
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(call(objects[0], i)).toBe(`a:${i}:${i + 1}:2`);
            expect(call(objects[1], i)).toEqual(["b", i]);
        }
    });
});

describe("inlined methods of callees copied to other registers", () => {
    test("methods called through a copy of the callee", () => {
        class A {
            m(x) {
                return typeof x === "function" ? 10 : 1;
            }
        }
        class B {
            m(x) {
                return typeof x === "function" ? 20 : 2;
            }
        }
        function call(object) {
            const m = object.m;
            const n = m;
            return m() + n() + m(m);
        }
        const objects = [new A(), new B()];
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(call(objects[i % 2])).toBe(i % 2 ? 2 + 2 + 20 : 1 + 1 + 10);
    });
});

describe("methods replaced again and again", () => {
    test("methods redefined on a prototype many times", () => {
        class A {
            value() {
                return 0;
            }
        }
        function call(object) {
            return object.value();
        }
        const object = new A();
        for (let round = 1; round <= 20; ++round) {
            Object.defineProperty(A.prototype, "value", {
                value: () => round,
                writable: true,
                configurable: true,
            });
            for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(call(object)).toBe(round);
        }
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/polymorphic-stores.js
// JIT code stores named properties through every entry of polymorphic and
// megamorphic property caches, not only the most recently used one. These
// tests run every function many times, so that with a low JIT threshold they
// are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

function store(object, value) {
    object.value = value;
}

// Objects of many shapes that all have a `value` data property.
function objectsOfManyShapes(count) {
    const objects = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        const object = {};
        object[`key${i}`] = i;
        object.value = 0;
        objects.push(object);
    }
    return objects;
}

describe("Polymorphic and megamorphic stores in JIT code", () => {
    test("changing existing properties of many shapes", () => {
        const objects = objectsOfManyShapes(40);
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            for (const object of objects) store(object, i);
        }
        for (const object of objects) expect(object.value).toBe(iterations - 1);
    });

    test("adding properties to objects of many shapes", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const objects = [];
            for (let j = 0; j < 20; ++j) {
                const object = {};
                object[`key${j}`] = j;
                store(object, i);
                objects.push(object);
            }
            for (let j = 0; j < 20; ++j) {
                expect(objects[j].value).toBe(i);
                expect(Object.keys(objects[j])).toEqual([`key${j}`, "value"]);
            }
        }
    });

    test("a few shapes, with additions and changes", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const a = { a: 1 };
            const b = { b: 1 };
            const c = { c: 1, value: 1 };
            store(a, i);
            store(b, i);
            store(c, i);
            store(a, i + 1);
            expect(a.value).toBe(i + 1);
            expect(b.value).toBe(i);
            expect(c.value).toBe(i);
        }
    });

    test("stores that must not go through the cache", () => {
        const objects = objectsOfManyShapes(40);
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            for (const object of objects) store(object, i);
        }

        const frozen = Object.freeze(objectsOfManyShapes(1)[0]);
        store(frozen, "frozen");
        expect(frozen.value).toBe(0);

        const nonWritable = objectsOfManyShapes(1)[0];
        Object.defineProperty(nonWritable, "value", { writable: false });
        store(nonWritable, "non-writable");
        expect(nonWritable.value).toBe(0);

        let setterValue;
        const withSetter = objectsOfManyShapes(1)[0];
        Object.defineProperty(withSetter, "value", {
            set(value) {
                setterValue = value;
            },
        });
        store(withSetter, "setter");
        expect(setterValue).toBe("setter");

        const nonExtensible = Object.preventExtensions({ key0: 0 });
        store(nonExtensible, "added");
        expect(Object.hasOwn(nonExtensible, "value")).toBeFalse();

        let prototypeSetterValue;
        const withPrototypeSetter = Object.create({
            set value(value) {
                prototypeSetterValue = value;
            },
        });
        withPrototypeSetter.key0 = 0;
        store(withPrototypeSetter, "prototype setter");
        expect(prototypeSetterValue).toBe("prototype setter");
        expect(Object.hasOwn(withPrototypeSetter, "value")).toBeFalse();
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/primitive-property-gets.js
// JIT code looks up the named properties of numbers and booleans in their
// prototypes inline, like those of strings. These tests run every function
// many times, so that with a low JIT threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

function getToString(value) {
    return value.toString;
}

function hex(value) {
    return value.toString(16);
}

function getFlag(value) {
    return value.flag;
}

describe("Property gets on primitives in JIT code", () => {
    test("methods of numbers and booleans", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(hex(i)).toBe(i.toString(16));
            expect(hex(i + 0.5)).toBe((i + 0.5).toString(16));
            expect(getToString(i)).toBe(Number.prototype.toString);
            expect(getToString(i % 2 === 0)).toBe(Boolean.prototype.toString);
            expect(getToString("string")).toBe(String.prototype.toString);
            expect(getToString({})).toBe(Object.prototype.toString);
        }
        expect(hex(-0)).toBe("0");
        expect(hex(NaN)).toBe("NaN");
        expect(hex(Infinity)).toBe("Infinity");
        expect(() => getToString(undefined)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(() => getToString(null)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(getToString(Symbol())).toBe(Symbol.prototype.toString);
        expect(getToString(1n)).toBe(BigInt.prototype.toString);
    });

    test("prototype properties that change", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(getFlag(i)).toBeUndefined();
        Number.prototype.flag = "number";
        Boolean.prototype.flag = "boolean";
        try {
            for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
                expect(getFlag(i)).toBe("number");
                expect(getFlag(i + 0.25)).toBe("number");
                expect(getFlag(i % 2 === 0)).toBe("boolean");
            }
            Number.prototype.flag = "changed";
            expect(getFlag(1)).toBe("changed");
            let receiver;
            Object.defineProperty(Number.prototype, "flag", {
                get() {
                    "use strict";
                    receiver = this;
                    return "getter";
                },
                configurable: true,
            });
            expect(getFlag(42)).toBe("getter");
            expect(receiver).toBe(42);
            expect(getFlag(true)).toBe("boolean");
        } finally {
            delete Number.prototype.flag;
            delete Boolean.prototype.flag;
        }
        expect(getFlag(1)).toBeUndefined();
        expect(getFlag(false)).toBeUndefined();
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/profiling-feedback.js
// The feedback the profiling tier records for functions that jit.prepare() moved to it, as jit.feedback() describes
// it: one line per instruction with feedback slots, with what each slot recorded. Loads and calls keep the last value
// they produced, which jit.feedback() folds into the kinds of values its slot saw.

// Without the JIT nothing is profiled, and the harness's repeated runs of a test would add to what the first run
// recorded, so the body runs once.
function profilingTest(name, body) {
    let ran = false;
    test(name, () => {
        if (!jit.enabled || ran) return;
        ran = true;
        body();
    });
}

// What the slots of the first instruction named `name` in the feedback of `f` recorded.
function feedbackOf(f, name) {
    const marker = `] ${name} `;
    const line = jit
        .feedback(f)
        .split("\n")
        .find(line => line.includes(marker));
    return line?.substring(line.indexOf(marker) + marker.length);
}

profilingTest("arithmetic records the kinds of its operands", () => {
    function add(a, b) {
        return a + b;
    }
    jit.prepare(add);
    add(1, 2);
    expect(feedbackOf(add, "Add")).toBe("arith#0: Int32");
    add(1, 0.5);
    add(0x7fffffff, 1);
    expect(feedbackOf(add, "Add")).toBe("arith#0: Int32|Double|Int32Overflow");
    add("a", 1);
    add(1n, 2n);
    expect(feedbackOf(add, "Add")).toBe("arith#0: Int32|Double|Int32Overflow|String|BigInt");

    function negate(value) {
        return -value;
    }
    jit.prepare(negate);
    negate({});
    expect(feedbackOf(negate, "UnaryMinus")).toBe("arith#0: Other");
});

profilingTest("comparisons record the kinds of their operands", () => {
    function less(a, b) {
        return a < b;
    }
    function same(a, b) {
        return a === b;
    }
    jit.prepare(less);
    jit.prepare(same);
    less(1, 2);
    less(1.5, 2);
    same("a", "a");
    expect(feedbackOf(less, "LessThan")).toBe("arith#0: Int32|Double");
    expect(feedbackOf(same, "StrictlyEquals")).toBe("arith#0: String");
});

profilingTest("loads and calls record the kinds of the values they produce", () => {
    function read(object) {
        return object.value;
    }
    jit.prepare(read);
    read({ value: 1 });
    expect(feedbackOf(read, "GetById")).toBe("value of cache#0: Int32");
    read({ value: "string" });
    expect(feedbackOf(read, "GetById")).toBe("value of cache#0: Int32|String");
    read({ value: undefined });
    expect(feedbackOf(read, "GetById")).toBe("value of cache#0: Int32|String|Undefined");

    // Loads record into the slots of their property lookup caches, which stores and the other loads have too.
    function readAfterWrites(object) {
        object.first = 1;
        object.second = 2;
        const length = object.length;
        return [length, object.value];
    }
    jit.prepare(readAfterWrites);
    readAfterWrites({ value: true, length: 1.5 });
    expect(feedbackOf(readAfterWrites, "GetLength")).toBe("value of cache#2: Double keyed#0: keys=none elements=Other");
    expect(feedbackOf(readAfterWrites, "GetById")).toBe("value of cache#3: Boolean");

    function call(f) {
        return f();
    }
    jit.prepare(call);
    // NB: The feedback only holds its targets weakly, so the functions stay alive until the end of the test.
    const returnsNull = () => null;
    const returnsDouble = () => 1.5;
    call(returnsNull);
    expect(feedbackOf(call, "Call")).toBe("call#0: target=function returnsNull flags=none returned: Null");
    call(returnsDouble);
    expect(feedbackOf(call, "Call")).toBe(
        "call#0: target=function returnsNull flags=Polymorphic|OtherFunctions returned: Double|Null"
    );
    expect(returnsDouble()).toBe(1.5);
    expect(returnsNull()).toBeNull();
});

profilingTest("calls record where their callee forwarded them to", () => {
    function target(a, b) {
        return a + b;
    }
    function viaCall(f) {
        return f.call(null, 1, 2);
    }
    function viaApply(f) {
        return f.apply(null, [1, 2, 3]);
    }
    function viaBound(f) {
        return f(2);
    }
    let sum = 0;
    function add(value) {
        sum += value;
    }
    function viaCallback(values) {
        sum = 0;
        values.forEach(add);
        return sum;
    }
    for (const f of [viaCall, viaApply, viaBound, viaCallback]) jit.prepare(f);
    viaCall(target);
    viaApply(target);
    viaBound(target.bind(null, 1));
    viaCallback([1, 2]);
    expect(feedbackOf(viaCall, "Call")).toBe(
        "call#0: target=native function call flags=SawNative forwarded by call with 2 arguments to function target returned: Int32"
    );
    expect(feedbackOf(viaApply, "Call")).toBe(
        "call#0: target=native function apply flags=SawNative forwarded by apply with 3 arguments to function target returned: Int32"
    );
    expect(feedbackOf(viaBound, "Call")).toBe(
        "call#0: target=function target flags=SawNative forwarded by bound with 2 arguments to function target returned: Int32"
    );
    expect(feedbackOf(viaCallback, "Call")).toBe(
        "call#0: target=native function forEach flags=SawNative forwarded by callback with 0 arguments to function add returned: none"
    );

    function other(a, b) {
        return a * b;
    }
    viaCall(other);
    expect(feedbackOf(viaCall, "Call")).toBe(
        "call#0: target=native function call flags=SawNative|ForwardedPolymorphic forwarded by call with 2 arguments to function target returned: Int32"
    );
    // NB: The feedback only holds its targets weakly, so `add` stays alive until here.
    expect(add.name).toBe("add");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/profiling-tier.js
// Functions that jit.prepare() moved to the profiling handlers run alongside plain ones. The handlers switch dispatch
// tables whenever they continue in another frame, so every frame runs with the handlers of its own executable.

// Without the JIT nothing is profiled, and the harness's repeated runs of a test would add to what the first run
// recorded, so the body runs once.
function profilingTest(name, body) {
    let ran = false;
    test(name, () => {
        if (!jit.enabled || ran) return;
        ran = true;
        body();
    });
}

profilingTest("calls between profiled and plain functions", () => {
    function plainCallee(a, b) {
        return a * b;
    }
    function profiledCallee(a, b) {
        return a + b;
    }
    function profiledCaller(n) {
        let sum = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) sum += plainCallee(i, 2) + profiledCallee(i, 1);
        return sum;
    }
    function plainCaller(n) {
        let sum = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < n; ++i) sum += profiledCaller(i);
        return sum;
    }
    jit.prepare(profiledCallee);
    jit.prepare(profiledCaller);
    expect(profiledCaller(10)).toBe(145);
    expect(plainCaller(5)).toBe(40);
});

profilingTest("exceptions thrown across profiled and plain frames", () => {
    function thrower(value) {
        if (value > 2) throw new Error(`too big: ${value}`);
        return value;
    }
    function profiledCatcher(value) {
        try {
            return thrower(value);
        } catch (error) {
            return error.message;
        }
    }
    function profiledPasser(value) {
        return thrower(value) + 1;
    }
    jit.prepare(profiledCatcher);
    jit.prepare(profiledPasser);
    expect(profiledCatcher(1)).toBe(1);
    expect(profiledCatcher(3)).toBe("too big: 3");
    expect(() => profiledPasser(4)).toThrowWithMessage(Error, "too big: 4");
    expect(profiledPasser(2)).toBe(3);
});

profilingTest("getters and constructors run as inline frames", () => {
    class Point {
        constructor(x, y) {
            this.x = x;
            this.y = y;
        }
        get length() {
            return Math.abs(this.x) + Math.abs(this.y);
        }
    }
    function make(x, y) {
        return new Point(x, y).length;
    }
    jit.prepare(make);
    jit.prepare(Point);
    expect(make(1, -2)).toBe(3);
    expect(make(-4, 5)).toBe(9);
});

        for (let i = 0; i < limit; ++i) yield i;
    }

        let total = 0;
        for (const value of values) total += await value;
        return total;
    }
    jit.prepare(counter);
    jit.prepare(sum);
    expect([...counter(4)]).toEqual([0, 1, 2, 3]);
    let result;
    sum([1, Promise.resolve(2), 3]).then(value => {
        result = value;
    });
    runQueuedPromiseJobs();
    expect(result).toBe(6);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/property-access-with-shape-changes.js
// Named property gets and puts, compiled after warming up with objects of one shape, then given every other kind of
// receiver: other shapes, prototype properties, accessors, proxies, frozen and dictionary objects, primitives. The
// compiled code must do what the interpreter does (see compareCompiledWithInterpreter in test-common.js).

// Receivers for gets and puts of the property `x`, by name. Each makes a fresh receiver with the call's log.
const receivers = {
    "same shape": (log, i) => ({ x: i, y: 2 }),
    "other order": (log, i) => ({ y: 2, x: i }),
    "more properties": (log, i) => ({ x: i, y: 2, z: 3, w: 4 }),
    "missing property": (log, i) => ({ y: i }),
    "on the prototype": (log, i) => Object.create({ x: i }),
    "deep on the prototype": (log, i) => Object.create(Object.create(Object.create({ x: i }))),
    "own getter": (log, i) => ({
        get x() {
            log.push("get");
            return i * 10;
        },
        set x(value) {
            log.push(`set ${value}`);
        },
    }),
    "getter on the prototype": (log, i) =>
        Object.create({
            get x() {
                log.push("proto get");
                return this.y;
            },
            set x(value) {
                log.push(`proto set ${value}`);
            },
            y: i,
        }),
    "throwing getter": log => ({
        get x() {
            log.push("throw");
            throw new RangeError("getter threw");
        },
        set x(value) {
            throw new RangeError(`setter threw ${value}`);
        },
    }),
    proxy: (log, i) =>
        new Proxy(
            { x: i },
            {
                get(target, key, receiver) {
                    log.push(`proxy get ${String(key)}`);
                    return Reflect.get(target, key, receiver);
                },
                set(target, key, value, receiver) {
                    log.push(`proxy set ${String(key)}`);
                    return Reflect.set(target, key, value, receiver);
                },
            }
        ),
    frozen: (log, i) => Object.freeze({ x: i, y: 2 }),
    sealed: (log, i) => Object.seal({ y: 2 }),
    "non-extensible": (log, i) => Object.preventExtensions({ y: i }),
    "non-writable": (log, i) => Object.defineProperty({ y: 2 }, "x", { value: i, writable: false }),
    "non-writable on the prototype": (log, i) =>
        Object.create(Object.defineProperty({}, "x", { value: i, writable: false })),
    dictionary: (log, i) => {
        const object = { a: 1, b: 2, x: i };
        for (let k = 0; k < 40; ++k) object[`p${k}`] = k;
        delete object.a;
        return object;
    },
    "deleted property": (log, i) => {
        const object = { x: i, y: 2 };
        delete object.x;
        return object;
    },
    "null prototype": (log, i) => Object.assign(Object.create(null), { x: i }),
    array: (log, i) => [i, 2, 3],
    function: () => function x() {},
    string: (log, i) => `string ${i}`,
    number: (log, i) => i + 0.5,
    boolean: () => true,
    symbol: () => Symbol("receiver"),
    bigint: () => 5n,
    undefined: () => undefined,
    null: () => null,
    "class instance": (log, i) =>
        new (class {
            constructor() {
                this.x = i;
            }
        })(),
    "private-looking": (log, i) => ({ ["x"]: i, ["#x"]: 1 }),
};

const probes = {};
for (const [name, make] of Object.entries(receivers)) probes[name] = (log, i) => [make(log, i), log, i];

const warmUp = (log, i) => [{ x: i, y: 2 }, log, i];

describe("named property gets", () => {
    const forms = {
        get: () => object => object.x,
        "get and add": () => object => object.x + object.y,
        "get in a loop": () => object => {
            let sum = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) sum += object.x;
            return sum;
        },
        "get of a method call": () => object => {
            const value = object.x;
            return typeof value === "function" ? value.call(object) : value;
        },
        "optional chaining": () => object => object?.x,
        "get through a helper": () => {
            const read = object => object.x;
            return object => read(object) ?? "nothing";
        },
        in: () => object => (typeof object === "object" && object !== null ? "x" in object : "primitive"),
        hasOwnProperty: () => object =>
            object === null || object === undefined ? "nullish" : Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(object, "x"),
    };
    for (const [name, factory] of Object.entries(forms)) {
        test(name, () => {
            expect(compareCompiledWithInterpreter(factory, { warmUp, probes })).toEqual([]);
        });
    }
});

describe("named property puts", () => {
    const forms = {
        put: () => (object, log, i) => {
            object.x = i;
            return object.x;
        },
        "strict put": () => (object, log, i) => {
            "use strict";
            object.x = i;
            return object.x;
        },
        "put of a new property": () => (object, log, i) => {
            object.added = i;
            return [object.added, object.x];
        },
        increment: () => object => {
            object.x++;
            return object.x;
        },
        "compound assignment": () => (object, log, i) => {
            object.x += i;
            return object.x;
        },
        delete: () => object => {
            const deleted = delete object.x;
            return [deleted, object.x];
        },
    };
    for (const [name, factory] of Object.entries(forms)) {
        test(name, () => {
            expect(compareCompiledWithInterpreter(factory, { warmUp, probes })).toEqual([]);
        });
    }
});

describe("polymorphic receivers", () => {
    test("gets warmed up with two shapes", () => {
        const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(() => object => object.x, {
            warmUp: (log, i) => [i % 2 ? { x: i } : { y: 1, x: i }],
            probes,
        });
        expect(failures).toEqual([]);
    });

    test("gets warmed up with five shapes", () => {
        const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(() => object => object.x, {
            warmUp: (log, i) => {
                const object = { x: i };
                object[`p${i % 5}`] = 1;
                return [object];
            },
            probes,
        });
        expect(failures).toEqual([]);
    });
});

describe("prototype changes after compilation", () => {
    test("a prototype gains a getter", () => {
        const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
            () => {
                const prototype = { x: 1 };
                return (mutate, log) => {
                    if (mutate === 1)
                        Object.defineProperty(prototype, "x", {
                            get() {
                                log.push("getter");
                                return 2;
                            },
                            configurable: true,
                        });
                    if (mutate === 2) Object.defineProperty(prototype, "x", { value: 3, configurable: true });
                    return Object.create(prototype).x;
                };
            },
            {
                warmUp: log => [0, log],
                probes: { getter: log => [1, log], "data again": log => [2, log] },
            }
        );
        expect(failures).toEqual([]);
    });

    test("an object's prototype is replaced", () => {
        const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
            () => {
                const object = Object.create({ x: 1, method: () => "first" });
                return swap => {
                    if (swap) Object.setPrototypeOf(object, { x: 2, method: () => "second" });
                    return [object.x, object.method()];
                };
            },
            { warmUp: () => [false], probes: { swapped: () => [true] } }
        );
        expect(failures).toEqual([]);
    });

    test("a property shadows the prototype's", () => {
        const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
            () => {
                const prototype = { x: 1 };
                const object = Object.create(prototype);
                return shadow => {
                    if (shadow) object.x = 5;
                    return object.x;
                };
            },
            { warmUp: () => [false], probes: { shadowed: () => [true] } }
        );
        expect(failures).toEqual([]);
    });

    test("Object.prototype gains the property", () => {
        const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
            () => (add, log) => {
                const object = { y: 1 };
                if (add) Object.prototype.jitTestProperty = "from Object.prototype";
                try {
                    return object.jitTestProperty;
                } finally {
                    delete Object.prototype.jitTestProperty;
                }
            },
            { warmUp: log => [false, log], probes: { added: log => [true, log] } }
        );
        expect(failures).toEqual([]);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/property-additions.js
// JIT code adds properties to objects it allocated directly, also through
// property caches that saw several shapes. These tests run every function
// many times, so that with a low JIT threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

describe("property additions to allocated objects", () => {
    test("a helper adding a property to objects of several shapes", () => {
        function setName(object, name) {
            object.name = name;
        }
        function makeA(i) {
            const object = { a: i };
            setName(object, "a");
            return object;
        }
        function makeB(i) {
            const object = { b: i, c: 2 };
            setName(object, "bb");
            return object.b + object.c + object.name.length;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const a = makeA(i);
            expect(Object.keys(a)).toEqual(["a", "name"]);
            expect(a.name).toBe("a");
            expect(makeB(i)).toBe(i + 4);
        }
    });

    test("a helper adding a property or writing an existing one", () => {
        function setValue(object, value) {
            object.value = value;
        }
        function fresh(i) {
            const object = {};
            setValue(object, i);
            return object;
        }
        function existing(i) {
            const object = { value: 0 };
            setValue(object, i);
            return object;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(fresh(i)).toEqual({ value: i });
            expect(existing(i)).toEqual({ value: i });
        }
    });

    test("objects other code can see are not assumed unchanged", () => {
        function mutate(object) {
            for (const key of Object.keys(object)) object[key] = key;
            object.extra = true;
        }
        function passed(i) {
            const object = { a: i };
            mutate(object);
            return [object.a, object.extra];
        }
        function throughPhi(i, other) {
            const object = { a: i };
            const either = i % 2 ? object : other;
            mutate(either);
            return object.a;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(passed(i)).toEqual(["a", true]);
            expect(throughPhi(i, {})).toBe(i % 2 ? "a" : i);
        }
    });

    test("exits after additions", () => {
        function setFlag(object) {
            object.flag = true;
        }
        function build(i, reveal) {
            const object = i % 2 ? { odd: i } : { even: i, extra: 0 };
            setFlag(object);
            if (reveal) return reveal(object);
            return object.flag;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(build(i, null)).toBeTrue();
        expect(build(3, object => object)).toEqual({ odd: 3, flag: true });
        expect(build(4, object => object)).toEqual({ even: 4, extra: 0, flag: true });
    });
});

describe("property additions after preventing extensions", () => {
    const lockers = {
        preventExtensions: object => Object.preventExtensions(object),
        reflectPreventExtensions: object => Reflect.preventExtensions(object),
        seal: object => Object.seal(object),
        freeze: object => Object.freeze(object),
    };
    function gatedLockers(lock) {
        const state = { armed: false };
        // Keep the call polymorphic so it is not inlined and its cold locking branch cannot exit the caller.
        const callbacks = [
            object => {
                if (state.armed) lock(object);
            },
            object => {
                if (state.armed) lock(object);
            },
        ];
        return { state, callbacks };
    }

    for (const [name, lock] of Object.entries(lockers)) {
        for (const strict of [false, true]) {
            const directive = strict ? "'use strict';" : "";
            const mode = strict ? "strict" : "sloppy";

            test(`${mode} object literal: ${name}`, () => {
                const { state, callbacks } = gatedLockers(lock);
                const make = new Function(
                    "lock",
                    "p",
                    `${directive} const object = {}; if (p) lock(object); object.x = 1; return object;`
                );
                jit.prepare(make);
                for (let i = 0; i < 50; ++i) make(callbacks[i % 2], true);
                expect(jit.compile(make)).toBe(jit.enabled);

                state.armed = true;
                if (strict) {
                    expect(() => make(callbacks[0], true)).toThrow(TypeError);
                } else {
                    const object = make(callbacks[0], true);
                    expect(Object.hasOwn(object, "x")).toBeFalse();
                    expect(Object.isExtensible(object)).toBeFalse();
                }
                expect(make(lock, false).x).toBe(1);
            });

            test(`${mode} inlined constructor: ${name}`, () => {
                const { state, callbacks } = gatedLockers(lock);
                const Constructor = new Function("lock", "p", `${directive} if (p) lock(this); this.x = 1;`);
                const make = new Function("Constructor", "lock", "p", "return new Constructor(lock, p);");
                jit.prepare(make);
                for (let i = 0; i < 50; ++i) make(Constructor, callbacks[i % 2], true);
                expect(jit.compile(make)).toBe(jit.enabled);

                state.armed = true;
                if (strict) {
                    expect(() => make(Constructor, callbacks[0], true)).toThrow(TypeError);
                } else {
                    const object = make(Constructor, callbacks[0], true);
                    expect(Object.hasOwn(object, "x")).toBeFalse();
                    expect(Object.isExtensible(object)).toBeFalse();
                }
                expect(make(Constructor, lock, false).x).toBe(1);
            });
        }
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/published-frames.js
// Slow paths and calls in inlined callees run in the frames of the inlined calls, which the runtime publishes with
// their headers only: their function, `this`, arguments and position. Frames that do not continue are written in
// full.

function callsValue(value) {
    return value();
}

function callsCallsValue(value) {
    return callsValue(value);
}

const callees = [() => 1, () => 2, () => 3, () => 4];

test("calls that throw in inlined callees show every frame", () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; ++i) expect(callsCallsValue(callees[i % callees.length])).toBe((i % callees.length) + 1);
    let stack = "";
    try {
        callsCallsValue(5);
    } catch (error) {
        stack = error.stack;
    }
    expect(stack.includes("at callsValue (")).toBeTrue();
    expect(stack.includes("at callsCallsValue (")).toBeTrue();
});

test("calls in inlined callees see their callers at their call sites", () => {
    const stackOfCaller = () => new Error().stack;
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; ++i) {
        const stack = callsCallsValue(i % 2 ? stackOfCaller : () => new Error().stack);
        expect(stack.includes("at callsValue (")).toBeTrue();
        expect(/at callsCallsValue \(.*:10:\d+\)/.test(stack)).toBeTrue();
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/regexp-exec-builtin.js
// JIT code calls RegExp.prototype.exec through its runtime helper where
// RegExpBuiltinExec runs no code, and calls the function for anything else.

function compileCalls(f, ...args) {
    jit.prepare(f);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) f(...args);
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return f;
}

describe("RegExp.prototype.exec in JIT code", () => {
    test("matches, captures and misses", () => {
        const exec = compileCalls((re, s) => re.exec(s), /(a)(b)?/, "xa");
        let match = exec(/(a)(b)?/, "xab");
        expect(match).toEqual(["ab", "a", "b"]);
        expect(match.index).toBe(1);
        expect(match.input).toBe("xab");
        match = exec(/(a)(b)?/, "xa");
        expect(match[2]).toBeUndefined();
        expect(exec(/a/, "zzz")).toBeNull();
        expect(exec(/(?<letter>[a-z])/, "1q").groups.letter).toBe("q");
        expect(RegExp.$1).toBe("q");
        expect(jit.exitCount(exec)).toBe(0);
    });

    test("global and sticky regular expressions update lastIndex", () => {
        const exec = compileCalls((re, s) => re.exec(s), /a/g, "aa");
        const global = /a/g;
        expect(exec(global, "aba").index).toBe(0);
        expect(global.lastIndex).toBe(1);
        expect(exec(global, "aba").index).toBe(2);
        expect(global.lastIndex).toBe(3);
        expect(exec(global, "aba")).toBeNull();
        expect(global.lastIndex).toBe(0);
        const sticky = /a/y;
        sticky.lastIndex = 1;
        expect(exec(sticky, "aba")).toBeNull();
        expect(sticky.lastIndex).toBe(0);
        global.lastIndex = 100;
        expect(exec(global, "aba")).toBeNull();
        expect(global.lastIndex).toBe(0);
        const nonGlobal = /a/;
        nonGlobal.lastIndex = 2;
        expect(exec(nonGlobal, "aba").index).toBe(0);
        expect(nonGlobal.lastIndex).toBe(2);
    });

    test("observable lastIndex values go through the function", () => {
        const exec = compileCalls((re, s) => re.exec(s), /a/g, "aa");
        const regexp = /a/g;
        let conversions = 0;
        regexp.lastIndex = {
            valueOf() {
                ++conversions;
                return 1;
            },
        };
        expect(exec(regexp, "aa").index).toBe(1);
        expect(conversions).toBe(1);
        expect(regexp.lastIndex).toBe(2);
        const frozen = /a/g;
        Object.freeze(frozen);
        expect(() => exec(frozen, "a")).toThrow(TypeError);
        const readOnly = /a/g;
        Object.defineProperty(readOnly, "lastIndex", { writable: false });
        expect(() => exec(readOnly, "a")).toThrow(TypeError);
        const extended = /a/g;
        extended.extra = 1;
        expect(exec(extended, "aa").index).toBe(0);
        expect(extended.lastIndex).toBe(1);
        const frozenNonGlobal = Object.freeze(/a/);
        expect(exec(frozenNonGlobal, "a").index).toBe(0);
    });

    test("other receivers and arguments go through the function", () => {
        const exec = compileCalls((re, s) => re.exec(s), /a/, "a");
        expect(exec(/1/, 1).index).toBe(0);
        expect(() => exec({ exec: RegExp.prototype.exec }, "a")).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(exec({ exec: () => "own" }, "a")).toBe("own");
        const execCall = compileCalls((re, s) => RegExp.prototype.exec.call(re, s), /a/, "a");
        expect(() => execCall("not a regexp", "a")).toThrow(TypeError);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/regress/catch-blocks-after-stack-overflows.js
// JIT code recurses on the native stack, unlike the interpreter. When it ran into the native stack limit, the catch
// block of the deepest frame called a native function with no stack left, which threw another stack overflow into the
// next frame's catch block, and so on for thousands of frames, each error capturing a stack trace thousands of frames
// deep. JIT code leaves headroom below the native stack limit for such code now.

test("the catch block that handles a stack overflow can call native functions", () => {
    const re = /\w/;
    let caught = 0;
    function recurse() {
        try {
            return recurse();
        } catch (e) {
            ++caught;
            return re.test("b");
        }
    }
    expect(recurse()).toBeTrue();
    // NB: The interpreter runs the catch blocks of the two deepest frames: the native call in the deepest one finds
    //     no interpreter stack left either.
    expect(caught).toBeLessThanOrEqual(2);
});

test("stack overflows in compiled code are still RangeErrors", () => {
    function recurse(depth) {
        return recurse(depth + 1) + 1;
    }
    expect(() => recurse(0)).toThrowWithMessage(InternalError, "Call stack size limit exceeded");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/regress/deep-recursion-exits.js
// Unwinding a deep recursion that catches the stack overflow exits compiled code in every frame, at an addition that
// never ran before. Each exit looked for the frames its code remembered among all live frames, one stack walk per
// remembered frame, so measuring the stack depth like this took minutes.

test("measuring the stack depth with a recursion that catches the stack overflow finishes", () => {
    function depth(warm) {
        if (warm) return 0;
        try {
            return 1 + depth(false);
        } catch {
            return 1;
        }
    }
    jit.prepare(depth);
    depth(true);
    expect(jit.compile(depth)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(depth(false)).toBeGreaterThan(1000);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/regress/inlined-closures-sharing-an-executable.js
// A function created in an inlined call of a closure must get that closure's environment, even where another closure
// of the same function is inlined in the same compiled code.

function make(prefix, suffix) {
    return function (value) {
        const join = suffix ? rest => `${prefix}/${suffix}/${rest}` : null;
        return join ? join(value) : `${prefix}/-/${value}`;
    };
}

test("closures of one function inlined in one caller", () => {
    const callees = { plain: make("plain"), withSuffix: make("with", "suffix") };
    function caller(value) {
        if (value === undefined) return callees.plain("x");
        return callees.withSuffix(value);
    }
    jit.prepare(caller);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
        expect(caller()).toBe("plain/-/x");
        expect(caller("y")).toBe("with/suffix/y");
    }
    jit.compile(caller);
    expect(caller()).toBe("plain/-/x");
    expect(caller("y")).toBe("with/suffix/y");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/regress/lazy-lengths-and-names-in-has-property-checks.js
// A compiled `in` or `hasOwnProperty` check of a function's `length` or `name` must not lose code or corrupt objects.

function makeCallee(parameters, body) {
    return new Function("pad", ...parameters, `if (pad === 1) { ${"pad = pad + 1; ".repeat(100)}} ${body}`);
}

function makeTarget() {
    const target = function target() {};
    target.a = 1;
    target.b = 2;
    return target;
}

function testCheck(check, key) {
    const callee = makeCallee(
        ["target", "key", "object", "hasOwnProperty"],
        `const a = target.a; const result = ${check}; target.b = 3; return [result, a, object.name];`
    );
    const caller = (target, key, object) => callee(undefined, target, key, object, Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty);
    jit.prepare(callee);
    jit.prepare(caller);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) expect(caller(makeTarget(), "c", { name: "first" })).toEqual([false, 1, "first"]);
    jit.compile(callee);
    jit.compile(caller);
    const target = makeTarget();
    expect(caller(target, key, { other: 1, name: "second" })).toEqual([true, 1, "second"]);
    expect(target.b).toBe(3);
    expect(target.length).toBe(0);
    expect(target.name).toBe("target");
}

test("in", () => {
    testCheck("key in target", "length");
    testCheck("key in target", "name");
});

test("hasOwnProperty", () => {
    testCheck("hasOwnProperty.call(target, key)", "length");
    testCheck("hasOwnProperty.call(target, key)", "name");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/regress/lazy-prototypes-in-has-property-checks.js
// Checking whether a function has a `prototype` creates the prototype the first time. If the function is the
// prototype of another object, this throws away compiled code that reads properties of that object. A compiled
// function that runs such a check must keep its code. The callee has an unused branch so that it is too large to
// inline, and the caller calls it directly. It gets `hasOwnProperty` as a parameter, because looking up `Object` in
// it would register its frame early and hide the bug. The last call passes an object of another shape, so that the
// callee falls back to the interpreter after the check, which fails if its code is gone.

function makeCallee(parameters, body) {
    return new Function("pad", ...parameters, `if (pad === 1) { ${"pad = pad + 1; ".repeat(16)}} ${body}`);
}

function testPrototypeCheck(check) {
    const callee = makeCallee(["target", "object", "hasOwnProperty"], `return [${check}, object.name];`);
    const caller = (target, object) => callee(undefined, target, object, Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty);
    const target = function target() {};
    const object = Object.create(target);
    jit.prepare(callee);
    jit.prepare(caller);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) expect(caller({}, object)).toEqual([false, "target"]);
    jit.compile(callee);
    jit.compile(caller);
    expect(caller(target, { name: "other" })).toEqual([true, "other"]);
}

test("in", () => {
    testPrototypeCheck(`"prototype" in target`);
});

test("hasOwnProperty", () => {
    testPrototypeCheck(`hasOwnProperty.call(target, "prototype")`);
});

// Compiled code allocating an object literal must store the last of several initializations of the same property:
// `{ a: 1, a: 2, a: 3 }` has `a === 3`, and `{ a: x, a: 3 }` has `a === 3`.
