FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/regress/slow-path-inputs-in-the-output-register.js
// A slow path call whose output register also holds one of its inputs must pass the slow path that input, not another
// one: `p >>> v1` with `p` an object must not call the slow path with `p` for both operands, which made the loop take
// the wrong branch on its first iteration.

test("slow path calls pass inputs that share the output register", () => {
    const out = [];
    class Shape0 {}
    function f0(p) {
        let v0 = new Shape0();
        let v1 = ((p !== p) | v0) >> (p * p == "x" in Object(v0));
        for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
            if ((p >>> v1) * ((v1 ^ 0) <= p - -2147483648)) {
                out.push("t" + i);
            } else {
                out.push(arguments.length);
                p *= (v1 - i != typeof v0) / (p | 0);
            }
        }
    }
    jit.prepare(f0);
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; ++i) f0(new Shape0());
    jit.compile(f0);
    out.length = 0;
    f0({
        valueOf() {
            return 4;
        },
    });
    expect(out).toEqual(["t0", "t1", "t2"]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/regress/slow-path-outputs-in-callee-saved-registers.js
// A slow path call whose output register is preserved by calls and also holds one of its inputs must leave spilled
// values intact. The null checks fill every register, even with two more on AArch64, and put `x` in one that calls
// preserve. The later slow paths of `aN + 1` keep the values in use, so that `x + 1` reuses the register of `x`. The
// result is joined because the comparison only checks the first 16 elements of an array.

test("slow path calls keep spilled values when their output register is preserved by calls", () => {
    const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
        () => {
            const names = Array.from({ length: 26 }, (_, i) => `a${i}`);
            const checks = [...names.slice(0, 18), "x", ...names.slice(18)].map(
                name => `if (${name} === null) return 0;`
            );
            const results = names.map(name => `${name} + 1`);
            return new Function("x", ...names, `${checks.join("\n")} const y = x + 1; return [${results}, y].join();`);
        },
        {
            warmUp: (log, i) => Array(27).fill(i % 3 ? i : { valueOf: () => 5 }),
            probes: { object: () => [{ valueOf: () => 5 }, ...Array.from({ length: 26 }, (_, i) => i + 1)] },
        }
    );
    expect(failures).toEqual([]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/short-string-concatenation.js
// JIT code finds the results of short string concatenations in the VM's
// cache of strings, and the strings of small integers it concatenates in the
// VM's cache of those. These tests run every function many times, so that with
// a low JIT threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

function concatenate(a, b) {
    return a + b;
}

describe("Short string concatenation in JIT code", () => {
    test("results up to and beyond the short string length", () => {
        const pieces = ["a", "bc", "def", "ghij", "klmno", "pqrstu", "vwxyz12"];
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            for (const a of pieces) {
                for (const b of pieces) {
                    const result = concatenate(a, b);
                    expect(result).toBe(a + b);
                    expect(result.length).toBe(a.length + b.length);
                    expect(result.charCodeAt(a.length)).toBe(b.charCodeAt(0));
                }
            }
        }
    });

    test("strings beyond ASCII, empty strings and other values", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(concatenate("é", "t")).toBe("ét");
            expect(concatenate("t", "é")).toBe("té");
            expect(concatenate("", "ab")).toBe("ab");
            expect(concatenate("ab", "")).toBe("ab");
            expect(concatenate("on", "click")).toBe("onclick");
            expect(concatenate("x", i % 10)).toBe("x" + (i % 10));
            expect(concatenate(i % 10, "_d")).toBe((i % 10) + "_d");
            expect(concatenate("a", null)).toBe("anull");
        }
    });

    test("results used as property keys and compared", () => {
        const object = { onclick: 1, onfocus: 2 };
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const type = i % 2 ? "click" : "focus";
            expect(object[concatenate("on", type)]).toBe(i % 2 ? 1 : 2);
            expect(concatenate("on", type) === "on" + type).toBeTrue();
        }
    });

    test("integers and strings", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations * 20; ++i) {
            const n = i % 2000;
            expect(concatenate(n, "_d")).toBe(String(n) + "_d");
            expect(concatenate("item", n)).toBe("item" + String(n));
            expect(concatenate("", n)).toBe(String(n));
            expect(concatenate(n, "")).toBe(String(n));
            expect(concatenate(-n, "x")).toBe(String(-n) + "x");
            expect(concatenate(n, n)).toBe(2 * n);
            expect(concatenate(n + 0.5, "x")).toBe(String(n + 0.5) + "x");
        }
        expect(concatenate(2147483647, 1)).toBe(2147483648);
        expect(concatenate("x", 2147483647)).toBe("x2147483647");
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/slow-paths-on-values.js
// Compiled code runs the slow paths of instructions and generic calls on SSA values: the operands are inputs, the
// outputs are values, and the frame only gets what it needs where the slow path does not continue.

test("slow paths with several outputs", () => {
    const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
        () => {
            return values => {
                let sum = 0;
                for (const value of values) sum += value;
                const [first, second] = values;
                return [sum, first, second];
            };
        },
        {
            warmUp: (log, i) => [[i, 1, 2]],
            probes: { double: () => [[0.5, 1]], string: () => [["s", 1]], empty: () => [[]] },
        }
    );
    expect(failures).toEqual([]);
});

test("slow paths that read and write their output", () => {
    const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
        () => {
            return (a, b) => `${a}-${b}-${a + b}`;
        },
        { warmUp: (log, i) => [i, i + 1], probes: { double: () => [0.5, 1], string: () => ["x", "y"] } }
    );
    expect(failures).toEqual([]);
});

test("a call that throws leaves its destination's old value for the handler", () => {
    const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
        () => {
            function maybeThrow(value) {
                if (value > 100) throw new RangeError(`too big: ${value}`);
                return value * 2;
            }
            return value => {
                let result = 1;
                try {
                    result = maybeThrow(value);
                } catch (e) {
                    return [result, e.message];
                }
                return [result];
            };
        },
        { warmUp: (log, i) => [i], probes: { throws: () => [200], double: () => [0.5] } }
    );
    expect(failures).toEqual([]);
});

test("calls with many operands and constant arguments, also in inlined callees", () => {
    const failures = compareCompiledWithInterpreter(
        () => {
            function wide(a, b, c, d, e, f) {
                return [a, b, c, d, e, f].join(",");
            }
            function make(message) {
                return new TypeError(message + " with a constant");
            }
            function inlined(value) {
                return [
                    wide(value, 1, "two", 3, value, undefined),
                    make("made").message,
                    new RangeError("constant").message,
                ];
            }
            return value => inlined(value);
        },
        { warmUp: (log, i) => [i], probes: { double: () => [0.5], string: () => ["s"] } }
    );
    expect(failures).toEqual([]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/stable-shapes.js
// JIT code assumes that objects keep stable shapes (shapes no object has
// left yet) while it calls other code, and is invalidated when an object
// leaves one.
// These tests run every function many times, so that with a low JIT
// threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

describe("stable shapes in JIT code", () => {
    test("objects that gain properties during a call", () => {
        function make() {
            return { a: 1, b: 2 };
        }
        function sum(object, call) {
            const before = object.a;
            call(object);
            return before + object.a + object.b;
        }
        const leave = object => {
            object.c = 3;
        };
        const stay = () => {};
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(sum(make(), stay)).toBe(4);
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(sum(make(), leave)).toBe(4);
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(sum(make(), stay)).toBe(4);
    });

    test("objects whose properties are deleted during a call", () => {
        function make() {
            return { first: 1, second: 2, third: 3 };
        }
        function read(object, call) {
            const first = object.first;
            call(object);
            return [first, object.second, object.third];
        }
        const remove = object => {
            delete object.first;
        };
        const stay = () => {};
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(read(make(), stay)).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(read(make(), remove)).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
    });

    test("objects that become dictionaries during a call", () => {
        function make() {
            return { x: 10, y: 20 };
        }
        function read(object, call) {
            const x = object.x;
            call(object);
            return x + object.y;
        }
        const grow = object => {
            for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) object["key" + i] = i;
            delete object.key0;
            object.y = 5;
        };
        const stay = () => {};
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(read(make(), stay)).toBe(30);
        expect(read(make(), grow)).toBe(15);
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(read(make(), stay)).toBe(30);
    });

    test("objects whose prototype changes during a call", () => {
        const proto = {
            get value() {
                return "prototype";
            },
        };
        function make() {
            return { own: 1 };
        }
        function read(object, call) {
            const own = object.own;
            call(object);
            return own + ":" + object.own + ":" + object.value;
        }
        const reparent = object => {
            Object.setPrototypeOf(object, proto);
        };
        const stay = () => {};
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(read(make(), stay)).toBe("1:1:undefined");
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(read(make(), reparent)).toBe("1:1:prototype");
    });

    test("loops whose calls change objects late", () => {
        function make() {
            return { count: 0, step: 1 };
        }
        function run(object, call) {
            let total = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < 200; ++i) {
                total += object.step;
                call(object, i);
            }
            return total + object.count;
        }
        const change = (object, i) => {
            if (i === 150) {
                object.extra = true;
                object.step = 2;
            }
        };
        const stay = () => {};
        for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i) expect(run(make(), stay)).toBe(200);
        expect(run(make(), change)).toBe(151 + 49 * 2);
        for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i) expect(run(make(), stay)).toBe(200);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/string-character-builtins.js
// JIT code reads characters for String.prototype.charCodeAt and charAt
// calls inline. These tests run every function many times, so that with a
// low JIT threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

function codes(string) {
    const result = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < string.length; ++i) result.push(string.charCodeAt(i));
    return result;
}

function characters(string) {
    const result = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < string.length; ++i) result.push(string.charAt(i));
    return result;
}

function codeAt(string, index) {
    return string.charCodeAt(index);
}

function characterAt(string, index) {
    return string.charAt(index);
}

describe("charCodeAt and charAt in JIT code", () => {
    test("short, long and wide strings", () => {
        const long = "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog";
        const wide = "aé中😀z";
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(codes("abc")).toEqual([97, 98, 99]);
            expect(characters("abc")).toEqual(["a", "b", "c"]);
            expect(String.fromCharCode(...codes(long))).toBe(long);
            expect(characters(long).join("")).toBe(long);
            expect(codes(wide)).toEqual([0x61, 0xe9, 0x4e2d, 0xd83d, 0xde00, 0x7a]);
            expect(characters(wide)).toEqual(["a", "é", "中", "\ud83d", "\ude00", "z"]);
            const rope = "prefix-" + i;
            expect(characters(rope).join("")).toBe(rope);
        }
    });

    test("indices outside the string and of other types", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(codeAt("abc", 3)).toBeNaN();
            expect(codeAt("abc", -1)).toBeNaN();
            expect(codeAt("abc", 1.5)).toBe(98);
            expect(codeAt("abc", "2")).toBe(99);
            expect(codeAt("abc", undefined)).toBe(97);
            expect(characterAt("abc", 3)).toBe("");
            expect(characterAt("abc", -1)).toBe("");
            expect(characterAt("abc", 1.5)).toBe("b");
            expect(characterAt("abc", {})).toBe("a");
        }
    });

    test("other this values and replaced builtins", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(codeAt(new String("xyz"), 1)).toBe(121);
            expect(characterAt(new String("xyz"), 1)).toBe("y");
            expect(codeAt({ charCodeAt: index => index * 2 }, 21)).toBe(42);
            expect(characterAt({ charAt: () => "mine" }, 0)).toBe("mine");
        }
        expect(() => codeAt(undefined, 0)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(() => String.prototype.charCodeAt.call(null, 0)).toThrow(TypeError);

        const original = String.prototype.charCodeAt;
        String.prototype.charCodeAt = function (index) {
            return `replaced ${index}`;
        };
        try {
            expect(codeAt("abc", 1)).toBe("replaced 1");
        } finally {
            String.prototype.charCodeAt = original;
        }
        expect(codeAt("abc", 1)).toBe(98);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/string-characters.js
// JIT code reads the characters of strings by index inline. These tests run
// every function many times, so that with a low JIT threshold they are
// compiled.

const iterations = 100;

function at(string, index) {
    return string[index];
}

function characters(string) {
    const result = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < string.length; ++i) result.push(string[i]);
    return result;
}

describe("String characters in JIT code", () => {
    test("short and long strings", () => {
        const long = "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog";
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(characters("abc")).toEqual(["a", "b", "c"]);
            expect(characters(long).join("")).toBe(long);
            expect(at(long, i % long.length)).toBe(long.charAt(i % long.length));
        }
    });

    test("characters beyond ASCII", () => {
        const string = "aé中😀z";
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(characters(string)).toEqual(["a", "é", "中", "\ud83d", "\ude00", "z"]);
        }
    });

    test("strings made at run time", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const rope = "prefix-" + i + "-suffix";
            expect(at(rope, 7)).toBe(String(i)[0]);
            expect(characters(rope).join("")).toBe(rope);
            const slice = rope.slice(1, 5);
            expect(at(slice, 0)).toBe("r");
        }
    });

    test("indices outside the string", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(at("abc", 3)).toBeUndefined();
            expect(at("abc", -1)).toBeUndefined();
            expect(at("abc", 1.5)).toBeUndefined();
            expect(at("abc", 1)).toBe("b");
            expect(at("abc", "1")).toBe("b");
            expect(at("abc", "length")).toBe(3);
        }
        String.prototype[3] = "from the prototype";
        try {
            expect(at("abc", 3)).toBe("from the prototype");
            expect(at("abc", 2)).toBe("c");
        } finally {
            delete String.prototype[3];
        }
        expect(at("abc", 3)).toBeUndefined();
    });

    test("other bases", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(at(new String("xyz"), 1)).toBe("y");
            expect(at(["x", "y"], 1)).toBe("y");
            expect(at(5, 0)).toBeUndefined();
        }
        expect(() => at(undefined, 0)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(() => at(null, 0)).toThrow(TypeError);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/string-concatenation.js
// JIT code concatenates two strings into a rope string inline. These tests run
// every function many times, so that with a low JIT threshold they are
// compiled after seeing strings.

const iterations = 100;

describe("string concatenation in JIT code", () => {
    test("ropes, empty strings and short strings", () => {
        function concatenate(a, b) {
            return a + b;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const long = concatenate("a fairly long string ", "and another one " + i);
            expect(long).toBe("a fairly long string and another one " + i);
            expect(long.length).toBe(37 + String(i).length);
            expect(concatenate("", "right")).toBe("right");
            expect(concatenate("left", "")).toBe("left");
            expect(concatenate("", "")).toBe("");
            expect(concatenate("ab", "cd")).toBe("abcd");
            expect(concatenate("été ", "et hiver, saisons longues")).toBe("été et hiver, saisons longues");
            expect(concatenate(1, 2)).toBe(3);
            expect(concatenate(1.5, "x")).toBe("1.5x");
            expect(concatenate("x", { toString: () => "y" })).toBe("xy");
        }
    });

    test("ropes of ropes, with collections in between", () => {
        function append(buffer, piece) {
            buffer += piece;
            return buffer;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            let buffer = "";
            let expected = "";
            for (let j = 0; j < 20; ++j) {
                const piece = '<li data-id="' + j + '">item ' + i + "</li>";
                buffer = append(buffer, piece);
                expected = expected.concat(piece);
                if (j % 7 === 0) gc();
            }
            expect(buffer).toBe(expected);
            expect(buffer.length).toBe(expected.length);
            expect(buffer.charCodeAt(buffer.length - 1)).toBe(62);
        }
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/string-equality.js
// JIT code compares strings by their lengths and, for short strings, their
// contents inline. These tests run every function many times, so that with
// a low JIT threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

function equals(a, b) {
    return a === b;
}

function looselyEquals(a, b) {
    return a == b;
}

function differs(a, b) {
    return a !== b;
}

function made(...parts) {
    return parts.join("");
}

describe("String equality in JIT code", () => {
    test("strings made at run time", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            const short = made("a", "b", String(i % 10));
            expect(equals(short, "ab" + (i % 10))).toBeTrue();
            expect(equals(short, "ab" + ((i + 1) % 10))).toBeFalse();
            expect(differs(short, "ab" + (i % 10))).toBeFalse();
            expect(looselyEquals(short, "ab" + (i % 10))).toBeTrue();
            expect(equals(short, "abc" + i)).toBeFalse();

            const long = made("a longer string ", String(i));
            expect(equals(long, "a longer string " + i)).toBeTrue();
            expect(equals(long, "a longer strinG " + i)).toBeFalse();
            expect(equals(long, "a longer string " + i + "!")).toBeFalse();

            const rope = "left part " + i + " right part";
            expect(equals(rope, made("left part ", String(i), " right part"))).toBeTrue();
            expect(equals(rope, "left part " + i + " right parT")).toBeFalse();
        }
    });

    test("strings beyond ASCII and empty strings", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(equals(made("é", "té"), "été")).toBeTrue();
            expect(equals(made("é", "té"), "eté")).toBeFalse();
            expect(equals(made("ab", "c"), made("a", "bc"))).toBeTrue();
            expect(equals(made(""), "")).toBeTrue();
            expect(equals(made(""), "x")).toBeFalse();
            expect(equals(made("x"), made("x"))).toBeTrue();
        }
    });

    test("strings and other values", () => {
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(equals("1", 1)).toBeFalse();
            expect(looselyEquals("1", 1)).toBeTrue();
            expect(equals(made("ab"), { toString: () => "ab" })).toBeFalse();
            expect(looselyEquals(made("ab"), { toString: () => "ab" })).toBeTrue();
            expect(equals(made("null"), null)).toBeFalse();
        }
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/string-prototype-builtins.js
// JIT code calls String.prototype builtins like indexOf, slice and trim
// through their runtime helpers without a native frame for strings and int32
// positions, and calls the functions for anything else.

function compileCalls(f, ...args) {
    jit.prepare(f);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) f(...args);
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return f;
}

describe("String.prototype builtins in JIT code", () => {
    test("indexOf of strings", () => {
        const indexOf = compileCalls((s, t) => s.indexOf(t), "abc", "b");
        const indexOfFrom = compileCalls((s, t, p) => s.indexOf(t, p), "abcabc", "b", 2);
        expect(indexOf("hello", "l")).toBe(2);
        expect(indexOf("hello", "z")).toBe(-1);
        expect(indexOf("hello", "")).toBe(0);
        expect(indexOf("", "a")).toBe(-1);
        expect(indexOf("aé中😀z", "😀")).toBe(3);
        expect(indexOf("prefix-" + indexOf.length, "-1")).toBe(-1);
        expect(indexOf("prefix-" + 12, "-1")).toBe(6);
        expect(indexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", 2)).toBe(4);
        expect(indexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", -5)).toBe(1);
        expect(indexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", 100)).toBe(-1);
        expect(indexOfFrom("abc", "", 100)).toBe(3);
        expect(jit.exitCount(indexOf)).toBe(0);
        expect(jit.exitCount(indexOfFrom)).toBe(0);
    });

    test("indexOf of other values", () => {
        const indexOf = compileCalls((s, t) => s.indexOf(t), "abc", "b");
        const indexOfFrom = compileCalls((s, t, p) => s.indexOf(t, p), "abcabc", "b", 2);
        expect(indexOf("a1b", 1)).toBe(1);
        expect(indexOf("an undefined", undefined)).toBe(3);
        expect(indexOf(new String("abc"), "c")).toBe(2);
        expect(() => indexOf(null, "a")).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(indexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", 1.5)).toBe(1);
        expect(indexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", "3")).toBe(4);
        expect(indexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", undefined)).toBe(1);
        expect(indexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", Infinity)).toBe(-1);
        expect(indexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", -Infinity)).toBe(1);
        let conversions = 0;
        const counted = {
            toString() {
                ++conversions;
                return "c";
            },
        };
        expect(indexOf("abc", counted)).toBe(2);
        expect(conversions).toBe(1);
    });

    test("toLowerCase and toUpperCase of strings", () => {
        const lower = compileCalls(s => s.toLowerCase(), "ABC");
        const upper = compileCalls(s => s.toUpperCase(), "abc");
        expect(lower("HeLLo")).toBe("hello");
        expect(upper("HeLLo")).toBe("HELLO");
        expect(lower("")).toBe("");
        expect(upper("ß")).toBe("SS");
        expect(lower("İ")).toBe("i̇");
        expect(lower("ÀÉÎ")).toBe("àéî");
        expect(upper("rope-" + lower.length)).toBe("ROPE-1");
        expect(jit.exitCount(lower)).toBe(0);
        expect(jit.exitCount(upper)).toBe(0);
    });

    test("toLowerCase and toUpperCase of other values", () => {
        const lower = compileCalls(s => s.toLowerCase(), "ABC");
        const upper = compileCalls(s => s.toUpperCase(), "abc");
        expect(lower(new String("ABC"))).toBe("abc");
        expect(() => upper(undefined)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(lower({ toLowerCase: () => "own" })).toBe("own");
    });

    test("lastIndexOf, includes, startsWith and endsWith of strings", () => {
        const lastIndexOf = compileCalls((s, t) => s.lastIndexOf(t), "abcabc", "b");
        const lastIndexOfFrom = compileCalls((s, t, p) => s.lastIndexOf(t, p), "abcabc", "b", 3);
        const includes = compileCalls((s, t) => s.includes(t), "abc", "b");
        const includesFrom = compileCalls((s, t, p) => s.includes(t, p), "abc", "b", 1);
        const startsWith = compileCalls((s, t) => s.startsWith(t), "abc", "a");
        const startsWithAt = compileCalls((s, t, p) => s.startsWith(t, p), "abc", "b", 1);
        const endsWith = compileCalls((s, t) => s.endsWith(t), "abc", "c");
        const endsWithAt = compileCalls((s, t, p) => s.endsWith(t, p), "abc", "b", 2);
        expect(lastIndexOf("abcabc", "b")).toBe(4);
        expect(lastIndexOf("abcabc", "z")).toBe(-1);
        expect(lastIndexOf("abc", "")).toBe(3);
        expect(lastIndexOf("ab", "abc")).toBe(-1);
        expect(lastIndexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", 3)).toBe(1);
        expect(lastIndexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", -1)).toBe(-1);
        expect(lastIndexOfFrom("abcabc", "a", -1)).toBe(0);
        expect(lastIndexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", 2147483647)).toBe(4);
        expect(includes("hello", "ell")).toBeTrue();
        expect(includes("hello", "")).toBeTrue();
        expect(includes("hello", "x")).toBeFalse();
        expect(includesFrom("hello", "h", 1)).toBeFalse();
        expect(includesFrom("hello", "h", -3)).toBeTrue();
        expect(startsWith("hello", "he")).toBeTrue();
        expect(startsWith("hello", "hello!")).toBeFalse();
        expect(startsWithAt("hello", "lo", 3)).toBeTrue();
        expect(startsWithAt("hello", "", 100)).toBeTrue();
        expect(endsWith("hello", "lo")).toBeTrue();
        expect(endsWith("hello", "he")).toBeFalse();
        expect(endsWithAt("hello", "he", 2)).toBeTrue();
        expect(endsWithAt("hello", "lo", 2147483647)).toBeTrue();
        expect(endsWithAt("hello", "h", -5)).toBeFalse();
        for (const f of [
            lastIndexOf,
            lastIndexOfFrom,
            includes,
            includesFrom,
            startsWith,
            startsWithAt,
            endsWith,
            endsWithAt,
        ])
            expect(jit.exitCount(f)).toBe(0);
    });

    test("lastIndexOf, includes, startsWith and endsWith of other values", () => {
        const lastIndexOfFrom = compileCalls((s, t, p) => s.lastIndexOf(t, p), "abcabc", "b", 3);
        const includes = compileCalls((s, t) => s.includes(t), "abc", "b");
        const startsWithAt = compileCalls((s, t, p) => s.startsWith(t, p), "abc", "b", 1);
        const endsWith = compileCalls((s, t) => s.endsWith(t), "abc", "c");
        expect(lastIndexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", NaN)).toBe(4);
        expect(lastIndexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", undefined)).toBe(4);
        expect(lastIndexOfFrom("abcabc", "b", 3.9)).toBe(1);
        expect(includes("a1", 1)).toBeTrue();
        expect(() => includes("abc", /b/)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(() => endsWith("abc", /c/)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(startsWithAt("abc", "b", "1")).toBeTrue();
        expect(startsWithAt("abc", "a", -Infinity)).toBeTrue();
        expect(endsWith(new String("abc"), "c")).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("slice and substring of strings", () => {
        const slice = compileCalls((s, a, b) => s.slice(a, b), "abcdef", 1, 3);
        const sliceFrom = compileCalls((s, a) => s.slice(a), "abcdef", 1);
        const sliceAll = compileCalls(s => s.slice(), "abcdef");
        const substring = compileCalls((s, a, b) => s.substring(a, b), "abcdef", 1, 3);
        const substringFrom = compileCalls((s, a) => s.substring(a), "abcdef", 1);
        expect(slice("abcdef", 1, 3)).toBe("bc");
        expect(slice("abcdef", -3, -1)).toBe("de");
        expect(slice("abcdef", 4, 2)).toBe("");
        expect(slice("abcdef", -100, 100)).toBe("abcdef");
        expect(slice("abcdef", 2, 2147483647)).toBe("cdef");
        expect(slice("aé中😀z", 3, 5)).toBe("😀");
        expect(sliceFrom("abcdef", -2)).toBe("ef");
        expect(sliceAll("abc")).toBe("abc");
        expect(substring("abcdef", 1, 3)).toBe("bc");
        expect(substring("abcdef", 3, 1)).toBe("bc");
        expect(substring("abcdef", -3, 2)).toBe("ab");
        expect(substring("abcdef", 2, 2147483647)).toBe("cdef");
        expect(substringFrom("abcdef", 4)).toBe("ef");
        expect(substringFrom("rope-" + slice.length, 2)).toBe("pe-3");
        for (const f of [slice, sliceFrom, sliceAll, substring, substringFrom]) expect(jit.exitCount(f)).toBe(0);
    });

    test("slice and substring of other values", () => {
        const slice = compileCalls((s, a, b) => s.slice(a, b), "abcdef", 1, 3);
        const substring = compileCalls((s, a, b) => s.substring(a, b), "abcdef", 1, 3);
        expect(slice("abcdef", 1.5, 3.5)).toBe("bc");
        expect(slice("abcdef", 1, undefined)).toBe("bcdef");
        expect(slice("abcdef", -Infinity, Infinity)).toBe("abcdef");
        expect(slice([1, 2, 3], 1, 2)).toEqual([2]);
        expect(substring("abcdef", "1", NaN)).toBe("a");
        expect(substring(new String("12345"), 1, 3)).toBe("23");
    });

    test("trim, trimStart and trimEnd of strings", () => {
        const trim = compileCalls(s => s.trim(), " a ");
        const trimStart = compileCalls(s => s.trimStart(), " a ");
        const trimEnd = compileCalls(s => s.trimEnd(), " a ");
        expect(trim("  a b  ")).toBe("a b");
        expect(trim("ab")).toBe("ab");
        expect(trim("   ")).toBe("");
        expect(trim("\t\n\u00a0\ufeffx\u2028")).toBe("x");
        expect(trimStart("  a  ")).toBe("a  ");
        expect(trimEnd("  a  ")).toBe("  a");
        expect(trim("  rope-" + trim.length + "  ")).toBe("rope-1");
        for (const f of [trim, trimStart, trimEnd]) expect(jit.exitCount(f)).toBe(0);
    });

    test("replaced functions are called", () => {
        const indexOf = compileCalls((s, t) => s.indexOf(t), "abc", "b");
        const original = String.prototype.indexOf;
        String.prototype.indexOf = () => "replaced";
        try {
            expect(indexOf("abc", "b")).toBe("replaced");
        } finally {
            String.prototype.indexOf = original;
        }
        expect(indexOf("abc", "b")).toBe(1);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/testing-api.js
// The jit object that test-js defines, which tests of the JIT use to compile functions where they choose and to check
// what their compiled code did. Without the JIT (LIBJS_JIT=off), nothing is compiled, and the checks of compiled
// code are skipped.
//
// NB: The functions come from new Function, so that each run of a test (see LIBJS_TEST_REPEAT) compiles new ones.

describe("jit testing object", () => {
    test("compiles prepared functions on demand", () => {
        const add = new Function("a", "b", "return a + b;");
        jit.prepare(add);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) expect(add(i, 1)).toBe(i + 1);
        expect(jit.isCompiled(add)).toBeFalse();
        expect(jit.compile(add)).toBe(jit.enabled);
        expect(jit.isCompiled(add)).toBe(jit.enabled);
        expect(add(2, 3)).toBe(5);
        expect(jit.exitCount(add)).toBe(0);
    });

    test("counts and records exits", () => {
        const add = new Function("a", "b", "return a + b;");
        jit.prepare(add);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) add(i, 1);
        jit.compile(add);
        expect(add(2147483647, 1)).toBe(2147483648);
        expect(add("a", 1)).toBe("a1");
        if (!jit.enabled) {
            expect(jit.exitCount(add)).toBe(0);
            expect(jit.exitSites(add)).toEqual([]);
            return;
        }
        // NB: Exits forced at random checks may come before the ones these calls cause, and are not counted.
        if (jit.forcesExits) {
            expect(jit.exitCount(add)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(2);
            return;
        }
        expect(jit.exitCount(add)).toBe(2);
        const kinds = jit.exitSites(add).map(site => site.split("@")[0]);
        expect(kinds).toContain("Overflow");
        expect(kinds).toContain("NotInt32");
    });

    test("discards code", () => {
        const negate = new Function("a", "return -a;");
        jit.prepare(negate);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) negate(i);
        jit.compile(negate);
        jit.discard(negate);
        expect(jit.isCompiled(negate)).toBeFalse();
        expect(jit.discardCount(negate)).toBe(jit.enabled ? 1 : 0);
        expect(negate(3)).toBe(-3);
        expect(jit.compile(negate)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    });

    test("never compiles functions it is told not to", () => {
        const f = new Function("a", "return a * 2;");
        jit.neverCompile(f);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) f(i);
        expect(jit.compile(f)).toBeFalse();
        expect(jit.isCompiled(f)).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("never compiles functions whose code was discarded while it ran", () => {
        // NB: The functions discard their own code, so frames still run it until they return.
        const other = new Function("");
        const f = new Function("target", "jit.discard(target); return 1;");
        jit.prepare(f);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) f(other);
        jit.compile(f);
        expect(f(f)).toBe(1);
        jit.neverCompile(f);
        expect(jit.discardCount(f)).toBe(jit.enabled ? 1 : 0);
        expect(jit.compile(f)).toBeFalse();

        const g = new Function("target", "jit.discard(target); jit.neverCompile(target); return 1;");
        jit.prepare(g);
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) g(other);
        jit.compile(g);
        expect(g(g)).toBe(1);
        expect(jit.compile(g)).toBeFalse();
        expect(jit.discardCount(g)).toBe(jit.enabled ? 1 : 0);
    });

    function checkCompiledCaller() {
        const probe = new Function("return jit.inCompiledCode();");
        jit.prepare(probe);
        expect(probe()).toBeFalse();
        jit.compile(probe);
        if (!jit.forcesExits) expect(probe()).toBe(jit.enabled);
        expect(jit.inCompiledCode()).toBeFalse();
    }
    // NB: The caller of the final probe must stay in the interpreter even when the harness repeats this test.
    jit.neverCompile(checkCompiledCaller);
    test("tells whether its caller runs in compiled code", checkCompiledCaller);

    test("only takes ECMAScript functions", () => {
        expect(() => jit.compile(Math.max)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(() => jit.prepare(1)).toThrow(TypeError);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/truncated-int32-arithmetic.js
function compiled(source, ...warmupArguments) {
    const parameters = source
        .match(/^\(([^)]*)\)/)[1]
        .split(",")
        .map(parameter => parameter.trim());
    const body = source.slice(source.indexOf("=>") + 2);
    const f = new Function(...parameters, body);
    jit.prepare(f);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) f(...warmupArguments);
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return f;
}

test("sums and differences that only reach ToInt32 wrap without exiting", () => {
    const sum = compiled("(a, b) => return (a + b) | 0;", 1, 2);
    expect(sum(0x7fffffff, 1)).toBe(-0x80000000);
    expect(sum(-0x80000000, -1)).toBe(0x7fffffff);
    expect(sum(-0x80000000, -0x80000000)).toBe(0);

    const difference = compiled("(a, b) => return (a - b) | 0;", 5, 2);
    expect(difference(-0x80000000, 1)).toBe(0x7fffffff);
    expect(difference(0x7fffffff, -1)).toBe(-0x80000000);

    // NB: Like asm.js code, coerce the parameters first: the checks of
    //     parameters read later exit with the exact sums before them.
    const chain = compiled("(a, b, c) => a = a | 0; b = b | 0; c = c | 0; return (a + b + c - a) | 0;", 1, 2, 3);
    expect(chain(0x7fffffff, 0x7fffffff, 0x7fffffff)).toBe((0x7fffffff + 0x7fffffff + 0x7fffffff - 0x7fffffff) | 0);

    const shifted = compiled("(a, b) => return (a + b) >> 1;", 1, 2);
    expect(shifted(0x7fffffff, 0x7fffffff)).toBe(-1);

    const unsigned = compiled("(a, b) => b = b | 0; return ((a >>> 0) + b) | 0;", 1, 2);
    expect(unsigned(-1, 1)).toBe(0);

    for (const f of [sum, difference, chain, shifted, unsigned]) expect(jit.exitCount(f)).toBe(0);
});

test("sums stored to integer typed arrays wrap, clamped ones saturate", () => {
    const store = compiled("(array, a, b) => array[0] = a + b; return array[0];", new Int32Array(1), 1, 2);
    expect(store(new Int32Array(1), 0x7fffffff, 1)).toBe(-0x80000000);
    expect(store(new Int16Array(1), 0x7fffffff, 1)).toBe(0);
    expect(store(new Uint8Array(1), 0x7fffffff, 0x7fffffff)).toBe(254);

    const clamped = compiled("(array, a, b) => array[0] = a + b; return array[0];", new Uint8ClampedArray(1), 1, 2);
    expect(clamped(new Uint8ClampedArray(1), 0x7fffffff, 1)).toBe(255);
    expect(clamped(new Uint8ClampedArray(1), -0x80000000, -1)).toBe(0);
});

test("sums with other users keep their exact values", () => {
    const both = compiled("(a, b) => { const sum = a + b; return [sum | 0, sum]; }", 1, 2);
    expect(both(0x7fffffff, 1)).toEqual([-0x80000000, 0x80000000]);

    const compared = compiled("(a, b) => return (a + b) > 0 ? (a + b) | 0 : 0;", 1, 2);
    expect(compared(0x7fffffff, 1)).toBe(-0x80000000);

    const unsigned = compiled("(a, b) => return (a + b) >>> 0;", 1, 2);
    expect(unsigned(-1, 0)).toBe(0xffffffff);
});

test("loops of asm.js style arithmetic wrap", () => {
    const hash = compiled(
        "(n) => { let h = 0; for (let i = 0; (i | 0) < (n | 0); i = (i + 1) | 0) h = (h + ((h << 5) + i)) | 0; return h; }",
        3
    );
    let expected = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) expected = (expected + ((expected << 5) + i)) | 0;
    expect(hash(1000)).toBe(expected);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/truthiness.js
// JIT code branches on the truthiness of strings and doubles inline. These
// tests run every function many times, so that with a low JIT threshold they
// are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

function truthy(value) {
    if (value) return true;
    return false;
}

function negated(value) {
    return !value;
}

describe("Truthiness in JIT code", () => {
    test("strings", () => {
        const long = "a long string, ".repeat(3);
        const cases = [
            ["", false],
            ["a", true],
            ["0", true],
            ["false", true],
            [long, true],
            [long + long, true],
            [long.substring(5, 5), false],
            [long.substring(5, 25), true],
            ["é", true],
            [String.fromCharCode(0), true],
        ];
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            for (const [value, expected] of cases) {
                expect(truthy(value)).toBe(expected);
                expect(negated(value)).toBe(!expected);
            }
        }
    });

    test("doubles", () => {
        const cases = [
            [0.5, true],
            [-1.5, true],
            [0, false],
            [-0, false],
            [NaN, false],
            [Infinity, true],
            [-Infinity, true],
            [Number.MIN_VALUE, true],
            [-Number.MIN_VALUE, true],
            [2 ** 40, true],
        ];
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            for (const [value, expected] of cases) {
                expect(truthy(value)).toBe(expected);
                expect(negated(value)).toBe(!expected);
            }
        }
    });

    test("other values", () => {
        const cases = [
            [Symbol("s"), true],
            [0n, false],
            [1n, true],
            [undefined, false],
            [null, false],
            [{}, true],
            [[], true],
            [() => {}, true],
        ];
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            for (const [value, expected] of cases) {
                expect(truthy(value)).toBe(expected);
                expect(negated(value)).toBe(!expected);
            }
        }
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/typed-array-length.js
function compileLength() {
    const lengthOf = new Function("array", "return array.length;");
    jit.prepare(lengthOf);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
        lengthOf(new Uint8Array(3));
        lengthOf(new Float64Array(4));
    }
    expect(jit.compile(lengthOf)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return lengthOf;
}

test("typed arrays of several kinds read their length", () => {
    const lengthOf = compileLength();
    expect(lengthOf(new Uint8Array(7))).toBe(7);
    expect(lengthOf(new Float64Array(2))).toBe(2);
    expect(lengthOf(new Uint8Array(new ArrayBuffer(16), 4, 5))).toBe(5);
    expect(jit.exitCount(lengthOf)).toBe(0);
});

test("typed arrays without a cached length exit, then take the slow path", () => {
    const lengthOf = compileLength();
    expect(lengthOf(new Uint8Array(0))).toBe(0);
    if (jit.enabled && !jit.forcesExits) expect(jit.exitCount(lengthOf)).toBe(1);
    jit.discard(lengthOf);
    expect(jit.compile(lengthOf)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    expect(lengthOf(new Uint8Array(0))).toBe(0);

    const detached = new Uint8Array(new ArrayBuffer(8));
    detached.buffer.transfer();
    expect(lengthOf(detached)).toBe(0);

    const buffer = new ArrayBuffer(4, { maxByteLength: 16 });
    const tracking = new Uint8Array(buffer);
    expect(lengthOf(tracking)).toBe(4);
    buffer.resize(12);
    expect(lengthOf(tracking)).toBe(12);
    const fixed = new Uint8Array(buffer, 8, 4);
    buffer.resize(10);
    expect(lengthOf(fixed)).toBe(0);
    // NB: An exit forced before the one of the empty typed array leaves the site unrecorded, so the code exits again.
    if (!jit.forcesExits) expect(jit.exitCount(lengthOf)).toBe(0);
});

test("objects that inherit from a typed array prototype call the getter", () => {
    const lengthOf = compileLength();
    expect(() => lengthOf(Object.create(Uint8Array.prototype))).toThrowWithMessage(
        TypeError,
        "Not an object of type TypedArray"
    );
    expect(lengthOf(new Uint8Array(3))).toBe(3);
});

test("own and redefined length properties are read", () => {
    const lengthOf = compileLength();
    const array = new Uint8Array(3);
    Object.defineProperty(array, "length", { value: 42 });
    expect(lengthOf(array)).toBe(42);

    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(Object.getPrototypeOf(Uint8Array.prototype), "length");
    Object.defineProperty(Object.getPrototypeOf(Uint8Array.prototype), "length", {
        get() {
            return "redefined";
        },
        configurable: true,
    });
    try {
        expect(lengthOf(new Uint8Array(3))).toBe("redefined");
    } finally {
        Object.defineProperty(Object.getPrototypeOf(Uint8Array.prototype), "length", descriptor);
    }
    expect(lengthOf(new Uint8Array(3))).toBe(3);
});

test("length properties of one kind's prototype are read", () => {
    const lengthOf = compileLength();
    Object.defineProperty(Float64Array.prototype, "length", { value: "shadowed", configurable: true });
    try {
        expect(lengthOf(new Float64Array(4))).toBe("shadowed");
        expect(lengthOf(new Uint8Array(3))).toBe(3);
    } finally {
        delete Float64Array.prototype.length;
    }
    expect(lengthOf(new Float64Array(4))).toBe(4);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/typed-array-storage.js
const storageConstructors = [
    Int8Array,
    Uint8Array,
    Uint8ClampedArray,
    Int16Array,
    Uint16Array,
    Int32Array,
    Uint32Array,
    Float32Array,
    Float64Array,
];

function compileStorage(f, args) {
    jit.prepare(f);
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) f(...args);
    expect(jit.compile(f)).toBe(jit.enabled);
    return f;
}

test("constant and dynamic indices use the storage of offset views", () => {
    for (const Constructor of storageConstructors) {
        const parent = new Constructor(8);
        parent.fill(99);
        const view = parent.subarray(2, 6);
        const access = compileStorage(
            new Function(
                "array",
                "index",
                "array[0] = 11; array[2] = 22; array[index] = 33; return array[0] + array[2] + array[index];"
            ),
            [view, 1]
        );
        expect(access(view, 1)).toBe(66);
        expect(Array.from(parent)).toEqual([99, 99, 11, 33, 22, 99, 99, 99]);
        const other = new Constructor([0, 0, 0, 0]);
        expect(access(other, 3)).toBe(66);
        expect(Array.from(other)).toEqual([11, 0, 22, 33]);
        expect(jit.exitCount(access)).toBe(0);
    }
});

test("constant negative and large indices stay out of bounds", () => {
    for (const Constructor of storageConstructors) {
        for (const index of [-1, -2147483648, 2147483647, 4294967295, 3]) {
            const array = new Constructor([1, 2, 3]);
            const access = compileStorage(new Function("array", `array[${index}] = 77; return array[${index}];`), [
                array,
            ]);
            expect(access(array)).toBeUndefined();
            expect(Array.from(array)).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
        }
    }
});

test("calls that detach a buffer invalidate reused typed-array storage", () => {
    for (const Constructor of storageConstructors) {
        const array = new Constructor([1, 2, 3]);
        const access = compileStorage(
            new Function(
                "array",
                "callback",
                "array[0] = 11; const before = array[0]; callback(); array[1] = 22; return [before, array[0], array[1]];"
            ),
            [array, () => {}]
        );
        const detach = () => detachArrayBuffer(array.buffer);
        jit.neverCompile(detach);
        expect(access(array, detach)).toEqual([11, undefined, undefined]);
        expect(array.length).toBe(0);
    }
});

test("storage loads in loops observe detachment between iterations", () => {
    const array = new Int32Array([42]);
    let shouldDetach = false;
    const detach = i => {
        if (shouldDetach && i === 1) detachArrayBuffer(array.buffer);
    };
    jit.neverCompile(detach);
    const access = compileStorage(
        new Function(
            "array",
            "callback",
            "const values = []; for (let i = 0; i < 4; ++i) { values.push(array[0]); callback(i); array[0] = 42; } return values;"
        ),
        [array, detach]
    );
    shouldDetach = true;
    expect(access(array, detach)).toEqual([42, 42, undefined, undefined]);
});

test("resizable buffers are checked again after a call", () => {
    for (const Constructor of storageConstructors) {
        const size = Constructor.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT;
        const buffer = new ArrayBuffer(4 * size, { maxByteLength: 8 * size });
        const array = new Constructor(buffer);
        const access = compileStorage(
            new Function(
                "array",
                "callback",
                "array[2] = 33; const before = array[2]; callback(); array[2] = 44; return [before, array[2]];"
            ),
            [array, () => {}]
        );
        expect(access(array, () => buffer.resize(size))).toEqual([33, undefined]);
        expect(access(array, () => buffer.resize(8 * size))).toEqual([undefined, 44]);
    }
});

test("constant indices also work with packed and holey arrays", () => {
    for (const array of [
        [1, 2, 3],
        [1, , 3],
    ]) {
        const access = compileStorage(
            new Function(
                "array",
                "array[0] = 11; array[2] = 22; return [array[0], array[1], array[2], array[-1], array[2147483647]];"
            ),
            [array]
        );
        expect(access(array)).toEqual([11, array[1], 22, undefined, undefined]);
    }
});

test("captured fixed lengths keep a detachment guard for constant indices", () => {
    for (const Constructor of storageConstructors) {
        const parent = new Constructor([99, 1, 2, 3, 99]);
        const array = parent.subarray(1, 4);
        let shouldDetach = false;
        const detach = () => {
            if (shouldDetach) detachArrayBuffer(array.buffer);
        };
        jit.neverCompile(detach);
        const factory = new Function(
            "array",
            "return function access(callback) { array[0] = 11; const before = array[0]; callback(); array[1] = 22; return [before, array[0], array[1]]; };"
        );
        const access = compileStorage(factory(array), [detach]);
        gc();
        expect(access(detach)).toEqual([11, 11, 22]);
        expect(parent[0]).toBe(99);
        expect(parent[4]).toBe(99);
        shouldDetach = true;
        expect(access(detach)).toEqual([11, undefined, undefined]);
        shouldDetach = false;
        expect(access(detach)).toEqual([undefined, undefined, undefined]);
    }
});

test("captured resizable buffers retain dynamic length checks", () => {
    for (const Constructor of storageConstructors) {
        const size = Constructor.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT;
        const buffer = new ArrayBuffer(4 * size, { maxByteLength: 8 * size });
        const array = new Constructor(buffer);
        let length = 4 * size;
        const resize = () => buffer.resize(length);
        jit.neverCompile(resize);
        const factory = new Function(
            "array",
            "return function access(callback) { array[2] = 33; const before = array[2]; callback(); array[2] = 44; return [before, array[2]]; };"
        );
        const access = compileStorage(factory(array), [resize]);
        length = size;
        expect(access(resize)).toEqual([33, undefined]);
        length = 8 * size;
        expect(access(resize)).toEqual([undefined, 44]);
    }
});

const conditionalGlobalStorage = new Uint8Array(16);
function sumConditionalGlobalStorage(count, limit) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) if (i < limit) sum += conditionalGlobalStorage[0];
    return sum;
}

test("conditional constant-index loads of a global stay behind the storage check", () => {
    conditionalGlobalStorage[0] = 1;
    const sum = compileStorage(sumConditionalGlobalStorage, [100, 100]);
    expect(sum(100, 100)).toBe(100);
    conditionalGlobalStorage.buffer.transfer();
    expect(sum(3, 0)).toBe(0);
    expect(sum(3, 1)).toBeNaN();
});

test("conditional constant-index loads of a captured binding stay behind the storage check", () => {
    const factory = new Function(
        "return function sum(count, limit) { let storage = new Uint8Array(16); storage[0] = 1; " +
            "function inner(count, limit) { let sum = 0; for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) if (i < limit) sum += storage[0]; return sum; } " +
            "jit.prepare(inner); for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) inner(count, limit); jit.compile(inner); " +
            "const before = inner(count, limit); storage.buffer.transfer(); return [before, inner(3, 0), inner(3, 1)]; };"
    );
    const [before, skipped, loaded] = factory()(100, 100);
    expect(before).toBe(100);
    expect(skipped).toBe(0);
    expect(loaded).toBeNaN();
});

const detachedGlobalStorage = new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3, 4]);
function readDetachedGlobalStorage(index) {
    return detachedGlobalStorage[index];
}

test("keyed accesses compiled after out-of-bounds exits take the slow path once detached", () => {
    const capturedFactory = new Function("storage", "return function read(index) { return storage[index]; };");
    const captured = new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3, 4]);
    for (const [read, storage] of [
        [capturedFactory(captured), captured],
        [readDetachedGlobalStorage, detachedGlobalStorage],
    ]) {
        compileStorage(read, [2]);
        expect(read(2)).toBe(3);
        expect(read(10)).toBeUndefined();
        jit.discard(read);
        expect(jit.compile(read)).toBe(jit.enabled);
        expect(read(2)).toBe(3);
        expect(read(10)).toBeUndefined();
        storage.buffer.transfer();
        expect(read(2)).toBeUndefined();
        expect(read(0)).toBeUndefined();
        // NB: An exit forced at the bounds check comes before the out-of-bounds exit, which then goes unrecorded.
        if (!jit.forcesExits) expect(jit.exitCount(read)).toBe(0);
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/jit/typeof.js
// JIT code computes `typeof` inline. These tests run every function many
// times, so that with a low JIT threshold they are compiled.

const iterations = 100;

function typeOf(value) {
    return typeof value;
}

function isFunction(value) {
    return typeof value === "function";
}

// Every comparison of typeof with a constant, strict and loose, and their
// negations.
function kinds(value) {
    const result = [];
    if (typeof value === "undefined") result.push("undefined");
    if (typeof value == "object") result.push("object");
    if (typeof value === "boolean") result.push("boolean");
    if (typeof value === "number") result.push("number");
    if (typeof value === "string") result.push("string");
    if (typeof value === "symbol") result.push("symbol");
    if (typeof value === "bigint") result.push("bigint");
    if (typeof value === "function") result.push("function");
    if (typeof value !== "object" && typeof value != "function") result.push("primitive");
    if ("number" === typeof value) result.push("reversed");
    if (typeof value === "Function") result.push("never");
    return result.join(",");
}

describe("typeof in JIT code", () => {
    test("every kind of value", () => {
        const values = [
            [undefined, "undefined"],
            [null, "object"],
            [true, "boolean"],
            [false, "boolean"],
            [0, "number"],
            [-1, "number"],
            [1.5, "number"],
            [-0, "number"],
            [NaN, "number"],
            [Infinity, "number"],
            ["", "string"],
            ["x", "string"],
            ["a longer string", "string"],
            [Symbol("s"), "symbol"],
            [1n, "bigint"],
            [{}, "object"],
            [[], "object"],
            [/x/, "object"],
            [new Proxy({}, {}), "object"],
            [function () {}, "function"],
            [() => {}, "function"],
            [class {}, "function"],
            [Math.max, "function"],
            [function () {}.bind(null), "function"],
            [new Proxy(function () {}, {}), "function"],
            [async function () {}, "function"],
            [function* () {}, "function"],
        ];
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            for (const [value, expected] of values) {
                expect(typeOf(value)).toBe(expected);
                expect(isFunction(value)).toBe(expected === "function");
                const primitive = expected !== "object" && expected !== "function" ? ",primitive" : "";
                const reversed = expected === "number" ? ",reversed" : "";
                expect(kinds(value)).toBe(expected + primitive + reversed);
            }
            expect(typeOf("rope " + i)).toBe("string");
        }
    });
});

var globalNumber = 1;
let globalLet = "s";
const globalConst = {};
function globalFunction() {}

describe("typeof of global variables", () => {
    test("variables of the global object and the global declarative environment", () => {
        function types() {
            return [
                typeof globalNumber,
                typeof globalLet,
                typeof globalConst,
                typeof globalFunction,
                typeof notDeclaredAnywhere,
                typeof Math,
            ];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i)
            expect(types()).toEqual(["number", "string", "object", "function", "undefined", "object"]);
        globalNumber = "now a string";
        globalLet = 1n;
        expect(types()).toEqual(["string", "bigint", "object", "function", "undefined", "object"]);
        globalThis.notDeclaredAnywhere = 1;
        expect(types()[4]).toBe("number");
        delete globalThis.notDeclaredAnywhere;
        expect(types()[4]).toBe("undefined");
    });

    test("global properties that change", () => {
        function type() {
            return typeof changingGlobal;
        }
        globalThis.changingGlobal = 1;
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(type()).toBe("number");
        delete globalThis.changingGlobal;
        expect(type()).toBe("undefined");
        let getterCalls = 0;
        Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "changingGlobal", {
            get() {
                ++getterCalls;
                return "from a getter";
            },
            configurable: true,
        });
        expect(type()).toBe("string");
        expect(getterCalls).toBe(1);
        delete globalThis.changingGlobal;
    });

    test("global lexical bindings in their temporal dead zone throw", () => {
        expect(() => typeof laterGlobalLet).toThrow(ReferenceError);
    });
});
