FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/loops/for-of-basic.js
describe("correct behavior", () => {
    test("iterate through array", () => {
        const a = [];
        for (const num of [1, 2, 3]) {
            a.push(num);
        }
        expect(a).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
    });

    test("iterate through string", () => {
        const a = [];
        for (const char of "hello") {
            a.push(char);
        }
        expect(a).toEqual(["h", "e", "l", "l", "o"]);
    });

    test("iterate through string object", () => {
        const a = [];
        for (const char of new String("hello")) {
            a.push(char);
        }
        expect(a).toEqual(["h", "e", "l", "l", "o"]);
    });

    test("use already-declared variable", () => {
        var char;
        for (char of "abc");
        expect(char).toBe("c");
    });

    test("respects custom Symbol.iterator method", () => {
        const o = {
            [Symbol.iterator]() {
                return {
                    i: 0,
                    next() {
                        if (this.i++ == 3) {
                            return { done: true };
                        }
                        return { value: this.i, done: false };
                    },
                };
            },
        };

        const a = [];
        for (const k of o) {
            a.push(k);
        }

        expect(a).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
    });

    test("loops through custom iterator if there is an exception thrown part way through", () => {
        // This tests against the way custom iterators used to be implemented, where the values
        // were all collected at once before the for-of body was executed, instead of getting
        // the values one at a time
        const o = {
            [Symbol.iterator]() {
                return {
                    i: 0,
                    next() {
                        if (this.i++ === 3) {
                            throw new Error();
                        }
                        return { value: this.i };
                    },
                };
            },
        };

        const a = [];

        try {
            for (let k of o) {
                a.push(k);
            }
            expect().fail();
        } catch (e) {
            expect(a).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
        }
    });
});

describe("errors", () => {
    test("right hand side is a primitive", () => {
        expect(() => {
            for (const _ of 123) {
            }
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "123 is not iterable");
    });

    test("right hand side is an object", () => {
        expect(() => {
            for (const _ of { foo: 1, bar: 2 }) {
            }
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "[object Object] is not iterable");
    });
});

test("allow binding patterns", () => {
    let counter = 0;
    for (let [a, b] of [
        [1, 2],
        [3, 4],
        [5, 6],
    ]) {
        expect(a + 1).toBe(b);
        counter++;
    }
    expect(counter).toBe(3);
});

describe("special left hand sides", () => {
    test("allow member expression as variable", () => {
        const f = {};
        for (f.a of "abc");
        expect(f.a).toBe("c");
    });

    test("allow member expression of function call", () => {
        const b = {};
        function f() {
            return b;
        }

        for (f().a of "abc");

        expect(f().a).toBe("c");
    });

    test("call expression as for-of LHS is valid in non-strict mode", () => {
        // In non-strict mode, call expressions are allowed as for-of LHS
        // (web compat), but they fail at runtime with ReferenceError.
        expect("for (f() of []);").toEval();
        expect("for (f() of [0]) {}").toEval();
    });

    test("call expression as for-of LHS is SyntaxError in strict mode", () => {
        expect("'use strict'; for (f() of []);").not.toEval();
    });

    test("variable in its temporal dead zone", () => {
        function assignLet() {
            for (value of [1]);
            let value;
        }
        function assignConst() {
            for (value of [1]);
            const value = 0;
        }
        function assignInForIn() {
            for (value in { key: 1 });
            let value;
        }

        expect(assignLet).toThrow(ReferenceError);
        expect(assignConst).toThrow(ReferenceError);
        expect(assignInForIn).toThrow(ReferenceError);
    });

    test("Cannot change constant declaration in body", () => {
        const vals = [];
        for (const v of [1, 2]) {
            expect(() => v++).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Invalid assignment to const variable");
            vals.push(v);
        }

        expect(vals).toEqual([1, 2]);
    });

    test("Cannot change destructured constant declaration in body", () => {
        const vals = [];
        for (const [value] of [[1], [2]]) {
            expect(() => {
                value = 3;
            }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Invalid assignment to const variable");
            vals.push(value);
        }

        expect(vals).toEqual([1, 2]);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/loops/for-of-fast-array.js
// for-of loops and array destructuring patterns step through plain arrays without making array iterators. These tests
// check that they still behave like array iterators do.

const ArrayIteratorPrototype = Object.getPrototypeOf([][Symbol.iterator]());

function collect(iterable) {
    const values = [];
    for (const value of iterable) values.push(value);
    return values;
}

function firstTwo(iterable) {
    const [first, second] = iterable;
    return [first, second];
}

function restAfterFirst(iterable) {
    const [first, ...rest] = iterable;
    return [first, rest];
}

describe("elements", () => {
    test("packed arrays", () => {
        expect(collect([1, 2, 3])).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
        expect(collect([])).toEqual([]);
        expect(firstTwo([1, 2, 3])).toEqual([1, 2]);
        expect(firstTwo([1])).toEqual([1, undefined]);
        expect(restAfterFirst([1, 2, 3])).toEqual([1, [2, 3]]);
        expect(restAfterFirst([])).toEqual([undefined, []]);
    });

    test("holes read undefined", () => {
        expect(collect([1, , 3])).toEqual([1, undefined, 3]);
        expect(collect(new Array(3))).toEqual([undefined, undefined, undefined]);
        expect(firstTwo(new Array(5))).toEqual([undefined, undefined]);
        expect(restAfterFirst([1, , 3])).toEqual([1, [undefined, 3]]);
    });

    test("holes read the prototype chain", () => {
        Array.prototype[1] = "from Array.prototype";
        Object.prototype[2] = "from Object.prototype";
        try {
            expect(collect([0, , , 3])).toEqual([0, "from Array.prototype", "from Object.prototype", 3]);
            expect(firstTwo(new Array(2))).toEqual([undefined, "from Array.prototype"]);
            expect(restAfterFirst(new Array(3))).toEqual([
                undefined,
                ["from Array.prototype", "from Object.prototype"],
            ]);
        } finally {
            delete Array.prototype[1];
            delete Object.prototype[2];
        }
    });

    test("getters on the prototype run once per hole", () => {
        let getterCalls = 0;
        Object.defineProperty(Array.prototype, 1, {
            get() {
                ++getterCalls;
                return "from getter";
            },
            configurable: true,
        });
        try {
            let seen = "";
            for (const value of new Array(3)) seen += `${value},`;
            expect(seen).toBe("undefined,from getter,undefined,");
            expect(getterCalls).toBe(1);
        } finally {
            delete Array.prototype[1];
        }
    });

    test("subclasses of Array", () => {
        class MyArray extends Array {}
        const array = MyArray.from([1, 2, 3]);
        expect(collect(array)).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
        expect(firstTwo(array)).toEqual([1, 2]);
    });

    test("frozen arrays", () => {
        const array = Object.freeze([1, 2, 3]);
        expect(collect(array)).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
        expect(restAfterFirst(array)).toEqual([1, [2, 3]]);
    });
});

describe("changes during the iteration", () => {
    test("arrays that grow", () => {
        const array = [1, 2];
        const values = [];
        for (const value of array) {
            values.push(value);
            if (array.length < 4) array.push(value * 10);
        }
        expect(values).toEqual([1, 2, 10, 20]);
    });

    test("arrays that shrink", () => {
        const array = [1, 2, 3, 4];
        const values = [];
        for (const value of array) {
            values.push(value);
            array.length = 2;
        }
        expect(values).toEqual([1, 2]);
    });

    test("arrays that get holes", () => {
        const array = [1, 2, 3];
        const values = [];
        for (const value of array) {
            values.push(value);
            delete array[1];
        }
        expect(values).toEqual([1, undefined, 3]);
    });

    test("an iteration that is done stays done when the array grows", () => {
        const array = [1];
        const values = [];
        for (const value of array) values.push(value);
        array.push(2);
        expect(values).toEqual([1]);

        const [first, second, third] = array;
        expect([first, second, third]).toEqual([1, 2, undefined]);
    });

    test("next replaced during the iteration is not called", () => {
        const originalNext = ArrayIteratorPrototype.next;
        const values = [];
        try {
            for (const value of [1, 2, 3]) {
                values.push(value);
                ArrayIteratorPrototype.next = () => ({ value: "replaced", done: false });
            }
        } finally {
            ArrayIteratorPrototype.next = originalNext;
        }
        expect(values).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
    });
});

describe("iterator methods", () => {
    test("an own iterator method of the array", () => {
        const array = [1, 2, 3];
        array[Symbol.iterator] = function* () {
            yield "own";
        };
        expect(collect(array)).toEqual(["own"]);
        expect(firstTwo(array)).toEqual(["own", undefined]);
    });

    test("an iterator getter runs once per iteration", () => {
        let getterCalls = 0;
        const array = [1, 2, 3];
        Object.defineProperty(array, Symbol.iterator, {
            get() {
                ++getterCalls;
                return Array.prototype.values;
            },
        });
        expect(collect(array)).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
        expect(firstTwo(array)).toEqual([1, 2]);
        expect(getterCalls).toBe(2);
    });

    test("an iterator that is an array with a next property that is not callable", () => {
        const iterator = [1, 2, 3];
        iterator.next = 0;
        const iterable = { [Symbol.iterator]: () => iterator };
        expect(() => collect(iterable)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(() => firstTwo(iterable)).toThrow(TypeError);
    });

    test("arrays of another iteration method", () => {
        const array = [1, 2, 3];
        expect(collect(array.keys())).toEqual([0, 1, 2]);
        expect(collect(array.entries())).toEqual([
            [0, 1],
            [1, 2],
            [2, 3],
        ]);
        expect(firstTwo(array.values())).toEqual([1, 2]);
    });
});

describe("closing", () => {
    function expectClosedAt(close, expectedNextValue) {
        const receivers = [];
        ArrayIteratorPrototype.return = function () {
            receivers.push(this);
            expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(this)).toBe(ArrayIteratorPrototype);
            expect(this.next()).toEqual(expectedNextValue);
            return {};
        };
        try {
            close();
        } finally {
            delete ArrayIteratorPrototype.return;
        }
        expect(receivers).toHaveLength(1);
    }

    test("break, return and throw close at the next element", () => {
        expectClosedAt(
            () => {
                for (const value of [1, 2, 3]) break;
            },
            { value: 2, done: false }
        );
        expectClosedAt(
            () => {
                (() => {
                    for (const value of [1, 2, 3]) if (value === 2) return;
                })();
            },
            { value: 3, done: false }
        );
        expectClosedAt(
            () => {
                expect(() => {
                    for (const value of [1, 2, 3]) throw new Error("thrown");
                }).toThrowWithMessage(Error, "thrown");
            },
            { value: 2, done: false }
        );
    });

    test("a return method added during the iteration is called", () => {
        const receivers = [];
        try {
            for (const value of [1, 2, 3]) {
                ArrayIteratorPrototype.return = function () {
                    receivers.push(this.next());
                    return {};
                };
                break;
            }
        } finally {
            delete ArrayIteratorPrototype.return;
        }
        expect(receivers).toEqual([{ value: 2, done: false }]);
    });

    test("destructuring closes unless the pattern reads past the end", () => {
        expectClosedAt(
            () => {
                const [first] = [1, 2, 3];
            },
            { value: 2, done: false }
        );
        expectClosedAt(
            () => {
                const [first, second] = [1, 2];
            },
            { value: undefined, done: true }
        );

        let returnCalls = 0;
        ArrayIteratorPrototype.return = () => {
            ++returnCalls;
            return {};
        };
        try {
            const [first, second] = [1];
            const [third, ...rest] = [1, 2, 3];
        } finally {
            delete ArrayIteratorPrototype.return;
        }
        expect(returnCalls).toBe(0);
    });

    test("a throwing return method and a throwing body", () => {
        ArrayIteratorPrototype.return = () => {
            throw new Error("from return");
        };
        try {
            expect(() => {
                for (const value of [1, 2]) throw new Error("from body");
            }).toThrowWithMessage(Error, "from body");
            expect(() => {
                for (const value of [1, 2]) break;
            }).toThrowWithMessage(Error, "from return");
        } finally {
            delete ArrayIteratorPrototype.return;
        }
    });
});

describe("other consumers of iterators", () => {
    test("yield* over arrays", () => {
        function* delegate(array) {
            return yield* array;
        }
        expect([...delegate([1, 2, 3])]).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
        const generator = delegate([1, 2, 3]);
        generator.next();
        expect(generator.return(5)).toEqual({ value: 5, done: true });
    });

    test("a generator suspended inside a for-of over an array", () => {
        function* generator(array) {
            for (const value of array) yield value * 2;
        }
        const iterator = generator([1, 2, 3]);
        expect(iterator.next()).toEqual({ value: 2, done: false });
        expect(iterator.next()).toEqual({ value: 4, done: false });
        expect(iterator.return(7)).toEqual({ value: 7, done: true });
        expect([...generator([4, 5])]).toEqual([8, 10]);
    });

    test("for await over arrays", async () => {
        const values = [];
        for await (const value of [1, Promise.resolve(2), 3]) values.push(value);
        expect(values).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
    });

    test("nested patterns, defaults and elisions", () => {
        const [[a, b] = [9, 9], , c = 7, ...[d, e]] = [[1, 2], 0, undefined, 4, 5];
        expect([a, b, c, d, e]).toEqual([1, 2, 7, 4, 5]);
        const [x = 1, y = 2] = [];
        expect([x, y]).toEqual([1, 2]);
    });

    test("assignment patterns", () => {
        let first;
        let second;
        [first, second] = [1, 2, 3];
        expect([first, second]).toEqual([1, 2]);
        [second, first] = [first, second];
        expect([first, second]).toEqual([2, 1]);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/loops/for-of-iterator-close.js
function makeIterator(values) {
    let returnCalled = false;
    let returnArgument = undefined;
    let index = 0;
    const iterator = {
        [Symbol.iterator]() {
            return {
                next() {
                    if (index < values.length) return { value: values[index++], done: false };
                    return { done: true };
                },
                return(value) {
                    returnCalled = true;
                    returnArgument = value;
                    return { done: true };
                },
            };
        },
        get returnCalled() {
            return returnCalled;
        },
        get returnArgument() {
            return returnArgument;
        },
    };
    return iterator;
}

describe("for-of iterator close on abrupt completion", () => {
    test("break calls return()", () => {
        const iter = makeIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        for (const x of iter) {
            if (x === 2) break;
        }
        expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("break calls an own return() on a built-in iterator", () => {
        let returnCalls = 0;
        const iterator = [1][Symbol.iterator]();
        iterator.return = () => {
            ++returnCalls;
            throw new Error("close error");
        };

        expect(() => {
            for (const value of { [Symbol.iterator]: () => iterator }) break;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(Error, "close error");
        expect(returnCalls).toBe(1);
    });

    test("return from function calls return()", () => {
        const iter = makeIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        (function () {
            for (const x of iter) {
                if (x === 1) return;
            }
        })();
        expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("throw from body calls return()", () => {
        const iter = makeIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        try {
            for (const x of iter) {
                throw new Error("oops");
            }
        } catch {}
        expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("continue to same loop does NOT call return()", () => {
        const iter = makeIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        for (const x of iter) {
            continue;
        }
        expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("continue to outer label calls return()", () => {
        const iter = makeIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        outer: for (let i = 0; i < 1; i++) {
            for (const x of iter) {
                continue outer;
            }
        }
        expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("normal completion does NOT call return()", () => {
        const iter = makeIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        for (const x of iter) {
            // exhaust normally
        }
        expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("iterator without return() method: no error on break", () => {
        let index = 0;
        const iter = {
            [Symbol.iterator]() {
                return {
                    next() {
                        if (index < 3) return { value: index++, done: false };
                        return { done: true };
                    },
                    // no return() method
                };
            },
        };
        expect(() => {
            for (const x of iter) {
                break;
            }
        }).not.toThrow();
    });

    test("return() that throws during non-throw exit: close error propagates", () => {
        const iter = {
            [Symbol.iterator]() {
                return {
                    next() {
                        return { value: 1, done: false };
                    },
                    return() {
                        throw new Error("close error");
                    },
                };
            },
        };
        expect(() => {
            for (const x of iter) {
                break;
            }
        }).toThrowWithMessage(Error, "close error");
    });

    test("return() that throws during throw exit: original throw takes precedence", () => {
        const iter = {
            [Symbol.iterator]() {
                return {
                    next() {
                        return { value: 1, done: false };
                    },
                    return() {
                        throw new Error("close error");
                    },
                };
            },
        };
        expect(() => {
            for (const x of iter) {
                throw new Error("body error");
            }
        }).toThrowWithMessage(Error, "body error");
    });

    test("LHS destructuring that throws calls return()", () => {
        let returnCalled = false;
        const iter = {
            [Symbol.iterator]() {
                return {
                    next() {
                        return { value: 42, done: false };
                    },
                    return() {
                        returnCalled = true;
                        return { done: true };
                    },
                };
            },
        };
        try {
            for (const [a, b] of iter) {
                // destructuring a non-iterable (42) should throw
            }
        } catch {}
        expect(returnCalled).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("break from for-of inside try/finally: both finally and return() run", () => {
        const events = [];
        const iter = {
            [Symbol.iterator]() {
                return {
                    next() {
                        return { value: 1, done: false };
                    },
                    return() {
                        events.push("return");
                        return { done: true };
                    },
                };
            },
        };
        try {
            for (const x of iter) {
                break;
            }
        } finally {
            events.push("finally");
        }
        expect(events).toEqual(["return", "finally"]);
    });

    test("for-of with var binding and break", () => {
        const iter = makeIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        for (var x of iter) {
            if (x === 2) break;
        }
        expect(x).toBe(2);
        expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("for-of with let binding and break", () => {
        const iter = makeIterator([10, 20, 30]);
        let last;
        for (let x of iter) {
            last = x;
            if (x === 20) break;
        }
        expect(last).toBe(20);
        expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("nested for-of: break from inner closes inner, not outer", () => {
        const outerIter = makeIterator([1, 2]);
        const innerIter = makeIterator(["a", "b", "c"]);
        const results = [];
        for (const x of outerIter) {
            for (const y of innerIter) {
                results.push(`${x}${y}`);
                if (y === "a") break;
            }
        }
        expect(innerIter.returnCalled).toBeTrue();
        // outerIter is exhausted normally (only 2 elements)
        expect(outerIter.returnCalled).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("break to outer label from nested for-of closes both", () => {
        let outerReturnCalled = false;
        let innerReturnCalled = false;

        const outerIter = {
            [Symbol.iterator]() {
                return {
                    i: 0,
                    next() {
                        return this.i++ < 3 ? { value: this.i, done: false } : { done: true };
                    },
                    return() {
                        outerReturnCalled = true;
                        return { done: true };
                    },
                };
            },
        };

        const innerIter = {
            [Symbol.iterator]() {
                return {
                    i: 0,
                    next() {
                        return this.i++ < 3 ? { value: this.i, done: false } : { done: true };
                    },
                    return() {
                        innerReturnCalled = true;
                        return { done: true };
                    },
                };
            },
        };

        outer: for (const x of outerIter) {
            for (const y of innerIter) {
                break outer;
            }
        }

        expect(innerReturnCalled).toBeTrue();
        expect(outerReturnCalled).toBeTrue();
    });
});

describe("for-await-of iterator close on abrupt completion", () => {
    function makeAsyncIterator(values) {
        let returnCalled = false;
        return {
            [Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
                let index = 0;
                return {
                    next() {
                        if (index < values.length) return Promise.resolve({ value: values[index++], done: false });
                        return Promise.resolve({ done: true });
                    },
                    return() {
                        returnCalled = true;
                        return Promise.resolve({ done: true });
                    },
                };
            },
            get returnCalled() {
                return returnCalled;
            },
        };
    }

    test("break calls return()", () => {
        const iter = makeAsyncIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        return (async () => {
            for await (const x of iter) {
                break;
            }
        })().then(() => {
            expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeTrue();
        });
    });

    test("return from async function calls return()", () => {
        const iter = makeAsyncIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        return (async () => {
            for await (const x of iter) {
                return x;
            }
        })().then(() => {
            expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeTrue();
        });
    });

    test("throw from body calls return()", () => {
        const iter = makeAsyncIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        return (async () => {
            for await (const x of iter) {
                throw new Error("oops");
            }
        })().catch(() => {
            expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeTrue();
        });
    });

    test("continue to same loop does NOT call return()", () => {
        const iter = makeAsyncIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        return (async () => {
            for await (const x of iter) {
                continue;
            }
        })().then(() => {
            expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeFalse();
        });
    });

    test("normal completion does NOT call return()", () => {
        const iter = makeAsyncIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        return (async () => {
            for await (const x of iter) {
                // exhaust normally
            }
        })().then(() => {
            expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeFalse();
        });
    });

    test("continue to outer label calls return()", () => {
        const iter = makeAsyncIterator([1, 2, 3]);
        return (async () => {
            outer: for (let i = 0; i < 1; i++) {
                for await (const x of iter) {
                    continue outer;
                }
            }
        })().then(() => {
            expect(iter.returnCalled).toBeTrue();
        });
    });

    test("return() that throws during non-throw exit: close error propagates", () => {
        const iter = {
            [Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
                return {
                    next() {
                        return Promise.resolve({ value: 1, done: false });
                    },
                    return() {
                        return Promise.reject(new Error("close error"));
                    },
                };
            },
        };
        return (async () => {
            for await (const x of iter) {
                break;
            }
        })().then(
            () => {
                expect().fail("should have thrown");
            },
            error => {
                expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(Error);
                expect(error.message).toBe("close error");
            }
        );
    });

    test("return() that throws during throw exit: original throw takes precedence", () => {
        const iter = {
            [Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
                return {
                    next() {
                        return Promise.resolve({ value: 1, done: false });
                    },
                    return() {
                        return Promise.reject(new Error("close error"));
                    },
                };
            },
        };
        return (async () => {
            for await (const x of iter) {
                throw new Error("body error");
            }
        })().then(
            () => {
                expect().fail("should have thrown");
            },
            error => {
                expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(Error);
                expect(error.message).toBe("body error");
            }
        );
    });

    test("iterator without return() method: no error on break", () => {
        const iter = {
            [Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
                let index = 0;
                return {
                    next() {
                        return Promise.resolve(index++ < 3 ? { value: index, done: false } : { done: true });
                    },
                };
            },
        };
        return (async () => {
            for await (const x of iter) {
                break;
            }
        })();
    });

    test("GetMethod throwing during throw exit: original throw takes precedence", () => {
        const iter = {
            [Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
                return {
                    next() {
                        return Promise.resolve({ value: 1, done: false });
                    },
                    get return() {
                        throw { name: "inner error" };
                    },
                };
            },
        };
        return (async () => {
            for await (const x of iter) {
                throw new Error("original");
            }
        })().then(
            () => {
                expect().fail("should have thrown");
            },
            error => {
                expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(Error);
                expect(error.message).toBe("original");
            }
        );
    });

    test("non-callable return during throw exit: original throw takes precedence", () => {
        const iter = {
            [Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
                return {
                    next() {
                        return Promise.resolve({ value: 1, done: false });
                    },
                    return: true,
                };
            },
        };
        return (async () => {
            for await (const x of iter) {
                throw new Error("original");
            }
        })().then(
            () => {
                expect().fail("should have thrown");
            },
            error => {
                expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(Error);
                expect(error.message).toBe("original");
            }
        );
    });

    test("sync iterator with rejected promise value: return() called only once", () => {
        let returnCount = 0;
        const syncIter = {
            [Symbol.iterator]() {
                return {
                    next() {
                        return { value: Promise.reject("reject"), done: false };
                    },
                    return() {
                        returnCount += 1;
                    },
                };
            },
        };

        return (async () => {
            for await (const x of syncIter) {
                // The rejected promise causes the async-from-sync iterator
                // to call return() internally. Our for-await-of close logic
                // must not double-close.
            }
        })().catch(() => {
            expect(returnCount).toBe(1);
        });
    });
});

test("let variables captured by value", () => {
    let result = "";
    let functionList = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
        result += i;
        functionList.push(function () {
            return i;
        });
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < functionList.length; i++) {
        result += functionList[i]();
    }

    expect(result).toEqual("012345678012345678");
});

test("let variables captured by value when the body continues", () => {
    const functions = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        functions.push(() => i);
        continue;
    }
    expect(functions.map(f => f())).toEqual([0, 1, 2]);

    functions.length = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        functions.push(() => i);
        if (i % 2 === 0) continue;
    }
    expect(functions.map(f => f())).toEqual([0, 1, 2, 3]);

    functions.length = 0;
    outer: for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        for (;;) {
            functions.push(() => i);
            continue outer;
        }
    }
    expect(functions.map(f => f())).toEqual([0, 1, 2]);
});

describe("a lexical binding is uninitialized again on each iteration", () => {
    test("let in a loop body", () => {
        function loop() {
            const results = [];
            for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
                try {
                    results.push(value);
                } catch (error) {
                    results.push(error.name);
                }
                let value = i;
            }
            return results;
        }

        expect(loop()).toEqual(["ReferenceError", "ReferenceError"]);
    });

    test("typeof in a loop body", () => {
        function loop() {
            const results = [];
            let i = 0;
            while (i < 2) {
                try {
                    results.push(typeof value);
                } catch (error) {
                    results.push(error.name);
                }
                const value = i++;
            }
            return results;
        }

        expect(loop()).toEqual(["ReferenceError", "ReferenceError"]);
    });

    test("class declaration in a loop body", () => {
        function loop() {
            const results = [];
            for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
                try {
                    results.push(typeof C);
                } catch (error) {
                    results.push(error.name);
                }
                class C {}
            }
            return results;
        }

        expect(loop()).toEqual(["ReferenceError", "ReferenceError"]);
    });

    test("initializer that throws after starting to build its value", () => {

            for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
                try {
                    try {
                        results.push(value);
                    } catch (error) {
                        results.push(error.name);
                    }
                    let value = [
                        i,
                        ...(() => {
                            throw new Error();
                        })(),
                    ];
                } catch {}
            }
            return results;
        }

        expect(loop()).toEqual(["ReferenceError", "ReferenceError"]);
    });

    test("switch case entered after an earlier iteration declared the binding", () => {

                            results.push(value);
                        } catch (error) {
                            results.push(error.name);
                        }

    test("a loop that reads a binding of the scope around it keeps the binding", () => {
        function afterClass() {
            const results = [];
            {
                class C {}
                for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) results.push(typeof C);
            }
            return results;
        }

        function afterCase(which) {
            const results = [];
            switch (which) {
                case 0:
                    let value = "initialized";
                case 1:
                    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
                        try {
                            results.push(value);
                        } catch (error) {
                            results.push(error.name);
                        }
                    }
            }
            return results;
        }

        expect(afterClass()).toEqual(["function", "function"]);
        expect(afterCase(0)).toEqual(["initialized", "initialized"]);
        expect(afterCase(1)).toEqual(["ReferenceError", "ReferenceError"]);
    });

    test("loop bodies that a statement around the scope starts", () => {
        function whileLoop() {
            const results = [];
            let i = 0;
            while (i < 2) {
                if (i >= 0) {
                    try {
                        results.push(value);
                    } catch (error) {
                        results.push(error.name);
                    }
                    let value = i++;
                }
            }
            return results;
        }

        function doWhileLoop() {
            const results = [];
            let i = 0;
            do {
                label: {
                    try {
                        results.push(value);
                    } catch (error) {
                        results.push(error.name);
                    }
                    let value = i++;
                    if (i > 0) break label;
                }
            } while (i < 2);
            return results;
        }

        function forInLoop() {
            const results = [];
            for (const key in { a: 1, b: 2 }) {
                try {
                    results.push(value);
                } catch (error) {
                    results.push(error.name);
                }
                let value = key;
            }
            return results;
        }

        function forOfLoop() {
            const results = [];
            for (const element of [1, 2]) {
                try {
                    results.push(value);
                } catch (error) {
                    results.push(error.name);
                }
                let value = element;
            }
            return results;
        }

        function* generatorLoop() {
            for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
                try {
                    yield value;
                } catch (error) {
                    yield error.name;
                }
                let value = i;
                yield "initialized";
            }
        }

        const twice = ["ReferenceError", "ReferenceError"];
        expect(whileLoop()).toEqual(twice);
        expect(doWhileLoop()).toEqual(twice);
        expect(forInLoop()).toEqual(twice);
        expect(forOfLoop()).toEqual(twice);
        expect([...generatorLoop()]).toEqual(["ReferenceError", "initialized", "ReferenceError", "initialized"]);
    });

    test("head of a loop in a loop without a block around it", () => {
        function forLoopHead() {
            const results = [];
            for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++)
                try {
                    for (let value = value; ; ) break;
                } catch (error) {
                    results.push(error.name);
                }
            return results;
        }

        function forOfHeadInIf() {
            const results = [];
            for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
                try {
                    if (i >= 0) for (let value of i === 0 ? [i] : [value]) results.push(value);
                } catch (error) {
                    results.push(error.name);
                }
            }
            return results;
        }

        function forInHeadInLabel() {
            const results = [];
            for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
                try {
                    label: for (let value in i === 0 ? { key: 1 } : value) results.push(value);
                } catch (error) {
                    results.push(error.name);
                }
            }
            return results;
        }

        expect(forLoopHead()).toEqual(["ReferenceError", "ReferenceError"]);
        expect(forOfHeadInIf()).toEqual([0, "ReferenceError"]);
        expect(forInHeadInLabel()).toEqual(["key", "ReferenceError"]);
    });

    test("code that a function does not hold the locals of", () => {
        expect(
            eval(`
                const results = [];
                for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
                    try {
                        results.push(value);
                    } catch (error) {
                        results.push(error.name);
                    }
                    let value = i;
                }
                results;
            `)
        ).toEqual(["ReferenceError", "ReferenceError"]);

        const results = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
            class C {
                static {
                    for (let j = 0; j < 2; j++) {

                            results.push(value);
                        } catch (error) {
                            results.push(error.name);
                        }
                        let value = j;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        expect(results).toEqual(["ReferenceError", "ReferenceError", "ReferenceError", "ReferenceError"]);
    });

    test("for-in and for-of patterns that read their own bindings", () => {
        function run(loop) {
            const results = [];
            try {
                loop(results);
            } catch (error) {
                results.push(error.name);
            }
            return results;
        }

        expect(
            run(results => {
                for (let [a = b, b] of [
                    [1, 2],
                    [undefined, 3],
                ])
                    results.push(a);
            })
        ).toEqual([1, "ReferenceError"]);
        expect(
            run(results => {
                for (let [a = a] of [[1], []]) results.push(a);
            })
        ).toEqual([1, "ReferenceError"]);
        expect(
            run(results => {
                for (const { a = b, b } of [{ a: 1, b: 2 }, { b: 3 }]) results.push(a);
            })
        ).toEqual([1, "ReferenceError"]);
        expect(
            run(results => {
                for (let { [b]: a, b } of [{ x: 1, b: "x" }, { b: "y" }]) results.push(a);
            })
        ).toEqual(["ReferenceError"]);
        expect(
            run(results => {
                for (let [a = b, b] in { ab: 1, "": 2 }) results.push(a);
            })
        ).toEqual(["a", "ReferenceError"]);
    });

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/many-cache-sites.js
// The sites of a function past the last one of a cache table share one slot. What one of them sees must never give
// another one a wrong value.

test("property lookups past the last cache slot", () => {
    const count = 70000;
    const f = new Function(
        "a",
        "b",
        "let s = 0;" + "s += a.x;".repeat(count) + "s += a.y; s += b.z; s += a.x; s += b.w; return s;"
    );
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; ++i) {
        expect(f({ x: 1, y: 2 }, { z: 3, w: 4 })).toBe(count + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4);
        expect(f({ y: 20, x: 10 }, { w: 40, z: 30 })).toBe(count * 10 + 10 + 20 + 30 + 40);
    }
});

test("dynamic global variable reads past the last cache slot", () => {
    globalThis.manyCacheSitesOne = 1;
    globalThis.manyCacheSitesTwo = 2;
    const count = 70000;
    const f = new Function(
        "let s = 0;" +
            "s += manyCacheSitesOne;".repeat(count) +
            "s += manyCacheSitesTwo; s += manyCacheSitesOne; return s;"
    );
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; ++i) {
        expect(f()).toBe(count + 2 + 1);
    }
    globalThis.manyCacheSitesTwo = 5;
    expect(f()).toBe(count + 5 + 1);
});

test("the shared slot outlives the functions that use it", () => {
    const count = 70000;
    const makeFunction = () => new Function("a", "let s = 0;" + "s += a.y;".repeat(count) + "return s;");
    for (let i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        expect(makeFunction()({ x: 1, y: 2 })).toBe(count * 2);
        gc();
    }
    const getX = new Function("o", "let s = 0;" + "s += o.x;".repeat(1000) + "return s;");
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        expect(getX({ x: 1, y: 2 })).toBe(1000);
    }
    const f = makeFunction();
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        expect(f({ x: 1, y: 2 })).toBe(count * 2);
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/many-functions-and-literal-properties.js
// Bytecode holds the index of a function and the slot of an object literal property in 16 bits. Past that, the code
// takes another way, which must give the same results.

test("functions of an executable past the first 65536", () => {
    const count = 66000;
    let source = "return [";
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) source += `() => ${i},`;
    source +=
        "function named() { return 'named'; }, { method() { return super.toString === Object.prototype.toString; } }];";
    const functions = new Function(source)();
    expect(functions).toHaveLength(count + 2);
    for (const i of [0, 1, 65534, 65535, 65536, 65537, count - 1]) {
        expect(functions[i]()).toBe(i);
    }
    expect(functions[count]()).toBe("named");
    expect(functions[count].name).toBe("named");
    expect(functions[count + 1].method()).toBeTrue();
});

test("properties of an object literal past the first 65536", () => {
    const count = 66000;
    let source = "return {";
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) source += `p${i}: ${i},`;
    source += "};";
    const make = new Function(source);
    // NB: The second and later literals start out with the shape the first one ended up with.
    for (let run = 0; run < 3; ++run) {
        const object = make();
        const keys = Object.keys(object);
        expect(keys).toHaveLength(count);
        for (const i of [0, 1, 65534, 65535, 65536, 65537, count - 1]) {
            expect(keys[i]).toBe(`p${i}`);
            expect(object[`p${i}`]).toBe(i);
        }
    }
});

test("object literals of an executable past the last shape cache slot", () => {
    const count = 66000;
    let source = "const objects = [];";
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) source += `objects.push({ a: ${i}, b: ${i + 1} });`;
    source += "return objects;";
    const make = new Function(source);
    for (let run = 0; run < 3; ++run) {
        const objects = make();
        for (const i of [0, 65534, 65535, 65536, count - 1]) {
            expect(Object.keys(objects[i])).toEqual(["a", "b"]);
            expect(objects[i].a).toBe(i);
            expect(objects[i].b).toBe(i + 1);
        }
    }
});

test("entry module can suspend on an async wait", () => {
    const evaluation = evaluateModule("./modules/atomics-wait-async-entry.mjs");
    expect(evaluation).toBeInstanceOf(Promise);
    expect(globalThis.asyncWaitModuleResult).toBeUndefined();
    gc();
    runAsyncWaitJobs();
    expect(globalThis.asyncWaitModuleResult).toBe("timed-out");
});

test("entry module evaluation does not block a promise reaction", () => {
    globalThis.asyncWaitModuleResult = undefined;
    const order = [];
    Promise.resolve().then(() => {
        evaluateModule("./modules/atomics-wait-async-entry.mjs").then(() => {
            order.push(globalThis.asyncWaitModuleResult);
        });
        order.push("evaluation returned");
    });
    Promise.resolve().then(() => order.push("next reaction"));
    runAsyncWaitJobs();
    expect(order).toEqual(["evaluation returned", "next reaction", "timed-out"]);
});

test("entry module rejection after an async wait is observable", () => {
    let message;
    evaluateModule("./modules/atomics-wait-async-entry-reject.mjs").catch(error => {
        message = error.message;
    });
    runAsyncWaitJobs();
    expect(message).toBe("module failed after waiting");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/modules/basic-modules.js
// Because you can't easily load modules directly we load them via here and check
// if they passed by checking the result

function validTestModule(filename) {
    if (!filename.endsWith(".mjs") || !filename.startsWith("./")) {
        throw new ExpectationError(`Expected module name to start with './' and end with '.mjs' but got '${filename}'`);
    }
}

function expectModulePassed(filename, options = undefined) {
    validTestModule(filename);

    let moduleLoaded = false;
    let moduleResult = null;
    let thrownError = null;

    import(filename, options)
        .then(result => {
            moduleLoaded = true;
            moduleResult = result;
            expect(moduleResult).toHaveProperty("passed", true);
        })
        .catch(error => {
            thrownError = error;
        });

    runQueuedPromiseJobs();

    if (thrownError) {
        throw thrownError;
    }

    expect(moduleLoaded).toBeTrue();
    return moduleResult;
}

function expectedModuleToThrowSyntaxError(filename, message) {
    validTestModule(filename);

    let moduleLoaded = false;
    let thrownError = null;

    import(filename)
        .then(() => {
            moduleLoaded = true;
        })
        .catch(error => {
            thrownError = error;
        });

    runQueuedPromiseJobs();

    if (thrownError) {
        expect(() => {
            throw thrownError;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, message);
    } else {
        throw new ExpectationError(
            `Expected module: '${filename}' to fail to load with a syntax error but did not throw.`
        );
    }
}

describe("testing behavior", () => {
    // To ensure the other tests are interpreter correctly we first test the underlying
    // mechanisms so these tests don't use expectModulePassed.

    test("can load a module", () => {
        let passed = false;
        let error = null;

        import("./empty.mjs")
            .then(() => {
                passed = true;
            })
            .catch(err => {
                error = err;
            });

        runQueuedPromiseJobs();
        if (error) throw error;

        expect(passed).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("can load a module twice", () => {
        let passed = false;
        let error = null;

        import("./empty.mjs")
            .then(() => {
                passed = true;
            })
            .catch(err => {
                error = err;
            });

        runQueuedPromiseJobs();
        if (error) throw error;

        expect(passed).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("can retrieve exported value", () => {
        async function getValue(filename) {
            const imported = await import(filename);
            expect(imported).toHaveProperty("passed", true);
        }

        let passed = false;
        let error = null;

        getValue("./single-const-export.mjs")
            .then(obj => {
                passed = true;
            })
            .catch(err => {
                error = err;
            });

        runQueuedPromiseJobs();

        if (error) throw error;

        expect(passed).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("reads the specifier before evaluating the options", () => {
        let specifier = "./empty.mjs";
        let passed = false;
        let error = null;

        import(specifier, ((specifier = "./does-not-exist.mjs"), undefined))
            .then(() => {
                passed = true;
            })
            .catch(err => {
                error = err;
            });

        runQueuedPromiseJobs();
        if (error) throw error;

        expect(passed).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("expectModulePassed works", () => {
        expectModulePassed("./single-const-export.mjs");
    });

    test("can call expectModulePassed with options", () => {
        expectModulePassed("./single-const-export.mjs", { key: "value" });

describe("basic behavior", () => {
    test("can import json modules (with import function)", () => {
        let passed = false;
        let error = null;
        let result = null;

        import("./json-module.json", { with: { type: "json" } })
            .then(jsonObj => {
                passed = true;
                result = jsonObj;
            })
            .catch(err => {
                error = err;
            });

        runQueuedPromiseJobs();

        if (error) throw error;

        console.log(JSON.stringify(result));
        expect(passed).toBeTrue();

        expect(result).not.toBeNull();
        expect(result).not.toBeUndefined();

        const jsonResult = result.default;
        expect(jsonResult).not.toBeNull();
        expect(jsonResult).not.toBeUndefined();

        expect(jsonResult).toHaveProperty("value", "value");
        expect(jsonResult).toHaveProperty("array", [1, 2, 3]);
        expect(jsonResult).toHaveProperty("map", { innerValue: "innerValue" });
    });

    test("can import json modules (with import statement)", () => {
        let passed = false;
        let error = null;
        let result = null;

        import("./json-module.mjs")
            .then(jsonObj => {
                passed = true;
                result = jsonObj;
            })
            .catch(err => {
                error = err;
            });

        runQueuedPromiseJobs();

        if (error) throw error;

        console.log(JSON.stringify(result));
        expect(passed).toBeTrue();

        expect(result).not.toBeNull();
        expect(result).not.toBeUndefined();

        const jsonResult = result.default;
        expect(jsonResult).not.toBeNull();
        expect(jsonResult).not.toBeUndefined();

        expect(jsonResult).toHaveProperty("value", "value");
        expect(jsonResult).toHaveProperty("array", [1, 2, 3]);
        expect(jsonResult).toHaveProperty("map", { innerValue: "innerValue" });
    });
});

for (const usePromise of [false, true]) {
    const order = [];
    Promise.resolve()
        .then(() => order.push("tick 1"))
        .then(() => order.push("tick 2"))
        .then(() => order.push("tick 3"))
        .then(() => order.push("tick 4"));

    .then(() => orderBeforeAwait.push("tick 4"));

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/modules/top-level-for-await.mjs
const log = [];

for await (const value of [1, Promise.resolve(2)]) {
    log.push(value);
}

async function* letters() {
    try {
        yield "a";
        yield "b";
        yield "c";
    } finally {
        log.push("closed");
    }
}

for await (const letter of letters()) {
    log.push(letter);
    if (letter === "b") break;
}

async function* failing() {
    yield "first";
    throw new Error("iterator failed");
}

try {
    for await (const value of failing()) {
        log.push(value);
    }
} catch (error) {
    log.push(error.message);
}

outer: for await (const number of [1, 2]) {
    for await (const letter of ["x", "y"]) {
        if (letter === "y") continue outer;
        log.push(`${number}${letter}`);
    }
}

export const result = log;
export const passed = true;

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/name-table-indices-past-instruction-fields.js
// Instructions hold the indices of names in 16 bits. Larger ones go in another instruction before them, which must
// give the same results.

const count = 65400;

test("identifiers of an executable past the first 65280", () => {
    let source = "";
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) source += `typeof g${i};`;
    source += "wideGlobal = wideGlobal + 1;";
    source += "const wideFunction = function () { return wideGlobal; };";
    source += "const WideClass = class { static value() { return wideGlobal; } };";
    source += "let error; try { wideMissing; } catch (e) { error = e; }";
    source += "return [wideFunction.name, wideFunction(), WideClass.name, WideClass.value(), error.message];";
    globalThis.wideGlobal = 1;
    const f = new Function(source);
    expect(f()).toEqual(["wideFunction", 2, "WideClass", 2, "'wideMissing' is not defined"]);
    expect(f()).toEqual(["wideFunction", 3, "WideClass", 3, "'wideMissing' is not defined"]);
    delete globalThis.wideGlobal;
});

test("identifiers past the first 65280 in a function with more frame slots than operands can name", () => {
    let source = "";
    for (let i = 0; i < 300; ++i) source += `let l${i} = ${i};`;
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) source += `typeof g${i};`;
    source += "wideSpilled = l299; return [wideSpilled, l0 + l150];";
    const f = new Function(source);
    expect(f()).toEqual([299, 150]);
    expect(globalThis.wideSpilled).toBe(299);
    delete globalThis.wideSpilled;
});

test("property keys of an executable past the first 65280", () => {
    let source = "const o = {};";
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) source += `o.k${i};`;
    source += "o.wideKey = 1; o.wideKey += 1; return [o.wideKey, delete o.wideKey, o.wideKey];";
    const f = new Function(source);
    expect(f()).toEqual([2, true, undefined]);
    expect(f()).toEqual([2, true, undefined]);
});

test("strings of an executable past the first 65280", () => {
    let source = "const regexps = [];";
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) source += `/s${i}/;`;
    source += "return /wide/gi;";
    const f = new Function(source);
    const regexp = f();
    expect(regexp.source).toBe("wide");
    expect(regexp.flags).toBe("gi");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/nested-computed-destructuring-assignment.js
test("nested computed object pattern preserves the assignment result", () => {
    let value;
    const key = "length";
    const source = { x: "abc" };
    const result = ({
        x: { [key]: value },
    } = source);
    expect(value).toBe(3);
    expect(result).toBe(source);
});

test("nested computed object pattern preserves the callee, receiver, and earlier arguments", () => {
    let value;
    const key = "length";
    const source = { x: "abc" };
    const receiver = {
        check(first, result, last) {
            expect(this).toBe(receiver);
            expect(first).toBe("before");
            expect(result).toBe(source);
            expect(last).toBe(3);
            return "called";
        },
    };
    expect(
        receiver.check(
            "before",
            ({
                x: { [key]: value },
            } = source),
            value
        )
    ).toBe("called");
});

test("computed object pattern in an array preserves the assignment result", () => {
    let value;
    const key = "length";
    const source = ["abc"];
    const result = ([{ [key]: value }] = source);
    expect(value).toBe(3);
    expect(result).toBe(source);
});

test("computed object pattern in an array rest element preserves the assignment result", () => {
    let first, length;
    const key = "length";
    const source = [1, 2, 3];
    const result = ([first, ...{ [key]: length }] = source);
    expect(first).toBe(1);
    expect(length).toBe(2);
    expect(result).toBe(source);
});

test("nested computed object pattern evaluates keys, defaults, and rest in order", () => {
    let value, rest;
    const events = [];
    const source = {
        get x() {
            events.push("outer getter");
            return {
                get a() {
                    events.push("value getter");
                    return undefined;
                },
                b: 2,
            };
        },
    };
    const key = {
        toString() {
            events.push("key conversion");
            return "a";
        },
    };
    const result = ({
        x: { [(events.push("key expression"), key)]: value = (events.push("default"), 7), ...rest },
    } = source);
    expect(result).toBe(source);
    expect(value).toBe(7);
    expect(rest).toEqual({ b: 2 });
    expect(events).toEqual(["outer getter", "key expression", "key conversion", "value getter", "default"]);
});

test("object literals in computed keys and nested defaults still create objects", () => {
    let value;
    const source = {};
    const result = ({ x: { [{ key: "a" }.key]: value } = { a: 9 } } = source);
    expect(result).toBe(source);
    expect(value).toBe(9);
});

test("computed object patterns in arrow parameters preserve their defaults", () => {
    const key = "length";
    const read = ({ x: { [key]: value } } = { x: "abc" }) => value;
    expect(read()).toBe(3);
    expect(read({ x: "hello" })).toBe(5);
});

test("nested array pattern that starts with a rest element preserves the assignment result", () => {

test("nested array pattern that starts with a rest element preserves the values around it", () => {

    expect(array).toEqual([1, [[2]], 3]);
    expect(o.x).toEqual([2]);

    expect(object).toEqual({ a: 1, b: [[3, 4]] });

test("nested array pattern that starts with a rest element preserves the callee and earlier arguments", () => {
    const o = {};
    const source = { p: [1] };
    const receiver = {
        check(first, result) {
            expect(this).toBe(receiver);
            expect(first).toBe("before");
            expect(result).toBe(source);
            return "called";
        },
    };
    expect(
        receiver.check(
            "before",
            ({
                p: [...o.x],
            } = source)
        )
    ).toBe("called");
    expect(o.x).toEqual([1]);
});

test("rest elements with targets of every kind at the start of a nested array pattern", () => {
    const key = "k";
    const o = {};
    class Base {
        set x(value) {
            this.fromSuper = value;
        }
    }
    class Derived extends Base {
        #p;
        run() {
            return [
                ([[...o[key]]] = [[1]]),
                ([[...super.x]] = [[2]]),
                ([[...this.#p]] = [[3]]),
                ([[...[o.a]]] = [[4]]),
                ([[...{ [key]: o.b }]] = [[5]]),
                ([[...o.c] = [6]] = []),
                ([...[...o.d]] = [7]),
                ([, [...o.e]] = [0, [8]]),
            ].length;
        }
        get p() {
            return this.#p;
        }
    }
    const derived = new Derived();
    expect(derived.run()).toBe(8);
    expect(o.k).toEqual([1]);
    expect(derived.fromSuper).toEqual([2]);
    expect(derived.p).toEqual([3]);
    expect(o.a).toBe(4);
    expect(o.b).toBeUndefined();
    expect(o.c).toEqual([6]);
    expect(o.d).toEqual([7]);
    expect(o.e).toEqual([8]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/null-or-undefined-access.js
test("null/undefined object", () => {
    [null, undefined].forEach(value => {
        let foo = value;

        expect(() => {
            foo.bar;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, `Cannot access property "bar" on ${value} object "foo"`);

        expect(() => {
            foo.bar = 1;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, `Cannot access property "bar" on ${value} object "foo"`);

        expect(() => {
            foo[0];
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, `Cannot access property "0" on ${value} object "foo"`);

        expect(() => {
            foo[0] = 1;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, `Cannot access property "0" on ${value} object "foo"`);
    });
});

test("null/undefined object key", () => {
    [null, undefined].forEach(value => {
        let foo = { bar: value };

        expect(() => {
            foo.bar.baz;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, `Cannot access property "baz" on ${value} object "foo.bar"`);

        expect(() => {
            foo.bar.baz = 1;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, `Cannot access property "baz" on ${value} object "foo.bar"`);

        expect(() => {
            foo["bar"].baz;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, `Cannot access property "baz" on ${value} object "foo['bar']"`);

        expect(() => {
            foo["bar"].baz = 1;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, `Cannot access property "baz" on ${value} object "foo['bar']"`);
    });
});

test("null/undefined array index", () => {
    [null, undefined].forEach(value => {
        let foo = [value];
        let index = 0;

        expect(() => {
            foo[0].bar;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, `Cannot access property "bar" on ${value} object "foo[0]"`);

        expect(() => {
            foo[0].bar = 1;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, `Cannot access property "bar" on ${value} object "foo[0]"`);

        expect(() => {
            foo[index].bar;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, `Cannot access property "bar" on ${value} object "foo[index]"`);

        expect(() => {
            foo[index].bar = 1;
        }).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, `Cannot access property "bar" on ${value} object "foo[index]"`);
    });

describe("correct behavior", () => {
    test("numeric indexing", () => {
        const o = { 1: 23 };

        expect(o[1]).toBe(23);
        expect(o[1n]).toBe(23);
        expect(o["1"]).toBe(23);

        o[10] = "123";
        expect(o[10]).toBe("123");
        expect(o["10"]).toBe("123");

        o[10n] = "1234";
        expect(o[10]).toBe("1234");
        expect(o["10"]).toBe("1234");
    });

    test("string indexing", () => {
        let foo = "bar";

        const o = {
            foo,
            bar: "baz",
            qux: true ? 10 : 20,
            hello: "friends",
        };

        expect(o.foo).toBe("bar");
        expect(o["foo"]).toBe("bar");
        expect(o.qux).toBe(10);
        expect(o.hello).toBe("friends");
        expect(o["hello"]).toBe("friends");
    });

    test("symbol keys", () => {
        let object = {};
        let symbol = Symbol("foo");

        object[symbol] = 2;
        expect(object[symbol]).toBe(2);
    });

    test("numeric keys", () => {
        const hex = { 0x10: "16" };
        const oct = { 0o10: "8" };
        const bin = { 0b10: "2" };
        const float = { 0.5: "0.5" };

        expect(hex["16"]).toBe("16");
        expect(oct["8"]).toBe("8");
        expect(bin["2"]).toBe("2");
        expect(float["0.5"]).toBe("0.5");
    });

    test("computed properties", () => {
        const foo = "bar";
        const computed = "computed";
        const o = {
            [1 + 2]: 42,
            [`I am a ${computed} key`]: foo,
        };

        expect(o[3]).toBe(42);
        expect(o["I am a computed key"]).toBe("bar");
    });

    test("duplicate keys", () => {
        const o = {
            duplicate: "hello",
            duplicate: "world",
        };
        expect(o.duplicate).toBe("world");
    });

    test("assigning after creation", () => {
        const o = {};
        o.baz = "test";

        expect(o.baz).toBe("test");
        expect(o["baz"]).toBe("test");

        expect(o[-1]).toBeUndefined();
        o[-1] = "hello friends";
        expect(o[-1]).toBe("hello friends");
        expect(o["-1"]).toBe("hello friends");
    });

    test("floating point keys", () => {
        const math = { 3.14: "pi" };
        expect(math["3.14"]).toBe("pi");
        expect(math[3.14]).toBe("pi");
    });

    test("keywords as property keys", () => {
        const o2 = {
            return: 1,
            yield: 1,
            for: 1,
            catch: 1,
            break: 1,
        };

        expect(o2.return).toBe(1);
        expect(o2.yield).toBe(1);
        expect(o2.for).toBe(1);
        expect(o2.catch).toBe(1);
        expect(o2.break).toBe(1);
    });

    test("prototypical inheritance", () => {
        var base = {
            getNumber() {
                return 10;
            },
        };

        var derived = {
            getNumber() {
                return 20 + super.getNumber();
            },
        };

        Object.setPrototypeOf(derived, base);
        expect(derived.getNumber()).toBe(30);
    });

    test("assigning object expression with destination referenced in object expression", () => {
        function go(i) {
            var i = { f: i };
            return i;
        }
        expect(go("foo")).toEqual({ f: "foo" });
    });
});

describe("side effects", () => {
    let a;
    const append = x => {
        a.push(x);
    };

    test("computed key side effects", () => {
        a = [];
        const o3 = { [append(1)]: 1, [append(2)]: 2, [append(3)]: 3 };
        expect(a).toHaveLength(3);
        expect(a[0]).toBe(1);
        expect(a[1]).toBe(2);
        expect(a[2]).toBe(3);
        expect(o3.undefined).toBe(3);
    });

    test("value side effects", () => {
        a = [];
        const o4 = { test: append(1), test: append(2), test: append(3) };
        expect(a).toHaveLength(3);
        expect(a[0]).toBe(1);
        expect(a[1]).toBe(2);
        expect(a[2]).toBe(3);
        expect(o4.test).toBeUndefined();
    });
});

describe("shorthanded properties with special names", () => {
    test("keywords cannot be used", () => {
        expect("({ function, })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ var, })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ const, })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ class, })").not.toEval();
    });

    test("reserved words are allowed in non-strict mode", () => {
        {
            var implements = 3;
            expect({ implements }).toEqual({ implements: 3 });
        }
        {
            var public = "a";
            expect({ public }).toEqual({ public: "a" });
        }
        {
            var let = 9;
            expect({ let }).toEqual({ let: 9 });
        }
        {
            var await = 8;
            expect({ await }).toEqual({ await: 8 });
        }
        {
            var async = 7;
            expect({ async }).toEqual({ async: 7 });
        }
        {
            var yield = 6;
            expect({ yield }).toEqual({ yield: 6 });
        }
    });

    test("reserved words are not allowed in strict mode", () => {
        expect('"use strict"; var implements = 3; ({ implements })').not.toEval();
        expect("\"use strict\"; var public = 'a'; ({ public })").not.toEval();
        expect('"use strict"; var let = 9; ({ let, })').not.toEval();
        expect('"use strict"; var yield = 6; ({ yield, })').not.toEval();
    });

    test("special non reserved words are allowed even in strict mode", () => {
        expect('"use strict"; var await = 8; ({ await, })').toEval();
        expect('"use strict"; var async = 7; ({ async, })').toEval();
    });

    test("async functions as properties", () => {
        expect("({ async async() {} });").toEval();
        expect('"use strict"; ({ async async() {} });').toEval();

        expect("({ async async });").not.toEval();
        expect("({ async async, });").not.toEval();
        expect("({ async async() });").not.toEval();
        expect("({ async async: 0 });").not.toEval();
        expect("({ async async = 0 });").not.toEval();

        expect("({ async foo });").not.toEval();
        expect("({ async foo, });").not.toEval();
        expect("({ async foo() });").not.toEval();
        expect("({ async foo: 0 });").not.toEval();
        expect("({ async foo = 0 });").not.toEval();
    });
});

describe("errors", () => {
    test("syntax errors", () => {
        expect("({ foo: function() { super.bar; } })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ get ...foo })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ get... foo })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ get foo })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ get foo: bar })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ get [foo]: bar })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ get ...[foo] })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ get foo(bar) {} })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ set foo() {} })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ set foo(...bar) {} })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ set foo(bar, baz) {} })").not.toEval();
        expect("({ ...foo: bar })").not.toEval();
    });
});

describe("naming of anon functions", () => {
    test("method has name", () => {
        expect({ func() {} }.func.name).toBe("func");
    });

    test("getter has name", () => {
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor({ get func() {} }, "func").get.name).toBe("get func");
    });

    test("setter has name", () => {
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor({ set func(v) {} }, "func").set.name).toBe("set func");
    });

    test("anon function property", () => {
        expect({ func: function () {} }.func.name).toBe("func");
    });

    test("anon function from within parenthesis", () => {
        expect({ func: function () {} }.func.name).toBe("func");
    });

    test("anon function from indirect expression", () => {
        expect({ func: (0, function () {}) }.func.name).toBe("");
    });

    test("function from function call does not get named", () => {
        function f() {
            return function () {};
        }

        expect(f().name).toBe("");
        expect({ func: f() }.func.name).toBe("");
    });
});

test("numeric properties", () => {
    const i32Max = 2 ** 31 - 1;
    const u32Max = 2 ** 32 - 1;
    const o = {
        [-1]: "foo",
        0: "foo",
        1: "foo",
        [i32Max - 1]: "foo",
        [i32Max]: "foo",
        [i32Max + 1]: "foo",
        [u32Max - 1]: "foo",
        [u32Max]: "foo",
        [u32Max + 1]: "foo",
    };
    // Numeric properties come first in Object.getOwnPropertyNames()'s output,
    // which means we can test what each is treated as internally.
    expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(o)).toEqual([
        // Numeric properties
        "0",
        "1",
        "2147483646",
        "2147483647",
        "2147483648",
        "4294967294",
        // Non-numeric properties
        "-1",
        "4294967295", // >= 2^32 - 1
        "4294967296", // >= 2^32 - 1
    ]);
});
