    expect(parseInt("0")).toBe(0);
    expect(parseInt("100")).toBe(100);
    expect(parseInt("1000", 16)).toBe(4096);
    expect(parseInt("0xF", 16)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt("F", 16)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt("17", 8)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt(021, 8)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt("015", 10)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt(15.99, 10)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt("15,123", 10)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt("FXX123", 16)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt("1111", 2)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt("15 * 3", 10)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt("15e2", 10)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt("15px", 10)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt("12", 13)).toBe(15);
    expect(parseInt("Hello", 8)).toBeNaN();
    expect(parseInt("546", 2)).toBeNaN();
    expect(parseInt("-F", 16)).toBe(-15);
    expect(parseInt("-0F", 16)).toBe(-15);
    expect(parseInt("-0XF", 16)).toBe(-15);
    expect(parseInt(-15.1, 10)).toBe(-15);
    expect(parseInt("-17", 8)).toBe(-15);
    expect(parseInt("-15", 10)).toBe(-15);
    expect(parseInt("-1111", 2)).toBe(-15);
    expect(parseInt("-15e1", 10)).toBe(-15);
    expect(parseInt("-12", 13)).toBe(-15);
    expect(parseInt(4.7, 10)).toBe(4);
    expect(parseInt("0e0", 16)).toBe(224);
    expect(parseInt("123_456")).toBe(123);
    expect(parseInt("UVWXYZ", 36)).toBe(1867590395);
    expect(parseInt(4.7 * 1e22, 10)).toBe(4);
    expect(parseInt(0.00000000000434, 10)).toBe(4);
    expect(parseInt(0.0000001, 11)).toBe(1);
    expect(parseInt(0.000000124, 10)).toBe(1);
    expect(parseInt(1e-7, 10)).toBe(1);
    expect(parseInt(1000000000000100000000, 10)).toBe(1);
    expect(parseInt(123000000000010000000000, 10)).toBe(1);
    expect(parseInt(1e21, 10)).toBe(1);
    expect(parseInt("900719925474099267n")).toBe(900719925474099300);
    expect(parseInt("18446462598732840000")).toBe(0xffff000000000000);
});

test("parseInt() rounds long digit runs correctly", () => {
    expect(parseInt("-900719925474099267")).toBe(-900719925474099300);
    expect(parseInt("0000000000000000900719925474099267")).toBe(900719925474099300);
    expect(parseInt("9".repeat(400))).toBe(Infinity);

    expect(parseInt("200000000000011", 16)).toBe(2 ** 57 + 32);
    expect(parseInt("fffffffffffffc", 16)).toBe(2 ** 56);
    expect(parseInt("1" + "0".repeat(52) + "11", 2)).toBe(2 ** 54 + 4);
    expect(parseInt("7".repeat(31), 8)).toBe(2 ** 93);
    expect(parseInt("v".repeat(20), 32)).toBe(2 ** 100);
    expect(parseInt("f".repeat(300), 16)).toBe(Infinity);
});

test("parseInt() radix is coerced to a number", () => {
    const obj = {
        valueOf() {
            return 8;
        },
    };
    expect(parseInt("11", obj)).toBe(9);
    obj.valueOf = function () {
        return 1;
    };
    expect(parseInt("11", obj)).toBeNaN();
    obj.valueOf = function () {
        return Infinity;
    };
    expect(parseInt("11", obj)).toBe(11);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/parser-line-terminators.js
/*
These tests deliberately produce syntax errors to check what line the parser thinks we're on.
Note that line numbers are higher than you might expect as the parsed code is:

function anonymous(
) {
<code>
}

⚠ PLEASE MAKE SURE TO NOT LET YOUR EDITOR REMOVE THE LS/PS LINE TERMINATORS!
*/

test("LINE FEED is a line terminator", () => {
    expect(() => {
        Function("\n\n@");
    }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "Unexpected token '@'. Expected '}' (line: 4, column: 1)");
});

test("CARRIAGE RETURN is a line terminator", () => {
    expect(() => {
        Function("\r\r@");
    }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "Unexpected token '@'. Expected '}' (line: 4, column: 1)");
});

test("LINE SEPARATOR is a line terminator", () => {
    expect(() => {
        Function("  @");
    }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "Unexpected token '@'. Expected '}' (line: 4, column: 1)");
});

test("PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR is a line terminator", () => {
    expect(() => {
        Function("  @");
    }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "Unexpected token '@'. Expected '}' (line: 4, column: 1)");
});

test("CR LF is counted as only one line terminator", () => {
    expect(() => {
        Function("\r\n\r\n@");
    }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "Unexpected token '@'. Expected '}' (line: 4, column: 1)");
});

test("LF/CR are not allowed in string literal", () => {
    expect(() => {
        Function(`"
        "`);
    }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "Unterminated string literal");
});

test("LS/PS are allowed in string literal", () => {
    expect(`" "`).toEval();
    expect(`" "`).toEval();
});

test("line terminators can be mixed (but please don't)", () => {
    expect(() => {
        Function("\r \r\n \n\r@");
    }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "Unexpected token '@'. Expected '}' (line: 8, column: 1)");
});

test("all line terminators are valid for line continuations", () => {
    expect(Function('return "a\\\nb"')()).toBe("ab");
    expect(Function('return "a\\\rb"')()).toBe("ab");
    expect(Function('return "a\\\r\nb"')()).toBe("ab");
    expect(Function('return "a\\ b"')()).toBe("ab");
    expect(Function('return "a\\ b"')()).toBe("ab");
});

test("template-literals raw and real value", () => {
    let lastTemplate;
    let lastRaw;

    function tag(cs) {
        lastTemplate = cs[0];
        lastRaw = cs.raw[0];
    }

    function checkTemplate(string_value, expected_template, expected_raw) {
        eval("tag`" + string_value + "`");
        expect(lastTemplate).toBe(expected_template);
        expect(lastRaw).toBe(expected_raw);
    }

    checkTemplate("", "", "");
    checkTemplate("\n", "\n", "\n");
    checkTemplate("\r", "\n", "\n");
    checkTemplate("\r\n", "\n", "\n");
    checkTemplate("\n\r\n", "\n\n", "\n\n");

    checkTemplate("a\\\nb", "ab", "a\\\nb");
    checkTemplate("a\\\rb", "ab", "a\\\nb");
    checkTemplate("a\\ b", "ab", "a\\ b");
    checkTemplate("a\\ b", "ab", "a\\ b");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/permanently-screwed-by-eval.js
test("basic that non-strict direct eval() prevents non-local access caching", () => {
    function foo(do_eval) {
        var c = 1;
        function bar(do_eval) {
            if (do_eval) eval("var c = 2;");
            return c;
        }
        return bar(do_eval);
    }

    expect(foo(false)).toBe(1);
    expect(foo(true)).toBe(2);
});

        var c;
        eval("var a = 'eval'");
        a += "!";
        return [a, b()];
    }
    expect(foo("parameter")).toEqual(["eval!", "parameter"]);
});

    function foo(a, b = 1) {
        var c;
        {
            eval("function a() {}");
        }
        return typeof a;
    }
    expect(foo(1)).toBe("function");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/polymorphic-property-caches.js
const readValue = object => object.value;

describe("polymorphic property caches", () => {
    test("own and inherited data properties of objects with different shapes", () => {
        const prototype = { value: "inherited" };
        const objects = [{ value: 1 }, { other: 0, value: 2 }, Object.create(prototype), { a: 0, b: 0, value: 4 }];
        for (let round = 0; round < 3; ++round) {
            expect(objects.map(readValue)).toEqual([1, 2, "inherited", 4]);
        }
        prototype.value = "changed";
        expect(objects.map(readValue)).toEqual([1, 2, "changed", 4]);
        Object.defineProperty(prototype, "value", { get: () => "getter" });
        expect(objects.map(readValue)).toEqual([1, 2, "getter", 4]);
    });

    test("prototype chains that change after being cached", () => {
        const base = { value: "base" };
        const middle = Object.create(base);
        const objects = [{ value: 1 }, { x: 0, value: 2 }, Object.create(middle), { y: 0, value: 4 }];
        for (let round = 0; round < 3; ++round) expect(readValue(objects[2])).toBe("base");
        middle.value = "middle";
        expect(objects.map(readValue)).toEqual([1, 2, "middle", 4]);
        delete middle.value;
        expect(objects.map(readValue)).toEqual([1, 2, "base", 4]);
        Object.setPrototypeOf(middle, { value: "replaced" });
        expect(objects.map(readValue)).toEqual([1, 2, "replaced", 4]);
    });

    test("accessors, missing properties and dictionary objects", () => {
        let calls = 0;
        const withGetter = {
            get value() {
                ++calls;
                return "getter";
            },
        };
        const dictionary = {};
        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) dictionary["p" + i] = i;
        dictionary.value = "dictionary";
        const objects = [{ value: 1 }, withGetter, { missing: true }, dictionary];
        for (let round = 0; round < 3; ++round) {
            expect(objects.map(readValue)).toEqual([1, "getter", undefined, "dictionary"]);
        }
        expect(calls).toBe(3);
        delete dictionary.p50;
        dictionary.value = "changed";
        expect(objects.map(readValue)).toEqual([1, "getter", undefined, "changed"]);
        delete dictionary.value;
        expect(readValue(dictionary)).toBeUndefined();
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/primitive-property-access-caches.js
// Indices of strings and named properties of primitives have fast paths in the interpreter. These tests run each
// access site many times, so that the fast paths and their caches are used, and then change what they find.

const iterations = 50;

describe("indices of strings", () => {
    test("ASCII and other code units, and indices out of range", () => {
        function at(string, index) {
            return string[index];
        }
        const string = "abé\u{1F600}";
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(at(string, 0)).toBe("a");
            expect(at(string, 1)).toBe("b");
            expect(at(string, 2)).toBe("é");
            expect(at(string, 3)).toBe("\ud83d");
            expect(at(string, 4)).toBe("\ude00");
            expect(at(string, 5)).toBeUndefined();
            expect(at(string, -1)).toBeUndefined();
            expect(at("x".repeat(100) + "y", 100)).toBe("y");
        }
    });

    test("indices beyond the string find the properties of String.prototype", () => {
        function at(string, index) {
            return string[index];
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(at("abc", 5)).toBeUndefined();
        String.prototype[5] = "five";
        try {
            expect(at("abc", 5)).toBe("five");
            expect(at("abc", 1)).toBe("b");
        } finally {
            delete String.prototype[5];
        }
    });
});

describe("named properties of primitives", () => {
    test("methods of the prototype of each kind", () => {
        function method(value) {
            return value.toString;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) {
            expect(method("a")).toBe(String.prototype.toString);
            expect(method(1)).toBe(Number.prototype.toString);
            expect(method(true)).toBe(Boolean.prototype.toString);
            expect(method(1n)).toBe(BigInt.prototype.toString);
            expect(method(Symbol.iterator)).toBe(Symbol.prototype.toString);
        }
    });

    test("changes to the prototype are seen", () => {
        function get(value) {
            return value.shout;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(get("a")).toBeUndefined();
        String.prototype.shout = 1;
        try {
            for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(get("a")).toBe(1);
            Object.defineProperty(String.prototype, "shout", {
                get() {
                    "use strict";
                    return typeof this;
                },
                configurable: true,
            });
            expect(get("a")).toBe("string");
        } finally {
            delete String.prototype.shout;
        }
        expect(get("a")).toBeUndefined();
    });

    test("nullish bases still throw", () => {
        function get(value) {
            return value.foo;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < iterations; ++i) expect(get("a")).toBeUndefined();
        expect(() => get(null)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(() => get(undefined)).toThrow(TypeError);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/promise-capability-gc.js
test("resolving functions from a custom constructor survive garbage collection", () => {
    const settlements = [];

    function CustomConstructor(executor) {
        executor(
            value => settlements.push(`resolved ${value}`),
            reason => settlements.push(`rejected ${reason}`)
        );
    }

    collectGarbageOnEveryAllocation(() => {
        Promise.resolve.call(CustomConstructor, 1);
        Promise.reject.call(CustomConstructor, 2);
    });

    expect(settlements).toEqual(["resolved 1", "rejected 2"]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/property-caches-of-changing-shapes.js
// Some shapes gain properties in place, like those of functions creating their prototype
// lazily. Property caches remember the dictionary generation of every shape, so that
// their entries stop applying when that happens.

const readName = value => value.name;
const readLength = value => value.length;
const readMissing = value => value.missing;

test("own properties of functions before and after their prototype is created", () => {
    for (let round = 0; round < 50; ++round) {
        const functions = [function first(a) {}, function second(a, b) {}];
        expect(functions.map(readName)).toEqual(["first", "second"]);
        expect(functions.map(readMissing)).toEqual([undefined, undefined]);
        expect(functions[0].prototype.constructor).toBe(functions[0]);
        expect(functions.map(readName)).toEqual(["first", "second"]);
        expect(functions.map(readLength)).toEqual([1, 2]);
        expect(functions.map(readMissing)).toEqual([undefined, undefined]);
        functions[1].missing = "added";
        expect(functions.map(readMissing)).toEqual([undefined, "added"]);
    }
});

test("writes to own properties of functions", () => {
    function counter() {}
    counter.count = 0;
    const increment = target => {
        target.count = target.count + 1;
    };
    for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) increment(counter);
    expect(counter.prototype.constructor).toBe(counter);
    for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) increment(counter);
    expect(counter.count).toBe(200);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/property-lookup-cache-dead-cells.js
describe("property lookup cache entries whose cells were collected", () => {
    test("property found on a prototype that is no longer in the chain", () => {
        function makeMiddle() {
            return Object.create({ x: "inherited" });
        }
        function read(object) {
            return object.x;
        }

        const middle = makeMiddle();
        const receiver = Object.create(middle);
        receiver.y = "own";
        expect(read(receiver)).toBe("inherited");

        Object.setPrototypeOf(middle, null);
        gc();
        expect(read(receiver)).toBeUndefined();
    });

    test("property addition after a setter was defined on the prototype chain", () => {
        const base = {};
        const prototype = Object.create(base);
        function make() {
            const object = Object.create(prototype);
            object.x = 1;
            return object;
        }

        const plain = Object.create(prototype);
        const withX = make();

        let calls = 0;
        Object.defineProperty(base, "x", {
            set(value) {
                ++calls;
            },
        });
        gc();

        const object = make();
        expect(calls).toBe(1);
        expect(Object.hasOwn(object, "x")).toBeFalse();
        expect(Object.hasOwn(plain, "x")).toBeFalse();
        expect(withX.x).toBe(1);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/property-store-caches-respect-exotic-objects.js
describe("cached property additions do not bypass exotic [[Set]] behavior", () => {
    test("typed array with a named key", () => {
        function put(object, value) {
            object["-0"] = value;
        }
        put(Object.create(Int8Array.prototype), 1);
        const typedArray = new Int8Array(2);
        put(typedArray, 7);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(typedArray)).toEqual(["0", "1"]);
    });

    test("array length with a named key", () => {
        function put(object, value) {
            object.length = value;
        }
        put(Object.create(Array.prototype), 5);
        const array = [1, 2, 3];
        put(array, 1);
        expect(array).toEqual([1]);
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(array)).toEqual(["0", "length"]);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/property-store-caches-respect-non-writable-properties.js
describe("cached property stores do not write to non-writable properties", () => {
    function defineSetter(object) {
        Object.defineProperty(object, "x", { set(value) {} });
        return object;
    }

    function defineNonWritable(object) {
        Object.defineProperty(object, "x", { value: 1 });
        return object;
    }

    test("named key in strict mode", () => {
        function put(object, value) {
            "use strict";
            object.x = value;
        }
        put(defineSetter({}), 7);
        const victim = defineNonWritable({});
        expect(() => put(victim, 8)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(victim.x).toBe(1);
    });

    test("named key in sloppy mode", () => {
        function put(object, value) {
            object.x = value;
        }
        put(defineSetter({}), 7);
        const victim = defineNonWritable({});
        put(victim, 8);
        expect(victim.x).toBe(1);
    });

    test("setter that redefines itself as a non-writable property", () => {
        function put(object, value) {
            "use strict";
            object.x = value;
        }
        const object = {};
        Object.defineProperty(object, "x", {
            configurable: true,
            set(value) {
                Object.defineProperty(this, "x", { value: 1 });
            },
        });
        put(object, 5);
        expect(object.x).toBe(1);
        expect(() => put(object, 9)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(object.x).toBe(1);
    });

    test("global variable", () => {
        Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "nonWritableGlobalAfterSetter", {
            configurable: true,
            set(value) {
                Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "nonWritableGlobalAfterSetter", { value: 1, configurable: true });
            },
        });
        function put(value) {
            "use strict";
            nonWritableGlobalAfterSetter = value;
        }
        put(5);
        expect(nonWritableGlobalAfterSetter).toBe(1);
        expect(() => put(9)).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(nonWritableGlobalAfterSetter).toBe(1);
    });

    test("global variable update in strict mode", () => {
        Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "nonWritableGlobalAfterSetterUpdate", {
            configurable: true,
            set(value) {
                Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "nonWritableGlobalAfterSetterUpdate", {
                    value: 1,
                    configurable: true,
                });
            },
        });
        function increment() {
            "use strict";
            nonWritableGlobalAfterSetterUpdate++;
        }
        increment();
        expect(nonWritableGlobalAfterSetterUpdate).toBe(1);
        expect(() => increment()).toThrow(TypeError);
        expect(nonWritableGlobalAfterSetterUpdate).toBe(1);
    });

    test("global variable in sloppy mode", () => {
        Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "nonWritableGlobalAfterSetterSloppy", {
            configurable: true,
            set(value) {
                Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "nonWritableGlobalAfterSetterSloppy", {
                    value: 1,
                    configurable: true,
                });
            },
        });
        function put(value) {
            nonWritableGlobalAfterSetterSloppy = value;
        }
        put(5);
        expect(nonWritableGlobalAfterSetterSloppy).toBe(1);
        put(9);
        expect(nonWritableGlobalAfterSetterSloppy).toBe(1);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/prototype-transition-cache.js
// Objects made with a prototype get their shape through the VM's cache of
// recent prototype transitions, in front of the transition tables of shapes.

test("objects made with the same prototype share a shape", () => {
    const prototype = { greet() {} };
    expect(haveSameShape(Object.create(prototype), Object.create(prototype))).toBeTrue();
    expect(haveSameShape(Object.create(prototype), Object.create({}))).toBeFalse();
    class Point {}
    expect(haveSameShape(new Point(), new Point())).toBeTrue();
    expect(haveSameShape(/a/.exec("a"), /b/.exec("b"))).toBeTrue();
});

test("many prototypes", () => {
    const prototypes = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) prototypes.push({ index: i });
    for (let round = 0; round < 3; ++round) {
        for (let i = 0; i < prototypes.length; ++i) {
            const object = Object.create(prototypes[i]);
            expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(object)).toBe(prototypes[i]);
            expect(object.index).toBe(i);
        }
    }
});

test("shapes stay shared across garbage collection", () => {
    const prototype = {};
    const kept = Object.create(prototype);
    gc();
    expect(haveSameShape(Object.create(prototype), kept)).toBeTrue();
});

test("objects made with a prototype do not keep it alive once they are gone", () => {
    evaluateSource(`
        var __cachedTransitionPrototype = {};
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) Object.create(__cachedTransitionPrototype);
    `);
    const registry = new FinalizationRegistry(() => {});
    registry.register(globalThis.__cachedTransitionPrototype, "prototype");
    markAsGarbage("__cachedTransitionPrototype");
    gc();

    let collected = false;
    cleanupFinalizationRegistry(registry, () => {
        collected = true;
    });
    expect(collected).toBeTrue();

    // Prototypes made after the collection, which may reuse its cells, get shapes of their own.
    for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) {
        const prototype = { index: i };
        expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(Object.create(prototype))).toBe(prototype);
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/redefine-next-in-builtin-iterators.js
describe("redefine next() in built in iterators", () => {
    test("redefine next() in ArrayIteratorPrototype", () => {
        let arrayIteratorPrototype = Object.getPrototypeOf([].values());
        let originalNext = arrayIteratorPrototype.next;
        let counter = 0;
        arrayIteratorPrototype.next = function () {
            counter++;
            return originalNext.apply(this, arguments);
        };
        for (let i of [1, 2, 3]) {
        }
        expect(counter).toBe(4);
    });

    test("redefine next() in MapIteratorPrototype", () => {
        let m = new Map([
            [1, 1],
            [2, 2],
            [3, 3],
        ]);
        let mapIteratorPrototype = Object.getPrototypeOf(m.values());
        let originalNext = mapIteratorPrototype.next;
        let counter = 0;
        mapIteratorPrototype.next = function () {
            counter++;
            return originalNext.apply(this, arguments);
        };
        for (let v of m.values()) {
        }
        expect(counter).toBe(4);
    });

    test("redefine next() in SetIteratorPrototype", () => {
        let s = new Set([1, 2, 3]);
        let setIteratorPrototype = Object.getPrototypeOf(s.values());
        let originalNext = setIteratorPrototype.next;
        let counter = 0;
        setIteratorPrototype.next = function () {
            counter++;
            return originalNext.apply(this, arguments);
        };
        for (let v of s.values()) {
        }
        expect(counter).toBe(4);
    });

    test("redefine next() in %GeneratorPrototype%", () => {
        function* generator() {
            yield 1;
            yield 2;
            yield 3;
        }
        let generatorPrototype = Object.getPrototypeOf(generator.prototype);
        let originalNext = generatorPrototype.next;
        let counter = 0;
        generatorPrototype.next = function () {
            counter++;
            return originalNext.apply(this, arguments);
        };
        for (let v of generator()) {
        }
        expect(counter).toBe(4);
    });
});

describe("redefine next() in built in iterators", () => {
    test("override next() on individual Array iterator via setPrototypeOf", () => {
        const iter = [1, 2, 3][Symbol.iterator]();
        const originalNext = iter.next;
        let count = 0;
        const newProto = {
            next(...args) {
                count++;
                return originalNext.apply(this, args);
            },
            [Symbol.iterator]() {
                return this;
            },
        };
        Object.setPrototypeOf(iter, newProto);
        for (const v of iter) {
        }
        expect(count).toBe(4);
    });

            [1, 1],

// The text of a reference comes from the source when an error gets thrown, so that how the source is written matters.
const object = {
    m() {
        return this;
    },
    g: 1,
    K: function () {},
    a2: [1, 2],
    tag() {},
};
object.o = object;

function Constructor() {}
Constructor.prototype = object;
Constructor.nope = undefined;

class Base {}
Base.prototype.m = function () {
    return this;
};

const names = ["o", "u", "nk", "kg", "i0", "a2", "nf", "C", "K0", "f0", "tag", "it"];
const values = [
    object,
    undefined,
    "nope",
    "g",
    0,
    [1, 2],
    5,
    Constructor,
    Base,
    function () {},
    function () {},
    { [Symbol.iterator]: () => ({ next: () => ({ done: true }) }) },
];

function expectMessage(source, message) {
    const f = new Function(...names, source);
    expect(() => f.call(object, ...values)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, message);
}

        ['a2["z"]\n    .x', 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object "a2[\'z\']"'],
        ["a2['z'].x", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object "a2[\'z\']"'],
        ["a2['z']\n    .x", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object "a2[\'z\']"'],
        ["a2[`z`].x", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object "a2"'],
        ["a2[`z`]\n    .x", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object "a2"'],
        ["a2[this].x", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object "a2[this]"'],
        ["a2[this]\n    .x", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object "a2[this]"'],
        ["this.u0.x", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object "this.u0"'],
        ["this\n    .u0\n    .x", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object "this.u0"'],
        ["new C().nope.x", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object ".nope"'],
        ["new C(\n   )\n    .nope\n    .x", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object ".nope"'],
        ["new C().nope.x = 1", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object ".nope"'],
        ["new C(\n   )\n    .nope\n    .x\n    =\n    1", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object ".nope"'],
        ["new o.nope.x", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object "o.nope"'],
        ["new o\n    .nope\n    .x", 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object "o.nope"'],
    ];
    for (const [source, message] of cases) expectMessage(source, message);
});

test("references that are longer than what gets looked at", () => {
    const long = "a".repeat(5000);
    expect(new Function(`new '${long}'.nope();`)).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(new Function(`'${long}'.nope();`)).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(new Function(`var ${long} = {}; ${long}.nope();`)).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(new Function(`var ${long}; ${long}.nope = 1;`)).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(new Function(`[${long}].nope.x = 1; var ${long};`)).toThrow(TypeError);
});

test("source that looks like something else", () => {
    expectMessage("o /* ) */ .nope();", "undefined is not a function (evaluated from 'o.nope')");
    expectMessage("o // )\n  .nope();", "undefined is not a function (evaluated from 'o.nope')");
    expectMessage("o[')'].nope();", `Cannot access property "nope" on undefined object "o[')']"`);
    expectMessage("o[']'].nope();", `Cannot access property "nope" on undefined object "o[']']"`);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/reference-text-near-stack-limit.js
test("the text of a long chain of calls in an error near the call stack size limit", () => {
    const o = {
        m() {
            return o;
        },
    };
    const callee = new Function("o", "return o" + ".m()".repeat(200) + ".nope();");
    const base = new Function("o", "return o" + ".m()".repeat(200) + ".nope.x;");
    const calleeMessage = "undefined is not a function (evaluated from '<object>.nope')";
    const baseMessage = 'Cannot access property "x" on undefined object ".nope"';
    expect(() => callee(o)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, calleeMessage);
    expect(() => base(o)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, baseMessage);

    const messages = new Set();
    let levels = 0;
    function recurse() {
        try {
            Reflect.apply(recurse, null, []);
        } catch {}
        if (levels++ > 100) return;
        for (const chain of [callee, base]) {
            try {
                chain(o);
            } catch (error) {
                if (error instanceof TypeError) messages.add(error.message);
            }
        }
    }
    recurse();
    expect([...messages].sort()).toEqual([baseMessage, calleeMessage].sort());
});

test("the text of a reference in more brackets than a text keeps track of", () => {
    const a = { b: {} };
    const inBrackets = count => new Function("a", `${"(".repeat(count)}a.b${")".repeat(count)}.c.d;`);
    expect(() => inBrackets(6)(a)).toThrowWithMessage(
        TypeError,
        'Cannot access property "d" on undefined object "a.b.c"'
    );
    expect(() => inBrackets(10)(a)).toThrowWithMessage(
        TypeError,
        'Cannot access property "d" on undefined object ".c"'
    );
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regexp-literal-reparse-near-stack-limit.js
test("regular expression literals reparsed near the call stack size limit", () => {
    // How much stack is left when a reparse runs depends on the frames above it, so this tries several patterns.
    const patterns = [100, 200, 300].map(depth => "(".repeat(depth) + "x" + ")".repeat(depth));
    function recurse() {
        for (const pattern of patterns) {
            try {
                eval(`(/${pattern}/)`);
            } catch {}
        }
        recurse();
    }
    expect(recurse).toThrowWithMessage(InternalError, "Call stack size limit exceeded");
});

test("regular expression literals at the deepest nesting that the stack allows", () => {
    // The search tries the depth right above the deepest one that parses, which has the least stack to spare.
    // NB: How deep a literal parses depends on the frames above the eval, so each depth is tried only once.
    let low = 0;
    let high = 1 << 20;
    let errorAtHigh;
    while (low + 1 < high) {
        const middle = (low + high) >> 1;
        try {
            (0, eval)(`(/${"(".repeat(middle)}x${")".repeat(middle)}/)`);
            low = middle;
        } catch (error) {
            high = middle;
            errorAtHigh = error;
        }
    }
    expect(low).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(errorAtHigh).toBeInstanceOf(SyntaxError);
    expect(errorAtHigh.message.includes("Maximum parser recursion depth exceeded")).toBeTrue();
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regexp-sticky-anchored-exec.js
test("sticky literal exec and test stay anchored at lastIndex", () => {
    let literal = /foobar/y;

    literal.lastIndex = 0;
    expect(literal.exec("..foobar")).toBeNull();
    expect(literal.lastIndex).toBe(0);

    literal.lastIndex = 2;
    let match = literal.exec("..foobar");
    expect(match).not.toBeNull();
    expect(match[0]).toBe("foobar");
    expect(match.index).toBe(2);
    expect(match.input).toBe("..foobar");
    expect(literal.lastIndex).toBe(8);

    literal.lastIndex = 0;
    expect(literal.test("..foobar")).toBeFalse();
    expect(literal.lastIndex).toBe(0);

    literal.lastIndex = 2;
    expect(literal.test("..foobar")).toBeTrue();
    expect(literal.lastIndex).toBe(8);
});

test("sticky word-boundary literal stays anchored at lastIndex", () => {
    let word = /\bfoo\b/y;

    word.lastIndex = 2;
    expect(word.exec("xx foo yy")).toBeNull();
    expect(word.lastIndex).toBe(0);

    word.lastIndex = 3;
    let match = word.exec("xx foo yy");
    expect(match).not.toBeNull();
    expect(match[0]).toBe("foo");
    expect(match.index).toBe(3);
    expect(word.lastIndex).toBe(6);

    word.lastIndex = 2;
    expect(word.test("xx foo yy")).toBeFalse();
    expect(word.lastIndex).toBe(0);

    word.lastIndex = 3;
    expect(word.test("xx foo yy")).toBeTrue();
    expect(word.lastIndex).toBe(6);
});

test("sticky literal alternation respects source order at lastIndex", () => {
    let first_shorter = /foo|foobar/y;
    first_shorter.lastIndex = 0;
    let shorter_match = first_shorter.exec("foobar");
    expect(shorter_match).not.toBeNull();
    expect(shorter_match[0]).toBe("foo");
    expect(first_shorter.lastIndex).toBe(3);

    let first_longer = /foobar|foo/y;
    first_longer.lastIndex = 0;
    let longer_match = first_longer.exec("foobar");
    expect(longer_match).not.toBeNull();
    expect(longer_match[0]).toBe("foobar");
    expect(first_longer.lastIndex).toBe(6);

    mismatch.lastIndex = 0;
    expect(mismatch.exec("xxbar")).toBeNull();
    expect(mismatch.lastIndex).toBe(0);

    mismatch.lastIndex = 2;
    let bar_match = mismatch.exec("xxbar");
    expect(bar_match).not.toBeNull();
    expect(bar_match[0]).toBe("bar");
    expect(bar_match.index).toBe(2);
    expect(mismatch.lastIndex).toBe(5);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regexp-unicode-sets-escapes.js
describe("escapes in a v-mode class", () => {
    test("every ClassSetReservedPunctuator can be escaped", () => {
        for (const punctuator of "&-!#%,:;<=>@`~") {
            const regex = new RegExp(`[\\${punctuator}]`, "v");
            expect(regex.test(punctuator)).toBeTrue();
            expect(regex.test("a")).toBeFalse();
        }
    });

    test("an escaped punctuator works in ranges and set operations", () => {
        expect(/[\&-\)]/v.test("'")).toBeTrue();
        expect(/[\p{L}--\&]/v.test("a")).toBeTrue();
        expect(/[\p{L}--\&]/v.test("&")).toBeFalse();
        expect(/[\&&&\&]/v.test("&")).toBeTrue();
        expect(/[\!\!]/v.test("!")).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("a control escape", () => {
        expect(/[\cJ]/v.test("\n")).toBeTrue();
        expect(/[\q{\cJ}]/v.test("\n")).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("\\q{} takes the same escapes", () => {
        expect(/[\q{\&}]/v.test("&")).toBeTrue();
        expect(/^[\q{a\!b}]$/v.test("a!b")).toBeTrue();
        expect(/[\q{\/}]/v.test("/")).toBeTrue();
        expect(/[\q{\^}]/v.test("^")).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("other escapes are still syntax errors", () => {
        const cases = [
            ["[\\_]", "invalid escape '\\_'"],
            ['[\\"]', `invalid escape '\\"'`],
            ["[\\']", "invalid escape '\\''"],
            ["[\\c1]", "invalid escape '\\c'"],
            ["[\\q{\\_}]", "invalid escape '\\_'"],
            ["[\\q{\\01}]", "invalid escape '\\0'"],
        ];
        for (const [pattern, message] of cases) {
            expect(() => new RegExp(pattern, "v")).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, message);
        }
    });
});

test("a reserved punctuator still can't be escaped outside a class", () => {
    expect(() => new RegExp("\\&", "v")).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "invalid escape '\\&'");
});

test("a reserved double punctuator still can't appear unescaped in a class", () => {
    expect(() => new RegExp("[!!]", "v")).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "invalid character class");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regexp-unicode-zero-width-surrogate-positions.js
for (const flag of ["u", "v"]) {
    test(`/${flag} zero-width searches skip surrogate interiors`, () => {
        const match = new RegExp("(?!😀)", flag).exec("😀");
        expect(match[0]).toBe("");
        expect(match.index).toBe(2);
        expect(new RegExp("(?!\\W)$", flag).test("😀")).toBeTrue();
        expect(new RegExp("(?!\\W)(?=.)", flag).test("😀")).toBeFalse();
    });

    for (const [source, indices, replacement] of [
        ["(?<g1>.{0}\\k<g1>)", [0, 2, 4, 6], "#😀#😀#😀#"],
        ["(?<a>)\\k<a>(?<!.)", [0], "#😀😀😀"],
        ["(?!\\W)", [6], "😀😀😀#"],
        ["(?<!.)", [0], "#😀😀😀"],
        ["\\B", [0, 2, 4, 6], "#😀#😀#😀#"],
    ]) {
        test(`/${source}/g${flag} matches only at code-point boundaries`, () => {
            const matcher = new RegExp(source, "g" + flag);
            expect(Array.from("😀😀😀".matchAll(matcher), match => match.index)).toEqual(indices);
            expect("😀😀😀".match(matcher)).toEqual(indices.map(() => ""));
            expect("😀😀😀".replace(matcher, "#")).toBe(replacement);
            expect("😀😀😀".replace(matcher, () => "#")).toBe(replacement);
        });
    }

    test(`/${flag} searches retain lone surrogates`, () => {
        const matcher = new RegExp("(?!😀)", "g" + flag);
        const input = "\uD83Da\uDE00😀";
        expect(Array.from(input.matchAll(matcher), match => match.index)).toEqual([0, 1, 2, 5]);
    });

    for (const source of ["\\B", "(?!😀)"]) {
        test(`/${source}/g${flag} searches past a pair containing lastIndex`, () => {
            const matcher = new RegExp(source, "dg" + flag);
            matcher.lastIndex = 2;
            const match = matcher.exec("A😀");
            expect(match[0]).toBe("");
            expect(match.index).toBe(3);
            expect(match.indices).toEqual([[3, 3]]);
            expect(matcher.lastIndex).toBe(3);
        });

        for (const flags of ["y" + flag, "gy" + flag]) {
            test(`/${source}/${flags} does not retry inside a surrogate pair`, () => {
                const matcher = new RegExp(source, flags);
                matcher.lastIndex = 2;
                expect(matcher.exec("A😀")).toBeNull();
                expect(matcher.lastIndex).toBe(0);

                matcher.lastIndex = 2;
                expect(matcher.test("A😀")).toBeFalse();
                expect(matcher.lastIndex).toBe(0);
            });
        }

        test(`/${source}/y${flag} replacement does not split a surrogate pair`, () => {
            const matcher = new RegExp(source, "y" + flag);
            matcher.lastIndex = 2;
            expect("A😀".replace(matcher, "#")).toBe("A😀");
            expect(matcher.lastIndex).toBe(0);

            matcher.lastIndex = 2;
            expect("A😀".replace(matcher, () => "#")).toBe("A😀");
            expect(matcher.lastIndex).toBe(0);
        });
    }

    for (const flags of ["g" + flag, "y" + flag]) {
        for (const [source, matched, end] of [
            ["(?:)", "", 1],
            [".", "😀", 3],
        ]) {
            test(`/${source}/${flags} starts at the code point containing lastIndex`, () => {
                const matcher = new RegExp(source, flags);
                matcher.lastIndex = 2;
                const match = matcher.exec("A😀");
                expect(match[0]).toBe(matched);
                expect(match.index).toBe(1);
                expect(matcher.lastIndex).toBe(end);
            });
        }
    }
}

test("non-Unicode zero-width patterns can match inside surrogate pairs", () => {
    expect(Array.from("😀".matchAll(/\B/g), match => match.index)).toEqual([0, 1, 2]);
    const matcher = /\B/y;
    matcher.lastIndex = 2;
    expect(matcher.exec("A😀").index).toBe(2);
    expect(matcher.lastIndex).toBe(2);
});

test("closure-capturing callees do not drain promise jobs before the caller resumes", () => {
    let order = [];

    function inner() {
        let x = 1;
        order.push("inner");
        return () => x;
    }

    inner();
    order.length = 0;

    function outer() {
        inner();
        order.push("outer");
    }

    Promise.resolve().then(() => order.push("micro"));

    outer();
    expect(order).toEqual(["inner", "outer"]);

    runQueuedPromiseJobs();
    expect(order).toEqual(["inner", "outer", "micro"]);
});

    order.length = 0;

    function outer() {
        (1).__asmInlineCallMicrotaskOrder();
        order.push("outer");
    }

    Promise.resolve().then(() => order.push("micro"));

    outer();
    expect(order).toEqual(["inner", "outer"]);

    runQueuedPromiseJobs();
    expect(order).toEqual(["inner", "outer", "micro"]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/assignment-to-class-binding-reads-it.js
describe("an assignment to a class declaration's binding can read the binding", () => {
    test("in a function", () => {
        function f() {
            class C {}
            C = C;
            return typeof C;
        }
        expect(f()).toBe("function");
    });

    test("in a block", () => {
        function f() {
            {
                class C {}
                C = [C][0];
                return typeof C;
            }
        }
        expect(f()).toBe("function");
    });

    test("as a call argument", () => {
        function f() {
            class C {}
            C = ((c, d) => d)([], C);
            return C.name;
        }
        expect(f()).toBe("C");
    });

    test("in a compound assignment", () => {
        function f() {
            class C {}
            C += "";
            return typeof C;
        }
        expect(f()).toBe("string");
    });

    test("in a logical assignment", () => {
        function f() {
            class C {}
            C ??= 1;
            return typeof C;
        }
        expect(f()).toBe("function");
    });
});

test("a class declaration's binding is still in its dead zone before the declaration", () => {
    expect(() => {
        C = C;
        class C {}
    }).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "is not initialized");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/async-generator-function-set-completion-type.js
test("test", () => {
    var obj = {
        [Symbol.iterator]() {
            return {
                next() {
                    return { value: 1, done: false };
                },
            };
        },
    };

    async function* asyncg() {
        yield* obj;
    }

    let fail = false;
    let done = false;

    function FAIL() {
        fail = true;
    }

    function DONE() {
        done = true;
    }

    var iter = asyncg();

    iter.next()
        .then(function (result) {
            iter.return()
                .then(function (result) {
                    expect(result.done).toBeTrue();
                    expect(result.value).toBeUndefined();
                })
                .catch(FAIL);
        })
        .catch(FAIL)
        .then(DONE);
    runQueuedPromiseJobs();
    expect(fail).toBe(false);
    expect(done).toBe(true);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/async-yield-star-rejected-return.js
describe("async yield* with a rejected return value", () => {
    for (const method of ["next", "throw", "return"]) {
        test(`forwards the rejection after yielding from ${method}()`, () => {
            const reason = {};
            const calls = [];
            const delegate = {
                [Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
                    return this;
                },
                next() {
                    calls.push("next");
                    return { value: "next", done: false };
                },
                throw(value) {
                    calls.push(["throw", value]);
                    return { value: "handled", done: value === reason };
                },
                return(value) {
                    calls.push(["return", value]);
                    return { value: "return", done: false };
                },
            };
            async function* outer() {
                const value = yield* delegate;
                calls.push(["resumed", value]);
                return "finished";
            }

            let result;
            let rejection;
            (async () => {
                const iterator = outer();
                await iterator.next();
                if (method !== "next") {
                    await iterator[method]("continue");
                }
                return iterator.return(Promise.reject(reason));
            })().then(
                value => (result = value),
                error => (rejection = error)
            );
            runQueuedPromiseJobs();

            expect(rejection).toBeUndefined();
            expect(result).toEqual({ value: "finished", done: true });
            const expected = ["next"];
            if (method !== "next") {
                expected.push([method, "continue"]);
            }
            expected.push(["throw", reason], ["resumed", "handled"]);
            expect(calls).toEqual(expected);
        });
    }

    test("can yield again from the delegated throw() method", () => {
        const reason = {};
        const calls = [];
        let nextCount = 0;
        const delegate = {
            [Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
                return this;
            },
            next(value) {
                calls.push(["next", value]);
                return { value: ++nextCount, done: nextCount === 2 };
            },
            throw(value) {
                calls.push(["throw", value]);
                return { value: "recovered", done: false };
            },
        };
        async function* outer() {
            return yield* delegate;
        }

        let results;
        let rejection;
        (async () => {
            const iterator = outer();
            await iterator.next();
            return [await iterator.return(Promise.reject(reason)), await iterator.next("continue")];
        })().then(
            value => (results = value),
            error => (rejection = error)
        );
        runQueuedPromiseJobs();

        expect(rejection).toBeUndefined();
        expect(results).toEqual([
            { value: "recovered", done: false },
            { value: 2, done: true },
        ]);
        expect(calls).toEqual([
            ["next", undefined],
            ["throw", reason],
            ["next", "continue"],
        ]);
    });

    for (const cleanupThrows of [false, true]) {
        test(`awaits cleanup when throw() is missing and cleanup ${cleanupThrows ? "throws" : "succeeds"}`, () => {
            const reason = {};
            const cleanupError = {};
            const calls = [];
            const delegate = {
                [Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
                    return this;
                },
                next() {
                    return { value: 1, done: false };
                },
                async return() {
                    calls.push("cleanup started");
                    await Promise.resolve();
                    calls.push("cleanup finished");
                    if (cleanupThrows) {
                        throw cleanupError;
                    }
                    return { done: true };
                },
            };
            async function* outer() {
                yield* delegate;
            }

            let rejection;
            (async () => {
                const iterator = outer();
                await iterator.next();
                return iterator.return(Promise.reject(reason));
            })().catch(error => {
                calls.push("rejected");
                rejection = error;
            });
            runQueuedPromiseJobs();

            expect(calls).toEqual(["cleanup started", "cleanup finished", "rejected"]);
            if (cleanupThrows) {
                expect(rejection).toBe(cleanupError);
            } else {
                expect(rejection).toBeInstanceOf(TypeError);
            }
        });
    }

    test("a rejected return still throws into an ordinary async yield", () => {
        const reason = {};
        let caught;
        async function* generator() {
            try {
                yield 1;
            } catch (error) {
                caught = error;
                yield "recovered";
            }
        }

        let result;
        let rejection;
        (async () => {
            const iterator = generator();
            await iterator.next();
            return iterator.return(Promise.reject(reason));
        })().then(
            value => (result = value),
            error => (rejection = error)
        );
        runQueuedPromiseJobs();

        expect(rejection).toBeUndefined();
        expect(caught).toBe(reason);
        expect(result).toEqual({ value: "recovered", done: false });
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/bytecode-generator-operand-lifetimes.js
describe("bytecode generator operand lifetime regressions", () => {
    test("computed member calls keep the original base", () => {
        function callMethod() {
            let base = {
                name: "old",
                method() {
                    return this.name;
                },
            };
            const newer = {
                name: "new",
                method() {
                    return this.name;
                },
            };
            return base[((base = newer), "method")]();
        }

        expect(callMethod()).toBe("old");
    });

    test("tagged templates preserve the tag, receiver, and earlier substitutions", () => {
        function localTag() {
            let tag = () => "old";
            return tag`${(tag = () => "new")}`;
        }

        function memberTag() {
            let base = {
                name: "old",
                tag() {
                    return this.name;
                },
            };
            const newer = {
                name: "new",
                tag() {
                    return this.name;
                },
            };
            return base.tag`${(base = newer)}`;
        }

        function substitutionTag() {
            let value = 1;
            return ((strings, first, second) => [first, second])`${value}${(value = 2)}`;
        }

        expect(localTag()).toBe("old");
        expect(memberTag()).toBe("old");
        expect(substitutionTag()).toEqual([1, 2]);
    });

    test("computed delete keeps the original base", () => {
        function deleteProperty() {
            let base = { x: 1 };
            const old = base;
            const newer = { x: 1 };
            delete base[((base = newer), "x")];
            return [Object.hasOwn(old, "x"), Object.hasOwn(newer, "x")];
        }

        expect(deleteProperty()).toEqual([false, true]);
    });

    test("destructuring assignment keeps its evaluated member base", () => {
        function assignPattern() {
            let base = { x: 0 };
            const old = base;
            const newer = { x: 0 };
            [base[((base = newer), "x")]] = [7];
            return [old.x, newer.x];
        }

        expect(assignPattern()).toEqual([7, 0]);
    });

    test("for-of expression targets keep their evaluated member base", () => {
        function assignLoopTarget() {
            let base = { x: 0 };
            const old = base;
            const newer = { x: 0 };
            for (base[((base = newer), "x")] of [7]) {
            }
            return [old.x, newer.x];
        }

        expect(assignLoopTarget()).toEqual([7, 0]);
    });

    test("computed member reads keep the original base", () => {
        function read() {
            let base = { x: "old" };
            const newer = { x: "new" };
            return base[((base = newer), "x")];
        }

        function optionalRead() {
            let base = { x: "old" };
            const newer = { x: "new" };
            return base?.[((base = newer), "x")];
        }

        expect(read()).toBe("old");
        expect(optionalRead()).toBe("old");
    });

    test("converting a computed key keeps the value of `this`", () => {
        const receiver = {
            toString() {
                return "key";
            },
        };

        function objectLiteral() {
            const object = { [this]: 1 };
            return [this, object.key];
        }

        function bindingPattern() {
            const { [this]: value } = { key: 1 };
            return [this, value];
        }

        function classElement() {
            class C {
                [this]() {}
            }
            return [this, Object.hasOwn(C.prototype, "key")];
        }

        expect(objectLiteral.call(receiver)).toEqual([receiver, 1]);
        expect(bindingPattern.call(receiver)).toEqual([receiver, 1]);
        expect(classElement.call(receiver)).toEqual([receiver, true]);
    });

    test("a destructuring assignment evaluates to the value it started with", () => {
        function objectPattern() {
            const source = { a: 1 };
            let value = source;
            const result = ({ a: value } = value);
            return [result === source, value];
        }

        function arrayPattern() {
            const source = [1];
            let value = source;
            const result = ([value] = value);
            return [result === source, value];
        }

        function computedKey() {
            const source = { a: 1 };
            let value = source;
            let target;
            const result = ({ [((value = null), "a")]: target } = value);
            return [result === source, target];
        }

        expect(objectPattern()).toEqual([true, 1]);
        expect(arrayPattern()).toEqual([true, 1]);
        expect(computedKey()).toEqual([true, 1]);
    });
});

describe("UpdateEmpty completion value semantics for loops and switch", () => {
    test("while: break with no value keeps undefined", () => {
        expect(eval("1; while (true) { break; }")).toBeUndefined();
    });

    test("while: break preserves last value", () => {
        expect(eval("2; while (true) { 3; break; }")).toBe(3);
    });

    test("do-while: break with no value keeps undefined", () => {
        expect(eval("1; do { break; } while (false)")).toBeUndefined();
    });

    test("do-while: break preserves last value", () => {
        expect(eval("2; do { 3; break; } while (false)")).toBe(3);
    });

    test("for: break with no value keeps undefined", () => {
        expect(eval("1; for (;;) { break; }")).toBeUndefined();
    });

    test("for: break preserves last value", () => {
        expect(eval("2; for (;;) { 3; break; }")).toBe(3);
    });

    test("for: empty body returns undefined", () => {
        expect(eval("2; for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) { }")).toBeUndefined();
    });

    test("switch: break with no value keeps undefined", () => {
        expect(eval('1; switch ("a") { case "a": break; }')).toBeUndefined();
    });

    test("switch: break preserves last value", () => {
        expect(eval('2; switch ("a") { case "a": { 3; break; } }')).toBe(3);
    });

    test("nested: continue outer with value", () => {
        expect(eval("5; outer: do { while (true) { 6; continue outer; } } while (false)")).toBe(6);
    });

    test("nested: continue outer with no value keeps undefined", () => {
        expect(eval("4; outer: do { while (true) { continue outer; } } while (false)")).toBeUndefined();
    });

    test("nested: break outer with value", () => {
        expect(eval("1; outer: while (true) { while (true) { 7; break outer; } }")).toBe(7);
    });

    test("for-in: break preserves last value", () => {
        expect(eval("1; for (var x in {a: 1}) { 8; break; }")).toBe(8);
    });

    test("for-of: break preserves last value", () => {
        expect(eval("1; for (var x of [1]) { 9; break; }")).toBe(9);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/computed-destructuring-key-registers.js
test("computed destructuring keys survive their targets and defaults", () => {
    const events = [];
    const key = name => {
        events.push(`key ${name}`);
        return {
            toString() {
                events.push(`convert ${name}`);
                return name;
            },
        };
    };
    const target = {};
    const destination = name => {
        events.push(`target ${name}`);
        return target;
    };
    const defaultValue = value => {
        events.push(`default ${value}`);
        return { value };
    };
    const source = {
        get a() {
            events.push("get a");
        },
        get b() {
            events.push("get b");
        },
    };
    const result = ({
        [key("a")]: destination("first")[key("first")] = defaultValue(1),
        [key("b")]: destination("second")[key("second")] = defaultValue(2),
    } = source);
    expect(result).toBe(source);
    expect(target).toEqual({ first: { value: 1 }, second: { value: 2 } });
    expect(events).toEqual([
        "key a",
        "convert a",
        "target first",
        "key first",
        "get a",
        "default 1",
        "convert first",
        "key b",
        "convert b",
        "target second",
        "key second",
        "get b",
        "default 2",
        "convert second",
    ]);
});

test("object rest keeps earlier computed keys across nested patterns and defaults", () => {
    const symbol = Symbol("key");
    const key = name => ({ toString: () => name });
    const source = { a: undefined, b: 2, [symbol]: 3, remaining: 4 };
    const {
        [key("a")]: { [key("value")]: first } = { value: 1 },
        [key("b")]: second,
        [symbol]: third,
        ...rest
    } = source;
    expect([first, second, third]).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
    expect(rest).toEqual({ remaining: 4 });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/environment-coordinate-cache-type-confusion.js
// https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/issues/3622
// A nested function declared in an async function's "finally" block reads a parameter whose binding we used to look up
// through a mis-typed environment coordinate cache, leading to an OOB read. The binding must resolve to the real value.
test("binding lookup through a nested async finally function does not confuse environment types", () => {
    async function f0(a1) {
        try {
            let [] = this;
        } catch (e17) {
            a1.h = a1;
            try {
            } catch (e20) {}
        } finally {
            function f21() {
                a1;
            }
            f21();
        }
    }

    f0().catch(() => {});
    f0(f0).catch(() => {});

    // f0(f0) takes the catch path and runs a1.h = a1 with a1 === f0. A mis-typed environment lookup would store garbage
    // instead of f0 here (or crash).
    expect(f0.h).toBe(f0);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/function-bind-arguments.js
test("Some function.bind cases", () => {
    function collectArguments() {
        let a = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < arguments.length; ++i) a.push(arguments[i]);
        return a;
    }

    let b = collectArguments.bind(null);
    expect(b()).toEqual([]);
    expect(b(3, 4)).toEqual([3, 4]);
    expect(b(3, 4, 5, 6)).toEqual([3, 4, 5, 6]);

    let b12 = collectArguments.bind(null, 1, 2);
    expect(b12()).toEqual([1, 2]);
    expect(b12(3, 4)).toEqual([1, 2, 3, 4]);
    expect(b12(3, 4, 5, 6)).toEqual([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/large-call-argument-lists.js
function argumentList(count, expression = "value++") {
    return Array(count).fill(expression).join(",");
}

function range(count, start = 0) {
    return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) => start + index);
}

describe("large call argument lists", () => {
    test("arguments are evaluated once, from left to right, across the operand limit", () => {
        for (const count of [199, 200, 201, 300]) {
            const call = new Function("collect", "value", `return collect(${argumentList(count)});`);
            expect(call((...values) => values, 0)).toEqual(range(count));
        }
    });

    test("later arguments preserve the callee, receiver, and earlier argument values", () => {
        const first = {
            method(...values) {
                return [this, values];
            },
        };
        const second = { method: () => "wrong method" };
        const call = new Function(
            "first",
            "second",
            "value",
            `let receiver = first;
             return receiver.method(${argumentList(200, "value")}, receiver = second, value = 99);`
        );
        expect(call(first, second, 1)).toEqual([first, [...Array(200).fill(1), second, 99]]);
    });

    test("optional calls skip every argument when the callee is nullish", () => {
        const call = new Function(
            "callee",
            "value",
            `const result = callee?.(${argumentList(300)}); return [result, value];`
        );
        expect(call(null, 0)).toEqual([undefined, 0]);
        expect(call((...values) => values, 0)).toEqual([range(300), 300]);
    });

    test("constructors and super calls receive every argument and the original new.target", () => {
        class Base {
            constructor(...values) {
                this.values = values;
                this.target = new.target;
            }
        }
        const construct = new Function("Base", "value", `return new Base(${argumentList(300)});`);
        const base = construct(Base, 0);
        expect(base.values).toEqual(range(300));
        expect(base.target).toBe(Base);

        const makeDerived = new Function(
            "Base",
            "value",
            `return class Derived extends Base { constructor() { super(${argumentList(300)}); } };`
        );
        const Derived = makeDerived(Base, 0);
        const derived = new Derived();
        expect(derived.values).toEqual(range(300));
        expect(derived.target).toBe(Derived);

        const makeDerivedWithSpread = new Function(
            "Base",
            "value",
            "iterable",
            `return class Derived extends Base { constructor() { super(${argumentList(201)}, ...iterable); } };`
        );
        const DerivedWithSpread = makeDerivedWithSpread(Base, 0, [700, 701]);
        expect(new DerivedWithSpread().values).toEqual([...range(201), 700, 701]);
    });

    test("direct eval retains the lexical environment and the evaluated callee", () => {
        const call = new Function(
            "eval",
            "value",
            `let visible = 37;
             return eval("visible", ${argumentList(199)}, eval = () => 99);`
        );
        expect(call(eval, 0)).toBe(37);
    });

    test("calls named async, nested calls, and spreads retain argument order", () => {
        const callAsync = new Function("async", "value", `return async(${argumentList(300)});`);
        expect(callAsync((...values) => values, 0)).toEqual(range(300));

        const call = new Function(
            "collect",
            "value",
            "iterable",
            `return collect(${argumentList(200)}, ...iterable, collect(${argumentList(300)}));`
        );
        expect(call((...values) => values, 0, [700, 701])).toEqual([...range(200), 700, 701, range(300, 200)]);
    });

    test("a large async arrow cover remains a parameter list", () => {
        let seen;
        const parameters = range(300)
            .map(index => `p${index}`)
            .join(",");
        const arrow = eval(`(async (${parameters}) => { seen = [p0, p299]; })`);
        expect(arrow).toHaveLength(300);
        expect(seen).toBeUndefined();
        arrow(...range(300));
        expect(seen).toEqual([0, 299]);
    });

    test("an abrupt argument stops evaluation before the call", () => {
        const error = new Error("argument failed");
        let evaluated = 0;
        let called = false;
        const call = new Function(
            "callee",
            "next",
            "fail",
            `return callee(${argumentList(200, "next()")}, fail(), ${argumentList(20, "next()")});`
        );
        try {
            call(
                () => {
                    called = true;
                },
                () => evaluated++,
                () => {
                    throw error;
                }
            );
            expect().fail("the argument should throw");
        } catch (caught) {
            expect(caught).toBe(error);
        }
        expect(evaluated).toBe(200);
        expect(called).toBeFalse();
    });
});

// https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/issues/3584
// Converting a pathologically-deep-prototype-chain object to a primitive used to recurse Object::internal_get til the
// native stack overflowed. The code now throws a catchable "call stack size exceeded" error instead.

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/object-destructuring-rebinds-source-variable.js
describe("object destructuring keeps reading from the original value after rebinding its source", () => {
    test("var declaration whose pattern rebinds the source variable", () => {
        function run(source) {
            var { first, second: source, third, fourth = "default" } = source;
            return { first, source, third, fourth };
        }
        const result = run({ first: 1, second: 2, third: 3 });
        expect(result.first).toBe(1);
        expect(result.source).toBe(2);
        expect(result.third).toBe(3);
        expect(result.fourth).toBe("default");
    });

    test("destructuring assignment whose pattern rebinds the source variable", () => {
        let source = { first: 1, second: 2 };
        let first, second;
        ({ first, second: source, second } = source);
        expect(first).toBe(1);
        expect(source).toBe(2);
        expect(second).toBe(2);
    });

    test("nested pattern rebinding the outer source variable", () => {
        function run(source) {
            var {
                inner: { value: source },
                after,
            } = source;
            return { source, after };
        }
        const result = run({ inner: { value: "inner" }, after: "after" });
        expect(result.source).toBe("inner");
        expect(result.after).toBe("after");
    });

    test("rest property collected after the source variable is rebound", () => {
        function run(source) {
            var { first: source, ...rest } = source;
            return { source, rest };
        }
        const result = run({ first: 1, second: 2, third: 3 });
        expect(result.source).toBe(1);
        expect(result.rest).toEqual({ second: 2, third: 3 });
    });

    test("computed key read after the source variable is rebound", () => {
        function run(source) {
            var key = "second";
            var { first: source, [key]: second } = source;
            return { source, second };
        }
        const result = run({ first: 1, second: 2 });
        expect(result.source).toBe(1);
        expect(result.second).toBe(2);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/promise-job-queue-reentrancy.js
test("nested promise job checkpoints wait for the current reaction to finish", () => {
    const order = [];
    Promise.resolve()
        .then(() => {
            order.push("reaction start");
            Promise.resolve().then(() => order.push("queued reaction"));
            runQueuedPromiseJobs();
            order.push("reaction end");
        })
        .then(() => order.push("chained reaction"));

    runQueuedPromiseJobs();
    expect(order).toEqual(["reaction start", "reaction end", "queued reaction", "chained reaction"]);
});

test("disposeAsync() resumes disposal from promise jobs in order", () => {
    for (const reject of [false, true]) {
        const order = [];
        Promise.resolve().then(() => {
            const stack = new AsyncDisposableStack();
            stack.defer(() => {
                order.push("second dispose");
            });
            stack.defer(() => {
                order.push("first dispose");
                Promise.resolve()
                    .then(() => order.push("tick 1"))
                    .then(() => order.push("tick 2"))
                    .then(() => order.push("tick 3"));
                return reject ? Promise.reject("disposal failed") : Promise.resolve();
            });
            stack.disposeAsync().then(
                () => order.push("fulfilled"),
                () => order.push("rejected")
            );
            order.push("dispose returned");
        });

        runQueuedPromiseJobs();
        expect(order).toEqual([
            "first dispose",
            "dispose returned",
            "tick 1",
            "second dispose",
            "tick 2",
            "tick 3",
            reject ? "rejected" : "fulfilled",
        ]);
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/shared-local-snapshots.js
function take(...values) {
    return values;
}

test("each write takes a fresh shared snapshot", () => {
    function repeatedWrites(x) {
        return take(x, x, (x = 2), x, x, (x = 3), x);
    }
    expect(repeatedWrites(1)).toEqual([1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3]);

    function rawObject() {
        let value = { valueOf: () => 4 };
        const original = value;
        const result = take(value, value, value++);
        return [result[0] === original, result[1] === original, result[2], value];
    }
    expect(rawObject()).toEqual([true, true, 4, 5]);
});

test("shared snapshots preserve callees, receivers, and assignment targets", () => {
    function callee() {
        let fn = function old(a, b, c) {
            return [a === old, b === old, c.name];
        };
        return fn(fn, fn, (fn = function newer() {}));
    }
    expect(callee()).toEqual([true, true, "newer"]);

    function receiver(flag) {
        let base = {
            name: "old",
            method(a, b) {
                return [this.name, a.name, b.name];
            },
        };
        return base.method(base, flag ? (base = { name: "new" }) : base);
    }
    expect(receiver(true)).toEqual(["old", "old", "new"]);
    expect(receiver(false)).toEqual(["old", "old", "old"]);

    function indexedTarget() {
        const object = {};
        let key = "x";
        const result = take(key, (object[key] = key = "y"), key);
        return [result, object.x, Object.hasOwn(object, "y")];
    }
    expect(indexedTarget()).toEqual([["x", "y", "y"], "y", false]);
});

test("shared snapshots survive held registers and distinguish locals from arguments", () => {
    function classKey(flag, x) {
        const result = take(
            x,
            x,
            class {
                [flag ? (x = 2) : (x = 3)]() {}
            },
            x
        );
        return [result[0], result[1], Object.hasOwn(result[2].prototype, flag ? "2" : "3"), result[3]];
    }
    expect(classKey(true, 1)).toEqual([1, 1, true, 2]);
    expect(classKey(false, 1)).toEqual([1, 1, true, 3]);

    function pattern(x) {
        return take(x, x, ([x] = [7]), x);
    }
    expect(pattern(1)).toEqual([1, 1, [7], 7]);

    function distinct(argument, flag) {
        let local = 2;
        return take(argument, local, argument, local, flag ? ((argument = 3), (local = 4)) : null, argument, local);
    }
    expect(distinct(1, true)).toEqual([1, 2, 1, 2, 4, 3, 4]);
    expect(distinct(1, false)).toEqual([1, 2, 1, 2, null, 1, 2]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/string-to-number-and-bigint-non-decimal-prefixes.js
// Literal-only regression tests that pin non-decimal prefix behavior in
// numeric and bigint coercion expressions.

function expectLooseNumberEquality(value, target, expected) {
    expect(value == target).toBe(expected);
    expect(value != target).toBe(!expected);
    expect(target == value).toBe(expected);
    expect(target != value).toBe(!expected);
}

function expectLooseBigIntEquality(value, target, expected) {
    expect(value == target).toBe(expected);
    expect(value != target).toBe(!expected);
    expect(target == value).toBe(expected);
    expect(target != value).toBe(!expected);
}

function expectLooseEquality(value, numberTarget, bigintTarget, expected) {
    expectLooseNumberEquality(value, numberTarget, expected);
    expectLooseBigIntEquality(value, bigintTarget, expected);
}

test("naked non-decimal prefixes stay invalid in folded number contexts", () => {
    for (const value of ["0x", "0o", "0b"]) expect(+value).toBeNaN();
});

test("uppercase naked prefixes stay invalid in folded number contexts", () => {
    for (const value of ["0X", "0O", "0B"]) expect(+value).toBeNaN();
});

test("uppercase prefixed literals stay valid in folded loose equality", () => {
    for (const [value, numberTarget, bigintTarget] of [
        ["0X10", 16, 16n],
        ["0O10", 8, 8n],
        ["0B10", 2, 2n],
    ]) {
        expectLooseEquality(value, numberTarget, bigintTarget, true);
    }
});

test("trimmed uppercase prefixed literals stay valid in folded loose equality", () => {
    for (const [value, numberTarget, bigintTarget] of [
        ["  0X10  ", 16, 16n],
        ["  0O10  ", 8, 8n],
        ["  0B10  ", 2, 2n],
    ]) {
        expectLooseEquality(value, numberTarget, bigintTarget, true);
    }
});

test("valid non-decimal literals stay valid in folded number contexts", () => {
    expect(+"0x10").toBe(16);
    expect(+"0o10").toBe(8);
    expect(+"0b10").toBe(2);

    expect(+"  0X10  ").toBe(16);
    expect(+"  0O10  ").toBe(8);
    expect(+"  0B10  ").toBe(2);
});

test("non-JS suffix syntax stays invalid in folded number contexts", () => {
    for (const value of ["0x+1", "0x1_0", "0b+1", "0b1_0", "0o+7", "0o1_0"]) expect(+value).toBeNaN();
});

test("naked non-decimal prefixes stay invalid in folded bigint relational contexts", () => {
    for (const value of ["0x", "0o", "0b"]) {
        expect(value < 1n).toBeFalse();
        expect(1n < value).toBeFalse();
    }
});

test("naked prefixes stay invalid in folded loose equality", () => {
    for (const value of ["0x", "0o", "0b"]) expectLooseEquality(value, 0, 0n, false);
});

test("invalid prefixed digits stay invalid in folded loose equality", () => {
    for (const value of ["0xg", "0b2", "0o8"]) expectLooseEquality(value, 0, 0n, false);
});

test("non-JS suffix syntax stays invalid in folded loose equality", () => {
    for (const [value, numberTarget, bigintTarget] of [
        ["0x+1", 1, 1n],
        ["0x1_0", 16, 16n],
        ["0b+1", 1, 1n],
        ["0b1_0", 2, 2n],
        ["0o+7", 7, 7n],
        ["0o1_0", 8, 8n],
    ]) {
        expectLooseEquality(value, numberTarget, bigintTarget, false);
    }
});

test("valid prefixed digits stay valid in folded loose equality", () => {
    for (const [value, numberTarget, bigintTarget] of [
        ["0x10", 16, 16n],
        ["0o10", 8, 8n],
        ["0b10", 2, 2n],
    ]) {
        expectLooseEquality(value, numberTarget, bigintTarget, true);
    }
});

// https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-putvalue
// https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinarysetwithowndescriptor
describe("setting a super property with a non-object this value", () => {
    test("throws a TypeError for a data property", () => {
        class A {
            setNamed() {
                super.x = 1;
            }

            setComputed(key) {
                super[key] = 1;
            }
        }

        for (const thisValue of [null, undefined, 1, "foo", Symbol(), 1n]) {
            expect(() => A.prototype.setNamed.call(thisValue)).toThrowWithMessage(
                TypeError,
                "Cannot set property 'x' of"
            );
            expect(() => A.prototype.setComputed.call(thisValue, "y")).toThrowWithMessage(
                TypeError,
                "Cannot set property 'y' of"
            );
        }
    });

    test("throws a TypeError after the caches have seen an object this value", () => {
        class A {
            set() {
                super.x = 1;
            }
        }

        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
            const object = new A();
            A.prototype.set.call(object);
            expect(object.x).toBe(1);
        }

        expect(() => A.prototype.set.call(null)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Cannot set property 'x' of");
        expect(Object.hasOwn(A.prototype, "x")).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("calls a setter with the non-object this value", () => {
        const receivers = [];

        class A {
            set x(value) {
                receivers.push(this);
            }
        }

        class B extends A {
            set() {
                super.x = 1;
            }
        }

        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {
            B.prototype.set.call(new B());
        }
        receivers.length = 0;

        B.prototype.set.call(null);
        B.prototype.set.call(undefined);
        B.prototype.set.call(42);

        expect(receivers).toEqual([null, undefined, 42]);
    });
});
