FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/regress/yield-star-branch-registers.js
for (const cleanupThrows of [false, true]) {
    test(`async yield* preserves state across return and missing throw when cleanup throws: ${cleanupThrows}`, () => {
        const kept = { tag: "kept" };
        const cleanupError = {};
        const events = [];
        let caught;
        const delegate = {
            [Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
                return this;
            },
            next() {
                return { value: "first", done: false };
            },
            async return() {
                events.push(`return:${arguments.length}`);
                if (arguments.length !== 0) {
                    return { value: "return yield", done: false };
                }
                await Promise.resolve();
                events.push("cleanup finished");
                if (cleanupThrows) {
                    throw cleanupError;
                }
                return { done: false };
            },
        };
        async function* outer() {
            try {
                return [{ kept }, yield* delegate];
            } catch (error) {
                caught = error;
                yield kept;
                return "recovered";
            } finally {
                events.push(kept.tag);
            }
        }

        let results;
        let rejection;
        (async () => {
            const iterator = outer();
            return [
                await iterator.next(),
                await iterator.return("continue"),
                await iterator.throw("original"),
                await iterator.next(),
            ];
        })().then(
            value => (results = value),
            error => (rejection = error)
        );
        runQueuedPromiseJobs();

        expect(rejection).toBeUndefined();
        expect(results).toEqual([
            { value: "first", done: false },
            { value: "return yield", done: false },
            { value: kept, done: false },
            { value: "recovered", done: true },
        ]);
        expect(events).toEqual(["return:1", "return:0", "cleanup finished", "kept"]);
        if (cleanupThrows) {
            expect(caught).toBe(cleanupError);
        } else {
            expect(caught).toBeInstanceOf(TypeError);
        }
    });
}

test("async yield* preserves an earlier expression value through delegation", () => {
    const kept = {};
    async function* delegate() {
        yield 1;
        return 2;
    }
    async function* outer() {
        return [{ kept }, yield* delegate()];
    }

    let results;
    let rejection;
    (async () => {
        const iterator = outer();
        return [await iterator.next(), await iterator.next()];
    })().then(
        value => (results = value),
        error => (rejection = error)
    );
    runQueuedPromiseJobs();

    expect(rejection).toBeUndefined();
    expect(results).toEqual([
        { value: 1, done: false },
        { value: [{ kept }, 2], done: true },
    ]);
    expect(results[1].value[0].kept).toBe(kept);
});

        indirect("return 1;");
    }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "'return' not allowed outside of a function");

        eval("return 1;");
    }

    expect(() => {
        foo();
    }).toThrowWithMessage(SyntaxError, "'return' not allowed outside of a function");

        indirect("return 1;");

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/runtime-error-call-stack-size.js
test("infinite recursion", () => {
    function infiniteRecursion() {
        infiniteRecursion();
    }

    try {
        infiniteRecursion();
    } catch (e) {
        expect(e).toBeInstanceOf(InternalError);
        expect(e.name).toBe("InternalError");
        expect(e.message).toBe("Call stack size limit exceeded");
    }

    expect(() => {
        JSON.stringify({}, () => ({ foo: "bar" }));
    }).toThrowWithMessage(InternalError, "Call stack size limit exceeded");

    expect(() => {
        new Proxy({}, { get: (_, __, p) => p.foo }).foo;
    }).toThrowWithMessage(InternalError, "Call stack size limit exceeded");

    expect(() => {
        function outer() {
            async function inner() {
                await outer;
            }
            inner();
            outer();
        }

        outer();
    }).toThrowWithMessage(InternalError, "Call stack size limit exceeded");
});

test("async-from-sync iterators created at the call stack size limit", () => {
    // Every frame of the recursion starts a for-await loop over an array, the deepest ones with almost no stack left,
    // and its async function catches the overflow in its rejected promise. See #12217.
    const recurse = async () => {
        try {
            recurse();
        } catch {}
        for await (const _ of [0]);
    };
    expect(() => {
        recurse();
        gc();
    }).not.toThrow();
});

describe("scope-local eval deoptimization", () => {
    test("eval in child function does not affect parent lookups", () => {
        function outer() {
            let x = 100;
            function inner() {
                eval("var y = 200");
                return y;
            }
            let innerResult = inner();
            return x + innerResult;
        }
        expect(outer()).toBe(300);
    });

    test("eval shadows variable from outer function within same function", () => {
        function outer() {
            var c = 1;
            function inner() {
                let before = c;
                eval("var c = 2");
                let after = c;
                return before * 10 + after;
            }
            return inner();
        }
        expect(outer()).toBe(12);
    });

    test("conditional eval - false", () => {
        function foo(doEval) {
            var c = 1;
            function bar(doEval) {
                if (doEval) eval("var c = 2;");
                return c;
            }
            return bar(doEval);
        }
        expect(foo(false)).toBe(1);
    });

    test("conditional eval - true", () => {
        function foo(doEval) {
            var c = 1;
            function bar(doEval) {
                if (doEval) eval("var c = 2;");
                return c;
            }
            return bar(doEval);
        }
        expect(foo(true)).toBe(2);
    });

    test("block scope within function containing eval", () => {
        function foo() {
            let outerLet = 10;
            let result = 0;
            {
                let blockLet = 20;
                eval("var evalVar = 30");
                result = outerLet + blockLet + evalVar;
            }
            return result + outerLet;
        }
        expect(foo()).toBe(70);
    });

    test("multiple levels of nesting", () => {
        function a() {
            let aVar = 1;
            function b() {
                let bVar = 2;
                function c() {
                    let cVar = 3;
                    eval("var evalVar = 4");
                    return cVar + evalVar;
                }
                return bVar + c();
            }
            return aVar + b();
        }
        expect(a()).toBe(10);
    });

    test("eval in multiple nested functions at different levels", () => {
        function a() {
            let aVar = 1;
            eval("var aEval = 10");
            function b() {
                let bVar = 2;
                eval("var bEval = 20");
                function c() {
                    let cVar = 3;
                    eval("var cEval = 30");
                    return cVar + cEval;
                }
                return bVar + bEval + c();
            }
            return aVar + aEval + b();
        }
        expect(a()).toBe(66);
    });

    test("arrow function containing eval", () => {
        function outer() {
            let x = 5;
            const arrow = () => {
                eval("var y = 10");
                return x + y;
            };
            let result = arrow();
            return result + x;
        }
        expect(outer()).toBe(20);
    });

    test("eval in for loop", () => {
        function foo() {
            let sum = 0;
            for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
                eval("var loopVar = i * 10");
                sum += loopVar;
            }
            return sum;
        }
        expect(foo()).toBe(30);
    });

    test("eval creating variable that shadows outer scope", () => {
        var globalVar = 100;
        function foo() {
            let before = globalVar;
            eval("var globalVar = 200");
            let after = globalVar;
            return before * 1000 + after;
        }
        let result = foo();
        expect(result + globalVar).toBe(100300);
    });

    test("deep nesting where only innermost has eval", () => {

            let v1 = 1;
            function level2() {
                let v2 = 2;
                function level3() {
                    let v3 = 3;
                    function level4() {
                        eval("var v4 = 4");
                        return v1 + v2 + v3 + v4;
                    }
                    return level4();
                }

            }

                }

            }

        }

            }

        }

    });

            if (doEval) {

            }

    test("global-level eval creates global variable", () => {

    test("global-level eval can modify existing global", () => {

        globalEval("existingGlobal456 = 200");
        expect(globalThis.existingGlobal456).toBe(200);
        delete globalThis.existingGlobal456;
    });

    test("direct eval in function does not create true global", () => {
        function foo() {
            eval("var localToFoo = 42");
            return localToFoo;
        }
        expect(foo()).toBe(42);
        expect(typeof localToFoo).toBe("undefined");
    });

    test("direct eval can delete a function environment var binding", () => {
        function foo() {
            eval("var localToFoo = 42; delete localToFoo;");
            return typeof localToFoo;
        }
        expect(foo()).toBe("undefined");
    });

    test("assignment keeps the resolved binding through direct eval var declarations", () => {
        function foo() {
            var x = 0;
            var innerX = (function () {
                x = (eval("var x;"), 1);
                return x;
            })();
            return [innerX, x];
        }

        expect(foo()).toEqual([undefined, 1]);
    });

    test("eval shadowing global does not modify actual global", () => {
        globalThis.testGlobal789 = "original";
        function foo() {
            eval("var testGlobal789 = 'shadowed'");
            return testGlobal789;
        }
        expect(foo()).toBe("shadowed");
        expect(globalThis.testGlobal789).toBe("original");
        delete globalThis.testGlobal789;
    });

    test("nested function accesses eval-created var in parent, not global", () => {
        globalThis.sharedName111 = "global";
        function outer() {
            eval("var sharedName111 = 'local'");
            function inner() {
                return sharedName111;
            }
            return inner();
        }
        expect(outer()).toBe("local");
        expect(globalThis.sharedName111).toBe("global");
        delete globalThis.sharedName111;
    });

    test("eval as subexpression of binary operator", () => {
        function foo(n) {
            let local = n | 0;
            let code = "local + 11";
            return eval(code) | 0;
        }
        expect(foo(3)).toBe(14);
    });

    test("eval as subexpression of ternary operator", () => {
        function foo(n) {
            let local = n;
            return eval("local") ? "truthy" : "falsy";
        }
        expect(foo(1)).toBe("truthy");
        expect(foo(0)).toBe("falsy");
    });

    test("eval as argument to another function call", () => {
        function foo(n) {
            let local = n * 2;
            return String(eval("local"));
        }
        expect(foo(21)).toBe("42");
    });

    test("eval in comma expression", () => {
        function foo(n) {
            let local = n;
            return (0, eval("local + 1"));
        }
        expect(foo(5)).toBe(6);
    });

    test("eval result used in assignment expression", () => {
        function foo(n) {
            let local = n;
            let result = eval("local") + 100;
            return result;
        }
        expect(foo(23)).toBe(123);
    });

    test("repeated calls keep eval-created vars separate from cached function bindings", () => {
        function outer(seed, createEvalVar) {
            var captured = seed;
            function readCaptured() {
                return captured;
            }
            if (createEvalVar) {
                eval("var injected = captured + 100; delete injected;");
                return readCaptured() + ":" + typeof injected;
            }
            return readCaptured() + ":" + typeof injected;
        }

        expect(outer(1, false)).toBe("1:undefined");
        expect(outer(2, true)).toBe("2:undefined");
        expect(outer(3, false)).toBe("3:undefined");
    });
});

describe("assigning a property the receiver does not have", () => {
    test("creates an own data property", () => {
        const o = {};
        o.foo = 1;
        o[3] = 2;
        expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(o, "foo")).toEqual({
            value: 1,
            writable: true,
            enumerable: true,
            configurable: true,
        });
        expect(o[3]).toBe(2);
        expect(Object.keys(o)).toEqual(["3", "foo"]);
    });

    test("calls an inherited setter with the receiver", () => {
        let receiver;
        const p = {
            set foo(value) {
                receiver = this;
                this._foo = value;
            },
        };
        const o = Object.create(Object.create(p));
        o.foo = 1;
        expect(receiver).toBe(o);
        expect(o._foo).toBe(1);
        expect(Object.hasOwn(o, "foo")).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("respects an inherited read-only property", () => {
        const p = Object.defineProperty({}, "foo", { value: 1, writable: false });
        const o = Object.create(p);
        expect(() => {
            "use strict";
            o.foo = 2;
        }).toThrow(TypeError);
        o.foo = 2;
        expect(o.foo).toBe(1);
        expect(Object.hasOwn(o, "foo")).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("respects an inherited accessor without a setter", () => {
        const p = {
            get foo() {
                return 1;
            },
        };
        const o = Object.create(p);
        expect(Reflect.set(o, "foo", 2)).toBeFalse();
        expect(Object.hasOwn(o, "foo")).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("does not add to a non-extensible receiver", () => {
        const o = Object.preventExtensions(Object.create({ bar: 1 }));
        expect(Reflect.set(o, "foo", 1)).toBeFalse();
        expect(Object.hasOwn(o, "foo")).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("goes through a proxy prototype's set trap", () => {
        let trapReceiver;
        const proxy = new Proxy(
            {},
            {
                set(target, key, value, receiver) {
                    trapReceiver = receiver;
                    return Reflect.set(target, key, value, receiver);
                },
            }
        );
        const o = Object.create(Object.create(proxy));
        o.foo = 1;
        expect(trapReceiver).toBe(o);
        expect(Object.hasOwn(o, "foo")).toBeTrue();
        expect(Object.hasOwn(proxy, "foo")).toBeFalse();
    });

    test("forwards through a proxy prototype without a set trap", () => {
        const proxy = new Proxy(
            {
                set bar(value) {
                    this._bar = value;
                },
            },
            {}
        );
        const o = Object.create(proxy);
        o.foo = 1;
        o.bar = 2;
        expect(Object.hasOwn(o, "foo")).toBeTrue();
        expect(o._bar).toBe(2);
    });

    test("goes through a typed array prototype's [[Set]]", () => {
        const o = Object.create(new Uint8Array(2));
        o[5] = 1;
        expect(Object.hasOwn(o, "5")).toBeFalse();
        o[1] = 1;
        expect(Object.hasOwn(o, "1")).toBeTrue();
        expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(o)[1]).toBe(0);
    });

    test("respects a string object prototype's read-only indices", () => {
        const o = Object.create(new String("ab"));
        expect(Reflect.set(o, "1", "x")).toBeFalse();
        expect(Reflect.set(o, "2", "x")).toBeTrue();
        expect(Object.hasOwn(o, "2")).toBeTrue();
    });

    test("respects a function prototype's lazily created properties", () => {
        function f() {}
        const o = Object.create(f);
        o.prototype = 1;
        expect(Object.hasOwn(o, "prototype")).toBeTrue();
        expect(f.prototype).not.toBe(1);
    });

    test("adds to an arguments object", () => {
        function f(a) {
            arguments.foo = 1;
            arguments[3] = 2;
            return arguments;
        }
        const args = f(0);
        expect(args.foo).toBe(1);
        expect(args[3]).toBe(2);
        expect(args.length).toBe(1);
    });

    test("Object.assign calls inherited setters on the target", () => {
        let setterValue;
        const target = Object.create({
            set foo(value) {
                setterValue = value;
            },
        });
        Object.assign(target, { foo: 1, bar: 2 });
        expect(setterValue).toBe(1);
        expect(Object.hasOwn(target, "foo")).toBeFalse();
        expect(target.bar).toBe(2);
    });

    test("Object.assign throws on an inherited read-only property", () => {
        const target = Object.create(Object.defineProperty({}, "foo", { value: 1, writable: false }));
        expect(() => Object.assign(target, { foo: 2 })).toThrow(TypeError);
    });
});

test("objects built by a constructor keep their shape across garbage collection", () => {
    function Point(x, y) {
        this.x = x;
        this.y = y;
        this.z = x + y;
    }
    const kept = new Point(1, 2);
    // Only `kept` uses the Point shapes; the shapes it went through while being built are referenced by nothing else.
    for (let i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) new Point(3, 4);
    gc();
    gc();
    expect(haveSameShape(new Point(3, 4), kept)).toBeTrue();
});

test("objects built by a literal and additions keep their shape across garbage collection", () => {
    const build = () => {
        const object = {};
        object.first = 1;
        object.second = 2;
        delete object.second;
        object.third = 3;
        return object;
    };
    const kept = build();
    gc();
    gc();
    expect(haveSameShape(build(), kept)).toBeTrue();
});

test("transition chains that no object uses are collected", () => {
    evaluateSource(`
        var __shapeChainPrototype = {};
        var __shapeChainObject = Object.create(__shapeChainPrototype);
        __shapeChainObject.a = 1;
        __shapeChainObject.b = 2;
    `);
    const registry = new FinalizationRegistry(() => {});
    registry.register(globalThis.__shapeChainPrototype, "prototype");
    markAsGarbage("__shapeChainPrototype");
    markAsGarbage("__shapeChainObject");
    gc();

    // The shapes of the object keep its prototype alive, so the prototype dies only if its shapes do.
    let collected = false;
    cleanupFinalizationRegistry(registry, () => {
        collected = true;
    });
    expect(collected).toBeTrue();
});

test("haveSameShape() needs objects", () => {
    expect(() => haveSameShape({}, 1)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "1 is not an object");
    expect(haveSameShape({ a: 1 }, { a: 2 })).toBeTrue();
    expect(haveSameShape({ a: 1 }, { b: 2 })).toBeFalse();
});

test("an object that changes its prototype does not keep its old prototypes alive", () => {

        var __replacedPrototype = {};

        Object.setPrototypeOf(__changingPrototypeObject, {});
    `);
    const registry = new FinalizationRegistry(() => {});
    registry.register(globalThis.__replacedPrototype, "replaced prototype");
    markAsGarbage("__replacedPrototype");
    gc();

    let collected = false;
    cleanupFinalizationRegistry(registry, () => {
        collected = true;
    });
    expect(collected).toBeTrue();
});

test("slow paths return values without overwriting destinations on exceptions", () => {
    const number = { valueOf: () => 7 };
    expect(number + 3).toBe(10);
    expect(number * 3).toBe(21);
    expect(number < 8).toBeTrue();
    expect(number | 8).toBe(15);

    const thrown = {};
    let destination = 42;
    try {
        destination =
            {
                valueOf() {
                    throw thrown;
                },
            } + 1;
    } catch (error) {
        expect(error).toBe(thrown);
    }
    expect(destination).toBe(42);
});

test("postfix slow paths return both the old and updated values", () => {
    let value = { valueOf: () => 12345678901234567890n };
    expect(value++).toBe(12345678901234567890n);
    expect(value).toBe(12345678901234567891n);
    expect(value--).toBe(12345678901234567891n);
    expect(value).toBe(12345678901234567890n);
    value = value++;
    expect(value).toBe(12345678901234567890n);
});

test("cache-only helpers distinguish returned values from cache misses", () => {
    function read(object) {
        return object.value;
    }
    let getterCalls = 0;
    const cases = [
        [{ a: 1, value: false }, false],
        [{ b: 1, value: 0 }, 0],
        [{ c: 1, value: "" }, ""],
        [{ d: 1, value: undefined }, undefined],
        [{ e: 1, value: null }, null],
        [{ missing: 1 }, undefined],
        [
            {
                get value() {
                    ++getterCalls;
                    return "getter";
                },
            },
            "getter",
        ],
    ];
    for (let iteration = 0; iteration < 10; ++iteration)
        for (const [object, expected] of cases) expect(read(object)).toBe(expected);
    expect(getterCalls).toBe(10);
});

test("variable-length slow-path inputs survive nested calls and collection", () => {
    const call = new Function("callee", "value", `return callee(${Array(600).fill("value").join(",")})`);
    const value = {};
    function callee() {
        gc();
        expect(arguments.length).toBe(600);
        for (const argument of arguments) expect(argument).toBe(value);
        return value;
    }
    const bound = callee.bind(null);
    for (let iteration = 0; iteration < 3; ++iteration) expect(call(bound, value)).toBe(value);

    const throwing = function () {
        throw value;
    }.bind(null);
    expect(() => call(throwing, value)).toThrow(value);
    expect(call(bound, value)).toBe(value);
});

test("iterator slow paths preserve done state when extracting a value throws", () => {
    const thrown = {};
    let closed = false;
    const iterable = {
        [Symbol.iterator]() {
            return {
                next() {
                    return {
                        done: false,
                        get value() {
                            throw thrown;
                        },
                    };
                },
                return() {
                    closed = true;
                    return {};
                },
            };
        },
    };
    expect(() => {
        const [value] = iterable;
    }).toThrow(thrown);
    expect(closed).toBeFalse();
});

test("exhausted iterator outputs remain safe across collection", () => {
    function* values() {
        yield 42;
    }
    const iterator = values();
    for (let iteration = 0; iteration < 3; ++iteration) {
        const [first, second = "default"] = iterator;
        gc();
        expect(first).toBe(iteration === 0 ? 42 : undefined);
        expect(second).toBe("default");
    }
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/source-positions-of-errors.js
// Each source has an @ where the instruction that matters is.
function positionOfMarker(source) {
    const before = source.slice(0, source.indexOf("@")).split("\n");
    // NB: The function around the source starts two lines above it.
    return [before.length + 2, before[before.length - 1].length + 1];
}

function positionInStack(stack) {
    const frame = stack.split("\n").find(line => line.includes("at anonymous"));
    const match = frame.match(/(\d+):(\d+)\)?$/);
    return [Number(match[1]), Number(match[2])];
}

function positionSeenByProbe(source) {
    let position = null;
    const probe = () => {
        position ??= positionInStack(new Error().stack);
    };
    const object = {
        get getter() {
            probe();
            return 1;
        },
        set setter(value) {
            probe();
        },
        get callable() {
            probe();
            return () => {};
        },
        method() {
            probe();
        },
    };
    object.object = object;
    const value = {
        toString() {
            probe();
            return "";
        },
    };
    const iterable = {
        [Symbol.iterator]() {
            probe();
            return { next: () => ({ done: true }) };
        },
    };
    const proxy = new Proxy(
        {},
        {
            ownKeys() {
                probe();
                return [];
            },
            has(target, key) {
                if (key !== Symbol.unscopables) probe();
                return true;
            },
            get: () => () => {},
        }
    );
    new Function("object", "value", "iterable", "proxy", "call", "Class", "key", source.replace("@", ""))(
        object,
        value,
        iterable,
        proxy,
        () => probe(),
        function () {
            probe();
        },
        "setter"
    );
    return position;
}

function expectProbePositions(sources) {
    for (const source of sources)
        expect([source, positionSeenByProbe(source)]).toEqual([source, positionOfMarker(source)]);
}

function positionOfError(source) {
    const u = undefined;
    const object = {};
    try {
        new Function("u", "object", "key", source.replace("@", ""))(u, object, "key");
    } catch (error) {
        return positionInStack(error.stack);
    }
    return null;
}

function expectErrorPositions(sources) {
    for (const source of sources) expect([source, positionOfError(source)]).toEqual([source, positionOfMarker(source)]);
}

test("stores are where their operator is", () => {
    expectProbePositions([
        "object.setter @= 1;",
        "object.object.setter @= 1;",
        'object["setter"] @= 1;',
        "object[key] @= 1;",
        "(object).setter @= 1;",
        "object\n    .setter\n    @= 1;",
        "object.setter @+= 1;",
        "object[key] @+= 1;",
        "object.setter @||= 1;",
        "object.setter @??= 1;",
        "object.setter@++;",
        "object.setter@--;",
        "object[key]@++;",
        "@++object.setter;",
        "@--object[key];",
    ]);
});

test("stores of patterns are where the assignment is", () => {
    expectProbePositions([
        "[object.setter] @= [1];",
        "({ a: object.setter } @= { a: 1 });",
        "[object.setter = 1] @= [];",
        "[...object.setter] @= [];",
    ]);
});

test("stores of loop heads are where the keyword is", () => {
    expectProbePositions(["for (object.setter @of [1]);", "for (object.setter @in { a: 1 });"]);
});

test("calls are where their arguments start", () => {
    expectProbePositions([
        "call@();",
        "object.method@();",
        'object["method"]@();',
        "object\n    .method@();",
        "(object.method)@();",
        "@new Class();",
        "@new Class;",
    ]);
});

test("reading what gets called is where the call is", () => {
    expectProbePositions(["object.callable@();", "object\n    .callable\n    @();"]);
});

test("member accesses are where their operator is", () => {
    expectProbePositions([
        "object@.getter;",
        "object.object@.getter;",
        "object\n    @.getter;",
        'object@["getter"];',
        "object.object@['getter'];",
    ]);
});

test("everything in an optional chain is where the chain starts", () => {
    expectProbePositions(["object@?.getter;", "object@?.object.getter;", "object@?.method();", "object.method@?.();"]);
});

test("iteration of a spread element is where what it is in is", () => {
    expectProbePositions(["@[...iterable];", "@[1, ...iterable];", "call@(...iterable);", "@new Class(...iterable);"]);
});

test("patterns of declarations are where the declaration is", () => {
    expectProbePositions([
        "@var [a] = iterable;",
        "@let [a] = iterable;",
        "@const { getter } = object;",
        "for (var a @of iterable);",
        "@try { throw object; } catch ({ getter }) {}",
    ]);
});

test("other constructs", () => {
    expectProbePositions([
        "@`${value}`;",
        "(@{ ...proxy });",
        "with (proxy) { missing@(); }",
        "with (proxy) { missing @= 1; }",
        "with (proxy) { @typeof missing; }",
        "with (proxy) { @delete missing; }",
    ]);
});

test("errors", () => {
    expectErrorPositions([
        "u@.x;",
        "u@[key];",
        "u.x @= 1;",
        "u[key] @= 1;",
        "u.x @+= 1;",
        "u.x@++;",
        "@++u.x;",
        "u.x@();",
        "object.missing@();",
        "object.missing@.x;",
        "object.missing.x @= 1;",
        "@new u();",
        "@class C extends u {}",
        "@with (u) {}",
        "typeof @tdz; let tdz;",
    ]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/source-text-parking.js
// The text of a large source that nothing read for a while is compressed, and decompressed when something reads it
// again. parkSourceTexts() compresses every text that is large enough, and code must behave the same afterwards.

// NB: Only large sources are parked, so the code under test comes from an eval of a long string.
const padding = "/* padding */\n".repeat(2000);

function evalLargeSource(code) {
    return (0, eval)(`${padding}${code}\n${padding}`);
}

describe("parked source texts", () => {
    test("a function compiles for the first time from a parked source", () => {
        const outer = evalLargeSource("(function outer() { return function inner(a, b) { return a + b; }; })");
        expect(parkSourceTexts()).toBeGreaterThan(0);
        expect(outer()(1, 2)).toBe(3);
    });

    test("a function of a parked source has its source text", () => {
        const f = evalLargeSource("(function named(a, b) { return 'caf\u00e9 \u2019 \ud83d\ude00'; })");
        expect(parkSourceTexts()).toBeGreaterThan(0);
        expect(f.toString()).toBe("function named(a, b) { return 'caf\u00e9 \u2019 \ud83d\ude00'; }");
        expect(f()).toBe("caf\u00e9 \u2019 \ud83d\ude00");
    });

    test("an error thrown from a parked source reports its position", () => {
        const f = evalLargeSource("(function thrower() {\n    return undefinedName.property;\n})");
        expect(parkSourceTexts()).toBeGreaterThan(0);
        expect(f).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "'undefinedName' is not defined");
        expect(parkSourceTexts()).toBeGreaterThan(0);
        expect(f).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "'undefinedName' is not defined");
    });

    test("a text can be parked again after it was read", () => {
        const outer = evalLargeSource(
            "(function () { return [function a() { return 1; }, function b() { return 2; }]; })"
        );
        expect(parkSourceTexts()).toBeGreaterThan(0);
        const [a, b] = outer();
        expect(a()).toBe(1);
        expect(parkSourceTexts()).toBeGreaterThan(0);
        expect(b()).toBe(2);
        expect(b.toString()).toBe("function b() { return 2; }");
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/special-property-cache.js
// Conversions of objects to primitives remember what Get of toString, valueOf, @@toPrimitive and @@toStringTag gives
// for the objects of a shape. These tests change those properties after conversions that remembered them.

const convertOften = (object, count = 50) => {
    let result;
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) result = `${object}`;
    return result;
};

const withRestoredObjectPrototype = callback => {
    const keys = ["toString", "valueOf", Symbol.toPrimitive, Symbol.toStringTag];
    const descriptors = keys.map(key => Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(Object.prototype, key));
    try {
        callback();
    } finally {
        keys.forEach((key, index) => {
            if (descriptors[index]) Object.defineProperty(Object.prototype, key, descriptors[index]);
            else delete Object.prototype[key];
        });
    }
};

describe("replacing the values of properties of Object.prototype", () => {
    test("toString", () => {
        withRestoredObjectPrototype(() => {
            const object = { a: 1 };
            expect(convertOften(object)).toBe("[object Object]");
            Object.prototype.toString = () => "replaced";
            expect(`${object}`).toBe("replaced");
            expect(String(object)).toBe("replaced");
            expect([object, object].join()).toBe("replaced,replaced");
        });
    });

    test("valueOf", () => {
        withRestoredObjectPrototype(() => {
            const object = { b: 1 };
            expect(object + "").toBe("[object Object]");
            expect(object + "").toBe("[object Object]");
            Object.prototype.valueOf = () => 21;
            expect(object * 2).toBe(42);
            expect(object + "").toBe("21");
            expect(`${object}`).toBe("[object Object]");
        });
    });

    test("with assignments that property lookup caches make", () => {
        withRestoredObjectPrototype(() => {
            const object = { c: 1 };
            const replacements = [() => "first", () => "second"];
            const original = Object.prototype.toString;
            const results = [];
            for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) {
                expect(convertOften(object, 2)).toBe(i === 0 ? "[object Object]" : "second");
                Object.prototype.toString = replacements[0];
                results.push(`${object}`);
                Object.prototype.toString = replacements[1];
                results.push(`${object}`);
            }
            Object.prototype.toString = original;
            expect(`${object}`).toBe("[object Object]");
            for (let i = 0; i < results.length; ++i) expect(results[i]).toBe(i % 2 === 0 ? "first" : "second");
        });
    });

    test("with Object.assign", () => {
        withRestoredObjectPrototype(() => {
            const object = { d: 1 };
            expect(convertOften(object)).toBe("[object Object]");
            Object.assign(Object.prototype, { toString: () => "assigned" });
            expect(`${object}`).toBe("assigned");
        });
    });

    test("with Object.defineProperty", () => {
        withRestoredObjectPrototype(() => {
            const object = { e: 1 };
            expect(convertOften(object)).toBe("[object Object]");
            Object.defineProperty(Object.prototype, "toString", { value: () => "defined" });
            expect(`${object}`).toBe("defined");
            Object.defineProperty(Object.prototype, "toString", { get: () => () => "from getter" });
            expect(`${object}`).toBe("from getter");
        });
    });
});

describe("adding properties to prototypes", () => {
    test("@@toPrimitive on Object.prototype", () => {
        withRestoredObjectPrototype(() => {
            const object = { f: 1 };
            expect(convertOften(object)).toBe("[object Object]");
            Object.prototype[Symbol.toPrimitive] = hint => `primitive ${hint}`;
            expect(`${object}`).toBe("primitive string");
            expect(object + "").toBe("primitive default");
        });
    });

    test("@@toStringTag on Object.prototype", () => {
        withRestoredObjectPrototype(() => {
            const object = { g: 1 };
            expect(convertOften(object)).toBe("[object Object]");
            expect(Object.prototype.toString.call(object)).toBe("[object Object]");
            Object.prototype[Symbol.toStringTag] = "Tagged";
            expect(`${object}`).toBe("[object Tagged]");
            expect(Object.prototype.toString.call(object)).toBe("[object Tagged]");
        });
    });

    test("toString on a prototype between the object and Object.prototype", () => {
        class Base {}
        class Derived extends Base {}
        const object = new Derived();
        expect(convertOften(object)).toBe("[object Object]");
        Base.prototype.toString = () => "from Base";
        expect(`${object}`).toBe("from Base");
        Derived.prototype.toString = () => "from Derived";
        expect(`${object}`).toBe("from Derived");
        delete Derived.prototype.toString;
        expect(`${object}`).toBe("from Base");
        delete Base.prototype.toString;
        expect(`${object}`).toBe("[object Object]");
    });

    test("changing the prototype of a prototype", () => {
        const middle = {};
        const object = Object.create(middle);
        expect(convertOften(object)).toBe("[object Object]");
        Object.setPrototypeOf(middle, { toString: () => "new chain" });
        expect(`${object}`).toBe("new chain");
        Object.setPrototypeOf(middle, null);
        expect(() => `${object}`).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, "Cannot convert object to string");
    });

    test("a prototype with many properties", () => {
        const prototype = {};
        for (let i = 0; i < 200; ++i) prototype[`property${i}`] = i;
        const object = Object.create(prototype);
        expect(convertOften(object)).toBe("[object Object]");
        prototype.toString = () => "dictionary";
        expect(`${object}`).toBe("dictionary");
        prototype.toString = () => "dictionary again";
        expect(`${object}`).toBe("dictionary again");
        delete prototype.property5;
        expect(`${object}`).toBe("dictionary again");
        delete prototype.toString;
        expect(`${object}`).toBe("[object Object]");
    });
});

describe("toJSON in JSON.stringify", () => {
    test("added to Object.prototype", () => {
        const object = { h: 1 };
        try {
            for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) expect(JSON.stringify(object)).toBe('{"h":1}');
            Object.prototype.toJSON = () => "added";
            expect(JSON.stringify(object)).toBe('"added"');
            expect(JSON.stringify([object, { i: 2 }])).toBe('"added"');
        } finally {
            delete Object.prototype.toJSON;
        }
        expect(JSON.stringify(object)).toBe('{"h":1}');
    });

    test("replaced on a prototype", () => {
        class Point {
            constructor(x) {
                this.x = x;
            }
            toJSON() {
                return `point ${this.x}`;
            }
        }
        const points = [new Point(1), new Point(2)];
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) expect(JSON.stringify(points)).toBe('["point 1","point 2"]');
        Point.prototype.toJSON = function () {
            return this.x * 10;
        };
        expect(JSON.stringify(points)).toBe("[10,20]");
        delete Point.prototype.toJSON;
        expect(JSON.stringify(points)).toBe('[{"x":1},{"x":2}]');
    });

    test("Date.prototype.toJSON replaced", () => {
        const original = Date.prototype.toJSON;
        const date = new Date(0);
        try {
            for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) expect(JSON.stringify(date)).toBe('"1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"');
            Date.prototype.toJSON = () => "replaced";
            expect(JSON.stringify(date)).toBe('"replaced"');
        } finally {
            Date.prototype.toJSON = original;
        }
        expect(JSON.stringify(date)).toBe('"1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"');
    });
});

test("@@toStringTag getter that changes @@toStringTag", () => {
    const prototype = {};
    const first = Object.create(prototype);
    const second = Object.create(prototype);
    let calls = 0;
    Object.defineProperty(prototype, Symbol.toStringTag, {
        configurable: true,
        get() {
            if (calls++ === 0) {
                Object.defineProperty(prototype, Symbol.toStringTag, { value: "X", configurable: true });
                expect(Object.prototype.toString.call(second)).toBe("[object X]");
            }
            return "Y";
        },
    });
    expect(Object.prototype.toString.call(first)).toBe("[object Y]");
    expect(Object.prototype.toString.call(first)).toBe("[object X]");
    expect(Object.prototype.toString.call(second)).toBe("[object X]");
    expect(`${first}`).toBe("[object X]");
});

describe("then and constructor in promise resolution", () => {
    const resolveOften = (makeValue, count = 50) => {
        const results = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i)
            Promise.resolve()
                .then(() => makeValue())
                .then(value => results.push(value));
        runQueuedPromiseJobs();
        return results;
    };

    test("then added to Object.prototype", () => {
        const results = resolveOften(() => ({ a: 1 }));
        expect(results).toHaveLength(50);
        expect(results[0]).toEqual({ a: 1 });
        Object.prototype.then = function (resolve) {
            resolve("from then");
        };
        try {
            expect(resolveOften(() => ({ a: 1 }), 1)).toEqual(["from then"]);
        } finally {
            delete Object.prototype.then;
        }
        expect(resolveOften(() => ({ a: 1 }), 1)).toEqual([{ a: 1 }]);
    });

    test("Promise.prototype.then replaced", () => {
        resolveOften(() => Promise.resolve(1));
        const originalThen = Promise.prototype.then;
        let calls = 0;
        Promise.prototype.then = function (...args) {
            ++calls;
            return originalThen.apply(this, args);
        };
        try {
            let result;
            originalThen.call(
                Promise.resolve().then(() => Promise.resolve(2)),
                value => (result = value)
            );
            runQueuedPromiseJobs();
            expect(result).toBe(2);
            expect(calls).toBeGreaterThan(0);
        } finally {
            Promise.prototype.then = originalThen;
        }
    });

    test("Promise.prototype.constructor replaced", () => {
        const promise = Promise.resolve(3);
        for (let i = 0; i < 50; ++i) expect(Promise.resolve(promise)).toBe(promise);
        const originalConstructor = Promise.prototype.constructor;
        Promise.prototype.constructor = function () {};
        try {
            expect(Promise.resolve(promise)).not.toBe(promise);
        } finally {
            Promise.prototype.constructor = originalConstructor;
        }
        expect(Promise.resolve(promise)).toBe(promise);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/stack-trace-caller-positions.js
// Callers in a stack trace are shown at their call sites, also when the interpreter takes its fast paths for
// calls that it has made before.

function callerFrame(stack, name) {
    const frame = stack.split("\n").find(line => line.includes(`at ${name} (`));
    return frame.match(/:(\d+:\d+)\)$/)[1];
}

function inner() {
    return new Error().stack;
}

function callsInner() {
    let unrelated = 1;
    unrelated += 1;
    return inner();
}

function callsGetter() {
    const object = {
        get value() {
            return new Error().stack;
        },
    };
    return object.value;
}

function needsEnvironment() {
    let captured = 1;
    const closure = () => captured;
    return new Error().stack;
}

function callsNeedsEnvironment() {
    let unrelated = 1;
    unrelated += 1;
    return needsEnvironment();
}

test("caller of a plain call", () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) expect(callerFrame(callsInner(), "callsInner")).toBe("16:17");
});

test("caller of an inline getter call", () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) expect(callerFrame(callsGetter(), "callsGetter")).toBe("25:18");
});

test("caller of a call to a function that needs an environment", () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) expect(callerFrame(callsNeedsEnvironment(), "callsNeedsEnvironment")).toBe("37:28");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/strict-global-assignment.js
// These run as strict mode scripts, whose global-looking assignment targets are resolved before the right-hand side
// is evaluated.
function runStrictScript(source) {
    return new Function(`"use strict"; ${source}`)();
}

test("assignments to declared globals", () => {
    globalThis.strictGlobalCounter = 0;
    runStrictScript("for (let i = 0; i < 10; ++i) strictGlobalCounter = strictGlobalCounter + 1;");
    expect(globalThis.strictGlobalCounter).toBe(10);
    delete globalThis.strictGlobalCounter;
});

test("assignments to unresolvable references throw after the right-hand side", () => {
    delete globalThis.strictGlobalLater;
    expect(() => runStrictScript("strictGlobalLater = (globalThis.strictGlobalLater = 1);")).toThrowWithMessage(
        ReferenceError,
        "'strictGlobalLater' is not defined"
    );
    expect(globalThis.strictGlobalLater).toBe(1);
    runStrictScript("strictGlobalLater = 2;");
    expect(globalThis.strictGlobalLater).toBe(2);
    delete globalThis.strictGlobalLater;
    expect(() => runStrictScript("strictGlobalLater = 3;")).toThrow(ReferenceError);
});

test("bindings deleted by the right-hand side", () => {
    globalThis.strictGlobalDeleted = 1;
    expect(() =>
        runStrictScript("strictGlobalDeleted = (delete globalThis.strictGlobalDeleted, 2);")
    ).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "'strictGlobalDeleted' is not defined");
    expect(globalThis.strictGlobalDeleted).toBeUndefined();
});

test("read-only and accessor globals", () => {
    Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "strictGlobalReadOnly", { value: 1, writable: false, configurable: true });
    expect(() => runStrictScript("strictGlobalReadOnly = 2;")).toThrow(TypeError);
    delete globalThis.strictGlobalReadOnly;

    let stored;
    Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "strictGlobalAccessor", {
        set(value) {
            stored = value;
        },
        configurable: true,
    });
    runStrictScript("strictGlobalAccessor = 3; strictGlobalAccessor = 4;");
    expect(stored).toBe(4);
    delete globalThis.strictGlobalAccessor;
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/strict-mode-class-body-in-sloppy-function.js
function assignsInComputedKey() {
    class C {
        [(undeclaredInComputedKey = "a")]() {}
    }
}

function assignsInHeritage() {
    class C extends (undeclaredInHeritage = Object) {}
}

function assignsAfterClass() {
    class C {
        m() {}
    }
    undeclaredAfterClass = 1;
    return undeclaredAfterClass;
}

function deletesBeforeAndAfterClass() {
    const object = Object.freeze({ a: 1 });
    const before = delete object.a;
    class C {}
    const after = delete object.a;
    return [before, after];
}

test("assignments in a class heritage or computed key are strict", () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        expect(assignsInComputedKey).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "'undeclaredInComputedKey' is not defined");
        expect(assignsInHeritage).toThrowWithMessage(ReferenceError, "'undeclaredInHeritage' is not defined");
    }
});

test("code around a class in a sloppy function stays sloppy", () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        expect(assignsAfterClass()).toBe(1);
        expect(deletesBeforeAndAfterClass()).toEqual([false, false]);
    }
});

test("primitive string object destructuring sees virtual indexed properties", () => {
    const { 0: first, 1: second, length } = "ab";
    expect(first).toBe("a");
    expect(second).toBe("b");
    expect(length).toBe(2);

    const values = [];
    for (const { 0: c } of "ab") {
        values.push(c);
    }
    expect(values).toEqual(["a", "b"]);
});
test("string object: string property name access", () => {
    expect(new String("").length).toBe(0);
    expect(new String("foo").length).toBe(3);
    expect(new String("foo").bar).toBeUndefined();
    expect(new String("foo").foo).toBe("foo");
    expect(typeof new String("foo").strictThis).toBe("object");
    let str = new String("foo");
    expect(str.strictThis).toBe(str);
    expect(typeof str.nonStrictThis).toBe("object");
    expect(str.nonStrictThis === str.nonStrictThis).toBeTrue();
    expect(str.nonStrictThis !== String.prototype).toBeTrue();
    expect(str.nonStrictThis instanceof String).toBeTrue();
    expect(new String("foo").nonStrictThis !== new String("foo").nonStrictThis).toBeTrue();
    expect(new String("foo").strictThis !== new String("foo").strictThis).toBeTrue();

    lastSetThisValue = null;
    expect(() => str.strictGetPrivate).toThrow();
    expect(lastSetThisValue).toBeNull();
    lastSetThisValue = null;
    expect(() => str.nonStrictGetPrivate).toThrow();
    expect(lastSetThisValue).toBeNull();
    lastSetThisValue = null;
    expect(() => (str.strictSetPrivate = "wat")).toThrow();
    expect(lastSetThisValue).toBeNull();
    lastSetThisValue = null;
    expect(() => (str.nonStrictSetPrivate = "wat")).toThrow();
    expect(lastSetThisValue).toBeNull();
    lastSetThisValue = null;
});

test("oversized deferred concatenations throw", () => {
    let string = "abcdefgh";
    for (let i = 0; i < 28; ++i) string = string + string;
    expect(string.length).toBe(2 ** 31);

    expect(() => string + string).toThrowWithMessage(RangeError, "Invalid string length");
    expect(() => string.concat(string)).toThrowWithMessage(RangeError, "Invalid string length");
    expect(() => `${string}${string}`).toThrowWithMessage(RangeError, "Invalid string length");

    let suffix = "ab";
    for (let i = 0; i < 30; ++i) {
        string += suffix;
        suffix += suffix;
    }
    expect(string.length).toBe(2 ** 32 - 2);
    expect((string + "").length).toBe(2 ** 32 - 2);
    expect(("" + string).length).toBe(2 ** 32 - 2);
    expect(() => string + "a").toThrowWithMessage(RangeError, "Invalid string length");
    expect(() => "a" + string).toThrowWithMessage(RangeError, "Invalid string length");
    expect(() => string.concat("a")).toThrowWithMessage(RangeError, "Invalid string length");
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/string-keys-made-at-run-time.js
// Strings made at run time become property keys the first time they are used as one. With a low JIT threshold the
// functions are compiled, so later accesses go through the keyed caches of JIT code.

function write(object, key, value) {
    object[key] = value;
}

function read(object, key) {
    return object[key];
}

function makeKeys() {
    const digits = "0123456789".split("");
    const unicode = "äöüåæø中文\u{1f600}";
    return {
        inline: digits.map(digit => "inline_key_" + digit),
        rope: digits.map(digit => "a_rope_that_is_too_long_for_a_cell_" + digit),
        unicodeRope: digits.map(digit => unicode + "_rope_" + digit),
        substring: digits.map(digit => ("substring_source_" + digit + "_with_a_tail_of_some_length").slice(0, 18)),
        longSubstring: digits.map(digit =>
            ("a_substring_that_is_too_long_for_a_cell_" + digit + "_and_its_tail").substring(2, 42)
        ),
        unicodeSubstring: digits.map(digit => (unicode + unicode + "_" + digit + "_tail").slice(3, 22)),
        joined: digits.map(digit => ["a_joined_key_", digit].join("")),
        lowercased: digits.map(digit => ("A_LOWERCASED_KEY_THAT_IS_TOO_LONG_FOR_A_CELL_" + digit).toLowerCase()),
        json: digits.map(digit => JSON.stringify({ digit, unicode, padding: "x".repeat(100) })),
    };
}

describe("string keys made at run time", () => {
    for (const [kind, keys] of Object.entries(makeKeys())) {
        test(`${kind} strings`, () => {
            const expected = keys.map(key => Array.from(key, character => character.codePointAt(0)));
            const object = {};
            for (let round = 0; round < 200; ++round) {
                for (let i = 0; i < keys.length; ++i) write(object, keys[i], round * keys.length + i);
            }
            for (let i = 0; i < keys.length; ++i) {
                const key = keys[i];
                expect(read(object, key)).toBe(199 * keys.length + i);
                // An equal string that was made otherwise names the same property.
                expect(read(object, key.split("").join(""))).toBe(199 * keys.length + i);
                expect(Object.hasOwn(object, key)).toBeTrue();
                // The strings are unchanged by being keys.
                expect(Array.from(key, character => character.codePointAt(0))).toEqual(expected[i]);
                expect(key.length).toBe(key.split("").length);
                expect(key + "!").toBe(key.split("").join("") + "!");
                expect(key.slice(1)).toBe(key.split("").slice(1).join(""));
            }
            expect(Object.keys(object)).toEqual(keys);
        });
    }

    test("keys that are put together again for every access", () => {
        const names = ["click", "change", "keydown", "focus", "blur", "input", "submit", "dblclick"];
        const handlers = {};
        for (const name of names) write(handlers, "on" + name, name.length);
        let sum = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 4000; ++i) sum += read(handlers, "on" + names[i & 7]);
        expect(sum).toBe(500 * (5 + 6 + 7 + 5 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 8));
        expect(Object.keys(handlers)).toEqual(names.map(name => "on" + name));

        // Ropes of ropes, of substrings and of strings with a NUL character find the same properties.
        const object = {};
        for (let i = 0; i < 400; ++i) {
            const digit = String(i % 10);
            write(object, "a_" + digit + ("_nested_" + digit) + "_rope", i);
            write(object, "from_" + ("a_substring_source_" + digit).slice(2, 11) + "_" + digit, i);
            write(object, "nul\0" + "_key_" + digit, i);
            write(object, "nul" + "_key_" + digit, -i);
            // 32 characters fit in a string cell, and 33 do not.
            write(object, "a_key_of_32_characters_in_all_" + digit + digit, i);
            write(object, "a_key_of_33_characters_in_total_" + digit, i);
        }
        expect(Object.keys(object).length).toBe(60);
        for (let digit = 0; digit < 10; ++digit) {
            expect(read(object, ["a_", digit, "_nested_", digit, "_rope"].join(""))).toBe(390 + digit);
            expect(read(object, `from_substring_${digit}`)).toBe(390 + digit);
            expect(read(object, `nul\0_key_${digit}`)).toBe(390 + digit);
            expect(read(object, `nul_key_${digit}`)).toBe(-390 - digit);
            expect(read(object, `a_key_of_32_characters_in_all_${digit}${digit}`)).toBe(390 + digit);
            expect(read(object, `a_key_of_33_characters_in_total_${digit}`)).toBe(390 + digit);
        }

        // A key keeps its property across a collection, which empties the VM's cache of such keys.
        gc();
        expect(read(handlers, "on" + names[7])).toBe(8);
        expect(read(object, "a_" + "9" + ("_nested_" + "9") + "_rope")).toBe(399);
    });

    test("keys that the access itself puts together", () => {
        const names = ["click", "change", "keydown", "focus", "blur", "input", "submit", "dblclick"];
        const unicode = "äöü中文";
        const object = {};
        const array = [];
        const keys = [];
        let sum = 0;
        let found = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 4000; ++i) {
            const name = names[i & 7];
            object["on" + name] = i;
            sum += object["on" + name];
            if ("on" + name in object) ++found;
            if (Object.hasOwn(object, "off" + name)) --found;
            // A key that is used as a value too is the same string either way.
            const key = "data-" + name;
            object[key] = key;
            if (i < 8) keys.push(key);
            // Keys that are not ASCII, that are too long for the VM to remember, or that are indices.
            object[unicode + name] = i;
            object["a_key_of_more_than_32_characters_" + name] = i;
            array["1000" + "0000" + (i & 7)] = i;
            // A key in a local variable that the paths of a branch assign.
            let either;
            if (i & 1) either = "odd_" + name;
            else either = "even_" + name;
            object[either] = i;
        }
        expect(sum).toBe((3999 * 4000) / 2);
        expect(found).toBe(4000);
        expect(keys).toEqual(names.map(name => `data-${name}`));
        for (let i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
            const name = names[i];
            expect(object[["on", name].join("")]).toBe(3992 + i);
            expect(object[["data-", name].join("")]).toBe(`data-${name}`);
            expect(object[[unicode, name].join("")]).toBe(3992 + i);
            expect(object[["a_key_of_more_than_32_characters_", name].join("")]).toBe(3992 + i);
            expect(object[[i & 1 ? "odd_" : "even_", name].join("")]).toBe(3992 + i);
            expect(array[100000000 + i]).toBe(3992 + i);
            expect(keys[i].length).toBe(5 + name.length);
            expect(keys[i] + "!").toBe(`data-${name}!`);
        }
        expect(Object.keys(object).length).toBe(40);
        expect(array.length).toBe(100000008);
    });

    test("keys that are put together while garbage is collected", () => {
        const names = ["click", "change", "keydown", "focus", "blur", "input", "submit", "dblclick"];
        // Most of these strings are never keys, and the ones that are have many different characters.
        function touch(object, i) {
            const key = "rarely_" + names[i & 7] + (i & 63);
            if ((i & 3) === 0) object[key] = i;
            return key.length;
        }
        const object = {};
        let length = 0;
        let expectedLength = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 2000; ++i) {
            length += touch(object, i);
            expectedLength += ["rarely_", names[i & 7], i & 63].join("").length;
        }
        collectGarbageOnEveryAllocation(() => {
            for (let i = 0; i < 256; ++i) length += touch(object, i);
        });
        for (let i = 0; i < 256; ++i) expectedLength += ["rarely_", names[i & 7], i & 63].join("").length;
        expect(length).toBe(expectedLength);
        expect(Object.keys(object).length).toBe(16);
        expect(object.rarely_click0).toBe(192);
        expect(object.rarely_blur60).toBe(252);
    });

    test("index keys", () => {
        const array = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < 100; ++i) {
            const inlineIndex = "1000" + "0000" + (i % 10);
            const ropeIndex = "4000" + "0000" + "0";
            write(array, inlineIndex, i);
            write(array, ropeIndex.slice(0, 9), i);
        }
        expect(array.length).toBe(400000001);
        expect(array[100000009]).toBe(99);
        expect(array[400000000]).toBe(99);
        expect(read(array, "1000" + "00009")).toBe(99);
        expect(Object.keys(array).length).toBe(11);
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/string-rope-resolution.js
// Concatenated strings are ropes until something reads their code units. These tests read ropes of different shapes
// and sizes, small and large ones, built on either side, mixing ASCII and other code units.

function pieces(count, mixed) {
    const result = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count; ++i) result.push(mixed && i % 3 === 1 ? `é${i}\u{1F600}` : `p${i}`);
    return result;
}

describe("resolving ropes", () => {
    test("ropes built left to right", () => {
        for (const mixed of [false, true]) {
            for (let count = 2; count < 40; ++count) {
                const parts = pieces(count, mixed);
                let rope = "";
                for (const part of parts) rope = rope + part;
                expect(rope.indexOf(parts[count - 1])).toBe(rope.length - parts[count - 1].length);
                expect(rope).toBe(parts.join(""));
            }
        }
    });

    test("ropes built right to left and as trees", () => {
        for (const mixed of [false, true]) {
            for (let count = 2; count < 40; ++count) {
                const parts = pieces(count, mixed);
                let rope = "";
                for (let i = count - 1; i >= 0; --i) rope = parts[i] + rope;
                expect(rope).toBe(parts.join(""));

                const tree = (from, to) =>
                    to - from === 1 ? parts[from] : tree(from, (from + to) >> 1) + tree((from + to) >> 1, to);
                const balanced = tree(0, count);
                expect(balanced.charCodeAt(balanced.length - 1)).toBe(parts.join("").charCodeAt(balanced.length - 1));
                expect(balanced).toBe(parts.join(""));
            }
        }
    });

    test("ropes that share sides", () => {
        const left = "a" + "b";
        const both = left + left;
        const again = both + left + both;
        expect(again).toBe("abababababab".slice(0, 10));
        expect(both).toBe("abab");
    });
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/string-short-ascii.js
// Strings of a few ASCII characters, made by concatenation, substrings and JSON.parse, of every length around the ones
// that keep their characters inline.
const lengths = Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, i) => i + 1);
const alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789";

function expectSameString(actual, expected) {
    expect(actual).toBe(expected);
    expect(actual.length).toBe(expected.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < expected.length; ++i) {
        expect(actual.charCodeAt(i)).toBe(expected.charCodeAt(i));
        expect(actual.charAt(i)).toBe(expected[i]);
        expect(actual[i]).toBe(expected[i]);
    }
    expect(actual.charCodeAt(expected.length)).toBeNaN();
    expect(actual.charAt(expected.length)).toBe("");
}

test("concatenation", () => {
    for (const length of lengths) {
        const expected = alphabet.slice(0, length);
        for (let split = 0; split <= length; ++split) {
            const lhs = alphabet.slice(0, split);
            const rhs = alphabet.slice(split, length);
            expectSameString(lhs + rhs, expected);
            expectSameString(`${lhs}${rhs}`, expected);
            expectSameString(lhs.concat(rhs), expected);
        }
    }
});

test("concatenation with non-ASCII strings", () => {
    expectSameString("abcdefgh" + "é", "abcdefghé");
    expectSameString("é" + "abcdefgh", "éabcdefgh");
    expectSameString("abcdefgh" + "\u{1F600}", "abcdefgh\u{1F600}");
});

test("substrings", () => {
    const source = alphabet + alphabet;
    for (const length of lengths) {
        for (const start of [0, 1, 7, 30]) {
            const expected = Array.from({ length }, (_, i) => source[start + i]).join("");
            expectSameString(source.slice(start, start + length), expected);
            expectSameString(source.substring(start, start + length), expected);
            expectSameString((source + "!").slice(start, start + length), expected);
        }
    }
    const nonAscii = "é" + alphabet;
    expectSameString(nonAscii.slice(1, 20), alphabet.slice(0, 19));
    expectSameString(nonAscii.slice(0, 20), "é" + alphabet.slice(0, 19));
});

test("strings of JSON texts", () => {
    for (const length of lengths) {
        const expected = alphabet.slice(0, length);
        expectSameString(JSON.parse(`"${expected}"`), expected);
        expectSameString(JSON.parse(`["${expected}"]`)[0], expected);
    }
});

test("as property keys, in collections and compared", () => {
    const object = {};
    const map = new Map();
    const set = new Set();
    for (const length of lengths) {
        const flat = alphabet.slice(0, length);
        const made = alphabet.slice(0, length >> 1) + alphabet.slice(length >> 1, length);
        object[made] = length;
        map.set(made, length);
        set.add(made);
        expect(object[flat]).toBe(length);
        expect(map.get(flat)).toBe(length);
        expect(set.has(flat)).toBeTrue();
        expect(made === flat).toBeTrue();
        expect(made < flat + "!").toBeTrue();
        expect(Object.keys(object).includes(flat)).toBeTrue();
    }
    expect(Object.keys(object)).toHaveLength(lengths.length);
    expect(map.size).toBe(lengths.length);
    expect(set.size).toBe(lengths.length);

    const index = "1234567" + "8";
    const array = [];
    array[index] = "x";
    expect(array[12345678]).toBe("x");
});

test("string methods", () => {
    const string = "Hello" + ", world" + "!!";
    expect(string).toBe("Hello, world!!");
    expect(string.toUpperCase()).toBe("HELLO, WORLD!!");
    expect(string.indexOf("world")).toBe(7);
    expect(string.split(", ")).toEqual(["Hello", "world!!"]);
    expect(string.replace("world", "there")).toBe("Hello, there!!");
    expect(string.replace(/o/g, "0")).toBe("Hell0, w0rld!!");
    expect(string.at(-1)).toBe("!");
    expect(string.startsWith("Hello")).toBeTrue();
    expect([...string]).toHaveLength(14);
    expect(String(string)).toBe(string);
    expect(new String(string).length).toBe(14);
    expect(JSON.stringify(string)).toBe('"Hello, world!!"');
    expect(parseInt("123456" + "78")).toBe(12345678);
    expect(Number("1234" + ".5678")).toBe(1234.5678);
    expect(Symbol.for("symbol" + " key") === Symbol.for("symbol key")).toBeTrue();
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/super-computed-property-key.js
test("super property with computed key using Symbol.toPrimitive", () => {
    let callOrder = [];

    let keyObj = {
        [Symbol.toPrimitive]() {
            callOrder.push("toPrimitive");
            return "testProp";
        },
    };

    class Parent {
        constructor() {
            Parent.prototype.testProp = "parent-value";
        }
    }

    class Child extends Parent {
        testMethod() {
            callOrder.push("before-access");
            const result = super[keyObj];
            callOrder.push("after-access");
            return result;
        }
    }

    const child = new Child();
    const result = child.testMethod();

    expect(result).toBe("parent-value");
    expect(callOrder).toEqual(["before-access", "toPrimitive", "after-access"]);
});

test("super property assignment with computed key using Symbol.toPrimitive", () => {
    let callOrder = [];

    let keyObj = {
        [Symbol.toPrimitive]() {
            callOrder.push("toPrimitive");
            return "testProp";
        },
    };

    function getRhsValue() {
        callOrder.push("rhs-evaluation");
        return "new-value";
    }

    class Parent {
        constructor() {
            Parent.prototype.testProp = "original-value";
        }
    }

    class Child extends Parent {
        testMethod() {
            callOrder.push("before-assignment");
            super[keyObj] = getRhsValue();
            callOrder.push("after-assignment");
            return this.testProp;
        }
    }

    const child = new Child();
    const result = child.testMethod();

    expect(result).toBe("new-value");
    // For assignment super[b] = c, ToPropertyKey should happen after c evaluation.
    expect(callOrder).toEqual(["before-assignment", "rhs-evaluation", "toPrimitive", "after-assignment"]);
});

test("super property with computed key that throws in Symbol.toPrimitive", () => {
    let callOrder = [];

    let keyObj = {
        [Symbol.toPrimitive]() {
            callOrder.push("toPrimitive-throws");
            throw new Error("ToPropertyKey error");
        },
    };

    class Parent {
        constructor() {
            Parent.prototype.testProp = "parent-value";
        }
    }

    class Child extends Parent {
        testMethod() {
            callOrder.push("before-access");
            try {
                const result = super[keyObj];
                callOrder.push("should-not-reach");
                return result;
            } catch (e) {
                callOrder.push("caught-exception");
                return "error-value";
            }
        }
    }

    const child = new Child();
    const result = child.testMethod();

    expect(result).toBe("error-value");
    expect(callOrder).toEqual(["before-access", "toPrimitive-throws", "caught-exception"]);
});

test("super property base is resolved after the computed key is evaluated", () => {
    function basesUsed(makeHome) {
        const log = [];
        const first = {
            set x(value) {
                log.push("first");
            },
            get x() {
                log.push("first");
                return () => {};
            },
        };
        const second = {
            set x(value) {
                log.push("second");
            },
            get x() {
                log.push("second");
                return () => {};
            },
        };
        const home = makeHome(() => Object.setPrototypeOf(home, second));
        Object.setPrototypeOf(home, first);
        home.method();
        return log;
    }

    expect(
        basesUsed(changePrototype => ({
            method() {
                [super[(changePrototype(), "x")]] = [1];
            },
        }))
    ).toEqual(["second"]);
    expect(
        basesUsed(changePrototype => ({
            method() {
                for (super[(changePrototype(), "x")] of [1]);
            },
        }))
    ).toEqual(["second"]);
    expect(
        basesUsed(changePrototype => ({
            method() {
                super[(changePrototype(), "x")]?.();
            },
        }))
    ).toEqual(["second"]);
});

test("super property assignment keeps a computed key the right-hand side reassigns", () => {
    const log = [];
    const parent = {
        set first(value) {
            log.push(`first = ${value}`);
        },
        set second(value) {
            log.push(`second = ${value}`);
        },
    };
    const home = {
        method() {
            let key = "first";
            super[key] = ((key = "second"), 1);
        },
    };
    Object.setPrototypeOf(home, parent);
    home.method();

    expect(log).toEqual(["first = 1"]);
});

FILE: Tests/LibJS/Runtime/switch-basic.js
describe("basic switch tests", () => {
    test("string case does not match number target", () => {
        switch (1 + 2) {
            case "3":
                expect().fail();
            case 3:
                return;
            case 5:
            case 1:
                break;
            default:
                break;
        }

        expect().fail();
    });

    test("string concatenation in target", () => {
        var a = "foo";

        switch (a + "bar") {
            case 1:
                expect().fail();
            case "foobar":
            case 2:
                return;
        }
        expect().fail();
    });

    test("default", () => {
        switch (100) {
            default:
                return;
        }

        expect().fail();
    });

    test("return from switch statement", () => {
        function foo(value) {
            switch (value) {
                case 42:
                    return "return from 'case 42'";
                default:
                    return "return from 'default'";
            }
        }
        expect(foo(42)).toBe("return from 'case 42'");
        expect(foo(43)).toBe("return from 'default'");
    });

    test("continue from switch statement", () => {
        let i = 0;
        for (; i < 5; ++i) {
            switch (i) {
                case 0:
                    continue;
                    expect().fail();
                case 0:
                    expect().fail();
                default:
                    continue;
                    expect().fail();
            }
            expect().fail();
        }
        expect(i).toBe(5);
    });

    test("default branch is not taken if more exact branch exists", () => {
        function switchTest(i) {
            let result = 0;
            switch (i) {
                case 1:
                    result += 1;
                    break;
                case 1:
                    expect().fail();
                case 2:
                    result += 2;
                default:
                    result += 4;
                case 3:
                    result += 8;
                    break;
                case 2:
                    expect().fail();
            }
            return result;
        }

        expect(switchTest(1)).toBe(1);
        expect(switchTest(2)).toBe(14);
        expect(switchTest(3)).toBe(8);
        expect(switchTest(4)).toBe(12);
    });

    test("lexical declaration of a case skipped by the dispatch is uninitialized in a later case", () => {
        function read(value) {
            switch (value) {
                case 0:
                    let binding = 5;
                case 1:
                    return binding;
            }
        }
        function call(value) {
            switch (value) {
                case 0:
                    const callee = () => 5;
                default:
                    return callee();
            }
        }
        function write(value) {
            switch (value) {
                case 0:
                    let binding = 5;
                case 1:
                    binding = 7;
                    return binding;
            }
        }

        expect(read(0)).toBe(5);
        expect(() => read(1)).toThrow(ReferenceError);
        expect(call(0)).toBe(5);
        expect(() => call(1)).toThrow(ReferenceError);
        expect(write(0)).toBe(7);
        expect(() => write(1)).toThrow(ReferenceError);
    });

    test("case tests compare against the discriminant as it was evaluated", () => {
        function local(value) {
            let discriminant = value;
            switch (discriminant) {
                case ((discriminant = 2), 2):
                    return "reassigned";
                case 1:
                    return "original";
            }
            return "none";
        }
        expect(local(1)).toBe("original");

        function argument(discriminant) {
            switch (discriminant) {
                case ((discriminant = 2), 2):
                    return "reassigned";
                case 1:
                    return "original";
            }
            return "none";
        }
        expect(argument(1)).toBe("original");
    });
});

describe("errors", () => {
    test("syntax errors", () => {
        expect("switch () {}").not.toEval();
        expect("switch () { case 1: continue; }").not.toEval();
        expect("switch () { case 1: break doesnotexist; }").not.toEval();
        expect("label: switch () { case 1: break not_the_right_label; }").not.toEval();
        expect("label: switch () { case 1: continue label; }").not.toEval();
        expect("switch (foo) { bar }").not.toEval();
        expect("switch (foo) { default: default: }").not.toEval();
    });
});
