// Touches what a realm sets up lazily or caches outside of the VM: shapes, interned strings, regular expressions, typed
// arrays in primitive storage, and enough functions and allocations for the JIT and the collector to get involved.
static constexpr auto TEST_SCRIPT = R"(
    class Point {
        constructor(x, y) { this.x = x; this.y = y; }
        get length() { return Math.hypot(this.x, this.y); }
    }

    function work(seed) {
        const points = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < 2000; ++i)
            points.push(new Point(i, seed));

        const map = new Map();
        const weak = new WeakMap();
        for (const point of points) {
            map.set(`point-${point.x}`, point);
            weak.set(point, point.length);
        }

        const bytes = new Uint8Array(4096);
        bytes.fill(seed & 0xff);

        const words = "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog".replace(/\b\w/gu, c => c.toUpperCase()).split(" ");
        const json = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify({ words, sum: bytes.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) }));
        const date = new Date(0).toISOString();

        let total = 0;
        for (const point of points)
            total += weak.get(map.get(`point-${point.x}`)) > 0 ? 1 : 0;
        return total + json.words.length + json.sum + date.length;
    }

    let result = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; ++i)
        result = work(1);
    try {
        null.property;
    } catch (error) {
        result += error.stack.length > 0 ? 1 : 0;
    }
    result;
)"sv;

// 2000 points, 9 words, 4096 bytes of 1, the 24 characters of the date, and the error.
static constexpr double EXPECTED_RESULT = 2000 + 9 + 4096 + 24 + 1;

static void run_script_in_a_new_vm()
{
    auto vm = JS::VM::create();
    EXPECT_EQ(&JS::VM::the(), vm.ptr());
    EXPECT_EQ(&GC::Heap::the(), &vm->heap());
    vm->heap().set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);

    auto root_execution_context = JS::create_simple_execution_context<JS::GlobalObject>(*vm);
    auto source_text = Utf16String::from_utf8_without_validation(TEST_SCRIPT.bytes());
    auto script = JS::Script::parse(source_text.utf16_view(), *root_execution_context->realm());
    VERIFY(!script.is_error());
    auto result = vm->run(script.value());
    VERIFY(!result.is_error());
    EXPECT_EQ(result.value().as_double(), EXPECTED_RESULT);
}

template<typename Callback>
static void run_on_vm_threads(size_t thread_count, IGNORE_USE_IN_ESCAPING_LAMBDA Callback callback)
{
    Vector<NonnullRefPtr<Threading::Thread>> threads;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < thread_count; ++i) {
        auto thread = Threading::Thread::construct("VMThreadTest"sv, [&callback] {
            callback();
            return static_cast<intptr_t>(0);
        });
        thread->set_stack_size(JS::VM::MINIMUM_THREAD_STACK_SIZE);
        thread->start();
        threads.append(move(thread));
    }
    for (auto& thread : threads)
        MUST(thread->join());
}

TEST_CASE(vm_threads_get_the_stack_they_asked_for)
{
    run_on_vm_threads(1, [] {
        EXPECT(StackInfo {}.size() >= JS::VM::MINIMUM_THREAD_STACK_SIZE);
    });
}

TEST_CASE(a_vm_runs_on_a_thread_that_is_not_the_main_thread)
{
    run_on_vm_threads(1, [] { run_script_in_a_new_vm(); });
}

TEST_CASE(several_vms_run_at_once)
{
    run_on_vm_threads(8, [] { run_script_in_a_new_vm(); });
}

TEST_CASE(vms_come_and_go_while_others_run)
{
    run_on_vm_threads(4, [] {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < 5; ++i)
            run_script_in_a_new_vm();
    });
}

TEST_CASE(a_vm_on_the_main_thread_runs_beside_vms_on_other_threads)
{
    auto vm = JS::VM::create();
    run_on_vm_threads(4, [] { run_script_in_a_new_vm(); });
    EXPECT_EQ(&JS::VM::the(), vm.ptr());
}

TEST_CASE(heap_blocks_come_back_when_vms_go_away)
{
    auto run_round = [] {
        run_on_vm_threads(4, [] { run_script_in_a_new_vm(); });
    };

    run_round();
    auto committed_end = GC::BlockAllocator::heap_region_committed_end();
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 10; ++i)
        run_round();
    // NB: Timing can make the threads of a round overlap more than those of the first one, so allow for a few chunks.
    //     A round that leaked its blocks would take more than all of this.
    EXPECT(GC::BlockAllocator::heap_region_committed_end() <= committed_end + 16 * MiB);
}

namespace {

// What a block holds, in terms that mean the same in every heap: the descriptor of a Rust type goes with its heap.
struct BlockContents {
    void const* type { nullptr };
    size_t cell_size { 0 };

    bool operator==(BlockContents const&) const = default;
};

}

static HashMap<FlatPtr, BlockContents> contents_of_blocks(GC::Heap& heap)
{
    HashMap<FlatPtr, BlockContents> blocks;
    heap.for_each_block([&](GC::HeapBlock& block) {
        auto const* foreign_type = block.foreign_type();
        auto const* type = foreign_type ? foreign_type : &block.cell_allocator().descriptor();
        blocks.set(bit_cast<FlatPtr>(&block), { type, block.cell_size() });
        return IterationDecision::Continue;
    });
    return blocks;
}

static void run_script(JS::VM& vm, JS::Realm& realm, StringView source)
{
    auto source_text = Utf16String::from_utf8_without_validation(source.bytes());
    auto script = JS::Script::parse(source_text.utf16_view(), realm);
    VERIFY(!script.is_error());
    VERIFY(!vm.run(script.value()).is_error());
}

TEST_CASE(block_addresses_stay_with_their_type_across_vms)
{
    // Keeps what it allocates, as the blocks are looked at while the VM still has them.
    static constexpr auto FIRST_SCRIPT = R"(
        globalThis.kept = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < 40000; ++i)
            kept.push({ i }, [i], `string-${i}`, () => i, new Map(), Symbol("s"));
    )"sv;
    // Different types, in different amounts.
    static constexpr auto SECOND_SCRIPT = R"(
        globalThis.kept = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < 40000; ++i)
            kept.push(new Date(i), new Set([i]), new Uint8Array(4), /a/g, new Error("e"), `string-${i}`, { i, j: i, k: i, l: i });
    )"sv;

    HashMap<FlatPtr, BlockContents> first_blocks;
    run_on_vm_threads(1, [&] {
        auto vm = JS::VM::create();
        vm->heap().set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
        auto root_execution_context = JS::create_simple_execution_context<JS::GlobalObject>(*vm);
        run_script(*vm, *root_execution_context->realm(), FIRST_SCRIPT);
        first_blocks = contents_of_blocks(vm->heap());
    });

    run_on_vm_threads(1, [&] {
        auto vm = JS::VM::create();
        vm->heap().set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
        auto root_execution_context = JS::create_simple_execution_context<JS::GlobalObject>(*vm);
        run_script(*vm, *root_execution_context->realm(), SECOND_SCRIPT);

        size_t reused_blocks = 0;
        for (auto const& [address, contents] : contents_of_blocks(vm->heap())) {
            auto first_contents = first_blocks.get(address);
            if (!first_contents.has_value())
                continue;
            ++reused_blocks;
            EXPECT(first_contents.value() == contents);
        }
        // Realms, shapes and strings, at least.
        EXPECT(reused_blocks > 10);
    });
}

TEST_CASE(a_host_class_keeps_its_blocks_across_vms)
{
    static JSHostClass const host_class = JS::make_host_class(JS_HOST_CLASS_OBJECT, "TestHostObject"sv, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, 0);

    auto allocate_host_objects = [](JS::VM& vm) {
        auto root_execution_context = JS::create_simple_execution_context<JS::GlobalObject>(vm);
        GC::DeferGC defer_gc { vm.heap() };
        HashTable<FlatPtr> blocks;
        while (blocks.size() < 16) {
            auto object = JS::HostObject::create(*root_execution_context->realm(), host_class, nullptr);
            blocks.set(bit_cast<FlatPtr>(GC::HeapBlock::from_cell(GC::as_cell(object.ptr()))));
        }
        return blocks;
    };

    HashTable<FlatPtr> first_blocks;
    run_on_vm_threads(1, [&] {
        auto vm = JS::VM::create();
        first_blocks = allocate_host_objects(*vm);
    });
    run_on_vm_threads(1, [&] {
        auto vm = JS::VM::create();
        for (auto block : allocate_host_objects(*vm))
            EXPECT(first_blocks.contains(block));
    });
}

// Scripts that never end by themselves. Those that set `reached` show what an interrupt must not let run.
static constexpr StringView NEVER_ENDING_SCRIPTS[] = {
    "while (true) {}"sv,
    "let i = 0; for (;;) i++;"sv,
    "let i = 0; for (;;) i = (i + 1) | 0;"sv,
    "for (;;) { for (let i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) {} }"sv,
    "function spin() { let i = 0; while (true) i += 2; } spin();"sv,
    "const array = [1, 2, 3]; function sum() { let s = 0; for (let i = 0; i < array.length; ++i) s += array[i]; return s; } while (true) sum();"sv,

    // Generators and async functions.
    "function* forever() { for (;;) yield 1; } for (const value of forever()) {}"sv,
    "function* forever() { while (true) {} } forever().next();"sv,
    "async function forever() { while (true) {} } forever();"sv,

    // Nothing may catch it or run after it.
    "try { while (true) {} } catch (error) { globalThis.reached = true; }"sv,
    "try { while (true) {} } finally { globalThis.reached = true; while (true) {} }"sv,
    "function caught() { try { while (true) {} } finally { globalThis.reached = true; } } try { caught(); } catch (error) { globalThis.reached = true; }"sv,
    "while (true) { try { while (true) {} } catch (error) { globalThis.reached = true; } }"sv,
    "while (true) { try { null.property; } catch (error) {} }"sv,
    "const iterator = { [Symbol.iterator]() { return this; }, next() { return { value: 1, done: false }; }, return() { globalThis.reached = true; return {}; } }; for (const value of iterator) { while (true) {} }"sv,
    "function* withFinally() { try { yield 1; while (true) {} } finally { globalThis.reached = true; } } for (const value of withFinally()) {}"sv,

    // Native code that catches, and calls that run script.
    "while (true) { new Promise(() => { throw 1; }); }"sv,
    "[1].forEach(function again() { [1].forEach(() => {}); while (true) {} });"sv,
    "[3, 2, 1].sort(() => { while (true) {} });"sv,
    "new Promise(() => { while (true) {} }).catch(() => { globalThis.reached = true; });"sv,
    "({ get property() { while (true) {} } }).property;"sv,
    "class Thing { constructor() { while (true) {} } } new Thing();"sv,
    "eval('while (true) {}');"sv,
    "new Proxy({}, { get() { while (true) {} } }).property;"sv,
    "`${{ toString() { while (true) {} } }}`;"sv,

    // Recursion, also without any loop.
    "function deep() { deep(); } while (true) { try { deep(); } catch (error) {} }"sv,
    "function wide(n) { return n == 0 ? 0 : wide(n - 1) + wide(n - 1); } wide(100);"sv,

    // Native code that does not run script.
    "/(a|aa)+$/.test('a'.repeat(50000) + '!');"sv,
    "/(a|aa)+$/u.test('a'.repeat(50000) + '!');"sv,
    "Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(8)), 0, 0);"sv,
    "Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(8)), 0, 0, 1e9);"sv,
    "Atomics.wait(new BigInt64Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(8)), 0, 0n);"sv,
    "while (true) Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(8)), 0, 0, 1);"sv,
};

// These only run in promise jobs, after the script itself completed normally. Each job calls jobRan(), so that the
// test interrupts them only once they are in one.
static constexpr StringView NEVER_ENDING_PROMISE_JOBS[] = {
    "async function forever() { for (;;) { await 0; jobRan(); } } forever();"sv,
    "async function* forever() { for (;;) yield 1; } (async () => { for await (const value of forever()) jobRan(); })();"sv,
    "function again() { Promise.resolve().then(() => { jobRan(); again(); }); } again();"sv,
    "function again() { Promise.resolve().then(() => { throw 1; }).catch(() => { jobRan(); again(); }); } again();"sv,
};

// NB: The native function the script calls sets this, so it is shared with the function's captures.
struct JobRanFlag : AtomicRefCounted<JobRanFlag> {
    GC_HOLDS_NO_CELL_EDGES;

    Atomic<bool> value { false };
};

struct InterruptedScript {
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    StringView source;
    bool is_promise_job { false };
    Atomic<JS::VM*> vm { nullptr };
    NonnullRefPtr<JobRanFlag> job_ran { make_ref_counted<JobRanFlag>() };
    bool did_throw { false };
    bool reached { false };
    MonotonicTime interrupted_at { MonotonicTime::now() };
    MonotonicTime stopped_at { MonotonicTime::now() };
};

static void run_script_until_it_is_interrupted(InterruptedScript& interrupted)
{
    auto vm = JS::VM::create();
    vm->heap().set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);

    auto root_execution_context = JS::create_simple_execution_context<JS::GlobalObject>(*vm);
    auto& realm = *root_execution_context->realm();
    auto job_ran = JS::NativeFunction::create(realm, GC::create_function(vm->heap(), GC::captures(interrupted.job_ran), [](NonnullRefPtr<JobRanFlag>& job_ran, JS::VM&) -> JS::ThrowCompletionOr<JS::Value> {
        job_ran->value = true;
        return JS::js_undefined(); }), 0, JS::PropertyKey { "jobRan"_utf16_fly_string });
    realm.global_object().define_direct_property(JS::PropertyKey { "jobRan"_utf16_fly_string }, job_ran, JS::default_attributes);
    auto source_text = Utf16String::from_utf8_without_validation(interrupted.source.bytes());
    auto script = JS::Script::parse(source_text.utf16_view(), realm);
    VERIFY(!script.is_error());

    interrupted.vm = vm.ptr();
    auto result = vm->run(script.value());
    interrupted.did_throw = result.is_error();

    // NB: Nothing runs on this VM anymore, but the property holds a plain value.
    auto reached = MUST(realm.global_object().get(JS::PropertyKey { "reached"_utf16_fly_string }));
    interrupted.reached = !reached.is_undefined();

    interrupted.stopped_at = MonotonicTime::now();
    if (!vm->interrupt_requested())
        warnln("This ended by itself: {}", interrupted.source);
    EXPECT(vm->interrupt_requested());

    // NB: The thread that interrupts this VM has to be done with it first.
    while (interrupted.vm)
        MUST(Core::System::sleep_ms(1));
}

// NB: The scripts run at the same time, and every JIT mode is another round, as VMs read LIBJS_JIT when they start.
static void interrupt_every_never_ending_script(StringView jit_options)
{
    MUST(Core::Environment::set("LIBJS_JIT"sv, jit_options, Core::Environment::Overwrite::Yes));

    Vector<NonnullOwnPtr<InterruptedScript>> scripts;
    Vector<NonnullRefPtr<Threading::Thread>> threads;
    auto start_script = [&](StringView source, bool is_promise_job) {
        auto script = make<InterruptedScript>();
        script->source = source;
        script->is_promise_job = is_promise_job;
        auto thread = Threading::Thread::construct("VMThreadTest"sv, [&interrupted = *script] {
            run_script_until_it_is_interrupted(interrupted);
            return static_cast<intptr_t>(0);
        });
        thread->set_stack_size(JS::VM::MINIMUM_THREAD_STACK_SIZE);
        thread->start();
        scripts.append(move(script));
        threads.append(move(thread));
    };
    for (auto source : NEVER_ENDING_SCRIPTS)
        start_script(source, false);
    for (auto source : NEVER_ENDING_PROMISE_JOBS)
        start_script(source, true);

    // NB: Nothing tells when a script got into compiled code, but the modes that compile without a warmup take a few
    //     iterations to do so. A slow machine may still be in the interpreter here, which this test covers as well.
    MUST(Core::System::sleep_ms(50));

    for (auto& script : scripts) {
        while (!script->vm || (script->is_promise_job && !script->job_ran->value))
            MUST(Core::System::sleep_ms(1));
        script->interrupted_at = MonotonicTime::now();
        script->vm.load()->request_interrupt();
        script->vm = nullptr;
    }
    for (auto& thread : threads)
        MUST(thread->join());
    MUST(Core::Environment::unset("LIBJS_JIT"sv));

    for (auto const& script : scripts) {
        if (script->did_throw == script->is_promise_job || script->reached)
            warnln("Interrupting this went wrong: {}", script->source);
        EXPECT_NE(script->did_throw, script->is_promise_job);
        EXPECT(!script->reached);
        // NB: This has to hold on a busy machine as well, and only a script that does not stop gets anywhere near it.
        EXPECT(script->stopped_at - script->interrupted_at < AK::Duration::from_seconds(5));
    }
}

TEST_CASE(interrupting_script_in_the_interpreter)
{
    interrupt_every_never_ending_script("off"sv);
}

TEST_CASE(interrupting_script_in_compiled_code)
{
    interrupt_every_never_ending_script("on,sync,threshold=1,warmup=0"sv);
}

TEST_CASE(interrupting_script_that_tiers_up_on_the_way)
{
    interrupt_every_never_ending_script("on,threshold=100,warmup=2"sv);
}

TEST_CASE(interrupting_script_that_has_no_feedback)
{
    interrupt_every_never_ending_script("on,sync,threshold=0,warmup=0"sv);
}

TEST_CASE(an_interrupted_vm_runs_nothing_anymore)
{
    run_on_vm_threads(1, [] {
        auto vm = JS::VM::create();
        auto root_execution_context = JS::create_simple_execution_context<JS::GlobalObject>(*vm);
        auto run = [&](StringView source) {
            auto source_text = Utf16String::from_utf8_without_validation(source.bytes());
            auto script = JS::Script::parse(source_text.utf16_view(), *root_execution_context->realm());
            VERIFY(!script.is_error());
            return vm->run(script.value());
        };

        EXPECT(!run("globalThis.count = 1;"sv).is_error());
        vm->request_interrupt();
        EXPECT(run("globalThis.count = 2;"sv).is_error());

        auto count = MUST(root_execution_context->realm()->global_object().get(JS::PropertyKey { "count"_utf16_fly_string }));
        EXPECT_EQ(count.as_i32(), 1);
    });
}

// The words of the memory that the scripts below share, each of which sees it as the Int32Array `words`. Only the word
// they wait on is touched by anything that could wake them.
static constexpr size_t WAIT_WORD = 0;
static constexpr size_t STARTED_COUNT_WORD = 1;
static constexpr size_t WOKEN_COUNT_WORD = 2;
static constexpr size_t RESULT_WORDS = 8;

// What a script that waits leaves in its result word. Word 0 stays what it is unless a test changes it.
static constexpr i32 RESULT_OK = 1;
static constexpr i32 RESULT_NOT_EQUAL = 2;
static constexpr i32 RESULT_TIMED_OUT = 3;

class SharedMemoryScripts {
public:
    SharedMemoryScripts()
    {
        // NB: The agent that created the memory keeps it for the test, as the others come and go.
        auto owner = Threading::Thread::construct("VMThreadTestOwner"sv, [this] {
            own_memory();
            return static_cast<intptr_t>(0);
        });
        owner->set_stack_size(JS::VM::MINIMUM_THREAD_STACK_SIZE);
        owner->start();
        m_threads.append(move(owner));
        while (!m_words.load())
            MUST(Core::System::sleep_ms(1));
    }

    ~SharedMemoryScripts()
    {
        m_may_destroy_vms = true;
        for (auto& thread : m_threads)
            MUST(thread->join());
    }

    // Runs a script on a VM and thread of its own, which shares the memory as a worker's agent would.
    void start(ByteString source, Optional<size_t> index = {})
    {
        auto thread = Threading::Thread::construct("VMThreadTest"sv, [this, source = move(source), index] {
            run(source, index);
            return static_cast<intptr_t>(0);
        });
        thread->set_stack_size(JS::VM::MINIMUM_THREAD_STACK_SIZE);
        thread->start();
        m_threads.append(move(thread));
    }

    // Starts a script that waits on WAIT_WORD, and returns once it is about to. Its result goes in RESULT_WORDS + index,
    // after it counted itself as woken: the result is the count, plus the outcome in the upper bits.
    void start_waiter(size_t index, StringView timeout = "Infinity"sv)
    {
        auto started = word(STARTED_COUNT_WORD).load();
        start(ByteString::formatted(R"(
            const outcomes = {{ ok: {}, "not-equal": {}, "timed-out": {} }};
            Atomics.add(words, {}, 1);
            const outcome = outcomes[Atomics.wait(words, {}, 0, {})];
            const position = Atomics.add(words, {}, 1) + 1;
            Atomics.store(words, {}, outcome * 256 + position);
        )",
                  RESULT_OK, RESULT_NOT_EQUAL, RESULT_TIMED_OUT, STARTED_COUNT_WORD, WAIT_WORD, timeout, WOKEN_COUNT_WORD, RESULT_WORDS + index),
            index);
        while (word(STARTED_COUNT_WORD).load() == started)
            MUST(Core::System::sleep_ms(1));
        // NB: A wait with a short timeout may be over before this sees it.
        while (!has_result(index) && !m_vms[index].load()->is_waiting_on_shared_memory())
            MUST(Core::System::sleep_ms(1));
    }

    // What Atomics.notify() returned, in a VM of its own.
    i32 notify(i32 count)
    {
        static constexpr size_t NOTIFY_RESULT_WORD = RESULT_WORDS - 1;
        word(NOTIFY_RESULT_WORD).store(-1);
        start(ByteString::formatted("Atomics.store(words, {}, Atomics.notify(words, {}, {}));", NOTIFY_RESULT_WORD, WAIT_WORD, count));
        while (word(NOTIFY_RESULT_WORD).load() == -1)
            MUST(Core::System::sleep_ms(1));
        return word(NOTIFY_RESULT_WORD).load();
    }

    i32 wait_for_result(size_t index)
    {
        while (word(RESULT_WORDS + index).load() == 0)
            MUST(Core::System::sleep_ms(1));
        return word(RESULT_WORDS + index).load();
    }

    bool has_result(size_t index) { return word(RESULT_WORDS + index).load() != 0; }

    // Stops a script from start_waiter(), and returns whether its wait ended as an interrupt: the script threw, and ran
    // nothing past the wait.
    bool interrupt_and_check_that_it_ended(size_t index)
    {
        m_vms[index].load()->request_interrupt();
        while (!m_is_finished[index])
            MUST(Core::System::sleep_ms(1));
        return m_did_throw[index] && !has_result(index);
    }

    AK::Atomic<i32>& word(size_t index) { return m_words.load()[index]; }

private:
    void own_memory()
    {
        auto vm = JS::VM::create();
        vm->heap().set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
        auto root_execution_context = JS::create_simple_execution_context<JS::GlobalObject>(*vm);
        auto& realm = *root_execution_context->realm();

        auto source_text = "new SharedArrayBuffer(4096)"_utf16;
        auto script = JS::Script::parse(source_text.utf16_view(), realm);
        VERIFY(!script.is_error());
        auto& buffer = as<JS::ArrayBuffer>(vm->run(script.value()).value().as_object());
        EXPECT_NE(buffer.shared_store_id(), 0u);
        m_shared_store_id = buffer.shared_store_id();
        m_words = reinterpret_cast<AK::Atomic<i32>*>(const_cast<u8*>(buffer.data_at(0)));

        while (!m_may_destroy_vms)
            MUST(Core::System::sleep_ms(1));
    }

    void run(ByteString const& source, Optional<size_t> index)
    {
        auto vm = JS::VM::create();
        vm->heap().set_incremental_sweep_enabled(false);
        auto root_execution_context = JS::create_simple_execution_context<JS::GlobalObject>(*vm);
        auto& realm = *root_execution_context->realm();

        auto buffer = JS::ArrayBuffer::create_from_shared_store(realm, m_shared_store_id.load());
        VERIFY(buffer);
        MUST(realm.global_object().set(JS::PropertyKey { "memory"_utf16_fly_string }, buffer, JS::Object::ShouldThrowExceptions::Yes));

        auto text = ByteString::formatted("const words = new Int32Array(memory); {}", source);
        auto source_text = Utf16String::from_utf8_without_validation(text.bytes());
        auto script = JS::Script::parse(source_text.utf16_view(), realm);
        VERIFY(!script.is_error());
        if (index.has_value())
            m_vms[*index] = vm.ptr();
        auto result = vm->run(script.value());
        if (!index.has_value())
            return;
        m_did_throw[*index] = result.is_error();
        m_is_finished[*index] = true;

        // NB: The thread that interrupts this VM has to be done with it first.
        while (!m_may_destroy_vms)
            MUST(Core::System::sleep_ms(1));
    }

    static constexpr size_t MAX_WAITER_COUNT = 8;

    AK::Atomic<u64> m_shared_store_id { 0 };
    AK::Atomic<AK::Atomic<i32>*> m_words { nullptr };
    Vector<NonnullRefPtr<Threading::Thread>> m_threads;
    Array<AK::Atomic<JS::VM*>, MAX_WAITER_COUNT> m_vms;
    Array<AK::Atomic<bool>, MAX_WAITER_COUNT> m_did_throw;
    Array<AK::Atomic<bool>, MAX_WAITER_COUNT> m_is_finished;
    AK::Atomic<bool> m_may_destroy_vms { false };
};

TEST_CASE(a_notify_wakes_a_waiter_of_a_word_that_did_not_change)
{
    SharedMemoryScripts scripts;
    scripts.start_waiter(0);
    EXPECT_EQ(scripts.notify(1), 1);
    EXPECT_EQ(scripts.wait_for_result(0), RESULT_OK * 256 + 1);
    EXPECT_EQ(scripts.word(WAIT_WORD).load(), 0);
}

TEST_CASE(a_word_that_changes_without_a_notify_ends_no_wait)
{
    SharedMemoryScripts scripts;
    scripts.start_waiter(0, "30"sv);
    scripts.word(WAIT_WORD).store(1);
    EXPECT_EQ(scripts.wait_for_result(0), RESULT_TIMED_OUT * 256 + 1);
}

TEST_CASE(notifies_wake_in_order_and_count_every_waiter)
{
    static constexpr size_t WAITER_COUNT = 5;
    SharedMemoryScripts scripts;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < WAITER_COUNT; ++i)
        scripts.start_waiter(i);

    EXPECT_EQ(scripts.notify(0), 0);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {
        EXPECT_EQ(scripts.notify(1), 1);
        EXPECT_EQ(scripts.wait_for_result(i), RESULT_OK * 256 + static_cast<i32>(i) + 1);
    }
    EXPECT(!scripts.has_result(2));

    EXPECT_EQ(scripts.notify(100), static_cast<i32>(WAITER_COUNT) - 2);
    for (size_t i = 2; i < WAITER_COUNT; ++i)
        EXPECT_EQ(scripts.wait_for_result(i) / 256, RESULT_OK);
    EXPECT_EQ(scripts.notify(100), 0);
}

TEST_CASE(an_interrupt_ends_a_wait_as_terminated_and_leaves_other_waiters_alone)
{
    SharedMemoryScripts scripts;
    scripts.start_waiter(0);
    scripts.start_waiter(1, "600000"sv);
    scripts.start_waiter(2);
    scripts.start_waiter(3, "600000"sv);

    EXPECT(scripts.interrupt_and_check_that_it_ended(0));
    EXPECT(scripts.interrupt_and_check_that_it_ended(1));
    EXPECT(!scripts.has_result(2));
    EXPECT(!scripts.has_result(3));

    // NB: The waiters that are left kept their places.
    EXPECT_EQ(scripts.notify(1), 1);
    EXPECT_EQ(scripts.wait_for_result(2), RESULT_OK * 256 + 1);
    EXPECT_EQ(scripts.notify(100), 1);
    EXPECT_EQ(scripts.wait_for_result(3), RESULT_OK * 256 + 2);
}

TEST_CASE(logging_an_exception_only_reads_its_message_with_a_running_context)
{
    static size_t message_reads;
    struct Traits {
        static JS::ThrowCompletionOr<JS::Value> get(JS::HostObject const&, JS::PropertyKey const&, JS::Value, JS::CacheableGetPropertyMetadata*, JS::Object::PropertyLookupPhase)
        {
            ++message_reads;
            return JS::js_undefined();
        }
    };
    static constexpr auto hooks = JS::make_host_object_hooks<Traits>();
    static constexpr auto host_class = JS::make_host_class(JS_HOST_CLASS_OBJECT, "TestException"sv, nullptr, &hooks, nullptr, 0);

    run_on_vm_threads(1, [] {
        auto vm = JS::VM::create();
        auto context = JS::create_simple_execution_context<JS::GlobalObject>(*vm);
        auto exception = JS::HostObject::create(*context->realm(), host_class, nullptr);
        message_reads = 0;
        JS::set_log_all_js_exceptions(true);
        (void)JS::throw_completion(exception);
        EXPECT_EQ(message_reads, 1u);
        vm->pop_execution_context();
        (void)JS::throw_completion(exception);
        JS::set_log_all_js_exceptions(false);
        EXPECT_EQ(message_reads, 1u);
        vm->push_execution_context(*context);
    });
}

TEST_CASE(dictionary_elements_distinguish_holes_from_undefined)
{
    run_on_vm_threads(1, [] {
        auto vm = JS::VM::create();
        auto context = JS::create_simple_execution_context<JS::GlobalObject>(*vm);
        auto object = JS::Object::create(*context->realm(), nullptr);
        object->define_direct_property(0u, JS::js_undefined(), 0);
        object->indexed_append(JS::js_special_empty_value());
        object->indexed_append(JS::js_undefined());
        EXPECT_EQ(object->indexed_array_like_size(), 3u);
        EXPECT(object->has_own_property(0u).release_value());
        EXPECT(!object->has_own_property(1u).release_value());
        EXPECT(object->has_own_property(2u).release_value());
    });
}

TEST_CASE(taking_the_first_dictionary_element_shifts_the_remaining_indices)
{
    run_on_vm_threads(1, [] {
        auto vm = JS::VM::create();
        auto context = JS::create_simple_execution_context<JS::GlobalObject>(*vm);
        auto object = JS::Object::create(*context->realm(), nullptr);
        object->define_direct_property(0u, JS::js_undefined(), 0);
        object->define_direct_property(2u, JS::js_undefined(), 0);

        object->indexed_take_first();
        EXPECT_EQ(object->indexed_array_like_size(), 2u);
        EXPECT(!object->has_own_property(0u).release_value());
        EXPECT(object->has_own_property(1u).release_value());
        EXPECT(!object->has_own_property(2u).release_value());

        object->indexed_take_first();
        EXPECT_EQ(object->indexed_array_like_size(), 1u);
        EXPECT(object->has_own_property(0u).release_value());
    });
}

/*

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

#pragma once

#include <AK/AtomicRefCounted.h>
#include <AK/ConditionVariable.h>
#include <AK/Mutex.h>
#include <AK/NeverDestroyed.h>
#include <AK/RefPtr.h>
#include <LibMedia/DecoderRegistrations.h>
#include <LibMediaCodecs/AudioDecoder.h>
#include <LibMediaCodecs/AudioDecoderRegistry.h>

// Tells a StateLosingAudioDecoder when to lose its state, and holds the decoding that follows until the test resumes it.
class AudioDecoderStateLoss final : public AtomicRefCounted<AudioDecoderStateLoss> {
public:
    explicit AudioDecoderStateLoss(size_t block_index_that_loses_state)
        : m_block_index_that_loses_state(block_index_that_loses_state)
    {
    }

    bool wait_until_decoding_is_held_after_the_loss(AK::Duration timeout)
    {
        auto deadline = MonotonicTime::now() + timeout;
        MutexLocker locker { m_mutex };
        while (!m_decoding_is_held) {
            auto now = MonotonicTime::now();
            if (now >= deadline)
                return false;
            m_state_changed.wait_for(deadline - now);
        }
        return true;
    }

    void resume_decoding()
    {
        MutexLocker locker { m_mutex };
        m_holds_decoding = false;
        m_state_changed.broadcast();
    }

private:
    friend class StateLosingAudioDecoder;

    Mutex m_mutex;
    ConditionVariable m_state_changed { m_mutex };
    size_t const m_block_index_that_loses_state;
    size_t m_written_block_count { 0 };
    bool m_state_was_lost { false };
    bool m_holds_decoding { true };
    bool m_decoding_is_held { false };
};

// Decodes with the first installed decoder that accepts the codec, but reports that it lost its state once, instead of
// writing the block at the chosen index.
class StateLosingAudioDecoder final : public Media::AudioDecoder {
public:
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    // Decoders created while this is set lose their state there; the installed registration is skipped otherwise.
    static void set_state_loss_for_new_decoders(RefPtr<AudioDecoderStateLoss> state_loss)
    {
        MutexLocker locker { *s_state_loss_mutex };
        *s_state_loss_for_new_decoders = move(state_loss);
    }

    static ReadonlySpan<Media::AudioDecoderRegistration> registrations()
    {
        static constexpr Array registrations {
            Media::AudioDecoderRegistration { capabilities, create },
        };
        return registrations.span();
    }

    virtual Media::DecoderErrorOr<void> receive_coded_data(Media::CodedFrame const& coded_frame) override
    {
        {
            MutexLocker locker { m_state_loss->m_mutex };
            while (m_state_loss->m_state_was_lost && m_state_loss->m_holds_decoding) {
                m_state_loss->m_decoding_is_held = true;
                m_state_loss->m_state_changed.broadcast();
                m_state_loss->m_state_changed.wait();
            }
        }
        return m_inner->receive_coded_data(coded_frame);
    }

    virtual void signal_end_of_stream() override { m_inner->signal_end_of_stream(); }

    virtual Media::DecoderErrorOr<void> write_next_block(Media::AudioBlock& block) override
    {
        {
            MutexLocker locker { m_state_loss->m_mutex };
            if (!m_state_loss->m_state_was_lost && m_state_loss->m_written_block_count == m_state_loss->m_block_index_that_loses_state) {
                m_state_loss->m_state_was_lost = true;
                return Media::DecoderError::with_description(Media::DecoderErrorCategory::NeedsResubmission, "The decoder lost its state"sv);
            }
        }
        TRY(m_inner->write_next_block(block));
        MutexLocker locker { m_state_loss->m_mutex };
        m_state_loss->m_written_block_count++;
        return {};
    }

    virtual void flush() override { m_inner->flush(); }

private:
    static Optional<Media::DecoderCapabilities> capabilities(Media::ParsedCodec const& codec)
    {
        {
            MutexLocker locker { *s_state_loss_mutex };
            if (*s_state_loss_for_new_decoders == nullptr)
                return {};
        }
        for (auto const& registration : Media::audio_decoders()) {
            if (auto capabilities = registration.capabilities(codec); capabilities.has_value())
                return capabilities;
        }
        return {};
    }

    static Media::DecoderErrorOr<NonnullOwnPtr<Media::AudioDecoder>> create(Media::CodecID codec_id, Audio::SampleSpecification const& sample_specification, ReadonlyBytes codec_initialization_data)
    {
        RefPtr<AudioDecoderStateLoss> state_loss;
        {
            MutexLocker locker { *s_state_loss_mutex };
            state_loss = *s_state_loss_for_new_decoders;
        }
        if (state_loss == nullptr)
            return Media::DecoderError::with_description(Media::DecoderErrorCategory::NotImplemented, "No test is losing decoder state"sv);
        for (auto const& registration : Media::audio_decoders()) {
            auto inner = registration.create(codec_id, sample_specification, codec_initialization_data);
            if (!inner.is_error())
                return NonnullOwnPtr<Media::AudioDecoder> { adopt_own(*new StateLosingAudioDecoder(state_loss.release_nonnull(), inner.release_value())) };
        }
        return Media::DecoderError::with_description(Media::DecoderErrorCategory::NotImplemented, "No installed decoder accepts the codec"sv);
    }

    StateLosingAudioDecoder(NonnullRefPtr<AudioDecoderStateLoss> state_loss, NonnullOwnPtr<Media::AudioDecoder> inner)
        : m_state_loss(move(state_loss))
        , m_inner(move(inner))
    {
    }

    static inline NeverDestroyed<Mutex> s_state_loss_mutex;
    static inline NeverDestroyed<RefPtr<AudioDecoderStateLoss>> s_state_loss_for_new_decoders;

    NonnullRefPtr<AudioDecoderStateLoss> m_state_loss;
    NonnullOwnPtr<Media::AudioDecoder> m_inner;
};

/*

#include <AK/Array.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibCore/File.h>
#include <LibMedia/Containers/ADTS/ADTSDemuxer.h>
#include <LibMedia/DemuxerRegistry.h>
#include <LibMedia/IncrementallyPopulatedStream.h>
#include <LibMediaCodecs/CodedFrame.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>
#include <LibThreading/Thread.h>

#include "TransientlyAbortingStream.h"

static constexpr size_t FRAME_BYTE_SIZE = 256;

// 44100 Hz stereo AAC-LC frames carrying no CRC and one block each.
static void append_frames(Vector<u8>& bytes, size_t count)
{
    for (size_t index = 0; index < count; index++) {
        bytes.append(0xFF);
        bytes.append(0xF1);
        bytes.append(0x50);
        bytes.append(static_cast<u8>(0x80 | ((FRAME_BYTE_SIZE >> 11) & 3)));
        bytes.append(static_cast<u8>((FRAME_BYTE_SIZE >> 3) & 0xFF));
        bytes.append(static_cast<u8>(((FRAME_BYTE_SIZE & 7) << 5) | 0x1F));
        bytes.append(0xFC);
        for (size_t padding = Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::SIZE; padding < FRAME_BYTE_SIZE; padding++)
            bytes.append(0);
    }
}

static NonnullRefPtr<Media::Demuxer> create_demuxer(StringView path)
{
    auto file = MUST(Core::File::open(path, Core::File::OpenMode::Read));
    auto stream = Media::IncrementallyPopulatedStream::create_from_buffer(MUST(file->read_until_eof()));
    return MUST(Media::ADTS::ADTSDemuxer::from_stream(stream));
}

static void expect_durations_within(AK::Duration left, AK::Duration right, AK::Duration tolerance)
{
    EXPECT(left - right < tolerance);
    EXPECT(right - left < tolerance);
}

static Media::Track audio_track(Media::Demuxer& demuxer)
{
    auto track = MUST(demuxer.get_preferred_track_for_type(Media::TrackType::Audio));
    VERIFY(track.has_value());
    MUST(demuxer.create_context_for_track(*track));
    return *track;
}

static NonnullRefPtr<Media::Demuxer> create_demuxer_for(ReadonlyBytes bytes)
{
    auto stream = Media::IncrementallyPopulatedStream::create_from_buffer(MUST(ByteBuffer::copy(bytes)));
    return MUST(Media::ADTS::ADTSDemuxer::from_stream(stream));
}

static Vector<AK::Duration> timestamps_of_every_frame(Media::Demuxer& demuxer, Media::Track const& track)
{
    Vector<AK::Duration> timestamps;
    while (true) {
        auto frame = demuxer.get_next_sample_for_track(track);
        if (frame.is_error()) {
            EXPECT_EQ(frame.error().category(), Media::DecoderErrorCategory::EndOfStream);
            break;
        }
        timestamps.append(frame.value().presentation_timestamp());
    }
    return timestamps;
}

static void expect_a_transient_abort_to_resume_with_its_frame(ReadonlyBytes bytes, size_t aborted_read_position)
{
    Vector<AK::Duration> expected_timestamps;
    {
        auto demuxer = create_demuxer_for(bytes);
        auto track = audio_track(*demuxer);
        expected_timestamps = timestamps_of_every_frame(*demuxer, track);
    }

    auto stream = TransientlyAbortingStream::create(MUST(ByteBuffer::copy(bytes)), aborted_read_position);
    auto demuxer = MUST(Media::ADTS::ADTSDemuxer::from_stream(stream));
    auto track = audio_track(*demuxer);

    Vector<AK::Duration> actual_timestamps;
    size_t aborted_read_count = 0;
    while (true) {
        auto frame = demuxer->get_next_sample_for_track(track);
        if (frame.is_error()) {
            if (frame.error().category() != Media::DecoderErrorCategory::Aborted) {
                EXPECT_EQ(frame.error().category(), Media::DecoderErrorCategory::EndOfStream);
                break;
            }
            aborted_read_count++;
            continue;
        }
        actual_timestamps.append(frame.value().presentation_timestamp());
    }
    EXPECT(stream->has_aborted_a_read());
    EXPECT_EQ(aborted_read_count, 1u);
    EXPECT_EQ(actual_timestamps, expected_timestamps);
}

static void expect_an_aborted_read_to_resume_with_its_frame(ReadonlyBytes bytes, size_t initial_byte_count)
{
    Vector<AK::Duration> expected_timestamps;
    {
        auto demuxer = create_demuxer_for(bytes);
        auto track = audio_track(*demuxer);
        expected_timestamps = timestamps_of_every_frame(*demuxer, track);
    }

    auto stream = Media::IncrementallyPopulatedStream::create_empty();
    stream->set_expected_size(bytes.size());
    stream->add_chunk_at(0, bytes.trim(initial_byte_count));

    IGNORE_USE_IN_ESCAPING_LAMBDA auto demuxer = MUST(Media::ADTS::ADTSDemuxer::from_stream(stream));
    IGNORE_USE_IN_ESCAPING_LAMBDA auto track = audio_track(*demuxer);

    IGNORE_USE_IN_ESCAPING_LAMBDA Atomic<bool> read_blocked { false };
    IGNORE_USE_IN_ESCAPING_LAMBDA Atomic<bool> read_was_aborted { false };
    demuxer->set_read_blocked_change_handler_for_track(track, [&](Media::ReadBlocked blocked) {
        read_blocked = blocked == Media::ReadBlocked::Yes;
    });

    IGNORE_USE_IN_ESCAPING_LAMBDA Vector<AK::Duration> actual_timestamps;
    auto reader_thread = Threading::Thread::construct("TestReader"sv, [&]() -> intptr_t {
        while (true) {
            auto frame = demuxer->get_next_sample_for_track(track);
            if (frame.is_error()) {
                EXPECT_EQ(frame.error().category(), Media::DecoderErrorCategory::Aborted);
                break;
            }
            actual_timestamps.append(frame.value().presentation_timestamp());
        }
        demuxer->reset_blocking_reads_aborted_for_track(track);
        read_was_aborted = true;
        actual_timestamps.extend(timestamps_of_every_frame(*demuxer, track));
        return 0;
    });
    reader_thread->start();

    while (!read_blocked.load()) { }
    demuxer->set_blocking_reads_aborted_for_track(track);
    while (!read_was_aborted.load()) { }

    stream->add_chunk_at(initial_byte_count, bytes.slice(initial_byte_count));
    stream->close();
    MUST(reader_thread->join());

    EXPECT_EQ(actual_timestamps, expected_timestamps);
}

enum class SeekInterruption : u8 {
    AbortedReads,
    PermanentlyUnavailableData,
};

static void expect_an_interrupted_seek_to_keep_the_position(ReadonlyBytes bytes, size_t available_byte_count, SeekInterruption interruption)
{
    Vector<AK::Duration> expected_timestamps;
    {
        auto demuxer = create_demuxer_for(bytes);
        auto track = audio_track(*demuxer);
        expected_timestamps = timestamps_of_every_frame(*demuxer, track);
    }

    auto stream = Media::IncrementallyPopulatedStream::create_empty();
    stream->set_expected_size(bytes.size());
    stream->add_chunk_at(0, bytes.trim(available_byte_count));
    auto demuxer = MUST(Media::ADTS::ADTSDemuxer::from_stream(stream));
    auto track = audio_track(*demuxer);

    constexpr size_t frames_read_before_seeking = 3;
    for (size_t index = 0; index < frames_read_before_seeking; index++)
        EXPECT_EQ(MUST(demuxer->get_next_sample_for_track(track)).presentation_timestamp(), expected_timestamps[index]);

    auto expected_category = Media::DecoderErrorCategory::Aborted;
    if (interruption == SeekInterruption::AbortedReads) {
        demuxer->set_blocking_reads_aborted_for_track(track);
    } else {
        stream->make_missing_data_permanently_unavailable();
        expected_category = Media::DecoderErrorCategory::PermanentlyUnavailable;
    }

    // The target lies in data the stream does not have, so the seek has to read it.
    auto seek_result = demuxer->seek_to_most_recent_keyframe(track, expected_timestamps.last(), Media::DemuxerSeekOptions::None);
    EXPECT(seek_result.is_error());
    if (seek_result.is_error())
        EXPECT_EQ(seek_result.error().category(), expected_category);

    if (interruption == SeekInterruption::AbortedReads)
        demuxer->reset_blocking_reads_aborted_for_track(track);
    // A demuxer that moved into the missing data fails this read instead of waiting on it forever.
    stream->make_missing_data_permanently_unavailable();
    EXPECT_EQ(MUST(demuxer->get_next_sample_for_track(track)).presentation_timestamp(), expected_timestamps[frames_read_before_seeking]);
}

TEST_CASE(demuxer_reads_a_stream_of_nothing_but_frames)
{
    // Nine ADTS AAC-LC frames containing 48 kHz stereo silence, as an encoder wrote them. The first
    // frame carries the fill element naming the encoder, so the audio is not all that a frame holds.
    // clang-format off
    static constexpr auto raw_aac_data = to_array<u8>({
        0xff, 0xf1, 0x4c, 0x80, 0x03, 0xdf, 0xfc, 0xde, 0x02, 0x00, 0x4c, 0x61,
        0x76, 0x63, 0x36, 0x31, 0x2e, 0x31, 0x39, 0x2e, 0x31, 0x30, 0x31, 0x00,
        0x42, 0x20, 0x08, 0xc1, 0x18, 0x38, 0xff, 0xf1, 0x4c, 0x80, 0x01, 0xbf,
        0xfc, 0x21, 0x10, 0x04, 0x60, 0x8c, 0x1c, 0xff, 0xf1, 0x4c, 0x80, 0x01,
        0xbf, 0xfc, 0x21, 0x10, 0x04, 0x60, 0x8c, 0x1c, 0xff, 0xf1, 0x4c, 0x80,
        0x01, 0xbf, 0xfc, 0x21, 0x10, 0x04, 0x60, 0x8c, 0x1c, 0xff, 0xf1, 0x4c,
        0x80, 0x01, 0xbf, 0xfc, 0x21, 0x10, 0x04, 0x60, 0x8c, 0x1c, 0xff, 0xf1,
        0x4c, 0x80, 0x01, 0xbf, 0xfc, 0x21, 0x10, 0x04, 0x60, 0x8c, 0x1c, 0xff,
        0xf1, 0x4c, 0x80, 0x01, 0xbf, 0xfc, 0x21, 0x10, 0x04, 0x60, 0x8c, 0x1c,
        0xff, 0xf1, 0x4c, 0x80, 0x01, 0xbf, 0xfc, 0x21, 0x10, 0x04, 0x60, 0x8c,
        0x1c, 0xff, 0xf1, 0x4c, 0x80, 0x01, 0xbf, 0xfc, 0x21, 0x10, 0x04, 0x60,
        0x8c, 0x1c,
    });
    // clang-format on

    auto stream = Media::IncrementallyPopulatedStream::create_from_data(raw_aac_data);
    auto demuxer = MUST(Media::ADTS::ADTSDemuxer::from_stream(stream));

    auto tracks = MUST(demuxer->get_tracks_for_type(Media::TrackType::Audio));
    EXPECT_EQ(tracks.size(), 1u);
    EXPECT_EQ(tracks[0].audio_data().sample_specification.sample_rate(), 48000u);
    EXPECT_EQ(tracks[0].audio_data().sample_specification.channel_count(), 2);

    auto track = audio_track(*demuxer);
    size_t frame_count = 0;
    while (!demuxer->get_next_sample_for_track(track).is_error())
        frame_count++;
    EXPECT_EQ(frame_count, 9u);

    // Every frame of the stream was walked, so its length is known rather than extrapolated.
    EXPECT_EQ(MUST(demuxer->total_duration()), AK::Duration::from_time_units(9 * 1024, 1, 48000));
}

TEST_CASE(demuxer_describes_the_only_track_of_the_stream)
{
    auto demuxer = create_demuxer("bbb.adts"sv);

    EXPECT(MUST(demuxer->get_tracks_for_type(Media::TrackType::Video)).is_empty());

    auto tracks = MUST(demuxer->get_tracks_for_type(Media::TrackType::Audio));
    EXPECT_EQ(tracks.size(), 1u);
    EXPECT_EQ(tracks[0].audio_data().sample_specification.sample_rate(), 44100u);
    EXPECT_EQ(tracks[0].audio_data().sample_specification.channel_count(), 2);
    EXPECT_EQ(tracks[0].parsed_codec().codec_id(), Media::CodecID::AAC);
}

TEST_CASE(demuxer_reads_every_frame_of_the_stream)
{
    auto demuxer = create_demuxer("bbb.adts"sv);
    auto track = audio_track(*demuxer);

    size_t frame_count = 0;
    auto expected_timestamp = AK::Duration::zero();
    while (true) {
        auto frame = demuxer->get_next_sample_for_track(track);
        if (frame.is_error()) {
            EXPECT_EQ(frame.error().category(), Media::DecoderErrorCategory::EndOfStream);
            break;
        }
        EXPECT_EQ(frame.value().presentation_timestamp(), expected_timestamp);
        EXPECT(frame.value().is_keyframe());
        expected_timestamp += frame.value().duration();
        frame_count++;
    }

    EXPECT_EQ(frame_count, 219u);

    // Each frame is rounded to the clock a timestamp is kept on, so the timestamps of a stream add
    // up to its length rather than landing on it exactly.
    expect_durations_within(expected_timestamp, AK::Duration::from_time_units(219 * 1024, 1, 44100), AK::Duration::from_microseconds(1));
}

TEST_CASE(demuxer_hands_the_decoder_the_configuration_that_the_headers_imply)
{
    auto demuxer = create_demuxer("bbb.adts"sv);
    auto track = audio_track(*demuxer);

    auto frame = MUST(demuxer->get_next_sample_for_track(track));
    auto configuration = frame.new_codec_configuration();
    EXPECT(configuration.has_value());

    // An Audio Specific Config of object type 2, sampling frequency index 4 and channel
    // configuration 2, which is what a 44100 Hz stereo AAC-LC stream would carry in a container
    // that describes its codec.
    EXPECT_EQ(configuration->size(), 2u);
    EXPECT_EQ((*configuration)[0], 0x12);
    EXPECT_EQ((*configuration)[1], 0x10);

    // Only the frame that begins a decode sequence carries it.
    auto second = MUST(demuxer->get_next_sample_for_track(track));
    EXPECT(!second.new_codec_configuration().has_value());
}

TEST_CASE(demuxer_carries_the_audio_without_the_framing_around_it)
{
    Vector<u8> bytes;
    append_frames(bytes, 4);

    auto stream = Media::IncrementallyPopulatedStream::create_from_buffer(MUST(ByteBuffer::copy(bytes.span())));
    auto demuxer = MUST(Media::ADTS::ADTSDemuxer::from_stream(stream));
    auto track = audio_track(*demuxer);

    auto frame = MUST(demuxer->get_next_sample_for_track(track));
    EXPECT_EQ(frame.data().size(), FRAME_BYTE_SIZE - Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::SIZE);
}

TEST_CASE(demuxer_seeks_to_the_frame_holding_a_timestamp)
{
    auto demuxer = create_demuxer("bbb.adts"sv);
    auto track = audio_track(*demuxer);

    auto target = AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(2'500);
    EXPECT_EQ(MUST(demuxer->seek_to_most_recent_keyframe(track, target)), Media::DemuxerSeekResult::MovedPosition);

    auto frame = MUST(demuxer->get_next_sample_for_track(track));
    EXPECT(frame.presentation_timestamp() <= target);
    EXPECT(frame.presentation_timestamp() + frame.duration() > target);

    // Seeking back to the start returns the first frame of the stream.
    EXPECT_EQ(MUST(demuxer->seek_to_most_recent_keyframe(track, AK::Duration::zero())), Media::DemuxerSeekResult::MovedPosition);
    EXPECT_EQ(MUST(demuxer->get_next_sample_for_track(track)).presentation_timestamp(), AK::Duration::zero());
}

TEST_CASE(demuxer_reads_the_frames_that_resume_after_damage)

TEST_CASE(demuxer_declines_a_stream_of_mpeg_audio_frames)
{
    // MPEG audio frames carry a layer, which ADTS requires to be absent, so the two formats do not
    // answer for one another however alike their sync codes look.
    Vector<u8> bytes;
    for (size_t index = 0; index < 8; index++) {
        bytes.append(0xFF);
        bytes.append(0xFB);
        bytes.append(0x94);
        bytes.append(0x00);
        for (size_t padding = 4; padding < 384; padding++)
            bytes.append(0);
    }

    auto stream = Media::IncrementallyPopulatedStream::create_from_buffer(MUST(ByteBuffer::copy(bytes.span())));
    EXPECT(Media::ADTS::ADTSDemuxer::from_stream(stream).is_error());
}

/*

#include <AK/Array.h>
#include <LibMedia/Containers/ADTS/FrameHeader.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>

TEST_CASE(frame_header_describes_an_mpeg_4_low_complexity_frame)
{
    // The first frame of a 48 kHz stereo AAC-LC stream muxed by FFmpeg.
    Array<u8, 7> bytes { 0xFF, 0xF1, 0x4C, 0x80, 0x31, 0x1F, 0xFC };

    auto header = Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::parse(bytes);
    EXPECT(header.has_value());
    EXPECT_EQ(header->version, Media::ADTS::MPEGVersion::Version4);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->audio_object_type, 2);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->sample_rate, 48000u);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->channel_count, 2);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->sample_count, 1024);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->frame_byte_size, 392);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->block_count, 1);
    EXPECT(!header->has_crc);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->payload_offset(), 7u);
}

TEST_CASE(frame_header_describes_an_mpeg_2_high_efficiency_frame)
{
    // High Efficiency AAC describes itself at the sample rate of its core, which is half of what it
    // decodes to, so a frame still covers 1024 samples of the rate the header names.
    Array<u8, 7> bytes { 0xFF, 0xF9, 0x58, 0xA0, 0x04, 0x20, 0x00 };

    auto header = Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::parse(bytes);
    EXPECT(header.has_value());
    EXPECT_EQ(header->version, Media::ADTS::MPEGVersion::Version2);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->audio_object_type, 2);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->sample_rate, 24000u);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->channel_count, 2);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->frame_byte_size, 33);
}

TEST_CASE(frame_header_reads_the_channel_configuration_across_its_two_bytes)
{
    // Parametric stereo describes a single core channel, and the field spans the byte boundary.
    Array<u8, 7> bytes { 0xFF, 0xF9, 0x58, 0x60, 0x02, 0xE0, 0x00 };

    auto header = Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::parse(bytes);
    EXPECT(header.has_value());
    EXPECT_EQ(header->channel_count, 1);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->frame_byte_size, 23);
}

TEST_CASE(frame_header_accounts_for_the_crc_that_the_protection_bit_announces)
{
    // Clearing the protection bit puts a CRC between the header and the audio.
    Array<u8, 7> bytes { 0xFF, 0xF0, 0x4C, 0x80, 0x31, 0x1F, 0xFC };

    auto header = Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::parse(bytes);
    EXPECT(header.has_value());
    EXPECT(header->has_crc);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->payload_offset(), 9u);

    // The length the header states covers the CRC, so the audio is shorter, not the frame longer.
    EXPECT_EQ(header->frame_byte_size, 392);
}

TEST_CASE(frame_header_counts_the_blocks_a_frame_carries)
{
    Array<u8, 7> bytes { 0xFF, 0xF1, 0x4C, 0x80, 0x31, 0x1F, 0xFF };

    auto header = Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::parse(bytes);
    EXPECT(header.has_value());
    EXPECT_EQ(header->block_count, 4);
    EXPECT_EQ(header->sample_count, 4096);
}

TEST_CASE(frame_header_declines_what_does_not_describe_a_frame)
{
    // No sync code.
    Array<u8, 7> not_a_frame { 0x00, 0x00, 0x4C, 0x80, 0x31, 0x1F, 0xFC };
    EXPECT(!Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::parse(not_a_frame).has_value());

    // A layer other than zero is not ADTS.
    Array<u8, 7> layered { 0xFF, 0xF3, 0x4C, 0x80, 0x31, 0x1F, 0xFC };
    EXPECT(!Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::parse(layered).has_value());

    // Sampling frequency index 13 is reserved.
    Array<u8, 7> reserved_rate { 0xFF, 0xF1, 0x74, 0x80, 0x31, 0x1F, 0xFC };
    EXPECT(!Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::parse(reserved_rate).has_value());

    // Channel configuration zero leaves the layout to a configuration ADTS does not carry.
    Array<u8, 7> no_channels { 0xFF, 0xF1, 0x4C, 0x00, 0x31, 0x1F, 0xFC };
    EXPECT(!Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::parse(no_channels).has_value());

    // A frame that claims to be shorter than its own header describes nothing.
    Array<u8, 7> too_short { 0xFF, 0xF1, 0x4C, 0x80, 0x00, 0x3F, 0xFC };
    EXPECT(!Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::parse(too_short).has_value());

    // A header cut short reads past its end.
    Array<u8, 4> truncated { 0xFF, 0xF1, 0x4C, 0x80 };
    EXPECT(!Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::parse(truncated).has_value());
}

/*

#include <AK/Array.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibCore/File.h>
#include <LibMedia/Containers/ADTS/Reader.h>
#include <LibMedia/ReadonlyBytesCursor.h>
#include <LibTest/TestCase.h>

static constexpr size_t FRAME_BYTE_SIZE = 256;

// 44100 Hz stereo AAC-LC frames carrying no CRC and one block each.
static void append_frames(Vector<u8>& bytes, size_t count, size_t frame_byte_size = FRAME_BYTE_SIZE)
{
    for (size_t index = 0; index < count; index++) {
        bytes.append(0xFF);
        bytes.append(0xF1);
        bytes.append(0x50);
        bytes.append(static_cast<u8>(0x80 | ((frame_byte_size >> 11) & 3)));
        bytes.append(static_cast<u8>((frame_byte_size >> 3) & 0xFF));
        bytes.append(static_cast<u8>(((frame_byte_size & 7) << 5) | 0x1F));
        bytes.append(0xFC);
        for (size_t padding = Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::SIZE; padding < frame_byte_size; padding++)
            bytes.append(0);
    }
}

static NonnullRefPtr<Media::ReadonlyBytesCursor> create_cursor(ReadonlyBytes bytes)
{
    return make_ref_counted<Media::ReadonlyBytesCursor>(bytes);
}

static Optional<Media::ADTS::Reader> read(Vector<u8> const& bytes)
{
    return MUST(Media::ADTS::Reader::from_stream(create_cursor(bytes)));
}

static ByteBuffer read_fixture(StringView path)
{
    auto file = MUST(Core::File::open(path, Core::File::OpenMode::Read));
    return MUST(file->read_until_eof());
}

TEST_CASE(reader_describes_the_stream_its_first_frame_announces)
{
    Vector<u8> bytes;
    append_frames(bytes, 8);

    auto reader = read(bytes);
    EXPECT(reader.has_value());
    EXPECT_EQ(reader->first_frame_position(), 0u);
    EXPECT_EQ(reader->frame_header().sample_rate, 44100u);
    EXPECT_EQ(reader->frame_header().channel_count, 2);
    EXPECT_EQ(reader->frame_header().audio_object_type, 2);
    EXPECT_EQ(reader->frame_header().frame_byte_size, FRAME_BYTE_SIZE);
}

TEST_CASE(reader_estimates_a_duration_from_the_bitrate_at_the_front_of_a_stream)
{
    // Every frame is the same size, so extrapolating from the front describes the whole stream.
    Vector<u8> bytes;
    append_frames(bytes, 200);

    auto reader = read(bytes);
    EXPECT(reader.has_value());
    EXPECT_EQ(reader->duration(), AK::Duration::from_time_units(200 * 1024, 1, 44100));
}

TEST_CASE(frame_iterator_walks_every_frame_of_a_stream)
{
    Vector<u8> bytes;
    append_frames(bytes, 12);

    Media::ADTS::FrameIterator iterator { create_cursor(bytes), 0, Media::ADTS::FrameIterator::Resynchronize::No };

    size_t frame_count = 0;
    size_t expected_position = 0;
    while (true) {
        auto frame = MUST(iterator.next());
        if (!frame.has_value())
            break;
        EXPECT_EQ(frame->position, expected_position);
        expected_position += FRAME_BYTE_SIZE;
        frame_count++;
    }
    EXPECT_EQ(frame_count, 12u);
}

TEST_CASE(frame_iterator_reads_the_audio_without_the_framing_around_it)
{
    Vector<u8> bytes;
    append_frames(bytes, 2);

    Media::ADTS::FrameIterator iterator { create_cursor(bytes), 0, Media::ADTS::FrameIterator::Resynchronize::No };
    auto frame = MUST(iterator.read_next_frame());
    EXPECT(frame.has_value());

    // The header frames the audio rather than describing it, and a decoder configured from the
    // record the header implies expects the access unit alone.
    EXPECT_EQ(frame->data.size(), FRAME_BYTE_SIZE - Media::ADTS::FrameHeader::SIZE);
}

TEST_CASE(frame_iterator_resumes_at_the_frames_that_follow_damage)
{
    Vector<u8> bytes;
    append_frames(bytes, 2);
    bytes.resize(bytes.size() + 500);
    append_frames(bytes, 3);

    Media::ADTS::FrameIterator iterator { create_cursor(bytes), 0, Media::ADTS::FrameIterator::Resynchronize::Yes };

    size_t frame_count = 0;
    while (MUST(iterator.next()).has_value())
        frame_count++;
    EXPECT_EQ(frame_count, 5u);
}

TEST_CASE(frame_iterator_stops_where_a_frame_header_can_no_longer_be_read)
{
    Vector<u8> bytes;
    append_frames(bytes, 3);
    bytes.resize(bytes.size() - (FRAME_BYTE_SIZE - 2));

    Media::ADTS::FrameIterator iterator { create_cursor(bytes), 0, Media::ADTS::FrameIterator::Resynchronize::No };

    size_t frame_count = 0;
    while (MUST(iterator.next()).has_value())
        frame_count++;
    EXPECT_EQ(frame_count, 2u);
}

TEST_CASE(frame_iterator_reports_a_frame_whose_audio_has_not_all_arrived)
{
    // A header states how far its frame reaches, so the frame is known before the audio behind it
    // has been read. What counts that frame towards a timeline is the byte range holding all of it.
    Vector<u8> bytes;
    append_frames(bytes, 2);
    bytes.resize(bytes.size() - 4);

    Media::ADTS::FrameIterator iterator { create_cursor(bytes), 0, Media::ADTS::FrameIterator::Resynchronize::No };
    EXPECT(MUST(iterator.next()).has_value());

    auto truncated_frame_position = iterator.position();
    auto truncated = MUST(iterator.next());
    EXPECT(truncated.has_value());
    EXPECT_EQ(truncated->header.frame_byte_size, FRAME_BYTE_SIZE);

    // Its data cannot be read in full, so reading it leaves the iterator at the frame.
    Media::ADTS::FrameIterator data_iterator { create_cursor(bytes), truncated_frame_position, Media::ADTS::FrameIterator::Resynchronize::No };
    EXPECT(data_iterator.read_next_frame().is_error());
    EXPECT_EQ(data_iterator.position(), truncated_frame_position);
}

TEST_CASE(reader_searches_past_bytes_that_precede_the_audio)
{
    Vector<u8> bytes;
    bytes.resize(1000);
    append_frames(bytes, 8);

    auto reader = read(bytes);
    EXPECT(reader.has_value());
    EXPECT_EQ(reader->first_frame_position(), 1000u);
}

TEST_CASE(reader_skips_an_identification_tag_that_precedes_the_audio)
{
    Vector<u8> bytes;
    // An ID3v2 tag of 100 bytes, whose size is stored as four seven-bit groups.
    for (auto byte : Array<u8, 10> { 'I', 'D', '3', 0x04, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 100 })
        bytes.append(byte);
    bytes.resize(110);
    append_frames(bytes, 8);

    auto reader = read(bytes);
    EXPECT(reader.has_value());
    EXPECT_EQ(reader->first_frame_position(), 110u);
}

    // A sync code with nothing behind it is not where the audio begins.
    Vector<u8> bytes;

    bytes[500] = 0xFF;
    bytes[501] = 0xF1;

    bytes[503] = 0x80;
    bytes[504] = 0x20;
    bytes[505] = 0x1F;
    bytes[506] = 0xFC;
    append_frames(bytes, 8);

    EXPECT(!read(bytes).has_value());
