namespace FetchTest {

// What the algorithms of a fetch saw, which the test reads once they have run.
struct AlgorithmCalls : RefCounted<AlgorithmCalls> {
    GC_HOLDS_NO_CELL_EDGES;

    Vector<StringView> calls;
    Vector<GC::Root<Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::ResponseView>> responses;
    Optional<ByteBuffer> consumed_bytes;
    size_t call_count { 0 };
    bool consumed_body { false };
};

// What reached the steps a test set up, which the test reads once they have run.
struct ReachedSteps : RefCounted<ReachedSteps> {
    GC_HOLDS_NO_CELL_EDGES;

    Vector<ByteString> steps;
    bool marker_reached { false };
};

// The commands posted to an engine that applies none of them, for the test to hand on.
struct PostedCommands : RefCounted<PostedCommands> {
    Vector<Web::Fetch::Engine::EngineCommand> commands;
};

inline ByteString describe_transport_control(Web::Fetch::Engine::Command::TransportControl::Operation const& operation, Web::Fetch::Engine::RequestId request_id, Web::Fetch::Engine::TransportEpoch transport_epoch)
{
    using Web::Fetch::Engine::Command::TransportControl;
    auto description = operation.visit(
        [](TransportControl::StopTransport) { return ByteString { "stop transport"sv }; },
        [](TransportControl::ReleaseNavigationHold) { return ByteString { "release navigation hold"sv }; },
        [](TransportControl::ReleaseNavigationHoldUpTo const& release) { return ByteString::formatted("release navigation hold up to {}", release.byte_count); });
    return ByteString::formatted("{} of request {} of epoch {}", description, request_id.value(), transport_epoch.value());
}

// Hands each event of a fetch on to the fetch's event sink, and records the ends of the fetch's bodies and of the fetch,
// and each event that comes after the fetch's end. It is destroyed with the fetch's engine record, and records that too.
class EventRecordingSink final : public Web::Fetch::Engine::EngineEventSink {
public:
    EventRecordingSink(NonnullOwnPtr<Web::Fetch::Engine::EngineEventSink> event_sink, NonnullRefPtr<ReachedSteps> reached, NonnullRefPtr<ReachedSteps> records_gone, ByteString fetch)
        : m_event_sink(move(event_sink))
        , m_reached(move(reached))
        , m_records_gone(move(records_gone))
        , m_fetch(move(fetch))
    {
    }

    virtual ~EventRecordingSink() override
    {
        m_records_gone->steps.append(m_fetch);
    }

    virtual void handle_event(Web::Fetch::Engine::EngineEvent event) override
    {
        if (m_fetch_ended)
            m_reached->steps.append(ByteString::formatted("event after the end of fetch {}", m_fetch));
        else if (event.has<Web::Fetch::Engine::Event::EndOfBody>())
            m_reached->steps.append(ByteString::formatted("end of body of {}", m_fetch));
        else if (event.has<Web::Fetch::Engine::Event::FetchEnded>())
            m_reached->steps.append(ByteString::formatted("end of fetch {}", m_fetch));
        m_fetch_ended |= event.has<Web::Fetch::Engine::Event::FetchEnded>();
        m_event_sink->handle_event(move(event));
    }

private:
    NonnullOwnPtr<Web::Fetch::Engine::EngineEventSink> m_event_sink;
    NonnullRefPtr<ReachedSteps> m_reached;
    NonnullRefPtr<ReachedSteps> m_records_gone;
    ByteString m_fetch;
    bool m_fetch_ended { false };
};

class IgnoringEventSink final : public Web::Fetch::Engine::EngineEventSink {
public:
    virtual void handle_event(Web::Fetch::Engine::EngineEvent) override { }
};

// A load of a fetch that an engine of its own starts, for a transport that a case drives itself.
inline NonnullRefPtr<Web::Fetch::Engine::FetchLoad> start_a_load_of_another_engine()
{
    Web::Fetch::Engine::FetchEngineRecords records { make<Web::Fetch::Engine::FetchEngineRecords::Agent>() };
    auto record = records.start(Web::Fetch::Engine::FetchId { 1 }, make<IgnoringEventSink>(), Web::Fetch::Engine::NetworkActivityObservers::create());
    return record->start_load();
}

// Records each command that reaches the fetch engine, then hands it to a fetch engine through its executor, keeps it
// for the test to hand on, or drops it. A fetch the recorder saw start is named by its number in the order of the
// starts, from 1, and any other fetch by its id. The fetch engine's events record the ends of the bodies of the
// fetches it starts, and of the fetches.
class CommandRecordingEngine final : public Web::Fetch::Engine::EngineCommandSink {
public:
    using Destination = Variant<Empty, NonnullRefPtr<PostedCommands>, NonnullRefPtr<Web::Fetch::Engine::FetchExecutor>>;

    explicit CommandRecordingEngine(NonnullRefPtr<ReachedSteps> reached, Destination destination = Empty {}, RefPtr<ReachedSteps> records_gone = {})
        : m_reached(move(reached))
        , m_records_gone(records_gone ? records_gone.release_nonnull() : make_ref_counted<ReachedSteps>())
        , m_destination(move(destination))
    {
    }

    virtual void handle_command(Web::Fetch::Engine::EngineCommand command) override
    {
        using namespace Web::Fetch::Engine::Command;
        m_reached->steps.append(describe(command));
        if (auto const* engine_executor = m_destination.get_pointer<NonnullRefPtr<Web::Fetch::Engine::FetchExecutor>>()) {
            if (auto* start = command.get_pointer<StartFetch>())
                start->input.event_sink = make<EventRecordingSink>(move(start->input.event_sink), m_reached, m_records_gone, fetch(start->input.fetch_id));
            (*engine_executor)->post(move(command));
            return;
        }

        // Without a fetch engine, a case expects only stops, transport controls and adopted navigation bodies.
        if (!command.has<Abort>() && !command.has<Terminate>() && !command.has<Stop>() && !command.has<TransportControl>() && !command.has<NavigationBodyAdopted>())
            FAIL("unexpected command");
        if (auto const* posted_commands = m_destination.get_pointer<NonnullRefPtr<PostedCommands>>())
            (*posted_commands)->commands.append(move(command));
    }

private:
    ByteString fetch(Web::Fetch::Engine::FetchId fetch_id) const
    {
        if (auto index = m_started_fetches.find_first_index(fetch_id); index.has_value())
            return ByteString::number(*index + 1);
        return ByteString::number(fetch_id.value());
    }

    ByteString describe(Web::Fetch::Engine::EngineCommand const& command)
    {
        using namespace Web::Fetch::Engine::Command;
        return command.visit(
            [&](StartFetch const& start) {
                m_started_fetches.append(start.input.fetch_id);
                return ByteString::formatted("start fetch {}", fetch(start.input.fetch_id));
            },
            [&](Abort const& abort) { return ByteString::formatted("abort {}", fetch(abort.fetch_id)); },
            [&](Terminate const& terminate) { return ByteString::formatted("terminate {}", fetch(terminate.fetch_id)); },
            [&](Stop const& stop) { return ByteString::formatted("stop {}", fetch(stop.fetch_id)); },
            [&](ResolveRedirect const& resolve) {
                return resolve.resolution.visit(
                    [&](ResolveRedirect::Follow) { return ByteString::formatted("follow redirect of {}", fetch(resolve.fetch_id)); },
                    [&](ResolveRedirect::AcceptAsFinal) { return ByteString::formatted("accept redirect of {} as final", fetch(resolve.fetch_id)); },
                    [&](ResolveRedirect::Abandon) { return ByteString::formatted("abandon redirect of {}", fetch(resolve.fetch_id)); });
            },
            [&](PreloadResponseResolved const& resolved) { return ByteString::formatted("preload response resolved {}", fetch(resolved.fetch_id)); },
            [&](PreloadWaitAbandoned const& abandoned) { return ByteString::formatted("abandon preload wait of {}", fetch(abandoned.fetch_id)); },
            [](TransportControl const& control) { return describe_transport_control(control.operation, control.request_id, control.transport_epoch); },
            [](NavigationBodyAdopted const&) { return ByteString { "navigation body adopted"sv }; },
            [](AdoptNetworkTransport const&) { return ByteString { "adopt network transport"sv }; });
    }

    NonnullRefPtr<ReachedSteps> m_reached;
    NonnullRefPtr<ReachedSteps> m_records_gone;
    Destination m_destination;
    Vector<Web::Fetch::Engine::FetchId> m_started_fetches;
};

// Runs the agent's tasks until the condition holds, or for the given time.
inline void run_tasks_until(GC::Heap& heap, GC::Ref<GC::Function<bool()>> condition, AK::Duration timeout = AK::Duration::from_seconds(10))
{
    auto deadline = Core::Timer::create_single_shot(timeout, [] { });
    deadline->start();
    Web::HTML::main_thread_event_loop().spin_until(GC::create_function(heap, GC::captures(condition, deadline->make_weak_ptr<Core::Timer>()), [](auto& condition, auto& deadline) {
        return condition->function()() || !deadline || !deadline->is_active();
    }));
}

struct FetchHarness {
    FetchHarness()
        : document(create_test_document())
        , realm(document->relevant_settings_object().realm())
    {
        // Each case has an event loop of its own, which the window agent's fetches have to run on.
        auto& agent = Web::HTML::surrounding_agent();
        agent.fetch_executor = Web::Fetch::Fetching::create_inline_fetch_executor(agent.network_activity_observers);
    }

    // Records each command the agent posts from now on, before the agent's fetch engine gets it, and the fetches whose
    // engine records are gone in records_gone.
    NonnullRefPtr<ReachedSteps> record_commands() const
    {
        auto commands = make_ref_counted<ReachedSteps>();
        auto& agent = Web::HTML::surrounding_agent();
        Web::Fetch::Engine::FetchExecutorServices services { .event_loop = Core::EventLoop::current_weak() };
        auto recording_engine = make<CommandRecordingEngine>(commands, NonnullRefPtr { *agent.fetch_executor }, records_gone);
        agent.fetch_executor = Web::Fetch::Engine::InlineFetchExecutor::create(move(services), move(recording_engine));
        return commands;
    }

    // An unknown scheme: scheme fetch returns a network error, which has no body.
    NonnullRefPtr<Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::Request> create_request() const
    {
        return create_request_for("unknown-scheme:network-error"sv);
    }

    NonnullRefPtr<Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::Request> create_request_for(StringView url_string) const
    {
        auto url = URL::Parser::basic_parse(url_string);
        VERIFY(url.has_value());

        auto request = Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::Request::create();
        request->set_url_list({ url.release_value() });
        request->set_client(document->relevant_settings_object().address());
        return request;
    }

    // A request like the one a navigation fetches, whose fetch hands each redirect over without following it.
    NonnullRefPtr<Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::Request> create_navigation_request_for(StringView url_string) const
    {
        using Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::Request;
        auto request = create_request_for(url_string);
        request->set_mode(Request::Mode::Navigate);
        request->set_destination(Request::Destination::Document);
        request->set_redirect_mode(Request::RedirectMode::Manual);
        return request;
    }

    // Fetches from the harness's document, or from the given one.
    GC::Ref<Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchController> fetch(Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::Request& request, Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchAlgorithms::Input input, GC::Ptr<Web::DOM::Document> from_document = {}) const
    {
        return fetch_with(request, Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchAlgorithms::create(move(input)), from_document);
    }

    GC::Ref<Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchController> fetch_with(Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::Request& request, Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchAlgorithms const& algorithms, GC::Ptr<Web::DOM::Document> from_document = {}) const
    {
        auto& settings = (from_document ? *from_document : *document).relevant_settings_object();
        request.set_client(settings.address());
        Web::HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext execution_context { settings.realm(), Web::HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext::CallbacksEnabled::Yes };
        return Web::Fetch::Fetching::fetch(settings.realm(), request, algorithms);
    }

    // Fetches as a navigation does: on a parallel queue, with a transfer lease on each response's body.
    GC::Ref<Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchController> fetch_as_a_navigation(Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::Request& request, Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchAlgorithms::Input input) const
    {
        Web::HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext execution_context { *realm, Web::HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext::CallbacksEnabled::Yes };
        auto algorithms = Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchAlgorithms::create(move(input));
        return Web::Fetch::Fetching::fetch(*realm, request, algorithms, Web::Fetch::Fetching::UseParallelQueue::Yes, Web::Fetch::Fetching::CreateResponseBodyTransferLease::Yes);
    }

    void with_execution_context(Function<void()> steps) const
    {
        Web::HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext execution_context { *realm, Web::HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext::CallbacksEnabled::Yes };
        steps();
    }

    // The event loop runs no task while the handle lives.
    Web::HTML::EventLoop::PauseHandle pause_event_loop() const
    {
        Web::HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext execution_context { *realm, Web::HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext::CallbacksEnabled::Yes };
        return Web::HTML::main_thread_event_loop().pause(Web::HTML::EventLoop::UpdateTheRendering::No);
    }

    // Runs the fetch's steps and the tasks they queue until the condition holds, or for the given time.
    void run_tasks_until(GC::Ref<GC::Function<bool()>> condition, AK::Duration timeout = AK::Duration::from_seconds(10)) const
    {
        FetchTest::run_tasks_until(realm->heap(), condition, timeout);
    }

    void run_until_step(NonnullRefPtr<ReachedSteps> const& reached, StringView step) const
    {
        auto expected = ByteString { step };
        run_tasks_until(GC::create_function(realm->heap(), GC::captures(reached, expected), [](auto& reached, auto& expected) { return reached->steps.contains_slow(expected); }));
    }

    void run_until_responses(NonnullRefPtr<AlgorithmCalls> const& record, size_t count) const
    {
        run_tasks_until(GC::create_function(realm->heap(), GC::captures(record, count), [](auto& record, auto& count) { return record->responses.size() == count; }));
        VERIFY(record->responses.size() == count);
    }

    // Runs everything for a while. What has not happened by then is taken not to happen.
    void settle(AK::Duration duration = AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(300)) const
    {
        run_tasks_until(GC::create_function(realm->heap(), [] { return false; }), duration);
    }

    // Runs the deferred invocations queued so far, then those that they queue.
    void run_queued_invocations() const
    {
        auto reached = make_ref_counted<ReachedSteps>();
        Core::deferred_invoke([reached] {
            Core::deferred_invoke([reached] { reached->marker_reached = true; });
        });
        run_tasks_until(GC::create_function(realm->heap(), GC::captures(reached), [](auto& reached) { return reached->marker_reached; }));
    }

    GC::Ref<Web::DOM::Document> document;
    GC::Ref<JS::Realm> realm;
    NonnullRefPtr<ReachedSteps> records_gone { make_ref_counted<ReachedSteps>() };
};

// What a RequestServer the test stands in for has been sent: each message, in the order it came, as
// "start <id> <method> <path>", "stop <id>", "release lease <id>", or the message's name.
struct RequestServerMessages : RefCounted<RequestServerMessages> {
    GC_HOLDS_NO_CELL_EDGES;

    void read()
    {
        (void)transport->read_as_many_messages_as_possible_without_blocking([this](auto&& raw_message) {
            auto message = MUST(RequestServerEndpoint::decode_message(raw_message.bytes.bytes(), raw_message.attachments));
            auto message_id = message->message_id();
            if (message_id == Messages::RequestServer::StartRequest::static_message_id()) {
                auto const& start = static_cast<Messages::RequestServer::StartRequest&>(*message);
                started_ids.append(start.request_id());
                started_methods.append(start.method());
                messages.append(ByteString::formatted("start {} {} {}", start.request_id(), start.method(), start.url().serialize_path()));
            } else if (message_id == Messages::RequestServer::StopRequest::static_message_id()) {
                auto const& stop = static_cast<Messages::RequestServer::StopRequest&>(*message);
                messages.append(ByteString::formatted("stop {}", stop.request_id()));
            } else if (message_id == Messages::RequestServer::ReleaseRequestTransferLease::static_message_id()) {
                auto const& release = static_cast<Messages::RequestServer::ReleaseRequestTransferLease&>(*message);
                messages.append(ByteString::formatted("release lease {}", release.source_request_id()));
            } else {
                messages.append(message->message_name());
            }
        });
    }

    IPC::Transport* transport { nullptr };
    Vector<ByteString> messages;
    Vector<u64> started_ids;
    Vector<ByteString> started_methods;
};

// A RequestServer client of the agent's resource loader, whose RequestServer end of the connection the test holds: it
// records each message RequestServer gets, and answers only as the test says.
class StandInRequestServer {
public:
    explicit StandInRequestServer(FetchHarness const& harness)
        : m_harness(harness)
    {
        Web::ResourceLoader::initialize(harness.realm->heap());
        auto pair = MUST(IPC::Transport::create_paired());
        m_client = make_ref_counted<Requests::RequestClient>(move(pair.local), 1);
        Web::ResourceLoader::the().set_client({}, *m_client);
        m_request_server = MUST(pair.remote_handle.create_transport());
        m_received->transport = m_request_server.ptr();
    }

    ~StandInRequestServer()
    {
        // The client can hear of its RequestServer's death after the resource loader is gone.
        m_client->on_request_server_died = nullptr;
        Web::ResourceLoader::shut_down();
    }

    // Runs the agent's tasks until another request with the method has started, and returns its id.
    u64 wait_for_request(StringView method)
    {
        // The RequestServer end is not part of the event loop, so keep the loop from sleeping until it has news.
        auto wake_timer = Core::Timer::create_repeating(AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(10), [] { });
        wake_timer->start();

        auto expected = ByteString { method };
        m_harness.run_tasks_until(GC::create_function(m_harness.realm->heap(), GC::captures(m_received, m_taken_count, expected), [](auto& received, auto& taken_count, auto& expected) {
            received->read();
            for (size_t index = taken_count; index < received->started_methods.size(); ++index) {
                if (received->started_methods[index] == expected)
                    return true;
            }
            return false;
        }));
        for (size_t index = m_taken_count; index < m_received->started_methods.size(); ++index) {
            if (m_received->started_methods[index] == method) {
                m_taken_count = index + 1;
                return m_received->started_ids[index];
            }
        }
        VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
    }

    // Runs the agent's tasks until RequestServer has been sent the message, named as messages() names it.
    void wait_for_message(StringView message)
    {
        auto wake_timer = Core::Timer::create_repeating(AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(10), [] { });
        wake_timer->start();

        auto expected = ByteString { message };
        m_harness.run_tasks_until(GC::create_function(m_harness.realm->heap(), GC::captures(m_received, expected), [](auto& received, auto& expected) {
            received->read();
            return received->messages.contains_slow(expected);
        }));
    }

    // The messages RequestServer has been sent so far.
    Vector<ByteString> const& messages() const
    {
        m_received->read();
        return m_received->messages;
    }

    void send(IPC::MessageBuffer message)
    {
        MUST(message.transfer_message(*m_request_server));
    }

    void send_headers(u64 request_id, u32 status_code, Vector<HTTP::Header> headers = {})
    {
        send(MUST(Messages::RequestClient::HeadersBecameAvailable::static_encode(request_id, URL::about_blank(), move(headers), status_code, Optional<String> {}, Requests::CacheState::NotCached, ByteString {})));
    }

    void send_finished(u64 request_id, Requests::RequestTimingInfo timing_info = {}, Optional<Requests::NetworkError> network_error = {})
    {
        send(MUST(Messages::RequestClient::RequestFinished::static_encode(request_id, 0, timing_info, network_error)));
    }

    // Delivers the body the file holds, as RequestServer does for a body it keeps in a file.
    void send_body_file(u64 request_id, ByteString const& path, size_t size)
    {
        auto file = IPC::File::adopt_file(MUST(Core::File::open(path, Core::File::OpenMode::Read)));
        send(MUST(Messages::RequestClient::RequestBodyFileAvailable::static_encode(request_id, file, 0, size)));
    }

    void send_transferred(u64 request_id)
    {
        send(MUST(Messages::RequestClient::RequestTransferred::static_encode(request_id)));
    }

private:
    FetchHarness const& m_harness;
    RefPtr<Requests::RequestClient> m_client;
    OwnPtr<IPC::Transport> m_request_server;
    NonnullRefPtr<RequestServerMessages> m_received { make_ref_counted<RequestServerMessages>() };
    // The started requests a wait has already returned or passed over.
    size_t m_taken_count { 0 };
};

inline Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchAlgorithms::Input recording_responses(GC::Heap& heap, NonnullRefPtr<AlgorithmCalls> const& record)
{
    Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchAlgorithms::Input input { Web::Fetch::Engine::BodyIntent::DrainAndDiscard };
    input.process_response = GC::create_function(heap, GC::captures(record), [](auto& record, GC::Ref<Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::ResponseView> response) {
        record->responses.append(GC::make_root(response));
    });
    return input;
}

// The token of the agent's fetch whose fetch params match, which a test holds instead of the fetch's controller.
inline NEVER_INLINE Optional<Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchControllerToken> token_of_fetch(Function<bool(Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchParams const&)> const& matches)
{
    for (auto const& controller : Web::HTML::surrounding_agent().fetch_controller_registry.controllers()) {
        auto fetch_params = controller->original_fetch_params();
        if (fetch_params && matches(*fetch_params))
            return controller->token();
    }
    return {};
}

// The token of the fetch whose request's first URL has the path.
inline Optional<Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchControllerToken> token_of_fetch_for(StringView path)
{
    return token_of_fetch([&](auto const& fetch_params) { return fetch_params.request()->url().serialize_path() == path; });
}

inline NEVER_INLINE GC::Ptr<Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchController> find_controller(Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchControllerToken token)
{
    return Web::HTML::surrounding_agent().fetch_controller_registry.find(token);
}

// Whether the fetch has handed a response over, whose process response task the handover queued.
inline bool was_handed_over(Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchController const& controller)
{
    return controller.control_block().agent_timing_info();
}

// Whether the agent's registry keeps the controller alive, as that of a fetch or of a fetch's CORS preflight.
inline bool is_rooted(Web::Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchControllerToken token)
{
    return Web::HTML::surrounding_agent().fetch_controller_registry.roots(token);
}

"""
Description:
    This script starts a simple HTTP and WebSocket echo server on localhost for use in our in-tree tests.
    The port is assigned by the OS on startup and printed to stdout.

Endpoints:
    - POST /echo <json body>, Creates an echo response for later use. See "Echo" class below for body properties.
    - Echo responses accept chunks=<byte-counts> and chunk_unblock_tokens=<tokens> query parameters.
    - Echo responses accept request_body_read_size=<bytes> and request_body_read_delay_ms=<ms> query parameters,
      which read the request's body that many bytes at a time, waiting that long before each read.
      Each named token holds the response after the corresponding chunk until GET /unblock/<token>.
    - An echo response's body may contain $BODY, which the server replaces with the request's body.
    - An echo answers a Range request with the requested part of its body, unless it was created with
      "ignore_range": true. Then it sends the entire body, as a server that doesn't support ranges does.
    - GET <any path> with an "Upgrade: websocket" header: Performs a WebSocket handshake and then echoes
      every text/binary frame back to the client verbatim. With a "send-binary=<size>" query parameter, the
      server first sends a binary frame of that many bytes: a 1, zeros, and then a 2.
    - GET /reflect-websocket-cookie with an "Upgrade: websocket" header: As above, but first sends the
      handshake's Cookie header (or an empty string) as a text frame.
    - GET /reflect-websocket-accept-language does the same for the handshake's Accept-Language header.
    - GET /websocket-close-without-response with an "Upgrade: websocket" header: Closes the connection without
      responding to the handshake.
    - GET /recorded-request-count/<echo path>: Responds with the number of requests the server has seen at <echo path>,
      with any query ignored.
    - GET /downloads/<name>: Reports the browser's download of <name> into the --downloads-directory: 404 while
      there is none, 202 while it is in progress, and the downloaded file once it has finished. A <name> longer
      than 188 bytes in UTF-8 gets a 400.
"""


class Echo:
    method: str
    path: str
    status: int
    headers: Dict[str, str]
    body: Optional[str]
    body_encoding: str
    delay_ms: Optional[int]
    reason_phrase: Optional[str]
    reflect_headers_in_body: bool
    close_connection: bool
    ignore_range: bool
    wait_for_unblock: Optional[str]

    def __eq__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Echo):
            return NotImplemented

        return (
            self.method == other.method
            and self.path == other.path
            and self.status == other.status
            and self.body == other.body
            and self.body_encoding == other.body_encoding
            and self.delay_ms == other.delay_ms
            and self.headers == other.headers
            and self.reason_phrase == other.reason_phrase
            and self.reflect_headers_in_body == other.reflect_headers_in_body
            and self.close_connection == other.close_connection
            and self.ignore_range == other.ignore_range
            and self.wait_for_unblock == other.wait_for_unblock
        )


# In-memory store for echo responses
echo_store: Dict[str, Echo] = {}

# Headers from the most recent request at each echo path, queryable via GET /recorded-request-headers<echo-path>.
recorded_request_headers: Dict[str, Dict[str, list]] = {}

# Number of requests seen at each echo path, query excluded, queryable via GET /recorded-request-count<echo-path>.
recorded_request_counts: Dict[str, int] = {}

stalled_tls_port = 0

# Per RFC 6455: appended to Sec-WebSocket-Key before hashing to compute the Sec-WebSocket-Accept value.
WEBSOCKET_ACCEPT_GUID = "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11"


def websocket_handshake_response(key):
    accept = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha1((key + WEBSOCKET_ACCEPT_GUID).encode("utf-8")).digest()).decode("ascii")
    return (
        "HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\n"
        "Upgrade: websocket\r\n"
        "Connection: Upgrade\r\n"
        f"Sec-WebSocket-Accept: {accept}\r\n"
        "\r\n"
    ).encode("ascii")


# The browser saves a download as <name>.<id>.<uuid>.download until it finishes. That suffix takes at most 67 of the
# 255 bytes a filename may have, so a name of up to 188 bytes is never cut short.
MAXIMUM_REPORTED_DOWNLOAD_NAME_LENGTH = 188


def name_of_download_in_progress(filename: str) -> Optional[str]:
    if not filename.endswith(".download"):
        return None
    parts = filename[: -len(".download")].rsplit(".", 2)
    if len(parts) != 3:
        return None
    name, download_id, uuid = parts
    if not (download_id.isascii() and download_id.isdigit()) or len(uuid) != 36:
        return None
    return name


def test_web_host_for(hostname):
    # A test's subdomains and its -alt host belong to the test-web-*.localhost or test-web-*.test host of the test.
    rest, _, top_level_domain = hostname.rpartition(".")
    host = rest.rpartition(".")[2].removesuffix("-alt")
    if top_level_domain not in ("localhost", "test") or not host.startswith("test-web-"):
        return None
    return f"{host}.{top_level_domain}"


class WPTContext:
    def __init__(self, wpt_directory):
        vendored_tools_root = os.path.join(wpt_directory, "_wpttools")

        for path in (wpt_directory, vendored_tools_root):
            sys.path.insert(0, path)

        import _wpttools as vendored_tools
        import localpaths

        # Make the copied tree behave like the upstream `tools` package so
        # vendored modules can keep importing `tools.*` and `localpaths`.
        cast(Any, vendored_tools).localpaths = localpaths
        sys.modules["tools"] = vendored_tools
        sys.modules["tools.localpaths"] = localpaths
        sys.modules["localpaths"] = localpaths
        localpaths.repo_root = os.path.abspath(wpt_directory)

        from wptserve.config import ConfigBuilder
        from wptserve.handlers import AsIsHandler
        from wptserve.handlers import FileHandler
        from wptserve.handlers import python_script_handler
        from wptserve.request import Request
        from wptserve.request import Server
        from wptserve.response import Response
        from wptserve.stash import Stash
        from wptserve.stash import start_server as start_stash_server
        from wptserve.utils import HTTPException

        class TestWebConfigBuilder(ConfigBuilder):
            # Our own servers serve HTTPS, not wptserve's, so keep the HTTPS ports that wptserve drops when its own TLS
            # support is not configured.
            def _get_ports(self, data):
                return defaultdict(list, {scheme: list(ports) for scheme, ports in data["ports"].items()})

        self.config_builder_class = TestWebConfigBuilder
        self.server_class = Server

        self.request_class = Request
        self.response_class = Response
        self.file_handler_class = FileHandler
        self.as_is_handler_class = AsIsHandler
        self.python_script_handler = python_script_handler
        self.http_exception = HTTPException
        self.stash_class = Stash
        self.stash_manager, self.stash_address, self.stash_authkey = start_stash_server()

    def create_file_handler(self, base_path, url_base="/"):
        file_handler = self.file_handler_class(base_path=base_path, url_base=url_base)
        as_is_handler = self.as_is_handler_class(base_path=base_path, url_base=url_base)

        def handler(request, response):
            # Like upstream wptserve, send .asis files without generating any response headers.
            if request.url_parts.path.endswith(".asis"):
                return as_is_handler(request, response)
            return file_handler(request, response)

        return handler

    def configure_server(self, http_ports, https_ports):
        # The HTTP(S) servers also accept WebSocket connections.
        self.ports = {"http": http_ports, "https": https_ports, "ws": http_ports[:1], "wss": https_ports}
        self.configs_by_host = {}
        self.configs_by_host_lock = threading.Lock()
        cast(Any, self.server_class).config = self._build_config("web-platform.localhost")

    def _build_config(self, browser_host, alternate_host="not-localhost.localhost"):
        def make_subdomains_product(subdomains, depth=2):
            return {
                ".".join(labels)
                for length in range(1, depth + 1)
                for labels in itertools.product(subdomains, repeat=length)
            }

        subdomains = make_subdomains_product({"www", "www1", "www2"})
        not_subdomains = make_subdomains_product({"nonexistent"})
        logger = logging.getLogger("test-web-wptserve")
        with self.config_builder_class(
            logger,
            browser_host=browser_host,
            alternate_hosts={"alt": alternate_host},
            ports=self.ports,
            subdomains=subdomains,
            not_subdomains=not_subdomains,
            check_subdomains=False,
        ) as config:
            return config

    def apply_config_for_request(self, request):
        # test-web uses unique test-web-*.localhost hosts, or test-web-*.test for insecure-origin tests.
        # Substitutions like {{host}} and {{domains[www1]}} must name that test host and its subdomains.
        hostname = request.url_parts.hostname or ""
        test_host = test_web_host_for(hostname)
        if not test_host:
            return

        is_https = request.url_parts.scheme == "https"
        key = (test_host, is_https)
        with self.configs_by_host_lock:
            config = self.configs_by_host.get(key)
            if config is None:
                # Each test has its own host, so only keep the configs of the most recent ones.
                if len(self.configs_by_host) >= 64:
                    self.configs_by_host.pop(next(iter(self.configs_by_host)))
                if is_https:
                    config = self._build_config(test_host, test_host.removesuffix(".localhost") + "-alt.localhost")
                else:
                    config = self._build_config(test_host)
                self.configs_by_host[key] = config
        request.server.config = config

    def close(self):
        self.stash_manager.shutdown()

        # Leave the handshake to the first read, which happens on the request's own thread.

class TestHTTPRequestHandler(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    static_directory: str
    wpt_directory: str
    downloads_directory: Optional[str] = None
    aia_artifacts: dict
    aia_config: Optional[dict]

    def __init__(self, *arguments, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*arguments, directory=self.static_directory, **kwargs)

    def _test_server(self):
        return cast(TestHTTPServer, self.server)

    def end_headers(self):
        extra_headers = getattr(self, "_extra_headers", None)
        if extra_headers is not None:
            self._sending_extra_headers = True
            for key, value in extra_headers:
                self.send_header(key, value)
            self._sending_extra_headers = False
            delattr(self, "_extra_headers")
            delattr(self, "_extra_header_names")
        super().end_headers()

    def send_header(self, keyword, value):
        # Headers from .headers files override headers created by SimpleHTTPRequestHandler.
        extra_header_names = getattr(self, "_extra_header_names", None)
        if (
            extra_header_names is not None
            and not getattr(self, "_sending_extra_headers", False)
            and keyword.lower() in extra_header_names
        ):
            return
        super().send_header(keyword, value)

    def _request_target(self):
        if self.path.startswith("/static/"):
            # Explicit /static/ URLs continue to serve files from the general test root.
            return self.static_directory, self.path[7:]

        # All other non-echo URLs are served from the imported WPT tree.
        # This lets absolute WPT paths like /html/... resolve through the test server.
        return self.wpt_directory, self.path

    def _serve_wpt_python_script(self):
        self.directory, self.path = self._request_target()
        server = self._test_server()
        server.router.doc_root = self.directory

        request, response = self._create_wpt_request_response()

        try:
            server.wpt.python_script_handler(request, response)
        except server.wpt.http_exception as exception:
            response.set_error(exception.code, exception)
        except Exception as exception:
            response.set_error(500, exception)

        if not response.writer.content_written:
            response.write()
        if response.close_connection:
            self.close_connection = True
        request.close()

    def _create_wpt_request_response(self):
        server = self._test_server()
        request = server.wpt.request_class(self)
        server.wpt.apply_config_for_request(request)
        request.server._stash = server.wpt.stash_class(
            request.url_parts.path,
            server.wpt.stash_address,
            server.wpt.stash_authkey,
        )
        response = server.wpt.response_class(self, request)
        return request, response

    def _serve_wpt_file_request(self):
        self.directory, _ = self._request_target()
        server = self._test_server()
        server.router.doc_root = self.directory

        request, response = self._create_wpt_request_response()

        if self.path.startswith("/static/"):
            handler = server.static_file_handler
        else:
            handler = server.wpt_file_handler

        try:
            handler(request, response)
        except server.wpt.http_exception as exception:
            response.set_error(exception.code, exception)
        except Exception as exception:
            response.set_error(500, exception)

        if not response.writer.content_written:
            response.write()
        if response.close_connection:
            self.close_connection = True
        request.close()

    def _serve_static_request(self):
        self._serve_wpt_file_request()

    def _serve_aia_artifact(self, request_path):
        # Serves the intermediate certificate that the broken-chain HTTPS hosts point at via their AIA caIssuers URL.
        # Fetched by RequestServer, not by the page.
        entry = getattr(TestHTTPRequestHandler, "aia_artifacts", {}).get(request_path)
        if entry is None:
            # for example, /aia/dead: a deliberately missing artifact, to exercise the failure path.
            self.send_error(404, "Not Found")
            return
        content_type, body = entry
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", content_type)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _serve_stalled_tls_config(self):
        # Lets the test page discover a port that accepts connections and never answers a TLS handshake, and how many
        # connections it has accepted so far.
        body = json.dumps({"port": stalled_tls_port, "connections": stalled_tls_connection_count}).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _serve_aia_config(self):
        # Lets the test page discover the per-scenario HTTPS ports (each an OS-assigned port).
        config = getattr(TestHTTPRequestHandler, "aia_config", None)
        body = json.dumps(config or {}).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(200 if config else 503)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_GET(self):
        if self.headers.get("Upgrade", "").lower() == "websocket":
            self._serve_websocket_echo()
            return

        request_path = self.path.partition("?")[0]

        if request_path.startswith("/unblock/"):
            self._serve_unblock()
        elif request_path.startswith("/echo"):
            self.handle_echo()
        elif request_path.startswith("/recorded-request-headers/"):
            self._serve_recorded_request_headers()
        elif request_path.startswith("/recorded-request-count/"):
            self._serve_recorded_request_count()
        elif request_path.startswith("/downloads/"):
            self._serve_download()
        elif request_path.endswith(".py"):
            self._serve_wpt_python_script()
        elif request_path.startswith("/aia/"):
            self._serve_aia_artifact(request_path)
        elif request_path == "/aia-test/config":
            self._serve_aia_config()
        elif request_path == "/stalled-tls/config":
            self._serve_stalled_tls_config()
        else:
            self._serve_static_request()

    def do_POST(self):
        request_path = self.path.partition("?")[0]

        if request_path == "/echo":
            self._register_echo()
        elif request_path.startswith("/echo/"):
            self.handle_echo()
        elif request_path.endswith(".py"):
            self._serve_wpt_python_script()
        else:
            self.send_error(405, "Method Not Allowed")

    def do_OPTIONS(self):
        request_path = self.path.partition("?")[0]

        if request_path.startswith("/echo"):
            # Requests with "credentials=include" cannot have "Access-Control-Allow-Origin=*". If the test registered
            # an OPTIONS echo, return the headers that it specified.
            key = f"OPTIONS {self.path}"
            if key in echo_store:
                self.handle_echo()
                return

            self.send_response(204)
            self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
            self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Methods", "*")
            self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "*")
            self.end_headers()
        else:
            self.do_other()

    def do_PUT(self):
        self.do_other()

    def do_HEAD(self):
        self.do_other()

    def do_DELETE(self):
        self.do_other()

    def do_PROPFIND(self):
        self.do_other()

    def do_REPORT(self):
        self.do_other()

    def do_SAFE(self):
        self.do_other()

    def do_safe(self):
        self.do_other()

    def _register_echo(self):
        """Handle a request to register an echo server handler"""
        content_length = int(self.headers["Content-Length"])
        post_data = self.rfile.read(content_length)
        data = json.loads(post_data.decode("utf-8"))

        echo = Echo()
        echo.method = data.get("method", None)
        echo.path = data.get("path", None)
        echo.status = data.get("status", None)
        echo.body = data.get("body", None)
        echo.body_encoding = data.get("body_encoding", "raw")
        echo.delay_ms = data.get("delay_ms", None)
        echo.headers = data.get("headers", {})
        echo.reason_phrase = data.get("reason_phrase", None)
        echo.reflect_headers_in_body = data.get("reflect_headers_in_body", False)
        echo.close_connection = data.get("close_connection", False)
        echo.ignore_range = data.get("ignore_range", False)
        echo.wait_for_unblock = data.get("wait_for_unblock", None)

        is_invalid_echo_path = echo.path is None or not echo.path.startswith("/echo/")

        # Return 400: Bad Request if invalid params are given or a reserved path is given
        if (
            echo.method is None
            or echo.path is None
            or echo.status is None
            or echo.body_encoding not in ("raw", "base64")
            or (echo.body is not None and "$HEADERS" not in echo.body and echo.reflect_headers_in_body)
            or is_invalid_echo_path
        ):
            self.send_response(400)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
            self.end_headers()
            return

        # Return 409: Conflict if the method+path combination already exists
        key = f"{echo.method} {urllib.parse.urlparse(echo.path).path}"
        if key in echo_store and echo_store[key] != echo:
            self.send_response(409)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
            self.end_headers()
            message = (
                "Echo already exists for method+path, but with a different definition.\n"
                f"key: {key}\n"
                "Hint: Use a unique path per test run (or keep the same definition).\n"
            )
            self.wfile.write(message.encode("utf-8"))
            return

        echo_store[key] = echo
        if echo.wait_for_unblock is not None:
            unblock_events[echo.wait_for_unblock] = threading.Event()

        host = self.headers.get("host", "localhost")
        path = echo.path.lstrip("/")
        fetch_url = f"http://{host}/{path}"

        # The params to use on the client when making a request to the newly created echo endpoint
        fetch_config = {
            "method": echo.method,
            "url": fetch_url,
        }

        self.send_response(201)
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(json.dumps(fetch_config).encode("utf-8"))

    def _serve_unblock(self):
        token = urllib.parse.unquote(self.path.partition("?")[0][len("/unblock/") :])
        event = unblock_events.setdefault(token, threading.Event())
        event.set()
        self.send_response(204)
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
        self.end_headers()

    def _serve_recorded_request_headers(self):
        echo_path = self.path[len("/recorded-request-headers") :]
        headers = recorded_request_headers.get(echo_path)
        if headers is None:
            self.send_error(404, f"No recorded request at {echo_path}")
            return
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(json.dumps(headers).encode("utf-8"))

    def _serve_recorded_request_count(self):
        echo_path = self.path.partition("?")[0][len("/recorded-request-count") :]
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(json.dumps(recorded_request_counts.get(echo_path, 0)).encode("utf-8"))

    def _serve_download(self):
        name = urllib.parse.unquote(self.path.partition("?")[0][len("/downloads/") :])
        directory = TestHTTPRequestHandler.downloads_directory
        body = b""
        status = 404
        if len(name.encode("utf-8")) > MAXIMUM_REPORTED_DOWNLOAD_NAME_LENGTH:
            status = 400
        elif directory is not None and name not in ("", ".", "..") and os.path.basename(name) == name:
            path = os.path.join(directory, name)
            if os.path.isfile(path):
                with open(path, "rb") as file:
                    body = file.read()
                status = 200
            elif any(name_of_download_in_progress(entry) == name for entry in os.listdir(directory)):
                status = 202

        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def handle_echo(self):
        method = self.command.upper()
        parsed_url = urllib.parse.urlparse(self.path)
        query = urllib.parse.parse_qs(parsed_url.query)
        key = f"{method} {self.path}"
        if key not in echo_store:
            key = f"{method} {parsed_url.path}"

        headers_for_path: Dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for header, value in self.headers.items():
            headers_for_path.setdefault(header, []).append(value)
        recorded_request_headers[self.path] = headers_for_path
        with recorded_request_counts_lock:
            recorded_request_counts[parsed_url.path] = recorded_request_counts.get(parsed_url.path, 0) + 1

        if parsed_url.path != self.path:
            recorded_request_headers[parsed_url.path] = recorded_request_headers[self.path]

        # The request's body is read before responding, so closing the connection does not reset it.
        content_length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        request_body = bytearray()
        if content_length:
            read_size = int(query.get("request_body_read_size", [content_length])[0])
            read_delay_ms = int(query.get("request_body_read_delay_ms", [0])[0])
            remaining = content_length
            while remaining > 0:
                if read_delay_ms:
                    time.sleep(read_delay_ms / 1000)
                data = self.rfile.read(min(read_size, remaining))
                # The client closed the connection before sending the whole body.
                if not data:
                    break
                request_body += data
                remaining -= len(data)

        is_revalidation_request = "If-Modified-Since" in self.headers
        send_not_modified = is_revalidation_request and "X-Ladybird-Respond-With-Not-Modified" in self.headers

        send_incomplete_response = "X-Ladybird-Respond-With-Incomplete-Response" in self.headers

        set_invalid_cookie = "X-Ladybird-Set-Invalid-Cookie" in self.headers

        if key not in echo_store:
            self.send_error(404, f"Echo response not found for {key}")
            return

        echo = echo_store[key]

        if echo.close_connection:
            self.connection.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)
            self.connection.close()
            return

        if echo.wait_for_unblock is not None:
            event = unblock_events.setdefault(echo.wait_for_unblock, threading.Event())
            event.wait()

        response_headers = echo.headers.copy()

        if echo.delay_ms is not None:
            time.sleep(echo.delay_ms / 1000)

        if send_not_modified:
            self.send_response(304)
        else:
            self.send_response_only(echo.status, echo.reason_phrase)

            if is_revalidation_request:
                # Override the Last-Modified header to prevent cURL from thinking the response is still fresh.
                response_headers["Last-Modified"] = "Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT"
            elif send_incomplete_response:
                # We emulate an incomplete response by advertising a 10KB file, but only sending 2KB.
                response_headers["Content-Length"] = str(10 * 1024)

        if set_invalid_cookie:
            response_headers["Set-Cookie"] = "invalid=foo; Domain=\xc3\xa9\x6c\xc3\xa8\x76\x65\xff"

        # Set only the headers defined in the echo definition
        if response_headers:
            for header, value in response_headers.items():
                self.send_header(header, value)
            self.end_headers()

        if send_not_modified:
            return

        if send_incomplete_response:
            self.wfile.write(b"a" * (2 * 1024))
            self.wfile.flush()

            self.connection.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)
            self.connection.close()
            return

        if echo.reflect_headers_in_body:
            headers = {}
            for key in self.headers.keys():
                headers[key] = self.headers.get_all(key)
            headers = json.dumps(headers)
            response_body = echo.body.replace("$HEADERS", headers) if echo.body else headers
        else:
            response_body = echo.body or ""
        response_body = response_body.replace("$BODY", request_body.decode("utf-8", "replace"))

        # FIXME: This only supports "Range: bytes=start-end" and "Range: bytes=start-". There are other formats to
        #        support if needed: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Range#syntax
        if "Range" in self.headers and not echo.ignore_range:
            range_value = self.headers["Range"].strip()
            assert range_value.startswith("bytes=")
            assert range_value.count("-") == 1

            range_value = range_value[len("bytes=") :]
            start, end = range_value.split("-")

            if end:
                response_body = response_body[int(start) : min(int(end), len(response_body))]
            else:
                response_body = response_body[int(start) :]

        if echo.body_encoding == "base64":
            response_body_bytes = base64.b64decode(response_body)
        else:
            response_body_bytes = response_body.encode("utf-8")

        chunks = query.get("chunks", [])
        chunk_delay_ms = int(query.get("chunk_delay_ms", [0])[0] or 0)
        if chunks:
            chunk_sizes = [int(chunk_size) for chunk_size in chunks[0].split(",") if chunk_size]
            offset = 0
            chunk_unblock_tokens = query.get("chunk_unblock_tokens", [""])[0].split(",")
            for chunk_index, chunk_size in enumerate(chunk_sizes):
                self.wfile.write(response_body_bytes[offset : offset + chunk_size])
                self.wfile.flush()
                offset += chunk_size
                if chunk_index < len(chunk_unblock_tokens) and chunk_unblock_tokens[chunk_index]:
                    token = chunk_unblock_tokens[chunk_index]
                    unblock_events.setdefault(token, threading.Event()).wait()
                if chunk_delay_ms > 0:
                    time.sleep(chunk_delay_ms / 1000)
            if offset < len(response_body_bytes):
                self.wfile.write(response_body_bytes[offset:])
            return

        self.wfile.write(response_body_bytes)

    def do_other(self):
        request_path = self.path.partition("?")[0]

        if request_path.startswith("/echo"):
            self.handle_echo()
        elif request_path.endswith(".py"):
            self._serve_wpt_python_script()
        else:
            self.send_error(405, "Method Not Allowed")

    # --- Minimal RFC 6455 WebSocket echo --------------------------------------------------------------
    # Reached when a request carries an "Upgrade: websocket" header. The tests use this in place of an
    # externally-hosted echo server, so they have no network dependency. The client sends first; every
    # text/binary frame it sends is echoed back verbatim.

    def _serve_websocket_echo(self):
        if self.path == "/websocket-close-without-response":
            self.close_connection = True
            return

        key = self.headers.get("Sec-WebSocket-Key")
        if not key:
            self.send_error(400, "Missing Sec-WebSocket-Key")
            return

        # We now own the raw socket; stop the HTTP handler from parsing another request on it.
        self.close_connection = True
        self.connection.sendall(websocket_handshake_response(key))

        if self.path == "/reflect-websocket-cookie":
            self._send_websocket_frame(self.headers.get("Cookie", "").encode("utf-8"))
        elif self.path == "/reflect-websocket-accept-language":
            self._send_websocket_frame(self.headers.get("Accept-Language", "").encode("utf-8"))

        query = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlsplit(self.path).query)
        if "send-binary" in query:
            payload = bytearray(int(query["send-binary"][0]))
            payload[0] = 1
            payload[-1] = 2
            self._send_websocket_frame(bytes(payload), opcode=0x2)

        while True:
            frame = self._read_websocket_frame()
            if frame is None:
                break
            opcode, payload = frame
            if opcode == 0x8:  # Close
                self._send_websocket_close()
                break
            if opcode == 0x9:  # Ping -> Pong
                self._send_websocket_frame(payload, opcode=0xA)
                continue
            if opcode in (0x1, 0x2):  # Text / Binary -> echo verbatim
                self._send_websocket_frame(payload, opcode=opcode)

    def _recv_exact(self, count):
        data = bytearray()
        while len(data) < count:
            chunk = self.rfile.read(count - len(data))
            if not chunk:
                return None
            data += chunk
        return bytes(data)

    def _read_websocket_frame(self):
        header = self._recv_exact(2)
        if header is None:
            return None

        opcode = header[0] & 0x0F
        is_masked = (header[1] & 0x80) != 0
        length = header[1] & 0x7F
        if length == 126:
            extended = self._recv_exact(2)
            if extended is None:
                return None
            length = int.from_bytes(extended, "big")
        elif length == 127:
            extended = self._recv_exact(8)
            if extended is None:
                return None
            length = int.from_bytes(extended, "big")

        mask = b""
        if is_masked:
            mask = self._recv_exact(4)
            if mask is None:
                return None

        payload = self._recv_exact(length) if length else b""
        if payload is None:
            return None
        if is_masked:
            payload = bytes(payload[i] ^ mask[i % 4] for i in range(length))
        return opcode, payload

    def _build_ws_frame(self, data, opcode=0x1):
        header = bytearray([0x80 | opcode])
        length = len(data)
        if length < 126:
            header.append(length)
        elif length < 65536:
            header.append(126)
            header += length.to_bytes(2, "big")
        else:
            header.append(127)
            header += length.to_bytes(8, "big")
        return bytes(header) + data

    def _send_websocket_frame(self, data, opcode=0x1):
        if isinstance(data, str):
            data = data.encode("utf-8")
        try:
            self.connection.sendall(self._build_ws_frame(data, opcode))
        except OSError:
            pass

    def _send_websocket_close(self):
        try:
            self.connection.sendall(bytes([0x88, 0x00]))  # FIN + Close opcode, empty payload.
        except OSError:
            pass


class AIALeafHandler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        if self.headers.get("Upgrade", "").lower() == "websocket":
            # Accept the handshake and hang up, so a test can tell whether a wss:// connection got past TLS.
            self.wfile.write(websocket_handshake_response(self.headers.get("Sec-WebSocket-Key", "")))
            self.close_connection = True
            return

        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", "2")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b"ok")

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: Any) -> None:
        pass


class AIATLSServer(socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer):
    daemon_threads = True
    allow_reuse_address = True

    def __init__(self, server_address, handler, ssl_context):
        super().__init__(server_address, handler)
        self._ssl_context = ssl_context

    def get_request(self):
        sock, addr = super().get_request()
        try:
            return self._ssl_context.wrap_socket(sock, server_side=True), addr
        except OSError:
            sock.close()
            raise


def _setup_tls_test_servers(http_port, ca_cert_output):
    import datetime
    import tempfile

    from cryptography import x509  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import ec  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import Encoding  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import NoEncryption  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import PrivateFormat  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import pkcs7  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
    from cryptography.x509.oid import AuthorityInformationAccessOID  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
    from cryptography.x509.oid import ExtendedKeyUsageOID  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
    from cryptography.x509.oid import NameOID  # type: ignore[import-not-found]

    def new_key():
        return ec.generate_private_key(ec.SECP256R1())

    def dn(common_name):
        return x509.Name([x509.NameAttribute(NameOID.COMMON_NAME, common_name)])

    not_before, not_after = datetime.datetime(2020, 1, 1), datetime.datetime(2050, 1, 1)

    root_key = new_key()
    root = (
        x509.CertificateBuilder()
        .subject_name(dn("Ladybird AIA Test Root"))
        .issuer_name(dn("Ladybird AIA Test Root"))
        .public_key(root_key.public_key())
        .serial_number(x509.random_serial_number())
        .not_valid_before(not_before)
        .not_valid_after(not_after)
        .add_extension(x509.BasicConstraints(ca=True, path_length=None), critical=True)
        .sign(root_key, hashes.SHA256())
    )

    aia_base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{http_port}/aia"
    artifacts = {}
    scenarios = {}

    def add_scenario(name, host, artifact_name, encoding, shared=None):
        # By default, each scenario gets its own intermediate — so fetching one never populates the cache for another
        # (which would mask whether that scenario's own fetch and parse ran). The de-dupe scenarios instead share one
        # intermediate — to check it's fetched only once.
        if shared is not None:
            intermediate, intermediate_key = shared
        else:
            intermediate_key = new_key()
            intermediate = (
                x509.CertificateBuilder()
                .subject_name(dn(f"Ladybird AIA Test Intermediate ({name})"))
                .issuer_name(root.subject)
                .public_key(intermediate_key.public_key())
                .serial_number(x509.random_serial_number())
                .not_valid_before(not_before)
                .not_valid_after(not_after)
                .add_extension(x509.BasicConstraints(ca=True, path_length=0), critical=True)
                .sign(root_key, hashes.SHA256())
            )
        if encoding == "der":
            artifacts[f"/aia/{artifact_name}"] = ("application/pkix-cert", intermediate.public_bytes(Encoding.DER))
            aia_url = f"{aia_base}/{artifact_name}"
        elif encoding == "pkcs7":
            artifacts[f"/aia/{artifact_name}"] = (
                "application/pkcs7-mime",
                pkcs7.serialize_certificates([intermediate], Encoding.DER),
            )
            aia_url = f"{aia_base}/{artifact_name}"
        else:
            aia_url = f"{aia_base}/dead"  # 404: the intermediate is never published

        leaf_key = new_key()
        leaf = (
            x509.CertificateBuilder()
            .subject_name(dn(host))
            .issuer_name(intermediate.subject)
            .public_key(leaf_key.public_key())
            .serial_number(x509.random_serial_number())
            .not_valid_before(not_before)
            .not_valid_after(not_after)
            .add_extension(x509.SubjectAlternativeName([x509.DNSName("localhost")]), critical=False)
            .add_extension(x509.ExtendedKeyUsage([ExtendedKeyUsageOID.SERVER_AUTH]), critical=False)
            .add_extension(
                x509.AuthorityInformationAccess(
                    [
                        x509.AccessDescription(
                            AuthorityInformationAccessOID.CA_ISSUERS, x509.UniformResourceIdentifier(aia_url)
                        )
                    ]
                ),
                critical=False,
            )
            .sign(intermediate_key, hashes.SHA256())
        )
        scenarios[name] = (leaf, leaf_key)
        return intermediate, intermediate_key

    add_scenario("good_der", "good-der.localhost", "intermediate-der.der", "der")
    add_scenario("good_pkcs7", "good-pkcs7.localhost", "intermediate-pkcs7.p7c", "pkcs7")
    add_scenario("dead", "dead.localhost", None, "dead")
    shared_intermediate = add_scenario("dedup_a", "dedup-a.localhost", "intermediate-dedup.der", "der")
    add_scenario("dedup_b", "dedup-b.localhost", "intermediate-dedup.der", "der", shared_intermediate)

    # Negative trust control: The caIssuers URL serves a self-signed cert that's *not* anchored in the trusted test
    # root. A fetched intermediate must never complete a chain to an untrusted anchor — so this host must fail to load.
    untrusted_key = new_key()
    untrusted = (
        x509.CertificateBuilder()
        .subject_name(dn("Ladybird AIA Test UNTRUSTED root"))
        .issuer_name(dn("Ladybird AIA Test UNTRUSTED root"))
        .public_key(untrusted_key.public_key())
        .serial_number(x509.random_serial_number())
        .not_valid_before(not_before)
        .not_valid_after(not_after)
        .add_extension(x509.BasicConstraints(ca=True, path_length=None), critical=True)
        .sign(untrusted_key, hashes.SHA256())
    )
    artifacts["/aia/untrusted.der"] = ("application/pkix-cert", untrusted.public_bytes(Encoding.DER))
    untrusted_leaf_key = new_key()
    untrusted_leaf = (
        x509.CertificateBuilder()
        .subject_name(dn("untrusted-leaf.localhost"))
        .issuer_name(untrusted.subject)
        .public_key(untrusted_leaf_key.public_key())
        .serial_number(x509.random_serial_number())
        .not_valid_before(not_before)
        .not_valid_after(not_after)
        .add_extension(x509.SubjectAlternativeName([x509.DNSName("localhost")]), critical=False)
        .add_extension(x509.ExtendedKeyUsage([ExtendedKeyUsageOID.SERVER_AUTH]), critical=False)
        .add_extension(
            x509.AuthorityInformationAccess(
                [
                    x509.AccessDescription(
                        AuthorityInformationAccessOID.CA_ISSUERS,
                        x509.UniformResourceIdentifier(f"{aia_base}/untrusted.der"),
                    )
                ]
            ),
            critical=False,
        )
        .sign(untrusted_key, hashes.SHA256())
    )
    scenarios["untrusted"] = (untrusted_leaf, untrusted_leaf_key)

    # Leaves issued by the root itself, naming localhost either only in the Common Name or also in a subjectAltName.
    def add_root_issued_scenario(name, subject_alt_names):
        leaf_key = new_key()
        builder = (
            x509.CertificateBuilder()
            .subject_name(dn("localhost"))
            .issuer_name(root.subject)
            .public_key(leaf_key.public_key())
            .serial_number(x509.random_serial_number())
            .not_valid_before(not_before)
            .not_valid_after(not_after)
            .add_extension(x509.ExtendedKeyUsage([ExtendedKeyUsageOID.SERVER_AUTH]), critical=False)
        )
        if subject_alt_names:
            builder = builder.add_extension(x509.SubjectAlternativeName(subject_alt_names), critical=False)
        scenarios[name] = (builder.sign(root_key, hashes.SHA256()), leaf_key)

    add_root_issued_scenario("common_name_only", [])
    add_root_issued_scenario("subject_alt_name", [x509.DNSName("localhost")])

    TestHTTPRequestHandler.aia_artifacts = artifacts

    # Write the root CA so RequestServer (via --certificate/CAINFO) trusts the completed chains.
    with open(ca_cert_output, "wb") as ca_file:
        ca_file.write(root.public_bytes(Encoding.PEM))

    # WPT tests reach HTTPS origins on localhost and 127.0.0.1, and cross-origin ones on the alternate host and its
    # subdomains ({{hosts[alt][]}} and {{hosts[alt][www]}}), so the WPT HTTPS server presents a leaf for all of them,
    # issued by the root itself.
    wpt_leaf_key = new_key()

    def make_wpt_leaf(names):
        return (
            x509.CertificateBuilder()
            .subject_name(dn("localhost"))
            .issuer_name(root.subject)
            .public_key(wpt_leaf_key.public_key())
            .serial_number(x509.random_serial_number())
            .not_valid_before(not_before)
            .not_valid_after(not_after)
            .add_extension(x509.SubjectAlternativeName(names), critical=False)
            .add_extension(x509.ExtendedKeyUsage([ExtendedKeyUsageOID.SERVER_AUTH]), critical=False)
            .sign(root_key, hashes.SHA256())
        )

    wpt_leaf = make_wpt_leaf(
        [
            x509.DNSName("localhost"),
            # NB: curl ignores a wildcard with fewer than two dots, so the alternate host is named outright.
            x509.DNSName("not-localhost.localhost"),
            x509.DNSName("*.not-localhost.localhost"),
            x509.IPAddress(ipaddress.ip_address("127.0.0.1")),
            x509.IPAddress(ipaddress.ip_address("::1")),
        ]
    )
    scenarios["wpt"] = (wpt_leaf, wpt_leaf_key)

    scratch = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ladybird-aia-")
    config = {}
    wpt_ssl_context = None
    for name, (leaf, leaf_key) in scenarios.items():
        # The cert file holds *only* the leaf — so, each HTTPS host presents a broken chain (the intermediate is omitted
        # and must be fetched via AIA).
        cert_path = os.path.join(scratch, f"{name}.crt")
        key_path = os.path.join(scratch, f"{name}.key")
        with open(cert_path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(leaf.public_bytes(Encoding.PEM))
        with open(key_path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(leaf_key.private_bytes(Encoding.PEM, PrivateFormat.TraditionalOpenSSL, NoEncryption()))
        context = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
        context.load_cert_chain(certfile=cert_path, keyfile=key_path)
        if name == "wpt":
            wpt_ssl_context = context
            continue
        server = AIATLSServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), AIALeafHandler, context)
        config[name] = server.socket.getsockname()[1]
        threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()

    # Tests reach HTTPS origins on unique *.localhost hosts, which no wildcard can cover, so each host gets a leaf.
    @lru_cache(maxsize=128)
    def context_for_host(host):
        leaf = make_wpt_leaf([x509.DNSName(host)])
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=scratch) as certificate_directory:
            certificate_path = os.path.join(certificate_directory, "leaf.pem")
            with open(certificate_path, "wb") as certificate:
                certificate.write(leaf.public_bytes(Encoding.PEM))
            context = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
            context.load_cert_chain(certfile=certificate_path, keyfile=os.path.join(scratch, "wpt.key"))
        return context

    def use_host_certificate(socket, server_name, _context):
        if server_name and server_name.endswith(".localhost"):
            socket.context = context_for_host(server_name)

    assert wpt_ssl_context is not None
    wpt_ssl_context.sni_callback = use_host_certificate

    TestHTTPRequestHandler.aia_config = config
    logging.info("AIA test servers ready: %s (root CA at %s)", config, ca_cert_output)
    return wpt_ssl_context


def start_mirror_server(server, server_class, address, ssl_context=None):
    mirror = server_class(address, TestHTTPRequestHandler)
    mirror.daemon_threads = True
    mirror.scheme = server.scheme
    if ssl_context:
        mirror.ssl_context = ssl_context
        mirror.scheme = "https"
    mirror.router = server.router
    mirror.wpt = server.wpt
    mirror.wpt_file_handler = server.wpt_file_handler
    mirror.static_file_handler = server.static_file_handler
    threading.Thread(target=mirror.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
    return mirror


def start_server(port, static_directory, ca_cert_output=None, exit_when_stdin_closes=False, downloads_directory=None):
    TestHTTPRequestHandler.static_directory = os.path.abspath(static_directory)
    TestHTTPRequestHandler.wpt_directory = os.path.join(
        TestHTTPRequestHandler.static_directory, "Text", "input", "wpt-import"
    )
    TestHTTPRequestHandler.downloads_directory = downloads_directory
    httpd = TestHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), TestHTTPRequestHandler)
    httpd.daemon_threads = True
    httpd.scheme = "http"
    httpd.router = SimpleNamespace(doc_root=TestHTTPRequestHandler.wpt_directory)
    httpd.wpt = WPTContext(TestHTTPRequestHandler.wpt_directory)
    httpd.wpt_file_handler = httpd.wpt.create_file_handler(base_path=TestHTTPRequestHandler.wpt_directory)
    httpd.static_file_handler = httpd.wpt.create_file_handler(
        base_path=TestHTTPRequestHandler.static_directory,
        url_base="/static/",
    )

    # WPT tests reach a second HTTP origin through {{ports[http][1]}}, so serve the same content on another port.
    alternate_httpd = start_mirror_server(httpd, TestHTTPServer, ("127.0.0.1", 0))

    https_httpd = None
    if ca_cert_output:
        # Avoid trusting a stale CA if setup fails. Preserve the inode granted by the sandbox.
        open(ca_cert_output, "wb").close()

        try:
            wpt_ssl_context = _setup_tls_test_servers(httpd.socket.getsockname()[1], ca_cert_output)
            if wpt_ssl_context:
                # WPT tests reach HTTPS origins through {{ports[https][0]}}, so serve the same content over TLS too.
                https_httpd = start_mirror_server(httpd, TestHTTPSServer, ("127.0.0.1", 0), wpt_ssl_context)
        except Exception as error:
            logging.exception("TLS test setup failed: %s", error)

    # A localhost name resolves to ::1 first, which Windows is slow to refuse, so serve there too.
    ipv6_servers = []
    for server in (httpd, alternate_httpd):
        try:
            ipv6_servers.append(start_mirror_server(server, TestHTTPServerIPv6, ("::1", server.server_address[1])))
        except OSError as error:
            logging.warning("Not serving on ::1: %s", error)
    if https_httpd:
        try:
            ipv6_servers.append(
                start_mirror_server(
                    https_httpd, TestHTTPSServerIPv6, ("::1", https_httpd.server_address[1]), https_httpd.ssl_context
                )
            )
        except OSError as error:
            logging.warning("Not serving HTTPS on ::1: %s", error)

    https_ports = [https_httpd.socket.getsockname()[1]] if https_httpd else []
    httpd.wpt.configure_server([httpd.socket.getsockname()[1], alternate_httpd.socket.getsockname()[1]], https_ports)

    start_stalled_tls_listener()

    # The first line holds the HTTP port, followed by the HTTPS port if there is one.
    print(" ".join(str(port) for port in [httpd.socket.getsockname()[1], *https_ports]))
    sys.stdout.flush()

    if exit_when_stdin_closes:

        def shut_down_when_stdin_closes():
            sys.stdin.buffer.read()
            httpd.shutdown()

        threading.Thread(target=shut_down_when_stdin_closes, daemon=True).start()

    try:
        httpd.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        httpd.wpt.close()
        for server in ipv6_servers:
            server.server_close()
        alternate_httpd.server_close()
        if https_httpd:
            https_httpd.server_close()
        httpd.server_close()


def start_stalled_tls_listener():
    global stalled_tls_port

    listener = socket.create_server(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    stalled_tls_port = listener.getsockname()[1]

    def hold_until_closed(connection):
        with connection:
            try:
                while connection.recv(4096):
                    pass
            except OSError:
                pass

    def accept_connections():
        global stalled_tls_connection_count

        while True:
            connection = listener.accept()[0]
            stalled_tls_connection_count += 1
            threading.Thread(target=hold_until_closed, args=(connection,), daemon=True).start()

    threading.Thread(target=accept_connections, daemon=True).start()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run a HTTP echo server")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-d",
        "--directory",
        type=str,
        default=".",
        help="Directory to serve static files from",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-p",
        "--port",
        type=int,
        default=0,
        help="Port to run the server on",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--exit-when-stdin-closes",
        action="store_true",
        help="Shut down once stdin reaches end-of-file, as when the process that started the server closes it or exits",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--ca-cert-output",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Path to write the AIA test root CA (PEM) to; enables the AIA broken-chain HTTPS servers",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--downloads-directory",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Directory the browser saves downloads to, as reported by GET /downloads/<name>",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    start_server(
        port=args.port,
        static_directory=args.directory,
        ca_cert_output=args.ca_cert_output,
        exit_when_stdin_closes=args.exit_when_stdin_closes,
        downloads_directory=args.downloads_directory,
    )

     first and last content lines. -->
<div class="frame" style="width: 130px;">
    <span class="rel">aa bb<br>cccccccc dddddd<br>ee<span class="cb"></span></span>
</div>

     the block, last content line after it, the block itself excluded. -->
<div class="frame">
    <span class="rel">before<div style="height: 40px;">block</div>after<span class="cb"></span></span>
</div>

     border contraction. -->

    aa <span class="rel" dir="rtl" style="border-left: 4px solid; border-right: 8px solid;">bb cc<span class="cb"></span></span> dd
</div>

     inline-start and inline-end borders. -->
<div class="frame" dir="rtl">
    aa <span class="rel" style="border-left: 4px solid; border-right: 8px solid;">bb cc<span class="cb"></span></span> dd
</div>

     extent instead of a line-height-derived one. -->

    <span class="rel">x<span style="display: inline-block; width: 30px; height: 60px; vertical-align: bottom;"></span>y<span class="cb"></span></span>
</div>

<table><tr><td style="width: 200px;"><span class="rel">cell text<span class="cb"></span></span></td></tr></table>

     context while its containing block is the outer inline: the containing
     block rect arrives through the standalone hoisted record. -->
